children.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

children.text: lalitavistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitavistara</s>.

children.text: // om namo daśadiganantāparyantalokadhātupratiṣṭhitasarvabuddhabodhisattvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: // <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, Noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> established in the world-systems of the ten directions, boundless and infinite — past, future, and present! //

body.text: START Parivarta 1
body.translated_text: START Chapter 1

body.text: nidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Nidāna</s> chapter, the first.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasminsamaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ / tadyathā - āyuṣmatā ca jñānakauṇḍinyena / āyuṣmatā cāśvajitā / āyuṣmatā ca bāṣpeṇa / āyuṣmatā ca mahānāmnā / āyuṣmatā ca bhadrikeṇa / āyuṣmatā ca yaśodevena / āyuṣmatā ca vimalena / āyuṣmatā ca subāhunā / āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇena / āyuṣmatā ca gavāṃpatinā / āyuṣmatā corubilvākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca nadīkāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca gayākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa / āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena / āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca mahākātyāyanena / āyuṣmatā ca kaphilena / āyuṣmatā ca kauṇḍinyena / āyuṣmatā ca cunandena / āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputreṇa / āyuṣmatā cāniruddhena / āyuṣmatā ca nandikena / āyuṣmatā ca kasphilena / āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā / āyuṣmatā ca revatena / āyuṣmatā ca khadiravanikena / āyuṣmatā cāmogharājena / āyuṣmatā ca mahāpāraṇikena / āyuṣmatā ca bakkulena / āyuṣmatā ca nandena / āyuṣmatā ca rāhulena / āyuṣmatā ca svāgatena / āyuṣmatā cānandena / evaṃpramukhairdvādaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ dvātriṃśatā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sarvairekajātipratibaddhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapāramitānirjātaiḥ sarvabodhisattvābhijñatāvikrīḍitaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratibhānapratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvadhāraṇīpratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapraṇidhānasuparipūrṇaiḥ sarvabodhisattvapratisamyaggatiṃgataiḥ sarvabodhisattvasamādhivaśitāprāptaiḥ sarvabodhisattvavaśitāpratilabdhaiḥ sarvabodhisattvakṣāntyavakīrṇaiḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmiparipūrṇaiḥ / tadyathā - maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / dharaṇīśvararājena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / siṃhaketunā
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks, twelve thousand monks. Namely: the venerable <s>Jñānakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, the venerable <s>Bāṣpa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānāman</s>, the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>, the venerable <s>Yaśodeva</s>, the venerable <s>Vimala</s>, the venerable <s>Subāhu</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the venerable <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, the venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Kaphila</s>, the venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Cunanda</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, the venerable <s>Nandika</s>, the venerable <s>Kasphila</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Khadiravanika</s>, the venerable <s>Amogharāja</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāpāraṇika</s>, the venerable <s>Bakkula</s>, the venerable <s>Nanda</s>, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>, the venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Together with twelve thousand monks headed by these, and thirty-two thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all bound by a single birth [before Buddhahood], having accomplished all <s>Bodhisattva</s> perfections (<s>pāramitās</s>), sporting in all <s>Bodhisattva</s> super-knowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>), having attained all <s>Bodhisattva</s> retentive powers (<s>dhāraṇīs</s>) and eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), having attained all <s>Bodhisattva</s> retentive powers, having perfectly fulfilled all <s>Bodhisattva</s> vows (<s>praṇidhānas</s>), having gone to their proper course in all <s>Bodhisattva</s> [stages], having attained mastery over all <s>Bodhisattva</s> concentrations (<s>samādhis</s>), having attained all <s>Bodhisattva</s> masteries (<s>vaśitās</s>), adorned with all <s>Bodhisattva</s> patient endurances (<s>kṣāntis</s>), and having fulfilled all <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharaṇīśvararāja</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>

body.text: ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / siddhārthamatinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / praśāntacāritramatinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / pratisaṃvitprāptena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / nityodyuktena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / mahākaruṇācandriṇā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / evaṃpramukhairdvātriṃśatā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Siṃhaketu</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Siddhārthamati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Praśāntacāritramati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Pratisaṃvitprāpta</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Nityodyukta</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahākaruṇācandrin</s>. Together with thirty-two thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> headed by these. //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīmupaniśritya viharati sma satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaśca tisṛṇāṃ pariṣadāṃ rājñāṃ rājakumārāṇāṃ rājamantriṇāṃ rājamahāmātrāṇāṃ rājapādamūlikānāṃ kṣatriyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatyamātyapārṣadyānāṃ paurajānapadānāmanyatīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakānām / lābhī ca bhagavān prabhūtānāṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyamāsvādanīyākalpikānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām / lābhāgryayaśogryaprāptaśca bhagavān sarvatra cānupaliptaḥ padma iva jalena / udāraśca bhagavataḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko loke 'bhyudgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavit paraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān pañcacakṣuḥsamanvāgataḥ / sa imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇīn prajān sadevamānuṣān svayaṃ vijñāya sākṣātkṛtya upasaṃpadya viharati sma / saddharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ vrahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Now at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, dwelling near the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, was honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the three assemblies: kings, princes, royal ministers, chief royal officers, those at the feet of kings, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, counselors and their retinues, citizens and countryfolk, and wandering ascetics of other schools — <s>Śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and <s>Parivrājakas</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> received abundant offerings — food to be chewed and eaten, savories, and requisites of robes, alms-bowl, bedding, and medicines for the sick. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having attained the foremost of gains and the foremost of fame, was everywhere unstained, like a lotus by water. And the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s lofty renown, fame, and reputation had arisen in the world: an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), well-gone (<s>Sugata</s>), knower of the world (<s>Lokavid</s>), supreme, charioteer of persons to be tamed (<s>Puruṣadamyasārathi</s>), teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, endowed with the five eyes. He, having known and directly realized this world and the next, with its gods, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, its generations of ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, its gods and humans — dwelt [thus]. He taught the true <s>Dharma</s>, good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, with the right meaning and the right words, complete, perfect, pure, and utterly purified; he proclaimed the holy life (<s>Brahmacarya</s>). //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān rātryāṃ madhyame yāme buddhālaṃkāravyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūt / samanantarasamāpannasya ca bhagavata imaṃ buddhālaṃkāravyūhaṃ nāma samādhimatha tatkṣaṇameva bhagavata upariṣṭānmūrdhnaḥ saṃdhāvuṣṇīṣavivarāntarāt pūrvabuddhānusmṛtyasaṅgājñānālokālaṃkāraṃ nāma raśmiścacāra / sā sarvā śuddhāvāsān devabhavanānyavabhāsya maheśvaradevaputrapramukhānaprameyān devaputrān saṃcodayāmāsa / tataśca tathāgataraśmijālānniścārya imāḥ saṃcodanāgāthā niścaranti sma //
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered a concentration called 'the Array of the <s>Buddha</s>'s Adornments' (<s>Buddhālaṃkāravyūha</s>). And immediately upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s entering this concentration called 'the Array of the <s>Buddha</s>'s Adornments,' at that very moment, from above the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s head, from the opening of the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance), there issued forth a ray of light called 'the Adornment of the Unhindered Light of Knowledge of the Recollection of Former <s>Buddhas</s>' (<s>Pūrvabuddhānusmṛtyasaṅgājñānālokālaṃkāra</s>). That [ray], having illuminated all the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) celestial mansions, roused the immeasurable <s>Devaputras</s> headed by the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>. And then from the net of rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, these verses of exhortation issued forth: //

children.text: jñānaprabhaṃ hatatamasaṃ prabhākaraṃ śubhraprabhaṃ śubhavimalāgratejasam /
children.translated_text: The light of knowledge, destroyer of darkness, radiant, of brilliant and pure luminance, of the foremost splendor,

children.text: praśāntakāyaṃ śubhaśāntamānasaṃ muniṃ samāśliṣyata śākyasiṃham // Lal_1.1 //
children.translated_text: of pacified body and auspicious, tranquil mind — embrace the Sage, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>! // Lal_1.1 //

children.text: jñānodadhiṃ śuddhamahānubhāvaṃ dharmeśvaraṃ sarvavidaṃ munīśam /
children.translated_text: The ocean of knowledge, of pure and great majesty, the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, omniscient, the Lord of Sages,

children.text: devātidevaṃ naradevapūjyaṃ dharme svayaṃbhuṃ vaśinaṃ śrayadhvam // Lal_1.2 //
children.translated_text: the god beyond gods, venerable among divine and human beings, self-arisen in <s>Dharma</s>, the master — take refuge in Him! // Lal_1.2 //

children.text: yo durdamaṃ cittamavartayadvaśe yo mārapāśairavamuktamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who brought the untamable mind under control, whose mind is freed from the snares of <s>Māra</s>,

children.text: yasyāpyavandhyāviha darśanaśravāstyayāntataḥ śāntavimokṣapāragaḥ // Lal_1.3 //
children.translated_text: whose vision and hearing are never fruitless here, and who has reached the further shore of peace and liberation. // Lal_1.3 //

children.text: ālokyabhūtaṃ tamatulyadharmaṃ tamonudaṃ sannayaveditāram /
children.translated_text: Having beheld this incomparable <s>Dharma</s> that has come into being, the dispeller of darkness, the knower of the right way,

children.text: śāntakriyaṃ buddhamameyabuddhiṃ bhaktyā samastā upasaṃkramadhvam // Lal_1.4 //
children.translated_text: the maker of peace, the <s>Buddha</s> of immeasurable wisdom — approach Him all together with devotion! // Lal_1.4 //

children.text: sa vaidyarājo 'mṛtabheṣajapradaḥ sa vādiśūraḥ kugaṇipratāpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the king of physicians, the giver of the nectar-medicine; He is the champion of debate, the queller of false logicians;

children.text: sa dharmabandhuḥ paramārthakovidaḥ sa nāyako 'nuttaramārgadeśakaḥ // Lal_1.5 //
children.translated_text: He is the friend in <s>Dharma</s>, skilled in the ultimate truth; He is the guide, the teacher of the unsurpassed path. // Lal_1.5 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: samanantaraspṛṣṭāśca khalu punaste śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ tasyā buddhānusmṛtyasaṅgājñānālokāyā raśmyā ābhiścaivaṃrūpābhirgāthābhiḥ saṃcoditāḥ samantataḥ praśāntāḥ samādhervyutthāya tān buddhānubhāvenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāgaṇanāsamatikrāntakalpātikrāntān buddhān bhagavanto 'nusmaranti sma / teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ yāni buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhātparṣanmaṇḍalāni yāśca dharmadeśanāstā āsan, tān sarvānanusmaranti sma //
body.translated_text: Now those <s>Devaputras</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> host, touched by that ray of the 'Light of the Unhindered Knowledge of the Recollection of Former <s>Buddhas</s>' and exhorted by these and similar verses, became completely pacified everywhere, rose from concentration, and by the power of the <s>Buddha</s> recollected the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> who had passed beyond immeasurable, incalculable, innumerable, and surpassing <s>kalpas</s>. And they recollected the assemblies and <s>maṇḍalas</s> of those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, adorned with the qualities of their <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and the <s>Dharma</s>-teachings they had given. //

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ rātrau praśāntāyāmīśvaraśca nāma śuddhāvāsakāyiko devaputro maheśvaro nāma nandaśca sunandaśca candanaśca mahitaśca praśāntaśca praśāntavinīteśvaraścaite cānye ca saṃbahulāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā atikrāntātikrāntairvarṇaiḥ sarvāvantaṃ jetavanaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāman, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte tasthuḥ / ekānte sthitāśca te śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā bhagavantametadavocan - asti bhagavan lalitavistaro nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ sūtrānto mahāvaipulyanicayo bodhisattvakuśalamūlasamudbhāvanaḥ tuṣitavarabhavanavikiraṇasaṃcintyāvakramaṇavikrīḍanagarbhasthānaviśeṣasaṃdarśano 'bhijātajanmabhūmiprabhāvasaṃdarśanaḥ sarvabālacaryāguṇaviśeṣasamatikramasarvalaukikaśilpasthānakarmasthānalipisaṃkhyāmudrā - gaṇanāsidhanukalāpayuddhasālambhasarvasattvaprativiśiṣṭasaṃdarśanāntaḥpuraviṣayopabhogasaṃdarśanaḥ sarvabodhisattvacariniṣpandaniṣpattiphalādhigamaparikīrtano bodhisattvavikrīḍitaḥ sarvamāramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanaḥ tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāṣṭādaśāveṇikasamuccayo
body.translated_text: Then, during that peaceful night, the <s>Devaputra</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> host named <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Praśānta</s>, <s>Praśāntavinīteśvara</s>, and many other <s>Devaputras</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> host, illuminating the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with divine radiance of surpassing hues, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached, bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, those <s>Devaputras</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> host addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'There is, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the <s>Lalitavistara</s>, a <s>sūtra</s>, a great extensive collection, which brings forth the roots of merit of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, which displays the splendors of the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven — the deliberate descent, the sport [of birth], the womb-state, the special manifestations — which displays the greatness of the noble birth and its realm, which surpasses all the special qualities of childhood conduct, all worldly crafts and arts, writing, counting, symbolic gestures, mathematics, archery, sports, wrestling, and the display of being distinguished from all beings, the display of inner-chamber life and enjoyment of sense-pleasures, which proclaims all the conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — its unmovingness, accomplishment, and the attainment of the fruit — the sport of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the destruction of all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, the gathering of the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the [four] fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique [qualities],'

body.text: 'pramāṇabuddhadharmanirdeśaḥ pūrvakairapi tathāgatairbhāṣitapūrvaḥ / tadyathā - bhagavatā padmottareṇa ca dharmaketunā ca dīpaṃkareṇa ca guṇaketunā ca mahākareṇa ca ṛṣidevena ca śrītejasā ca satyaketunā ca vajrasaṃhatena ca sarvābhibhuvā ca hemavarṇena ca atyuccagāminā ca pravāhasāgareṇa ca puṣpaketunā ca vararūpeṇa ca sulocanena ca ṛṣiguptena ca jinavaktreṇa ca unnatena ca puṣpitena ca ūrṇatejasā ca puṣkareṇa ca suraśminā ca maṅgalena ca sudarśanena ca mahāsiṃhatejasā ca sthitabuddhidattena ca vasantagandhinā ca satyadharmavipulakīrtinā ca tiṣyeṇa ca puṣyeṇa ca lokasundareṇa ca vistīrṇabhedena ca ratnakīrtinā ca ugratejasā ca brahmatejasā ca sughoṣeṇa ca supuṣṣeṇa ca sumanojñaghoṣeṇa ca suceṣṭarūpeṇa ca prahasitanetreṇa ca guṇarāśinā ca meghasvareṇa ca sundaravarṇena ca āyustejasā ca salīlagajagāminā ca lokābhilāṣitena ca jitaśatruṇā ca saṃpūjitena ca vipaśyinā ca śikhinā ca viśvabhuvā ca kakucchandena ca kanakamuninā ca kāśyapena ca tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena bhāṣitapūrvaḥ, taṃ bhagavānapyetarhi saṃprakāśayet bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / asya ca mahāyānodbhāvanārthaṃ sarvaparapravādināṃ ca nigrahārthaṃ sarvabodhisattvānāṃ codbhāvanārthaṃ sarvamārāṇāṃ cābhibhavanārthaṃ sarvabodhisattvayānikānāṃ ca pudgalānāṃ vīryārambhasaṃjananārthaṃ saddharmasya cānuparigrahārthaṃ triratnavaṃśasyānuparigrahārthaṃ triratnavaṃśasyānupacchedanārthaṃ buddhakāryasya ca parisaṃdarśanārthamiti / adhivāsayati sma bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena sadevakasya lokasyānukampāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: 'an exposition of the immeasurable <s>Buddhadharma</s>, spoken previously by former <s>Tathāgatas</s> as well. Namely: by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Padmottara</s>, <s>Dharmaketu</s>, <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, <s>Guṇaketu</s>, <s>Mahākara</s>, <s>Ṛṣideva</s>, <s>Śrītejas</s>, <s>Satyaketu</s>, <s>Vajrasaṃhata</s>, <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, <s>Hemavarṇa</s>, <s>Atyuccagāmin</s>, <s>Pravāhasāgara</s>, <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, <s>Vararūpa</s>, <s>Sulocana</s>, <s>Ṛṣigupta</s>, <s>Jinavaktra</s>, <s>Unnata</s>, <s>Puṣpita</s>, <s>Ūrṇatejas</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Suraśmi</s>, <s>Maṅgala</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Mahāsiṃhatejas</s>, <s>Sthitabuddhidatta</s>, <s>Vasantagandhin</s>, <s>Satyadharmavipulakīrti</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Lokasundara</s>, <s>Vistīrṇabheda</s>, <s>Ratnakīrti</s>, <s>Ugratejas</s>, <s>Brahmatejas</s>, <s>Sughoṣa</s>, <s>Supuṣpa</s>, <s>Sumanojñaghoṣa</s>, <s>Suceṣṭarūpa</s>, <s>Prahasitanetra</s>, <s>Guṇarāśi</s>, <s>Meghasvara</s>, <s>Sundaravarṇa</s>, <s>Āyustejas</s>, <s>Salīlagajagāmin</s>, <s>Lokābhilāṣita</s>, <s>Jitaśatru</s>, <s>Saṃpūjita</s>, <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>, <s>Kakucchanda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> now also proclaim it — for the benefit and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare and happiness of the great multitude, of gods and humans; for the purpose of bringing forth the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, for the subduing of all opponents of other doctrines, for the bringing forth of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, for the overcoming of all <s>Māras</s>, for the arousal of vigor in all persons of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, for the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s>, for the preservation of the lineage of the Three Jewels, for the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the Three Jewels, and for the display of the <s>Buddha</s>'s work.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to those <s>Devaputras</s> by [His] silence, out of compassion for the world with its gods. //

body.text: atha khalu devaputrā bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya divyaiścandanacūrṇairagurucūrṇairmāndārapuṣpaiścābhyavakīrya tatraivāntardadhuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputras</s>, knowing of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through [His] silence, joyful, elated, delighted, and full of gladness and happiness, bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, scattered divine sandalwood powder, aloe powder, and <s>Māndāra</s> flowers, and vanished right there. //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāmeva rātryāmatyayena ca karīro maṇḍalamātravyūhastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavān prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdadbodhisattvagaṇapuraskṛtaḥ śrāvakasaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ / niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayati sma - iti hi bhikṣavo rātrau praśāntāyāmīśvaro nāma śuddhāvāsakāyiko devaputro maheśvaraśca nāma nandaśca sunandaśca candanaśca mahitaśca praśāntaśca vinīteśvaraścaite cānye ca saṃbahulāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ purvavadyāvattatraivāntardadhuḥ / atha khalu te bodhisattvāste ca mahāśrāvakā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocan - tatsādhu bhagavan, taṃ lalitavistaraṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayatu / tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca etarhi cāgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām / adhivāsayati sma bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasyānukampāmupādāya / tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, during that very night and after its passing, approached the circular arrangement of <s>Karīra</s>. Having approached, the Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat, preceded by the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, preceded by the community of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers). Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Thus, O monks, in the quiet of the night, the god-son named <s>Īśvara</s> belonging to the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) class, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, and <s>Nanda</s>, and <s>Sunanda</s>, and <s>Candana</s>, and <s>Mahita</s>, and <s>Praśānta</s>, and <s>Vinīteśvara</s>, and these and many other god-sons of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> class [came and] as before, up to the point where they disappeared right there. Then those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, having bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'It would be excellent, O Blessed One, if you would teach the <s>dharma</s> discourse called the Extensive Display (<s>Lalitavistara</s>). That will be for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great multitude, of gods and humans, and of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who have now assembled.' The Blessed One consented to those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> and to those great <s>Śrāvakas</s> by his silence, out of compassion for the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. And here this was said:

children.text: rātryāmihāsyāṃ mama bhikṣavo 'dya sukhopaviṣṭasya niraṅgaṇasya /
children.translated_text: On this night, O monks, while I was comfortably seated, free from defilements,

children.text: praviṣṭamānasya śubhairvihārairekāgracittasya samāhitasya // Lal_1.6 //
children.translated_text: having entered into auspicious meditative states, one-pointed in mind, concentrated — || Lal 1.6 ||

children.text: athāgaman devasutā maharddhayaḥ pratītavarṇa vimalaśriyojjvalāḥ /
children.translated_text: then came god-sons of great supernatural power, of well-known form, radiant with stainless splendor,

children.text: śriyāvabhāsyeha ca jetasāhvayaṃ vanaṃ mudā me 'ntikamabhyupāgatāḥ // Lal_1.7 //
children.translated_text: and illuminating this grove called <s>Jeta</s> with their glory, they joyfully approached my presence. || Lal 1.7 ||

children.text: maheśvaraścandana īśa nando praśāntacitto mahitaḥ sunandanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> and <s>Candana</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Praśāntacitta</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Sunandana</s>,

children.text: śāntāhvayaścāpyuta devaputrastāstāśca bahvyo 'tha ca devakoṭyaḥ // Lal_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and the god-son named <s>Śānta</s>, and those many other millions of gods — || Lal 1.8 ||

children.text: praṇamya pādau pratidakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvaiva māṃ tasthurihāgrato me /
children.translated_text: having bowed at my feet and performed circumambulation, they stood here before me,

children.text: pragṛhya caivāñjalimaṅgulībhiḥ sagauravā māmiha te yayācuḥ // Lal_1.9 //
children.translated_text: and with palms joined with their fingers, reverently they entreated me: || Lal 1.9 ||

children.text: idaṃ mune rāganisūdanāḍhya vaipulyasūtraṃ hi mahānidānam /
children.translated_text: 'O Sage, rich in the destruction of passion, this extensive <s>sūtra</s>, the great introduction —

children.text: yadbhāṣitaṃ sarvatathāgataiḥ prāg lokasya sarvasya hitārthametat // Lal_1.10 //
children.translated_text: that which was spoken by all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> before, for the benefit of the entire world — || Lal 1.10 ||

children.text: tatsādhvidānīmapi bhāṣato muniḥ sa bodhisattvaughaparigrahecchayā /
children.translated_text: may the Sage kindly speak it now too, with the desire to embrace the host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: paraṃ mahāyānamidaṃ prabhāṣayan parapravādānnamuciṃ ca dharṣayan // Lal_1.11 //
children.translated_text: proclaiming this supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>, challenging the heterodox teachers and <s>Namuci</s> (Māra).' || Lal 1.11 ||

children.text: adyeṣaṇāṃ devagaṇasya tūṣṇīmagṛhṇadevānadhivāsanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The entreaty of the host of gods he accepted in silence, and [gave] his consent.

children.text: sarve ca tuṣṭā muditā udagrāḥ puṣpāṇi cikṣepuravāptaharṣam // Lal_1.12 //
children.translated_text: All, satisfied, joyful, and elated, scattered flowers, having obtained delight. || Lal 1.12 ||

children.text: tadbhikṣavo me śṛṇuteha sarve vaipulyasūtraṃ hi mahānidānam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O monks, all of you, hear here the extensive <s>sūtra</s>, the great introduction,

children.text: yadbhāṣitaṃ sarvatathāgataiḥ prāg lokasya sarvasya hitārthamevam // Lal_1.13 //
children.translated_text: that which was spoken by all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> before, for the benefit of the entire world, thus.' || Lal 1.13 ||

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. ||

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare nidānaparivarto nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first chapter in the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, called the Introduction (<s>Nidānaparivarta</s>). ||

body.text: START Parivarta 2
body.translated_text: START Chapter 2

body.text: samutsāhaparivarto dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The second chapter, [called] the Chapter of Exhortation (<s>Samutsāhaparivarta</s>).

body.text: tatra bhikṣavaḥ katamaḥ sulalitavistaro nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ sūtrānto mahāvaipulyaḥ? iha bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya tuṣitavarabhavanāvasthitasya pūjyapūjitasyābhiṣekaprāptasya devaśatasahasrastutastaumitavarṇitapraśaṃsitasya labdhābhiṣekasya praṇidhānasamudgatasya sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgatabuddheḥ suvipulapariśuddhajñānanayanasya smṛtimatigatidhṛtyuttaptavipulabuddheḥ dānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāmahopāyakauśalyaparamapāramitāprāptasya mahāmaitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣābrahmapathakovidasya mahābhijñāsaṃgaṇāvaraṇajñānasaṃdarśanābhimukhībhūtasya smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇaṛddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgasarvabodhipakṣadharmasuparipūrṇakoṭiprāptasya aparimitapuṇyasaṃbhāralakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamalaṃkṛtakāyasya dīrghānuparivartino yathāvāditathākāryavitathavākkarmasamudāhārakasya ṛjvakuṭilāvaṅkāpratihatamānasasya sarvamānamadadarpabhayaviṣādāpagatasya sarvasattvasamacittasya aparimitabuddhakoṭinayutaśatasahasraparyupāsitasya bahubodhisattvakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāvalokitāvalokitavadanasya śakrabrahmamaheśvaralokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragarākṣasagaṇairabhinanditayaśasaḥ sarvapadaprabhedanirdeśāsaṅgapratisaṃvidavatārajñānakuśalasya sarvabuddhabhāṣitadhāraṇasmṛtibhājanāvikṣepānantāparyantadhāraṇīpratilabdhasya mahādharmanausmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇaṛdvipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgapāramitopāya - kauśalyadharmaratnapuṇyasamudānītamahāsārthavāhasya caturoghapāragāminābhiprāyasya nihatamānapratyarthikasya sarvaparapravādisunigṛhītasya saṃgrāmaśīrṣasupratiṣṭhitasya kleśaripugaṇanisūdanasya jñānavaravajradṛḍhapraharaṇasya bodhicittamūlamahākaruṇādaṇḍādhyāśayodgatasya gambhīravīryasalilābhiṣiktasya upāyakauśalakarṇikasya bodhyaṅgadhyānakeśarasya samādhikiñjalkasya guṇagaṇavimalasarasisujātasya vigatamadamānaparivāhaśaśivimalavistīrṇapatrasya śīlaśrutāprasādadaśadigapratihatagandhino loke jñānavṛddhasyāṣṭābhirlokadharmairanupaliptasya mahāpuruṣapadmasya puṇyajñānasaṃbhāravisṛtasurabhigandhinaḥ prajñājñānadinakarakiraṇairvikasitasuviśuddhaśatapatrapadmatapanasya caturṛddhipādaparamajāpajapitasya caturāryasatyasutīkṣṇanakhadaṃṣṭrasya caturbrahmavihāraniśritadarśanasya catuḥsaṃgrahavastususaṃgṛhītaśirasaḥ dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpādānubodhānupūrvasamudgatakāyasya saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣadharmasaṃpratipūrṇasuvijātināvidyājñānakeśariṇastrivimokṣamukhāvajṛmbhitasya śamathavidarśanāsuviśuddhanayanasya dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattigiridarīguhānivāsitasya caturīryāpathavinayanaupavanasuvardhitatarordaśabalavaiśāradyābhyāsībhāvitabalasya vigatabhavavibhavabhayalomaharṣasyāsaṃkucitaparākramasya tīrthyaśaśamṛgagaṇasaṃghaśamathanasya nairātmyaghoṣodāhāramahāsiṃhanādanādinaḥ puruṣasiṃhasya vimuktidhyānamaṇḍalaprajñaprabharaśmitīrthakarakhadyotagaṇaniḥprabhaṃkarasya
body.translated_text: Here, O monks, what is this <s>dharma</s> discourse, the <s>sūtra</s>-text, the great extensive [teaching], called the Beautiful Extensive Display (<s>Sulalitavistara</s>)? Here, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, venerated and honored, having received consecration, praised, lauded, described, and extolled by hundreds of thousands of gods, having obtained consecration, arisen through his vows, whose understanding had accumulated all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, whose eye of knowledge was vast and supremely pure, whose extensive understanding was refined through mindfulness, insight, penetration, and steadfastness; who had attained the supreme perfection of giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, and great skillful means; who was skilled in the <s>Brahma</s>-path of great friendliness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; who was face-to-face with the display of the knowledge that is free from all obstructions and endowed with the great superknowledges; who had attained the ultimate completion and perfection of the establishments of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, and all factors conducive to awakening; whose body was adorned with the marks and minor characteristics [produced by] limitless accumulations of merit; who was long-practiced, whose deeds matched his words, whose speech and action were never false; whose mind was straight, uncrooked, unbent, and unobstructed; who was free from all pride, intoxication, arrogance, fear, and despondency; who was equal-minded toward all beings; who had attended upon immeasurable millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddha</s> millions; whose face was beheld by many millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; whose fame was celebrated by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, the world-guardians, and the hosts of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>; who was skilled in the knowledge of descent through unobstructed analytical knowledge and the exposition of every category; who had obtained the <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions) that were endless, boundless, undistracted — vessels of the memory and retention of all the speech of the <s>Buddhas</s>; who was a great caravan-leader bringing forth the treasure of <s>dharma</s> through the great ship of <s>dharma</s>, the establishments of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, perfections, and skillful means, together with merit; whose intention was to cross beyond the four floods; who had vanquished the adversary of pride; who had well-subdued all heterodox disputants; who was well-established at the head of battle; who destroyed the host of affliction-enemies; who wielded the firm weapon of the vajra of supreme knowledge; who had arisen from the root of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), the staff of great compassion, and superior intention; who was anointed with the water of deep vigor; whose pericarp was skillful means; whose filaments were the factors of awakening in meditation; whose pistils were the concentrations; who was well-born in the stainless lake of the host of virtues, like [a lotus]; whose leaves were broad, stainless like the moon, free from the drainage of pride and arrogance; whose fragrance — of morality, learning, and serene faith — was unobstructed in the ten directions; who was mature in knowledge in the world, untainted by the eight worldly <s>dharmas</s>; [who was] the great lotus among persons; whose pleasing fragrance spread from the accumulations of merit and knowledge; whose supremely pure hundred-petaled lotus opened by the rays of the sun of wisdom and knowledge; whose supreme recitation was the four bases of supernatural power; whose sharp teeth and fangs were the four noble truths; whose abode of seeing was the four <s>Brahma</s>-abodes; whose head was well-gathered by the four means of attraction; whose body had arisen in gradual sequence through awakening to the twelve-limbed dependent origination; who was a well-born lion of noble lineage, complete with the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, who had rent open ignorance; whose gaping was the three doors of liberation; whose eyes were supremely purified through calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>); who dwelt in the mountain-caves of the meditations, liberations, concentrations, and attainments; who was a tree well-grown in the pleasure-grove of disciplining [himself] through the four modes of deportment, whose strength was cultivated through the practice of the ten powers and the [four] fearlessnesses; who was free from the hair-raising fear of existence and prosperity; whose valor was undiminished; who scattered the herds of heretic deer-like foxes; whose great lion's roar was the proclamation of the cry of selflessness; [who was] the lion among persons; who rendered the hosts of fireflies — the <s>tīrthakas</s> — lightless by the splendor of the rays of the jewel-maṇḍala of the liberation, meditation, and wisdom;

body.text: avidyātamondhakāratamaḥpaṭalavitimirakaraṇasyottaptabalavīryasya devamanuṣyeṣu puṇyatejastejitasya mahāpuruṣadinakarasya kṛṣṇapakṣāpagatasya śuklapakṣapratipūrṇasya manāpapriyadarśanasya apratihatacakṣurindriyasya devaśatasahasrajyotirgaṇapratimaṇḍitasya dhyānavimokṣajñānamaṇḍalasya bodhyaṅgasukharaśmiśaśikiraṇasya buddhavibuddhamanujakumudavibodhakasya mahāpuruṣacandrasamacatuṣparṣaddvīpānuparītasya saptabodhyaṅgaratnasamanvāgatasya sarvasattvasamacittaprayogasyāpratihatabuddheḥ daśakuśalakarmapathavratatapasaḥ susamṛddhapratipūrṇaviśeṣagamanābhiprāyasya apratihatadharmarājāvarapravaradharmaratnacakrapravartakasya cakravartivaṃśakulakuloditasya gambhīraduravagāhapratītyasamutpādasarvadharmaratnapratipūrṇasya atṛptaśrutavipulavistīrṇārambhajñānaśīlavelānatikramaṇasya mahāpadmagarbhekṣaṇasya sāgaravaradharavipulabuddheḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyusamacittasya merukalpadṛḍhabalāprakampamānasyānunayapratighāpagatasya body.translated_text: who dispelled the coverings and veils of the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); whose strength and vigor were refined; who blazed with the splendor of merit among gods and humans; [who was] the sun among great persons; free from the dark fortnight, full in the bright fortnight; pleasing and delightful to behold; whose faculty of sight was unobstructed; who was adorned by hundreds of thousands of god-like luminous hosts; whose maṇḍala was of meditation, liberation, and knowledge; whose moonbeams were the rays of the happiness of the factors of awakening; who caused the lotuses of awakened and awakening humans to bloom; [who was] the moon among great persons, surrounded by the four assemblies as if by continents; who was endowed with the seven jewels of the factors of awakening; whose endeavor was equal-minded toward all beings; whose understanding was unobstructed; whose vow and austerity was the ten courses of wholesome action; whose intention was of richly fulfilled and distinctly superior attainment; who was the supreme and best turner of the precious wheel of the unobstructed <s>dharma</s>-kingdom and supreme <s>dharma</s>; who had arisen in the lineage and family of the <s>Cakravartin</s> dynasty; who was filled with the <s>dharma</s>-jewel of the profound, hard-to-fathom dependent origination of all phenomena; who never transgressed the shore-limit of the knowledge and morality of the vast, extensive, insatiable learning; who had the eyes of a great lotus-womb; whose understanding was vast like an ocean and mountain; whose mind was equal to earth, water, fire, and wind; who was unshakable and of firm strength like <s>Meru</s>; who was free from attachment and aversion; whose understanding was stainless, vast, irresistible, and extensive like the expanse of the sky; whose superior intention was supremely pure; who had given well-given gifts; whose prior connections (<s>pūrvayoga</s>) were well-made; whose authority (<s>adhikāra</s>) was well-established; who had given his pledge of truth; who had sought out all roots of wholesome merit; whose impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) were perfumed; who was as it were the outflow of all roots of wholesome merit; whose all roots of wholesome merit had been accumulated over seven incalculable aeons; who had given the seven kinds of gifts; who had practiced the five kinds of meritorious activity; who had practiced threefold good conduct by body, fourfold by speech, threefold by mind; who had practiced the path of the ten family-karmas without seizing [wrong conduct]; who had practiced the right exertion endowed with forty aspects; who had made the right aspiration endowed with forty aspects; who had entered into the right superior intention endowed with forty aspects; who had fulfilled the right liberation endowed with forty aspects; who had cultivated the right conviction endowed with forty aspects; who had gone forth among forty <s>Buddha</s> millions of millions of hundreds of thousands; who had given gifts among fifty-five <s>Buddha</s> millions of millions of hundreds of thousands; who had established his authority among three and a half hundreds of millions of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; who had guided immeasurable and incalculable beings onto the path of heaven and liberation; who wished to fully awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening; who was bound by a single birth [to Buddhahood]; who, having departed from here, was dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven; [who was] the supreme god-son named <s>Śvetaketu</s>, worshipped by all the assemblies of gods; [about whom it was said:] 'He who has descended, emitting rays of immeasurable [light], born in the world of mortals, will before long fully awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: tasmin mahāvimāne sukhopaviṣṭasya dvātriṃśadbhūmisahasrapratisaṃsthite vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣakūṭāgāraprāsādatalasamalaṃkṛte ucchritachatradhvajapaṭākaratnakiṅkiṇījālavitānavitate māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpasaṃstaraṇasaṃstṛte apsarasaḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃgītisaṃpracalite atimuktakacampakapāṭalakovidāramucilindamahāmucilindāśokanyagrodhatindukāsanakarṇikārakeśarasālaratnavṛkṣopaśobhite hemajālasaṃchanne mahatā pūrṇakumbhopaśobhite samatalavyūhopaśobhite jyotirmālikāsumanovāte devakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrābhimukhanayanāvalokitāloke mahāvipuladharmasaṃgītisarvakāmarativegakleśacchedane vyapagatākhilakrodhapratighamānamadadarpāpanayane prītiprasādaprāmodyottaptavipulasmṛtisaṃjanane sukhopaviṣṭasya tasmin mahādharmasāṃkathye pravṛtte tebhyaścaturaśītibhyastūryasaṃgītisahasranirnāditebhyo bodhisattvasya pūrvaśubhakarmopacayenemāḥ saṃcodanāgāthā niścaranti sma -
body.translated_text: While he sat comfortably in that great palace — established upon thirty-two thousand levels, adorned with terraces, projecting balconies, arched gateways, latticed windows, turrets, and mansion-floors; festooned with raised parasols, banners, pennants, and nets of jewel-bells and canopies; strewn with couches of <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s> flowers; set in motion by the music of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>Apsarases</s>; beautified by <s>Atimukta</s>, <s>Campaka</s>, <s>Pāṭala</s>, <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s>, great <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Nyagrodha</s>, <s>Tinduka</s>, <s>Āsana</s>, <s>Karṇikāra</s>, <s>Keśara</s>, <s>Sāla</s>, and jeweled trees; covered with golden nets; beautified with great filled vases; beautified with a level arrangement; fragrant with garlands of lights and <s>Sumanā</s> flowers; [its] radiance beheld face-to-face by millions of hundreds of thousands of gods; [a palace] for the cutting off of the rush of all pleasure-seeking and afflictions through the great, vast <s>dharma</s>-concert; for the removal of all anger, aversion, pride, intoxication, and arrogance; for the generation of joy, serene faith, gladness, and vast, refined mindfulness — while he sat comfortably, and while that great <s>dharma</s>-conversation was in progress, and while those eighty-four thousand musical concerts resounded, these verses of exhortation issued forth through the accumulation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s prior wholesome deeds:

children.text: smara vipulapuṇyanicaya smṛtimatigatimanantaprajñāprabhākarin /
children.translated_text: Remember, O one rich in the accumulation of vast merit, mindfulness, insight, penetration, and the radiance of infinite wisdom!

children.text: atulabalavipulavikrama vyākaraṇaṃ dīpaṃkarasyāpi // Lal_2.1 //
children.translated_text: of incomparable strength, vast, and heroic — the prophecy by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> as well. || Lal_2.1 ||

children.text: smara vipulanirmalamanas trimalamalaprahīṇaśāntamadadoṣam /
children.translated_text: Remember, O one of vast, pure mind, who has abandoned the three stains, peaceful, free from pride and fault,

children.text: śubhavimalaśuddhacittā dāmacarī yādṛśā ti pure // Lal_2.2 //
children.translated_text: of pure, stainless, clean mind — what the practice of restraint (<s>dāmacarī</s>) was like in former times. || Lal_2.2 ||

children.text: smara kulakulīnā śamathaṃ śīlavrataṃ kṣamā damaṃ caiva /
children.translated_text: Remember — of noble birth and family — tranquility, moral conduct, vows, patience, self-control,

children.text: vīryabaladhyānaprajñā niṣevitā kalpa(koṭī)niyutāni // Lal_2.3 //
children.translated_text: effort, strength, meditation, and wisdom, practiced for millions of aeons. || Lal_2.3 ||

children.text: smara smara anantakīrte saṃpūjitā ye ti buddhaniyutāni /
children.translated_text: Remember, remember, O one of boundless fame — millions of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped.

children.text: sarvān karuṇāyamānaḥ kālo 'yaṃ mā upekṣasva // Lal_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Showing compassion toward all — this is the time; do not be indifferent! || Lal_2.4 ||

children.text: cyava cyava hi cyutividhijñā jaramaraṇakleśasūdanā virajā /
children.translated_text: Descend, descend — for you are skilled in the manner of descent, a destroyer of old age, death, and affliction, free from impurity.

children.text: samudīkṣante bahavo devāsuranāgayakṣagandharvā // Lal_2.5 //
children.translated_text: Many are looking on — gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>. || Lal_2.5 ||

children.text: kalpasahasra ramitvā tṛptirnāstyambhasīva samudre /
children.translated_text: Having delighted for thousands of aeons, there is no satisfaction, like the ocean with its waters.

children.text: sādhu bhava prajñātṛpta tarpaya janatāṃ ciratṛṣārtām // Lal_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Be good — O one filled with wisdom — and satisfy the people who have long been parched with thirst! || Lal_2.6 ||

children.text: kiṃ cāpyaninditayaśa(stvaṃ) dharmaratirato na cāsi kāmarataḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, O one of blameless fame, you delight in the <s>Dharma</s> and are not attached to sensual pleasures.

children.text: atha ca punaramalanayanā anukampā sadevakaṃ lokam // Lal_2.7 //
children.translated_text: And yet, with stainless eyes, have compassion upon the world together with its gods. || Lal_2.7 ||

children.text: kiṃ cāpi devanayutāḥ śrutvā dharmaṃ na te vitṛpyante /
children.translated_text: Moreover, though myriads of gods hear the <s>Dharma</s>, they are not satisfied.

children.text: atha ca puna rakṣaṇagatānapāyasaṃsthānapekṣasva // Lal_2.8 //
children.translated_text: And yet, look upon those who have gone to the protection of the lower realms, established in suffering. || Lal_2.8 ||

children.text: kiṃ cāpi vimalacakṣo paśyasi buddhān daśādiśi loke /
children.translated_text: Moreover, O one of stainless eyes, you see the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions of the world.

children.text: dharmaṃ śṛṇoṣi ca tatastaṃ dharmavaraṃ vibhaja loke // Lal_2.9 //
children.translated_text: And you hear the <s>Dharma</s> from them — distribute that excellent <s>Dharma</s> to the world. || Lal_2.9 ||

children.text: kiṃ cāpi tuṣitabhavanaṃ tava puṇyaśriyābhiśobhate śrīmān /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven shines with the glory of your merit, O glorious one.

children.text: atha ca puna karuṇamānasa pravarṣa jambudhvaje varṣam // Lal_2.10 //
children.translated_text: And yet, O compassionate one, rain down a shower upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! || Lal_2.10 ||

children.text: samatītya kāmadhātuṃ devā ye rūpadhātukāneke /
children.translated_text: The gods who are in the realm of form, having surpassed the desire-realm — the many [gods] of the form-realm —

children.text: sarve tyabhinandante spṛśeya siddhivrato bodhim // Lal_2.11 //
children.translated_text: all rejoice: 'May the one who has undertaken the vow of accomplishment touch awakening!' || Lal_2.11 ||

children.text: nihatā ti mārakarmā jitāstvayānye kutīrthikā nāthā /
children.translated_text: The deeds of <s>Māra</s> have been defeated, the other <s>tīrthika</s> leaders have been conquered by you.

children.text: kena sakalagata ti bodhī kālo 'yaṃ mā upekṣasva // Lal_2.12 //
children.translated_text: 'By whom has complete awakening been attained?' — This is the time; do not be indifferent! || Lal_2.12 ||

children.text: kleśāgninā pradīpte loke tvaṃ vīra meghavad vyāpya /
children.translated_text: In the world ablaze with the fire of afflictions, you, O hero, pervading like a cloud,

children.text: abhivarṣāmṛtavarṣaṃ śamaya kleśānnaramarūṇām // Lal_2.13 //
children.translated_text: rain down the rain of the deathless — extinguish the afflictions of gods and humans! || Lal_2.13 ||

children.text: tvaṃ vaidya dhātukuśala cirāturān satyavaidya satyavān /
children.translated_text: You are the physician, skilled in the elements, long treating the sick — O true physician, truthful one,

children.text: trivimokṣāgadayogairnirvāṇasukhe sthapaya śīghram // Lal_2.14 //
children.translated_text: establish [beings] swiftly in the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s> through the remedies of the three liberations! || Lal_2.14 ||

children.text: aśrutva siṃhanādaṃ kroṣṭukanādaṃ nadantyanutraṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Not having heard the lion's roar, the jackals howl boldly.

children.text: nada buddhasiṃhanādaṃ trāsaya paratīrthikaśṛgālān // Lal_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Roar the lion's roar of the <s>Buddha</s> — frighten the jackals of the rival teachers! || Lal_2.15 ||

children.text: prajñāpradīpahasto balavīryabalodito dharaṇimaṇḍe /
children.translated_text: With the lamp of wisdom in hand, risen with the power of strength and vigor upon the surface of the earth,

children.text: karatalavareṇa dharaṇīṃ parāhanitvā jinahi māram // Lal_2.16 //
children.translated_text: striking the earth with the best of your palms, conquer <s>Māra</s>, O <s>Jina</s>! || Lal_2.16 ||

children.text: samudīkṣante pālāścaturo ye tubhya dāsyate pātram /
children.translated_text: The four guardian kings are watching — they who will give you the bowl.

children.text: śakrāśca brahma nayutā ye jātaṃ tvāṃ grahīṣyanti // Lal_2.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> and myriads of <s>Brahmās</s> will receive you when you are born. || Lal_2.17 ||

children.text: vyavalokayābhiyaśā kularatnakuloditā kulakulīnā /
children.translated_text: Look, O renowned one — born in noble families, jewels of their lineages, of noble birth —

children.text: yatra sthitvā sumate darśeṣyasi bodhisattvacarim // Lal_2.18 //
children.translated_text: where, O wise one, having taken your stand, you will display the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. || Lal_2.18 ||

children.text: yatraiva bhājane 'smin maṇiratnaṃ tiṣṭhate bhavati śrīmān /
children.translated_text: Just as a jewel, when placed in a vessel, makes it glorious —

children.text: maṇiratnaṃ vimalabuddhe pravarṣa jambudhvaje varṣam // Lal_2.19 //
children.translated_text: O jewel of a stainless <s>Buddha</s>, rain down a shower upon <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! || Lal_2.19 ||

children.text: evaṃ bahuprakārā saṃgītiravānuniścarā gāthā /
children.translated_text: Thus, with verses of many kinds, the songs that were produced in concert

children.text: codenti karuṇāmanasaṃ ayaṃ sa kālo mā upekṣasva // Lal_2.20 //
children.translated_text: urge the compassionate one: 'This is the time — do not be indifferent!' || Lal_2.20 ||

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. ||

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare samutsāhaparivarto nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second chapter, called 'The Chapter on Exhortation (<s>Samutsāhaparivarta</s>),' in the Holy <s>Lalitavistara</s>. ||

body.text: START Parivarta 3
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 3.

body.text: kulapariśuddhiparivartastṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Third Chapter: On the Purity of Lineage (<s>Kulapariśuddhiparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattva evaṃ dharmakālasaṃcoditaḥ saṃstato mahāvimānānniṣkramya dharmoccayo nāma mahāprāsādo yatra niṣadya bodhisattvastuṣitebhyo devebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati sma, taṃ bodhisattvo 'bhirohati sma, abhiruhya ca sudharme siṃhāsane niṣīdati sma / atha ye devaputrā bodhisattvasya sabhāgāḥ samayānasaṃprasthitāste 'pi tameva prāsādamabhirohanti sma / ye ca daśadiksaṃnipatitā bodhisattvāḥ sabhāgacaritā bodhisattvasya devaputrāśca, te 'pi taṃ prāsādamabhiruhya yathāpratyarheṣu siṃhāsaneṣu svakasvakeṣu niṣīdanti, sma apagatāpsarogaṇā apagataprākṛtadevaputrāḥ samānādhyāśayaparivārā aṣṭaṣaṣṭikoṭisahasraparivārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, urged and exhorted by <s>Dharmakāla</s>, emerged from the great palace and ascended the great palace called '<s>Dharmoccaya</s>' (Accumulation of <s>Dharma</s>), where the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having seated himself, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods. Having ascended it, he sat upon the lion-throne in [the hall called] <s>Sudharma</s>. Then those divine sons who shared the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s nature and had set forth at the same time — they too ascended that very palace. And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had gathered from the ten directions, who shared the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conduct, and the divine sons — they too ascended that palace and sat upon their respective lion-thrones as befitted their rank, with the hosts of <s>apsarases</s> departed, with the ordinary divine sons departed, surrounded by an assembly of like aspiration, surrounded by sixty-eight million billion [beings]. ||

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo dvādaśabhirvarṣairbodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakramiṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, in twelve years the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would descend into the mother's womb. ||

body.text: atha śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā jambudvīpamāgatya divyaṃ varṇamantardhāpya brāhmaṇaveṣeṇa brāhmaṇān vedānadhyāpayanti sma / yasyaivarūpā garbhāvakrāntirbhavati, sa dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati / yaiḥ samanvāgatasya dve gatī bhavato na tṛtīyā / sacedagāramadhyāvasati, rājā bhavatī cakravartī caturaṅgo vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhavanti / tadyathā - cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ strīratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam //
body.translated_text: Then the divine sons from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) came to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, concealed their divine form, and in the guise of brahmins taught the <s>Vedas</s> to the brahmins: 'One who has a birth of such a kind is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person. For one so endowed, there are two destinations and no third: if he dwells in a household, he becomes a king, a <s>cakravartin</s>, a righteous <s>dharma</s>-king, possessed of the four divisions [of the army], victorious, endowed with the seven jewels. These are his seven jewels, namely: the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the woman-jewel, the gem-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the counselor-jewel as the seventh.' ||

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī cakraratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya tadeva poṣadheyaṃ ca pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātasyopavāsoṣitasyopariprāsādatalagatasya stryāgāraparivṛtasya pūrvasyāṃ diśi divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prādurbhavati / sahasrāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ suvarṇavarṇakarmālaṃkṛtaṃ saptatālamuccaiḥ samantād dṛṣṭvāntaḥpuraṃ rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya taddivyaṃ cakraratnameva bhavati / śrutaṃ khalu mayā yasya kila rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya tadeva poṣadheyaṃ pañcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātasyopavāsoṣitasyopariprāsādatalagatasya stryāgāraparivṛtasya pūrvasyāṃ diśi divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prādurbhavati, sa bhavati rājā cakravartī / nūnamahaṃ rājā cakravartī yannvahaṃ divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ mīmāṃsayeyam / atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikta ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ prārthayedevaṃ cāvedayet - pravartayasva bhaṭṭa divyaṃ cakraratnaṃ dharmeṇa mādharmeṇa / atha taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ rājñā kṣatriyeṇa mūrdhābhiṣiktena pravartitaṃ samyageva ṛddhau vihāyasā pūrveṇa vrajati / anveti rājā cakravartī sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena / yatra ca pṛthivīpradeśe taddivyaṃ cakraratnaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate, tatra rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto vāsaṃ kalpayati sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena / atha ye te bhavanti pūrvasyāṃ diśi rājāno maṇḍalinaḥ, te rūpyapātrīṃ vā
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the king, the <s>cakravartin</s>, endowed with the wheel-jewel? Here, on the fifteenth day, the observance day, when the king — the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — has bathed his head, has kept the fast, is on the upper terrace of the palace, surrounded by the women's quarters: in the eastern direction, a divine wheel-jewel appears — thousand-spoked, with rim, with hub, golden in color, adorned with craftsmanship, seven palm-trees high all around. Having seen it, the inner court of the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — that very divine wheel-jewel becomes his. 'I have indeed heard that for whichever king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, on the fifteenth day, the observance day, when he has bathed his head, has kept the fast, is on the upper terrace of the palace, surrounded by the women's quarters — a divine wheel-jewel appears in the eastern direction — he becomes a <s>cakravartin</s> king. Surely I am a <s>cakravartin</s> king, since I should examine this divine wheel-jewel.' Then the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, having arranged his upper garment over one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, extends his right hand and beseeches that divine wheel-jewel and declares thus: 'Roll forth, lord, the divine wheel-jewel — by <s>dharma</s>, not by <s>adharma</s>!' Then that divine wheel-jewel, set in motion by the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, proceeds correctly, flying through the air toward the east. The <s>cakravartin</s> king follows together with the fourfold army. Wherever on the earth that divine wheel-jewel stops, there the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, makes his camp together with the fourfold army. Then those kings who are subordinate rulers in the eastern direction approach the <s>cakravartin</s> king,

body.text: suvarṇacūrṇaparipūrṇāmādāya svarṇapātrīṃ vā rūpyacūrṇaparipūrṇāmādāya rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ pratyuttiṣṭhanti - ehi deva svāgataṃ devāya, idaṃ devasya rājyamṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca / adhyāvasatu deva svakaṃ vijitamanuprāptam / evamukte rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastrātā tān rājño maṇḍalina etadavocat - kārayantu bhavantaḥ svakāni rājyāni dharmeṇa / hanta bhavanto mā prāṇinaṃ ghātayiṣyatha, mādattādāsyatha, mā kāmeṣu mithyā cariṣyatha, mā mṛṣā vakṣyatha, yāvanmā bhe vijite adharmamutpadyate, mādharmacāriṇo rocetha / evaṃ khalu rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ vijayati / pūrvāṃ diśaṃ vijitaḥ pūrvaṃ samudramavagāhya pūrvaṃ samudramavatarati / pūrvaṃ samudramavatīrya samyageva ṛddhyā vihāyasā dakṣiṇena vrajati / anveti rājā cakravartī sārdhaṃ caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena / pūrvavadevaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ vijayati / yathā dakṣiṇāmevaṃ paścimāmuttarāṃ diśaṃ vijayati / uttarāṃ diśaṃ vijitya uttarasamudramavagāhate / avagāhyottarātsamudrātpratyuttarati / pratyuttīrya samyageva ṛddhyā vihāyasā rājadhānīmāgatyopari antaḥpuradvāre 'kṣatamevāsthāt / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaścakraratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: carrying a silver vessel filled with gold dust or a golden vessel filled with silver dust, and say: 'Come, O Lord, welcome to the Lord! This kingdom of the Lord is prosperous, thriving, secure, abundant in food, delightful, and teeming with many people. Let the Lord govern his own dominion that has been attained.' When thus addressed, the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, the protector, says to those subordinate kings: 'Govern your own kingdoms by <s>dharma</s>! Come, sirs — you shall not kill living beings, you shall not take what is not given, you shall not engage in sexual misconduct, you shall not speak falsehood, and so on — let no <s>adharma</s> arise in my dominion; do not approve of those who act against <s>dharma</s>.' Thus indeed the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, conquers the eastern direction. Having conquered the eastern direction, having plunged into the eastern ocean, he crosses the eastern ocean. Having crossed the eastern ocean, [the wheel-jewel] proceeds correctly, flying through the air toward the south. The <s>cakravartin</s> king follows together with the fourfold army. Just as the eastern direction, so he conquers the southern direction. As the southern, so the western and the northern directions. Having conquered the northern direction, he plunges into the northern ocean. Having plunged in, he emerges from the northern ocean. Having emerged, [the wheel] proceeds correctly, flying through the air to the royal capital, and stands intact above the gateway of the inner palace. Of such a kind is the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, endowed with the wheel-jewel. ||

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī hastiratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavaddhastiratnamutpadyate / sarvaśvetaṃ saptāṅgasupratiṣṭhitaṃ svarṇacūḍakaṃ svarṇadhvajaṃ svarṇālaṃkāraṃ hemajālapraticchannaṃ ṛddhimantaṃ vihāyasā gāminaṃ vikurvaṇādharmiṇaṃ yaduta bodhirnāma nāgarājā / yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastaddhastiratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati, atha sūryasyābhyudgamanavelāyāṃ taddhastiratnamabhiruhya imāmeva mahāpṛthivīṃ samudraparikhāṃ samudraparyantāṃ samantato 'nvāhiṇḍya rājadhānīmāgatya praśāsanaratiḥ pratyanubhavati / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī hastiratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the elephant-jewel? Here, as before, an elephant-jewel appears for the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — entirely white, seven-limbed, well-proportioned, with a golden crest, a golden banner, golden ornaments, covered with a golden net, possessing supernatural power, able to travel through the air, capable of magical transformation — namely, the <s>nāga</s>-king called <s>Bodhi</s>. And when the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, wishes to test that elephant-jewel, then at sunrise he mounts that elephant-jewel, traverses this entire great earth — bounded by the ocean, extending to the ocean — in all directions, returns to the royal capital, and enjoys the pleasure of governance. Of such a kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the elephant-jewel. ||

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī aśvaratnena samanvāgato bhavati? atha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavadaśvaratnamutpadyate / sarvanīlaṃ kṛṣṇaśirasaṃ muñjakeśamādṛtavadanaṃ svarṇadhvajaṃ svarṇālaṃkāraṃ hemajālapraticchannaṃ ṛddhimantaṃ vihāyasā gāminaṃ vikurvaṇādharmiṇaṃ yaduta bālāhako nāmāśvarājam / yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto 'śvaratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati, atha sūryasyābhyudgamanavelāyāmaśvaratnamabhiruhya imāmeva mahāpṛthvīṃ samudraparikhāṃ samudraparyantāṃ samantanto 'nvāhiṇḍya rājadhānīmāgatya praśāsanaratiḥ pratyanubhavati / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartīṃ aśvaratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the horse-jewel? Then, as before, a horse-jewel appears for the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — entirely blue-black, with a black head, with mane like <s>muñja</s> grass, with an eager countenance, with a golden banner, golden ornaments, covered with a golden net, possessing supernatural power, able to travel through the air, capable of magical transformation — namely, the horse-king called <s>Bālāhaka</s>. And when the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, wishes to test the horse-jewel, then at sunrise he mounts the horse-jewel, traverses this entire great earth — bounded by the ocean, extending to the ocean — in all directions, returns to the royal capital, and enjoys the pleasure of governance. Of such a kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the horse-jewel. ||

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartīṃ maṇiratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavanmaṇiratnamutpadyate śuddhanīlavaiḍūryamaṣṭāṃśaṃ suparikarmakṛtam / tasya khalu punarmaṇiratnasyābhayā sarvamantaḥpuramavabhāsyena sphuṭaṃ bhavati / yadā ca rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktastaṃ
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the gem-jewel? Here, as before, a gem-jewel appears for the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — pure blue lapis lazuli, octagonal, well-fashioned. By the radiance of that gem-jewel, the entire inner palace is illuminated and made bright. And when the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, that

body.text: maṇiratnaṃ mīmāṃsitukāmo bhavati, atha rātryāmardharātrasamaye 'ndhakāratamisrāyāṃ taṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre ucchrāpayitvā udyānabhūmiṃ niryāti subhūmidarśanāya / tasya khalu punarmaṇiratnasyābhayāsarvāvantaṃ caturaṅgabalakāyamavabhāsena sphuṭībhavati sāmantena yojanam / ye khalu punastasya maṇiratnasya sāmantake manuṣyāḥ prativasanti, te tenāvabhāsenāsphuṭa samānā anyonyaṃ saṃjānanti, anyonyaṃ paśyanti, anyonyamāhuḥ - uttiṣṭha bhadramukhāḥ karmāntāni kārayataḥ āpaṇāni prasārayata, divā manyāmahe sūryamabhyudgatam / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto maṇiratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: wishes to examine the jewel-gem. Then, at midnight in the dark of night, he raises that jewel-gem upon the top of a banner and goes out to the garden grounds to view the beautiful terrain. By the radiance of that jewel-gem, the entire fourfold army in its vicinity becomes clearly visible, for a <s>yojana</s> around. And those people who dwell in the vicinity of that jewel-gem, illuminated by that radiance, recognize one another, see one another, and say to one another: 'Arise, good people! Carry out your tasks! Open your shops! We think it is daytime and the sun has risen.' Endowed with a jewel-gem of such a kind is the anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> king. //

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī strīratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavatstrīratnamutpadyate / sadṛśī kṣatriyā nātidīrghā nātihrasvā nātisthūlā nātikṛśā nātigaurī nātikṛṣṇā abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā / tasyāḥ sarvaromakūpebhyaścandanagandhaṃ pravāti, mukhāccotpalagandhaṃ pravāti / kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśā / śītalakāle cāsyā uṣṇasaṃsparśāni gātrāṇi bhavanti, uṣṇakāle ca śītasaṃsparśāni / sā rājānaṃ cakravartinaṃ muktvā nānyasmin manasāpi rāgaṃ karoti kiṃ punaḥ kāyena / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī strīratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the woman-jewel? Here, for the anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> king, a woman-jewel arises as before — a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman of good family, neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too thin, neither too fair nor too dark, beautiful, graceful, and pleasing to behold. From all the pores of her body wafts the fragrance of sandalwood, and from her mouth wafts the fragrance of the blue lotus. Her touch is as pleasant as <s>Kācilinḍika</s> cloth. In the cold season her limbs are warm to the touch, and in the hot season they are cool to the touch. She does not feel desire, even mentally, for anyone other than the <s>cakravartin</s> king — how much less with her body. Endowed with a woman-jewel of such a kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king. //

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī gṛhapatiratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya pūrvavad gṛhapatiratnamutpadyate paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī divyacakṣuḥ / sa tena divyacakṣuṣā sāmantena yojanaṃ sasvāmikāni nidhānāni paśyati, asvāmikāni nidhānāni paśyati / sa yāni tāni bhavanti asvāmikāni, tai rājñaścakravartino dhanena karaṇīyaṃ karoti / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī gṛhapatiratnena samanvāgato bhavati //
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the householder-jewel? Here, for the anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> king, a householder-jewel arises as before — learned, capable, intelligent, possessing the divine eye. With that divine eye he sees, for a <s>yojana</s> around, treasures that have owners and treasures that have no owners. Those that are ownerless — with those he accomplishes whatever needs to be done with the <s>cakravartin</s> king's wealth. Endowed with a householder-jewel of such a kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king. //

body.text: kathaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī pariṇāyakaratnena samanvāgato bhavati? iha rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhāṣibhiktasya pūrvavatpariṇāyakaratnamutpadyate paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī / rājñacakravartinaścintitamātreṇa udyojayitavyaṃ senāmudyojayati sma / evaṃrūpeṇa rājā cakravartī pariṇāyakaratnena samanvāgato bhavati / ebhiḥ saptaratnaiḥ samanvāgato bhaviṣyati / bhavati cāsya putrasahasraṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām / sa imāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ sasāgaraparyantāmakhilāmakaṇṭakāmadaṇḍenāśastreṇābhinirjityādhyāsayati / sacedagārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati, vāntachandarāgo netā ananyadevaḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king endowed with the general-jewel? Here, for the anointed <s>kṣatriya</s> king, a general-jewel arises as before — learned, capable, and intelligent. By the mere thought of the <s>cakravartin</s> king, he would mobilize the army. Endowed with a general-jewel of such a kind is the <s>cakravartin</s> king. He will be endowed with these seven jewels. And he will have a thousand sons — heroes, valiant ones, of beautiful form, crushers of enemy armies. He will conquer this great earth, bounded by the ocean, whole and unobstructed, without violence and without weapons, and rule over it. And if he should go forth from the household life into homelessness, having abandoned desire and passion, he will become a guide, having no other deity, a teacher of gods and humans. //

body.text: tathā anye 'pi devaputrā jambudvīpamāgatya pratyekabuddhebhya ārocayanti sma - riñcata mārṣā buddhakṣetram / ito dvādaśavatsare bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakramiṣyati //
body.translated_text: Likewise, other <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) also went to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and announced to the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>: 'Vacate the <s>Buddha</s>-field, venerable ones! In twelve years the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will descend into his mother's womb.' //

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena rājagṛhe mahānagare golāṅgulaparivartane parvate mātaṅgo nāma pratyekabuddho viharati sma / sa taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā kardama iva śilāyāṃ prasthāya vihāyasā saptatālamātramatyudgamya ca tejodhātuṃ samāpadyolkeva parinirvāṇo 'yam / yattasya pittaśleṣmasnāyvasthimāṃsarudhiraṃ
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on the mountain called <s>Golāṅgulaparivartana</s>, there dwelt a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Mātaṅga</s>. Having heard that announcement, like a clod of clay from a rock, he departed, rose into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, entered the fire-element, and attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> like a flame. Whatever was his bile, phlegm, sinews, bones, flesh, and blood —

body.text: cāsīt, tatsarvaṃ tejasā paryavadānamagacchat / śuddhaśarīrāṇyeva bhūmau prāpatan / adyāpi ca tāni ṛṣipadānyeva saṃjñāyante //
body.translated_text: — all of that was consumed by the fire. Only the purified bones fell to the ground. And to this day that place is known as <s>Ṛṣipada</s> (the Sage's Footprint). //

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena vārāṇasyāṃ ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve pañca pratyekabuddhaśatāni viharanti sma / te 'pi taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā vihāyasā saptatālamātramatyudgamya tejodhātuṃ samāpadyolkeva parinirvānti sma / yatteṣāṃ pittaśleṣmamāṃsāsthisnāyurudhiraṃ cābhūt, tatsarvaṃ tejasā paryavadānamagacchat / śuddhaśarīrāṇyeva bhūmau prāpatan / asminnṛṣayaḥ patitā iti tasmātprabhṛti ṛṣipatanasaṃjñodapādi / abhayadattāśca tasmin mṛgāḥ prativasanti iti tadagreṇa mṛgadāvasya mṛgadāva iti saṃjñodapādi //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Sages' Descent), in the Deer Park, five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> were dwelling. They too, having heard that announcement, rose into the sky to the height of seven palm trees, entered the fire-element, and attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> like flames. Whatever was their bile, phlegm, flesh, bones, sinews, and blood — all of that was consumed by the fire. Only the purified bones fell to the ground. 'In this place the sages fell' — from that time onward, the name <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Sages' Descent) arose. And since fearless deer dwelt there, from that [fact] the name Deer Park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>) arose. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanasthitaścatvāri mahāvilokitāni vilokayati sma / katamāni catvāri? tadyathā - kālavilokitaṃ dvīpavilokitaṃ deśavilokitaṃ kulavilokitam //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, contemplated the four great contemplations. What are the four? Namely: the contemplation of the time, the contemplation of the continent, the contemplation of the region, and the contemplation of the family. //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ kālavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma? na bodhisattva ādipravṛtte loke sattvasaṃvartanīkālasamaye mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati, atha tarhi yadā vyakto lokaḥ susthito bhavati, jāti prajñāyate, jarā prajñāyate, vyādhi prajñāyate, maraṇaṃ prajñāyate, tadā bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati //
body.translated_text: For what reason, O monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> contemplate the time? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not descend into his mother's womb at the beginning of the world's evolution, at the time of the gathering of beings. Rather, when the world is fully developed and well-established, when birth is recognized, when old age is recognized, when disease is recognized, when death is recognized — then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> descends into his mother's womb. //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bodhisattvo dvīpavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma? na bodhisattvā pratyantadvīpā upapadyante, na purvavidehe, nāparagodānīye, na cottarakurau / atha tarhi jambudvīpa evopapadyante //
body.translated_text: For what reason did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> contemplate the continent? <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not born in outlying continents, not in <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, not in <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, not in <s>Uttarakuru</s>. Rather, they are born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> alone. //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvo deśavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma? na bodhisattvāḥ pratyantajanapadeṣūpapadyante, yeṣu manuṣyā andhajātyā jaḍā eḍamūkajātīyā abhavyāḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāmarthaṃ jñātum / atha tarhi bodhisattvā madhyameṣveva janapadeṣūpapadyante //
body.translated_text: For what reason, O monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> contemplate the region? <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not born in outlying regions, where people are born blind, dull, deaf and mute by nature, and incapable of understanding the meaning of what is well-spoken and ill-spoken. Rather, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are born in the central regions alone. //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ kulavilokitaṃ vilokayati sma? na bodhisattvā hīnakuleṣūpapadyante caṇḍālakuleṣu vā veṇukārakule vā rathakārakule vā puṣkasakule vā / atha tarhi kuladvaye evopapadyante brāhmaṇakule kṣatriyakule ca / tatra yadā brāhmaṇaguruko loko bhavati, tadā brāhmaṇakule upapadyante / yadā kṣatriyaguruko loko bhavati, tadā kṣatriyakule upapadyante / etarhi bhikṣavaḥ kṣatriyaguruko lokaḥ / tasmādbodhisattvāḥ kṣatriyakule upapadyante / tamarthaṃ ca saṃpratītya bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanasthaścatvāri mahāvilokitāni vilokayati sma //
body.translated_text: For what reason, O monks, did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> contemplate the family? <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not born in low families — in <s>caṇḍāla</s> families, bamboo-worker families, chariot-maker families, or <s>puṣkasa</s> families. Rather, they are born in only two kinds of families: <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families and <s>kṣatriya</s> families. When the world honors <s>brāhmaṇas</s> as foremost, then they are born in <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families. When the world honors <s>kṣatriyas</s> as foremost, then they are born in <s>kṣatriya</s> families. At present, O monks, the world honors <s>kṣatriyas</s> as foremost. Therefore, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are born in <s>kṣatriya</s> families. And understanding this very meaning, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, contemplated the four great contemplations. //

body.text: evaṃ cāvalokya tūṣṇīmabhūt / iti hi bhikṣavaste devaputrāḥ bodhisattvasyānyonyaṃ paripṛcchanti sma - katamasmin kularatne kiyadrūpāyāṃ jananyāṃ bodhisattvaḥ pratiṣṭhateti / tatra kecidāhuḥ - idaṃ vaidehīkulaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca / idaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhasthānam / apare tvāhuḥ - na tatpratirūpam / tatkasmāt? tathā hi - tanna
body.translated_text: Having thus contemplated, he fell silent. Then, O monks, the <s>devaputras</s> inquired of each other about the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'In what jewel of a family, and in what kind of mother, will the <s>Bodhisattva</s> take his stand?' Therein, some said: 'This <s>Vaidehī</s> family in the <s>Magadha</s> region is prosperous, thriving, secure, and well-provisioned. This is suitable as the place of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-dwelling.' But others said: 'That is not suitable. Why? Because that [family] is not

body.text: mātṛśuddhaṃ pitṛśuddhaṃ aplutaṃ cañcalamanavasthitaṃ parittapuṇyābhiṣyanditaṃ na vipulapuṇyābhiṣiktaṃ satkulapradeśopacāraṃ nodyānasarastaḍāgākīrṇaṃ karvaṭamiva pratyantavāsam / tena na tatpratirūpam //
body.translated_text: pure on the mother's side or the father's side; it is unstable and wavering, sprinkled with limited merit and not anointed with abundant merit, situated near a poor locality, not abounding in gardens, lakes, and ponds — like a hamlet in an outlying region. Therefore, that is not suitable.' //

body.text: apare tvāhuḥ - idaṃ punaḥ kauśalakulaṃ mahāvāhanaṃ ca mahāparivāraṃ ca mahādhanaṃ ca / tatpratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / apare 'pyāhuḥ - tadapyapratirūpam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi - kauśalakulaṃ mātaṅgacyutyupapannaṃ na mātṛpitṛśuddham / hīnādhimuktikaṃ na ca kuloditaṃ na cāparimitadhanaratnanidhisamutthitam / tena na tatpratirūpam //
body.translated_text: Others said: 'This <s>Kauśala</s> family has great armies, great retinue, and great wealth. It is suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' Yet others said: 'That too is not suitable. Why? Because the <s>Kauśala</s> family is of <s>Mātaṅga</s> (outcast) descent, not pure on the mother's or father's side, of low aspirations, not of distinguished lineage, and not possessed of limitless wealth and treasure-stores. Therefore, that is not suitable.' //

body.text: apare tvāhuḥ - idaṃ vaṃśarājakulaṃ ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca / idaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhasthānamiti / apara evamāhuḥ - idamapyapratirūpam / kiṃ kāraṇam? tathāhi - vaṃśarājakulaṃ prākṛtaṃ ca caṇḍaṃ ca na cojjvalitatejasaṃ parapuruṣajanmāvṛtaṃ ca na mātṛpitṛsvatejaḥ karmābhinirvṛttaṃ ca / ucchedavādī ca tatra rājā / tena tadapyapratirūpam //
body.translated_text: Others said: 'This <s>Vaṃśarāja</s> family is prosperous, thriving, secure, and well-provisioned. This is suitable as the place of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-dwelling.' Yet others said: 'This too is not suitable. Why? Because the <s>Vaṃśarāja</s> family is common and fierce, not brilliant in splendor, concealed by the birth of alien men, not accomplished through the power of the mother's and father's own merit. And the king there holds the doctrine of annihilationism. Therefore, that too is not suitable.' //

body.text: apare 'pyāhuḥ - iyaṃ vaiśālī mahānagarī ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ramaṇīyā cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādatalasamalaṃkṛtā ca puṣpavāṭikāvanarājisaṃkusumitā ca amarabhavanapuraprākāśyā / sā pratirūpāsya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / apara āhuḥ - sāpyapratirūpā / kiṃ kāraṇam? tathā hi - teṣāṃ nāsti parasparanyāyavāditā, nāsti dharmācaraṇam, noccamadhyavṛddhajyeṣṭhānupālitā / ekaika eva manyate - ahaṃ rājā, ahaṃ rājeti / na ca kasyacicchiṣyatvamabhyupagacchati na dharmatvam / tena sāpyapratirūpā //
body.translated_text: Yet others said: 'This great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> is prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, teeming with many people, adorned with terraces, projections, arched gateways, latticed windows, mansions, turrets, and palaces, blossoming with groves of flowers and forest rows, resembling the city of the immortals. It is suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' Others said: 'That too is not suitable. Why? Because among them there is no mutual adherence to justice, no practice of <s>dharma</s>, no honoring of the elder, the middle-aged, and the senior. Each one thinks: "I am the king, I am the king." No one accepts the status of a disciple or of one governed by <s>dharma</s>. Therefore, that too is not suitable.' //
