body.text: apare tvevamāhuḥ - idaṃ pradyotakulaṃ mahābalaṃ ca mahāvāhanaṃ ca paracamūśirasi vijayalabdhaṃ ca / tatpratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / apare tvevamāhuḥ - tadapyapratirūpam / kiṃ kāraṇam? tathā hi - te caṇḍāśca capalāśca raudrāśca paruṣāśca sāhasikāśca, na ca karmadarśinaḥ / tena tadapyapratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti //
body.translated_text: Yet others said: 'This <s>Pradyota</s> family is of great strength, great armies, and has won victory over the heads of enemy forces. It is suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' Yet others said: 'That too is not suitable. Why? Because they are fierce, fickle, savage, harsh, and reckless, and they do not believe in <s>karma</s>. Therefore, that too is not suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' //

body.text: apara evamāhuḥ - iyaṃ mathurā nagarī ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca / rājñaḥ subāhoḥ kaṃsakulasya śūraseneśvarasya rājadhāniḥ / sā pratirūpāsya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / apare tvāhuḥ - sāpyapratirūpā / kiṃ kāraṇam? tathāhi - sa rājā mithyādṛṣṭikulavaṃśaprasūto dasyurājā / na yujyate caramabhavikasya bodhisattvasya mithyādṛṣṭikule upapattum / tena sāpyapratirūpā //
body.translated_text: Others said: 'This city of <s>Mathurā</s> is prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. It is the royal capital of King <s>Subāhu</s> of the <s>Kaṃsa</s> family, lord of the <s>Śūrasenas</s>. It is suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' But others said: 'That too is not suitable. Why? Because that king is born in a lineage of wrong views, a king of bandits. It is not fitting for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence to be born in a family of wrong views. Therefore, that too is not suitable.' //

body.text: apare 'pyāhuḥ - ayaṃ hastināpure mahānagare rājā pāṇḍavakulavaṃśaprasūtaḥ śūro vīryavān varāṅgarūpasaṃpannaḥ parasainyapramardakānāṃ tatkulaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / apare 'pyāhuḥ - tadapyapratirūpam / kiṃ kāraṇam? tathā hi - pāṇḍavakulaprasūtaiḥ kulavaṃśo 'tivyākulīkṛto
body.translated_text: Yet others said: 'In the great city of <s>Hastināpura</s>, the king is born of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> lineage — heroic, valiant, endowed with beautiful form, a crusher of enemy armies. That family is suitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s womb-establishment.' Yet others said: 'That too is not suitable. Why? Because the family lineage has been greatly thrown into confusion by those born of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> family.

body.text: yudhiṣṭhiro dharmasya putra iti kathayati, bhīmaseno vāyoḥ, arjuna indrasya, nakulasahadevāvaśvinoriti / tena tadapi kulamapratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhasaṃsthānāyeti //
body.translated_text: <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> is said to be the son of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Bhīmasena</s> of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> of <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> of the <s>Aśvins</s>. Therefore, that family too is unsuitable for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conception in the womb. //

body.text: apara āhuḥ - iyaṃ mithilā nagarī atīva ramaṇīyā maithilasya rājñaḥ sumitrasya nivāsabhūmiḥ / sa rājā prabhūtahastyaśvarathapadātibalakāyasamanvitaḥ prabhūtahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavittopakaraṇaḥ sarvasāmantarājābhītabalaparākramo mitravān dharmavatsalaḥ / tatkulaṃ pratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti / anya ūcuḥ - tadapyapratirūpam / astyasau rājā sumitra evaṃguṇayuktaḥ, kiṃ tvativṛddho na samarthaḥ prajāmutpādayitumatibahuputraśca / tasmāttadapi kulamapratirūpamasya bodhisattvasya garbhapratisaṃsthānāyeti //
body.translated_text: Others said: 'This city of <s>Mithilā</s> is exceedingly delightful, the dwelling-place of King <s>Sumitra</s> of <s>Maithila</s>. That king is endowed with a great military force of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry; possessed of abundant gold, silver, gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch, crystal, coral, refined gold, and silver treasures and provisions; fearless in might and valor before all neighboring kings; having allies; devoted to <s>dharma</s>. That family is suitable for this <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conception in the womb.' Others said: 'That too is unsuitable. That King <s>Sumitra</s> is indeed endowed with such qualities, but he is too old and unable to beget offspring, and has too many sons already. Therefore, that family too is unsuitable for this <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conception in the womb.' //

body.text: evaṃ bhikṣavaste bodhisattvā devaputrāśca sarvasmin jambudvīpe ṣoḍaśajānapadeṣu yāni kāniciduccoccāni rājakulāni, tāni sarvāṇi vyavalokayantaḥ(tāni) sarvāṇi sadoṣāṇyadrākṣuḥ / teṣāṃ cintāmanaskāraprayuktānāṃ jñānaketudhvajo nāma devaputro 'vaivartiko bodhāya kṛtaniścayo 'sminmahāyāne / sa tāṃ mahatīṃ bodhisattvadevaparṣadametadavocat - etanmārṣā etameva bodhisattvamupasaṃkramya pariprakṣyāmaḥ - kīdṛgguṇasaṃpanne kule caramabhaviko bodhisattvaḥ pratyājāyata iti / sādhviti te sarve kṛtāñjalipuṭā bodhisattvamupasaṃkramya paryaprākṣuḥ - kīdṛgguṇasaṃpanne satpuruṣakularatne caramabhaviko bodhisattvaḥ pratyājāyata iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>devaputras</s>, surveying all the prominent royal families in the sixteen great regions of all <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, saw them all to be defective. While they were engaged in reflection and deliberation, a <s>devaputra</s> named <s>Jñānaketudhvaja</s> — irreversible in his resolve for awakening, firmly established in this <s>Mahāyāna</s> — addressed that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and gods: 'Venerable ones! Let us approach this very <s>Bodhisattva</s> and ask him: In a family endowed with what qualities is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence reborn?' 'Excellent!' they all said, and with palms joined they approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and asked: 'In a family jewel of noble persons endowed with what qualities is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence reborn?' //

body.text: tato bodhisattvastaṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ devagaṇaṃ ca vyavalokya etadavocat - catuṣṣaṣṭyākārairmārṣāḥ saṃpannakulaṃ bhavati yatra caramabhaviko bodhisattvaḥ pratyājāyate / katamaiścatuṣṣaṣṭyākāraiḥ? tadyathā / abhijñātaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / akṣudrānupaghāti ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / jātisaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / gotrasaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / pūrvapuruṣayugasaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / abhijātapuruṣayugasaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / abhilakṣitapuruṣayugasaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / maheśākhyapuruṣayugasaṃpannaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / bahustrīkaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / bahupuruṣaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / abhītaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / adīnālīnaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / alubdhaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / śīlavacca tatkulaṃ bhavati / prajñāvacca tatkulaṃ bhavati / amātyāvekṣitaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati bhogān paribhunakti / avandhyaśilpaniveśanaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati bhogān paribhunakti / dṛḍhamitraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / tiryagyonigataprāṇānuparodhakaraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / kṛtajñaṃ ca kṛtaveditaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / acchandagāminaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / adoṣagāminaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / amohagāminaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / abhayagāminaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / anavadyabhīru ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / amohavihāri ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / sthūlabhikṣaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / kriyādhimuktaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / tyāgādhimuktaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / dānādhimuktaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / paruṣakāramati ca tatkulaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surveying that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and gods, spoke thus: 'The family, venerable ones, is endowed with sixty-four characteristics, in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence is reborn. What are those sixty-four characteristics? Namely: that family is well-known; that family is neither mean nor harmful; that family is endowed with [noble] birth; that family is endowed with [good] lineage; that family is endowed with a succession of ancient forebears; that family is endowed with a succession of noble-born men; that family is endowed with a succession of distinguished men; that family is endowed with a succession of men of great renown; that family has many women; that family has many men; that family is fearless; that family is neither dejected nor dispirited; that family is not greedy; that family is virtuous; that family is wise; that family enjoys its wealth under the supervision of ministers; that family enjoys its wealth with arts and trades that are not unproductive; that family has firm friends; that family does not harm living beings born in the animal realm; that family is grateful and acknowledges kindness; that family does not act from desire; that family does not act from hatred; that family does not act from delusion; that family does not act from fear; that family fears what is blameworthy; that family dwells free from delusion; that family is abundant in provisions; that family is devoted to ritual action; that family is devoted to renunciation; that family is devoted to generosity; that family is resolute in

body.text: bhavati / dṛḍhavikramaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / balavikramaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / śreṣṭhavikramaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / ṛṣipūjakaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / devatāpūjakaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / caityapūjakaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / pūrvapretapūjakaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / apratibaddhavairaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / daśadigvighuṣṭaśabdaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / mahāparivāraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / abhedyaparivāraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / anuttaraparivāraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / kulajyeṣṭhaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / kulaśreṣṭhaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / kulavaśitāprāptaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / maheśākhyaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / mātṛjñaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / pitṛjñaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / śrāmaṇyaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / brāhmaṇyaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / prabhūtadhanadhānyakoṣakoṣṭhāgāraṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / prabhūtahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktājātarūparajatavittopakaraṇaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / prabhūtahastyaśvoṣṭragaveḍakaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / prabhūtadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / duṣpradharṣaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / sarvārthasiddhaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / cakravartikulaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / pūrvakuśalamūlasahāyopacitaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / bodhisattvakulakuloditaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati / anavadyaṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati sarvajātivādadoṣaiḥ sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyām / ebhirmārṣāścatuṣṣaṣṭyākāraiḥ samanvāgataṃ ca tatkulaṃ bhavati yasmiṃścaramaḥ bhaviko bodhisattva utpadyate //
body.translated_text: dealing with hardship; that family has firm valor; that family has powerful valor; that family has supreme valor; that family honors sages; that family honors deities; that family honors <s>caityas</s> (shrines); that family honors the departed ancestors; that family harbors no unbroken enmities; that family's fame resounds in the ten directions; that family has a great retinue; that family has an unbreakable retinue; that family has an unsurpassed retinue; that family is the eldest of families; that family is the foremost of families; that family has attained mastery over families; that family is of great renown; that family knows [how to honor] its mother; that family knows [how to honor] its father; that family upholds the ways of ascetics; that family upholds the ways of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; that family is rich in wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses; that family is rich in gold, silver, gems, pearls, refined gold, silver, treasures, and provisions; that family is rich in elephants, horses, camels, cows, and sheep; that family has abundant servants, male and female, laborers, and attendants; that family is hard to assail; that family has achieved all purposes; that family is a <s>Cakravartin</s>'s family; that family has accumulated former roots of merit as companions; that family has arisen in the lineage of <s>Bodhisattva</s> families; that family is blameless among all castes and classes in this world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the community of ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Venerable ones, the family endowed with these sixty-four characteristics is the one in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence is born. //

body.text: dvātriṃśatā mārṣā guṇākāraiḥ samanvāgatā sā strī bhavati yasyāḥ striyāścaramabhaviko bodhisattvaḥ kukṣāvavakrāmati / katamairdvātriṃśatā? yaduta abhijñātāyāṃ striyāṃ kukṣau caramabhaviko bodhisattvo 'vakrāmati / abhilakṣitāyā acchidropacārāyā jātisaṃpannāyāḥ kulasaṃpannāyā rūpasaṃpannāyā nāmasaṃpannāyā ārohapariṇāhasaṃpannāyā aprasūtāyāḥ śīlasaṃpannāyāḥ tyāgasaṃpannāyāḥ smitamukhāyāḥ pradakṣiṇagrāhiṇyā vyaktāyā vinītāyā viśāradāyā bahuśrutāyāḥ paṇḍitāyā aśaṭhāyā amāyāvinyā akrodhanāyā apagaterṣyāyā amatsarāyā acañcalāyā acapalāyā amukharāyāḥ kṣāntisaurabhyasaṃpannāyā hryapatrāpyasaṃpannāyā mandarāgadveṣamohāyā apagatamātṛgrāmadoṣāyāḥ pativratāyāḥ sarvākāraguṇasaṃpannāyāḥ striyāḥ kukṣau caramabhaviko bodhisattvo 'vakrāmati / ebhirmārṣā dvātriṃśatākāraiḥ samanvāgatā sā strī yasyāḥ striyāḥ kukṣau caramabhaviko bodhisattvo 'vakrāmati //
body.translated_text: The woman, venerable ones, in whose womb the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence descends is endowed with thirty-two qualities. Which thirty-two? Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence descends into the womb of a woman who is well-known; who is distinguished; whose conduct is without fault; who is endowed with [noble] birth; who is endowed with [good] family; who is endowed with beauty; who is endowed with [a good] name; who is endowed with proper stature and girth; who has not previously given birth; who is endowed with virtue; who is endowed with generosity; who is of smiling countenance; who turns to the right; who is articulate; who is well-trained; who is confident; who is learned; who is wise; who is not deceitful; who is not crafty; who is not prone to anger; who is free from jealousy; who is not envious; who is not fickle; who is not frivolous; who is not garrulous; who is endowed with the fragrance of patience; who is endowed with modesty and shame; who has mild passion, hatred, and delusion; who is free from the faults of womankind; who is devoted to her husband; who is endowed with all manner of virtues. In the womb of such a woman, endowed with these thirty-two qualities, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence descends. //

body.text: na khalu punarmārṣāḥ kṛṣṇapakṣe bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣāvavakrāmati, api tu śuklapakṣe / evaṃ pañcadaśyāṃ pūrṇāyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ puṣyanakṣatrayoge poṣadhaparigṛhītāyā mātuḥ kukṣau caramabhaviko bodhisattvo 'vakrāmati //
body.translated_text: Moreover, venerable ones, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not descend into his mother's womb during the dark fortnight, but only during the bright fortnight. Thus, on the fifteenth, the full-moon day, in conjunction with the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence descends into the womb of his mother who has observed the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day). //

body.text: atha khalu te bodhisattvāste ca devaputrā bodhisattvasyāntikādimāmevarūpāṃ kulapariśuddhiṃ mātṛpariśuddhiṃ ca śrutvā cintāmanaskārā abhūvan / katamaṃ kulaṃ evaṃguṇasamanvāgataṃ bhavedyāvadvidhamanena satpuruṣeṇa nirdiṣṭam? teṣāṃ cintāmanaskāraprayuktānāmetadabhūt - idaṃ khalvapi śākyakulaṃ ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca / rājā śuddhodano mātṛśuddhaḥ
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>devaputras</s>, having heard from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> this description of the purification of the family and of the mother, were engaged in reflection: 'Which family could be endowed with such qualities as described by this noble being?' While they were engaged in reflection, this occurred to them: 'Now, this <s>Śākya</s> clan is prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, and teeming with many people. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> is pure on his mother's side,

body.text: pitṛśuddhaḥ patnīśuddho 'parikṛṣṭasaṃpannāyāḥ svākārasuvijñāpakaḥ puṇyatejastejito mahāsaṃmatakule prasūtaścakravartivaṃśakulakulodito 'parimitadhananidhiratnasamanvāgataḥ karmadṛkca vigatapāpadṛṣṭikaśca / sarvaśākyaviṣaye caikarājā pūjito mānitaḥ śreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyapāriṣadyānāṃ prāsādiko darśanīyo nātivṛddho nātitaruṇo 'bhirūpaḥ sarvaguṇopetaḥ śilpajñaḥ kālajña ātmajño dharmajñastattvajño lokajño lakṣaṇajño dharmarājo dharmeṇānuśāstā avaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ kapilavastumahānilayaḥ / ye 'pi tatropapannāste 'pi tatsvabhāvā eva / rājñaśca śuddhodanasya māyā nāma devī suprabuddhasya śākyādhipaterduhitā navataruṇī rūpayauvanasaṃpannā aprasūtā apagataputraduhitṛkā surūpā salekhyavicitreva darśanīyā devakanyeva sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitā apagatamātṛgrāmadoṣā satyavādinyakarkaśā aparuṣā acapalānavadyā kokilasvarā apralāpinī madhurapriyavādinī vyapagatākhilakrodhamadamānadarpapratighā anīrṣukā kālavādinī tyāgasaṃpannā śīlavatī patisaṃtuṣṭā pativratā parapuruṣacintāmanaskārāpagatā samasaṃhataśiraḥkarṇanāsā bhramavarasadṛśakeśī sulalāṭī subhrūrvyapagatabhrukuṭikā smitamukhī pūrvābhilāpinī ślakṣṇamadhuravacanā pradakṣiṇagrāhiṇī ṛjvī akuṭilā aśaṭhā amāyāvinī hryapatrāpyasaṃpannā acapalā acañcalā amukharā avikīrṇavacanā mandarāgadveṣamohā kṣāntisaurabhyasaṃpannā karacaraṇanayanasvārakṣitabuddhiḥ mṛdutaruṇahastapādā kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśā navanalinendīvarapatrasuviśuddhanayanā raktatuṅganāsā supratiṣṭhitāṅgī sendrāyudhamiva yaṣṭiḥ suvinītā suvibhaktāṅgapratyaṅgā aninditāṅgī bimboṣṭhī cārudaśanā anupūrvagrīvā svalaṃkṛtā sumanā vārṣikī suviśuddhadarśanā suvinītāṃsā anupūrvasujātabāhuścāpodarī anupahatapārśvā gambhīranābhimaṇḍalā vṛttasuvistīrṇaślakṣṇakaṭhinakaṭirvajrasaṃhananakalpasadṛśamātrā gajabhujasamasamāhitasadṛśorū aiṇeyamṛgasadṛśajaṅghā lākṣārasasadṛśapāṇipādā jagati nayanābhiramyā apratihatacakṣurindriyā manāpapriyadarśanā strīratnarūpaprativiśiṣṭā māyānirmitamiva bimbaṃ māyānāmasaṃketā kalāvicakṣaṇā nandana ivāpsaraḥ - prakāśā śuddhodanasya mahārājasyāntaḥpuramadhyagatā / sā pratirūpā bodhisattvasya jananī / yā ceyaṃ kulapariśuddhirbodhisattvenodāhṛtā, sā śākyakula eva saṃdṛśyate //
body.translated_text: pure on his father's side, pure in his wife; endowed with an unblemished lineage; well-spoken in manner; radiant with the splendor of merit; born in the family of <s>Mahāsammata</s>; descended from the lineage of the <s>Cakravartin</s> dynasty; possessed of immeasurable wealth, stores, and jewels; one who sees <s>karma</s>; free from wrong views. In the entire <s>Śākya</s> domain he is the sole king, honored and respected. He is gracious to merchants, householders, ministers, and courtiers; handsome; neither too old nor too young; well-formed; endowed with all virtues; skilled in crafts; knowing the proper time; knowing himself; knowing <s>dharma</s>; knowing truth; knowing the world; knowing the marks [of character]; a righteous king who rules by <s>dharma</s>; and his city <s>Kapilavastu</s> is the great abode of beings whose roots of merit have been planted. Those born there are of that very nature. And King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s queen, named <s>Māyā</s>, is the daughter of <s>Suprabuddha</s>, chief of the <s>Śākyas</s> — young, endowed with beauty and youth, who has not previously given birth, without sons or daughters, of beautiful form, lovely to behold like a painted image, like a divine maiden adorned with all ornaments, free from the faults of womankind, speaking truth, not harsh, not rough, not frivolous, blameless, with a voice like a cuckoo, not given to idle talk, speaking sweetly and pleasantly, free from all anger, pride, conceit, arrogance, and resentment, not jealous, speaking at the proper time, endowed with generosity, virtuous, content with her husband, devoted to her husband, free from thoughts directed toward other men, with well-proportioned head, ears, and nose, with hair like the finest bees, with a beautiful forehead and brows, free from frowning, of smiling face, speaking first, of smooth and sweet speech, turning to the right, upright, not crooked, not deceitful, not crafty, endowed with modesty and shame, not frivolous, not fickle, not garrulous, not scattering her words, with mild passion, hatred, and delusion, endowed with the fragrance of patience, with well-guarded intellect in hands, feet, eyes, and speech, with soft and tender hands and feet, pleasant to touch like <s>kācilindika</s> [silk], with eyes as pure as the petals of a fresh blue lotus, with a red and prominent nose, with well-proportioned limbs, like a staff with a rainbow, well-trained, with well-shaped major and minor limbs, with unblemished body, with <s>bimba</s>-red lips, with beautiful teeth, with a graceful neck, well-adorned, of good disposition, like the <s>Vārṣikī</s> [jasmine], of pure appearance, with well-formed shoulders, with well-shaped and naturally lovely arms, with a slender waist, with uninjured sides, with a deep navel-circle, with round, broad, smooth, and firm hips, of a stature like unto an adamantine frame, with thighs like the well-composed trunk of an elephant, with calves like those of an <s>aiṇeya</s> deer, with hands and feet [red] like lac juice, a delight to the eyes of the world, with unobstructed sense of sight, of pleasing and beautiful appearance, surpassing the beauty of a woman-jewel, like an image fashioned by illusion, bearing the name <s>Māyā</s>, skilled in the arts, radiant like an <s>Apsaras</s> in [the garden of] <s>Nandana</s> — she dwells in the inner apartments of the great King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. She is a suitable mother for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And the purification of the family described by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is seen to exist in the <s>Śākya</s> clan alone.' //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: prāsādi dharmoccayi śuddhasattvaḥ sudharmasiṃhāsani saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Gracious, accumulating <s>dharma</s>, of pure being, seated on the excellent throne of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sabhāgadevaiḥ parivārito ṛṣiḥ saṃbodhisattvebhi mahāyaśobhiḥ // Lal_3.1 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by kindred gods and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great fame, the Sage [spoke]. // Lal_3.1 //

body.text: tatropaviṣṭāna abhūṣi cintā katamatkulaṃ śuddhasusaṃprajānam /
body.translated_text: While seated there, the thought arose: 'Which lineage is pure and of right understanding,

body.text: yadbodhisattve pratirūpajanme mātā pitā kutra ca śuddhabhāvāḥ // Lal_3.2 //
body.translated_text: befitting the birth of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>? And where are the mother and father of pure nature?' // Lal_3.2 //

children.text: vyavalokayantaḥ khalu jambusāhvayaṃ yaḥ kṣatriyo rājakulo mahātmā /
children.translated_text: Looking down upon the land called <s>Jambu</s> — which noble <s>Kṣatriya</s> royal family is of great soul?

children.text: sarvān sadoṣānanucintayantaḥ śākyaṃ kulaṃ cādṛśu vītadoṣam // Lal_3.3 //
children.translated_text: Reflecting that all [families] have faults, they saw the <s>Śākya</s> clan as free from fault. // Lal_3.3 //

children.text: śuddhodano rājakule kulīno narendravaṃśe suviśuddhagātraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddhodana</s>, of noble birth in the royal family, of thoroughly pure body in the line of kings,

children.text: ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca nirākulaṃ ca sagauravaṃ sajjanadhārmikaṃ ca // Lal_3.4 //
children.translated_text: prosperous, abundant, free from turmoil, respected, righteous, and devoted to good people. // Lal_3.4 //

children.text: anye 'pi sattvāḥ kapilāhvaye pure sarve suśuddhāśaya dharmayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the other beings in the city called <s>Kapila</s> are all of pure intentions and devoted to <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: udyānaārāmavihāramaṇḍitā kapilāhvaye śobhati janmabhūmiḥ // Lal_3.5 //
children.translated_text: adorned with gardens, parks, and monasteries, the birthplace shines in the city called <s>Kapila</s>. // Lal_3.5 //

children.text: sarve mahānagna balairupetā vistīrṇahastī navaratnavanti /
children.translated_text: All [the Śākyas] are great wrestlers endowed with strength, of broad chest, possessing the nine gems,

children.text: iṣvastraśikṣāsu ca pāramiṃ gatā na cāparaṃ hiṃsiṣu jīvitārtham // Lal_3.6 //
children.translated_text: having reached perfection in the training of bow and weapons, yet not harming others for the sake of livelihood. // Lal_3.6 //

children.text: śuddhodanasya pramadā pradhānā nārīsahasreṣu hi sāgraprāptā /
children.translated_text: The chief consort of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, foremost among thousands of women,

children.text: manoramā māyakṛteva bimbaṃ nāmena sā ucyati māyādevī // Lal_3.7 //
children.translated_text: beautiful, as if a form fashioned by <s>Māyā</s> — she is called by the name <s>Māyādevī</s>. // Lal_3.7 //

children.text: surūparūyā yatha devakanyā suvibhaktagātrā śubhanirmalāṅgī /
children.translated_text: Beautiful in form like a divine maiden, with well-proportioned limbs and auspicious, stainless body —

children.text: na so 'sti devo na ca mānuṣo vā yo māya dṛṣṭvātha labheta tṛptim // Lal_3.8 //
children.translated_text: there is no god nor human being who, having seen <s>Māyā</s>, could be satiated. // Lal_3.8 //

body.text: na rāgaraktā na ca doṣaduṣṭā ślakṣṇā mṛdū sā ṛjusnigdhavākyā /
body.translated_text: Not stained by passion, nor corrupted by fault; gentle, soft, of straight and affectionate speech;

body.text: akarkaśā cāparuṣā ca saumyā smitīmukhā sā bhrukuṭīprahīṇā // Lal_3.9 //
body.translated_text: neither harsh nor rough, but mild; smiling-faced, she has abandoned frowning. // Lal_3.9 //

children.text: hrīmā vyapatrāpiṇī dharmacāriṇī nirmāṇa astabdha acañcalā ca /
children.translated_text: Modest, conscientious, observing <s>Dharma</s>; without deceit, not proud, not restless;

children.text: anīrṣukā cāpyaśaṭhā amāyā tyāgānuraktā sahamaitracittā // Lal_3.10 //
children.translated_text: free from envy, without guile, without cunning; delighting in generosity, with a mind of friendliness and compassion. // Lal_3.10 //

children.text: karmekṣiṇī mithyaprayogahīnā satye sthitā kāyamanaḥsusaṃvṛtā /
children.translated_text: Watching over her actions, free from wrong conduct, established in truth, well-restrained in body and mind;

children.text: strīdoṣajālaṃ bhuvi yatprabhūtaṃ sarvaṃ tato 'syāḥ khalu naiva vidyate // Lal_3.11 //
children.translated_text: the whole net of womanly faults that abounds in the world — none of it is found in her. // Lal_3.11 //

children.text: na vidyate kanya manuṣyaloke gandharvaloke 'tha ca devaloke /
children.translated_text: There is no maiden in the human world, in the <s>Gandharva</s> world, or in the world of gods

children.text: māyāya devīya samā kuto 'ntarī pratirūpa sā vai jananī maharṣeḥ // Lal_3.12 //
children.translated_text: who is equal to <s>Māyādevī</s> — how much less a superior! She is the fitting mother of the Great Sage. // Lal_3.12 //

children.text: jātīśatāṃ pañcamanūnakāri sā bodhisattvasya babhūva mātā /
children.translated_text: For less than five hundred births, she has been the mother of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: pitā ca śuddhodanu tatra tatra pratirūpa tasmājjananī guṇānvitā // Lal_3.13 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Śuddhodana</s> has been [his] father there and there [in those lives] — therefore she is the fitting and virtuous mother. // Lal_3.13 //

children.text: vratastha sā tiṣṭhati tāpasīva vratānucārī sahadharmacāriṇī /
children.translated_text: She abides observing vows like an ascetic woman, following her vows, a companion in the <s>Dharma</s>-life.

children.text: rājñābhyanujñāta varapralabdhā dvātriṃśa māsāmava kāma sevahi // Lal_3.14 //
children.translated_text: Permitted by the king, having obtained the boon: 'For thirty-two months, enjoy sense-pleasures.' // Lal_3.14 //

children.text: yatra pradeśe sthihate niṣīdate śayyāgatā ca kramaṇaṃ ca tasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever place she stands in, sits in, lies in, or walks through —

children.text: obhāsito bhoti sadevabhāgo ābhāya tasyāḥ śubhakarmaniṣṭhayā // Lal_3.15 //
children.translated_text: the realm including the gods is illuminated by her radiance, through the fulfillment of her auspicious deeds. // Lal_3.15 //

body.text: na so 'sti devāsura mānuṣo vā yo rāgacittena samartha prekṣitum /
body.translated_text: There is no god, <s>Asura</s>, or human who is able to look upon her with a mind of passion;

body.text: paśyanti mātāṃ duhitāṃ ca sarve īryāpatheṣṭāryaguṇopapetā // Lal_3.16 //
body.translated_text: all see the mother [and the daughter] as endowed with noble qualities in all deportments. // Lal_3.16 //

children.text: māyāya devyāḥ śubhakarmahetunā vivardhate rājakulaṃ viśālam /
children.translated_text: Through the merit of <s>Māyādevī</s>'s auspicious deeds, the vast royal family prospers;

children.text: pradeśarājñāmapi cāpracāro vivardhate kīrti yaśaśca pārthive // Lal_3.17 //
children.translated_text: and even the territories of vassal kings flourish, and fame and glory increase for the monarch. // Lal_3.17 //

children.text: yathā ca māyā pratirūpabhājanaṃ yathāryasattvaḥ paramaṃ virājate /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Māyā</s> is a fitting vessel, just as the noble being shines supreme —

children.text: paśyeta evāvadhikaṃ guṇānvitā dayā sutā sā jananī ca māyā // Lal_3.18 //
children.translated_text: behold her, endowed with surpassing virtues, compassionate [toward her] children — that mother <s>Māyā</s>! // Lal_3.18 //

children.text: jambudhvaje 'nyā na hi sāsti nārī yasyā samarthā dharituṃ narottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, in the <s>Jambu</s> continent there is no other woman capable of bearing the Foremost of Men,

children.text: anyatra devyātiguṇānvitāyā daśanāgasāhasrabalaṃ hi yasyāḥ // Lal_3.19 //
children.translated_text: except the <s>Devī</s>, endowed with supreme virtues, who has the strength of ten thousand <s>Nāga</s> elephants. // Lal_3.19 //

children.text: evaṃ hi te devasutā mahātmā saṃbodhisattvāśca viśālaprajñā /
children.translated_text: Thus those great-souled <s>Devaputras</s> and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of vast wisdom

children.text: varṇanti māyāṃ jananīṃ guṇānvitāṃ pratirūpa sā śākyakulanandanasya // Lal_3.20 //
children.translated_text: praise <s>Māyā</s>, the virtuous mother, fitting for the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> family. // Lal_3.20 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare kulapariśuddhiparivarto nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Purification of the Lineage' (<s>Kulapariśuddhiparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 4
body.translated_text: START Chapter 4

body.text: dharmālokamukhaparivartaścaturthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmālokamukha</s> (Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>) chapter, the fourth.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo janmakulaṃ vyavalokya uccadhvajaṃ nāma tuṣitālaye mahāvimānaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiyojanānyāyāmavistāreṇa yasmin bodhisattvaḥ saṃniṣadya tuṣitebhyo devebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati sma, taṃ mahāvimānaṃ bodhisattvo 'bhirohati sma / abhiruhya ca sarvān tuṣitakāyikān devaputrānāmantrayate sma - saṃnipatantu bhavantaḥ cyutyākāraprayogaṃ nāma dharmānusmṛticaryānuśāsanīṃ paścimaṃ bodhisattvasyāntikāddharmaśravaṇaṃ śroṣyatheti / idaṃ khalvapi vacanaṃ śrutvā sarve tuṣitakāyikā devaputrāḥ sāpsarogaṇāstasmin vimāne saṃnipatanti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, having surveyed the birth-family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> ascended the great celestial palace named <s>Uccadhvaja</s> (Lofty Banner) in <s>Tuṣita</s>, sixty-four <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth, in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having sat down, used to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods. Having ascended that great palace, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> addressed all the <s>Tuṣita</s>-dwelling <s>Devaputras</s>: 'Assemble, good sirs! You shall hear the teaching called the <s>Cyutyākāraprayoga</s> (Practice of the Mode of Descent), a <s>Dharma</s>-recollection instruction — the last hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having heard this word, all the <s>Tuṣita</s>-dwelling <s>Devaputras</s>, together with their hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, assembled in that palace. //

body.text: tatra bodhisattvena caturmahādvīpake lokadhātuvistarapramāṇo maṇḍalamātrādhiṣṭhito 'bhūt, tāvaccitrastāvaddarśanīyastāvatsvalaṃkṛtastāvatsuruciro yāvatsarve kāmāvacarā devā rūpāvacarāśca devaputrāḥ sveṣu bhavanavyūheṣu śmaśānasaṃjñāmutpādayāmāsuḥ //
body.translated_text: There, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a <s>maṇḍala</s> of the extent of a world-system of four great continents was empowered — so colorful, so beautiful to behold, so well-adorned, so splendid that all the gods of the Desire Realm and the <s>Devaputras</s> of the Form Realm generated the perception of a charnel ground regarding their own celestial palace-arrays. //

body.text: tatra bodhisattvaḥ svapuṇyavipākaniṣyandaparimaṇḍite siṃhāsane niṣīdati sma anekamaṇiratnapādapratyupte anekapuṣpasaṃstarasaṃskṛte anekadivyagandhavāsopavāsite anekasāravaragandhanirdhūpite anekavarṇadivyapuṣpagandhasaṃstarasaṃskṛte anekamaṇiratnakṛtaśatasahasraprabhojjvālitatejasi anekamaṇiratnajālasaṃchanne anekakiṃkiṇījālasamīritābhinādite anekaratnaghaṇṭāśatasahasraraṇitanirghoṣe anekaratnajālaśatasahasraparisphuṭe anekaratnagaṇaśatasahasrasaṃchādite anekapaṭṭaśatasahasrābhipralambite anekapaṭṭadāmamālyaśatasahasrasamalaṃkṛte anekāpsaraḥśatasahasranṛtyagītavāditaparigīte anekaguṇaśatasahasravarṇite anekalokapālaśatasahasrānupālite anekaśakraśatasahasranamaskṛte anekabrahmaśatasahasrapraṇate anekabodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparigṛhīte daśadiganekabuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasamanvāhṛte aparimitakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrapāramitāsaṃbhārapuṇyavipākaniṣyandasamudgate / iti hi bhikṣava evaṃguṇasamanvāgate siṃhāsane niṣadya bodhisattvastāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadamāmantrayate sma - vyavalokayata mārṣā bodhisattvasya kāyaṃ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtam / vyavalokayata pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarāsvadha ūrdhvaṃ samantāddaśadikṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāgaṇanāsamatikrāntān bodhisattvān, ye tuṣitavarabhavanasthāḥ sarve caramabhavābhimukhā devagaṇaparivṛtāścyavanākāraṃ devatāsaṃharṣaṇaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ saṃprakāśayanti / adrākṣīt sā sarvā devaparṣad bodhisattvādhisthānena tān bodhisattvān / dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena bodhisattvastena sāñjaliṃ praṇamya pañcamaṇḍalairnamasyanti sma / evaṃ codānamudānayanti
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat upon a lion-throne, adorned by the fruition of his own merit — inlaid with many gem-jewel pedestals, prepared with many flower-spread coverings, perfumed with many divine fragrance-scents, fumigated with many excellent aromatic essences, adorned with multi-colored divine flower-fragrance-coverings, blazing with the splendor of hundreds of thousands of many gem-jewels, canopied by nets of many gem-jewels, resounding with the tinkling of many networks of bells, reverberating with the ringing of hundreds of thousands of many gem-bells, studded with hundreds of thousands of many jewel-nets, covered with hundreds of thousands of many jewel-clusters, hung with hundreds of thousands of many silk [banners], decorated with hundreds of thousands of many garlands of silk streamers, accompanied by the singing, dancing, and music of hundreds of thousands of many <s>Apsarases</s>, extolled by hundreds of thousands of many qualities, protected by hundreds of thousands of many world-guardians, saluted by hundreds of thousands of many <s>Śakras</s>, venerated by hundreds of thousands of many <s>Brahmās</s>, surrounded by <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, blessed by <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of many <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions, arisen from the fruition of the accumulation of merit from the perfections over limitless <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. Thus, O monks, seated upon a lion-throne endowed with such qualities, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> addressed that great divine assembly: 'Behold, good sirs, the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, adorned with the marks of a hundred merits! Behold in the east, south, west, north, below, above, and in all the ten directions the immeasurable, incalculable, innumerable, and surpassing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who, dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> mansions, all facing their final birth, surrounded by hosts of gods, proclaim the mode of descent, the rejoicing of the deities, and the Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>.' That entire divine assembly, by the empowerment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, beheld those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And having beheld them, they bowed with joined palms toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, prostrating with the five points of the body, and uttered this exclamation

body.text: sma - sādhu acintyamidaṃ bodhisattvādhisthānaṃ yatra hi nāma vayaṃ vyavalokitamātreṇeyanto bodhisattvān paśyāma iti //
body.translated_text: of wonder: 'Excellent! Inconceivable is this empowerment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whereby by merely looking we behold these many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ punarapi tāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadamāmantryaivamāha - tena hi mārṣāḥ śṛṇuta cyutyākāraṃ devatāsaṃharṣaṇaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ yadete bodhisattvā ebhyo devaputrebhyo bhāṣante / aṣṭottaramidaṃ mārṣā dharmālokamukhaṃ śataṃ yadavaśyaṃ bodhisattvena cyavanakālasamaye devaparṣadi saṃprakāśayitavyam / katamattadaṣṭottaraśatam? yaduta śraddhā mārṣā dharmālokamukhamabhedyāśayatāyai saṃvartate / prasādo dharmālokamukhamāvilacittaprasādanatāyai saṃvartate / prāmodyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ prasiddhyai saṃvartate / prīti dharmālokamukhaṃ cittaviśuddhyai saṃvartate / kāyasaṃvaro dharmālokamukhaṃ trikāyapariśuddhyai saṃvartate / vāksaṃvaro dharmālokamukhaṃ caturvāgdoṣaparivarjanatāyai saṃvartate / manaḥsaṃvaro dharmālokamukhamabhidhyāvyāpādamithyādṛṣṭiprahāṇāya saṃvartate / buddhānusmṛtidharmālokamukhaṃ buddhadarśanaviśuddhyai saṃvartate / dharmānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ dharmadeśanāviśuddhyai saṃvartate / saṃghānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ nyāyākramaṇatāyai saṃvartate / tyāgānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvopadhipratiniḥsargāyai saṃvartate / śīlānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ praṇidhānaparipūrtyai saṃvartate / devatānusmṛti dharmālokamukhamudāracittatāyai saṃvartate / maitrī dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvopadhikapuṇyakriyāvastvabhibhāvanatāyai saṃvartate / karuṇā dharmālokamukhavihiṃsāparamatāyai saṃvartate / muditā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvāratyapakarṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / upekṣā dharmālokamukhaṃ kāmajugupsanatāyai saṃvartate / anityapratyavekṣā dharmālokamukhaṃ kāmarūpyārūpyarāgasamatikramāya saṃvartate / duḥkhapratyavekṣā dharmālokamukhaṃ praṇidhānasamucchedāya saṃvartate / anātmapratyavekṣā dharmālokamukhamātmānabhiniveśanatāyai saṃvartate / śāntapratyavekṣā dharmālokamukhamanunayāsaṃghukṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / hrī dharmālokamukhamadhyātmopaśamāya saṃvartate / apatrāpyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ bahirdhāpraśamāya saṃvartate / satyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ devamanuṣyāvisaṃvādanatāyai saṃvartate / bhūtaṃ dharmālokamukhamātmāvisaṃvādanatāyai saṃvartate / dharmacaraṇaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ dharmapratiśaraṇatāyai saṃvartate / triśaraṇagamanaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ tryapāyasamatikramāya saṃvartate / kṛtajñatā dharmālokamukhaṃ kṛtakuśalamūlāvipraṇāśāya saṃvartate / kṛtaveditā dharmālokamukhaṃ parābhimanyatāyai saṃvartate / ātmajñatā dharmālokamukhamātmānutkarṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / sattvajñatā dharmālokamukhaṃ parāpatsamānatāyai saṃvartate / dharmajñatā dharmālokamukhaṃ dharmānudharmapratipattyai saṃvartate / kālajñatā dharmālokamukhamamoghadarśanatāyai saṃvartate / nihatamānatā dharmālokamukhaṃ jñānatāparipūrtyai saṃvartate / apratihatacittatā dharmālokamukhamātmaparānurakṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / anupanāho dharmālokamukhamakaukṛtyāya saṃvartate / adhimukti dharmālokamukhamavicikitsāparamatāyai saṃvartate / aśubhapratyavekṣā dharmālokamukhaṃ kāmavitarkaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / avyāpādo dharmālokamukhaṃ vyāpādavitarkaprahāṇāya saṃvartate /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> again addressed that great divine assembly thus: 'Then, good sirs, listen to the Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s> — the mode of descent, the rejoicing of the deities — which these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are proclaiming to these <s>Devaputras</s>. Good sirs, this is a hundred and eight Gateways of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must proclaim in the divine assembly at the time of descent. What are these hundred and eight? Namely: Faith is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to unbreakable resolve. Joy (<s>prasāda</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the clarification of a turbid mind. Delight (<s>prāmodya</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to success. Rapture (<s>prīti</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the purification of the mind. Bodily restraint is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the purification of the three bodies [of action]. Verbal restraint is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the avoidance of the four faults of speech. Mental restraint is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the abandoning of covetousness, malice, and wrong views. Recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the purification of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>. Recollection of the <s>Dharma</s> is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the purification of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Recollection of the <s>Saṅgha</s> is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to entering the right path. Recollection of renunciation is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the complete relinquishment of all attachments. Recollection of moral conduct is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the fulfillment of vows. Recollection of the deities is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to noble-mindedness. Loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to surpassing all meritorious actions connected with attachments. Compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to supreme non-harmfulness. Sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to removing all discontent. Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to revulsion toward desires. Contemplation of impermanence is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to transcending attachment to the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm. Contemplation of suffering is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the cutting off of [worldly] aspirations. Contemplation of non-self is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to non-clinging to a self. Contemplation of peace is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the non-igniting of longing. Modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to inner pacification. Conscientiousness (<s>apatrāpya</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to outer pacification. Truth (<s>satya</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to non-deception of gods and humans. Genuineness (<s>bhūta</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to non-deception of oneself. Practice of <s>Dharma</s> is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to taking <s>Dharma</s> as one's refuge. Going for refuge in the Three [Jewels] is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to transcending the three lower realms. Gratitude (<s>kṛtajñatā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the non-destruction of roots of merit that have been established. Appreciation (<s>kṛtaveditā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to valuing others. Self-knowledge (<s>ātmajñatā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to not exalting oneself. Knowledge of beings (<s>sattvajñatā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to not belittling others. Knowledge of <s>Dharma</s> is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to practicing <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Knowledge of the right time is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to unfailing discernment. Humility (<s>nihatamānatā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the fulfillment of knowledge. Indomitable mind (<s>apratihatacittatā</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the protection of oneself and others. Non-resentment is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to freedom from remorse. Confidence (<s>adhimukti</s>) is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to supreme freedom from doubt. Contemplation of the unattractive is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the abandoning of thoughts of desire. Non-ill-will is a Gateway of the Light of <s>Dharma</s>, conducive to the abandoning of thoughts of ill-will.

body.text: amoho dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvājñānavidhamanatāyai saṃvartate / dharmārthikatā dharmālokamukhamarthapratiśaraṇatāyai saṃvartate / dharmakāmatā dharmālokamukhaṃ lokapratilambhāya saṃvartate / śrutaparyeṣṭi dharmālokamukhaṃ yoniśodharmapratyavekṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / samyakprayogo dharmālokamukhaṃ samyakpratipattyai saṃvartate / nāmarūpaparijñā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvasaṅgasamatikramāya saṃvartate / hetudṛṣṭisamuddhāto dharmālokamukhaṃ vidyādhimuktipratilambhāya saṃvartate / anunayapratighaprahāṇaṃ dharmālokamukhamanunnāmāvanāmanatāyai saṃvartate / skandhakauśalyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ duḥkhaparijñānatāyai saṃvartate / dhātusamatā dharmālokamukhaṃ samudayaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / āyatanāpakarṣaṇaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ mārgabhāvanatāyai saṃvartate / anutpādakṣānti dharmālokamukhaṃ nirodhasākṣātkriyāyai saṃvartate / kāyagatānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ kāyavivekatāyai saṃvartate / vedanāgatānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvaveditapratipraśrabdhyai saṃvartate / cittagatānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ māyopamacittapratyavekṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / dharmagatānusmṛti dharmālokamukhaṃ vitimirajñānatāyai saṃvartate / catvāri samyakprahāṇāni dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇāya sarvakuśaladharmaparipūrtyai saṃvartate / catvāra ṛddhipādā dharmālokamukhaṃ kāyacittalaghutvāya saṃvartate / śraddhendriyaṃ dharmālokamukhamaparapraṇeyatāyai saṃvartate / vīryendriyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ suvicintitajñānatāyai saṃvartate / smṛtīndriyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ sukṛtakarmatāyai saṃvartate / samādhīndriyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ cittavimuktyai saṃvartate / prajñendriyaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ pratyavekṣaṇajñānatāyai saṃvartate / śraddhābalaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ mārabalasamatikramāya saṃvartate / vīryabalaṃ dharmālokamukhamavaivartikatāyai saṃvartate / smṛtibalaṃ dharmālokamukhamasaṃhāryatāyai saṃvartate / samādhibalaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvavitarkaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / prajñābalaṃ dharmālokamukhamanavamūḍhyatāyai saṃvartate / smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ yathāvaddharmaprajānatāyai saṃvartate / dharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvadharmaparipūrtyai saṃvartate / vīryasaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ suvicitrabuddhitāyai saṃvartate / prītisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ samādhyāyikatāyai saṃvartate / praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ kṛtakaraṇīyatāyai saṃvartate / samādhisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ samatānubodhāya saṃvartate / upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvopapattijugupsanatāyai saṃvartate / samyagdṛṣṭi dharmālokamukhaṃ nyāyākramaṇatāyai saṃvartate / samyaksaṃkalpo dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvakalpavikalpaparikalpaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / samyagvāg dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvākṣararutaghoṣavākyapathapratiśrutkāsamatānubodhanatāyai saṃvartate / samyakkarmānto dharmālokamukhamakarmāvipākatāyai saṃvartate / samyagājīvo dharmālokamukhaṃ sarveṣaṇapratipraśrabdhyai saṃvartate / samyagvyāyāmo dharmālokamukhaṃ paratīragamanāya saṃvartate / samyaksmṛti dharmālokamukhamasmṛtyamanasikāratāyai saṃvartate / samyaksamādhi dharmālokamukhamakopyacetaḥsamādhipratilambhāya saṃvartate / bodhicittaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ triratnavaṃśānupacchedāya saṃvartate / āśayo dharmālokamukhaṃ hīnayānāspṛhaṇatāyai saṃvartate / adhyāśayo dharmālokamukhamudārabuddhadharmādyālambanatāyai
body.translated_text: Non-delusion is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light (<s>dharmālokamukha</s>), conducive to the dispelling of all ignorance. Desire for <s>dharma</s> is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to taking meaning as one's refuge. Love of <s>dharma</s> is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of the [true nature of the] world. Seeking learning is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the thorough investigation of <s>dharma</s> by proper method. Right exertion is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to right practice. Full comprehension of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the transcending of all attachments. The eradication of the view of [independent] causation is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of conviction in [true] knowledge. The abandonment of attraction and aversion is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to neither elation nor depression. Skill in the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the full comprehension of suffering. Equality of the elements (<s>dhātu</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of the origin [of suffering]. The withdrawal from the sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the cultivation of the path. Patience toward non-arising (<s>anutpādakṣānti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the direct realization of cessation. Mindfulness directed to the body (<s>kāyagatānusmṛti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to bodily seclusion. Mindfulness directed to feelings (<s>vedanāgatānusmṛti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the complete tranquility of all that is felt. Mindfulness directed to the mind (<s>cittagatānusmṛti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the investigation of the mind as illusion-like. Mindfulness directed to <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmagatānusmṛti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to knowledge free from darkness. The four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) are a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and the fulfillment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) are a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to lightness of body and mind. The faculty of faith (<s>śraddhendriya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to not being led by others. The faculty of vigor (<s>vīryendriya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to well-considered knowledge. The faculty of mindfulness (<s>smṛtīndriya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to well-performed action. The faculty of concentration (<s>samādhīndriya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the liberation of the mind. The faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the knowledge of investigation. The power of faith (<s>śraddhābala</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the transcending of <s>Māra</s>'s power. The power of vigor (<s>vīryabala</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to irreversibility. The power of mindfulness (<s>smṛtibala</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to being unassailable. The power of concentration (<s>samādhibala</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of all discursive thought. The power of wisdom (<s>prajñābala</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to being free from bewilderment. The awakening-factor of mindfulness (<s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to knowing <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. The awakening-factor of investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the fulfillment of all <s>dharmas</s>. The awakening-factor of vigor (<s>vīryasaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to well-varied wisdom. The awakening-factor of joy (<s>prītisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the ongoing practice of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). The awakening-factor of tranquility (<s>praśrabdhisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to having accomplished what was to be done. The awakening-factor of concentration (<s>samādhisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the awakening to equality. The awakening-factor of equanimity (<s>upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to aversion toward all [forms of] rebirth. Right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to treading the right course. Right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of all conceptualization, discrimination, and mental fabrication. Right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the awakening to the equality of all syllables, sounds, voices, sentences, verbal paths, and echoes. Right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the non-ripening of [unwholesome] action. Right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the complete tranquility of all seeking. Right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to reaching the further shore. Right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the state of non-forgetfulness and mental engagement. Right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of the unshakable mental concentration. <s>Bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the Three Jewels. Intention (<s>āśaya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to having no desire for the lesser vehicle. Superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to taking the exalted <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> and other [qualities] as one's object

body.text: saṃvartate / prayogo dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvakuśaladharmaparipūrtyai saṃvartate / dānapāramitā dharmālokamukhaṃ lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣatrapariśuddhyai matsarisattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / śīlapāramitā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvākṣaṇāpāyasamatikramāya duḥśīlasattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / kṣāntipāramitā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvavyāpādakhiladoṣamānamadadarpaprahāṇāya vyāpannacittasattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / vīryapāramitā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvakuśalamūladharmāraṅgottāraṇāya kuśīdasattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / dhyānapāramitā dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvajñānābhijñotpādāya vikṣiptacittasattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / prajñāpāramitā dharmālokamukhamavidyāmohatamondhakāropalambhadṛṣṭiprahāṇāya duṣprajñasattvaparipācanatāyai saṃvartate / upāyakauśalaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ yathādhimuktasattveryāpathasaṃdarśanāya sarvabuddhadharmāvidhamanatāyai saṃvartate / catvāri saṃgrahavastūni dharmālokamukhaṃ sattvasaṃgrahāya saṃbodhiprāptasya ca dharmasaṃpratyavekṣaṇatāyai saṃvartate / sattvaparipāko dharmālokamukhamātmasukhānadhyavasānāyāparikhedatāyai saṃvartate / saddharmaparigraho dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvasattvasaṃkleśaprahāṇāya saṃvartate / puṇyasaṃbhāro dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvasattvopajīvyatāyai saṃvartate / jñānasaṃbhāro dharmālokamukhaṃ daśabalapratipūrtyai saṃvartate / śamathasaṃbhāro dharmālokamukhaṃ tathāgatasamādhipratilambhāya saṃvartate / vidarśanāsaṃbhāro dharmālokamukhaṃ prajñācakṣuḥpratilambhāya saṃvartate / pratisaṃvidavatāro dharmālokamukhaṃ dharmacakṣuḥpratilambhāya saṃvartate / pratiśaraṇāvatāro dharmālokamukhaṃ buddhacakṣuḥpariśuddhyai saṃvartate / dhāraṇīpratilambho dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvabuddhabhāṣitādhāraṇatāyai saṃvartate / pratibhānapratilambho dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvasattvasubhāṣitasaṃtoṣaṇāyai saṃvartate / ānulomikadharmakṣānti dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvabuddhadharmānulomanatāyai saṃvartate / anutpattikadharmakṣānti dharmālokamukhaṃ vyākaraṇapratilambhāya saṃvartate / avaivartikabhūmi dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvabuddhadharmapratipūrtyai saṃvartate / bhūmerbhūmisaṃkrāntijñānaṃ dharmālokamukhaṃ sarvajñajñānābhiṣekatāyai saṃvartate / abhiṣekabhūmi dharmālokamukhamavakramaṇajanmābhiniṣkramaṇaduṣkaracaryābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamāra - dhvaṃsanabodhivibodhanadharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanatāyai saṃvartate / idaṃ tanmārṣā aṣṭottaraṃ dharmālokamukhaśataṃ yadavaśyaṃ bodhisattvena cyavanakālasamaye devaparṣadi saṃprakāśayitavyam //
body.translated_text: conducive [to their attainment]. Exertion (<s>prayoga</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the fulfillment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the purification of the marks, minor characteristics, and <s>Buddha</s>-field, and to the maturation of miserly beings. The perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the transcending of all inopportune states and lower realms, and to the maturation of immoral beings. The perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of all ill-will, hostility, faultfinding, conceit, intoxication, and arrogance, and to the maturation of beings with malicious minds. The perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the undertaking and advancement of all wholesome root-<s>dharmas</s>, and to the maturation of indolent beings. The perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the generation of all knowledge, superknowledges, and higher knowledges, and to the maturation of beings with distracted minds. The perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of ignorance, delusion, the darkness of obscuration, and the view of apprehension, and to the maturation of beings of poor wisdom. Skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to showing modes of conduct according to the dispositions of beings, and to the non-destruction of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. The four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) are a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the gathering of beings and, upon the attainment of awakening, to the thorough investigation of <s>dharma</s>. The maturation of beings (<s>sattvaparipāka</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to not being attached to one's own happiness and to being unwearied. The embrace of the true <s>dharma</s> (<s>saddharmaparigraha</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the abandonment of the defilements of all beings. The accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyasaṃbhāra</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to becoming the support of all beings. The accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasaṃbhāra</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the fulfillment of the ten powers. The accumulation of calm (<s>śamathasaṃbhāra</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s concentration. The accumulation of insight (<s>vidarśanāsaṃbhāra</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of the eye of wisdom. The entry into analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of the eye of <s>dharma</s>. The entry into [taking] refuge (<s>pratiśaraṇa</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-eye. The attainment of retentive powers (<s>dhāraṇī</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the retention of all the speech of the <s>Buddhas</s>. The attainment of eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the satisfaction of all beings through well-spoken words. Conformity-patience toward <s>dharmas</s> (<s>ānulomikadharmakṣānti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to conforming with all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Patience toward the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the attainment of prediction [of Buddhahood]. The irreversible stage (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the fulfillment of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. The knowledge of transition from stage to stage (<s>bhūmisaṃkrāntijñāna</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the consecration into the knowledge of the omniscient. The consecration stage (<s>abhiṣekabhūmi</s>) is a gate of <s>dharma</s>-light, conducive to the display of descent, birth, renunciation, austere practice, approaching the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), the destruction of <s>Māra</s>, the awakening to <s>bodhi</s>, the turning of the <s>dharma</s>-wheel, and the great final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This, O noble ones, is the one-hundred-and-eight gates of <s>dharma</s>-light which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must proclaim to the assembly of gods at the time of his descent. //

body.text: asmin khalu punarbhikṣavo dharmālokamukhaparivarte bodhisattvena nirdiśyamāne tasyāṃ devaparṣadi caturaśīterdevaputrasahasrāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpadyante / dvātriṃśateśca devaputrasahasrāṇāṃ pūrvaparikarmakṛtānāmanutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt / ṣaṭtriṃśateśca devaputranayutānāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham / sarvāvacca tuṣitavarabhavanaṃ jānumātraṃ divyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃchāditamabhūt //
body.translated_text: And further, O monks, when this chapter on the gates of <s>dharma</s>-light was being taught by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, eighty-four thousand <s>Devaputras</s> in that divine assembly generated the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening. Thirty-two thousand <s>Devaputras</s>, who had previously cultivated the preparatory practices, obtained patience toward the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. And thirty-six tens of thousands of <s>Devaputras</s> [had] the stainless, spotless <s>dharma</s>-eye purified regarding <s>dharmas</s>. And the entire excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven was covered knee-deep with divine flowers. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastasyā devaparṣado bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃharṣaṇārthaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the further delight and exhortation of that divine assembly, spoke this verse on that occasion:

children.text: tuṣitavarabhavananilayādyadā cyavati nāyakaḥ puruṣasiṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the leader, the lion among men, descends from the abode of the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s>,

children.text: āmantrayate devān pramādamakhilaṃ visarjayata // Lal_4.1 //
children.translated_text: he addresses the gods: 'Cast off all heedlessness!' // Lal_4.1 //

children.text: yā kāci rativiyūhā divyā mahasā vicintitā śrīmān /
children.translated_text: Whatever divine displays of delight, O glorious one, have been devised through [one's own] greatness —

children.text: sarvaśubhakarmahetoḥ phalamidaṃ śṛṇurasya karmasya // Lal_4.2 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of all wholesome <s>karma</s>; hear about this <s>karma</s>! // Lal_4.2 //

children.text: tasmādbhavata kṛtajñā apūrvaśubhasaṃcayaṃ kṣapitveha /
children.translated_text: Therefore, be grateful, and having exhausted here the unprecedented accumulation of merit,

children.text: mā gacchata punarapāyānasādhvasukhavedanā yatra // Lal_4.3 //
children.translated_text: do not go again to the lower realms, where there are dreadful and painful sensations. // Lal_4.3 //

children.text: dharmaśca yaḥ śruto 'yaṃ mamāntike gauravamupajanitvā /
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>dharma</s> you have heard in my presence, having generated reverence,

children.text: tatra pratipadyathā prāpsyatha niyataṃ sukhamanantam // Lal_4.4 //
children.translated_text: practice it accordingly — you will surely attain infinite happiness. // Lal_4.4 //

children.text: sarvamanitya kāmā adhruvaṃ na ca śāśvatā api na kalpāḥ /
children.translated_text: All pleasures are impermanent, unstable, and not eternal — even the <s>kalpas</s> [are not];

children.text: māyāmarīcisadṛśā vidyutphenopamā capalāḥ // Lal_4.5 //
children.translated_text: like illusions and mirages, like lightning and foam, they are fleeting. // Lal_4.5 //

children.text: na ca kāmaguṇaratībhiḥ tṛptirlavaṇodakaṃ yathā pītvā /
children.translated_text: And there is no satisfaction through the delights of the strands of sensual pleasure, like drinking salt water;

children.text: te tṛpta yeṣa prajñā āryā lokottarā virajā // Lal_4.6 //
children.translated_text: they are satisfied who possess the noble, supramundane, stainless wisdom. // Lal_4.6 //

children.text: na taraṅgatulyakalpāḥ saṃgīti ca apsarobhi saṃvāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>kalpas</s> are not equal to waves; association and cohabitation with <s>Apsarases</s>

children.text: anyonyagamayuktā yathaiva sāmāyi kāmaṃ ca // Lal_4.7 //
children.translated_text: are joined by mutual coming and going, like a gathering, and [likewise] pleasures. // Lal_4.7 //

children.text: na ca saṃskṛte sahāyā na mitra jñātījano ca parivārāḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the conditioned [world] there are no [lasting] companions, no friends, no kinsmen or retinue;

children.text: anyatra karma sukṛtādanubandhati pṛṣṭhato yāti // Lal_4.8 //
children.translated_text: apart from well-done <s>karma</s>, [nothing] follows along and goes behind [one]. // Lal_4.8 //

children.text: tasmātsahitasamagrā anyonyaṃ maitracitta hitacittāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, united and harmonious, with minds of friendliness and benevolence toward one another,

children.text: dharmacaraṇaṃ carethāḥ sucaritacaraṇā na tapyante // Lal_4.9 //
children.translated_text: practice the conduct of <s>dharma</s>! Those of good conduct do not suffer. // Lal_4.9 //

children.text: buddhamanusmarethā dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ tathāpramādaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Remember the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and also heedfulness!

children.text: śrutaśīladānaniratā kṣāntyā saurabhyasaṃpannāḥ // Lal_4.10 //
children.translated_text: Devoted to learning, morality, and giving, endowed with the fragrance of patience! // Lal_4.10 //

children.text: duḥkhamanityamanātmā nirīkṣathā yoniśo imā dharmā /
children.translated_text: Suffering, impermanent, and without self — examine these <s>dharmas</s> thoroughly!

children.text: hetupratyayayuktā vartante 'svāmikā jaḍābuddhyā // Lal_4.11 //
children.translated_text: Conjoined with causes and conditions, they proceed without a master, foolishly [perceived]. // Lal_4.11 //

children.text: yā kāci ṛddhi mahyaṃ paśyata pratibhāṃ ca jñānaguṇatāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever supernatural power is mine, behold my eloquence and the quality of [my] knowledge!

children.text: sarvaśubhakarmahetoḥ śīlena śrutena cāpramādena // Lal_4.12 //
children.translated_text: [This is] the result of all wholesome <s>karma</s>, through morality, learning, and heedfulness. // Lal_4.12 //

children.text: anuśiṣyadhvaṃ mahyaṃ śīlena śrutena cāpramādena /
children.translated_text: Follow my instruction — through morality, learning, and heedfulness,

children.text: dānadamasaṃyamenā sattvārtha hitārtha mitrārthaḥ // Lal_4.13 //
children.translated_text: through giving, self-restraint, and discipline, for the benefit of beings, for their welfare, as a friend! // Lal_4.13 //

children.text: na ca vākyarutaraveṇā śakyāḥ saṃpādituṃ kuśaladharmān /
children.translated_text: One cannot bring about wholesome <s>dharmas</s> by mere words, sounds, and utterances;

children.text: pratipattimārabhethā yathā ca vadathā tatha karothā // Lal_4.14 //
children.translated_text: begin the practice! As you speak, so act! // Lal_4.14 //

children.text: mā khalu parāvakāśaṃ svayaṃ yatadhvaṃ sadā prayatnena /
children.translated_text: Do not give occasion to others; strive always by your own effort!

children.text: na ca kaści kṛtva dadate na cāpyakṛtvā bhavati siddhiḥ // Lal_4.15 //
children.translated_text: No one gives [the fruit] without having done [the work], nor does accomplishment come without effort. // Lal_4.15 //

children.text: samanusmarathā pūrve yadduḥkhaṃ saṃsāre ciramanubhūtam /
children.translated_text: Remember the suffering long experienced in <s>saṃsāra</s> in former times!

children.text: na ca nirvṛtī virāgo samanugato mithya niyataiva // Lal_4.16 //
children.translated_text: And without cessation and dispassion following along, [the cycle] is surely endless and in vain. // Lal_4.16 //

children.text: tasmātkṣaṇaṃ labhitvā mitraṃ pratirūpa deśavāsaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having obtained the [right] moment, a suitable friend, and a [proper] place to dwell,

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ ca dharmaśravaṇaṃ śametha rāgādikān kleśān // Lal_4.17 //
children.translated_text: and the best hearing of the <s>dharma</s>, pacify the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of passion and the like. // Lal_4.17 //

children.text: mānamadadarpavigatāḥ sadārjavāmandavāśca aśaṭhāśca /
children.translated_text: Free from pride, intoxication, and arrogance, upright, gentle, and not deceitful,

children.text: nirvāṇagatiparāyaṇa yujyata mārgābhisamayāya // Lal_4.18 //
children.translated_text: devoted to the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, strive for the realization of the path. // Lal_4.18 //

children.text: mohakaluṣāndhakāraṃ prajñāpradīpena vidhamathā sarvam /
children.translated_text: Dispelling completely the darkness of the defilement of delusion with the lamp of wisdom,

children.text: sānuśayadoṣajālaṃ vidārayata jñānavajreṇa // Lal_4.19 //
children.translated_text: rend asunder the web of faults with their latent tendencies by the vajra of knowledge. // Lal_4.19 //

children.text: kimapi subahu vadeyaṃ dharmaṃ yuṣmākamarthasaṃyuktam /
children.translated_text: I could speak exceedingly much <s>dharma</s> to you, connected with [your] welfare,

children.text: na ca tatravatiṣṭhethā na tatra dharmasya aparādhaḥ // Lal_4.20 //
children.translated_text: yet you would not abide in it — therein lies no fault of the <s>dharma</s>. // Lal_4.20 //

children.text: bodhiryathā mi prāptā (syād) dharmaṃ ca pravarṣayedamṛtagāmim /
children.translated_text: Just as my <s>bodhi</s> may be attained, and I may shower the <s>dharma</s> leading to the deathless,

children.text: punarapi viśuddhacittā upetha varadharmaśravaṇāya // Lal_4.21 //
children.translated_text: again, with purified minds, come for the hearing of the excellent <s>dharma</s>. // Lal_4.21 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare dharmālokamukhaparivarto nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'The Gateway to the Illumination of <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>Dharmālokamukhaparivarta</s>), in the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>. //

body.text: START Parivarta 5
body.translated_text: START Chapter 5

body.text: pracalaparivartaḥ pañcamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The fifth chapter: The Descent (<s>Pracalaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadamanayā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya kṣamāpayitvā maṅgalyāṃ devaparṣadamāmantrayate sma - gamiṣyāmyahaṃ mārṣā jambudvīpam / mayā pūrvabodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sattvāścaturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhirnimantritā dānena priyavadyenārthakriyayā samānārthatayā ca / tadayuktametanmārṣā mama bhavedakṛtajñatā ca, yadahamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau nābhisaṃbuddheyam //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted that great divine assembly with this discourse on <s>dharma</s>, and having sought their leave, addressed the auspicious divine assembly: 'I shall go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, venerable ones. While practicing the conduct of former <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, I have invited beings by means of the four bases of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) — generosity, kind speech, beneficial action, and sharing of purpose. It would be unfitting, venerable ones — it would be ingratitude on my part — if I were not to awaken to supreme, perfect enlightenment.' //

body.text: atha te tuṣitakāyikā devaputrā rudanto bodhisattvasya caraṇau parigṛhyaivamāhuḥ - idaṃ khalu satpuruṣa tuṣitabhavanaṃ tvayā vihīnaṃ na bhrājiṣyate / atha bodhisattvastāṃ mahatī devaparṣadamevamāha - ayaṃ maitreyo bodhisattvo yuṣmākaṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati / atha bodhisattvaḥ svakācchirasaḥ paṭṭamaulaṃ cāvatārya maitreyasya bodhisattvasya śirasi pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / evaṃ cāvocat - mamāntareṇa tvaṃ satpuruṣa anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyase //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Tuṣita</s>-dwelling <s>devaputras</s>, weeping and grasping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, said: 'Noble one! This <s>Tuṣita</s> dwelling, bereft of you, shall not shine.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> addressed that great divine assembly thus: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> will teach you the <s>dharma</s>.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> removed the silk crown from his own head and placed it on the head of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>. And he spoke thus: 'After me, noble one, you shall awaken to supreme, perfect enlightenment.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ tuṣitabhavane 'bhiniṣadya punarapi tāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadamāmantrayate sma - kīdṛśenāhaṃ mārṣā rūpeṇa mātuḥ kukṣāvavakrāmeyam? tatra kecidāhuḥ - mārṣā mānavakarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - śakrarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - brahmarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - mahārājikarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - vaiśravaṇarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - gandharvarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - kinnararūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - mahoragarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - maheśvararūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - candrarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - sūryarūpeṇa / kecidāhuḥ - garuḍarūpeṇa / tatrogratejo nāma brahmakāyiko devaputraḥ pūrvarṣijanmacyuto 'vaivartiko 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, sa evamāha - yathā brāhmaṇānāṃ mantravedaśāstrapāṭheṣvāgacchati, tādṛśenaiva rūpeṇa bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣāvavakrāmitavyaḥ / tatpunaḥ kīdṛśam? gajavaramahāpramāṇaḥ ṣaḍdanto hemajālasaṃkāśaḥ suruciraḥ suraktaśīrṣaḥ sphuṭitagalitarūpavān / etacchrutvā rūpaṃ brāhmaṇavedaśāstratattvajño vyākarṣitaśca / ito vai bhāvī dvātriṃśallakṣaṇopetaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having enthroned <s>Maitreya</s> in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, again addressed that great divine assembly: 'In what form, venerable ones, should I descend into my mother's womb?' Some said: 'In human form, venerable one.' Some said: 'In the form of <s>Śakra</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of <s>Brahmā</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of a great king.' Some said: 'In the form of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of a <s>Gandharva</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of a <s>Kinnara</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of a great serpent.' Some said: 'In the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>.' Some said: 'In the form of the moon.' Some said: 'In the form of the sun.' Some said: 'In the form of <s>Garuḍa</s>.' Then a <s>devaputra</s> of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> class named <s>Ugrateja</s>, fallen from a former sage's birth, irreversible from supreme enlightenment, spoke thus: 'As it appears in the mantra, Veda, and scripture recitations of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — in just such a form should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> descend into his mother's womb. And what is that form? Of the great size of a supreme elephant, six-tusked, resembling a net of gold, exceedingly beautiful, with a brilliant red head, of radiant form.' Having heard this form [described], it was confirmed by one who knew the truth of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> Vedic scriptures. 'From this indeed, the future one shall be endowed with the thirty-two marks.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo janmakālamavalokya tuṣitavarabhavanasthaḥ evaṃ rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavare aṣṭau pūrvanimittānyupadarśayati sma / katamānyaṣṭau? tadyathā - vyapagatatṛṇakhāṇukaṇṭakaśarkarakaḍhalyanirmalaṃ suṣiktaṃ suśodhitamanākulavātatamorajovigatadaṃśakamakṣikāpataṅgasarīsṛpāpagatamavakīrṇakusumaṃ samaṃ pāṇitalajātaṃ tadgṛhaṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / idaṃ prathamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, observing the time of birth, displayed eight portents in the excellent house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. What were those eight? Namely: that house became free from grass, stumps, thorns, gravel, and pebbles, pure, well-watered, well-cleaned, free from disturbing wind, darkness, and dust, rid of gnats, flies, moths, and creeping things, strewn with flowers, level, smooth as the palm of the hand. This was the first portent that appeared. //

body.text: ye ca himavatparvatarājanivāsinaḥ patraguptaśukasārikākokilahaṃsakroñcamayūracakravākakuṇālakalaviṅkajīvaṃjīvakādayo vicitrarucirapakṣā manojñapriyabhāṣiṇaḥ śakunigaṇāḥ, te āgatya rājñaḥ
body.translated_text: And those flocks of birds dwelling on the king of mountains <s>Himavat</s> — parrots, <s>śārikās</s>, cuckoos, swans, cranes, peacocks, <s>cakravākas</s>, <s>kuṇālas</s>, sparrows, <s>jīvaṃjīvakas</s>, and the like — of variegated and beautiful plumage, speaking delightfully and sweetly — they came and, standing upon the

body.text: śuddhodanasya gṛhavare vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādataleṣu sthitvā pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātāḥ svakasvakāni rutānyudāharanti sma / iti dvitīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: terraces, balconies, arched gateways, windows, mansions, and upper chambers of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s excellent house — joyful, filled with delight and happiness — uttered their respective cries. This was the second portent that appeared. //

body.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyārāmaramaṇīyeṣu vanaramaṇīyeṣu codyānaramaṇīyeṣu nānāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣānānartukārikāḥ, te sarve saṃpuṣpitāḥ saṃkusumitā abhūvan / idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: And all the various flowering and fruit-bearing trees in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s delightful gardens, groves, and parks, which were not of the [current] season, all blossomed and flowered. This was the third portent that appeared. //

body.text: yāśca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya puṣkariṇyo jalaparibhogyasthāḥ, tāḥ sarvāḥ śakaṭacakrapramāṇairanekakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrapatraiḥ padmaiḥ saṃchāditā abhūvan / idaṃ caturthaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: And all the pools and water-gardens of King <s>Śuddhodana</s> became covered with lotuses the size of cart-wheels, with many millions of hundreds of thousands of petals. This was the fourth portent that appeared. //

body.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavare bhājanaviṣaye sarpistailamadhuphāṇitaśarkarādyānāṃ te paribhujyamānāḥ kṣayaṃ na gacchanti sma / paripūrṇā eva saṃdṛśyante sma / idaṃ pañcamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādūrabhūt //
body.translated_text: And the vessels in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s excellent house, containing ghee, oil, honey, molasses, sugar, and the like — though being consumed — did not diminish. They were seen to remain full. This was the fifth portent that appeared. //

body.text: ye ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavarapradhāne mahatyantaḥpure bherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavatūṇavavīṇāveṇuvallakīsaṃpatāḍaprabhṛtayastūryabhāṇḍāḥ, te sarve svayamaghaṭṭitā eva manojñaśabdaṃ muñcanti sma / idaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
