body.translated_text: And all the musical instruments in the great inner chambers of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s excellent house — drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, flutes, <s>vīṇās</s>, bamboo flutes, <s>vallakīs</s>, cymbals, and the like — all produced delightful sounds of their own accord, without being struck. This was the sixth portent that appeared. //

body.text: yāni ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhavarapradhāne suvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālādīnāṃ ratnānāṃ bhājanāni, tāni sarvāṇi niravaśeṣaṃ vivṛtavimalaviśuddhaparipūrṇānyevaṃ virocante sma / idaṃ saptamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: And all the vessels of gold, silver, gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch, crystal, coral, and other jewels in the chief hall of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s excellent house — all of them without exception shone forth, open, pure, clear, and full. This was the seventh portent that appeared. //

body.text: vimalaviśuddhayā candrasūryajihmīkaraṇayā prabhayā kāyacittodbilyasaṃjananyā tadgṛhaṃ samantādavabhāsitamabhūt / idamaṣṭamaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: And that house was illuminated on all sides by a pure and clear radiance that put the moon and sun to shame, generating joy of body and mind. This was the eighth portent that appeared. //

body.text: māyā ca devī snātānuliptagātrā vividhābharaṇaviṣkambhitabhujā suślakṣṇasulīlavastravaradhāriṇī prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā sārdhaṃ daśabhiḥ strīsahasraiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya saṃgītiprāsāde sukhopaviṣṭasyāntikamupasaṃkramya dakṣiṇe pārśve ratnajālapratyupte bhadrāsane niṣadya smitamukhī vyapagatabhṛkuṭikā prahasitavadanā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamābhirgāthābhirabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: And Queen <s>Māyā</s>, her body bathed and anointed, her arms adorned with various ornaments, wearing exceedingly fine and graceful garments, having attained a state of joy, delight, and serenity, surrounded and attended by ten thousand women, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, who was seated comfortably in his music hall, and sitting on a jewel-covered throne at his right side, with smiling face, free from frowning, with a laughing countenance, addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> with these verses:

children.text: sādho śṛṇuṣva mama pārthiva bhūmipālā yācāmi te nṛpatiradya varaṃ prayaccha /
children.translated_text: 'Good one, listen to me, O king, O guardian of the earth! I beseech you — grant me a boon today, O sovereign.' |

children.text: abhiprāyu mahya yatha cittamanaḥpraharṣaṃ tanme śṛṇuṣva bhava prītamanā udagraḥ // Lal_5.1 //
children.translated_text: 'Fulfill my heart's desire and joy of mind; hear me and be glad-hearted and elated.' // Lal_5.1 //

children.text: gṛhṇāmi deva vrataśīlavaropavāsaṃ aṣṭāṅgapoṣadhamahaṃ jagi maitracittā /
children.translated_text: 'I take up, O lord, the excellent vow and observance of moral discipline and fasting — the eightfold <s>poṣadha</s>, with a mind of friendliness toward the world.' |

children.text: prāṇeṣu hiṃsaviratā sada śuddhabhāvā premaṃ yathātmani pareṣu tathā karomi // Lal_5.2 //
children.translated_text: 'Abstaining always from harming living beings, always of pure disposition, I extend to others the same love as to myself.' // Lal_5.2 //

children.text: stainyādvivarjitamanā madalobhahīnā kāmeṣu mithya nṛpate na samācariṣye /
children.translated_text: 'With a mind turned away from stealing, free from intoxication and greed — in sensual matters I shall not practice wrongly, O king.' |

children.text: satye sthitā apiśunā paruṣaprahīṇā saṃdhipralāpamaśubhaṃ na samācariṣye // Lal_5.3 //
children.translated_text: 'Established in truth, without slander, abandoning harsh speech — I shall not practice unwholesome idle talk.' // Lal_5.3 //

children.text: vyāpādadoṣakhilamohamadaprahīṇā sarvā abhidhya vigatā svadhanena tuṣṭā /
children.translated_text: 'Abandoning ill-will, fault, hardness, delusion, and pride — all covetousness gone, content with my own wealth,' |

children.text: samyakprayukta akuhānilayā anirṣyu karmā yathā daśa ime kuśalā cariṣye // Lal_5.4 //
children.translated_text: 'rightly engaged, without hypocrisy, free from jealousy — I shall practice these ten wholesome courses of action.' // Lal_5.4 //

children.text: mā tvaṃ narendra mayi kāmatṛṣāṃ kuruṣva śīlavrateṣvabhiratāya susaṃvṛtāya /
children.translated_text: 'Do not harbor lustful desire toward me, O lord of men, for one who delights in moral vows and is well-restrained.' |

children.text: mā te apuṇya nṛpate bhavi dīrgharātramanumodayā hi mama śīlavratopavāsam // Lal_5.5 //
children.translated_text: 'May demerit not befall you, O king, for a long time — rather, rejoice in my moral observance and fasting.' // Lal_5.5 //

children.text: chando mameṣa nṛpate praviśādya śīghraṃ prāsādaharmyaśikhare sthita dhārtarāṣṭre /
children.translated_text: 'This is my wish, O king: let me today quickly enter and dwell on the top of the finest mansion, in the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> [tower].' |

children.text: sakhibhiḥ sadā parivṛtā sukha modayeyaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇaśayane mṛduke sugandhe // Lal_5.6 //
children.translated_text: 'Always surrounded by companions, may I rejoice happily on a soft, fragrant couch strewn with flowers.' // Lal_5.6 //

children.text: na ca kāñcukīya puruṣā na pi dārakāśca na ca istri prākṛta mamā purataḥ sthiheyā /
children.translated_text: 'Let no male chamberlains, no boys, no common women stand before me.' |

children.text: no cāmanāpa mama rūpa na śabdagandhān nānyatra iṣṭamadhurā śṛṇuyā suśabdān // Lal_5.7 //
children.translated_text: 'Let no unpleasant forms, sounds, or smells reach me; let me hear only agreeable and sweet sounds.' // Lal_5.7 //

children.text: ye rodhabandhanagatāḥ parimuñca sarvān dravyāmbarāśca puruṣāndhaninaḥ kuruṣva /
children.translated_text: 'Release all those held in prison and bondage; give them goods and garments, and make the poor men wealthy.' |

children.text: vastrānnapāna rathayugya tathāśvayānaṃ dada saptarātrikamidaṃ jagataḥ sukhārtham // Lal_5.8 //
children.translated_text: 'Give clothing, food, drink, chariots, yoked animals, and horse-vehicles for seven nights, for the happiness of the world.' // Lal_5.8 //

children.text: no co vivādakalahā na ca roṣavākyā cānyonyamaitramanaso hitasaumyacittā /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be no disputes or quarrels, no angry words — let all be of mutually friendly minds and benevolent, gentle hearts.' |

children.text: asmin pure puruṣa iṣṭika dārakāśca devāśca nandanagatā sahitā ramantām // Lal_5.9 //
children.translated_text: 'In this city, let men, women, and children, and even gods as if in <s>Nandana</s> garden, rejoice together.' // Lal_5.9 //

children.text: na ca rājadaṇḍanabhaṭā na tathā kudaṇḍā notpīḍanā na pi ca tarjanatāḍanā vā /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be no royal punishers, no harsh police, no oppression, no threatening or striking.' |

children.text: sarvān prasannamanaso hitamaitracitta vīkṣasva deva janatāṃ yatha ekaputram // Lal_5.10 //
children.translated_text: 'With minds serene and friendly and benevolent, look upon all people, O lord, as upon an only son.' // Lal_5.10 //

children.text: śrutvaiva rāja vacanaṃ paramaṃ udagraṃ prāhāstu sarvamidameva yathā tavecchā /
children.translated_text: Having heard [her words], the king, supremely elated, said: 'Let all this be just as you wish.' |

children.text: abhiprāyu tubhya manasā svanucintitāni yadyācase tava varaṃ tadahaṃ dadāmi // Lal_5.11 //
children.translated_text: 'Whatever your heart has contemplated and desires — whatever boon you ask, that I grant you.' // Lal_5.11 //

children.text: ājñāpyaḥ pārthivavaraḥ svakapāriṣadyāṃ prāsādaśreṣṭhaśikhare prakarotha ṛddhim /
children.translated_text: The best of kings commanded his courtiers: 'Create splendor on the topmost pinnacle of the finest mansion —' |

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇaruciraṃ varadhūpagandhaṃ chatrāpatākasamalaṃkṛtatālapaṃktim // Lal_5.12 //
children.translated_text: 'beautiful with scattered flowers, with the finest incense fragrance, adorned with rows of parasols, banners, and palm-trees.' // Lal_5.12 //

children.text: viṃśatsahasra raṇaśoṇḍa vicitravarmāṃ nārācaśūlaśaraśaktigṛhītakhaṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Twenty thousand battle-fierce warriors in variegated armor, bearing iron arrows, lances, shafts, spears, and drawn swords,' |

children.text: parivārayātha dhṛtarājyamanojñaghoṣaṃ devyā 'bhayārtha karuṇāsthita rakṣamāṇā // Lal_5.13 //
children.translated_text: 'stand guard around the royal majesty with delightful music, stationed in compassion for the Queen's safety.' // Lal_5.13 //

children.text: strībhistu sā parivṛtā yatha devakanyā snātānuliptapravarāmbarabhūṣitāṅgī /
children.translated_text: And she, surrounded by women like a divine maiden, her body bathed, anointed, and adorned with the finest garments,

children.text: tūryaiḥ sahasramanugītamanojñaghoṣaiḥ āruhya devyupaviveśa marutsnuṣeva // Lal_5.14 //
children.translated_text: with a thousand [instruments of] music with delightful melodies accompanying her, ascended and entered [the tower] like a daughter-in-law of the wind-god. // Lal_5.14 //

children.text: divyairmahārthasuvicitrasuratnapādaiḥ svāstīrṇapuṣpavividhaiḥ śayane manojñe /
children.translated_text: On a delightful couch with divine, precious, exquisitely variegated gem-supports, well-spread with various flowers,

children.text: śayane sthitā vigalitā maṇiratnacūḍā yatha miśrakāvanagatā khalu devakanyā // Lal_5.15 //
children.translated_text: she lay down, her jeweled crest-ornament loosened, like a divine maiden who has entered the <s>Miśraka</s> garden. // Lal_5.15 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaścatvāro mahārājānaḥ śakraśca devānāmindraḥ suyāmaśca devaputraḥ saṃtuṣitaśca sunirmitaśca paranirmitavaśavartī ca sārthavāhaśca māraputrabrahmā ca sahāṃpatirbrahmottaraśca purohitaḥ subrahmā ca purohitaḥ prabhāvyūhābhāsvaraśca maheśvaraśca śuddhāvāsakāyikā niṣṭhāgataścākaniṣṭhaśca etāni cānyāni cānekāni devaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatya anyonyamevāhuḥ - ayuktametanmārṣā asmākaṃ syādakṛtajñatā ca, yadvayamekākinamadvitīyaṃ bodhisattvamutsṛjema / ko 'smākaṃ mārṣā utsahate
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the four Great Kings, <s>Śakra</s> the lord of the gods, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, the caravan-leader <s>Māra</s>'s son, <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, the chaplain <s>Brahmottara</s>, the chaplain <s>Subrahmā</s>, <s>Prabhāvyūhābhāsvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods, <s>Niṣṭhāgata</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, and many other hundreds of thousands of gods, having assembled together, said to one another: 'It would be unfitting, venerable ones — it would be ingratitude on our part — if we were to abandon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone and without a companion. Who among us, venerable ones, is willing

body.text: bodhisattvaṃ satatasamitamanubaddhumavakramaṇagarbhasthānajanmayauvanabhūmidārakakrīḍāntaḥpuranāṭakasaṃdarśanābhiniṣkramaṇaduṣkaracaryābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇamāradharṣaṇabodhyabhisaṃbodhanadharmacakrapravartanaṃ yāvanmahāparinirvāṇāddhitacittatayā snigdhacittatayā priyacittatayā maitracittatayā saumyacittatayā? tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: to constantly follow the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from his descent, womb-dwelling, birth, youthful stage, princely sports, witnessing the spectacles of the inner palace, great renunciation, difficult austerities, approaching the seat of awakening, defeating <s>Māra</s>, fully awakening to <s>Bodhi</s>, and turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, up to the great <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — with benevolent mind, affectionate mind, loving mind, friendly mind, and gentle mind? At that moment, he spoke this verse:

children.text: ko votsaheta vararūpadharam anubandhayituṃ satataṃ prītamanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Who would be able to constantly follow the bearer of supreme form, with a joyful mind? /

children.text: kaḥ puṇyateja yaśasā vacasā svayamātmanecchati vibaddhayitum // Lal_5.16 //
children.translated_text: Who, of his own accord, wishes to bind himself through merit, splendor, fame, and speech? // Lal_5.16 //

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ tridaśadevapure divyaiḥ sukhairhi ramituṃ satatam /
children.translated_text: He whose wish is to sport constantly in the abode of the thirty-three gods with divine pleasures, /

children.text: paramāpsarobhiriha kāmaguṇaiḥ anubaddhitāṃ vimalacandramukham // Lal_5.17 //
children.translated_text: with supreme <s>Apsarases</s> and sense-pleasures — let him follow the one of stainless moon-like face. // Lal_5.17 //

children.text: tatha miśrake vanavare rucire divyākare ramitu devapure /
children.translated_text: Likewise, [he who wishes] to sport in the beautiful <s>Miśraka</s> grove, with divine splendor, in the divine abode, /

children.text: puṣpotkare kanakacūrṇanime anubandhatāṃ vimalatejadharam // Lal_5.18 //
children.translated_text: amidst heaps of flowers and showers of gold-dust — let him follow the bearer of stainless radiance. // Lal_5.18 //

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ ramituḥ citrarathe tatha nandane suravadhūsahitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose wish is to sport in <s>Citraratha</s> and <s>Nandana</s>, accompanied by divine maidens, /

children.text: māndāravaiḥ kusumapatracite anubandhatāmimu mahāpuruṣam // Lal_5.19 //
children.translated_text: adorned with <s>Māndārava</s> flowers and petals — let him follow this Great Being. // Lal_5.19 //

children.text: yāmādhipatyamatha vā tuṣitairatha vāpi prārthayati ceśvaratām /
children.translated_text: He who aspires to lordship over the <s>Yāma</s> [heaven], or with the <s>Tuṣita</s> [gods], or seeks sovereignty, /

children.text: pūjāraho bhavitu sarvajage anubandhatāmimu anantayaśam // Lal_5.20 //
children.translated_text: let him become worthy of worship in the entire world — let him follow this one of infinite fame. // Lal_5.20 //

children.text: yo icchati nirmitapure rucire vaśavartidevabhavane ramitum /
children.translated_text: He who wishes to sport in the beautiful <s>Nirmita</s> city, in the abode of the <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods, /

children.text: manasaiva sarvamanubhoktikriyā anubandhatāmimu guṇāgradharam // Lal_5.21 //
children.translated_text: where all enjoyment is accomplished by mere thought — let him follow this foremost bearer of virtues. // Lal_5.21 //

children.text: māreśvaro na ca praduṣṭamanā sarvavidhaiśvaryapāragataḥ /
children.translated_text: Let even the lord of <s>Māra</s>, without a corrupted mind, who has reached the shore of all forms of sovereignty, /

children.text: kāmeśvaro vaśitapāragato gacchatvasau hitakareṇa saha // Lal_5.22 //
children.translated_text: the lord of desires, who has reached the shore of mastery — let him go with this benefactor. // Lal_5.22 //

children.text: tatha kāmadhātu samatikramituṃ mati yasya brahmapuramāvasitum /
children.translated_text: Likewise, he whose mind is to transcend the desire-realm and dwell in the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, /

children.text: caturapramāṇaprabhatejadharaḥ so 'dyānubaddhatu mahāpuruṣam // Lal_5.23 //
children.translated_text: bearing the radiance and splendor of the four immeasurables — let him today follow the Great Being. // Lal_5.23 //

children.text: atha vāpi yasya manujeṣu mati varacakravartiviṣaye vipule /
children.translated_text: Or he whose mind is [set] among humans, in the vast domain of the supreme <s>Cakravartin</s>, /

children.text: ratnākaramabhayasaukhyadadam anubandhatāṃ vipulapuṇyadharam // Lal_5.24 //
children.translated_text: a mine of jewels, bestowing fearlessness and happiness — let him follow the bearer of vast merit. // Lal_5.24 //

children.text: pṛthivīśvarastatha pi śreṣṭhisuto āḍhyo mahādhanu mahānicayaḥ /
children.translated_text: A lord of the earth, or a son of the foremost merchant, wealthy, of great riches and great accumulations, /

children.text: parivāravānnihataśatrugaṇo gacchatvasau hitakareṇa saha // Lal_5.25 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by retinue, with enemies slain — let him go with this benefactor. // Lal_5.25 //

children.text: rūpaṃ ca bhogamapi ceśvaratā kīrtiryaśaśca balatā guṇavatī /
children.translated_text: Form, enjoyment, sovereignty, fame, renown, strength, and virtue, /

children.text: ādeyavākya bhavi grāhyaruto brahmeśvaraṃ samupayātu vidum // Lal_5.26 //
children.translated_text: persuasive speech and compelling voice — let the wise one approach this lord of <s>Brahmā</s>. // Lal_5.26 //

children.text: ye divya kāma tatha mānuṣakāṃ yo icchatī tribhavi sarvasukham /
children.translated_text: He who desires divine pleasures, and human pleasures, and all happiness in the three realms, /

children.text: dhyāne sukhaṃ ca pravivekasukhaṃ dharmeśvaraṃ samanubandhayatām // Lal_5.27 //
children.translated_text: and the happiness of meditation, and the happiness of solitude — let him follow this lord of <s>Dharma</s>. // Lal_5.27 //

children.text: rāgaprahāṇu tatha doṣamapī yo icchate tatha kileśajaham /
children.translated_text: He who desires the abandonment of passion, and of hatred, and the destruction of afflictions, /

children.text: śānta praśānta upaśāntamanā so dāntacittamanuyātu laghum // Lal_5.28 //
children.translated_text: peaceful, supremely peaceful, with pacified mind — let the one of subdued mind follow him quickly. // Lal_5.28 //

body.text: śaikṣā aśaikṣa tatha pratyekajinā sarvajñajñānamanuprāpuritum /
body.translated_text: Learners, non-learners, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — to attain omniscient knowledge, /

body.text: daśabhirbalairnaditu siṃha iva guṇasāgaraṃ samanuyātu vidum // Lal_5.29 //
body.translated_text: to roar with the ten powers like a lion — let the wise one follow this ocean of virtues. // Lal_5.29 //

children.text: pithituṃ apāyapatha yeṣa matir vivṛtuṃ ca ṣaṅgatipathaṃ hyamṛtam /
children.translated_text: He whose mind is to close the paths of the lower realms and open the six [good] destinies, the immortal path, /

children.text: aṣṭāṅgamārgagamanena gatim anubandhatāṃ gatipathāntakaram // Lal_5.30 //
children.translated_text: through progress on the eightfold noble path — let him follow the one who ends the paths [of rebirth]. // Lal_5.30 //

children.text: yo icchate sugata pūjayituṃ dharmaṃ ca teṣu śrutikāruṇike /
children.translated_text: He who wishes to worship the <s>Sugata</s> and the <s>Dharma</s> in those [teachings] of compassionate learning, /

children.text: prāpto guṇānapi ca saṃghagatān guṇasāgaraṃ samanuyātu imam // Lal_5.31 //
children.translated_text: and the virtues attained in the <s>Saṅgha</s> — let this wise one follow this ocean of virtues. // Lal_5.31 //

children.text: jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhakṣaye saṃsārabandhana vimokṣayitum /
children.translated_text: For the destruction of the suffering of birth, old age, and death, to liberate from the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, /

children.text: carituṃ viśuddhagamanāntasamaṃ so śuddhasattvamanubandhayatām // Lal_5.32 //
children.translated_text: to walk the pure path that ends [in liberation] — let him follow this supremely pure being. // Lal_5.32 //

children.text: iṣṭo manāpa priyu sarvajage varalakṣaṇo varaguṇopacitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beloved, delightful, dear to the entire world, endowed with supreme marks and supreme virtues, /

children.text: ātmā paraṃ ca tatha mocayituṃ priyadarśanaṃ samupayātu vidum // Lal_5.33 //
children.translated_text: to liberate both himself and others — let the wise one approach this pleasing-to-behold [being]. // Lal_5.33 //

children.text: śīlaṃ samādhi tatha prajñamayī gambhīradurdaśaduropagamam /
children.translated_text: Morality, concentration, and wisdom — profound, hard to see, and difficult to approach; /

children.text: yo icchate vidu vimukti labhe so vaidyarājamanuyātu laghum // Lal_5.34 //
children.translated_text: he who wishes, O wise one, to obtain liberation — let him quickly follow this king of physicians. // Lal_5.34 //

children.text: ete ca anya guṇa naikavidhā upapatti saukhya tatha nirvṛtiye /
children.translated_text: These and other virtues of many kinds, for the happiness of [good] rebirth and for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, /

children.text: sarvairguṇebhi pratipūrṇa siddhaye siddhavrataṃ samanuyātu vidum // Lal_5.35 //
children.translated_text: for the complete perfection filled with all virtues — let the wise one follow [this one] of fulfilled vows. // Lal_5.35 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: idaṃ khalu vacanaṃ śrutvā caturaśītisahasrāṇi cāturmahārājikānāṃ devānāṃ śatasahasraṃ trayatriṃśānāṃ śatasahasraṃ yāmānāṃ śatasahasraṃ tuṣitānāṃ śatasahasraṃ nirmāṇaratīnāṃ śatasahasraṃ paranirmitavaśavartīnāṃ devānāṃ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi mārakāyikānāṃ pūrvaśubhakarmaniryātānāṃ aṣṭaṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi brahmakāyikānāṃ bahūni śatasahasrāṇi yāvadakaniṣṭhānāṃ devānāṃ saṃnipatitānyabhūvan / anye ca
body.translated_text: Having heard these words, eighty-four thousand [gods] of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> [heaven], a hundred thousand of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods], a hundred thousand of the <s>Yāma</s> [gods], a hundred thousand of the <s>Tuṣita</s> [gods], a hundred thousand of the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> [gods], a hundred thousand of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, sixty thousand of the <s>Mārakāyika</s> [gods] — those whose previous wholesome <s>karma</s> had matured — sixty-eight thousand of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [gods], and many hundreds of thousands of gods up to those of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> [heaven] — all assembled. And other

body.text: bhūyaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarebhyo digbhyo bahūni devaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitānyabhūvan / tebhyo ye udāratamā devaputrāste tāṃ mahatīṃ devaparṣadaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣantaḥ -
body.translated_text: — still more hundreds of thousands of gods assembled from the eastern, southern, western, and northern directions. Among them, those <s>devaputras</s> who were the most exalted addressed that great assembly of gods in verses:

children.text: hanta śṛṇotha vacanaṃ amareśvarāho asmin vidhānamati yādṛśatatvabhūtā /
children.translated_text: Come, hear the words, O lords of the immortals! In this matter, such is the true arrangement: /

children.text: tyaktārthikāmarati dhyānasukhaṃ praṇītam anubandhayāma imamuttamaśuddhasattvam // Lal_5.36 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the pleasure of wealth and desire, [embracing] the exquisite happiness of meditation — let us follow this supremely pure being. // Lal_5.36 //

children.text: okrāntapāda tatha garbhasthitaṃ mahātmaṃ pūjārahaṃ atiśayamabhipūjayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Great Being who has descended and dwells in the womb, worthy of worship — let us worship him with surpassing honor; /

children.text: puṇyaiḥ surakṣitamṛṣiṃ parirakṣisanto yasyāvatāra labhate na manaḥ praduṣṭam // Lal_5.37 //
children.translated_text: guarding the sage who is protected by merit, at whose descent no mind becomes corrupted. // Lal_5.37 //

children.text: saṃgītitūryaracitaiśca suvādyakaiśca varṇāguṇāṃ kathayato guṇasāgarasya /
children.translated_text: With music, songs, and well-crafted instruments, /

children.text: kurvāma devamanujāna praharṣaṇīyaṃ yaṃ śrutva bodhivaracitta jane janeryā // Lal_5.38 //
children.translated_text: proclaiming the virtues of this ocean of qualities, let us create joy for gods and humans — hearing which, the supreme mind of awakening may arise in beings. // Lal_5.38 //

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇa nṛpateśca karoma gehaṃ kālāgurūttamasudhūpitasaumyagandham /
children.translated_text: Let us make the king's dwelling strewn with flowers, /

children.text: yaṃ ghrātva devamanujāśca bhavantyudagrā vigatajvarāśca sukhinaśca bhavantyarogāḥ // Lal_5.39 //
children.translated_text: fragrant with the finest aloe and incense of pleasant scent — smelling which, gods and humans become elated, free from fever, happy, and healthy. // Lal_5.39 //

children.text: māndāravaiśca kusumaistatha pārijātaiścandraiḥ sucandra tatha sthālavirocamānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With <s>Māndārava</s> flowers and <s>Pārijāta</s> blossoms, /

children.text: puṣpābhikīrṇa kapilāhvaya taṃ karoma pūjārtha pūrvaśubhakarmasamudgatasya // Lal_5.40 //
children.translated_text: with <s>Candra</s>, <s>Sucandra</s>, and brilliant <s>Sthāla</s> [flowers] — let us make that [city] called <s>Kapilā</s> strewn with flowers, for the worship of one arisen from prior wholesome <s>karma</s>. // Lal_5.40 //

children.text: yāvacca garbhi vasate trimalairalipto yāvajjarāmaraṇa cāntakaraḥ prasūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: As long as he dwells in the womb, unstained by the three defilements, /

children.text: tāvatprasannamanaso anubandhayāma eṣā matirmatidharasya karoma pūjām // Lal_5.41 //
children.translated_text: and as long as, being born, he makes an end of old age, death, and destruction — so long, with joyful minds, let us follow him; this is our intention — let us honor the bearer of wisdom. // Lal_5.41 //

children.text: lābhā sulabdha vipulāḥ suramānuṣāṇāṃ drakṣyanti jānu imu saptapadāṃ kramantam /
children.translated_text: Well-gained indeed are the abundant gains of gods and humans — they shall see him striding seven steps, /

children.text: śakraiśca brahmaṇakaraiḥ parigṛhyamānaṃ gandhodakaiḥ snapiyamāni suśuddhasattvam // Lal_5.42
children.translated_text: received by the hands of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, bathed with scented water — this supremely pure being. // Lal_5.42

children.text: yāvacca loki anuvartanatāṃ karoti antaḥpure vasati kāmakileśaghātī /
children.translated_text: As long as he acts in conformity with the world, dwelling in the inner palace, the slayer of desire and afflictions, /

children.text: yāvacca niṣkramati rājyamapāsya sarvaṃ tāvatprasannamanaso anubandhayāmaḥ // Lal_5.43 //
children.translated_text: and as long as he goes forth, renouncing all sovereignty — so long, with joyful minds, let us follow him. // Lal_5.43 //

children.text: yāvadupaiti mahimaṇḍi tṛṇāṃ gṛhītvā yāvacca bodhi spṛśate vinihatya māram /
children.translated_text: Until he approaches the great <s>maṇḍala</s> [of awakening], having taken [a seat of] grass, until he touches awakening, having vanquished <s>Māra</s>, /

children.text: adhyeṣṭu brāhmaṇayutebhi pravarti cakraṃ tāvatkaroma vipulāṃ sugatasya pūjām // Lal_5.44 //
children.translated_text: until entreated by multitudes of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> he turns the wheel [of <s>Dharma</s>] — so long let us make vast worship of the <s>Sugata</s>. // Lal_5.44 //

children.text: yada buddhakāryu kṛtu bheṣyati trisahasre sattvāna koṭinayutā amṛte vinītā /
children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s>'s task shall have been accomplished in the three-thousand [world-system], when millions of ten millions of beings have been trained in the immortal [<s>Dharma</s>], /

children.text: nirvāṇamārgamupayāsyati śītibhāvaṃ tāvanmahāśayamṛṣiṃ na jahāma sarve // Lal_5.45 //
children.translated_text: when he shall approach the path of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the state of coolness — until then, let none of us abandon this great-souled sage. // Lal_5.45 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ kāmadhātvīśvarāṇāṃ devakanyānāṃ bodhisattvasya rūpakāyapariniṣpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā etadabhavat - kīdṛśī tvasau kanyā bhaviṣyati yā imaṃ varapravaraśuddhasattvaṃ dhārayiṣyati / tāḥ kautūhalajātā varapravarapuṣpadhūpadīpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaraparigṛhītā divyamanomayātmabhāvapratilabdhāḥ puṇyavipākādhisthānādhisthitāḥ tasmin kṣaṇe 'marapurabhavanādantarhitāḥ kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare udyānaśatasahasraparimaṇḍite rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe dhṛtarāṣṭre mahāprāsāde amarabhavanaprakāśe vigalitāmbaradhāriṇyaḥ śubhavimalatejapratimaṇḍitā divyābharaṇastambhitabhujāḥ śayanavaragatāṃ māyādevīmekāṅgulikayopadarśayantyo gaganatalagatāḥ parasparaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the divine maidens of the lords of the desire-realm, having seen the perfection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s physical form, thought: 'What kind of woman will she be who shall bear this supremely noble pure being?' They, with curiosity aroused, bearing supremely excellent flowers, incense, lamps, perfume, garlands, ointments, powders, and robes, having obtained divine mind-made forms through the power of their meritorious <s>karma</s>, at that moment vanished from the abode of the immortal city. In the supreme great city called <s>Kapilā</s>, encompassed by a hundred thousand pleasure-groves, in the palace of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, in the great mansion called <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, resplendent like the abode of the immortals, with garments flowing, adorned with auspicious pure radiance, with arms adorned with divine ornaments, pointing with one finger at <s>Māyādevī</s> who was reclining on her excellent couch, hovering in the sky, they addressed each other in verses:

children.text: amarapuragatāna apsarāṇāṃ rūpa manorama dṛṣṭva bodhisattve /
children.translated_text: Having seen the beautiful, delightful form of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> among the <s>Apsarases</s> of the immortal city, /

children.text: matiriyamabhavattadā hi tāsāṃ pramada nu kīdṛśa bodhisattvamātā // Lal_5.46 //
children.translated_text: this thought arose in them then: 'What kind of woman will be the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother?' // Lal_5.46 //

children.text: tāśca sahitapuṣpamālyahastā upagami veśma nṛpasya jātakāṅkṣā /
children.translated_text: They, with flowers and garlands in hand, approached the king's palace, filled with curiosity; /

children.text: puṣpa tatha vilepanāṃ gṛhītvā daśanakhaañjalibhirnamasyamānāḥ // Lal_5.47 //
children.translated_text: having taken flowers and ointments, bowing with palms joined at [their] fingertips. // Lal_5.47 //

children.text: vigalitavasanāḥ salīlarūpāḥ karatala dakṣiṇi aṅgulīṃ praṇamya /
children.translated_text: With garments flowing, of graceful form, bending the forefinger of the right hand, /

children.text: śayanagata vidarśi māyadevīṃ sādhu nirīkṣatha rūpa mānuṣīṇām // Lal_5.48 //
children.translated_text: they showed <s>Māyādevī</s> reclining on her couch: 'Look well at the beauty of human women!' // Lal_5.48 //

children.text: vayamiha abhimanyayāma anye paramamanorama surūpa apsarāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'We here consider others to have the supremely delightful, beautiful form of <s>Apsarases</s>; /

children.text: ima nṛpativadhūṃ nirīkṣamāṇā jihma vipaśyatha divya ātmabhāvām // Lal_5.49 //
children.translated_text: but beholding this wife of the king — look! your own divine forms appear inferior!' // Lal_5.49 //

children.text: ratiriva sadṛśī guṇānvitā ca jananiriyaṃ pravarāgrapudgalasya /
children.translated_text: 'Like <s>Rati</s> herself, endowed with virtues — this mother of the supreme foremost being; /

children.text: maṇiratana yathā subhājanastha tatha iva bhājana devi devadeve // Lal_5.50 //
children.translated_text: like a jewel-gem in a fine vessel — so is this goddess a vessel for the God of gods.' // Lal_5.50 //

children.text: karacaraṇatalebhi yāvadūrdhvaṃ aṅga mahorama divya ātirekāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From the soles of her feet and hands upward, her limbs are supremely delightful, divine, surpassing; /

children.text: prekṣatu nayanānna cāsti tṛptiṃ bhūya praharṣati citta mānasaṃ ca // Lal_5.51 //
children.translated_text: though looking, the eyes find no satiation — the mind and heart rejoice yet more.' // Lal_5.51 //

children.text: śaśiriva gagane virājate 'syā vadanu varaṃ ca virāja gātrabhāsā /
children.translated_text: 'Her face shines like the moon in the sky, and her limbs radiate splendor; /

children.text: raviriva vimalā śaśīva dīptā tatha prabha niścarate 'sya ātmabhāvāt // Lal_5.52 //
children.translated_text: stainless like the sun, radiant like the moon — thus does brilliance issue forth from her person.' // Lal_5.52 //

children.text: kanakamiva sujātajātarūpā varṇa virocati deviye tathaiva /
children.translated_text: 'Like well-born refined gold is the complexion of the goddess, just so; /

children.text: bhramaravaranikāśa kuntalānī mṛdukasugandhaśravāsya mūrdhajāni // Lal_5.53 //
children.translated_text: her curls like the finest bees, her hair soft, fragrant, and flowing.' // Lal_5.53 //

children.text: kamaladalanibhe tathāsya netre daśanaviśuddha nabheva jyotiṣāṇi /
children.translated_text: 'Her eyes are like lotus petals; her teeth pure, like stars in the sky; /

children.text: cāpa iva tanūdarī viśālā pārśva samudgata māṃsi nāsti saṃdhiḥ // Lal_5.54 //
children.translated_text: slender-waisted, arched like a bow, with full sides, flesh rising — no [visible] joints.' // Lal_5.54 //

children.text: gajabhujasadṛśe 'sya ūrujaṅghe jānu sujātvanupūrvamudgatāsya /
children.translated_text: 'Her thighs and calves are like the arms of an elephant, well-formed, gradually tapering; /

children.text: karatalacaraṇā samā suraktā vyaktamiyaṃ khalu devakanya nānyā // Lal_5.55 //
children.translated_text: her palms and soles are even, beautifully red — truly this is a divine maiden, not another.' // Lal_5.55 //

body.text: eva bahuvidhaṃ nirīkṣya devīṃ kusuma kṣipitva pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kṛtvā /
body.translated_text: Thus having examined the queen in many ways, scattering flowers and making circumambulation, /

body.text: supiya yaśavatī jinasya mātā punarapi devapuraṃ gatā kṣaṇena // Lal_5.56 //
body.translated_text: 'Beloved and glorious is the mother of the <s>Jina</s>!' — and in a moment they returned to the divine city. // Lal_5.56 //

children.text: atha caturi caturdiśāsu pālāḥ śakra suyāma tathaiva nirmitāśca /
children.translated_text: Then the four guardians of the four directions, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, and likewise the <s>Nirmita</s> [gods], /

children.text: devagaṇa kumbhāṇḍa rākṣasāśca asura mahoraga kinnarāśca vocan // Lal_5.57 //
children.translated_text: hosts of gods, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s> spoke: // Lal_5.57 //

children.text: gacchata purato narottamasya puruṣavarasya karotha rakṣaguptim /
children.translated_text: 'Go before the foremost of men, the best of beings — provide guard and protection; /

children.text: mā kuruta jage manaḥpradoṣaṃ mā ca karota viheṭha mānuṣāṇām // Lal_5.58 //
children.translated_text: do not create corruption of mind in the world, nor cause harm to humans.' // Lal_5.58 //

children.text: yatra gṛhavarasmi māyadevī tatra samagra sapāriṣadya sarve /
children.translated_text: 'Where <s>Māyādevī</s> is in the excellent dwelling, there [go] all together with your retinues; /

children.text: asidhanuśaraśaktikhaṅgahastā gaganatalasmi sthitā nirīkṣayātha // Lal_5.59 //
children.translated_text: with swords, bows, arrows, spears, and swords in hand, stationed in the sky, keep watch.' // Lal_5.59 //

children.text: jñātva cyavanakāla devaputrā upagami māyasakāśa hṛṣṭacittā /
children.translated_text: Having known the time of descent, the <s>devaputras</s>, with joyful hearts, approached <s>Māyā</s>. /

children.text: puṣpa tatha vilepanāṃ gṛhītvā daśanakhaañjalibhirnamasyamānāḥ // Lal_5.60 //
children.translated_text: taking flowers and ointments, bowing with palms joined at the ten fingernails. // Lal_5.60 //

children.text: cyava cyava hi narendra śuddhasattvā ayu samayo bhavato 'dya vādisiṃha /
children.translated_text: Descend, descend, O lord of men, O pure-natured one! The time of your lifespan [here] has come today, O lion of speakers!

children.text: kṛpakaruṇa janitva sarvaloke asmi adhyeṣama dharmadānahetoḥ // Lal_5.61 //
children.translated_text: Having generated compassion and kindness toward the entire world, we beseech you for the sake of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_5.61 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya cyavanakālasamaye pūrvasyā diśo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi sarva ekajātipratibaddhāstuṣitavarabhavanavāsino yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe / evaṃ daśabhyo digbhyo ekaikasyā diśo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi sarva ekajātipratibaddhāstuṣitavarabhavanavāsino yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe / cāturmahārājakāyikebhyo devebhyaścaturaśītyapsaraḥśatasahasrāṇyevaṃ trayatriṃśato yāmebhyastuṣitebhyo nirmāṇaratibhyaḥ paranirmitavaśavartibhyo devebhyaścaturaśītyapsaraḥ - śatasahasrāṇi nānātūryasaṃgītivāditena yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at the time of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s descent, from the eastern direction many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — all facing their final birth and dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven — approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for the purpose of worshipping him. Likewise, from each of the ten directions, many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — all facing their final birth and dwelling in the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven — approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for the purpose of worshipping him. From the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, eighty-four hundred thousand <s>Apsarases</s> [came]; likewise from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, eighty-four hundred thousand <s>Apsarases</s> approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for the purpose of worshipping him, with the sound of various musical instruments and songs. //

body.text: atha khalu bodhisattvaḥ śrīgarbhasiṃhāsane sarvapuṇyasamudgate sarvadevanāgasaṃdarśane mahākūṭāgāre niṣadya sārdhaṃ bodhisattvairdevanāgayakṣakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtastuṣitavarabhavanāt
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seated upon the lion-throne called <s>Śrīgarbha</s> — arisen from the accumulation of all merit, visible to all gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and [beings] — in the great palace, together with the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and surrounded and attended by <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>, set forth from the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven

body.text: pracalati sma / pracalatā ca bhikṣavo bodhisattvena tathārūpā kāyāt prabhā muktābhūd yayā prabhayā ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturevaṃ vipulavistīrṇo mahatodāreṇa supracalitapūrveṇa divyaprabhāsamatikrāntenāvabhāsena parisphuṭo 'bhūt / yā api tā lokāntarikā aghā aghasphuṭā andhakārāstamisrā yatremau candrasūryāvevaṃ maharddhikāvevaṃ mahānubhāvāvevaṃ maheśākhyau ābhayā ābhāṃ varṇena varṇaṃ tejasā tejo nābhitapato nābhivirocataḥ, tatra ye sattvā upapannāste svakānapi bāhuprasāritānna paśyanti / tathāpi tasmin samaye mahata udārasyāvabhāsasya prādurbhāvo 'bhūt / ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāste tenaivāvabhāsena sphuṭāḥ samānā anyonyaṃ samyak paśyanti sma / anyonyaṃ saṃjānante sma / evaṃ cāhuḥ - anye 'pi kila bhoḥ sattvā ihopapannāḥ kila bho iti //
body.translated_text: And as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> set forth, O monks, such a radiance was emitted from his body that by that radiance this great trichiliocosm — so vast and extensive — was pervaded by a great, exalted, unprecedented, surpassingly divine splendor. Even those inter-cosmic voids — dark, pitch-dark, blind with darkness — where these sun and moon, possessing such great supernatural power, such great majesty, and such great sovereignty, do not illumine with their light, do not color with their color, do not heat with their heat — there, the beings who have been reborn cannot see even their own outstretched arms. Yet at that time, a great and exalted radiance appeared. And the beings reborn there, pervaded by that very radiance, saw one another clearly and recognized one another, saying: 'Ah, so other beings too have been reborn here!' //

body.text: ayaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāramaṣṭādaśamahānimittamabhūt / akampat prākampat saṃprākampat / avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat / acalat prācalat saṃprācalat / akṣubhyat prākṣubhyat saṃprākṣubhyat / araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat / agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat / ante 'vanamati sma, madhye unnamati sma / madhye 'vanamati sma, ante unnamati sma / pūrvasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, paścimāyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / paścimāyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, pūrvasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, uttarasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / uttarasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / tasmin samaye harṣaṇīyāstoṣaṇīyāḥ premaṇīyāḥ prasādanīyā avalokanīyāḥ prahlādanīyā nirvarṇanīyā asecanīyā apratikūlā anuttrāsakarāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante sma / na ca kasyacit sattvasya tasmin kṣaṇe viheṭhā vā trāso vā bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vābhūt / na ca bhūyaḥ sūryācandramasorna brahmaśakralokapālānāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe prabhā prajñāyate sma / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokopapannāśca sattvāstasmin kṣaṇe vigataduḥkhā abhūvan sarvasukhasamarpitāḥ / na ca kasyacit sattvasya rāgo bādhate sma, dveṣo vā moho vā, īrṣyā vā mātsaryaṃ vā, māno vā mrakṣo vā, mado vā krodho vā, vyāpādo vā paridāho vā / sarvasattvāstasmin kṣaṇe maitracittā hitacittāḥ parasparaṃ mātāpitṛsaṅgino 'bhūvan / aghaṭṭitāni ca divyamānuṣyakāṇi tūryakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi manojñaghoṣamutsṛjanti sma / devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi pāṇibhiraṃsaiḥ śirobhistaṃ mahāvimānaṃ vahanti sma / tāni cāpsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi svāṃ svāṃ saṃgītiṃ saṃprayujya purataḥ pṛṣṭhato vāmadakṣiṇena ca sthitvā bodhisattvaṃ saṃgītirutasvareṇābhistuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: And this great trichiliocosm was shaken with six kinds of trembling and eighteen great portents: it trembled, trembled greatly, trembled exceedingly; it shook, shook greatly, shook exceedingly; it quaked, quaked greatly, quaked exceedingly; it thundered, thundered greatly, thundered exceedingly; it rumbled, rumbled greatly, rumbled exceedingly; it roared, roared greatly, roared exceedingly. The edges sank down and the middle rose up; the middle sank down and the edges rose up. The eastern quarter sank down and the western quarter rose up; the western quarter sank down and the eastern quarter rose up. The southern quarter sank down and the northern quarter rose up; the northern quarter sank down and the southern quarter rose up. At that time, sounds were heard that were delightful, pleasing, charming, inspiring, beautiful, refreshing, worthy of contemplation, satisfying, agreeable, and non-terrifying. And for no being at that moment was there any harm, terror, fear, or paralysis. Moreover, at that moment, neither the light of sun and moon, nor of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and the world-guardians was perceived. And all beings reborn in the hells, animal realm, and world of <s>Yama</s> were at that moment freed from suffering and established in complete happiness. For no being did passion afflict, nor hatred, nor delusion, nor envy, nor jealousy, nor pride, nor deceit, nor intoxication, nor anger, nor ill-will, nor torment. All beings at that moment had minds of loving-kindness, benevolent minds; they regarded one another as mother and father. Untouched, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s> divine and human musical instruments produced melodious sounds. <s>Koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of gods bore that great celestial palace with their hands, shoulders, and heads. And those hundreds of thousands of <s>Apsarases</s>, each performing their own music, standing in front, behind, and to the left and right, praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with the sounds of their songs —

children.text: pūrvakarmaśubhasaṃcitasya te dīrgharātrakuśaloditasya te /
children.translated_text: For you whose merit has been well accumulated through former deeds, for you whose virtue has arisen over the long night [of <s>saṃsāra</s>],

children.text: satyadharmanayaśodhitasya te pūja adya vipulā pravartate // Lal_5.62 //
children.translated_text: for you whose truth and the way of <s>Dharma</s> have been purified — today vast worship proceeds! // Lal_5.62 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo dānu dattu priyaputradhītarā /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you gave in charity your beloved sons and daughters;

children.text: tasya dānacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena divya kusumāḥ pravarṣitāḥ // Lal_5.63 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of generosity, by which divine flowers are rained down! // Lal_5.63 //

children.text: ātmamāṃsa tulayitva te vibho so 'bhidattu priyapakṣikāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: O all-pervading one, you weighed your own flesh on the scales and gave it for the sake of a beloved bird;

children.text: tasya dānacaritasya tatphalaṃ pretaloki labhi pānabhojanam // Lal_5.64 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of generosity, by which beings in the realm of the hungry ghosts obtain food and drink! // Lal_5.64 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo śīla rakṣitamakhaṇḍanavratam /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you guarded moral conduct, [your] vow unbroken;

children.text: tasya śīlacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena akṣaṇa apāya śodhitāḥ // Lal_5.65 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of moral conduct, by which the unfavorable destinies and lower realms have been purified! // Lal_5.65 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo kṣānti bhāvita nidānabodhaye /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you cultivated patience for the sake of awakening;

children.text: tasya kṣānticaritasya tatphalaṃ maitracitta bhuta devamānuṣāḥ // Lal_5.66 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of patience, by which beings, gods, and humans have minds of loving-kindness! // Lal_5.66 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo vīryu bhāvitamalīnamuttamam /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you cultivated supreme, untainted vigor;

children.text: tasya vīryacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena kāyu yatha meru śobhate // Lal_5.67 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of vigor, by which [your] body shines like <s>Meru</s>! // Lal_5.67 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo dhyāna dhyāyita kileśadhyeṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you practiced meditation, seeking the destruction of the afflictions;

children.text: tasya dhyānacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena kleśa jagato na bādhate // Lal_5.68 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of meditation, by which the afflictions do not harm the world! // Lal_5.68 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhya bahukalpakoṭiyo prajña bhāvita kileśachedanī /
children.translated_text: In former times, for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, you cultivated wisdom, the cutter of afflictions;

children.text: tasya prajñacaritasya tatphalaṃ yena ābha paramā virocate // Lal_5.69 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of that practice of wisdom, by which the supreme radiance shines forth! // Lal_5.69 //

children.text: maitravarmita kileśasūdanā sarvasattvakaruṇāya udgatā /
children.translated_text: Armored in loving-kindness, destroyer of afflictions, arisen in compassion for all beings,

children.text: modiprāpta paramā upekṣakā brahmabhūta sugatā namo 'stu te // Lal_5.70 //
children.translated_text: having attained supreme joy [and] equanimity — homage to you who have become <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>Sugata</s>! // Lal_5.70 //

children.text: prajña ulkaprabha tejasodgatā sarvadoṣatamamohaśodhakā /
children.translated_text: Your wisdom blazes like a torch, arisen in splendor, purifying the darkness of all faults and delusion;

children.text: cakṣubhūta trisahasrināyakā mārgadeśika mune namo 'stu te // Lal_5.71 //
children.translated_text: you who are the eye [of the world], leader of the trichiliocosm, guide of the path — homage to you, O Sage! // Lal_5.71 //

children.text: ṛddhipādavarabhijñakovidā satyadarśi paramārthi śikṣitā /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the bases of supernatural power and the supreme higher knowledges, seer of truth, trained in the ultimate meaning,

children.text: tīrṇa tārayasi anyaprāṇino dāśabhūta sugatā namo 'stu te // Lal_5.72 //
children.translated_text: having crossed over, you ferry other beings across — homage to you who have become a ferryman, O <s>Sugata</s>! // Lal_5.72 //

children.text: sarvopāyavarabhijñakovidā darśayasi cyutimacyuticyutim /
children.translated_text: Skilled in all means and supreme higher knowledges, you display the appearance of descent though [you are] undeceased,

children.text: lokadharmabhavanābhivartase no ca loki kvaci opalipyase // Lal_5.73 //
children.translated_text: you engage in the world and worldly conduct, yet you are nowhere stained by the world. // Lal_5.73 //

children.text: lābha teṣa paramā acintiyā yeṣu darśana śravaṃ ca eṣyase /
children.translated_text: Supreme and inconceivable is the gain of those to whom you will come to be seen and heard;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ śṛṇuya yo tidharmatāṃ śraddha prīti vipulā janeṣyase // Lal_5.74 //
children.translated_text: how much more for one who will hear the <s>Dharma</s> — you will generate vast faith and joy in people! // Lal_5.74 //

children.text: jihma sarva tuṣitālayo bhuto jambudvīpi puri yo udāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Crooked is all the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode now that the one who arose in the city of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> [has departed];

children.text: prāṇikoṭinayutā acintiyāṃ bodhayiṣyasi prasupta kleśato // Lal_5.75 //
children.translated_text: you will awaken inconceivable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of beings who are asleep due to afflictions! // Lal_5.75 //

children.text: ṛddha sphīta puramadya bheṣyatī devakoṭinayutaiḥ samākulam /
children.translated_text: The prosperous, thriving city will now become filled with <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of gods,

children.text: apsarobhi turiyairnināditaṃ rājagehi madhuraṃ śruṇiṣyati // Lal_5.76 //
children.translated_text: resounding with <s>Apsarases</s> and instruments — the royal palace will hear sweet [sounds]. // Lal_5.76 //

children.text: puṇyatejabharitā śubhakarmaṇā nāri sā paramarūpaupetā /
children.translated_text: Filled with the glory of merit and good deeds, that woman endowed with supreme beauty,

children.text: yasya putra ayameva samṛddhaḥ tisraloki abhibhāti śīriye // Lal_5.77 //
children.translated_text: whose son is this very accomplished one — [she] outshines the triple world in glory! // Lal_5.77 //

children.text: no bhuyo puravarasmi dehināṃ lobhadoṣakalahā vivādakā /
children.translated_text: No more in the best of cities will there be greed, fault, quarrel, or dispute among beings;

children.text: sarva maitramanasaḥ sagauravā bhāvino naravarasya tejasā // Lal_5.78 //
children.translated_text: all will be friendly-minded and respectful, [transformed] by the splendor of the best of men. // Lal_5.78 //

children.text: rājavaṃśa nṛpateḥ pravardhate cakravartikularājasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The royal lineage of the king increases — born from the family of <s>cakravartin</s> kings;

children.text: bheṣyate kapilasāhvayaṃ puraṃ ratnakoṣabharitaṃ susamṛddham // Lal_5.79 //
children.translated_text: the city called <s>Kapila</s> will become filled with treasure stores, greatly prosperous! // Lal_5.79 //

children.text: yakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍaguhyakā devadānavagaṇāḥ saindrakāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, hosts of gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, together with <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: ye sthitā naravarasya rakṣakāḥ teṣu mokṣa nacireṇa bheṣyate // Lal_5.80 //
children.translated_text: those who stand as guardians of the best of men — for them, liberation will come before long! // Lal_5.80 //

children.text: puṇyupārjitu stavitva nāyakaṃ premagauravamupasthapisva nā /
children.translated_text: Having praised the leader whose merit has been well-earned, present [him] with love and respect;

children.text: sarva bodhi pariṇāmayāmahe kṣipra bhoma yatha tvaṃ narottama // Lal_5.81 //
children.translated_text: we dedicate all to awakening — may we swiftly become like you, O best of men! // Lal_5.81 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare pracalaparivarto nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Setting Forth' (<s>Pracalaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 6
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 6.

body.text: garbhāvakrāntiparivartaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Sixth Chapter: On the Descent into the Womb (<s>Garbhāvakrāntiparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ śiśirakālavinirgate vaiśākhamāse viśākhānakṣatrānugate ṛtupravare vasantakālasamaye taruvarapatrākīrṇe varapravarapuṣpasaṃkusumite śītoṣṇatamorajovigate mṛduśādvale susaṃsthite tribhuvanajyeṣṭho lokamahito vyavalokya ṛtukālasamaye pañcadaśyāṃ pūrṇamāsyāṃ poṣadhagṛhītāyā mātuḥ puṣyanakṣatrayogena bodhisattvastuṣitavarabhavanāccyutvā smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan pāṇḍuro gajapoto bhūtvā ṣaḍdanta indragopakaśirāḥ suvarṇarājīdantaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgo 'hīnendriyo jananyā dakṣiṇāyāṃ kukṣāvavakrāmat / avakrāntaśca sa dakṣiṇāvacaro 'bhūnna jātu vāmāvacaraḥ / māyādevī sukhaśayanaprasuptā imaṃ svapnamapaśyat -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the cool season had passed, in the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, under the <s>Viśākhā</s> constellation, in the best of seasons — the springtime — when the finest trees were covered with leaves, when the most excellent flowers were in full bloom, when cold, heat, darkness, and dust had departed, when the ground was soft, green, and well-formed — the foremost of the three worlds, honored by the world, having surveyed the season and the proper time, on the fifteenth day, the full-moon day, when the mother had taken the observance vow, under the conjunction of the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, descending from the excellent <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, mindful and fully aware, having taken the form of a white young elephant — six-tusked, with a head [adorned] like an <s>indragopaka</s> insect, with golden-striped tusks, with all limbs and minor limbs complete, with unimpaired faculties — descended into the right side of his mother's womb. And having descended, he remained on the right side, never on the left. <s>Māyādevī</s>, lying in comfortable sleep, beheld this dream —

children.text: himarajatanibhaśca ṣaḍviṣāṇaḥ sucaraṇa cārubhujaḥ suraktaśīrṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: White as snow and silver, six-tusked, with beautiful feet and lovely arms, with a brilliantly red head,

children.text: udaramupagato gajapradhāno lalitagatirdṛḍhavajragātrasaṃdhiḥ // Lal_6.1 //
children.translated_text: a lordly elephant entered [my] belly, of graceful gait, with limbs joined firm as adamant. // Lal_6.1 //

children.text: na ca mama sukha jātu evarūpaṃ dṛṣṭamapi śrutaṃ nāpi cānubhūtam /
children.translated_text: Never before have I experienced such happiness — neither seen, nor heard, nor felt;

children.text: kāyasukhacittasaukhyabhāvā yathariva dhyānasamāhitā abhūvam // Lal_6.2 //
children.translated_text: with bliss of body and joy of mind, I became as if absorbed in <s>dhyāna</s>. // Lal_6.2 //

body.text: atha khalu māyādevī ābharaṇavigalitavasanā prahlāditakāyacittā prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā śayanavaratalādutthāya nārīgaṇaparivṛtā puraskṛtā prāsādavaraśikharādavatīrya yenāśokavanikā tenopajagāma / sā aśokavanikāyāṃ sukhopaviṣṭā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya dūtaṃ preṣayati sma - āgacchatu devo devī te draṣṭukāmeti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, her ornaments and garments falling loose, her body and mind refreshed, having attained delight, joy, and serenity, rose from her excellent couch and, surrounded and attended by a company of women, descended from the peak of the palace and went to the <s>Aśoka</s> grove. Seated comfortably in the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, she sent a messenger to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Let the Lord come; the Queen wishes to see [him].' //

body.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodanastadvacanaṃ śrutvā praharṣitamanā ākampitaśarīro bhadrāsanādutthāya amātyanaigamapārṣadyabandhujanaparivṛto yenāśokavanikā tenopasaṃkrāmat, upasaṃkrāntaśca na śaknoti sma aśokavanikāṃ praveṣṭum / gurutaramivātmānaṃ manyate sma / aśokavanikādvāre sthito muhūrtaṃ saṃcintya tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having heard those words, his mind filled with joy, his body trembling, rose from the throne of state and, surrounded by ministers, guild-leaders, courtiers, and kinsmen, approached the <s>Aśoka</s> grove. Having approached, he was unable to enter the <s>Aśoka</s> grove. He felt himself to be exceedingly heavy. Standing at the gate of the <s>Aśoka</s> grove, reflecting for a moment, he uttered this verse at that time —

children.text: na smari raṇaśauṇḍi mūrdhasaṃsthasya mahyam eva guru śarīraṃ manyamī yādṛśo 'dya /
children.translated_text: I do not remember such a thing, O valiant warrior; even [my] body seems exceedingly heavy to me today, of a kind [I have not known before];

children.text: svakulagṛhamadya na prabhomi praveṣṭuṃ kimiha mama bhave 'ṅgo kānva pṛccheya cāham // Lal_6.3 //
children.translated_text: I am unable to enter my own family home today — what has happened to me in this birth? Whom should I ask? // Lal_6.3 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā gaganatalagatā ardhakāyamabhinirmāya rājānaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>-dwelling <s>Devaputras</s>, hovering in the sky and manifesting their upper bodies, addressed the king in verse —

children.text: vratatapaguṇayuktastisralokeṣu pūjyo maitrakaruṇalābhī puṇyajñānābhiṣiktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the virtues of vows and austerity, worshipped in the three worlds, having attained loving-kindness and compassion, anointed with merit and knowledge —

children.text: tuṣitapuri cyavitvā bodhisattvo mahātmā nṛpati tava sutatvaṃ māyakukṣaupapannaḥ // Lal_6.4 //
children.translated_text: the great-souled <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having descended from the <s>Tuṣita</s> city, O king, has entered the womb of <s>Māyā</s> as your son. // Lal_6.4 //

children.text: daśanakha tada kṛtvā svaṃ śiraṃ kampayanto nṛpatiranupraviṣṭaścitrikārānuyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then [the king], putting his ten nails [to his head], shaking his own head, entered [the queen's chamber], absorbed in wonder.

children.text: māya tada nirīkṣya mānadarpopanītāṃ vadahi kurumi kiṃ te kiṃ prayogo bhaṇāhi // Lal_6.5 //
children.translated_text: Beholding <s>Māyā</s>, who had been overcome by pride and elation, he said: 'Tell me — what shall I do for you? What effort [do you need]? Speak!' // Lal_6.5 //

body.text: devyāha -
body.translated_text: The queen said —

children.text: himarajatanikāśaścandrasūryātirekaḥ sucaraṇa suvibhaktaḥ ṣaḍviṣāṇo mahātmā /
children.translated_text: 'White as snow and silver, surpassing the moon and sun, with beautiful feet, well-proportioned, six-tusked, great-souled,

children.text: gajavaru dṛḍhasaṃdhirvajrakalpaḥ surūpaḥ udari mama praviṣṭastasya hetuṃ śruṇuṣva // Lal_6.6 //
children.translated_text: a supreme elephant, firm-jointed, adamantine, of beautiful form — it entered my belly. Hear the reason! // Lal_6.6 //

children.text: vitimira trisahasrāṃ paśyamī bhrājamānāṃ devanayuta devā ye stuvantī sayānā /
children.translated_text: I see the three-thousandfold [world] free from darkness, shining brightly; ten thousand gods are praising me as I lie [in repose].

children.text: na ca mama khiladoṣo naiva roṣo na moho dhyānasukhasamaṅgī jānamī śāntacittā // Lal_6.7 //
children.translated_text: I have no defilement or fault, no anger, no delusion; endowed with the bliss of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), I am tranquil-minded and aware. // Lal_6.7 //

children.text: sādhu nṛpati śīghraṃ brāhmaṇānānayāsmin vedasupinapāṭhā ye gṛheṣū vidhijñāḥ /
children.translated_text: Good king, quickly bring <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> here — those who know the <s>Vedas</s>, skilled in the interpretation of dreams, learned in the scriptures, dwelling in houses.

children.text: supinu mama hi yemaṃ vyākarī tattvayuktaṃ kimida mama bhaveyā śreyu pāpaṃ kulasya // Lal_6.8 //
children.translated_text: Let them interpret this dream of mine with truth: will this be for the good or ill of the family?' // Lal_6.8 //

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā pārthivastatkṣaṇena brāhmaṇa kṛtavedānānayacchāstrapāṭhān /
children.translated_text: Hearing this word, the king at that very moment brought <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, skilled in the scriptures.

children.text: māya purata sthitvā brāhmaṇānāmavocat supina mayi ha dṛṣṭastasya hetuṃ śṛṇotha // Lal_6.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, standing before the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, said: 'A dream has been seen by me — hear the reason for it!' // Lal_6.9 //

body.text: brāhmaṇā āhuḥ - brūhi devi tvayā kīdṛśaṃ svapnaṃ dṛṣṭam / śrutvā jñāsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said: 'Tell us, O queen — what kind of dream have you seen? Having heard, we shall know.'

body.text: devyāha -
body.translated_text: The queen said —

children.text: himarajatanikāśaścandrasūryātirekaḥ sucaraṇa suvibhaktaḥ ṣaḍviṣāṇo mahātmā /
children.translated_text: 'White as snow and silver, surpassing the moon and sun, with beautiful feet, well-proportioned, six-tusked, great-souled,

children.text: gajavaru dṛḍhasaṃdhirvajrakalpaḥ surūpaḥ udari mama praviṣṭastasya hetuṃ śṛṇotha // Lal_6.10 //
children.translated_text: a supreme elephant, firm-jointed, adamantine, of beautiful form — it entered my belly. Hear the reason!' // Lal_6.10 //

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā brāhmaṇā evamāhuḥ prīti vipula cintyā nāsti pāpaṃ kulasya /
children.translated_text: Hearing this word, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said thus: 'Great and vast is the joy to be pondered! There is no misfortune for the family.

children.text: putra tava janesī lakṣaṇairbhūṣitāṅgaṃ rājakulakulīnaṃ cakravarti mahātmaṃ // Lal_6.11 //
children.translated_text: You will bear a son whose limbs are adorned with [the auspicious] marks, of noble royal birth — a great-souled universal monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>). // Lal_6.11 //

children.text: sa ca pura vijahitvā kāmarājyaṃ ca gehaṃ pravrajita nirapekṣaḥ sarvalokānukampī /
children.translated_text: But he, having renounced the city, the kingdom of desires, and the home, will go forth [as a renunciant], without attachment, compassionate toward all the world.

children.text: buddho bhavati eṣo dakṣiṇīyastriloke amṛtarasavareṇā tarpayet sarvalokam // Lal_6.12 //
children.translated_text: He will become a <s>Buddha</s>, worthy of offerings in the three worlds; with the supreme nectar-essence he will satisfy the entire world.' // Lal_6.12 //

children.text: vyākaritva giraṃ saumyāṃ bhuktvā pārthivabhojanam /
children.translated_text: Having pronounced these auspicious words and partaken of the king's food,

children.text: ācchādanāni codgṛhya prakrāntā brāhmaṇāstataḥ // Lal_6.13 //
children.translated_text: and having received garments, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> departed from there. // Lal_6.13 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano brāhmaṇebhyo lakṣaṇanaimittikavaipañcakebhyaḥ svapnādhyāyīpāṭhakebhyaḥ pratiśrutya hṛṣṭastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastān brāhmaṇān prabhūtena khādanīyabhojanīyāsvādanīyena saṃtarpya saṃpravāryācchādanāni ca datvā visarjayati sma / tasyāṃ velāyāṃ kapilavastuni mahānagare caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu sarvanagaracatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu ca dānaṃ dāpayati sma annamannārthikebhyaḥ, pānaṃ pānārthikebhyaḥ, vastrāṇi vastrārthikebhyaḥ, yānāni yānārthikebhyaḥ / evaṃ gandhamālyavilepanaśayyopāśrayaṃ prājīvikaṃ prājīvikārthibhyo yāvadeva bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having heard from those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — experts in marks and signs, readers and interpreters of dreams — was joyful, pleased, elated, delighted, and full of gladness and happiness. Having satisfied those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with abundant food to be chewed, eaten, and savored, and having given them garments, he sent them away. At that time, in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, at the four city gates and at all the city crossroads and intersections, he had gifts distributed — food to those who desired food, drink to those who desired drink, garments to those who desired garments, vehicles to those who desired vehicles. Likewise, fragrances, garlands, ointments, bedding, and livelihood supplies to those who desired livelihood — all as an act of worship for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavat - katamasmin gṛhe māyādevī sukhamanupakliṣṭā viharediti / atha tatkṣaṇameva catvāro mahārājāno rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ -
body.translated_text: Now, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had this thought: 'In which residence could <s>Māyādevī</s> dwell happily and without distress?' Then at that very moment, the Four Great Kings approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said —

children.text: alpotsuko deva bhava sukhaṃ tiṣṭha upekṣako /
children.translated_text: 'Be at ease, O sovereign; rest in happiness and equanimity.

children.text: vayaṃ hi bodhisattvasya veśma vai māpayāmahe // Lal_6.14 //
children.translated_text: We shall build a dwelling for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // Lal_6.14 //

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said —

children.text: hīnā vimānā pālānāṃ trayatriṃśānamuttamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The palaces of the Guardians [of the four directions] are inferior; those of the Thirty-three [gods] are the highest.

children.text: vaijayantasamaṃ veśma bodhisattvasya dāmyaham // Lal_6.15 //
children.translated_text: I shall give a dwelling equal to <s>Vaijayanta</s> for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // Lal_6.15 //

body.text: atha khalu suyāmo devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamusaṃkramyaivamāha -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Suyāma</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said —

children.text: madīyaṃ bhavanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ śakrakoṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen my dwelling, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Śakras</s> are amazed.

children.text: suyāmabhavanaṃ śrīmadbodhisattvasya dāmyaham // Lal_6.16 //
children.translated_text: I shall give the splendid <s>Suyāma</s> dwelling for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // Lal_6.16 //

body.text: atha khalu saṃtuṣito devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said —

children.text: yatraiva uṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ tuṣiteṣu mahāyaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That very [mansion] in which the greatly famous one dwelt before, among the <s>Tuṣitas</s> —

children.text: tadeva bhavanaṃ ramyaṃ bodhisattvasya dāmyaham // Lal_6.17 //
children.translated_text: that delightful dwelling I shall give for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // Lal_6.17 //

body.text: atha khalu sunirmito devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Sunirmita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said —

children.text: manomayamahaṃ śrīmadvaśma tadratanāmayam /
children.translated_text: 'A mind-made, splendid dwelling, fashioned of jewels —

children.text: bodhisattvasya pūjārthamupaneṣyāmi pārthiva // Lal_6.18 //
children.translated_text: for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, I shall bring it, O king.' // Lal_6.18 //

body.text:
atha khalu paranirmitavaśavartī devaputro rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha -
yāvantaḥ kāmadhātusthā vimānāḥ śobhanāḥ kvacit /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said — 'However many beautiful celestial mansions exist anywhere in the Desire Realm,

body.text: bhābhiste madvimānasya bhavantyabhihataprabhāḥ // Lal_6.19 //
body.translated_text: their radiance is outshone by the radiance of my mansion. // Lal_6.19 //

children.text: tat prayacchāmyahaṃ śrīmadveśma ratnamayaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall give this splendid, jeweled, auspicious dwelling,

children.text: bodhisattvasya pūjārthamānayiṣyāmi pārthiva // Lal_6.20 //
children.translated_text: and I shall bring it for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O king. // Lal_6.20 //

children.text: divyaiḥ puṣpaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ divyagandhopavāsitam /
children.translated_text: Strewn with divine flowers, perfumed with divine fragrances —

children.text: upanāmayiṣye vipulaṃ yatra devī vasiṣyati // Lal_6.21 //
children.translated_text: I shall present this vast [palace] where the queen shall dwell.' // Lal_6.21 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ sarvaiḥ kāmāvacarraidaiveśvarairbodhisattvasya pūjārthaṃ kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare svakasvakāni gṛhāṇi māpitānyabhūvan / rājñā capi śuddhodanena manuṣyātikrāntaṃ divyāsaṃprāptaṃ gṛhataraṃ pratisaṃskāritamabhūt / tatra bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāvyūhasya samādheranubhāvena sarveṣu teṣu gṛheṣu māyādevīmupadarśayati sma / abhyantaragataśca bodhisattvo māyādevyāḥ kukṣau dakṣiṇe pārśve paryaṅkamābhujya niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt / sarve ca te deveśvarā ekaikamevaṃ saṃjānīte sma - mamaiva gṛhe bodhisattvamātā prativasati nānyatreti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, by all the divine lords of the Desire Realm, in the supreme great city called <s>Kapila</s>, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, their respective dwellings were fashioned. And by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> too, a dwelling surpassing human [craft] yet not reaching the divine was prepared. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, by the power of the concentration called <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array), displayed <s>Māyādevī</s> in all those dwellings. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, within, in <s>Māyādevī</s>'s womb, on the right side, sat cross-legged. And all those divine lords each believed: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother dwells in my dwelling alone, and nowhere else.' //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Thereupon this was said —

children.text: mahāvyūhāya sthitaḥ samādhiye acintiyā nirmita nirmiṇitvā /
children.translated_text: Abiding in the concentration of the Great Array, having created inconceivable emanations,

children.text: sarveṣa devānabhiprāya pūritā nṛpasya pūrṇaśca tadā manorathaḥ // Lal_6.22 //
children.translated_text: the intentions of all those gods were fulfilled, and the king's wish was also then fulfilled. // Lal_6.22 //

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ devaparṣadi keṣāṃciddevaputrāṇāmetadabhavat - ye 'pi tāvaccāturmahārājakāyikā devāste 'pi tāvanmanuṣyāśrayagatatvena nirvidyāpakramanti / kaḥ punarvādo ye tadanye udāratamā devāḥ trāyatriṃśā vā yāmā vā tuṣitā vā / tatkathaṃ hi nāma sarvalokābhyudgato bodhisattvaḥ śucirnirāmagandhaḥ sattvaratnaḥ saṃtuṣitāddevanikāyāccyutvā durgandhe manuṣyāśraye daśamāsān mātuḥ kukṣau sthita iti //
body.translated_text: Now, in that divine assembly, some <s>Devaputras</s> had this thought: 'Even the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, being established in a human abode, are disgusted and withdraw. What then to say of those other, more exalted gods — the <s>Trāyatriṃśas</s>, <s>Yāmas</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, and the like? How then can the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is exalted above all the worlds, pure, free from the smell of corruption, the jewel among beings — having descended from the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine assembly — remain for ten months in the mother's womb in the foul-smelling human abode?' //

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānando buddhānubhāvena bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvajjugupsanīyaśca mātṛgrāmastathāgatenokto yāvadrāgacaritaśca / idaṃ tu bhagavan āścaryataram / kathaṃ hi nāma sarvalokābhyudgato bhagavān pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūta eva tuṣitāddevanikāyāccyavitvā manuṣyāśraye (durgandhe) māturdakṣiṇe (pārśve) kukṣāvupapanna iti / nāhaṃ bhagavan idamutsahe evaṃ vaktaṃ yathaiva pūrve bhagavatā vyākṛtamiti / bhagavānāha - icchasi tvamānanda ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ draṣṭuṃ yo mātuḥ kukṣigatasya bodhisattvasya paribhogo 'bhūt / ānanda āha - ayamasya bhagavan kālaḥ, ayaṃ sugata samayaḥ, yattathāgatastaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogamupadarśayed yaṃ dṛṣṭvā prītiṃ vetsyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is amazing, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared the female sex to be so loathsome and given to passion. But this, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is even more amazing: how is it that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, exalted above all the worlds, formerly when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, descended from the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine assembly and was conceived in the mother's womb on the right side, in the foul-smelling human abode? I am not able, <s>Bhagavān</s>, to say this in the way it was formerly explained by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to see the <s>Ratnavyūha</s> (Jewel Array), the accoutrements enjoyed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> while in the mother's womb?' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'This is the time, <s>Bhagavān</s>; this is the moment, <s>Sugata</s>, for the <s>Tathāgata</s> to display those accoutrements of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing which we shall be filled with joy.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstathārūpanimittamakarot, yad brahmā sahāpatiḥ sārdhamaṣṭaṣaṣṭibrahmaśatasahasrairbrahmaloke 'ntarhito bhagavataḥ purataḥ pratyasthāt / sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte 'sthāt prāñjalībhūto bhagavantaṃ namasyan / tatra khalu bhagavān jānanneva brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatimāmantrayate sma - gṛhītastvayā brahman sa bodhisattvaparibhogo daśamāsiko yo mama pūrvaṃ bodhisattvabhūtasya mātuḥ kukṣigatasyābhūt / brahmā āha - evametadbhagavan, evametat sugata / bhagavānāha - kva sa idānīṃ brahman? upadarśaya tam / brahmā cāha - brahmaloke sa bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tena hi tvaṃ brahman upadarśaya taṃ daśamāsikaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogam, jñāsyanti kiyatsaṃskṛtamiti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> made a sign such that <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>Brahmās</s>, vanished from the <s>Brahmā</s>-world and appeared before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, stood to one side with joined palms, and saluted the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing [already], addressed <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>: 'Was the ten-month accoutrement of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> taken by you, O <s>Brahmā</s>, which was Mine when I was formerly a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the mother's womb?' <s>Brahmā</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Bhagavān</s>; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Where is it now, O <s>Brahmā</s>? Display it.' <s>Brahmā</s> said: 'It is in the <s>Brahmā</s>-world, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Then, O <s>Brahmā</s>, display that ten-month accoutrement of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. They shall know how well-wrought it is.' //

body.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatistān brāhmaṇānetadavocat - tiṣṭhatu tāvadbhavanto yāvadvayaṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogamānayiṣyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> addressed those <s>Brahmās</s> thus: 'Wait, good sirs, while we shall bring the <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the accoutrements of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' //

body.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatirbhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā bhagavataḥ purato 'ntarhitastatkṣaṇameva brahmaloke pratyasthāt //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, vanished from before the <s>Bhagavān</s> and at that very moment appeared in the <s>Brahmā</s>-world. //

body.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiḥ subrahmāṇaṃ devaputrametadavocat - gaccha tvaṃ mārṣā ito brahmalokamupādāya yāvattrāyatriṃśadbhavanam - śabdamudīraya, ghoṣamanuśrāvaya / ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ vayaṃ tathāgatasyāntikamupanāmayiṣyāmaḥ / yo yuṣmākaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ sa śīghramāgacchatviti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> addressed the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Subrahmā</s>: 'Go, good sir, from here throughout the <s>Brahmā</s>-world and up to the <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> heaven — raise the sound, proclaim the announcement: We shall bring the <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the accoutrements of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, before the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Whoever among you wishes to see it, let him come swiftly!' //

body.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiścaturaśītyā devakoṭyā nayutaśatasahasraḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ parigṛhya mahati brāhme vimāne triyojanaśatike pratiṣṭhāpyānekairdaivakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ samantato 'nuparivārya jambūdvīpamavatārayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred thousands of gods, having taken up that <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the accoutrements of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established it in a great <s>Brahmā</s> palace three hundred <s>yojanas</s> [in extent], and accompanied on all sides by many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred thousands of gods, brought it down to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāṃ mahāsaṃnipāto 'bhūt bhagavatsakāśe gantum / sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo divyairvastrairdivyairmālyairdivyairgandhairdivyaiḥ puṣpairdivyairvādyairdivyaiśca paribhaugairabhisaṃskṛto 'bhūt / tāvanmaheśākhyaiśca devaiḥ parivṛto 'bhūd yacchakro devānāmindraḥ sumerau(samudre) sthitvā dūrata eva mukhe tālacchatrakaṃ dattvā śīrṣavyavalokanenānuvilokayati sma unmeṣadhyāyikayā vā / na ca śaknoti sma draṣṭum / tatkasmāt? maheśākhyā hi devā brāhmaṇāḥ / itarāstrāyatriṃśā yāmāstuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartinaḥ / kaḥ punarvādaḥ śakro devānāmindraḥ / mohaṃ te vai yānti sma //
body.translated_text: Now at that time, there was a great assembly of the Desire Realm gods [gathered] to go into the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. That <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the accoutrements of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, was adorned with divine garments, divine garlands, divine fragrances, divine flowers, divine music, and divine furnishings. And it was surrounded by such great <s>Maheśa</s> gods that <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, standing on [Mount] <s>Sumeru</s> [by the ocean], placing a palm-leaf parasol over his face from afar, tried to look up at it by craning his neck or by squinting — but was unable to see it. Why? Because the <s>Maheśa</s> gods are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [i.e., Brahmā-class deities]. The others — the <s>Trāyatriṃśas</s>, <s>Yāmas</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s> — how much more so <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods? They were all bewildered. //

children.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstaṃ divyaṃ vādyanirghoṣamantardhāpayati sma /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> caused that divine sound of music to disappear.

children.text: tatkasmāt? yatsahaśravaṇādeva jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā unmādamāpatsyanta iti //
children.translated_text: Why? Because upon hearing it, the human beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> would have gone mad. //

body.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājānaḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ - kathaṃ devānāmindra kariṣyāmo na labhāmahe ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ draṣṭum / sa tānavocat - kimahaṃ mārṣāḥ kariṣyāmi? ahamapi na labhe draṣṭum / api tu khalu punarmārṣā bhagavatsamīpamupanītaṃ drakṣyāmaḥ / te tadā āhuḥ - tena hi devānāmindra tathā kuru yathāsya kṣipraṃ darśanaṃ bhavet / śakra āha - āgamayata mārṣā muhūrtaṃ yāvadatikrāntātikrāntatamā devaputrā bhagavantaṃ pratisaṃmodayante sma / tadekānte sthitvā śīrṣonmiñjitakayā bhagavantamanuvilokayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then the four Great Kings approached <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and said: 'How shall we proceed, O lord of the gods?
