We are unable to see the jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing.' He said to them: 'What can I do, venerable ones? I too am unable to see it. But, venerable ones, we shall see it when it is brought before the Lord.' They then said: 'Then, lord of the gods, make it so that his appearance may come quickly.' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Wait a moment, venerable ones, until the past <s>devaputras</s> have greeted the Lord.' Standing apart, they looked upon the Lord with gestures of tilting their heads. //

body.text: atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiḥ sārdhaṃ taiścaturaśītyā devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraistaṃ ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmayati sma / sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo 'bhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaścaturasraścatuṣṭhūṇaḥ / upariṣṭācca kūṭāgārasamalaṃkṛtaḥ / evaṃpramāṇaḥ tadyathāpi nāma ṣaṇmāsajāto
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, together with those eighty-four <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of gods, took up that jewel-array — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing — and brought it into the presence of the Lord. That jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, was beautiful, gracious, lovely to behold, four-cornered, with four pillars. Above, it was adorned with a pavilion. Its dimensions were as follows: in height, like a six-month-old

body.text: dāraka uccaistvena / tasya khalu punaḥ kūtāgārasya madhye paryaṅkaḥ prajñaptaḥ tadyathāpi nāma ṣaṇmāsajātasya dārakasya bhittīphalakaḥ / sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhoga evaṃ varṇasaṃsthāno yasya na kaścit sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sadṛśo 'sti ākṛtyā vā varṇena vā / devāḥ khalvapi taṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptā abhuvan / cakṣūṃṣi teṣāṃ vibhramanti sma / sa ca tathāgatasyāntika upanīto 'tīva bhāsate tapati virocate sma / tadyathāpi nāma dvinirdhāntaṃ suvarṇaṃ kuśalena karmakāreṇa supariniṣṭhitamapagatakācadoṣam, evaṃ (tasmin samaye) sa kūṭāgāro virājate sma / tasmin khalu punarbodhisattvaparibhoge paryaṅkaḥ prajñapto yasya sadevake loke nāsti kaścit sadṛśo varṇena vā saṃsthānena vā anyatra kambugrīvāyā
body.translated_text: child. In the middle of that pavilion, a couch was prepared, [with dimensions] like the side-panel of a six-month-old child. That jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, was of such color and form that nothing in the world with its gods, <s>Māra</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> was equal to it in shape or hue. Even the gods, having seen it, were filled with wonder. Their eyes were dazzled. And brought into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it shone, blazed, and radiated exceedingly. Just as twice-refined gold, well-finished by a skilled craftsman, free from the fault of impurities — so at that time that pavilion shone. And on that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, a couch was prepared whose equal in color or form did not exist in the world with its gods — except for the conch-necked

body.text: bodhisattvasya / yat khalu mahābrahmaṇā cīvaraṃ prāvṛtamabhūt, tattasya bodhisattvaparyaṅkasyāgrato na bhāsate sma tadyathāpi nāma vātavṛṣṭyābhihataḥ kṛṣṇakambalaḥ / sa khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāra uragasāracandanamayo yasyaikasuvarṇadharaṇī sāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ mūlyaṃ kṣamate, tathāvidhenoragasāracandanena sa kūṭāgāraḥ samantādanupaliptaḥ / tādṛśa eva dvitīyaḥ kūṭāgāraḥ kṛto yastasmin prathame kūṭāgāre 'bhyantarataḥ asakto 'baddhasthitaḥ / tādṛśa eva tṛtīyo 'pi kūṭāgāro yastasmin dvitīye kūṭāgāre 'bhyantare 'sakto 'baddhasthitaḥ / sa ca paryaṅkastasmin gandhamaye tṛtīye kūṭāgāre vyavasthitaḥ saṃpraticchannaḥ / tasya khalu punaruragasāracandanasyaivaṃrūpo varṇaḥ tadyathāpi nāma abhijātasya nīlaivaḍūryasya / tasya khalu punargandhakūṭāgārasyopari samantādyāvanti kāniciddivyātikrāntāni puṣpāṇi santi, tāni sarvāṇi tasmin kūṭāgāre bodhisattvasya pūrvakuśalamūlavipākenānuprāptānyeva jāyante sma / sa khalu puna ratnavyūho bodhisattvaparibhogo dṛḍhasāro 'bhedyo vajropamaḥ sparśena ca kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśaḥ / tasmin khalu puna ratnavyūhe bodhisattvaparibhoge ye kecit kāmāvacarāṇāṃ devānāṃ bhavanavyūhāste sarve tasmin saṃdṛśyante sma //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattva</s> [himself]. The robe that great <s>Brahmā</s> wore did not shine before that <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s couch — like a black blanket beaten by wind and rain. That pavilion was made of <s>uraga-sāra</s> (serpent-essence) sandalwood, a single gold-weight of which could buy the entire trichiliocosm in value; with such <s>uraga-sāra</s> sandalwood the pavilion was anointed on all sides. A second pavilion of exactly the same kind was made, which stood inside the first pavilion, unattached and unbound. A third pavilion of exactly the same kind stood inside the second, unattached and unbound. And the couch was placed within that third, fragrant pavilion, concealed. The color of that <s>uraga-sāra</s> sandalwood was like that of a noble blue lapis lazuli. Above and around that fragrant pavilion, whatever surpassingly divine flowers existed — they all appeared in that pavilion, arising by the ripening of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s former roots of merit. That jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, was of firm essence, unbreakable, adamantine, and to the touch, pleasant like <s>kācilindika</s> [silk]. In that jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, all the palace-arrays of the desire-realm gods were visible. //

body.text: yāmeva ca rātriṃ bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāntastāmeva rātrimadha āpaskandhamupādāya aṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasrāṇi mahāpṛthivīṃ bhittvā yāvad brahmalokaṃ padmabhyudgatamabhūt / na ca kaścittaṃ padmaṃ paśyati sma anyatra sārathinarottamāddaśaśatasāhasrikācca mahābrahmaṇaḥ / yacceha trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāvojo vā maṇḍo va raso vā, tatsarvaṃ tasmin mahāpadme madhubinduḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sma //
body.translated_text: On that very night when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> descended into his mother's womb, from below, taking the water-level as the base, a lotus emerged, having pierced the great earth for sixty-eight hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, reaching up to the <s>Brahma</s>-world. No one could see that lotus except the supreme charioteer of men [the <s>Buddha</s>] and the ten-hundred-thousand-fold great <s>Brahmā</s>. Whatever essence, cream, or nutriment existed in this trichiliocosm — all of that collected as a drop of honey in that great lotus. //

body.text: tamenaṃ mahābrahmā śubhe vaiḍūryabhājane prakṣipya bodhisattvasyopanāmayati sma / taṃ bodhisattvaḥ parigṛhya bhuṅkte sma mahābrahmaṇo 'nukampāmupādāya / nāsti sa kaścit sattvaḥ sattvanikāye yasya sa ojobinduḥ paribhuktaḥ samyak sukhena pariṇāmedanyatra caramabhavikādbodhisattvāt sarvabodhisattvabhūmiparipūrṇāt / kasya ca karmaṇo vipākena sa ojobindurbodhisattvasyopatiṣṭhate sma? dīrgharātraṃ khalvapi bodhisattvena pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā glānebhyaḥ sattvebhyo bhaiṣajyaṃ dattamāśatparāṇāṃ sattvānāmāśāḥ paripūritāḥ, śaraṇāgatāśca na parityaktāḥ, nityaṃ cāgrapuṣpamagraphalamagrarasaṃ tathāgatebhyastathāgatacaityebhyastathāgataśrāvakasaṃghebhyo mātāpitṛbhyaśca dattvā paścādātmanā paribhuktam / tasya karmaṇo vipākena mahābrahmā bodhisattvasya taṃ madhubindumupanāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: Great <s>Brahmā</s>, placing it in a beautiful lapis lazuli vessel, offered it to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking it, consumed it out of compassion for great <s>Brahmā</s>. There is no being in the world of beings who could properly digest that drop of essence with ease — except the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence, who has fulfilled all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. And by the ripening of what <s>karma</s> did that drop of essence appear for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? For a long time, while practicing the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in former lives, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had given medicine to sick beings, had fulfilled the hopes of those who were hopeful, had not abandoned those who came seeking refuge, and had always first offered the best flowers, the best fruits, and the best flavors to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrines, and to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s community of disciples, and to his parents, and only afterward consumed [things] himself. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, great <s>Brahmā</s> offered that drop of honey to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāre yāni kānicit santyatikrāntātikrāntāni māyāguṇaratikrīḍāsamavasṛtasthānāni, tāni sarvāṇi tasmin prādurbhāvāni saṃdṛśyante sma bodhisattvasya pūrvakarmavipākena //
body.translated_text: In that pavilion, whatever surpassingly wonderful places of amusement, play, and delight created by <s>māyā</s> existed — all of them appeared visible therein, by the ripening of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s former <s>karma</s>. //

body.text: tasmin khalu puna ratnavyūhe bodhisattvaparibhoge śatasahasravyūhaṃ nāma vāsoyugaṃ prādurbhūtam / na sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate yasya tatprādurbhavedanyatra caramabhavikād bodhisattvāt /
body.translated_text: In that jewel-array, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s furnishing, there appeared a garment-set called 'hundred-thousand-array.' There is no being in the world of beings for whom it would appear — except the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence.

body.text: na ca te kecana udārodārā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśā ye tasmin kūṭāgāre na saṃdṛśyante sma / sacetkūṭāgāraparibhoga evaṃ suparibhoga evaṃ supariniṣpannaḥ sāntarabahirevaṃ supariniṣṭhita evaṃ mṛdukaśca / tadyathāpi nāma kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśo nidarśanamātreṇa, na tu tasyopamā saṃvidyate / dharmatā khalveṣā bodhisattvasya pūrvakeṇa ca praṇidhānena iyaṃ cetanā ṛddhāvavaśyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena manuṣyaloka upapattavyamabhiniṣkramya cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartayitavyam / yasyā mātuḥ kukṣāvupapattirbhavati, tasyā dakṣiṇe kukṣāvādita eva ratnavyūhakūṭāgāro 'bhinirvartate / paścādbodhisattvastuṣitebhyaścyuttvā tasmin kūṭāgāre paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaḥ saṃbhavati / na hi caramabhavikasya bodhisattvasya kalalārbudaghanapeśībhāvaṃ kāyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate sma / atha tarhi sarvāṅgapratyaṅgalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇa eva prādurbhavati / svapnāntaragatā ca bodhisattvamātā māyādevī mahānāgakuñjaramavakrāntaṃ saṃjānīte sma //
body.translated_text: And there were no excellent or supreme forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, or touches that were not visible in that pavilion. If the pavilion-furnishing was thus well-furnished, thus well-accomplished, thus well-finished both inside and outside, and so soft — just as [the touch of] <s>kācilindika</s> [silk] is [merely] an illustration by comparison, for no true likeness of it exists. For this is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and by his former vow and intention: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being, must inevitably be reborn in the human world, must go forth, must awaken to supreme, perfect enlightenment, and must turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s>. In whichever mother's womb his rebirth occurs, in her right side, from the very beginning, the jewel-array pavilion manifests. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fallen from <s>Tuṣita</s>, comes into existence seated cross-legged in that pavilion. For the body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final existence does not remain in the states of <s>kalala</s> (embryonic fluid), <s>arbuda</s> (blister), <s>ghana</s> (lump), or <s>peśī</s> (flesh-mass). Rather, he manifests already seated, complete with all major and minor marks. And <s>Māyādevī</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, in a dream-state, perceives the descent of a great lord-elephant. //

body.text: tasya khalu punastathā niṣaṇṇasya śakro devānāmindraścatvāraśca mahārājāno 'ṣṭāviṃśatiśca mahāyakṣasenāpatayo guhyakādhipatiśca nāma yakṣakulaṃ yato vajrapāṇerutpattiste bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ viditvā satataṃ samitamanubaddhā bhavanti sma / santi khalu punaścatasro bodhisattvaparicārakā devatāḥ - utkhalī ca nāma samutkhalī ca nāma dhvajavatī ca nāma prabhāvatī ca nāma / tā api bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ viditvā satataṃ samitaṃ rakṣanti sma / śakro 'pi devānāmindraḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrairdevaputraśatairbodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ jñātvā satataṃ samitamanubadhnāti sma //
body.translated_text: When he was thus seated, <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, the four Great Kings, the twenty-eight great <s>Yakṣa</s> generals, and the <s>Yakṣa</s> clan called the Lord of Secrets — from which <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> arose — knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to be within his mother's womb, constantly and uninterruptedly attended him. And there are four deities who serve the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: <s>Utkhalī</s>, <s>Samutkhalī</s>, <s>Dhvajavatī</s>, and <s>Prabhāvatī</s>. They too, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to be within his mother's womb, constantly and uninterruptedly guarded him. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, too, together with five hundred <s>devaputras</s>, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to be within his mother's womb, constantly and uninterruptedly attended him. //

body.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarmātuḥ kukṣigatasya kāyastathāvidho 'bhūt, tadyathāpi nāma parvatamūrdhani rātrāvandhakāratamisrāyāṃ mahānagniskandho yojanādapi dṛśyate sma, yāvat pañcabhyā yojanebhyo dṛśyate sma / evameva bodhisattvasya mātuḥ kukṣigatasyātmabhāvo 'bhinirvṛtto 'bhūt prabhāsvaro 'bhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ / sa tasmin kūṭāgāre paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇo 'tīva śobhate sma / vaiḍūryapratyuptamivābhijātaṃ jātarūpam / bodhisattvasya mātā ca nidhyāya sthitā paśyati sma kukṣigataṃ bodhisattvam / tadyathāpi nāma mahato 'bhrakūṭādvidyuto niḥsṛtya mahāntamavabhāsaṃ saṃjanayanti, evameva bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigataḥ śriyā tejasā varṇena ca taṃ prathamaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma / avabhāsya dvitīyaṃ gandhakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma / dvitīyaṃ gandhakūṭāgāramavabhāsya tṛtīyaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsayati sma / tṛtīyaṃ ratnakūṭāgāramavabhāsya sarvāvantaṃ māturātmabhāvamavabhāsayati sma / tamavabhāsya yatra cāsane niṣaṇṇo bhavati sma tadavabhāsayati sma / tadavabhāsya sarvaṃ gṛhamavabhāsayati sma / sarvaṃ gṛhamavabhāsya gṛhasyopariṣṭānniḥsṛtya pūrvāṃ diśamavabhāsayati sma / evaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ paścimāṃ uttarāmadha ūrdhvaṃ samantāddaśadiśaḥ krośamātramekaikasyāṃ diśi mātuḥ kukṣigato bodhisattvaḥ śriyā tejasā varṇena cāvabhāsayati sma //
body.translated_text: The body of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within his mother's womb was of such a nature that, just as a great mass of fire on a mountain peak is visible even from a <s>yojana</s> away in the darkness of night — indeed, visible from five <s>yojanas</s> — so too, the being of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within his mother's womb was radiant, beautiful, gracious, and lovely to behold. Seated cross-legged in that pavilion, he shone exceedingly — like noble refined gold set with lapis lazuli. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, standing in meditation, could see the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within her womb. Just as lightning emerging from a great mass of clouds generates a great illumination, so the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within his mother's womb illuminated the first jewel-pavilion with his glory, splendor, and radiance. Having illuminated that, he illuminated the second fragrant pavilion. Having illuminated the second fragrant pavilion, he illuminated the third jewel-pavilion. Having illuminated the third jewel-pavilion, he illuminated the entire being of his mother. Having illuminated that, he illuminated the seat on which she sat. Having illuminated that, he illuminated the entire house. Having illuminated the entire house, emerging from above the house, he illuminated the eastern direction. Likewise the southern, western, and northern, below, above, and all around the ten directions — in each direction for the distance of a <s>krośa</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within his mother's womb illuminated [all] with his glory, splendor, and radiance. //

body.text: āgacchanti sma khalu punarbhikṣavaścatvāro mahārājāno 'ṣṭāviṃśacca mahāyakṣasenāpatayaḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrayakṣaśataiḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca / tadā bodhisattvastānāgatān viditvā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇimabhyutkṣipya ekāṅgulikayā āsanānyupadarśayati sma / niṣīdanti sma te lokapālādayo yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu / paśyanti sma bodhisattvaṃ mātuḥ kukṣigataṃ jātarūpamiva vigrahaṃ hastaṃ cālayantaṃ vicālayantam utkṣipantaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayantam / te prītiprāmodyaprasādapratilabdhā bodhisattvaṃ namaskurvanti sma / niṣaṇṇāṃśca tān viditvā bodhisattvo dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma / yadā ca prakramitukāmā bhavanti tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva vicintitaṃ vijñāya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇimutkṣipya saṃcārayati sma / saṃcārya vicārayati sma / mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma / tadā teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāmevaṃ bhavati sma - visarjitāḥ sma vayaṃ bodhisattveneti / te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya prakrāmanti sma / ayaṃ heturayaṃ pratyayo yadbodhisattvo rātryāṃ praśāntāyāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ saṃcārya vicārayati sma / vicārya punarapi smṛtaḥ saṃprajānaṃstaṃ pāṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati sma / punaraparaṃ yadā bodhisattvasya keciddarśanāyāgacchanti sma striyo vā puruṣo vā dārako vā dārikā vā, tān bodhisattvaḥ pūrvatarameva pratisaṃmodayate sma, paścādbodhisattvasya mātā //
body.translated_text: Moreover, O monks, the four great kings and twenty-eight great <s>Yakṣa</s> generals, together with approximately five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s>, would come in the forenoon to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, to pay homage, to attend upon him, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing they had arrived, would raise his right hand and with a single finger indicate their seats. The world-guardians and the others would sit upon the seats assigned to them. They would behold the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within his mother's womb — his form like wrought gold — moving his hand, waving it, raising it, and setting it down. Having attained delight, joy, and serenity, they would pay homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And knowing that they were seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would instruct them, encourage them, inspire them, and gladden them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. And when they wished to depart, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing the thought of their minds, would raise his right hand and wave it. Having waved it, he would lower it — and he did not disturb his mother. Then the thought arose in those four great kings: 'We have been dismissed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother three times, they would depart. This is the reason, this is the cause, why the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when the night was peaceful, would wave and lower his right hand; having lowered it, mindful and fully aware, he would set that hand down again. Furthermore, whenever any persons came to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — whether women or men, boys or girls — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would greet them first, [and only] afterward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigataḥ san sattvān pratisaṃmodanakuśalo bhavati smeti / na ca kaściddevo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā yaḥ śaknoti sma bodhisattvaṃ pūrvataraṃ pratisaṃmoditum / atha tarhi bodhisattva eva tāvat pūrvataraṃ pratisaṃmodate sma, paścādbodhisattvamātā //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, even while dwelling within his mother's womb, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was skilled in greeting beings. And there was no god, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, human, or non-human who was able to greet the <s>Bodhisattva</s> first. Rather, it was the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself who would greet [them] first, and afterward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother. //

body.text: nirgate khalu punaḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye madhyāhnakālasamaye pratyupasthite atha khalu śakro devānāmindro niṣkrāntaḥ / abhiniṣkrāntāśca trāyatriṃśaddevaputrā bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya / dharmaśravaṇāya cāgacchanti sma / tāṃśca bodhisattvo dūrata evāgacchato dṛṣṭvā dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya śakraṃ devānāmindraṃ devāṃśca trāyatriṃśān pratisaṃmodate sma / ekāṅgulikayā cāsanānyupadarśayati sma / na ca śaknoti sma bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindro bodhisattvasyājñāṃ pratiroddhum / niṣīdati sma śakro devānāmindrastadanye ca devaputrā yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu / tān bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇān viditvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma / yena ca bodhisattvaḥ pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma, tanmukhā bodhisattvamātā bhavati sma / tatasteṣāmevaṃ bhavati sma - asmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃmodate sma / ekaikaścaivaṃ saṃjānīte sma - mayaiva sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃlapati, māmeva pratisaṃmodate sma iti //
body.translated_text: When the forenoon had passed and the midday had arrived, then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, came forth. And the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> <s>Devaputras</s> came forth to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, to pay homage, to attend upon him, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing them coming from afar, would extend his right arm — golden in color — and greet <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. With a single finger he would indicate their seats. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, was unable, O monks, to resist the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s command. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the other <s>Devaputras</s> would sit upon the seats assigned to them. Knowing they were seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would instruct them, encourage them, inspire them, and gladden them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. And in whichever direction the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would wave his hand, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother would face that direction. Then the thought arose in them: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is conversing with us.' And each one understood thus: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is speaking with me alone; he is greeting me alone.' //

body.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ kūṭāgāre śakrasya devānāmindrasya trāyatriṃśānāṃ devānāṃ ca pratibhāsaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma / na khalu punaranyatraivaṃ pariśuddho bodhisattvaparibhogo bhavati yathā mātuḥ kukṣigatasya bodhisattvasya / yadā ca bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindrastadanye ca devaputrāḥ prakramitukāmā bhavanti sma, tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇimutkṣipya saṃcārayanti sma / saṃcārya vicārya punarapi smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan pratiṣṭhāpayati sma / mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma / tadā śakrasya devānāmindrasyānyeṣāṃ ca trāyatriṃśānāṃ devānāmevaṃ bhavati sma - visarjitā vayaṃ bodhisattveneti / te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya prakrāmanti sma //
body.translated_text: Moreover, in that palace, the reflection of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods was visible. Indeed, nowhere else is there such a pure dwelling for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is in his mother's womb. And when, O monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the other <s>Devaputras</s> wished to depart, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing the thought and deliberation of their minds, would raise his right hand and wave it. Having waved and lowered it, mindful and fully aware, he would set it down again — and he did not disturb his mother. Then the thought arose in <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the other <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: 'We have been dismissed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother three times, they would depart. //

body.text: nirgate ca khalu punarbhikṣavo madhyāhnakālasamaye sāyāhnakālasamaye pratyupasthite atha khalu brahmā sahāpatiranekairbrahmakāyikairdevaputraśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtastaṃ divyamojobindumādāya yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmati sma bodhisattvaṃ draṣṭuṃ vandituṃ paryupāsituṃ dharmaṃ ca śrotum / samanvāharati sma bhikṣavaḥ bodhisattvo brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatimāgacchantaṃ saparivāram / punareva ca bodhisattvo dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇapāṇimutkṣipya brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatiṃ brahmakāyikāṃśca devaputrān pratisaṃmodate sma / ekāṅgulikayā cāsanānyupadarśayati sma / na ca śaktirasti bhikṣavo brahmaṇaḥ sahāpaterbodhisattvasyājñāṃ pratiroddhum / niṣīdati sma bhikṣavo brahmā sahāpatistadanye ca brahmakāyikā devaputrā yathāprajñapteṣvāsaneṣu / tān bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇān viditvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma samādāpayati sma samuttejayati sma saṃpraharṣayati sma / yena ca bodhisattvaḥ pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma, tanmukhaiva māyādevī bhavati sma / tatasteṣāmekaikasyaivaṃ bhavati sma - mayā sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃlapati, māmeva pratisaṃmodate sma iti / yadā ca brahmā sahāpatistadanye ca brahmakāyikā devaputrā gantukāmā bhavanti sma, tadā bodhisattvasteṣāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya dakṣiṇaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhumutkṣipya saṃcārayati sma / saṃcārya vicārayati sma / saṃcārya vicārya avasādatākāreṇa pāṇiṃ saṃcārayati sma / mātaraṃ ca na bādhate sma / tato brahmaṇaḥ sahāpatestadanyeṣāṃ ca brahmakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāmevaṃ bhavati sma - visarjitā vayaṃ bodhisattveneti / te bodhisattvaṃ bodhisattvamātaraṃ ca tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya punareva prakrāmanti sma / bodhisattvaśca smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan pāṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati sma //
body.translated_text: When the midday had passed and the evening had arrived, then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>Devaputras</s>, taking the divine drop of nourishing essence, would approach the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to see him, to pay homage, to attend upon him, and to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O monks, would perceive <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> approaching with his retinue. And again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would raise his right hand — golden in color — and greet <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>Devaputras</s>. With a single finger he would indicate their seats. And <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> was unable, O monks, to resist the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s command. <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, O monks, and the other <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>Devaputras</s> would sit upon the seats assigned to them. Knowing they were seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would instruct them, encourage them, inspire them, and gladden them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. And in whichever direction the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would wave his hand, <s>Māyādevī</s> would face that very direction. Then the thought arose in each one of them: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is speaking with me; he is greeting me alone.' And when <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and the other <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>Devaputras</s> wished to depart, then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing the thought and deliberation of their minds, would raise his right arm — golden in color — and wave it. Having waved and lowered it, he would wave his hand with a gesture of dismissal — and he did not disturb his mother. Then the thought arose in <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> and the other <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>Devaputras</s>: 'We have been dismissed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother three times, they would again depart. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, mindful and fully aware, would set his hand down. //

body.text: āgacchanti sma khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarābhyo digbhyo 'dhastādupariṣṭāt santāddaśabhyo digbhyo bahūni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvasya darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca dharmasaṃgītisaṃgāyanāya ca / teṣāmāgatāgatānāṃ bodhisattvaḥ kāyāt prabhāmutsṛjya prabhāvyūhāni siṃhāsanānyabhinirmimīte sma / abhinirmāya tān bodhisattvāṃsteṣvāsaneṣu niṣīdayati sma / niṣaṇṇāṃścainān viditvā paripṛcchati sma paripraśnayati sma yadutāsyaiva bodhisattvasya mahāyānasya vistaravibhāgatāmupādāya / na ca tān kaścidanyaḥ paśyati sma anyatra sabhāgebhyo devaputrebhyaḥ / ayaṃ bhikṣavo heturayaṃ pratyayo yena bodhisattvaḥ praśāntāyāṃ rātryāṃ kāyāt prabhāmutsṛjati sma //
body.translated_text: Moreover, O monks, from the eastern, southern, western, northern, lower, upper — from all ten directions — many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> would come to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, to pay homage, to attend upon him, to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, and to participate in the recitation and rehearsal of the <s>Dharma</s>. As each group arrived, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would emit a radiance from his body and, by that display of radiance, would create lion-thrones for them. Having created them, he would seat those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> upon those thrones. Knowing they were seated, he would question them and engage them in inquiry regarding the detailed exposition of this very <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And no one else could see them, except the <s>Devaputras</s> of like aspiration. This is the reason, O monks, this is the cause, why the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would emit radiance from his body when the night was peaceful. //

body.text: na khalu punarbhikṣavo māyādevī bodhisattvakukṣigate gurukāyatāṃ saṃjānīte sma anyatra laghutāmeva mṛdutāmeva saukhyatāmeva / na codaragatāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavati sma / na ca rāgaparidāhena vā dveṣaparidāhena vā mohaparidāhena vā paridahyate sma / na ca kāmavitarkaṃ vā vyāpādavitarkaṃ vā vihiṃsāvitarkaṃ vā vitarkayati sma / na ca śītaṃ na coṣṇaṃ vā jighatsāṃ vā pipāsāṃ vā tamo vā rajo vā kleśaṃ vā saṃjānīte sma paśyati vā / na cāsyā amanāpā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśā vā ābhāsamāgacchanti sma / na ca pāpakān svapnān paśyati sma / na cāsyāḥ strīmāyā na śāṭhyaṃ nerṣyā na strīkleśā bādhante sma / pañcaśikṣāpadasamādattā khalu punaḥ śīlavatī daśakuśalakarmapathe pratiṣṭhitā tasmin samaye bodhisattvamātā bhavati sma / na ca bodhisattvamātuḥ kvacit puruṣe rāgacittamutpadyate sma, nāpi kasyacitpuruṣasya bodhisattvasya māturantike / ye ca kecitkapilāhvaye mahāpuravare anyeṣu vā janapadeṣu devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍabhūtāviṣṭāḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikā vā, te sarve bodhisattvamātuḥ sahadarśanādeva svasthāḥ smṛtipratilabdhā bhavanti sma / te cāmanuṣyāḥ kṣiprameva prakrāmanti sma / ye ca kecinnānārogaspṛṣṭāḥ sattvā bhavanti sma, vātapittaśleṣmasaṃnipātajai rogaiḥ pīḍyante sma, cakṣurogeṇa vā śrotrarogeṇa vā ghrāṇarogeṇa vā jihvārogeṇa vā oṣṭharogeṇa vā dantarogeṇa kaṇṭharogeṇa vā galagaṇḍarogeṇa vā uragaṇḍakuṣṭhakilāsaśoṣonmādāpasmārajvaragalagaṇḍapiṭakavisarpavicarcikādyai rogaiḥ saṃpīḍyante sma, teṣāṃ bodhisattvamātā dakṣiṇapāṇiṃ mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpayati sma / te sahapratiṣṭhāpite pāṇau vigatavyādhayo bhūtvā svakasvakāni gṛhāṇi gacchanti sma / antato māyādevī tṛṇagulmakamapi dharaṇitalādabhyutkṣipya glānebhyaḥ sattvebhyo 'nuprayacchati sma / te sahapratilambhādaroganirvikārā bhavanti sma / yadā ca māyādevī svaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ pratyavekṣate sma, tadā paśyati sma bodhisattvaṃ kukṣigatam, tadyathāpi nāma supariśuddha ādarśamaṇḍale mukhamaṇḍalaṃ dṛśyate / dṛṣṭvā ca punastuṣṭā udagrā āttamanā pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā bhavati sma //
body.translated_text: Moreover, O monks, <s>Māyādevī</s>, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in her womb, did not experience heaviness of body — only lightness, softness, and comfort. Nor did she experience pains in the belly. She was not burned by the torment of passion, or of hatred, or of delusion. She did not entertain thoughts of desire, or of ill-will, or of harming. She experienced and perceived neither cold, nor heat, nor hunger, nor thirst, nor darkness, nor dust, nor affliction. Unpleasant forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches did not come before her. She did not see evil dreams. She was not afflicted by women's deceitfulness, cunning, envy, or feminine vexations. She was one who had undertaken the five precepts, virtuous, established in the ten courses of wholesome action — such was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother at that time. And no lustful thought toward any man arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, nor did any man entertain [such a thought] toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother. And whatever beings in the great city called <s>Kapila</s> or in other territories — whether women, men, boys, or girls — who were possessed by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, or <s>Bhūtas</s>, they all, merely upon seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother, became well and recovered their mindfulness. And those non-human beings would swiftly depart. And whatever beings were afflicted by various diseases — tormented by ailments born of wind, bile, phlegm, or their combination; afflicted by diseases of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, lips, teeth, throat, goiter, rash, leprosy, vitiligo, consumption, madness, epilepsy, fever, boils, tumors, herpes, eczema, and other illnesses — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother would place her right hand upon their heads. And the moment her hand was placed [upon them], they became free from disease and went to their respective homes. Even if <s>Māyādevī</s> picked up [so much as] a blade of grass or a shrub from the ground and gave it to the sick beings, they became healthy and free from affliction the moment they received it. And whenever <s>Māyādevī</s> looked at her own right side, she would behold the <s>Bodhisattva</s> within her womb, just as one's face is seen in a well-polished mirror. And having seen him, she would be pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness. //

body.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarbhikṣavo mātuḥ kukṣigatasyādhiṣṭhitaṃ satataṃ samitaṃ rātriṃdivaṃ divyāni tūryāṇi abhi(nirmāya) pranadanti sma / divyāni ca puṣpāṇi abhipravarṣanti sma / kālena devā varṣanti sma / kālena vāyavo vānti sma / kālena ṛtavo nakṣatrāṇi ca parivartante sma / kṣemaṃ ca rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca sumanākulamanubhavati sma / sarve ca kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare śākyā anye ca sattvāḥ khādanti sma, pibanti sma, (ramante sma,) krīḍanti sma, pravicārayanti sma, dānāni ca dadanti sma, puṇyāni ca kurvanti sma, kaumodyāmiva cāturmāsyāmekāntare krīḍāsukhavihārairviharanti sma / rājāpi śuddhodanaḥ saṃprāptabrahmacaryoparatarāṣṭrakāryo 'pi supariśuddhastapovanagata iva dharmamevānuvartate sma //
body.translated_text: And further, O monks, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in his mother's womb, by his power, constantly, continuously, day and night, divine instruments would miraculously resound. Divine flowers would rain down. In due season the <s>Devas</s> would send rain. In due season the winds would blow. In due season the seasons and constellations would revolve. The kingdom was peaceful and prosperous, and the people were happy-minded. And all the <s>Śākyas</s> in the great city called <s>Kapilā</s>, and other beings, would eat, drink, take delight, play, go on excursions, give gifts, and perform meritorious deeds — they would dwell in the joy and ease of festivity as during a four-monthly <s>Kaumudī</s> festival, without interruption. And King <s>Śuddhodana</s> too, having undertaken the holy life and set aside the affairs of state, supremely purified, as if gone to a hermitage, devoted himself entirely to <s>dharma</s>. //

body.text: evaṃrūpeṇa bhikṣava ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt / tatra khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - drakṣyasi tvamānanda ratnavyūhaṃ bodhisattvaparibhogaṃ yatra bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato vyāhārṣīt / āha - paśyeyaṃ bhagavan paśyeyaṃ sugata / darśayati sma tathāgata āyuṣmata ānandasya śakrasya devānāmindrasya caturṇāṃ ca lokapālānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ ca devamanuṣyāṇām / dṛṣṭvā ca te tuṣṭā abhūvan udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātāḥ / sa ca brahmā sahāpatiḥ punareva brahmaloke samāropya pratiṣṭhāpayati sma caityārtham //
body.translated_text: Endowed with this kind of miraculous display, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Would you like to see, <s>Ānanda</s>, the jeweled array — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s dwelling — where the <s>Bodhisattva</s> resided in his mother's womb?' He said: 'I would see it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! I would see it, O <s>Sugata</s>!' The <s>Tathāgata</s> showed it to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, to <s>Śakra</s> the lord of gods, to the four <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), and to those other gods and humans. And having seen it, they were satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with rapture and gladness. And <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> once again raised it up and established it in the <s>Brahma</s>-world as a shrine. //

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavān punarapi bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma - iti hi bhikṣavo daśamāsakukṣigatena bodhisattvena ṣaṭtriṃśannayutāni devamanuṣyāṇāṃ triṣu yāneṣu paripācitānyabhūvan / yatredamucyate yat -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again addressed the monks: 'Thus, O monks, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was in the womb for ten months, thirty-six <s>nayutas</s> of gods and humans were ripened in the three vehicles.' Concerning this, it was said:

body.text: bodhisattva agrasattva mātukukṣisaṃsthitaḥ prakampitā ca ṣaḍvikāra medinī sakānanā / suvarṇavarṇa ābha mukta sarvāpāya śodhitā praharṣitāśca devasaṃgha dharmagañju bheṣyate // Lal_6.23 //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the foremost being, established in the mother's womb — the earth with its forests trembled in six ways; golden-hued light was emitted and all lower realms were purified, and the hosts of gods were delighted: 'He will be a treasury of <s>dharma</s>!' // Lal_6.23 //

children.text: suṃsaṃsthito mahāvimānu naikaratnacitrito yatra vīru āruhitva tiṣṭhate vināyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-established in a great palace adorned with manifold jewels, where the hero, the guide, ascended and abode —

children.text: gandhottamena candanena pūrito virocate yasyaikakarṣu trisahasramūlyaratnapūrito // Lal_6.24 //
children.translated_text: filled with the finest sandalwood fragrance, it shone; even a single fragment of which was worth the treasure of a trichiliocosm! // Lal_6.24 //

children.text: mahāsahasralokadhātu heṣvi bhindiyitvanā udāgato guṇākarasya padmaojabinduko /
children.translated_text: Splitting through the great trichiliocosm, there arose a drop of lotus-essence from the mine of virtues;

children.text: so saptarātra puṇyateja brahmaloki udgato gṛhītva brahma ojabindu bodhisattva nāmayī // Lal_6.25 //
children.translated_text: for seven nights it ascended to the <s>Brahma</s>-world by the splendor of merit, and <s>Brahmā</s>, having taken that drop of essence, dedicated it to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // Lal_6.25 //

children.text: na asti sarvasattvakāyi bhuktu yo jareya taṃ anyatra bhūri bodhisattva brahmakalpasaṃnibhe /
children.translated_text: There is no being in all the world who could consume and digest that [essence], save only the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is like <s>Brahmā</s> in extent;

children.text: anekakalpa puṇyateja ojabindu saṃsthito bhujitva sattva kāyacitta jñānaśuddha gacchiṣu // Lal_6.26 //
children.translated_text: established in the drop of essence produced by the splendor of merit of countless <s>kalpas</s>, having consumed it, beings would attain purity of body, mind, and knowledge. // Lal_6.26 //

children.text: śakra brahma lokapāla pūjanāya nāyakaṃ trīṇi kāla āgamitva bodhisattvamantikam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), to worship the leader, came three times [daily] into the presence of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>;

children.text: vandayitva pūjayitva dharma śṛṇute varaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ karitva sarva gacchiṣū yathāgatā // Lal_6.27 //
children.translated_text: having venerated and worshipped him, they heard the supreme <s>dharma</s>, performed circumambulation, and all departed as they had come. // Lal_6.27 //

children.text: bodhisattva dharmakāma enti lokadhātuṣu
children.translated_text: Those who desired <s>dharma</s> from the <s>Bodhisattva</s> came from [all] world-realms;

children.text: prabhāviyūha āsaneṣu te niṣaṇṇa dṛśyiṣu /
children.translated_text: they were seen seated on splendid, arrayed seats.

children.text: parasparaṃ ca śrutva dharma yānaśreṣṭhamuttamaṃ
children.translated_text: And having heard from one another the <s>dharma</s>, the supreme and foremost vehicle,

children.text: prayānti sarvi hṛṣṭacitta varṇamāla bhāṣato // Lal_6.28 //
children.translated_text: all departed with joyful hearts, speaking garlands of praise. // Lal_6.28 //

children.text: ye ca iṣṭidārakāsu duḥkhitā tadā abhūt bhūtaspṛṣṭa kṣiptacitta nagna pāṃśumrakṣitā /
children.translated_text: Those who at that time were afflicted at the crossroads — touched by spirits, deranged in mind, naked, covered in dust —

children.text: te ca sarva dṛṣṭva māya bhonti labdhacetanā smṛtīmatīgatīupeta gehi gehi gacchiṣu // Lal_6.29 //
children.translated_text: all of them, having seen [Queen] <s>Māyā</s>, regained their senses, and endowed with mindfulness, understanding, and good destiny, went home to their homes. // Lal_6.29 //

children.text: vātato va pittato va śleṣmasaṃnipātakaiḥ ye ca cakṣuroga śrotraroga kāyacittapīḍitā /
children.translated_text: Those afflicted by wind, or bile, or phlegm, or combinations thereof — those tormented by eye diseases, ear diseases, or bodily and mental afflictions,

children.text: naikarūpa naikajāti vyādhibhiśca ye hatā sthāpite sma māya mūrdhni pāṇi bhonti nirjarā // Lal_6.30 //
children.translated_text: those struck down by diseases of various forms and kinds — when <s>Māyā</s> placed her hand on their heads, they became free from illness. // Lal_6.30 //

children.text: athāpi vā tṛṇasya tūli bhūmito gṛhītvanā dadāti māya āturāṇa sarvi bhonti nirjarā /
children.translated_text: Or even taking a blade of grass or cotton from the ground, <s>Māyā</s> would give it to the sick, and all became free from illness;

children.text: saukhyaprāpti nirvikāra gehi gehi gacchiṣu bhaiṣajyabhūti vaidyarāji kukṣisaṃpratiṣṭhite // Lal_6.31 //
children.translated_text: attaining happiness, free from disturbance, they went home to their homes — [such] a source of medicine was the queen of physicians, with [the Bodhisattva] established in her womb! // Lal_6.31 //

children.text: yasmi kāli māyadevi svātanuṃ nirīkṣate adṛśāti bodhisattva kukṣiye pratiṣṭhitam /
children.translated_text: When Queen <s>Māyā</s> would look at her own body, she would see the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in her womb,

children.text: yathaiva candra antarīkṣa tārakai parīvṛtaṃ tathaiva nāthu bodhisattvalakṣaṇairalaṃkṛtam // Lal_6.32 //
children.translated_text: just as [one sees] the moon in the sky surrounded by stars, so too [she saw] the Lord, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, adorned with [the thirty-two] marks. // Lal_6.32 //

children.text: no ca tasya rāga doṣa naiva moha bādhate kāmachandu naiva tasya īrṣi naiva hiṃsitā /
children.translated_text: Neither desire, nor anger, nor delusion afflicted her; neither craving for sensual pleasures, nor envy, nor the wish to harm;

children.text: tuṣṭacitta hṛṣṭacitta prīti saumanasthitā kṣudhāpipāsa śīta uṣṇa naiva tasya bādhate // Lal_6.33 //
children.translated_text: with contented mind, joyful mind, abiding in rapture and gladness — neither hunger, thirst, cold, nor heat afflicted her. // Lal_6.33 //

children.text: aghaṭṭitāśca nityakāla divyatūrya vādiṣu pravarṣayanti divyapuṣpa gandhaśreṣṭha śobhanā /
children.translated_text: Without collision, at all times, divine instruments would play; supremely fragrant divine flowers would rain down;

children.text: deva paśyi mānuṣāśca mānuṣā amānuṣāṃ no viheṭhi no vihiṃsi tatra te parasyaram // Lal_6.34 //
children.translated_text: gods would see humans, and humans would see non-humans — none harassed, none harmed one another therein. // Lal_6.34 //

body.text: ramanti sattva krīḍayanti annapānudenti ca ānandaśabda ghoṣayanti hṛṣṭatuṣṭamānasāḥ //
body.translated_text: Beings took delight, played, and partook of food and drink; they resounded with cries of joy, their minds elated and contented.

body.text: kṣamā rajoanākulā ca kāli deva varṣate tṛṇāśca puṣpa oṣadhīya tasmi kāli rohiṣu // Lal_6.35 //
body.translated_text: The earth was free from dust and undisturbed, and in due season the gods sent rain; grasses, flowers, and medicinal herbs all thrived at that time. // Lal_6.35 //

children.text: rājagehi saptarātra ratnavarṣa varṣito yato daridrasattva gṛhya dāna denti bhuñjate /
children.translated_text: For seven nights a rain of jewels poured upon the royal palace, whereby destitute beings, taking [them] up, gave gifts and enjoyed [plenty];

children.text: nāsti sattva yo daridra yo ca āsi duḥkhito bherumūrdhni nandaneva eva sattva nandiṣu // Lal_6.36 //
children.translated_text: there was no being who was destitute, no one who was afflicted — like [the gods] in [the garden] <s>Nandana</s> upon the peak of [Mount] <s>Meru</s>, thus did beings rejoice! // Lal_6.36 //

children.text: so ca rāju śākiyāna poṣadhī upoṣito rājyakāryu no karoti dharmameva gocarī /
children.translated_text: And that king of the <s>Śākyas</s> observed the <s>poṣadha</s> (fast-day vow); he attended not to the affairs of the kingdom, but devoted himself solely to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: tapovanaṃ ca so praviṣṭa māyādevī pṛcchate kīdṛśenti kāyi saukhya agrasattva dhārati // Lal_6.37 //
children.translated_text: and he entered a hermitage, while <s>Māyādevī</s> was asked: 'What kind of bodily happiness does the foremost being sustain?' // Lal_6.37 //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare garbhāvakrāntiparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Descent into the Womb' (<s>Garbhāvakrāntiparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 7
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 7.

body.text: janmaparivartaḥ saptamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Seventh Chapter: On Birth (<s>Janmaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo daśamāseṣu nigateṣu bodhisattvasya janmakālasamaye pratyupasthite rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhodyāne dvātriṃśatpūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan / katamāni dvātriṃśat? sarvapuṣpāṇi suṅgībhūtāni na puṣpanti sma / puṣkariṇīṣu cotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāṇyabhyudgatāni kuḍmalībhūtāni na puṣpanti sma / tadā ca puṣpaphalavṛkṣā dharaṇītalādabhyudgamya kṣārakajātā na phalanti sma / aṣṭau ca ratnavṛkṣāḥ prādurabhūvan / viṃśati ca ratnanidhānaśatasahasrāṇyutplatya vyavasthitāni dṛśyante sma / antaḥpure ca ratnāṅkurāḥ prādurabhūvan / sugandhitailaparivāsitāśca gandhodakaśītoṣṇāḥ prasravanti sma / himavatparvatapārśvācca siṃhapotakā āgatyāgatyābhinadantaḥ kapilāhvayapuravaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya dvāramūleṣvavatiṣṭhante sma, na kaṃcitsattvaṃ viheṭhayanti sma / pañcaśatāni pāṇḍarāṇāṃ hastiśāvakānāmāgatya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāgrakaraiścaraṇāvabhilikhanti sma / mekhalībaddhakāśca devadārakā rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpure utsaṅgenotsaṅgamanuparivartamānāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / gaganatalagatārdhakāyā nāgakanyā nānāpūjopakaraṇaparigṛhītā adhyālambamānāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / daśa ca nāgakanyāsahasrāṇi mayūrāṅgahastakaparigṛhītā gagatatale 'vasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / daśa ca pūrṇakumbhasahasrāṇi kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkurvanti saṃdṛśyante sma / daśa ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi gandhodakabhṛṅgāraparigṛhītā mūrdhni dhārayantyo 'vasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / daśa ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi chatradhvajapatākāparigṛhītā avasthitāḥ saṃdṛśyate sma / bahūni cāpsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavaiḥ ghaṇṭāvasaktaiḥ pratīkṣamāṇānyavasthitāni saṃdṛśyante sma / sarve vāyavaścāvasthitā na vānti sma / sarvanadī ca prasravaṇāni ca na vahanti sma / candrasūryavimānāni nakṣatrajyotirgaṇāśca na vahanti sma / puṣyaṃ ca nakṣatrayuktamabhūt / ratnajālaparisphuṭaṃ ca rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhaṃ saṃsthitamabhūt / vaiśvānaraśca na jvalati sma / kūṭāgāraprāsādatoraṇadvārakataleṣu ca maṇiratnānyabhipralambamānāni ca saṃdṛśyante sma / dūṣyagañjāśca viviratnagañjāśca prāvṛtāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / kākolūkagṛdhravṛkaśṛgālaśabdāścāntarhitā abhūvan / sujātajātaśabdāśca śrūyante sma / sarvajanapadakarmāntāśca samucchinnā abhūvan / utkūlanikūlāśca pṛthivīpradeśāḥ samāḥ samavasthitāḥ sarvavīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakarathyāntarāpaṇamukhāni ca pāṇitalamṛṣṭānīva puṣpābhikīrṇāni virocante sma / sarvāśca gurviṇyaḥ samyaksukhena prasūyante sma / sarvaśālavanadevatāśca patreṣvardhakāyānabhinirmāya namyamānāḥ sthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma / imāni dvātriṃśatpūrvanimittāni prādurabhūvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when ten months had passed and the time of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth had arrived, thirty-two portents appeared in the garden of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s palace. What were the thirty-two? All flowers formed buds but did not bloom. In the lotus ponds, blue lotuses, red lotuses, night-lotuses, and white lotuses emerged but remained in bud and did not bloom. The fruit-bearing and flower-bearing trees rose up from the ground but only put forth alkaline sprouts and did not bear fruit. Eight jewel-trees appeared. Twenty hundred-thousands of jewel-treasuries, having risen up, stood visible. Within the inner palace, jewel-sprouts appeared. Streams of scented water, warm and cold, perfumed with fragrant oil, flowed forth. From the flanks of the <s>Himavat</s> mountain, young lions came again and again, roaring, circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilāhvaya</s>, and stationed themselves at the bases of the gates, yet they harmed no being. Five hundred young white elephants came and scratched at the feet of King <s>Śuddhodana</s> with their trunks. Divine children wearing girdles were seen moving about from lap to lap in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s inner palace. Half-bodied <s>Nāga</s> maidens, bearing various offerings, were seen hanging in the sky. Ten thousand <s>Nāga</s> maidens, holding peacock-feather fans, were seen standing in the sky. Ten thousand full vases were seen circumambulating the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Ten thousand divine maidens, holding pitchers of scented water, were seen standing with [them] on their heads. Ten thousand divine maidens, holding parasols, banners, and pennants, were seen standing [there]. Many hundreds of thousands of <s>Apsarases</s>, with conches, kettledrums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>paṇavas</s>, with bells attached, were seen standing in expectation. All winds ceased and did not blow. All rivers and springs ceased flowing. The chariots of the moon and sun, and the hosts of stars and luminaries, ceased moving. The <s>Puṣya</s> constellation was in conjunction. King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s palace was covered with a net of jewels. The household fire did not blaze. On the surfaces of the upper stories, palaces, arched gateways, and doors, jewels and gems were seen hanging forth. Treasure-stores of textiles and treasure-stores of various gems were seen open. The sounds of crows, owls, vultures, wolves, and jackals had vanished. The sounds of 'Well-born! Well-born!' were heard. All activities of the countryside had ceased. The uneven and steep places of the earth became level and evenly settled. All the streets, squares, crossroads, thoroughfares, and market-fronts shone as if polished smooth as the palm of the hand, strewn with flowers. All pregnant women gave birth safely and comfortably. All the forest deities of the <s>Śāla</s> groves were seen standing, bowing, having manifested half-bodies from the foliage. These thirty-two portents appeared. //

body.text: atha khalu māyādevī bodhisattvasya janmakālasamayaṃ jñātvā bodhisattvasyaiva tejonubhāvena rātryāṃ prathame yāme rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramya gāthābhirabhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Now <s>Māyādevī</s>, knowing that the time of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth had arrived, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own splendor and power, in the first watch of the night, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and addressed him in verses:

children.text: deva śṛṇu hi mahyaṃ bhāṣato yaṃ mataṃ me aciraciracireṇā jāta udyānabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: O lord, hear what I have to say — after so very long a time, a desire for the garden has arisen [in me];

children.text: yadi ca tava na roṣo naiva doṣo na mohaḥ kṣipramahu vrajeyā krīḍaudyānabhūmim // Lal_7.1 //
children.translated_text: if there is in you no anger, no fault, nor delusion, I would go quickly to the pleasure-ground of the garden! // Lal_7.1 //

children.text: tvamiha tapasi khinno dharmacittaprayukto ahu ca cirapraviṣṭā śuddhasattvaṃ dharentī /
children.translated_text: You here are wearied by austerity, devoted in mind to <s>dharma</s>; and I have long entered [the state of] bearing a pure being;

children.text: drumavara pratibuddhāḥ phullitā śālavṛkṣāḥ yukta bhaviya devā gantumudyānabhūmim // Lal_7.2 //
children.translated_text: the finest trees have awakened, the <s>Śāla</s> trees are in bloom — it is fitting, O lord, that we go to the garden-ground! // Lal_7.2 //

children.text: ṛtupravara vasanto yoṣitāṃ maṇḍanīyo bhramaravaravighuṣṭāḥ kokilabarhigītāḥ /
children.translated_text: The finest of seasons, spring, is the adornment of women; [the groves] resound with the humming of bees, with the songs of cuckoos and peacocks;

children.text: śuciruciravicitrā bhrāmyate puṣpareṇuḥ sādhu dadahi ājñāṃ gacchamo mā vilambaḥ // Lal_7.3 //
children.translated_text: the pure, charming, and variegated pollen of flowers drifts about — pray give the command, let us go without delay! // Lal_7.3 //

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitvā deviye pārthivendraḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard these words of the queen, the lord of the earth,

children.text: tuṣṭo muditacittaḥ pāriṣadyānavocat /
children.translated_text: satisfied and joyful in mind, said to [his] attendants:

children.text: hayagajarathaṃ paṅktyā vāhanā yojayadhvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Prepare horses, elephants, and chariots in procession!

children.text: pravaraguṇasamṛddhāṃ lumbinīṃ maṇḍayadhvam // Lal_7.4 //
children.translated_text: Adorn <s>Lumbinī</s>, endowed with the finest qualities and prosperity!' // Lal_7.4 //

children.text: nīlagirinikāśāṃ meghavarṇānubaddhāṃ viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ gajānām /
children.translated_text: 'Twenty thousand elephants, dark as blue mountains, bound together like clouds,

children.text: maṇikanakavicitrāṃ hemajālopagūḍhāṃ ghaṇṭarucirapārśvān ṣaḍviṣāṇāṃ gajendrān // Lal_7.5 //
children.translated_text: adorned with gems and gold, covered with golden nets, with bells on their lovely flanks, six-tusked bull-elephants — prepare them! // Lal_7.5 //

children.text: himarajatanikāśāṃ muñjakeśāṃ sukeśāṃ viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ hayānām /
children.translated_text: Twenty thousand horses, white as snow and silver, with <s>muñja</s>-manes, beautiful-maned,

children.text: kanakaracitapārśvā kiṅkiṇījālalambā pavanajavitavegā vāhanā pārthivasya // Lal_7.6 //
children.translated_text: with golden-wrought flanks, hung with nets of small bells, swift as the wind in speed — the mounts of the king — prepare them! // Lal_7.6 //

children.text: naragaṇa raṇaśauṇḍān śūra saṃgrāmakāmān asidhanuśaraśaktipāśakhaḍgāgrahastān /
children.translated_text: Warriors fierce in battle, heroes eager for combat, bearing swords, bows, arrows, spears, lassos, and swords in hand —

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasrān yojayadhvaṃ suśīghraṃ māya saparivārāṃ rakṣathā apramattā // Lal_7.7 //
children.translated_text: marshal twenty thousand swiftly! Guard <s>Māyā</s> with her retinue, be vigilant! // Lal_7.7 //

children.text: maṇikanakaniṣiktāṃ lumbinīṃ kārayadhvaṃ vividhavasanaratnaiḥ sarvavṛkṣāṃ pravethā /
children.translated_text: Prepare <s>Lumbinī</s>, inlaid with gems and gold; adorn all the trees with various garments and jewels;

children.text: vividhakusumacitraṃ nandanaṃ vā surāṇāṃ vadatha ca mama śīghraṃ sarvametaṃ vidhāya // Lal_7.8 //
children.translated_text: make it variegated with diverse flowers, like <s>Nandana</s> grove of the gods — and report to me quickly when all this has been done! // Lal_7.8 //

body.text: vacanamimu niśamyā pāriṣadyaiḥ kṣaṇena vāhana kṛta sajjā lumbinī maṇḍitā sā /
body.translated_text: Having heard this command, the attendants in an instant made the vehicles ready and <s>Lumbinī</s> was adorned;

body.text: pāriṣadya āha -
body.translated_text: The attendants said —

body.text: jaya jaya hi narendrā āyu pālehi dīrghaṃ sarva kṛtu yathoktaṃ kāru deva pratīkṣa // Lal_7.9 //
body.translated_text: Victory, victory, O king! May you live long! All has been done as commanded — behold, O lord! // Lal_7.9 //

children.text: so ca naravarendro hṛṣṭacitto bhavitvā gṛhavaramanuviṣṭo iṣṭikānevamāha /
children.translated_text: Then that best of kings, his mind delighted, having entered the excellent dwelling, spoke thus to his beloved ones:

children.text: yasya ahu manāpo yā ca me prītikāmā sā mi kuruta ājñāṃ maṇḍayitvātmabhāvam // Lal_7.10 //
children.translated_text: 'She who is dear to me and who desires my affection — fulfill my command, having adorned yourselves! // Lal_7.10 //

children.text: varasurabhisugandhāṃ bhāvaraṅgāṃ vicitrāṃ vasana mṛdumanojñāṃ prāvṛṇothā udagrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Put on the finest fragrant, colorful garments, soft and pleasing, with joy;

children.text: urasi vigalitānāṃ muktahārā bhavethā ābharaṇavibhūṣāṃ darśayethādya sarvāḥ // Lal_7.11 //
children.translated_text: let pearl necklaces hang loose upon your breasts — display all your ornamental adornments today! // Lal_7.11 //

children.text: tuṇapaṇavamṛdaṅgāṃ vīṇaveṇūmukuṇḍāṃ tūryaśatasahasrān yojayadhvaṃ manojñāṃ /
children.translated_text: Prepare hundreds of thousands of delightful musical instruments — drums, <s>paṇavas</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>vīṇās</s>, flutes, and <s>mukuṇḍas</s>;

children.text: bhūya kuruta harṣaṃ devakanyāna yūyaṃ śrutva madhuraghoṣaṃ devatāpi spṛheyuḥ // Lal_7.12 //
children.translated_text: furthermore, create joy for the divine maidens among you — hearing such sweet sounds, even the gods would feel longing! // Lal_7.12 //

children.text: ekarathavaresmiṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ māyadevī mā ca puruṣa istrī anya tatrāruheyā /
children.translated_text: Let <s>Māyādevī</s> stand in one excellent chariot alone — let no other man or woman mount that [chariot];

children.text: nāri vividhavarmā taṃ rathaṃ vāhayantāṃ mā ca pratikūlaṃ mā manāpaṃ śruṇeṣyā // Lal_7.13 //
children.translated_text: let women clad in various armor drive that chariot — let nothing disagreeable or unpleasant be heard! // Lal_7.13 //

children.text: hayagajarathapattīṃ sainyaśrīmadvicitrāṃ dvāri sthita nṛpasyā śrūyate uccaghoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Horses, elephants, chariots, and infantry — the splendid and variegated army — standing at the king's gate, loud sounds are heard;

children.text: kṣubhitajalanidhirvā śrūyate eva śabdo * * * * // Lal_7.14 //
children.translated_text: like a churning ocean is the sound heard * * * * // Lal_7.14 //

body.text: māya yada gṛhāto nirgatā dvāramūlaṃ ghaṇṭa śatasahasrā tāḍitā maṅgalārtham // Lal_7.15 //
body.translated_text: When <s>Māyā</s> emerged from the house to the gateway, a hundred thousand bells were struck for the auspicious occasion. // Lal_7.15 //

children.text: so ca ratha vicitro maṇḍitaḥ pārthivena api ca marusahasrairdivyasiṃhāsanebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That variegated chariot, adorned by the king, and also by thousands of gods with divine lion-thrones,

children.text: caturi ratanavṛkṣā patrapuṣpopapetā abhinaditamanojñāṃ haṃsakrauñcān mayūrān // Lal_7.16 //
children.translated_text: with four jewel-trees bearing leaves and flowers, resounding delightfully with swans, cranes, and peacocks — // Lal_7.16 //

children.text: chatradhvajapatākāścocchritā vaijayantyaḥ kiṅkiṇivarajālaiśchāditaṃ divyavastraiḥ /
children.translated_text: parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards raised aloft, covered with nets of the finest bells and divine garments;

children.text: maruvadhu gaganesmiṃ taṃ rathaṃ prekṣayante divyamadhuraghoṣaṃ śrāvayantyaḥ stuvanti // Lal_7.17 //
children.translated_text: the celestial maidens in the sky gaze at that chariot, sounding sweet divine music and singing praises. // Lal_7.17 //

children.text: upaviśati yadā sā māya siṃhāsanāgre pracalita trisahasrā medinī ṣaḍvikāram /
children.translated_text: When that <s>Māyā</s> sat upon the lion-throne, the great earth trembled in the trichiliocosm with six kinds of quaking;

children.text: puṣpa maru kṣipiṃsū ambarāṃ bhrāmayiṃsū adya jagati śreṣṭho jāyate lumbinīye // Lal_7.18 //
children.translated_text: the gods scattered flowers in the sky and whirled [them about]: 'Today the foremost in the world is born in <s>Lumbinī</s>!' // Lal_7.18 //

children.text: caturi jagatipālāstaṃ rathaṃ vāhayante tridaśapatirapīndro mārgaśuddhiṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: The four world-guardians drive that chariot; <s>Indra</s>, lord of the thirty-three, clears the path;

children.text: brahma puratu gacchī durjanāṃ vārayanto amaraśatasahasrāḥ prāñjalīkā namante // Lal_7.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> goes before, warding off evil beings; hundreds of thousands of immortals bow with palms joined. // Lal_7.19 //

children.text: nṛpati muditacitto vīkṣate tāṃ viyūhāṃ tasya bhavati evaṃ vyakta yaṃ devadevo /
children.translated_text: The king, his mind delighted, beholds that splendid array; this thought arises in him: 'Surely this is a God of gods,

children.text: yasya caturi pālā brahma sendrāśca devāḥ kuruta vipulapūjāṃ vyakta yaṃ śuddhabhāvī // Lal_7.20 //
children.translated_text: for whom the four guardians, <s>Brahmā</s>, the gods with <s>Indra</s>, perform vast worship — surely this [child] will be of supremely pure nature!' // Lal_7.20 //

children.text: nāsti tribhavi sattvo yaḥ sahetpūjametāṃ deva atha ca nāgāḥ śakra brahmā ca pālāḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no being in the three realms who could endure such worship — gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the guardians —

children.text: mūrdha tada phaleyā jīvitaṃ cāsya naśyet ayu puna atidevaḥ sarvapūjāṃ sahāti // Lal_7.21 //
children.translated_text: his head would burst and his life would perish; but this one who is beyond the gods endures all worship! // Lal_7.21 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo māyādevī caturaśītyā hayarathasahasraiḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaiḥ parivṛtā caturaśītyā gajarathasahasraiḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaiḥ caturaśītyā ca pattisahasraiḥ śūrairvīrairvarāṅgarūpibhiḥ susaṃnaddhadṛḍhavarmakavacitairanuparigṛhītā ṣaṣṭyā ca śākyakanyāsahasraiḥ puraskṛtā catvāriṃśatā ca sahasrai
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Māyādevī</s>, surrounded by eighty-four thousand horse-chariots adorned with all ornaments, eighty-four thousand elephant-chariots adorned with all ornaments, eighty-four thousand infantry — heroes, valiant ones, of beautiful form, well-armored with strong armor and mail — attended by sixty thousand <s>Śākya</s> maidens going before her, guarded by forty thousand

body.text: rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya jñātikulaprasūtaiḥ śākyaiḥ vṛddhadaharamadhyamaiḥ saṃrakṣitā, ṣaṣṭyā ca sahasrai rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpureṇa gītavādyasamyaktūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena parivṛtā, caturaśītyā ca devakanyāsahasraiḥ parivṛtā, caturaśītyā ca nāgakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā ca gandharvakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā ca kinnarakanyāsahasraiḥ caturaśītyā cāsurakanyāsahasraiḥ nānāvyūhālaṃkārālaṃkṛtābhiḥ nānāgītavādyavarṇabhāṣiṇībhiranugamyamānā niryāti sma / sarvaṃ ca lumbinīvanaṃ gandhodakasiktaṃ divyapuṣpābhikīrṇīkṛtamabhūt / sarvavṛkṣāśca tasmin vanavare akālapatrapuṣpaphalāni dadanti sma / devaiśca tathā tadvanaṃ samalaṃkṛtamabhūt tadyathāpi nāma miśrakāvanaṃ devānāṃ samalaṃkṛtam //
body.translated_text: <s>Śākyas</s> born from the kinsmen-families of King <s>Śuddhodana</s> — elders, youths, and those of middle age — surrounded by sixty thousand women of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s inner palace with songs, music, well-tuned instruments, cymbals, and singing being played, surrounded by eighty-four thousand divine maidens, eighty-four thousand <s>Nāga</s> maidens, eighty-four thousand <s>Gandharva</s> maidens, eighty-four thousand <s>Kinnara</s> maidens, and eighty-four thousand <s>Asura</s> maidens — adorned with various arrays of ornaments, singing various songs and speaking melodious words — she set forth. And the entire <s>Lumbinī</s> grove was sprinkled with scented water and strewn with divine flowers. All the trees in that excellent grove bore untimely leaves, flowers, and fruits. And the gods had adorned that grove just as the <s>Miśraka</s> grove of the gods is adorned.

body.text: atha khalu māyādevī lumbinīvanamanupraviśya tasmādrathavarādavatīrya naramarukanyāparivṛtā vṛkṣeṇa vṛkṣaṃ paryaṭantī vanādvanaṃ caṃkramyamāṇā drumād drumaṃ nirīkṣamāṇā anupūrveṇa yenāsau plakṣo mahādrumaratnavarapravaraḥ suvibhaktaśākhaḥ samapatramañjarīdharo divyamānuṣyanānāpuṣpasaṃpuṣpito varapravarasurabhigandhinānāgandhinānāraṅgavastrābhipralambito vividhamaṇivicitraprabhojjvalitaḥ sarvaratnamūladaṇḍaśākhāpatrasamalaṃkṛtaḥ suvibhaktavistīrṇaśākhaḥ karatalanibhe bhūmibhāge suvibhaktavistīrṇanīlatṛṇamayūragrīvāsaṃnibhe kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśe dharaṇītale saṃsthitaḥ pūrvajinajanetryābhinivāsitaḥ devasaṃgītyanugītaḥ śubhavimalaviśuddhaḥ śuddhāvāsadevaśatasahasraiḥ praśāntacittairabhinatajaṭāmakuṭāvalambitāvanatamūrdhabhirabhinandyamānastaṃ plakṣavṛkṣamupajagāma //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, having entered the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove and descended from that excellent chariot, surrounded by human and divine maidens, wandering from tree to tree, walking from grove to grove, gazing from bough to bough, gradually approached that <s>plakṣa</s> tree — the supreme, most excellent, great jewel-tree — with well-spread branches, bearing even leaves and flower-clusters, blooming with various divine and human flowers, draped with garments of supremely fragrant various scents and various colors, radiant with the brilliance of diverse, variegated gems, adorned with all precious stones on its trunk, branches, and leaves, with well-spread, broad branches, standing on a ground-surface smooth as the palm of the hand, on earth soft, broad, green, of the hue of a peacock's neck, pleasant to touch like <s>Kācilinḍika</s> cloth — a place where the mothers of former <s>Jinas</s> had dwelt, celebrated in divine songs, auspicious, stainless, and pure — being praised with bowed heads and bent matted crowns by hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods of pacified minds — she approached that <s>plakṣa</s> tree.

body.text: atha sa plakṣavṛkṣo bodhisattvasya tejonubhāvenāvanamya praṇamati sma / atha māyādevī gaganatalagateva vidyut dṛṣṭiṃ dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasārya plakṣaśākhāṃ gṛhītvā salīlaṃ gaganatalaṃ prekṣamāṇā vijṛmbhamānā sthitābhūt / atha tasmin samaye ṣaṣṭyapsaraḥśatasahasrāṇi kāmāvacaradevebhya upasaṃkramya māyādevyā upasthāne paricaryāṃ kurvanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>plakṣa</s> tree, by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s splendor, bent down in homage. Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, her gaze [directed] upward like lightning in the sky, extending her right arm and grasping a branch of the <s>plakṣa</s>, stood playfully gazing at the sky, stretching. At that moment, sixty <s>koṭis</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Apsarases</s> from the desire-realm gods approached and rendered service in attendance upon <s>Māyādevī</s>.

body.text: evaṃrūpeṇa khalu puna ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt / sa paripūrṇānāṃ daśānāṃ māsānāmatyayena māturdakṣiṇapārśvānniṣkramati sma smṛtaḥ saṃprajānannanupalipto garbhamalairyathā nānyaḥ kaściducyate 'nyeṣāṃ garbhamala iti //
body.translated_text: Endowed with such miraculous display, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb. At the completion of ten full months, he emerged from his mother's right side — mindful, fully aware, unstained by the impurities of the womb — as no other being is said [to be unstained] by what are called womb-impurities of others.

body.text: tasmin khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samaye śakro devānāmindro brahmā ca sahāpatiḥ purataḥ sthitāvabhūtām, yau bodhisattvaṃ paramagauravajātau divyakāśikavastrāntaritaṃ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaiḥ smṛtau saṃprajñau pratigṛhṇāte sma //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> stood before [him] — those two, filled with supreme reverence, received the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, wrapped in divine <s>Kāśika</s> cloth, with all his limbs and minor limbs [perfect], mindful and fully aware.

body.text: yasmiṃśca kūṭāgāre bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣigato 'sthāt, taṃ brahmā sahāpatirbrahmakāyikāśca devaputrā abhyutkṣipya brahmalokaṃ caityārthaṃ pūjārthaṃ copanāmayāmāsuḥ / aparigṛhītaḥ khalu punarbodhisattvaḥ kenacinmanuṣyabhūtena, atha tahi bodhisattvaṃ devatāḥ prathamataraṃ pratigṛhṇanti sma //
body.translated_text: The mansion in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had dwelt in his mother's womb — <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s> lifted it up and transported it to <s>Brahmaloka</s> as a shrine and object of worship. Indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was not received by any human being; rather, the deities received the <s>Bodhisattva</s> first.

body.text: atha bodhisattvo jātamātraḥ pṛthivyāmavatarati sma / samanantarāvatīrṇasya ca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāpṛthivīṃ bhittvā mahāpadmaṃ prādurabhūt / nandopanandau ca nāgarājānau gaganatale 'rdhakāyau
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just born, descended upon the earth. Immediately upon the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s descent, a great lotus appeared, bursting through the great earth. And the two <s>Nāga</s> kings, <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, standing half-bodied in the sky,

body.text: sthitvā śītoṣṇe dve vāridhāre 'bhinirbhiṃttvā bodhisattvaṃ snāpayataḥ sma / śakrabrahmalokapālāḥ pūrvaṃgamāścānye ca bahavo devaputrāḥ śatasahasrā ye bodhisattvaṃ jātamātraṃ nānāgandhodakamuktakusumaiḥ snāpayantyabhyavakiranti sma / antarikṣe ca dve cāmare ratnacchatraṃ ca prādurbhūtam / sa tasmin mahāpadme sthitvā caturdiśamavalokayati sma / (caturdiśamavalokya) siṃhāvalokitaṃ mahāpuruṣāvalokitaṃ vyavalokayati sma //
body.translated_text: releasing two streams of water, warm and cool, bathed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-guardians going before, and many other hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s> bathed and showered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just born, with various scented waters and scattered flowers. And in the sky, two fly-whisks and a jewel-parasol appeared. Standing on that great lotus, he surveyed the four directions. Having surveyed the four directions, he made the lion-gaze, the great-being gaze.

body.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ samaye bodhisattvaḥ pūrvakuśalamūlavipākajenāpratihatena divyacakṣuprādurbhūtena divyena cakṣuṣā sarvāvantaṃ trisāhastraṃ mahāsāhastraṃ lokadhātuṃ sanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṃ sadevamānuṣaṃ paśyati sma / sarvasattvānāṃ ca cittacaritaṃ ca prajānāti sma / jñātvā ca vyavalokayati sma - asti tvasau kaścitsattvo yo mayā sadṛśaḥ śīlena vā samādhinā vā prajñayā vā kuśalamūlacaryayā vā / yadā ca bodhisattvaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau na kaṃcitsattvamātmatulyaṃ paśyati sma, atha tasminsamaye bodhisattvaḥ siṃha iva vigatabhayabhairavo 'saṃtrastaḥ astambhī sucintitaṃ smṛtvā cintayitvā sarvasattvānāṃ cittacaritāni jñātvā aparigṛhīto bodhisattvaḥ pūrvāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ - pūrvaṃgamo bhaviṣyāmi sarveṣāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ dharmāṇām / tasya prakramata uparyantarīkṣe 'parigṛhītaṃ divyaśvetavipulachatraṃ cāmaraśubhe gacchantamanugacchanti sma - yatra yatra ca bodhisattvaḥ padamutkṣipati sma, tatra tatra padmāni prādurbhavanti sma / dakṣiṇāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ - dakṣiṇīyo bhaviṣyāmi devamanuṣyāṇām / paścimāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakāntaḥ / saptame sthitvā siṃha ivāhlādanātmikāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate sma - ahaṃ loke jyeṣṭho 'haṃ loke śreṣṭhaḥ / iyaṃ me paścimā jātiḥ / kariṣyāmi jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasyāntam / uttarāṃ diśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ - anuttaro bhaviṣyāmi sarvasattvānām / adhastāddiśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ - nihaniṣyāmi māraṃ ca mārasenāṃ ca / sarvanairayikāṇāṃ ca nirayāgnipratighātāya saha dharmameghavṛṣṭiṃ varṣiṣyāmi, yena te sukhasamarpitā bhaviṣyanti / upariṣṭāddiśamabhimukhaḥ sapta padāni prakrāntaḥ, urdhvaṃ cāvalokayati sma - ullokanīyo bhaviṣyāmi sarvasattvānām / samanantarabhāṣitā ceyaṃ bodhisattvena vākū / atha tasmin samaye ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ svareṇābhivijñāpto 'bhūt / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya karmavipākajā abhijñādharmatā //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the unobstructed divine eye arisen through the ripening of prior wholesome roots, beheld with that divine eye the entire trichiliocosmic world-system with its cities, towns, villages, kingdoms, and royal capitals, together with its gods and humans. He also knew the mental conduct of all beings. Having known, he surveyed [thus]: 'Is there any being who is equal to me in morality, or in concentration, or in wisdom, or in the practice of wholesome roots?' When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw no being in the trichiliocosmic world-system equal to himself, then at that time the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like a lion — fearless, intrepid, unfrightened, unshaken — having recalled well-considered [truths], having reflected, having known the mental conduct of all beings, unreceived [by any human], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> strode seven steps facing the eastern direction — 'I shall be the foremost of all wholesome-root <s>dharmas</s>.' As he strode, above in the sky an unattended divine white broad parasol and two auspicious fly-whisks followed the one who walked — and wherever the <s>Bodhisattva</s> raised his foot, there lotuses appeared. He strode seven steps facing the southern direction — 'I shall be worthy of offerings from gods and humans.' He strode seven steps facing the western direction. Standing at the seventh, like a lion he uttered a jubilant voice: 'I am the eldest in the world; I am the foremost in the world. This is my final birth. I shall make an end of the suffering of birth, old age, and death.' He strode seven steps facing the northern direction — 'I shall be unsurpassed among all beings.' He strode seven steps facing the downward direction — 'I shall defeat <s>Māra</s> and <s>Māra</s>'s army. And for all hell-beings, to quench the fires of hell, I shall rain a <s>Dharma</s>-cloud together [with them], by which they shall become established in happiness.' He strode seven steps facing the upward direction, and gazed upward — 'I shall be looked up to by all beings.' No sooner had this word been spoken by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> than at that moment this trichiliocosmic world-system was made aware by [his] voice. This is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>abhijñā</s>-<s>dharmatā</s>, born from the ripening of <s>karma</s>.

body.text: yadā bodhisattvaścaramabhavika upajāyate, yadā cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate, tadā asyemānyevaṃrūpāṇi ṛddhiprātihāryāṇi bhavanti - tasmin khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samaye saṃhṛṣitaromakūpajātāḥ sarvasattvā abhūvan / mahataśca pṛthivīcālasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt bhairavasya romaharṣaṇasya / aghaṭṭitāni ca divyamānuṣyakāni tūryāṇi saṃpravāditāni / sarvartukālikāśca
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is born in his final existence, and when he attains unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), then such miraculous displays of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) occur for him — Indeed, O monks, at that time, all beings became thrilled with their hair standing on end. And a great earthquake, fearsome and hair-raising, appeared in the world. And untouched divine and human musical instruments sounded forth of their own accord. And trees of every season in that

body.text: vṛkṣāstasmin samaye trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau saṃkusumitāḥ phalitāśca / viśuddhācca gaganatalānmeghaśabdaḥ śrūyate sma / apagatameghācca gaganācchanaiḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmo devaḥ pravarṣati sma / nānāvarṣadivyakusumavastrābharaṇagandhacūrṇavyāmiśrāḥ paramasukhasaṃsparśāśca saumyāḥ sugandhavātāḥ pravāyanti sma / vyapagatatamorajodhūmanīhārāśca sarvadiśaḥ suprasannā virājante sma / upariṣṭāccāntarikṣādadṛśyā gambhīrā mahābrahmaghoṣāḥ saṃśrūyante sma / sarvacandrasūryaśakrabrahmalokapālaprabhāścābhibhūtā abhūvan / paramasukhasaṃsparśayā ca sarvasattvakāyacittasukhasaṃjananyā lokottarayā anekaśatasahasravarṇaprabhayā sarvatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ parisphuṭo 'bhūt / samantarajātasya khalu punarbodhisattvasyaikāntasukhasamarpitāḥ sarvasattvā babhūvuḥ / sarvarāgadveṣamohadarpārativiṣādabhayalobherṣyāmātsaryavigatāḥ sarvākuśalakriyāprativiratā vyādhitānāṃ sattvānāṃ vyādhaya upaśāntāḥ / kṣutpipāsitānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣutpipāsā prasrabdhābhūt / madyamadamattānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ madāpagamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / unmattaiśca smṛtiḥ pratilabdhā / cakṣurvikalaiśca sattvaiścakṣuḥ pratilabdham, śrotravikalaiśca sattvaiḥ śrotram / aṅgapratyaṅgavikalendriyāścāvikalendriyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ / daridraiśca dhanāni pratilabdhāni / bandhanabaddhāśca bandhanebhyo vimuktāḥ / āvīcimādiṃ kṛtvā sarvanairayikāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvakāraṇād duḥkhaṃ tasminsamaye prasrabdham / tiyagyonikānāmanyonyabhakṣaṇādi duḥkham, yamalokikānāṃ sattvānāṃ kṣutpipāsādiduḥkhaṃ vyupaśāntamabhūt //
body.translated_text: <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) at that time burst into blossom and bore fruit. And from the pure vault of the sky a cloud-sound was heard. And from the cloudless sky a gentle, exceedingly fine divine rain fell. Showers of various divine flowers, garments, ornaments, fragrant powders were mingled [in the air], and gentle, fragrant breezes blew, supremely pleasant to the touch. And all directions, freed from darkness, dust, smoke, and mist, shone forth clear and radiant. And from above, from the sky, invisible, deep, great <s>Brahma</s>-sounds were heard. And the radiances of all the moons, suns, <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-guardians were outshone. And by a transcendent radiance of countless hundreds of thousands of colors, supremely pleasant to the touch, generating bodily and mental happiness for all beings, the entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s> (billion-world system) was pervaded. Indeed, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, all beings were established in supreme bliss. Free from all passion, hatred, delusion, pride, discontent, dejection, fear, greed, envy, and miserliness, they desisted from all unwholesome actions. The diseases of sick beings were pacified. The hunger and thirst of hungry and thirsty beings subsided. The intoxication of those maddened by drink was dispelled. The mad recovered their mindfulness. Beings blind in their eyes regained sight; those deaf in their ears regained hearing. Those whose limbs, sub-limbs, or faculties were impaired became whole. The poor obtained wealth. Those bound in chains were freed from their bonds. Beginning with <s>Avīci</s>, the suffering of all hell-beings from every torment subsided at that time. The suffering of animals — devouring one another and so forth — and the suffering of hunger, thirst, and the like for beings in the world of <s>Yama</s> was pacified. //

body.text: yadā ca bodhisattvo jātamātraḥ sapta padāni prakrānto 'bhūt, asaṃkhyeyākalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasraiḥ sucaritacaraṇairmahāvīryamahāsthāmadharmatāpratilambhena tasmin samaye daśadiglokadhātusthitā buddhā bhagavantastaṃ pṛthvīpradeśaṃ vajramayadhitiṣṭhanti sma / yena mahāpṛthivī tasmin pradeśe nāvatīryata, tāvanmahābalavegasamanvāgato hi bhikṣavo jātamātro bodhisattvaḥ sapta padāni prakrānto 'bhūt / sarvalokāntarikāśca tasmin samaye mahatāvabhāsena sphuṭā abhūvan / mahāṃśca tasmin samaye gītaśabdo 'bhūnnṛtyaśabdaḥ / aprameyāśca tasmin samaye puṣpacūrṇagandhamālyaratnābharaṇavastrameghā abhipravarṣanti sma / paramasukhasamarpitāśca sarvasattvā abhūvan / saṃkṣepādacintyā sā kriyābhūt, yadā bodhisattvo loke prādurabhūt sarvalokābhyudgataḥ //
body.translated_text: And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just born, had taken seven steps — by immeasurable <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of meritorious deeds and the attainment of great vigor, great strength, and <s>dharmatā</s> — at that time, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> abiding in the world-systems of the ten directions made that spot of earth diamond-firm.
