Thus the great earth did not sink at that spot, for, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just born, endowed with such great force and momentum, had taken seven steps. And all the inter-world spaces (<s>lokāntarikā</s>) at that time were pervaded with a great radiance. And at that time there was a great sound of singing and dancing. And immeasurable clouds of flower-powders, fragrances, garlands, jewels, ornaments, and garments rained down at that time. And all beings were established in supreme bliss. In brief, that deed was inconceivable — when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> appeared in the world, exalted above all worlds. //

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat - sarvasattvānāṃ bhagavaṃstathāgata āścaryabhūto 'bhūt, bodhisattvabhūt evādbhutadharmasamanvāgataśca / kaḥ punarvādaḥ evaṃ hyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / eṣo 'haṃ bhagavaṃścatuṣpañcakṛtvo 'pi daśakṛtvo 'pi yāvatpañcāśatkṛtvo 'pi śatakṛtvo 'pi yāvadanekaśatasahasraśo 'pyahaṃ bhagavan buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, extended his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, was a wonder for all beings. Even as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he was endowed with marvelous qualities. What then need be said of [the time when] he attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)? I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> — four times, five times, ten times, up to fifty times, a hundred times, up to many hundreds of thousands of times — I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>!' //

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat - bhaviṣyanti khalu punarānanda anāgate 'dhvani kecidbhikṣavo 'bhāvitakāyā abhāvitacittā abhāvitaśīlā abhāvitaprajñā bālā apaṇḍitā ābhimānikā uddhatā unnatā asaṃvṛtā vikṣiptacittāḥ kāṅkṣāparīttā vicikitsābahulā aśraddhāḥ śramaṇamalāḥ śramaṇapratirūpakāḥ / te na śraddāsyanti imāmevaṃrūpāṃ bodhisattvasya garbhāvakrāntipariśuddhim / te 'nyonyamekānte saṃnipātyaivaṃ vakṣyanti - paśyata bho yūyametadapūjyamānaṃ bodhisattvasya kila mātuḥ kukṣigatasyoccāraprasrāvamaṇḍoparimiśrasya īdṛśī vibhūtirāsīt / sa ca kila abhiniṣkrāman māturdakṣiṇāyāḥ kukṣeranupalipto garbhamalenābhūditi / kathametadyojyate? na punaste mohapuruṣā evaṃ jñāsyanti - na sukṛtakarmaṇāṃ sattvānāmuccāraprasrāvamaṇḍe kāyaḥ saṃbhavatīti / bhadrikā khalvapi tathārūpāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ garbhāvakrāntirbhavati / garbhāvasthitaśca sattvānukampayā hi bodhisattvo manuṣyaloke upapadyate, na devabhūta eva dharmacakraṃ pravartayati / tatkasmāt? mā khalvānanda sattvāḥ kausīdyamāpatsyante / devabhūtaḥ sa bhagavān tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, vayaṃ tu manuṣyamātrāḥ / na vayaṃ samarthāstatsthānaṃ paripūrayitumiti kausīdyamāpadyeran / na khalu punasteṣāṃ mohapuruṣāṇāṃ dharmastainyakānāmevaṃ bhaviṣyati - acintyo hi sa sattvaḥ, nāsāvasmābhiḥ prāmāṇikaḥ kartavya iti / api tu khalvānanda buddhaṛddhiprātihāryamapi te tasmin kāle nāvakalpayiṣyanti, kimaṅga punarbodhisattvabhūtasya tathāgatasya bodhisattvaprātihāryāṇi / paśya ānanda kiyantaṃ te mohapuruṣā bahvapuṇyābhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskariṣyanti, ye buddhadharmān pratikṣepsyanti lābhasatkāraślokābhibhūtā uccāralagnā lābhasatkārābhibhūtā itarajātīyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the future there will be certain monks — undeveloped in body, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in morality, undeveloped in wisdom — foolish, unlearned, conceited, agitated, proud, unrestrained, distracted in mind, of meager faith, full of doubt, faithless, blemishes upon the <s>Śramaṇa</s> order, mere imitations of <s>Śramaṇas</s>. They will not believe in this purity of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s conception (<s>garbhāvakrānti</s>). Meeting together in private, they will say thus: "Look, sirs, at this absurdity — while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was supposedly in his mother's womb, mixed with feces, urine, and filth, such splendor was his! And he, supposedly emerging from the mother's right side, was unstained by the impurities of the womb! How can this be reconciled?" But those deluded men will not understand this: that for beings whose actions are meritorious, the body does not originate in feces, urine, and filth. Indeed, the conception of such beings is auspicious. And though the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established in the womb, it is out of compassion for beings that he takes birth in the human world — he does not turn the Wheel of <s>Dharma</s> while remaining a god. Why? Lest, <s>Ānanda</s>, beings fall into laziness, [thinking]: "That <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is a god; we are mere humans. We are unable to fulfill that station" — and so fall into indolence. But those deluded men, those thieves of the <s>Dharma</s>, will not think thus: "That being is inconceivable; he is not to be measured by us." Rather, <s>Ānanda</s>, at that time they will not accept even the miraculous displays of the <s>Buddha</s> — how much less the miraculous displays of the <s>Tathāgata</s> while he was still a <s>Bodhisattva</s>! See, <s>Ānanda</s>, how great an accumulation of demerit those deluded men will generate — they who will reject the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, overpowered by gain and honor, attached to excrement [i.e., material things], overwhelmed by gain and honor, of inferior birth!' //

body.text: ānanda āha - mā maivaṃrūpā bhagavan anāgate 'dhvani bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti ya imāmevaṃ bhadrikāṃ sūtrāntāṃ pratikṣepsyanti pratipakṣaṃ pakṣanti ca //
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'May there not be, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, such monks in the future who will reject this auspicious <s>sūtrānta</s> and oppose it!' //

body.text: bhagavānāha - evaṃrūpāśca te ānanda sūtrāntāṃ prapikṣepsyanti, prativakṣyanti cānekaprakārān cānyān pāpakānabhisaṃskārānabhisaṃskariṣyanti / anarthikāśca te śrāmaṇyena bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Such men, <s>Ānanda</s>, will reject these <s>sūtrāntas</s>, will speak against them, and will generate many other kinds of evil <s>saṃskāras</s>. And they will be without purpose in the <s>Śramaṇa</s> life.' //

body.text: ānanda āha - kā punarbhagavan teṣāṃ tathārūpāṇāmasatpuruṣāṇāṃ gatirbhaviṣyati? ko 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ?
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'What then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, will be the destiny of such evil men? What will be their future state?' //

body.text: bhagavānāha - yā gatirbuddhabodhimantardhāyāpyatītānāgatapratyutpannāṃśca buddhān bhagavato 'tyākhyāya tāṃ te gatiṃ gamiṣyanti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The destiny of those who obstruct the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s> and who revile the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> of the past, future, and present — that destiny they will go to.' //

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandaḥ saṃharṣitaromakūpajāto namo buddhāya ityuktvā bhagavantametadavocatmūrchā me bhagavan kāyasyābhūdimaṃ teṣāmasatpuruṣāṇāṃ samudācāraṃ śrutvā //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, his hair standing on end with emotion, having said '<s>Namo Buddhāya</s>' (Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>), spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have become faint in body, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, upon hearing the conduct of those evil men.' //

body.text: bhagavānāha - na teṣāmānanda samācāro bhaviṣyati / viṣamasamudācārāḥ khalu punaste sattvā bhaviṣyanti / te tena viṣamena samudācāreṇavīcau mahānarake prapatiṣyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? ye kecidānanda bhikṣavo vā bhikṣuṇyo vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntān śrutvā nādhimokṣyanti na śraddhāsyanti na prativetsyanti, te cyutāḥ samānā avīcau mahānarake prapatiṣyanti / mā ānanda tathāgatāprāmāṇikaṃ akārṣuḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? aprameyo hyānanda tathāgato gambhīro vipulo duravagāhaḥ / yeṣāṃ keṣāṃcidānanda imānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntāñchrutvopapatsyate prītiprāmodyam, prasādalābhāstaiḥ sattvaiḥ sulabdhāḥ / amoghaṃ ca teṣāṃ jīvitam, amoghaṃ ca teṣāṃ mānuṣyam, sucaritacaraṇāśca te, ādattaṃ ca taiḥ sāram, muktāśca te tribhyo 'pāyebhyaḥ, bhaviṣyanti ca te putrāstathāgatasya, pariprāptaṃ ca taiḥ sarvakāryam, amoghaśca teṣāṃ śraddhāpratilambhaḥ, suvibhakta ca tai rāṣṭrapiṇḍam, prasannāśca te 'grasattvaiḥ, saṃchinnāstairmārapāśāḥ, nistīrṇaśca taiḥ saṃsārāṭavīkāntāraḥ, samuddhṛtaśca taiḥ śokaśalyaḥ, anuprāptaṃ ca taiḥ prāmodyavastu, sugṛhītāni ca taiḥ śaraṇagamanāni, dakṣiṇīyāśca te pūjārhāḥ, durlabhaprādurbhāvāśca te loke, dakṣiṇīyāśca te dhārayitavyāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi - te sarvaloke imamevaṃ sarvalokavipratyanīkaṃ tathāgatadharmaṃ śraddadhanti / na te ānanda sattvā avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhavanti / te cānanda sattvā mamaikajātipratibaddhāni mitrāṇi bhaviṣyanti / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? kaścidānanda śravaṇādeva priyo bhavati manāpaśca na tu darśanena / kaścidānanda darśanenāpi priyo bhavati manāpaśca na tu khalu punaḥ śravaṇena / kaścidānanda darśanenāpi śravaṇenāpi priyo bhavati manāpaśca / teṣāṃ keṣāṃcidānanda ahaṃ darśanena vā śravaṇena vā priyo manāpo bhaveyaṃ niṣṭhāṃ tvaṃ tatra gacchethāḥ - na tāni mamaikajātipratibaddhāni mitrāṇi / dṛṣṭāste tathāgatena, mocayitavyāste tathāgatena, te samaguṇapratyaṃśāḥ, te tathāgataguṇapratyaṃśāḥ, te tathāgatena kartavyā upāsakāḥ, te tathāgataṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ, upāttāste tathāgatena / mamāntikāt khalvapyānanda pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāmeva tāvaccarato ye kecidbhayārditāḥ sattvā āgatya abhayaṃ pratiyācante sma, tebhyo 'haṃ sattvebhyo 'bhayaṃ dattvān, kimaṅga punaretarhyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / śraddhāyāmānanda yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / idaṃ tathāgato vijñāpayati / yadānanda tathāgatena yuṣmākaṃ karaṇīyaṃ kṛtam, tattathāgatena śodhito mānaśalyaḥ / śravaṇenāpyānanda mitrasya nanu yojanaśatāntaramapi gacchanti, gatvā ca sukhitā bhavanti adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ mitraṃ dṛṣṭvā / kaḥ punarvādo ye māṃ niśritya kuśalamūlānyavaropayanti / jñāsyantyānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ - pūrva mitrāṇyete sattvāstathāgatānām, asmākamapyete mitrāṇi bhavantīti / tatkasmāt khalu punarānanda mitraṃ mitrasya priyaṃ ca manāpaṃ ca bhavati? tasyāpi (tadapi) priyameva bhavati, mitrasya yatpriyaṃ mitram, tadapi priyameva bhavati manāpaṃ ca / tasmāttarhyānanda ārocayāmi ca prativedayāmi ca / śraddhāmātrakamutpādayatha / anuparindiṣyāmo
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Their conduct will not be [exemplary], <s>Ānanda</s>. Those beings will be of crooked conduct. Through that crooked conduct they will fall into <s>Avīci</s>, the great hell. Why is that? Whatever monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen, <s>Ānanda</s>, having heard <s>sūtras</s> of this kind, will not have confidence in them, will not have faith, will not comprehend them — they, upon dying, will fall into <s>Avīci</s>, the great hell. Do not, <s>Ānanda</s>, regard the <s>Tathāgata</s> as unreliable! Why is that? For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is immeasurable, profound, vast, and unfathomable. Those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, who upon hearing <s>sūtras</s> of this kind will experience delight and joy — by those beings serenity has been well-gained. Their life is not in vain; their human birth is not in vain. They are of good conduct, they have grasped the essence, they are freed from the three lower realms, they will become sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they have accomplished all purposes, their attainment of faith is not fruitless, they have well-divided the country's offerings, they are esteemed by the foremost beings, they have cut <s>Māra</s>'s snares, they have crossed the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, they have extracted the dart of grief, they have attained the ground of joy, they have well-grasped the refuges, they are worthy of offerings and of worship, they are of rare appearance in the world, and they are to be honored as worthy of offerings. Why is that? Because they have faith in this <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, which goes against the entire world. Those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, are not endowed with a small root of merit. And those beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, will be my friends bound [to me] through the final birth. Why is that? Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and pleasing by hearing alone, not by sight. Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and pleasing by sight alone, not by hearing. Someone, <s>Ānanda</s>, becomes dear and pleasing both by sight and by hearing. As for those to whom I, <s>Ānanda</s>, might become dear and pleasing either by sight or by hearing — you should reach the conclusion that they are not my friends bound through the final birth. They have been seen by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; they are to be liberated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; they share equal qualities; they share the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities; they are to be made lay-followers by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; they have gone for refuge to the <s>Tathāgata</s>; they have been taken up by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Even formerly, <s>Ānanda</s>, when I was still practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s career, whoever came to me in distress and implored [me for] fearlessness — to those beings I gave fearlessness; how much more so now that I have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening! In faith, <s>Ānanda</s>, effort should be made — this the <s>Tathāgata</s> makes known. What had to be done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for you has been done, <s>Ānanda</s>; the dart of pride has been purified by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Even by hearing alone, <s>Ānanda</s>, do people not go even a hundred <s>yojanas</s> for the sake of a friend, and having gone, become happy upon seeing a friend never seen before? What then need be said of those who, relying on me, plant roots of merit? The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s> will know, <s>Ānanda</s>: 'These beings were former friends of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; they are our friends too.' Why then, <s>Ānanda</s>, is a friend dear and pleasing to a friend? Because what is dear to a friend is dear [to him] also, and what is pleasing to a friend is pleasing also. Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, I declare and make known: generate even a measure of faith! We will commend [you]

body.text: vayamanāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike, te 'smākamapi mitrāṇīti viditvā yathābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayiṣyanti / tadyathāpi nāma ānanda kasyacideva puruṣasyaikaputrako bhavet suvayāḥ pradakṣiṇagrāhī / sa ca puruṣo bahumitro bhavet / sa tasmin pitari kālagate na hi vihanyeta pitṛmitrasuparigṛhītaḥ / evabheva ānanda ye kecinmama śraddhāsyanti tānahamupādadāmi / mitrāṇīva mama tāni / (te) mama śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ / bahumitraśca tathāgataḥ / tāni ca tathāgatasya mitrāṇi bhūtavādīni na mṛṣāvādīni / anuparindāmyahaṃ bhūtavādīnām / yāni tathāgatasya mitrāṇyanāgatāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā / śraddhāyāmānanda yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / atrāhaṃ yuṣmān vijñāpayāmīti //
body.translated_text: in the presence of future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, and knowing that they too are our friends, [those Buddhas] will fulfill their aspirations. Just as, <s>Ānanda</s>, a certain man might have an only son — young and well-mannered — and that man might have many friends; if, when the father dies, [the son] would not be neglected, being well-supported by his father's friends — even so, <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever will have faith in me, I take them up. They are as my friends; they have gone to me for refuge. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> has many friends. And the friends of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are truthful, not false-speaking. I commend [beings] to those who are truthful — to the friends of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, [who are] the future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, fully awakened <s>Buddhas</s>. In faith, <s>Ānanda</s>, effort should be made — this I make known to you.' //

body.text: iti hi jāte bodhisattve gaganatalagatānyapsaraḥkoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi divyaiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanavastrābharaṇairmāyādevīmabhyavakiranti sma / tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Apsarases</s> stationed in the sky showered <s>Māyādevī</s> with divine flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, garments, and ornaments. Thereupon this was said —

children.text: śubhavimalaviśuddhahemaprabhā candrasūryaprabhā
children.translated_text: Of auspicious, stainless, pure, golden radiance, with the radiance of moon and sun,

children.text: ṣaṣṭi daśasahasra devāpsarā mañjughoṣasvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: sixty ten-thousand divine <s>Apsarases</s>, of sweet, melodious voices,

children.text: tasmi kṣaṇi upetya tāṃ lumbinīṃ māyadevyabruvan
children.translated_text: at that moment, having approached that <s>Lumbinī</s> [grove], said to <s>Māyādevī</s>:

children.text: mā khu jani viṣādu tuṣṭā bhavopasthāyikāṣte vayam // Lal_7.22 //
children.translated_text: 'Do not, we pray, be sorrowful — be content! We are your attendants.' // Lal_7.22 //

children.text: bhaṇahi kiṃ karaṇīyu kiṃ kurmahe kena kāryaṃ ca te
children.translated_text: 'Tell us what is to be done, what shall we do, what is your task?

children.text: vayaṃ tava susamarthopasthāyikā premabhāvasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: We are your capable attendants, established in affection.

children.text: api ca bhava udagra harṣānvitā mā ca khedaṃ janehi
children.translated_text: Moreover, be elated and filled with joy; do not produce grief!

children.text: jarāmaraṇavighāti vaidyottamaṃ adya devī janeṣī laghum // Lal_7.23 //
children.translated_text: Today, O Queen, you shall swiftly give birth to the supreme physician, the destroyer of old age and death!' // Lal_7.23 //

children.text: yatha druma pariphulla saṃpuṣpitā śālavṛkṣā ime
children.translated_text: 'Just as these <s>Śāla</s> trees are in full bloom, blossoming like trees in flower,

children.text: yatha ca marusahasra pārśve sthitā bhrāmayanto bhujān /
children.translated_text: just as thousands of gods stand at your side, waving their arms,

children.text: yatha ca cali sasāgarā medinī ṣaḍvikārā iyaṃ
children.translated_text: just as this earth with its oceans trembles with the six kinds of shaking —

children.text: divi divi ca vighuṣṭa lokottaraṃ tvaṃ janeṣī sutam // Lal_7.24 //
children.translated_text: in heaven after heaven it is proclaimed: you shall give birth to a transcendent son!' // Lal_7.24 //

children.text: yatha ca prabha viśuddha vibhrājate svarṇavarṇa śubhā
children.translated_text: 'Just as this pure, auspicious, golden-colored radiance blazes forth,

children.text: tūryaśata manojñā cāghaṭṭitā ghuṣyayante 'mbare /
children.translated_text: and hundreds of melodious instruments sound unstruck in the sky,

children.text: yatha ca śatasahasra śuddhā śubhā vītarāgāḥ surā
children.translated_text: just as hundreds of thousands of pure, auspicious, passionless gods

children.text: namiṣu muditacittā adyo jane sarvaloke hitam // Lal_7.25 //
children.translated_text: bow with joyful minds — today give birth to one who will benefit the entire world!' // Lal_7.25 //

children.text: śakramapi ca brahmapālāpi cānyā ca yā devatā
children.translated_text: '<s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the [world-]guardians, and whatever other deities —

children.text: tuṣṭamuditacittā pārśve sthitā nāmayanto bhujām /
children.translated_text: content and joyful in mind, standing at your side, bowing their arms —

children.text: so ca puruṣasiṃha śuddhavrato (bhittva) kukṣinirdhāvito
children.translated_text: that lion among men, of pure vows, having broken through the womb, has come forth,

children.text: kanakagirinikāśa śuddhavrato niṣkramī nāyakaḥ // Lal_7.26 //
children.translated_text: like a golden mountain in appearance, of pure vows — the leader has emerged!' // Lal_7.26 //

children.text: śakramapi ca brahma tau pāṇibhiḥ saṃpratīcchā muniṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> receive the Sage in their hands;

children.text: kṣetra śatasahasra saṃkampitā ābha muktā śubhā /
children.translated_text: hundreds of thousands of fields are shaken; auspicious radiance is emitted.

children.text: api ca triṣu apāyi sattvā sukhī nāsti duḥkhaṃ puna
children.translated_text: Moreover, beings in the three lower realms are happy — there is no more suffering.

children.text: amaraśatasahasra puṣpāṃ kṣipī bhrāmayantyambarān // Lal_7.27 //
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of immortals cast flowers, whirling them through the sky.' // Lal_7.27 //

children.text: vīryabalaupeta vajrātmikā medinī saṃsthitā ('bhuttadā)
children.translated_text: 'Endowed with the power of vigor, adamantine, the earth stood firm,

children.text: padmu ruciracitru abhyudgato yatra (cakrāṅgacitrebhiḥ) padbhyāṃ sthito ('pi) nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: and a beautiful, wondrous lotus sprang up where the leader stood with his feet marked with wheel-patterns.

children.text: sapta pada kramitva brahmasvaro muñci ghoṣottamaṃ
children.translated_text: Having taken seven steps, with a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice he uttered the supreme proclamation:

children.text: jaramaraṇavighāti vaidyottamo bheṣyi sattvottamaḥ // Lal_7.28 //
children.translated_text: "I shall be the supreme physician, the destroyer of old age and death, the best of beings!"' // Lal_7.28 //

children.text: gaganatala sthihitva brahmottamo śakradevottamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Standing in the sky, the supreme <s>Brahmā</s> and the supreme lord <s>Śakra</s>

children.text: śuciruciraprasannagandhodakairvisnapī nāyakam /
children.translated_text: bathed the leader with pure, beautiful, clear, fragrant water.

children.text: api ca uragarājā śītoṣṇa dve vāridhāre śubhe (vyamuñcatāntarīkṣe sthitāḥ)
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Nāga</s>-king [released] two auspicious streams of cool and warm water [standing in mid-air],

children.text: amara śatasahasra gandhodakairvisnapī nāyakam // Lal_7.29 //
children.translated_text: and hundreds of thousands of immortals bathed the leader with fragrant water.' // Lal_7.29 //

children.text: lokapālāśca saṃbhrānta saṃdhārayantī karaiḥ śobhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The world-guardians, in reverence, held [him] with their beautiful hands;

children.text: trisahasrā iyaṃ bhūmiḥ kampate sacarācarā // Lal_7.30 //
children.translated_text: this trichiliocosmic earth trembled, with all that moves and does not move.' // Lal_7.30 //

children.text: prabhā ca rucirā muktā apāyāśca viśodhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Beautiful radiance was emitted and the lower realms were purified;

children.text: kleśaduḥkhāśca te śāntā jāte lokavināyake // Lal_7.31 //
children.translated_text: the afflictions and sufferings were stilled when the guide of the world was born.' // Lal_7.31 //

children.text: kṣipanti marutaḥ puṣpaṃ jāte 'sminnaranāyake /
children.translated_text: 'The winds scatter flowers when this guide of men is born;

children.text: krama sapta padāṃ vīraḥ kramate balavīryavān // Lal_7.32 //
children.translated_text: the hero, endowed with strength and vigor, takes the seven steps.' // Lal_7.32 //

children.text: pādau nikṣipate yatra bhūmau padmavarāḥ śubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where he sets down his feet, beautiful, excellent lotuses

children.text: abhyudgacchaṃstato mahyāṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitāḥ // Lal_7.33 //
children.translated_text: spring up from the earth, adorned with every jewel.' // Lal_7.33 //

children.text: yadā sapta padāṃ gatvā brahmasvaramudāhari /
children.translated_text: 'When, having taken seven steps, he uttered the <s>Brahmā</s>-voice,

children.text: jarāmaraṇavighāti bhiṣagvara ivodgataḥ // Lal_7.34 //
children.translated_text: [he was] like a supreme physician arisen, the destroyer of old age and death.' // Lal_7.34 //

children.text: vyavalokayitvā ca viśārado diśaḥ tato girāṃ muñcati arthayuktām /
children.translated_text: 'Having surveyed the directions with confidence, he then uttered meaningful words:

children.text: jyeṣṭho 'haṃ sarvalokasya śraṣṭho (loke vināyakaḥ) iyaṃ ca jātirmama paścimā (iti) // Lal_7.35 //
children.translated_text: "I am the foremost in all the world, the best, the guide of the world — this is my final birth."' // Lal_7.35 //

children.text: hāsyaṃ ca muktaṃ naranāyakena salokapālairmarubhiśca sendraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A smile was released by the guide of men, and by the world-guardians and the gods together with <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: prasannacittairvaragandhavāribhiḥ saṃskārito lokahitārthakārī // Lal_7.36 //
children.translated_text: with serene minds, with excellent fragrant water, they consecrated the one who acts for the welfare of the world.' // Lal_7.36 //

children.text: api coragendraiḥ sahitaiḥ samagraiḥ gandhogradhārāvisaraiḥ snapiṃsu /
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, the <s>Nāga</s>-kings together, assembled, bathed [him] with streams of thick fragrant [water];

children.text: anye 'pi devā nayutā (sthitāḥ) 'ntarīkṣe snapiṃsu gandhāgrajine svayaṃbhum // Lal_7.37 //
children.translated_text: other gods too, <s>niyutas</s>, stationed in mid-air, bathed the self-born one with fragrant and finest [waters].' // Lal_7.37 //

children.text: śvetaṃ ca vipulaṃ chatraṃ cāmarāṃśca śubhāmbarān /
children.translated_text: 'A white and vast parasol, <s>cāmaras</s>, and beautiful garments —

children.text: antarīkṣe gatā devāḥ snāpayanti nararṣabham // Lal_7.38 //
children.translated_text: the gods stationed in mid-air bathe the bull among men.' // Lal_7.38 //

body.text: pañcakulikaśatāni prasūyante sma /
body.translated_text: Five hundred [Śākya sons] were born [simultaneously]. //

children.text: puruṣa tvaritu gatva śuddhodanamabravīt harṣito
children.translated_text: 'A man, going swiftly, said to <s>Śuddhodana</s> with joy:

children.text: vṛddhi vipula jātu devā suto bhūṣito lakṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Vast increase, O lord! A divine son adorned with the marks [has been born]!

children.text: mahakularatanasya (vṛddhibhūtā) vyakto asau cakravartīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Increase has come to the jewel of the great family — clearly he is a lord, a <s>Cakravartin</s>;

children.text: na ca bhavi pratiśatru jambudhvaje ekachatro bhavet // Lal_7.39 //
children.translated_text: there will be no rival on <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — he shall be the sole sovereign!"' // Lal_7.39 //

children.text: dvitiyu puruṣu gatva (rājñi) śuddhodane śleṣayitvā krame
children.translated_text: 'A second man, going to the queen of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, bowed in order and [said]:

children.text: vṛddhi vipula deva jātā nṛpe śākiyānāṃ kule /
children.translated_text: "Vast increase, O lord, has occurred in the family of the <s>Śākyas</s>, O king!

children.text: pañcaviṃśatisahasra jātāḥ sutāḥ śākiyānāṃ gṛhe
children.translated_text: Twenty-five thousand sons have been born in the homes of the <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: sarvi balaupeta nagnāḥ samā duṣpradharṣā paraiḥ // Lal_7.40 //
children.translated_text: all endowed with strength, vigorous, equal, invincible by enemies!"' // Lal_7.40 //

children.text: aparu puruṣa āha devā śruṇā nandaśabdaṃ mamā
children.translated_text: 'Another man said: "O lord, hear the joyful news from me!

children.text: chandakapramukhāni ceṭīsutā jāta aṣṭau śatā /
children.translated_text: Eight hundred servant-sons, headed by <s>Chandaka</s>, have been born.

children.text: api ca daśasahasra jātā hayāḥ kaṇṭhakasya sakhā
children.translated_text: Moreover, ten thousand horses have been born, companions of <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>,

children.text: turagavarapradhāna hemaprabhā mañjukeśā varāḥ // Lal_7.41 //
children.translated_text: the finest of excellent steeds, golden in radiance, with beautiful manes, superb!"' // Lal_7.41 //

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasra paryantakāḥ koṭṭarājāstathā
children.translated_text: 'Twenty thousand border-kings and fortress-kings likewise

children.text: nṛpati kramatalebhi cānvākramī sādhu devā jayā /
children.translated_text: followed in the footsteps of the king [and said]: "Well done, O lord, victory!

children.text: ājñā khalu dadāhi gacchāma kiṃ vā karomo nṛpā
children.translated_text: Command us — shall we go? What shall we do, O king?

children.text: tvamiha vaśitu prāptu bhṛtyā vayaṃ bhaṭṭa devā jayā // Lal_7.42 //
children.translated_text: You have obtained dominion here; we are your servants, O lord, victory!"' // Lal_7.42 //

children.text: viṃśati ca sahasra nāgottamā hemajālojjvalā
children.translated_text: 'Twenty thousand excellent <s>Nāgas</s>, blazing with golden nets,

children.text: tvaritamupagamiṃsu rājño gṛhaṃ garjamānā nabhe /
children.translated_text: swiftly approached the king's palace, trumpeting in the sky.

children.text: kṛṣṇaśabala vatsa gopāmukhā jāta ṣaṣṭiśatā
children.translated_text: Black-and-spotted calves, with cowherd faces (?), six hundred were born;

children.text: iyamapi suti devadevottame vṛddhi rājño gṛhe // Lal_7.43 //
children.translated_text: this too is an auspicious birth — increase in the king's house, when the supreme god of gods [was born]!' // Lal_7.43 //

children.text: api ca nṛpati gaccha prekṣa svayaṃ sarvameva prabho (puṇyateja prabho)
children.translated_text: 'Moreover, O king, go and see for yourself everything, O lord of merit's splendor!

children.text: naramarutasahasra ye harṣitā dṛṣṭva jāte guṇāṃ /
children.translated_text: Thousands of men and gods, having seen the qualities [manifested] at the birth, are overjoyed.

children.text: bodhivara aśoka saṃprasthitāḥ kṣipra bhomā jināḥ // Lal_7.44 //
children.translated_text: Having set forth on the supreme path of awakening and freedom from sorrow — may we swiftly become <s>Jinas</s>!' // Lal_7.44 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jāte bodhisattve tatkṣaṇaṃ dānanisargaḥ punaruttari pravartate sma / pañca ca kulikāśatāni prasūyante sma, daśa ca kanyāsahasrāṇi yaśovatīpramukhāni / aṣṭau dāsīśatāni aṣṭau dāsaśatāni chandakapramukhāni / daśa vaḍavāsahasrāṇi daśa kiśorasahasrāṇi kaṇṭhakapramukhāni / pañca kareṇusahasrāṇi pañca piṅgasahasrāṇi prasūyante sma / tāni sarvāṇi rājñā śuddhodanena pustavaropitāni kumārasya krīḍārthaṃ dattānyabhūvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, at that very moment a further outpouring of generous gifts occurred. Five hundred noble-born colts were born, and ten thousand maidens headed by <s>Yaśovatī</s>. Eight hundred female servants, eight hundred male servants headed by <s>Chandaka</s>. Ten thousand mares, ten thousand young horses headed by <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>. Five thousand she-elephants and five thousand bull-elephants were born. All of these were registered by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and given to the prince for his amusement. //

body.text: caturṇāṃ ca dvīpakoṭīśatasahasrāṇāṃ madhye pṛthivīpradeśe aśvatthayaṣṭiḥ prādurabhūdantardvīpe ca candanavanaṃ prādurbabhūva bodhisattvasya paribhogārthaṃ bodhisattvasyaivānubhāvena / pañca codyānaśatāni samantānnagarasya prādurbabhūvurbodhisattvasya paribhogāya / pañca ca nidhānasahasrāṇi dharaṇītalādutplutya mukhaṃ darśayanti sma / iti hi ye kecidrājñaḥ śuddhodanasyārthābhipretā abhūvan, te sarve samṛddhābhipretā abhūvan saṃsiddhāḥ //
body.translated_text: And in the midst of the hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of the four continents, on a spot of earth, an <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree appeared, and on the intermediate continent a sandalwood forest appeared, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s enjoyment, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own power. Five hundred parks appeared all around the city for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s enjoyment. And five thousand treasure-stores sprang up from the surface of the earth, showing their openings. Thus, whatever purposes King <s>Śuddhodana</s> desired — all of those were fulfilled and accomplished. //

body.text: tato rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhūt - kimahaṃ kumārasya nāmadheyaṃ kariṣyāmīti / tato 'syaitadabhūt - asya hi jātamātreṇa mama sarvārthāḥ saṃsiddhāḥ / yannvahamasya sarvārthasiddha iti nāma kuryām / tato rājā bodhisattvaṃ mahatā satkāreṇa satkṛtya sarvārthasiddho 'yaṃ kumāro nāmnā bhavatu iti nāmāsyākārṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'What name shall I give the prince?' Then this [thought] occurred to him: 'Indeed, at his very birth all my purposes have been accomplished. Let me therefore give him the name <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (All-Purposes-Accomplished).' Then the king, having honored the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with great reverence, gave him the name: 'Let this prince be called <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>!' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jāte bodhisattve mātuḥ kukṣipārśvamakṣatamanupahatamabhavadyathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt / tritaviṣyandāmbukūpāḥ prādurabhūvan api ca sugandhatailapuṣkariṇyaḥ / pañcāpsaraḥ - sahasrāṇi divyagandhaparivāsitatailaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyānulepanaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyagandhodakaparipūrṇaghaṭāparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / paccāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyānulepanaparigṛhītani bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyadārakācīvaraparigṛhītāni bodhisatvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujārajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / pañcāpsaraḥ - sahasrāṇi divyadārakābharaṇaparigṛhītāni bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / pañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyatūryasaṃgītisaṃprabhaṇitena bodhisattvamātaramupasaṃkramya sujātajāte tāmaklāntakāyatāṃ ca paripṛcchanti sma / yāvantaśceha jambudvīpe bāhyāḥ pañcabhijñā ṛṣayaste sarve gaganatalenāgatya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya purataḥ sthitvā jayavṛddhiśabdamanuśrāvayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, the mother's womb and flanks remained uninjured and unharmed — as before, so after. Springs of fresh water and wells appeared, as well as lotus-pools of fragrant oil. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing divine fragrant oil, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing divine unguents, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing pitchers filled with divine scented water, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing divine unguents, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing divine garments for the child, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, bearing divine ornaments for the child, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. Five thousand <s>Apsarases</s>, with the playing and singing of divine music, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother and inquired about [her] well-born child and [her] unwearied body. And as many external <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) possessing the five supernatural knowledges as there were in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — all of them, coming through the sky, standing before King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, proclaimed words of victory and blessing. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jātamātro bodhisattvaḥ saptarātraḥ lumbinīvane divyamānuṣyakaistūryatālāvacaraiḥ satkriyate sma, gurukriyate sma, mānyate sma, pūjyate sma, khādyabhojyasvādanīyāni
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, as soon as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, for seven nights in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove he was honored, venerated, esteemed, and worshipped with divine and human instrumental music and rhythmic performances; food, drink, and delicacies

body.text: viśrāṇyante sma / sarvaśākyagaṇāśca saṃnipātyānandaśabdamudīrayanti sma, dānāni ca dadanti sma, puṇyāni ca kurvanti sma / dvātriṃśacca brāhmaṇaśatasahasrāṇi dine dine saṃtarpyante sma / yeṣāṃ ca yenārthena tebhyastaddīyate sma / śakraśca devānāmindro brahmā ca tasyāṃ brāhmaṇaparṣadi māṇavakarūpamabhinirmāyāgrāsane niṣadyemāṃ maṅgalyāṃ gāthāmabhyabhāṣatām -
body.translated_text: were distributed. And all the <s>Śākya</s> clans, having assembled, raised cries of joy, gave gifts, and performed meritorious deeds. Thirty-two hundred-thousands of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were feasted day after day. And whatever anyone desired — that was given to them. And <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, and <s>Brahmā</s>, having manifested the forms of young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> students in that assembly of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, seated themselves on the foremost seat and spoke these auspicious verses —

children.text: apāyāśca yathā śāntā sukhī sarvaṃ yathā jagat /
children.translated_text: Just as the lower realms are pacified and the entire world is happy,

children.text: dhruvaṃ sukhāvaho jātaḥ sukhe sthāpayitā jagat // Lal_7.45 //
children.translated_text: surely one who brings happiness has been born, who will establish the world in happiness! // Lal_7.45 //

children.text: yathā vitimirā cābhā ravicandrasuraprabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the darkness-free radiance — the lights of the sun, moon, and gods —

children.text: abhibhūtā na bhāsante dhruvaṃ puṇyaprabhodbhavaḥ // Lal_7.46 //
children.translated_text: are outshone and do not shine [before him], surely he is born from the splendor of merit! // Lal_7.46 //

children.text: paśyantyanayanā yadvacchrotrahīnāḥ śruṇanti ca /
children.translated_text: Just as those without eyes see, and those bereft of hearing hear,

children.text: unmattakāḥ smṛtīmanto bhavitā lokacetiyaḥ // Lal_7.47 //
children.translated_text: and the deranged become mindful — he shall become a sacred shrine for the world! // Lal_7.47 //

children.text: na bādhante yathā kleśā jātaṃ maitrajanaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: Just as afflictions do not afflict [beings], and the world has become friendly and loving,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ brahmakoṭīnāṃ bhavitā pūjanārahaḥ // Lal_7.48 //
children.translated_text: without doubt he shall be worthy of worship by <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Brahmās</s>! // Lal_7.48 //

children.text: yathā saṃpuṣpitāḥ śālā medinī ca samā sthitā /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>Śāla</s> trees have blossomed and the earth stands level,

children.text: dhruvaṃ sarvajagatpūjyaḥ sarvajño 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati // Lal_7.49 //
children.translated_text: surely he shall be worshipped by the entire world — he shall become the Omniscient One! // Lal_7.49 //

children.text: yathā nirākulo loko mahāpadmo yathodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the world is free from disturbance and the great lotus has sprung forth,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ mahātejā lokanātho bhaviṣyati // Lal_7.50 //
children.translated_text: without doubt, [this] one of great splendor shall become the Lord of the World! // Lal_7.50 //

children.text: yathā ca mṛdukā vātā divyagandhopavāsitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as gentle winds, perfumed with divine fragrance,

children.text: śamenti vyādhiṃ sattvānāṃ vaidyarājo bhaviṣyati // Lal_7.51 //
children.translated_text: allay the diseases of beings — he shall become the King of Physicians! // Lal_7.51 //

children.text: vītarāgā yathā ceme rūpadhātau marucchatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as these hosts of gods in the <s>Rūpadhātu</s> (Form Realm), free from passion,

children.text: kṛtāñjaliṃ namasyante dakṣiṇīyo bhaviṣyati // Lal_7.52 //
children.translated_text: pay homage with joined palms — he shall become one worthy of offerings! // Lal_7.52 //

children.text: yathā ca manujā devān devāḥ paśyanti mānuṣān /
children.translated_text: Just as humans see gods and gods see humans,

children.text: heṭhayanti na cānyonyaṃ sārthavāho bhaviṣyati // Lal_7.53 //
children.translated_text: and none torment one another — he shall become the Caravan-Leader! // Lal_7.53 //

children.text: yathā ca jvalanaḥ śāntaḥ sarvā nadyaśca visthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as fire has been stilled and all rivers have ceased [flowing],

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ ca kampate bhūmiḥ bhavitā tattvadarśakaḥ // Lal_7.54 //
children.translated_text: and the earth trembles gently — he shall become the Seer of Truth! // Lal_7.54 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptarātrajātasya bodhisattvasya mātā māyādevī kālamakarot / sā kālagatā trāyatriṃśati deveṣūpapadyata / syāt khalu punarbhikṣavo yuṣmākamevaṃ bodhisattvāparādhena māyādevī kālagateti? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? etat paramaṃ hi tasyā āyuṣpramāṇamabhūt / atītānāmapi bhikṣavo bodhisattvānāṃ saptarātrajātānāṃ janetryaḥ kālamakurvanta / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? vivṛddhasya hi bodhisattvasya paripūrṇendriyasyābhiniṣkrāmato māturhṛdayaṃ sphuṭet //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was seven nights old, his mother <s>Māyādevī</s> passed away. Having passed away, she was reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods. Now, O monks, you might think: 'It was through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fault that <s>Māyādevī</s> passed away.' It should not be viewed thus. Why? Because that was indeed the full measure of her lifespan. O monks, the mothers of past <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too, when [their sons] were seven nights old, passed away. Why? Because, were the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to grow up with fully developed faculties and go forth [to renounce the world], the mother's heart would break. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptame divase yādṛśenaiva vyūhena māyādevī kapilavastuno mahānagarādudyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāntābhūt, tataḥ koṭīśatasahasraguṇottareṇa mahāvyūhena bodhisattvaḥ kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ prāvikṣat / tasya ca praviśataḥ pañca pūrṇakumbhasahasrāṇi gandhodakaparipūrṇāni purato nīyante sma / evaṃ pañcakanyāsahasrāṇi mayūrahastakamparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma / pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi tālavṛkṣakaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma / pañca sa kanyāsahasrāṇi gandhodakabhṛṅgāraparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma, mārgamavasiñcanti sma / pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi vicitrapaṭalakaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma / pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi navavicitrapralambanamālāparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma / pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi ratnabhadrālaṃkāraparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma, mārgaṃ śodhayanti sma / pañca ca kanyāsahasrāṇi bhadrāsanaparigṛhītāni purato gacchanti sma / pañca ca brāhmaṇasahasrāṇi ghaṇṭāparigṛhītāni māṅgalyaśabdaṃ śrāvayantaḥ purato gacchanti sma / viṃśati nāgasahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni purato gacchanti sma / viṃśati hayasahasrāṇi suvarṇālaṃkārasaṃchannāni sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni purato gacchanti sma / aśīti rathasahasrāṇi uchritachatradhvajapatākākiṅkiṇījālasamalaṃkṛtāni bodhisattvasya pṛṣṭhato 'nucchanti sma / cattvāriṃśatpadātisahasrāṇi śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgurūpiṇāṃ saṃnaddhadṛḍhavarmakavacānāṃ bodhisattvaṃ gacchantamanugacchanti sma / gaganatalagatāni cāprameyāsaṃkhyeyānyabhijñātāni kāmāvacarāṇāṃ rūpāvacaradevaputrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi nānāprakrāramanekavyūhairbodhisattvasya pūjāṃ kurvanto 'nugacchanti sma / yasmiṃśca varapravararathe bodhisattvaḥ samabhirūḍho 'bhūt, sa kāmāvacarairdevairanekairmahāvyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'bhūt / viṃśati ca devakanyāsahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāni ratnasūtraparigṛhītāni taṃ rathaṃ vahanti sma / dvayoścāpsarasormadhye ekā mānuṣī kanyā dvayormānuṣīkanyayormadhye ekāpsarā / na cāpsaraso mānuṣīṇāmāmagandhaṃ jighranti sma / na ca mānuṣā apsarasāṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā pramādamāpadyante sma yadidaṃ bodhisattvasya tejonubhāvena //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, on the seventh day, with a procession even more magnificent — a hundred-thousand <s>koṭī</s>-fold greater — than the one with which <s>Māyādevī</s> had gone forth from the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> to the garden grounds, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. And as he entered, five thousand full vases filled with scented water were carried before him. Likewise, five thousand maidens holding peacock-feather fans went before him. Five thousand maidens holding palm-leaf fans went before him. Five thousand maidens holding pitchers of scented water went before him, sprinkling the road. Five thousand maidens holding colorful canopies went before him. Five thousand maidens holding fresh and variegated hanging garlands went before him. Five thousand maidens holding jeweled auspicious ornaments went before him, purifying the road. Five thousand maidens holding fine seats went before him. Five thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> holding bells went before him, sounding auspicious words. Twenty thousand elephants, fully adorned with all ornaments, went before him. Twenty thousand horses, covered with golden ornaments and fully adorned, went before him. Eighty thousand chariots, embellished with raised parasols, banners, pennants, and nets of bells, followed behind the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Forty thousand foot-soldiers — brave, heroic, of excellent form, clad in strong armor and mail — followed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as he went. And in the sky, immeasurable and innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of distinguished <s>Kāmāvacara</s> and <s>Rūpāvacara</s> <s>devaputras</s> (divine princes), with manifold and diverse arrays, followed, worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And the excellent, supreme chariot upon which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had mounted was adorned by the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> gods with many magnificent arrays. Twenty thousand divine maidens, fully adorned with all ornaments, holding jeweled cords, drew that chariot. Between every two <s>Apsarases</s> stood one human maiden, and between every two human maidens stood one <s>Apsaras</s>. The <s>Apsarases</s> did not perceive the raw human scent of the human maidens, nor did the humans, upon seeing the beauty of the <s>Apsarases</s>, become infatuated — this by the splendor and power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ kapilāhvaye puravare sarvārthasiddhāya pañcamātraiḥ śākyaśataiḥ pañcagṛhaśatāni nirmāpitānyabhūvan bodhisattvamuddiśya / te bodhisattvaṃ nagaraṃ praviśantaṃ svasvagṛhadvāramūle sthitvā kṛtāñjalipuṭā abhinatakāyāḥ sagauravā evamāhuḥ - iha bhoḥ sarvārthasiddha praviśa / iha bho devātideva praviśa / iha bhoḥ śuddhasattva praviśa / iha bhoḥ sārathivara praviśa / iha bhoḥ prītiprāmodyakara praviśa / iha bho aninditayaśaḥ praviśa / iha bhoḥ samantacakṣu praviśa / iha bho asamasama praviśa / iha bho asadṛśaguṇatejodhara lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasvalaṃkṛtakāya praviśeti / tataścopādāya kumārasyeha sarvārthasiddhaḥ sarvārthasiddha iti saṃjñāmagamat //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, in the excellent city called <s>Kapila</s>, for <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, five hundred <s>Śākya</s> families had five hundred houses constructed, dedicated to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. They, standing at the bases of their respective house-gates as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the city, with palms joined, bodies bowed, with reverence, spoke thus: 'Come in, O <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, enter here! Come in, O god surpassing gods, enter here! Come in, O one of pure being, enter here! Come in, O supreme charioteer, enter here! Come in, O bringer of joy and delight, enter here! Come in, O one of unblemished fame, enter here! Come in, O all-seeing one, enter here! Come in, O equal to the unequaled, enter here! Come in, O bearer of incomparable qualities and splendor, whose body is beautifully adorned with the [major] marks and [minor] characteristics, enter here!' From that time onward, the prince came to be known by the name <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>. //

body.text: tatra rājā śuddhodanasteṣāṃ sarveṣāmanuvartanārthaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sarvagṛheṣu praveśya caturṇāṃ māsānāmatyayādbodhisattvaṃ svagṛhe praveśayati sma / tatra ca nānāratnavyūho nāma
body.translated_text: There, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, in order to comply with all of them, had the <s>Bodhisattva</s> taken into every house, and after a period of four months, had the <s>Bodhisattva</s> brought into his own house. And there, [a palace] called <s>Nānāratnavyūha</s> (Array of Various Jewels)

body.text: mahāprāsādastaṃ bodhisattvaḥ samārūḍho 'bhūt / tatra te bṛddhavṛddhāḥ śākyāḥ saṃnipatyaivaṃ mataṃ cārayanti sma - kā nu khalu samarthā bodhisattvaṃ gopāyituṃ kelayituṃ mamāyituṃ hitacittatayā maitracittatayā guṇacittatayā saumyacittatayā ceti / tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyavadhūśatāni / ekaikā evamāhūḥ - ahaṃ kumāramupasthāsya iti / tatra mahallakamahallikāḥ śākyā evamāhuḥ - sarvā etā vadhūkā navā dahnāstaruṇyaḥ rūpayauvanamadamattāḥ / naitāḥ samarthā bodhisattvaṃ kālena kālamupasthāpayitum / atha ca punariyaṃ mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumārasya mātṛsvasā / eṣā samarthā kumāraṃ samyaksukhena saṃvardhayitum, rājānaṃ ca śuddhodanamabhidhārayitum / iti hi te sarve samagrā bhūtvā mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīmutsāhayanti sma / iti hi mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumāraṃ saṃvardhayati sma / tatra bodhisattvasyārthe dvātriṃśaddhātryaḥ saṃsthāpitā abhuvan aṣṭāvaṅgadhātryaḥ, aṣṭau kṣīradhātryaḥ, aṣṭau maladhātryaḥ, aṣṭau krīḍādhātryaḥ //
body.translated_text: the great palace, which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had ascended. There those elder <s>Śākyas</s>, having assembled, deliberated thus: 'Who indeed is capable of guarding, playing with, cherishing, and caring for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a mind of benevolence, friendliness, virtue, and gentleness?' There were five hundred <s>Śākya</s> brides, and each one said: 'I will attend upon the prince.' Then the elder <s>Śākya</s> men and women said: 'All these brides are new, young, youthful, and intoxicated with the pride of beauty and youth. They are not capable of attending upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the proper times. But this <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> is the prince's maternal aunt. She is capable of rearing the prince properly and comfortably, and of supporting King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' Thus they all, having come to agreement, encouraged <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. And so <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> reared the prince. And for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sake, thirty-two nurses were appointed: eight limb-nurses, eight milk-nurses, eight cleansing-nurses, and eight play-nurses. //

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvaṃ śākyagaṇaṃ saṃnipātyaivaṃ mīmāṃsate sma - kiṃ nu khalvayaṃ kumāro rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī, āhosvidabhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai?
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having assembled the entire <s>Śākya</s> clan, deliberated: 'Will this prince become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>, or will he go forth into the homeless life?'

body.text: tena ca samayena himavataḥ parvatarājasya pārśve asito nāma maharṣiḥ prativasati sma pañcābhijñaḥ sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyena / sa bodhisattvasya jātamātrasya bahūnyāścaryādbhutaprātihāryāṇyadrākṣīt / gaganatalagatāṃśca devaputrān buddhaśabdamanuśrāvayato 'mbarāṇi ca bhrāmayata itastataḥ pramuditān bhramato 'drākṣīt / tasyaitadabhūt - yannvahaṃ vyavalokayeyamiti / sa divyena cakṣuṣā sarvaṃ jambudvīpamanuvilokayannadrākṣīt kapilāhvaye mahāpuravare rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe kumāraṃ jātaṃ śatapuṇyatejastejitaṃ sarvalokamahitaṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātram / dṛṣṭvā ca punarnaradattaṃ māṇavakamāmantrayate sma - yat khalu māṇavaka jānīyā jambudvīpe mahāratnamutpannam / kapilavastuni mahānagare rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhe kumāro jātaḥ śatapuṇyatejastejitaḥ sarvalokamahito dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ / sacetso 'gāramadhyāvasiṣyati, rājā bhaviṣyati caturaṅgaścakravartī vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājo jānapadasthāmavīryaprāptaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhavanti / tadyathā - cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam / evaṃ saptaratnasaṃpūrṇaśca / asya putrasahasraṃ bhaviṣyati śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām / sa imaṃ mahāpṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ samudraparikhamadaṇḍenāśastreṇa svena (dharmeṇa) balenābhibhūyābhinirjitya rājyaṃ kariṣyatyaiśvaryādhipatyena / sacetpunaragārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati, tathāgato bhaviṣyati arhan samyaksaṃbuddho netā ananyaneyaḥ śāstā loke saṃbuddhaḥ / tadetarhyupasaṃkramiṣyāvastad draṣṭumiti //
body.translated_text: At that time, on the slopes of the <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, there dwelt a great sage (<s>Maharṣi</s>) named <s>Asita</s>, possessing the five superknowledges, together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s>. He had seen the many wondrous and marvelous miracles at the very moment of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s birth. And he had seen <s>Devaputras</s> in the sky, proclaiming the word '<s>Buddha</s>!' and waving their garments here and there, moving about joyfully. He thought: 'Let me investigate this.' Looking with the divine eye over all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, he saw that in the great city called <s>Kapilā</s>, in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, a prince had been born — blazing with the splendor of a hundred merits, honored by the entire world, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person. Having seen this, he addressed the young <s>Naradatta</s>: 'Know, O young man, that a great jewel has appeared in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. In the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the house of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, a prince has been born — blazing with the splendor of a hundred merits, honored by the entire world, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person. If he remains in the household life, he will become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> with four armies — victorious, righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, having attained the strength and might of the realm, endowed with the seven jewels. His seven jewels will be these: the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the gem-jewel, the woman-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the general-jewel. Thus he will be complete with seven jewels. He will have a thousand sons — heroic, valiant, of noble form, crushers of enemy armies. He will rule this great circle of the earth, girt by the ocean, without rod or sword, by his own righteous power, with sovereignty and dominion. But if he goes forth from the household life to homelessness, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened one, a guide unled by others, a teacher awakened in the world. Come, let us go now to see him.' //

body.text: atha khalvasito maharṣiḥ sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyena rājahaṃsa iva gaganatalādabhyudgamya samutplutya yena kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya ṛddhiṃ pratisaṃhṛtya padbhyāmeva kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ praviśya yena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhadvāre 'sthāt //
body.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Asita</s>, together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s>, like a royal swan, rising up from the surface of the sky, flew to the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Having arrived, he withdrew his supernatural power and entered the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot, approaching the residence of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having approached, he stood at the gate of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s house. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'sito maharṣiḥ paśyati sma rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhadvāre 'nekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni / atha khalvasito maharṣirdauvārikamupasaṃkramyaivamāha - gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya, nivedaya dvāre ṛṣirvyavasthita iti / parameti dauvāriko 'sitasya maharṣeḥ pratiśrutya yena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya kṛtāñjalipuṭo rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha - yat khalu deva jānīyā ṛṣirjīrṇo vṛddho mahallako dvāre sthitaḥ / evaṃ ca vadati - rājānamahaṃ draṣṭukāma iti / atha rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣerāsanaṃ prajñāpya taṃ puruṣamevamāha - praviśatu ṛṣiriti / atha sa puruṣo rājakulānniṣkramyāsitaṃ maharṣimevamāha - praviśeti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the great sage <s>Asita</s> saw many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled at the gate of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s house. Then the great sage <s>Asita</s> approached the doorkeeper and said: 'Go, good man, and announce to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> that a sage stands at the gate.' 'Very well,' said the doorkeeper, and having assented to the great sage <s>Asita</s>, he approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having approached, with palms joined, he addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thus: 'May the lord know that an aged, old, and venerable sage stands at the gate. He says: "I wish to see the king."' Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having prepared a seat for the great sage <s>Asita</s>, said to that man: 'Let the sage enter.' Then that man, going out from the royal quarters, said to the great sage <s>Asita</s>: 'Enter.' //

body.text: atha khalvasito maharṣiryena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya purataḥ sthitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha - jaya jaya mahārāja, ciramāyuḥ pālaya, dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayeti //
body.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Asita</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having approached and standing before him, he addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thus: 'Victory, victory, O great king! May you live long! Rule your kingdom righteously!' //

body.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣerarghapādyamarcanaṃ ca kṛtvā sādhu suṣṭhu ca parigṛhya āsanenopanimantrayate sma / sukhopaviṣṭaṃ cainaṃ jñātvā sagauravaḥ supratīta evamāha - na smarāmyahaṃ tava ṛṣe darśanam / tatkenārthenehābhyāgato 'si, kiṃ prayojanam?
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having offered the great sage <s>Asita</s> water for the hands, water for the feet, and an oblation, and having received him well and properly, invited him to a seat. Knowing that he was comfortably seated, with respect and well-pleased, he said: 'I do not recall ever seeing you before, O sage. For what purpose have you come here? What is your intention?'

body.text: evamukte 'sito maharṣī rājānaṃ śuddhodanametadavocat - putraste mahārāja jātastamahaṃ draṣṭukāma ihāgata iti //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the great sage <s>Asita</s> said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Your son has been born, O great king. I have come here wishing to see him.' //

body.text: rājā āha - svapiti maharṣe kumāraḥ / muhūrtamāgamaya yāvadutthāsyatīti //
body.translated_text: The king said: 'The prince is sleeping, O great sage. Wait a moment until he awakens.' //

body.text: ṛṣiravocat - na mahārāja tādṛśā mahāpuruṣāściraṃ svapanti / jāgaraśīlāstādṛśāḥ satpuruṣā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: The sage said: 'Such great persons do not sleep for long, O great king. Such noble beings are by nature wakeful.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhasattvo 'sitasya maharṣeranukampayā jāgaraṇanimittamakarot / atha khalu rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvārthasiddhaṃ kumāramubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ sādhu ca suṣṭhu cānuparigṛhya asitasya maharṣerantikamupanāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, out of compassion for the great sage <s>Asita</s>, made the sign of awakening. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, taking the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> carefully and properly in both hands, presented him before the great sage <s>Asita</s>. //

body.text: iti hi asito maharṣirbodhisattvamavalokya dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatamaśītyanuvyañjanasuvicitragātraṃ śakrabrahmalokapālātirekavapuṣaṃ dinakaraśatasahasrātirekatejasaṃ sarvāṅgasundaraṃ dṛṣṭvā codānamudānayati sma - āścaryapudgalo batāyaṃ loke prādurbhūta, mahāścaryapudgalo batāyaṃ loke prādurbhūtaḥ ityutthāyāsanātkṛtāñjalipuṭo bodhisattvasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca bodhisattvamaṅkena parigṛhya nidhyāyannavasthito 'bhūt / so 'drākṣīdbodhisattvasya dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni yaiḥ samanvāgatasya puruṣapudgalasya dve gatī bhavato nānyā / sacedagāramadhyāvasati rājā bhavati caturaṅgaścakravartī pūrvavadyāvadevaiśvaryādhipatyena / sacetpunaragārādanagārikāṃ pravrajati tathāgato bhaviṣyati vighuṣṭaśabdaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā prārodīdaśrūṇi ca pravartayan gambhīraṃ ca niśvasati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus the great sage <s>Asita</s>, beholding the <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body beautifully adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, his form surpassing that of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s>, his splendor surpassing that of a hundred thousand suns, beautiful in all his limbs, and seeing [all this], he uttered this solemn utterance: 'A wondrous person has indeed appeared in the world! A most wondrous person has indeed appeared in the world!' And rising from his seat, with palms joined, he prostrated at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, circumambulated him, and then, taking the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his arms, stood gazing intently. He saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s thirty-two marks of a great person, by which a person endowed [with them] has two destinies and no other: if he remains in the household life, he becomes a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> with four armies, as described before, up to sovereignty and dominion; but if he goes forth from the household life to homelessness, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> whose fame is proclaimed, a perfectly awakened one. Having seen him, [<s>Asita</s>] wept, shed tears, and sighed deeply. //

body.text: adrākṣīdrājā śuddhodano 'sitaṃ maharṣiṃ rudantamaśrūṇi ca pravartayamānaṃ gambhīraṃ ca niśvasantam / dṛṣṭvā ca saṃharṣitaromakūpajātastvaritatvaritaṃ dīnamanā asitaṃ maharṣimetadavocat - kimidamṛṣe rodasi aśrūṇi ca pravartayasi gambhīraṃ ca niśvasasi? mā khalu kumārasya kācidvipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> saw the great sage <s>Asita</s> weeping, shedding tears, and sighing deeply. Seeing this, his hair standing on end, his mind anxious and alarmed, he said to the great sage <s>Asita</s>: 'Why do you weep, O sage, shed tears, and sigh deeply? Surely there is no misfortune for the prince?' //

body.text: evamukte 'sito maharṣī rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha - nāhaṃ mahārāja kumārasyārthena rodimi, nāpyasya kācidvipratipattiḥ / kiṃ tvātmānamahaṃ rodimi / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? ahaṃ ca mahārāja jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ / ayaṃ ca sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro 'vaśyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyati / abhisaṃbudhya cānuttaraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyati apravartitaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā anyena vā punaḥ kenacilloke sahadharmeṇa / sadevakasya lokasya hitāya sukhāya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam / svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ sattvānāṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyati / asmāttaṃ dharmaṃ śratvā jātidharmāṇaḥ sattvā jātyā parimokṣante / evaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimokṣante / rāgadveṣamohāgnisaṃtaptānāṃ sattvānāṃ saddharmajalavarṣeṇa prahlādanaṃ kariṣyati / nānākudṛṣṭigrahaṇapraskandhānāṃ sattvānāṃ kupathaprayātānāmṛjumārgeṇa nirvāṇapathamupaneṣyati / saṃsārapañjaracārakāvaruddhānāṃ kleśabandhanabaddhānāṃ bandhananirmokṣaṃ kariṣyati / ajñānatamastimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanayanānāṃ sattvānāṃ prajñācakṣurutpādayiṣyati / kleśaśalyaviddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ śalyoddharaṇaṃ kariṣyati / tadyathā mahārāja audumbarapuṣpaṃ kadācitkarhicilloke utpadyate, evameva mahārāja kadācitkarhicidbahubhiḥ kalpakoṭinayutairbuddhā bhagavanto loke utpadyante / so 'yaṃ kumāro 'vaśyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / abhisaṃbudhya ca sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsārasāgarāt pāramuttārayiṣyati, amṛte ca pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati / vayaṃ ca taṃ buddharatnaṃ na drakṣyāmaḥ / ityeva tadahaṃ mahārāja rodimi paridīnamanā dīrghaṃ ca niśvasāmi yadahamimaṃ nārogye 'pi rādhayiṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the great sage <s>Asita</s> said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'I do not weep on the prince's account, O great king, nor is there any misfortune for him. Rather, I weep on my own account. And for what reason? I, O great king, am aged, old, and decrepit. But this prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> will assuredly fully awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening. Having fully awakened, he will turn the unsurpassed <s>dharma</s>-wheel, which has not been turned by any <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, god, <s>Māra</s>, or anyone else in the world together with <s>dharma</s>. He will teach the <s>dharma</s> for the benefit and happiness of the world with its gods — good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end. He will proclaim the holy life to beings — with the right meaning, the right words, complete, perfect, pure, and utterly purified. Having heard that <s>dharma</s>, beings subject to birth will be liberated from birth. Likewise they will be liberated from old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, distress, and despair. For beings scorched by the fires of desire, hatred, and delusion, he will bring refreshment through the rain-shower of the true <s>dharma</s>. For beings who have seized various wrong views and gone astray on false paths, he will lead them to the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s> by the straight way. For beings imprisoned in the cage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, bound by the fetters of the afflictions, he will bring release from bondage. For beings whose eyes are covered by the film, veil, and darkness of ignorance, he will generate the eye of wisdom. For beings pierced by the thorns of the afflictions, he will extract the thorns. Just as, O great king, the flower of the <s>Udumbara</s> tree appears in the world only at rare intervals, even so, O great king, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> appear in the world only at rare intervals, after many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. This prince will assuredly fully awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening. And having fully awakened, he will ferry across <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of beings from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> to the further shore, and establish them in the deathless. But we shall not see that jewel of a <s>Buddha</s>. It is for this reason, O great king, that I weep, with a sorrowful mind, and sigh deeply — that I shall not live to witness even this [teaching].' //

body.text: yathā hyasmākaṃ mahārāja mantravedaśāstreṣvāgacchati - nārhati sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro 'gāramadhyāvasitum / tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samānvāgataḥ / katamairdvātriṃśatā? tadyathā / uṣṇīṣaśīrṣo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / anena mahārāja prathamena mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇena samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / bhinnāñjanamayūrakalāpābhinīlavallitapradakṣiṇāvartakeśaḥ / samavipulalalāṭaḥ / ūrṇā mahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya bhruvo rmadhye jātā himarajataprakāśā / gopakṣmanetraḥ / abhinīlanetraḥ / samacattvāriṃśaddantaḥ / aviraladantaḥ / śukladantaḥ / brahmasvaro mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / rasarasāgravān / prabhūtatanujihvaḥ / siṃhahanuḥ / susaṃvṛttaskandhaḥ / saptotsadaḥ / citāntarāṃsaḥ / sūkṣmasuvarṇavarṇacchaviḥ / sthito 'navanatapralambabāhu / siṃhapūrvārdhakāyaḥ / nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / ekaikaromā / ūrdhvāgrābhipradakṣiṇāvartaromāḥ /
body.translated_text: As it is found in our treatises on <s>mantras</s> and <s>Vedas</s>, O great king — the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in a household. For what reason? For, O great king, the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>). What are the thirty-two? Namely: The prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, has a crown-protuberance (<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>) on his head. By this first mark of a great being is the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> endowed. [He has] hair dark as collyrium, lustrous like a peacock's crest, curling to the right. A smooth, broad forehead. Between the eyebrows of the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, an <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft) has grown, luminous as snow and silver. Eyelashes like those of a cow. Eyes of deep blue. Forty even teeth. Teeth without gaps. White teeth. The prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, has the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>. He possesses the foremost essence of taste. A broad, thin tongue. A lion-jaw. Well-formed shoulders. Seven prominences (<s>saptotsada</s>). A filled-out chest between the shoulders. Skin of fine golden hue. Standing, his arms reach down without bending. A lion-like upper body. The prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, is proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree. Each hair-pore bears a single hair. Hairs rising upward, curling to the right.

body.text: kośopagatabastiguhyaḥ / suvivartitoruḥ / eṇeyamṛgarājajaṅghaḥ / dīrghāṅguliḥ / āyatapārṣṇipādaḥ / utsaṅgapādaḥ / mṛdutaruṇahastapādaḥ / jālāṅgulihastapādaḥ / dīrghāṅguliradhaḥkramatalayormahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya cakre jāte ci (arciṣmatī prabhāsvare site) sahasrāre sanemike sanābhike / supratiṣṭhitasamapādo mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / anena mahārāja dvātriṃśattamena mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇena samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / na ca mahārāja cakravartināmevaṃvidhāni lakṣaṇāni bhavanti / bodhisattvānāṃ ca tādṛśāni lakṣaṇāni bhavanti //
body.translated_text: His generative organ is concealed in a sheath. Well-rounded thighs. Calves like those of an <s>eṇeya</s> deer-king. Long fingers. Feet with extended heels. Arched feet. Hands and feet soft and tender. Hands and feet with webbed fingers. Long-fingered, on the soles of both feet of the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, wheels have appeared — radiant, luminous, white, with a thousand spokes, with rims, with hubs. The prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, has well-established, even feet. By this thirty-second mark of a great being is the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> endowed. And, O great king, <s>Cakravartins</s> do not have such marks. Such marks belong to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: saṃvidyante khalu punarmahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasya kāye 'śītyanuvyañjanāni, yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro nārhatyagāramadhyāvasitum / avaśyamabhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai / katamāni ca mahārāja tānyaśītyanuvyañjanāni? tadyathā - tuṅganakhaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / tāmranakhaśca snigdhanakhaśca vṛttāṅguliśca anupūrvacitrāṅguliśca gūḍhaśiraśca gūḍhagulphaśca ghanasaṃdhiśca aviṣamasamapādaśca āyatapārṣṇiśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / snigdhapāṇilekhaśca tulyapāṇilekhaśca gambhīrapāṇilekhaśca ajihmapāṇilekhaśca anupūrvapāṇilekhaśca bimboṣṭhaśca noccavacanaśabdaśca mṛdutaruṇatāmrajihvaśca gajagarjitābhistanitameghasvaramadhuramañjughoṣaśca paripūrṇavyañjanaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / pralambabāhuśca śucigātravastusaṃpannaśca mṛdugātraśca viśālagātraśca adīnagātraśca anupūrvonnatagātraśca susamāhitagātraśca suvibhaktagātraśca pṛthuvipulasuparipūrṇajānumaṇḍalaśca vṛttagātraśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / suparimṛṣṭagātraśca ajihmavṛṣabhagātraśca anupūrvagātraśca gambhīranābhiśca ajihmanābhiśca anupūrvanābhiśca śucyācāraśca ṛṣabhavatsamantaprāsādikaśca paramasuviśuddhavitimirālokasamantaprabhaśca nāgavilambitagatiśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / siṃhavikrāntagatiśca ṛṣabhavikrāntagatiśca haṃsavikrāntagatiśca abhipradakṣiṇāvartagatiśca vṛttakukṣiśca mṛṣṭakukṣiśca ajihmakukṣiśca cāpodaraśca vyapagatachandadoṣanīlakālakāduṣṭaśarīraśca vṛttadaṃṣṭraśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraśca anupūrvadaṃṣṭraśca tuṅganāsaśca śucinayanaśca vimalanayanaśca prahasitanayanaśca āyatanayanaśca viśālanayanaśca nīlakuvalayadalasadṛśanayanaśca sahitabhrūśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / citrabhrūśca asitabhrūśca saṃgatabhrūśca anupūrvabhrūśca pīnagaṇḍaśca aviṣamagaṇḍaśca vyapagatagaṇḍadoṣaśca anupahatakruṣṭaśca suviditendriyaśca suparipūrṇendriyaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / saṃgatamukhalalāṭaśca paripūrṇottamāṅgaśca asitakeśaśca sahitakeśaśca (susaṃgatakeśaśca) surabhikeśaśca aparuṣakeśaśca anākulakeśaśca anupūrvakeśaśca sukuñcitakeśaśca śrīvatsasvastikanandyāvartavardhamānasaṃsthānakeśaśca mahārāja sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / imāni tāni mahārāja sarvārthasiddhasya kumārasyāśītyanuvyañjanāni,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O great king, on the body of the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> there are eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), endowed with which the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in a household. He will certainly go forth to the homeless life. And what are those eighty minor marks, O great king? Namely: The prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>, O great king, has raised nails, copper-colored nails, smooth nails, round fingers, variegated and tapering fingers, concealed veins, concealed ankles, compact joints, even and well-proportioned feet. Smooth palm-lines, equal palm-lines, deep palm-lines, straight palm-lines, orderly palm-lines, <s>bimba</s>-red lips, neither high nor low voice, a tongue soft, tender, and copper-colored, a voice like the trumpeting of an elephant, the rumbling of thunder, sweet and melodious, fully articulated speech. Long arms, clean and well-formed body-substance, soft body, broad body, unwearied body, a body rising in orderly proportion, a well-composed body, a well-divided body, broad, full, and well-rounded knee-caps, a symmetrical body. A well-polished body, a straight bull-like body, an orderly body, a deep navel, an unbent navel, an orderly navel, clean conduct, a bull-like all-around graciousness, supremely pure radiance free from obscurity shining in all directions, a gait swaying like an elephant's. A gait striding like a lion, striding like a bull, striding like a swan, a gait turning to the right, a round belly, a clean belly, an unbent belly, a bow-shaped abdomen, a body free from blemish, dark spots, moles, or corruption, round canine teeth. Sharp canine teeth, orderly canine teeth, a prominent nose, clean eyes, spotless eyes, smiling eyes, wide eyes, broad eyes, eyes like blue lotus petals, joined eyebrows. Variegated eyebrows, dark eyebrows, connected eyebrows, orderly eyebrows, full cheeks, even cheeks, cheeks free from defect, an unimpaired voice, well-discerned faculties, fully developed faculties. A harmonious face and forehead, a well-formed head, dark hair, thick hair, (well-joined hair), fragrant hair, not-rough hair, untangled hair, orderly hair, beautifully curled hair, hair arranged in the patterns of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>svastika</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, and <s>vardhamāna</s>. These, O great king, are the eighty minor marks of the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>,

body.text: yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro nārhatyagāramadhyāvasitum / avaśyamabhiniṣkramiṣyati pravrajyāyai //
body.translated_text: endowed with which the prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is not fit to dwell in a household. He will certainly go forth to the homeless life. //

body.text: atha khalu rājā śuddhodano 'sitasya maharṣeḥ sakāśātkumārasyedaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā saṃtuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāta utthāyāsanādbodhisattvasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatyemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having heard this prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) concerning the prince from the great sage <s>Asita</s>, was satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness. Rising from his seat, he bowed at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and spoke this verse —

children.text: vanditastvaṃ suraiḥ sendraiḥ ṛṣibhiścāsi pūjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are worshipped by the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, and honored by the sages;

children.text: vaidya sarvasya lokasya vande 'hamapi tvāṃ vibho // Lal_7.55 //
children.translated_text: O physician of the entire world, I too bow to you, O mighty one! // Lal_7.55 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano 'sitaṃ maharṣi sārdhaṃ naradattena bhāgineyenānurūpeṇa bhaktena saṃtarpayati sma / saṃtarpyābhicchādya pradakṣiṇamakarot / atha khalvasito maharṣistata evarddhyā vihāyasā prākramat, yena svāśramastenopāsaṃkrāmat //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> satisfied the great sage <s>Asita</s> together with his nephew <s>Naradatta</s> with a fitting meal. Having satisfied and honored him, he circumambulated him. Then the great sage <s>Asita</s> departed from that very place by supernatural power through the sky, going to his own hermitage. //

body.text: atha khalu dvayaṃ saṃkramya tatra khalvasito maharṣirnaradattaṃ māṇavakametadavocat - yadā tvaṃ naradatta śṛṇuyā buddho loke utpanna iti, tadā tva gatvā tasya śāsane pravrajeḥ / tatte bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāyeti //
body.translated_text: Then, after both had departed, the great sage <s>Asita</s> said to the young student <s>Naradatta</s>: 'When you hear, <s>Naradatta</s>, that a <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world, then go and take ordination in his dispensation. That will be for your long-lasting welfare, benefit, and happiness.' //

body.text: tatredamucyate -

children.text: dṛṣṭvā devagaṇānnabhastalagatān buddhaśravodgāriṇo
children.translated_text: Having seen the hosts of gods traversing the sky, proclaiming [the word] '<s>Buddha</s>,'

children.text: devarṣīrasito 'drikandaragataḥ prītiṃ parāṃ prāptavān /
children.translated_text: the divine sage <s>Asita</s>, dwelling in a mountain cave, attained supreme joy.

children.text: buddho nāma padaṃ kimetadiha bho harṣāvahaṃ prāṇināṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddha</s>' — what is this word that brings delight to living beings?

children.text: prahlāda mama kāya eti sukhitaṃ śāntaṃ ca cittaṃ param // Lal_7.56 //
children.translated_text: Rapture [pervades] my body, blissful and supremely serene is my mind. // Lal_7.56 //

body.translated_text: Hereupon this was said —

children.text: kiṃ devo tvasuro 'thavāpi sa bhaved garuḍo 'thavā kinnaraḥ
children.translated_text: Is he a god, or an <s>Asura</s>, or a <s>Garuḍa</s>, or a <s>Kinnara</s>?

children.text: buddho nāma kimetadaśrutapadaṃ prītikaraṃ modanam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddha</s>' — what is this unprecedented word that brings joy and delight?

children.text: divyā cakṣuṣa prekṣate daśa diśaḥ śailān mahīṃ sāgarān
children.translated_text: With the divine eye he surveys the ten directions — mountains, the earth, and oceans;

children.text: bhūyaḥ paśyati cādbhutaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhūmau girau sāgare // Lal_7.57 //
children.translated_text: again he beholds many wondrous things on the earth, on the mountains, in the oceans. // Lal_7.57 //

children.text: ābheyaṃ pravirājate surucirā prahlādayantī tanuṃ
children.translated_text: This radiance shines forth, exceedingly beautiful, gladdening the body,

children.text: jātāścaiva yathā hi śailaśikhare snigdhāḥ pravālāṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: just as smooth coral-shoots appear upon a mountain peak;

children.text: vṛkṣāścaiva yathā supuṣpabharitā nānāphalairmaṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: and just as trees are laden with abundant blossoms and adorned with various fruits —

children.text: suvyaktaṃ tribhave bhaviṣyati laghu ratnodbhavaḥ śobhanaḥ // Lal_7.58 //
children.translated_text: clearly, in the three realms of existence, a splendid jewel-birth will soon occur. // Lal_7.58 //

children.text: bhūmirbhāti yathā ca pāṇisadṛśā sarvā samā nirmalā
children.translated_text: The earth shines as if [smooth] as a palm, all level and stainless;

children.text: devāścaiva yathā prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ khe bhrāmayantyambarān /
children.translated_text: and gods, their minds exultant, whirl garments in the sky;

children.text: yadvat sāgaranāgarājanilaye ratnāḥ plavante 'dbhutāḥ
children.translated_text: just as wondrous jewels float in the abode of the ocean-<s>Nāga</s> king —

children.text: suvyaktaṃ jinaratna jambunilaye dharmākarasyodbhavaḥ // Lal_7.59 //
children.translated_text: clearly, in the <s>Jambu</s> continent, a <s>Jina</s>-jewel has arisen, a source of <s>Dharma</s>. // Lal_7.59 //

children.text: yadvacchānta apāya duḥkhavigatāḥ sattvāśca saukhyānvitāḥ
