children.translated_text: Since the lower realms are pacified, suffering gone, and beings endowed with happiness;

children.text: yadvaddevagaṇā nabhastalagatā gacchanti harṣānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: since hosts of gods traverse the sky, proceeding with delight;

children.text: yatha ca snigdharavaṃ manojña śṛṇuyā divyāna saṃgītināṃ
children.translated_text: since one hears the sweet, melodious, enchanting divine singing —

children.text: ratanasyā iva prādurbhāvu tribhave yasyā nimittā ime // Lal_7.60 //
children.translated_text: it is as if the manifestation of a [supreme] jewel [has occurred] in the three realms, of which these are the signs. // Lal_7.60 //

children.text: asitaḥ prekṣati jambusāhvayamidaṃ divyena vai cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s> surveys this <s>Jambu</s>[-continent] with the divine eye;

children.text: so 'drākṣīt kapilāhvaye puravare śuddhodanasyālaye /
children.translated_text: he saw in the foremost city called <s>Kapila</s>, in the abode of <s>Śuddhodana</s>,

children.text: jāto lakṣaṇapuṇyatejabharito nārāyaṇasthāmavān
children.translated_text: one born, filled with the splendor of [auspicious] marks and merit, possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā cāttamanā udagramanasaḥ sthāmāsya saṃvardhitaḥ // Lal_7.61 //
children.translated_text: having seen [him], delighted, with uplifted mind, his strength was increased. // Lal_7.61 //

children.text: udyuktastvarito 'tivismitamanā cāsau svaśiṣyānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: Eager, hastening, his mind filled with great wonder, accompanied by his disciple,

children.text: āgatvā kapilāhvayaṃ puravaraṃ dvāri sthito bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: having come to the foremost city called <s>Kapila</s>, he stood at the gate of the king.

children.text: anubaddhā bahuprāṇikoṭinayutā dṛṣṭvā ṛṣirjīrṇakaḥ
children.translated_text: Followed by many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of beings, an aged sage was seen;

children.text: avacī sārathi rājña vedaya laghuṃ dvāre ṛṣistiṣṭhati // Lal_7.62 //
children.translated_text: the charioteer said: 'Announce quickly to the king — at the gate a sage stands!' // Lal_7.62 //

children.text: śrutvā cāśu praviśya rājabhavanaṃ rājñastamākhyātavān
children.translated_text: Having heard, swiftly entering the royal palace, he announced to the king:

children.text: dvāre deva tapasvi tiṣṭhati mahān jīrṇo ṛṣirjarjaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'At the gate, O lord, stands a great ascetic, aged, a venerable sage, decrepit.

children.text: so cāpī abhinandate ṛṣivaraḥ prāveṣṭu rājño gṛhaṃ
children.translated_text: And that best of sages is delighted to enter the king's house;

children.text: ājñā dīyatu tāva pārthivavarā demi praveśaṃ tesā // Lal_7.63 //
children.translated_text: may the command be given, O best of kings — I shall grant him entry.' // Lal_7.63 //

children.text: sthāpyā cāsanamasya cāha nṛpatiḥ gaccha praveśaṃ dada
children.translated_text: 'Set a seat for him,' said the king, 'go, grant him entry.'

children.text: asitaḥ sārathivākya śrutva muditaḥ prītyā sukhenānvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s>, hearing the charioteer's word, was delighted, filled with joy and happiness,

children.text: śītaṃ vāri yathābhikāṅkṣi tṛṣito bhuktvādito cāśanaṃ
children.translated_text: like one who, thirsty, [finds] cool water that he craves, having eaten food before —

children.text: tadvatsukhyabhinandito ṛṣivaraḥ taṃ draṣṭu sattvottamam // Lal_7.64 //
children.translated_text: just so, delighted in happiness, the best of sages [went] to see that supreme being. // Lal_7.64 //

children.text: jaya bhoḥ pārthiva ityuvāca mudito cāyuṃ ciraṃ pālaya
children.translated_text: 'Victory, O king!' he said joyfully, 'Long may you guard your life!'

children.text: vṛddhiṃ kṛtva niṣaṇṇa dāntamanasaḥ śāntendriyaḥ sūrataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having exchanged greetings, he sat down, tamed in mind, with senses pacified, of gentle disposition.

children.text: rājā vai abhivādya taṃ sunibhṛtaṃ provāca kiṃ kāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: The king, bowing to him respectfully, said: 'What is the reason

children.text: āgāmastava pārthivendra nilaye tad brūhi śīghraṃ mune // Lal_7.65 //
children.translated_text: you have come to the abode of this sovereign? Tell [me] quickly, O sage!' // Lal_7.65 //

children.text: putraste vararūpa pāramigato jāto mahātejavān
children.translated_text: 'A son has been born to you, of supreme form, who has gone to the [other] shore, of great splendor,

children.text: dvātriṃśadvaralakṣaṇaiḥ kavacito nārāyaṇasthāmavān /
children.translated_text: armored with the thirty-two excellent marks, possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: taṃ draṣṭuṃ hi mamepsitaṃ narapate sarvārthasiddhaṃ śiśum
children.translated_text: To see him is my desire, O lord of men — the child <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>;

children.text: ityarthaṃ samupāgato 'smi nṛpate nāstyanyakāryaṃ mama // Lal_7.66 //
children.translated_text: for this purpose I have come, O king — I have no other business.' // Lal_7.66 //

children.text: sādhu svāgatu yācase kilamitaḥ prīto 'smi te darśanāt
children.translated_text: 'Welcome! Excellent! You ask for [what I gladly grant]; I am delighted at your visit.

children.text: eṣo 'sau śayitaḥ kumāra varado draṣṭuṃ na śakyo 'dhunā /
children.translated_text: Here is that prince, the bestower of boons, lying down — he cannot be seen just now.

children.text: sādhū tāva mūhūrtamāgama ihā yad drakṣyase nirmalaṃ
children.translated_text: Wait but a moment here — you shall see him, the stainless one,

children.text: candraṃ vā yatha pūrṇamāsi vimalaṃ tārāgaṇairmaṇḍitam // Lal_7.67 //
children.translated_text: like the full moon on a clear night, adorned by the host of stars.' // Lal_7.67 //

children.text: yada cāsau pratibuddha sārathivaraḥ paripūrṇacandraprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: When that [prince] awakened, the foremost charioteer [announced it], he whose radiance equals the full moon;

children.text: tada rājā pratigṛhya vahnivapuṣaṃ sūryātirekaprabham /
children.translated_text: then the king, taking up [the child] of fire-like form, whose radiance surpasses the sun,

children.text: hantā paśya ṛṣe nṛdevamahitaṃ hemāgrabimbopamam
children.translated_text: [said]: 'Come, behold, O sage, the one honored by men and gods, like an image of supreme gold!'

children.text: asito dṛṣṭva ca tasya tau sucaraṇau cakrāṅkitau śobhanau // Lal_7.68 //
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s>, seeing those two beautiful feet marked with wheels — // Lal_7.68 //

children.text: pratyutthāya tataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo caraṇāni so vandate
children.translated_text: rising, with palms joined, he worshipped [the child's] feet;

children.text: aṅke gṛhya mahātmaśāstrakuśalo nidhyāyato prekṣate /
children.translated_text: taking him on his lap, the great-souled one, skilled in the treatises, gazed contemplatively.

children.text: so 'paśyadvaralakṣaṇaiḥ kavacitaṃ nārāyaṇasthāmavaṃ
children.translated_text: He saw [the child] armored with the excellent marks, possessing the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: śīrṣaṃ kampya sa vedaśāstrakuśalo dve tasya paśyadgatī // Lal_7.69 //
children.translated_text: shaking his head, that one skilled in the <s>Vedas</s> and treatises saw two destinies for him. // Lal_7.69 //

children.text: rājā vā bhavi cakravarti balavān buddho va lokottamaḥ
children.translated_text: Either he will become a powerful <s>Cakravartin</s> king, or a <s>Buddha</s>, the highest in the world;

children.text: bāṣpaṃ tyakta sudīnakāyamanaso gambhīra niśvasya ca /
children.translated_text: shedding tears, dejected in body and mind, sighing deeply —

children.text: udvignaśca babhūva pārthivavaraḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇo roditī
children.translated_text: The best of kings became alarmed: 'Why does the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> weep?

children.text: mā vighnaṃ khalu paśyate 'yamasitaḥ sarvārthasiddhasya me // Lal_7.70 //
children.translated_text: Surely no obstacle is seen for my <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>!' // Lal_7.70 //

children.text: bhūtaṃ vyāhara kiṃ tu rodiṣi ṛṣe śreyo 'tha kiṃ pāpakaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Speak the truth — why do you weep, O sage? Is it auspicious, or is it evil?'

children.text: pāpaṃ nāsti na cāntarāyamiha bhoḥ sarvārthasiddhasya te /
children.translated_text: 'There is no evil, nor any obstacle here, O lord, for your <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>;

children.text: ātmānaṃ bahu śocamī narapate jīrṇo 'smi yajjarjaraḥ
children.translated_text: it is for myself that I grieve much, O king — I am old and decrepit,

children.text: yadayaṃ bheṣyati buddha lokamahito dharmaṃ yadā vakṣyate // Lal_7.71 //
children.translated_text: for when this one shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, honored by the world, when he shall preach the <s>Dharma</s> — // Lal_7.71 //

children.text: na drakṣe ahu labdhaprītimanaso ityartha rodāmyahaṃ
children.translated_text: I shall not see it! Therefore I weep, I who have found delight of mind.'

children.text: yasyā kāyi bhavanti lakṣaṇavarā dvātriṃśati nirmalā /
children.translated_text: 'He on whose body are the thirty-two supreme marks, stainless —

children.text: dve tasyā gatayo na anya tṛtiyā jānīṣva evaṃ nṛpa
children.translated_text: for him there are two destinies, no other third — know this, O king:

children.text: rājā vā bhavi cakravarti balavān buddho 'tha lokottamaḥ // Lal_7.72 //
children.translated_text: either he becomes a mighty <s>Cakravartin</s> king, or a <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost in the world. // Lal_7.72 //

children.text: nāyaṃ kāmaguṇebhirarthiku punaḥ buddho ayaṃ bheṣyati
children.translated_text: This one will not desire sense-pleasures — he shall become a <s>Buddha</s>.'

children.text: śrutvā vyākaraṇaṃ ṛṣeḥ sa nṛpatiḥ prītiṃ sukhaṃ labdhavān /
children.translated_text: Having heard the sage's prophecy, that king obtained delight and happiness.

children.text: pratyutthāya tataḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo caraṇāvasau vandate
children.translated_text: Rising up, with palms joined, he bowed at [the sage's] feet:

children.text: devaistvaṃ svabhipūjitaḥ subalavān ṛṣibhiśca saṃvarṇitaḥ // Lal_7.73 //
children.translated_text: 'You are well-worshiped by the gods, O mighty one, and praised by the sages!' // Lal_7.73 //

body.text:
vande tvāṃ varasārthavāha tribhave sarve jage pūjitaṃ
asitaḥ prāha ca bhāgineya muditaḥ saṃśrūyatāṃ bhāṣato /
body.translated_text: 'I salute you, O excellent caravan-leader, worshiped in all the three worlds and in the entire universe!' And <s>Asita</s> spoke joyfully to his nephew: 'Listen to what I say —

body.text: buddhā bodhi yadā śṛṇoṣi jagato varteti cakraṃ hyayaṃ
body.translated_text: when you hear that this [child] has awakened to <s>Bodhi</s> and turns the Wheel for the world,

body.text: śīghraṃ pravraja śāsane 'sya munaye tatprāpsyase nirvṛtim // Lal_7.74 //
body.translated_text: go forth quickly into the teaching of this sage — thereby you shall attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!' // Lal_7.74 //

children.text: vanditvā caraṇau hyasau munivaraḥ kṛtvā ca prādakṣiṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Having bowed at the feet of the supreme sage and made circumambulation,

children.text: lābhā te nṛpate sulabdha vipulā yasyedṛśaste sutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Great are your gains, O king — well-gained and vast — [you] whose son is such as this!

children.text: eṣo loka sadevakaṃ samanujaṃ dharmeṇa tarpeṣyati
children.translated_text: He shall satisfy the world with its gods and humans through the <s>Dharma</s>.'

children.text: niṣkrāmaṃ kapilāhvayādṛṣivaro 'raṇye sthitaḥ svāśrame // Lal_7.75 //
children.translated_text: Departing from [the city] called <s>Kapilā</s>, the foremost sage remained in the forest, in his own hermitage. // Lal_7.75 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo jātamātrasya bodhisattvasya maheśvaro devaputraḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikān devaputrānāmantryaivamāha - yo 'sau mārṣā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrasukṛtakarmadānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyaśratacaraṇavratatapaḥsucaritacaraṇaḥ mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāmahāmuditāsamanvāgataḥ upekṣāsamudgatacittaḥ sarvasattvahitasukhodyataḥ dṛḍhavīryakavacasusaṃnāhasaṃnaddhaḥ pūrvajinakṛtakuśalamūloditaḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaḥ sukṛtaniścayaparākramaḥ paracakrapramathanaḥ suvimalaśuddhāśayasaṃpannaḥ sucaritacaraṇo mahājñānaketudhvajaḥ mārabalāntakaraṇaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasrasārthavāhaḥ devamanuṣyapūjitamahāyajñayaṣṭaḥ susamṛddhapuṇyanicayaniḥsaraṇābhiprāyo jātijarāmaraṇāntakaraḥ sujātajātaḥ ikṣvākurājakulasaṃbhūto jagadvibodhayitā bodhisattvo mahāsattvo manuṣyaloka upapannaḥ / na cirādasāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / hanta gacchāmastamabhivandituṃ mānayituṃ pūjayitumabhistotumanyeṣāṃ ca mānābhibhūtānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ mānamadadarpacchedanārtham / te 'smānabhivandamānān dṛṣṭvā te 'pi bodhisattvaṃ vandiṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti ca / tatteṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya yāvadamṛtādhigamāya / rājñaśca śuddhodanasya jayavṛddhiranuśrāvitā bhaviṣyati / tattvavyākaraṇena ca bodhisattvaṃ vyākṛtya punarapyāgamiṣyāma iti //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had just been born, <s>Maheśvara</s> <s>devaputra</s> addressed the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s> thus: 'Sirs, he who through innumerable <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands [of lives] has practiced well-performed deeds of generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, skillful means, and good conduct with vows and austerities; who is endowed with great loving-kindness, great compassion, and great joy; whose mind has arisen in equanimity; who strives for the welfare and happiness of all beings; who is well-armored with the armor of firm vigor; who has arisen from the wholesome roots planted under former <s>Jinas</s>; who is adorned with the marks [born of] a hundred merits; whose endeavor is firm in well-performed resolve; who crushes the forces of enemies; who is endowed with a supremely stainless, pure intention; who is of good conduct, bearing the banner of great knowledge; who makes an end of <s>Māra</s>'s forces; who is the caravan-leader of the trichiliocosm; who has sacrificed at the great sacrifice worshiped by gods and humans; who intends to emerge from the well-accumulated store of merit; who makes an end of birth, old age, and death; who is well-born of noble birth; who has arisen in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> royal lineage; the awakener of the world — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> has appeared in the human world. Before long he will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. Come, let us go to worship him, honor him, make offerings to him, praise him, and to cut off the pride, intoxication, and arrogance of other <s>devaputras</s> overcome by pride. Seeing us pay homage, they too will worship, honor, and make offerings to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. That will be for their long-term benefit, welfare, and happiness, even up to the attainment of the deathless. And a proclamation of victory and prosperity shall be made for King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having prophesied the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a truthful prophecy, we shall return again.'

body.text: atha khalu maheśvaro devaputro dvādaśabhirdevaputraśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ sarvakapilavastumahānagaramavabhāsena sphurayitvā yena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya dauvārike nivedya rājñābhyanujñāto rājakulaṃ praviśya bodhisattvasya pādau śirasābhivandyaikāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvāṃ anekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bodhisattvamaṅke samāropya rājānaṃ śuddhodanamāśvāsayati sma - tuṣṭo mahārāja bhava paramaprītaśca / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yathā mahārāja bodhisattvasya lakṣaṇairanuvyañjanaiśca kāyaḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ, yathā ca kumāro 'bhibhavati sadevamānuṣāsuralokaṃ varṇena tejasā ca yaśasā lakṣmyā ca, niḥsaṃśayaṃ mahārāja bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s> <s>devaputra</s>, surrounded and preceded by twelve hundred thousand <s>devaputras</s>, having illuminated the entire great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> with radiance, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s dwelling. Having approached, informing the doorkeeper, and being admitted by the king, he entered the royal household. Having bowed his head at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having made circumambulation many hundreds of thousands of times, having placed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on his lap, he reassured King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Be content, Great King, and supremely delighted! For what reason? Great King, just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body is adorned with the marks and minor marks, and just as the prince surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s> in beauty, splendor, glory, and majesty — without doubt, Great King, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo maheśvaro devaputraḥ sārdhaṃ śuddhāvāsakāyikairdevaputrairbodhisattvasya mahatpūjopasthānaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattvaṃ tattvavyākaraṇena vyākṛtya punarapi svabhavanaṃ prākrāmat //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, <s>Maheśvara</s> <s>devaputra</s>, together with the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s>, having performed great worship and attendance upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having prophesied the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a truthful prophecy, departed again to his own abode.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: jātasya tasya guṇasāgarasāgarasya jñātvā sureśvaramarud bruvate udagraḥ /
children.translated_text: When that ocean of virtues was born, the supreme lord of the gods, having learned [of it], spoke joyfully to the <s>Maruts</s>:

children.text: yasyā sudurlabhaśravo bahukalpakoṭyā hantetha taṃ vrajama pūjayituṃ munīndram // Lal_7.76 //
children.translated_text: 'He whose fame is exceedingly rare [even] over many <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s> — come, let us go to worship this lord of sages!' // Lal_7.76 //

children.text: paripūrṇadvādaśasahasra marudviśuddhā maṇiratnacūḍasamalaṃkṛta iryavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Twelve thousand <s>Maruts</s> in full, supremely pure, adorned with gem-jewel crests, of stately bearing,

children.text: kapilāhvayaṃ puravaraṃ samupetya śīghraṃ dvāri sthitā narapateḥ suvilambacūḍāḥ // Lal_7.77 //
children.translated_text: approached swiftly the excellent city called <s>Kapilā</s>, with their long crests, and stood at the gate of the king. // Lal_7.77 //

children.text: te dvārapālamavadan sumanojñaghoṣāḥ prativedayasva nṛpate bhavanaṃ praviśya /
children.translated_text: They spoke to the gate-keeper in sweet, melodious tones: 'Announce [us], having entered the king's dwelling!'

children.text: dauvāriko vacana śrutva gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ prahvaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo nṛpatiṃ babhāṣe // Lal_7.78 //
children.translated_text: The doorkeeper, having heard the words, entered the house, and bowing with palms joined, addressed the king: // Lal_7.78 //

children.text: jaya deva nityamanupālaya dīrghamāyuḥ dvāre sthitā vipulapuṇyaviśuddhabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Victory, O Lord! May you ever preserve a long life! At the gate stand [beings] of vast merit, of purified radiance,

children.text: maṇiratnacūḍasuvibhūṣita iryavantaḥ paripūrṇacandravadanā śaśinirmalābhāḥ // Lal_7.79 //
children.translated_text: adorned with gem-jewel crests, splendidly ornamented, of stately bearing, their faces like the full moon, of stainless lunar brilliance. // Lal_7.79 //

children.text: chāyāṃ na teṣa nṛpate kvacidapyapaśyan śabdaṃ na caiva caraṇotkṣipaṇe śṛṇomi /
children.translated_text: I see no shadow of theirs anywhere, O king; nor do I hear any sound when they raise their feet;

children.text: na ca medinīṃ vicarato rajamutkṣipanti tṛptiṃ na yānti ca janāḥ samudīkṣatāṃ vai // Lal_7.80 //
children.translated_text: nor do they raise dust from the earth as they walk — and people find no satiation in gazing upon them! // Lal_7.80 //

children.text: kāyaprabhā suvipulā ca vibhāti teṣāṃ vācā manojña yatha nāsti ha mānuṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: Their bodily radiance shines vast and broad; their speech is pleasing, unlike that of humans —

children.text: gambhiraślakṣṇasuśilā ca suākarā ca śaṅkā hi me suragaṇā na hi te manuṣyāḥ // Lal_7.81 //
children.translated_text: deep, smooth, gentle, and melodious — my suspicion is that these are hosts of gods, not humans! // Lal_7.81 //

children.text: varapuṣpamālyaanulepanapaṭṭadāmā pāṇī gṛhītvana udīkṣiṣu gauraveṇa /
children.translated_text: With excellent flowers, garlands, ointments, and silk banners in their hands, they look up with reverence;

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ nṛpati draṣṭu kumāramete devādhideva marutāgata pūjanārtham // Lal_7.82 //
children.translated_text: without doubt, O king, these gods have come to see the prince — gods beyond gods, <s>Maruts</s> come for worship!' // Lal_7.82 //

children.text: rājā niśāmya vacanaṃ paramaṃ udagro gacchā bhaṇāhi praviśantu gṛhaṃ bhavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king, hearing the words, supremely elated [said]: 'Go, tell them — let the noble ones enter the house!

children.text: na hi mānuṣāṇa iyamīdṛśa ṛddhi kāci yatha bhāṣase ca guṇa teṣa yathā ca iryā // Lal_7.83 //
children.translated_text: For humans do not possess such supernatural power as you describe, nor such qualities, nor such bearing.' // Lal_7.83 //

children.text: dauvārikaḥ kṛtapuṭo marutaivamāha praviśī bhavanta anujñātu narādhipena /
children.translated_text: The doorkeeper, with palms joined, spoke thus to the <s>Maruts</s>: 'Enter, noble ones — permission is given by the king of men.'

children.text: te hṛṣṭatuṣṭamanaso varamālyahastā gehaṃ praviṣṭa nṛpateramarālayaṃ vā // Lal_7.84 //
children.translated_text: They, delighted and satisfied, with excellent garlands in hand, entered the king's dwelling — or was it the abode of the immortals? // Lal_7.84 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ suravarāṃ praviśanta gehaṃ pratyutthito nṛpatirañjali saṃpragṛhya /
children.translated_text: Seeing those supreme gods entering the dwelling, the king rose up, grasping his palms joined [in salutation]:

children.text: saṃvidyayanta ima āsana ratnapādā atrā niṣīdata bhavannanukampya buddhyā // Lal_7.85 //
children.translated_text: 'Here are these jewel-footed seats prepared — sit here, noble ones, with compassionate intent!' // Lal_7.85 //

children.text: te mānadarpavigatā sthita āsaneṣu yasyārthi āgata ihā nṛpate śṛṇuṣva /
children.translated_text: They, free from pride and arrogance, seated upon the seats, [said]: 'For what purpose we have come here, O king, listen:

children.text: putrastavātipṛthupuṇyaviśuddhakāyo jātaḥ sujātacaraṇaṃ vaya draṣṭukāmāḥ // Lal_7.86 //
children.translated_text: your son, whose body is purified by supremely vast merit, is well-born — we wish to see his [auspicious] feet.' // Lal_7.86 //

children.text: asmo vidhijña varalakṣaṇalakṣaṇajñā yeṣāṃ tathā bhavati yā gati yaḥ prayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We are knowers of ritual, knowers of the excellent marks and their characteristics — for whom such destinies and practices exist [we can determine];

children.text: tatsādhu pārthivavara prajahasva khedaṃ paśyāma lakṣaṇavicitravibhūṣitāṅgam // Lal_7.87 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O best of kings, abandon anxiety — let us see [his] limbs adorned with variegated marks!' // Lal_7.87 //

children.text: sa strīgaṇaiḥ parivṛto nṛpatiḥ prahṛṣṭo gṛhya kumāramasamaṃ jvalanārcivarṇam /
children.translated_text: The king, delighted, surrounded by groups of women, taking the prince — incomparable, of blazing flame-like radiance —

children.text: upanāmayan suravarāṃ suvilambacūḍāṃ dvārāttu niṣkramatu kampita trisahasrāḥ // Lal_7.88 //
children.translated_text: presented [him] to those supreme gods with long crests; but as he emerged from the door, the trichiliocosm trembled! // Lal_7.88 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvaiva te suravarā krama nāyakasya tāmrā nakhāṃ vimalapatraviśuddhatejā /
children.translated_text: As soon as those supreme gods beheld the leader's feet — copper-nailed, of stainless, pure, leaf-like radiance —

children.text: te utthitā tvarita rūpavilambacūḍā mūrdhnābhivandiṣu kramāṃ vimalaprabhasya // Lal_7.89 //
children.translated_text: they rose up swiftly, those of beautiful form and long crests, and bowed their heads at the feet of that one of stainless brilliance. // Lal_7.89 //

body.text: yatha lakṣaṇā yatha ca darśita lakṣitā ca yatha puṇyateji śiri mūrdha vilokitaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Seeing such marks as are displayed and indicated, seeing the splendor of merit and glory upon his head,

body.text: yatha irya netra vimalāprabha ūrṇakośā niḥsaṃśayaṃ spṛśati bodhi vijitya māram // Lal_7.90 //
body.translated_text: seeing his bearing, his eyes, his stainless brilliance, his <s>ūrṇā</s>-curl — without doubt he shall touch <s>Bodhi</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s>! // Lal_7.90 //

children.text: te taṃ stuvanti guṇabhūta yathārthadarśī dhyāyī guṇāṃ vigatakleśatamonudasya /
children.translated_text: They praised that treasury of virtues, the seer of truth as it is, the meditator on the virtues of him who dispels the darkness of afflictions:

children.text: sucireṇa sattvaratanasya hi prādurbhāvo jātījarāmaraṇakleśaraṇaṃjahasya // Lal_7.91 //
children.translated_text: 'After a very long time is the appearance of this jewel among beings — the one who abandons the afflictions of birth, old age, and death! // Lal_7.91 //

children.text: ādīpta sarvatribhavaṃ tribhiragnitaptaṃ saṃkalparāgaviṣayāraṇiucchritena /
children.translated_text: All the three realms are ablaze, heated by the three fires, with the fire-stick of desire and passion raised in conceptual fabrication;

children.text: tvaṃ dharmamegha trisahasra spharitva dhīrā amṛtodakena praśameṣyasi kleśatāpam // Lal_7.92 //
children.translated_text: you, O steadfast one, spreading the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud over the trichiliocosm, shall quench the heat of afflictions with the water of the deathless! // Lal_7.92 //

children.text: tvaṃ maitravākya karuṇānvita ślakṣṇavākya brahmasvarāracitaghoṣa manojñavāṇi /
children.translated_text: You of loving speech, compassionate, of gentle words, with a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice, of charming, delightful utterance,

children.text: trisahasra ājñaparivijñapanī jagasya kṣipraṃ pramuñca bhagavan mahabuddhaghoṣam // Lal_7.93 //
children.translated_text: making known the teaching to the trichiliocosm for the world — quickly release, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great <s>Buddha</s>-sound! // Lal_7.93 //

children.text: bhagnā kutīrthikagaṇā viparītadṛṣṭiḥ bhavarāgabandhananimagna sthitā bhavāgre /
children.translated_text: The hosts of false <s>tīrthikas</s> with their wrong views shall be broken — those submerged in the bonds of passion for existence, dwelling at the summit of existence;

children.text: hetu pratītya bhava śūnya śruṇitva dharmā siṃhasya kroṣṭukagaṇaiva palāyināste // Lal_7.94 //
children.translated_text: hearing the <s>Dharma</s> [that teaches] dependent origination, emptiness — like packs of jackals before a lion, they shall flee! // Lal_7.94 //

children.text: bhittvā avidyapaṭalaṃ mahakleśadhūmaṃ paryutthitā janataye niyataprakāśe /
children.translated_text: Having pierced the covering of ignorance, the smoke of the great afflictions risen up over beings, with the certainty of illumination,

children.text: jñānārciprajñaprabhavidyuvilokitena sarvaṃ jage vidhamaye mahadandhakāram // Lal_7.95 //
children.translated_text: with the flame of knowledge, the light of wisdom, and the lightning-flash of insight — dispel all the great darkness in the world! // Lal_7.95 //

children.text: lābhā sulabdha vipulā marumānuṣāṇāṃ yatrodbhavā 'dbhuta ihedṛśi śuddhasattve /
children.translated_text: Great are the gains, well-gained and vast, of gods and humans, where there is the wondrous arising of such a pure being;

children.text: pithitā apāyapatha sphīta marutpathāni bheṣyanti sattvaratanena vibodhakena // Lal_7.96 //
children.translated_text: the paths of the lower realms shall be closed, the paths of the gods made abundant — [all] by this jewel among beings, the awakener!' // Lal_7.96 //

children.text: varṣitva divyakusumāṃ kapilāhvaye 'smin kṛtvā pradakṣiṇa stavitva ca gauraveṇa /
children.translated_text: Having rained divine flowers upon this [city] called <s>Kapilā</s>, having made circumambulation and praised [him] with reverence,

children.text: buddha subuddha iti vākyamudīrayantaḥ prakrānta te suragaṇā gagane salīlāḥ // Lal_7.97 //
children.translated_text: uttering the words '<s>Buddha</s>! Well-awakened!' — those hosts of gods departed playfully into the sky. // Lal_7.97 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare janmaparivarto nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Birth' (<s>Janmaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 8
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 8.

body.text: devakulopanayanaparivarto 'ṣṭamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Eighth Chapter: On Being Taken to the Temple (<s>Devakulopanayanaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāmeva rātriṃ bodhisattvo jātastasyāmeva rātryāṃ viṃśati kanyāsahasrāṇi kṣatriyabrāhmaṇanaigamagṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu jātāḥ / tāśca sarvā mātāpitṛbhirbodhisattvāya dattā upasthānaparicaryāyai / viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi rājñā śuddhodanena dattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai / viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi mitrāmātyātmajñātisālohitairdattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai / viṃśati ca kanyāsahasrāṇi amātyapārṣadyairdattāni bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāyai //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, on that very night when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born, twenty thousand maidens were born in <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, guild-merchant, and great householder families. All of them were given by their parents to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for attendance and service. Twenty thousand maidens were also given by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service. Twenty thousand maidens were given by friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relatives for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service. And twenty thousand maidens were given by the minister-attendants for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendance and service.

body.text: tadā ca bhikṣavo mahallakamahallikāḥ śākyāḥ saṃnipatya rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ - yatkhalu deva jānīyāḥ - devakulaṃ kumāra upanīyatāmiti / rājā āha - sādhu, upanīyatāṃ kumāraḥ / tena hi maṇḍyatāṃ nagaram / upaśobhyantāṃ vīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇarathyāmukhāni / apanīyantāmamaṅgalyāḥ kāṇakubjabadhirāndhamūkavisaṃsthitavirūparūpā aparipūrṇendriyāḥ / upanāmyantāṃ maṅgalāni / ghuṣyantāṃ puṇyabheryaḥ / tāḍyantāṃ maṅgalyaghaṇṭāḥ / samalaṃkriyantāṃ puravaradvārāṇi / vādyantāṃ sumanojñatūryatālāvacarāṇi / saṃnipātyantāṃ sarvakoṭṭarājānaḥ / ekībhavantu śreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyadauvārikapāriṣadyāḥ / yujyantāṃ kanyārathāḥ / upanāmyantāṃ pūrṇakumbhāḥ / saṃnipātyantāmadhīyānā brāhmaṇāḥ / alaṃkriyantāṃ devakulāni / iti hi bhikṣavo yathoktapūrvaṃ sarvaṃ kṛtamabhūt //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the elder Śākya men and women, having assembled, approached King Śuddhodana and said thus: 'May the lord know — let the prince be taken to the temple!' The king said: 'Very well, let the prince be taken. Therefore let the city be adorned! Let the streets, squares, crossroads, market-lanes, and carriage-ways be beautified! Let those of ill omen — the one-eyed, hunchbacked, deaf, blind, mute, deformed, and those with deficient faculties — be removed! Let auspicious things be brought forth! Let the drums of merit be sounded! Let the auspicious bells be struck! Let the gates of the excellent city be decorated! Let the most pleasant musical instruments, cymbals, and percussion be played! Let all the fortress-kings be assembled! Let the guild-masters, householders, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers come together! Let the maidens' chariots be yoked! Let full pitchers be brought forth! Let the Brāhmaṇas who are learned in the Vedas be assembled! Let the temples be decorated!' Thus, O monks, everything was done as ordered. //

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviśya mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīmāmantryaivamāha - alaṃkriyantāṃ kumāraḥ devakulamupaneṣyata iti / sādhviti pratiśrutya mahāprajāpatī gautamī kumāraṃ maṇḍayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, entering his own house, addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> thus: 'Let the prince be adorned — he is to be taken to the temple.' 'Very well,' agreed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>, and she adorned the prince. //

body.text: tataḥ kumāro maṇḍyamānaḥ prahasitavadano vyapagatabhṛkuṭikaḥ paramamadhurayā vācā mātṛsvasāramevamāha - amba kutrāhamupaneṣyata iti / āha - devakulaṃ putreti / tataḥ kumāraḥ smitamupadarśayan prahasitavadano mātṛsvasāraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the prince, while being adorned, with a smiling face and unfurrowed brow, said to his maternal aunt in the sweetest voice: 'Dear mother, where am I being taken?' She said: 'To the temple, my son.' Then the prince, displaying a smile, with a laughing face, addressed his maternal aunt in verses —

children.text: jātasya mahyamiha kampita trisahasraṃ śakraśca brahma asurāśca mahoragāśca /
children.translated_text: 'When I was born, the trichiliocosm trembled; <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and great <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: candraśca sūrya tatha vaiśravaṇaḥ kumāro mūrdhnā krameṣu nipatitva namasyayanti // Lal_8.1 //
children.translated_text: the Moon, the Sun, and the prince <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> — [all] fell at [my] feet and paid homage with their heads. // Lal_8.1 //

children.text: katamo 'nyu deva mama uttari yo viśiṣṭo yasmin mama praṇayase tvamihādya amba /
children.translated_text: What other god is there who is superior or more distinguished than me, to whom you would now bring me here, dear mother?

children.text: devātideva ahu uttamu sarvadevaiḥ devo na me 'sti sadṛśaḥ kuta uttaraṃ vā // Lal_8.2 //
children.translated_text: I am the god surpassing gods, supreme among all gods — there is no god equal to me, much less a superior! // Lal_8.2 //

body.text: lokānuvartana pratī iti amba yāsye dṛṣtvā vikurvita mamā janatā udagrāḥ /
body.translated_text: But to conform to worldly custom, dear mother, I shall go. Having seen my miraculous display, the people will be elated.

body.text: adhimātru gaurava kariṣyati citrakāraḥ jñāsyanti devamanujā svaya devadevaḥ // Lal_8.3 //
body.translated_text: The artist will show [even] greater reverence toward the mother — gods and humans shall themselves know [me as] the god of gods!' // Lal_8.3 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ sarvairvarṇaiḥ stutimaṅgalaiḥ pratyupasthitairaparimitālaṃkārālaṃkṛteṣu vīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇamukheṣvantaḥpure kumārasya rathamalaṃkṛtya rājā śuddhodano brāhmaṇanaigamaśreṣṭhigṛhapatyamātyakoṭṭarājadauvārikapāriṣadyamitrajñātiparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dhūpanadhūpitena muktapuṣpābhikīrṇena hayagajarathapattikalilenocchritachatradhvajapatākena nānātūryasaṃpravāditena mārgeṇa kumāraṃ gṛhītvā gacchati sma / devatāśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvasya rathaṃ vahanti sma / anekāni ca devaputrāpsaraḥkoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi gaganatalagatāni puṣpavarṣāṇyabhipravarṣanti sma / tūryāṇi ca pravādayanti sma / iti hi rājā śuddhodano mahatā rājavyūhena mahatā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena kumāraṃ gṛhītvā devakulaṃ praviśati sma / samanantarapratiṣṭhāpitaśca bodhisattvena dakṣiṇaścaraṇayoḥ kramatalastasmin devakule atha tā acetanyo devapratimāḥ tadyathā - śivaskandanārāyaṇakuberacandrasūryavaiśravaṇaśakrabrahmalokapālaprabhṛtayaḥ pratimāḥ - sarvāḥ svebhyaḥ svebhyaḥ sthānebhyo vyutthāya bodhisattvasya kramatalayornipatanti sma / tatra devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilakilāpramukhaiḥ prakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan / cailavikṣepāṇi cākārṣuḥ / sarvaṃ ca kapilavastumahānagaraṃ ṣaṅvikāraṃ prākampitam / divyāni ca kusumāni prāvarṣan / tūryaśatasahasrāṇi cāghaṭṭitāni praṇeduḥ / yeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ tāḥ pratimāḥ, te sarve svasvarūpamupadarśyemā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when all the castes had arrived with praises and auspicious [greetings], and the streets, squares, crossroads, market-lanes, and entranceways had been adorned with immeasurable decorations, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> — surrounded and attended by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, guild-leaders, chief householders, ministers, fortress-kings, doorkeepers, courtiers, friends, and kinsmen — taking the prince in his chariot adorned within the inner palace, went along a road fumigated with incense, strewn with flowers, thronging with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, with raised parasols, banners, and pennants, and resounding with various musical instruments. Hundreds of thousands of deities bore the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s chariot. Many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>Devaputras</s> and <s>Apsarases</s> stationed in the sky rained down showers of flowers and played musical instruments. Thus King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with a great royal array, with great royal magnificence, with great royal power, taking the prince, entered the temple. The moment the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet were set down, the soles touching [the ground] in that temple, then those lifeless deity-images — namely, the images of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the World-Guardians and others — all rose from their respective places and fell at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet. At that, hundreds of thousands of gods and men uttered hundreds of thousands of exclamations — cries of 'Hī hī!', shouts of 'Kila kila!', and other ejaculations. They waved their garments. The entire great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> trembled with the six kinds of shaking. Divine flowers rained down. Hundreds of thousands of untouched musical instruments sounded forth. And the gods whose images those were — they all, revealing their own true forms, spoke these verses —

children.text: no merū girirāja parvatavaro jātū name sarṣape
children.translated_text: 'Never does <s>Meru</s>, king of mountains, the supreme peak, bow to a mustard seed;

children.text: no vā sāgara nāgarājanilayo jātū name goṣpade /
children.translated_text: never does the ocean, abode of the king of <s>Nāgas</s>, bow to a cow's hoofprint.

children.text: candrāditya prabhaṃkarā prabhakarā khadyotake no name
children.translated_text: The sun and moon, the makers of light and radiance, do not bow to a firefly —

children.text: prajñāpuṇyakulodito guṇadharaḥ kasmānname devate // Lal_8.4 //
children.translated_text: why then should we deities bow to one arisen from the clan of wisdom and merit, the bearer of virtues? // Lal_8.4 //

children.text: yadvat sarṣapa goṣpade va salilaṃ khadyotakā vā bhavet
children.translated_text: Just as a mustard seed, or water in a hoofprint, or a firefly

children.text: evaṃ ca trisahasra devamanujā ye keci mānāśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: [is nothing] — so are the gods and humans of the trichiliocosm, whoever are given to pride.

children.text: merūsāgaracandrasūryasadṛśo loke svayaṃbhūttamo
children.translated_text: Like <s>Meru</s>, like the ocean, like the sun and moon — the supreme Self-Born One in the world,

children.text: yaṃ loko hyabhivandya lābha labhate svargaṃ tathā nirvṛtim // Lal_8.5 //
children.translated_text: whom the world, having worshipped, gains the reward of heaven and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' // Lal_8.5 //

body.text: asmin khalu punarbhikṣavo bodhisattvena mahāsattvena devakule praveśe saṃdarśyamāne dvātriṃśatāṃ devaputraśatasahasrāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpadyante / ayaṃ bhikṣavo heturayaṃ pratyayo yenopekṣako bodhisattvo bhavati sma devakulamupanīyamāna iti //
body.translated_text: Moreover, O monks, as the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>'s entry into the temple was being displayed, in thirty-two hundred thousands of <s>Devaputras</s>, the aspiration to unsurpassed, perfect awakening arose. This, O monks, is the reason, this is the cause, why the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was equanimous [about] being taken to the temple. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare devakulopanayanaparivarto nāma aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Taking [the Prince] to the Temple' (<s>Devakulopanayanaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 9
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 9.

body.text: ābharaṇaparivarto navamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Ninth Chapter: On Ornaments (<s>Ābharaṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣava udayano nāma brāhmaṇo rājñaḥ purohita udāyinaḥ pitā, sa pañcamātrairbrāhmaṇaśataiḥ parivṛto hastottare citrānakṣatre rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha - yatkhalu devo jānīyādābharaṇāni kumārāya kriyantāmiti / taṃ rājā āha - bāḍham / gāḍhaṃ kriyatāmiti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Udayana</s> — the king's chaplain, father of <s>Udāyin</s> — accompanied by approximately five hundred <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, at the auspicious <s>Hastottara</s> and <s>Citrā</s> constellation, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said: 'May the lord know — let ornaments be made for the prince.' The king said to him: 'Very well! Let them be made firmly.' //

body.text: tatra rājñā śuddhodanena pañcamātraiśca śakyaśataiḥ pañcamātrāṇyābharaṇaśatāni kāritānyabhūvan / tadyathā - hastābharaṇāni pādābharaṇāni mūrdhābharaṇāni kaṇṭhābharaṇāni mudrikābharaṇāni karṇikāyākeyūrāṇi mekhalāsuvarṇasūtrāṇi kiṅkiṇījālāni ratnajālāni maṇipratyuptāni pādukā nānāratnasamalaṃkṛtā hārāḥ kaṭakā harṣā mukuṭāni / kārayitvā ca puṣyanakṣatrayogenānuyuktena te śākyā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaivamāhuḥ - hanta deva maṇḍyatāṃ kumāra iti / rājā āha - alamalaṃkṛtaśca pūjitaśca bhavadbhiḥ kumāraḥ / mayāpi (kumārasya) sarvābharaṇāni kāritāni / te 'vocan - saptasaptarātriṃdivānyapyasmākamābharaṇāni kumāraḥ kāya ābadhnātu / tato 'smākamamogho vyāyāmo bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: There, by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and approximately five hundred <s>Śākya</s> [families], approximately five hundred [sets of] ornaments were made — namely: hand-ornaments, foot-ornaments, head-ornaments, neck-ornaments, ring-ornaments, earrings, armlets, girdles, gold chains, networks of tinkling bells, networks of jewels, jewel-studded sandals, necklaces adorned with various gems, bracelets, garlands, diadems, and crowns. Having had them made, those <s>Śākyas</s>, at the conjunction of the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said: 'Come, O lord, let the prince be adorned!' The king said: 'The prince has already been sufficiently adorned and worshipped by you. By me also, all ornaments for the prince have been made.' They said: 'Let the prince wear our ornaments on his body for seven times seven days and nights. Then our effort will not have been in vain.' //

body.text: tatra rātrau vinirgatāyāmāditya udite vimalavyūhanāmodyānaṃ tatra bodhisattvo nirgato 'bhūt / tatra mahāprajāpatyā gautamyā bodhisattvo 'ṅke gṛhīto 'bhut / aśītiśca strīsahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma / daśa ca kanyāsahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma / pañca ca brāhmaṇasahasrāṇi pratyudgamya bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ prekṣante sma / tatra yāni bhadrikeṇa śākyarājenābharaṇāni kāritānyabhūvan, tāni bodhisattvasya kāye ābadhyante sma / tāni samanantarābaddhāni bodhisattvasya kāyaprabhayā jihmīkṛtānyabhūvan, na bhāsante sma, na tapanti sma, na virocanti sma / tadyathāpi nāma jāmbūnadasya suvarṇasya purato masipiṇḍa upanikṣipto na bhāsati na tapati na virocate, evameva tānyābharaṇāni bodhisattvasya kāyaprabhayāspṛṣṭāni na bhāsante na tapanti na virocante sma / evaṃ yā yā ābharaṇavikṛtirbodhisattvasya kāya ābadhyate sma, sā sā jihmībhavati sma tadyathāpi nāma masipiṇḍaḥ //
body.translated_text: There, when the night had passed and the sun had risen, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> went out to the garden called <s>Vimalavyūha</s> (Stainless Array). There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was held on the lap of <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>. Eighty thousand women came forward to gaze at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s face. Ten thousand maidens came forward to gaze at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s face. Five thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> came forward to gaze at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s face. Then the ornaments that had been made by King <s>Bhadrika</s> of the <s>Śākyas</s> were fastened upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body. The moment they were fastened, they were dimmed by the radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body — they did not shine, they did not glow, they did not gleam. Just as a lump of ink placed before <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold neither shines, nor glows, nor gleams — even so, those ornaments, touched by the radiance of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body, did not shine, did not glow, did not gleam. Thus, whatever ornament was fastened upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body became dim, just like a lump of ink. //

body.text: tatra vimalā nāmodyānadevatā sā audārikamātmabhāvamabhisaṃdarśya purataḥ sthitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ śākyagaṇaṃ gāthābhirabhibhāṣate sma -
body.translated_text: There, a garden deity named <s>Vimalā</s>, having manifested a coarse visible form, standing before [them], addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great assembly of <s>Śākyas</s> in verses —

body.text: sarveyaṃ trisahasra medinī sanagaranigamā pūrṇā kāñcanasaṃcitā bhavet surucira vimalā /
body.translated_text: 'If this entire trichiliocosmic earth, with its cities and market-towns, were to be filled with heaped gold, beautiful and stainless,

body.text: ekā kākiṇi jāmbukāñcane bhavati upahatā nā bhāsī itaraḥ sa kāñcana prabhasirirahitaḥ // Lal_9.1 //
body.translated_text: a single small coin of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold would [make it] diminished — that [other] gold, devoid of its radiance and glory, would not shine. // Lal_9.1 //

children.text: jāmbūkāñcanasaṃnibhā punarbhavet sakara iya mahī
children.translated_text: And if [this earth] were again made to resemble <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, with its mountains — this entire earth,

children.text: rome ābha pramukta nāyake hirisiribharite /
children.translated_text: the radiance emitted from a single hair-pore of the leader, filled with glory and splendor,

children.text: nā bhāsī na tapī na śobhate na ca prabhavati
children.translated_text: would [make it] not shine, not glow, not gleam, and not prevail —

children.text: ābhāye sugatasya kāyi no bhavati yatha masiḥ // Lal_9.2 //
children.translated_text: before the radiance of the <s>Sugata</s>'s body, it would become like ink. // Lal_9.2 //

children.text: sve tejena ayaṃ svalaṃkṛto guṇaśatabharito
children.translated_text: He who is adorned by his own splendor, filled with a hundred virtues —

children.text: no tasyābharaṇā virociṣū suvimalavapuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: the ornaments do not shine on his stainlessly pure body.

children.text: candrasūryaprabhāśca jyotiṣā tatha maṇijvalanāḥ
children.translated_text: The radiance of the sun and moon, the light of blazing gems,

children.text: śakrabahmaprabhā na bhāsate purata śirighane // Lal_9.3 //
children.translated_text: the radiance of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> — none shine before the one dense with glory. // Lal_9.3 //

children.text: yasyā lakṣaṇi kāyu citritaḥ purimaśubhaphalaiḥ
children.translated_text: His body is painted with the [auspicious] marks — the fruits of former good deeds;

children.text: kiṃ tasyābharaṇebhiritvaraiḥ parakṛtakaraṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: what need has he for these inferior ornaments, made by others' hands?

children.text: apanethā bharaṇā ma heṭhatā abudha budhakaraṃ
children.translated_text: Remove the ornaments! Do not insult the awakener of the unawakened —

children.text: nāyaṃ kṛttimabhūṣaṇārthika paramamatikaraḥ // Lal_9.4 //
children.translated_text: he of supreme intellect is not one who desires adornment by artifice. // Lal_9.4 //

children.text: ceṭasyābharaṇāni dethime surucira vimalā
children.translated_text: Give these beautiful, stainless ornaments to the servant —

children.text: sahajāto ya subhūṣi chandako nṛpatikulaśubhe /
children.translated_text: to <s>Chandaka</s>, born along with him, well-adorned, in the noble royal family.'

children.text: tuṣṭā śākiya vismitāśca abhavanpramuditamanaso
children.translated_text: The <s>Śākyas</s> were pleased, amazed, and of joyful minds [hearing this]:

children.text: vṛddhiḥ śākyakulanandasya cottamā bhaviṣyati vipulā // Lal_9.5 //
children.translated_text: 'The increase of the delight of the <s>Śākya</s> family will be supreme and vast!' // Lal_9.5 //

body.text: ityuktvā sā devatā bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpairabhyavakīrya tatraivāntaradhāt //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that deity showered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with divine flowers and vanished right there. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare ābharaṇaparivarto nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the ninth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Ornaments' (<s>Ābharaṇaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 10
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 10.

body.text: lipiśālāsaṃdarśanaparivarto daśamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Tenth Chapter: On the Visit to the Writing School (<s>Lipiśālāsaṃdarśanaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saṃvṛddhaḥ kumāraḥ / tadā māṅgalyaśatasahasraiḥ lipiśālāmupanīyate sma daśabhirdārakasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ, daśabhiśca rathasahasraiḥ khādanīyabhojanīyasvādanīyaparipūrṇairhiraṇyasuvarṇaparipūrṇaiśca / yena kapilavastuni mahānagare vīthicatvararathyāntarāpaṇamukheṣvabhyavakīryate sma abhiviśrāmyante / aṣṭābhiśca tūryaśatasahasraiḥ praghuṣyamāṇairmahatā ca puṣpavarṣeṇābhipravarṣatā vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādataleṣu kanyāśatasahasrāṇi sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitāḥ sthitā abhūvan / bodhisattvaṃ prekṣamāṇāḥ kusumāni ca kṣipanti sma / aṣṭau ca marutkanyāsahasrāṇi vigalitālaṃkārābharaṇālaṃkṛtāni ratnabhadraṃkareṇa gṛhītāni mārgaṃ śodhayantyo bodhisattvasya purato gacchanti sma / devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāścārdhakāyikā gaganatalātpuṣpapaṭṭadāmānyabhipralambayanti sma / sarve ca śākyagaṇāḥ śuddhodanaṃ rājānaṃ puraskṛtya bodhisattvasya purato gacchanti sma / anenaivaṃrūpeṇa vyūhena bodhisattvo lipiśālāmupanīyate sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the prince had grown up, he was taken to the writing-school with a hundred thousand auspicious ceremonies, surrounded and attended by ten thousand boys, and by ten thousand chariots filled with food, drink, and delicacies, and filled with silver and gold — which were scattered about in the streets, squares, thoroughfares, crossroads, and market-fronts of the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. With eight hundred thousand musical instruments sounding and a great rain of flowers pouring down, hundreds of thousands of maidens fully adorned with all ornaments stood upon the balconies, projecting galleries, arched gateways, windows, mansions, upper-story chambers, and palace terraces — watching the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and scattering flowers. And eight thousand divine maidens, adorned with cascading ornaments and jewelry, holding jeweled auspicious brooms, went before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, sweeping the road. <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, half-bodied, let hang garlands of flowers and silk from the sky. All the <s>Śākya</s> clans, with King <s>Śuddhodana</s> at their head, went before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. With such a magnificent array the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was taken to the writing-school. //

body.text: samanantarapraveśitaśca bodhisattvo lipiśālām / atha viśvāmitro nāma dārakācāryo bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaścāsahamāno dharaṇitale niviṣṭo 'dhomukhaḥ prapatati sma / taṃ tathā prapatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā śubhāṅgo nāma tuṣitakāyiko devaputro dakṣiṇena karatalena parigṛhyotthāpayati sma / utthāpya ca gaganatalastho rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was immediately brought into the writing-school. Then the boys' teacher named <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, unable to bear the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s splendor and brilliance, fell face-down upon the ground. Seeing him thus fallen, a <s>devaputra</s> (divine prince) named <s>Śubhāṅga</s> from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, supporting him with his right hand, raised him up. And having raised him, standing in the sky, he addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great assembly of people in verses —

children.text: śāstrāṇi yāni pracalanti manuṣyaloke saṃkhyā lipiśca gaṇanāpi ca dhātutantram /
children.translated_text: The sciences that prevail in the human world — arithmetic, writing, calculation, and the system of grammatical elements,

children.text: ye śilpayoga pṛthu laukika aprameyāḥ teṣveṣu śikṣitu purā bahukalpakoṭyaḥ // Lal_10.1 //
children.translated_text: the arts and crafts, manifold, worldly, and immeasurable — in all these he trained previously for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>! // Lal_10.1 //

children.text: kiṃ tū janasya anuvartanatāṃ karoti lipiśālamāgatu suśikṣitu śiṣyaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: But he acts in conformity with the people; let him come to the writing-school to teach well, for the purpose of disciplining [others],

children.text: paripācanārtha bahudāraka agrayāne anyāṃśca sattvanayutānamṛte vinetum // Lal_10.2 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of ripening many boys in the supreme vehicle, and to guide other <s>nayutas</s> of beings to the deathless! // Lal_10.2 //

children.text: lokottareṣu catusatyapathe vidhijño hetupratītyakuśalo yatha saṃbhavanti /
children.translated_text: He who is skilled in the method of the supramundane path of the Four Noble Truths, expert in how causes and conditions arise,

children.text: yatha cānirodhakṣayu saṃsthitu śītibhāvaḥ tasminvidhijña kimatho lipiśāstramātre // Lal_10.3 //
children.translated_text: and how the state of peace abides without cessation or destruction — what, for one skilled in such methods, is a mere writing-treatise? // Lal_10.3 //

body.text: netasya ācariya uttari vā triloke sarveṣu devamanujeṣvayameva jeṣṭhaḥ /
body.translated_text: There is no teacher superior to him in the three worlds; among all gods and humans he alone is the foremost;

body.text: nāmāpi teṣa lipināṃ na hi vittha yūyaṃ yatreṣu śikṣitu purā bahukalpakoṭyaḥ // Lal_10.4 //
body.translated_text: even the names of those scripts you do not know — in which he trained previously for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>! // Lal_10.4 //

children.text: so cittadhāra jagatāṃ vividhā vicitrā ekakṣaṇena ayu jānati śuddhasattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, the pure being, knows in a single instant the manifold and variegated mental dispositions of beings,

children.text: adṛśyarūparahitasya gatiṃ ca vetti kiṃ vā puno 'tha lipino 'kṣaradṛśyarūpām // Lal_10.5 //
children.translated_text: and he knows the course of that which is invisible and formless — how much more then the visible forms of letters and writing! // Lal_10.5 //

body.text: ityuktvā sa devaputro bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ kusumairabhyarcya tatraivāntardadhe / tatra dhātryaśca ceṭīvargāśca sthāpitā abhūvan / pariśeṣāḥ śākyāḥ śuddhodanapramukhāḥ prakrāmantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that <s>devaputra</s>, having worshipped the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with divine flowers, vanished right there. There nurses and maidservants were stationed. The remaining <s>Śākyas</s>, with <s>Śuddhodana</s> at their head, departed. //

body.text: atha bodhisattva uragasāracandanamayaṃ lipiphalakamādāya divyārṣasuvarṇatirakaṃ samantānmaṇiratnapratyuptaṃ viśvāmitramācāryamevamāha - katamāṃ me bho upādhyāya lipiṃ śikṣāpayasi / brāhmīkharoṣṭīpuṣkarasāriṃ aṅgalipiṃ vaṅgalipiṃ magadhalipiṃ maṅgalyalipiṃ aṅgulīyalipiṃ śakārilipiṃ brahmavalilipiṃ pāruṣyalipiṃ drāviḍalipiṃ kirātalipiṃ dākṣiṇyalipiṃ ugralipiṃ saṃkhyālipiṃ anulomalipiṃ avamūrdhalipiṃ daradalipiṃ khāṣyalipiṃ cīnalipiṃ lūnalipiṃ hūṇalipiṃ madhyākṣaravistaralipiṃ puṣpalipiṃ devalipiṃ nāgalipiṃ yakṣalipiṃ gandharvalipiṃ kinnaralipiṃ mahoragalipiṃ asuralipiṃ garuḍalipiṃ mṛgacakralipiṃ vāyasarutalipiṃ bhaumadevalipiṃ antarīkṣadevalipiṃ uttarakurudvīpalipiṃ aparagoḍānīlipiṃ pūrvavidehalipiṃ utkṣepalipiṃ nikṣepalipiṃ vikṣepalipiṃ prakṣepalipiṃ sāgaralipiṃ vajralipiṃ lekhapratilekhalipiṃ anudrutalipiṃ śāstrāvartāṃ gaṇanāvartalipiṃ utkṣepāvartalipiṃ nikṣepāvartalipiṃ pādalikhitalipiṃ dviruttarapadasaṃdhilipiṃ yāvaddaśottarapadasaṃdhilipiṃ madhyāhāriṇīlipiṃ sarvarutasaṃgrahaṇīlipiṃ vidyānulomāvimiśritalipiṃ ṛṣitapastaptāṃ rocamānāṃ dharaṇīprekṣiṇīlipiṃ gaganaprekṣiṇīlipiṃ sarvauṣadhiniṣyandāṃ sarvasārasaṃgrahaṇīṃ sarvabhūtarutagrahaṇīm / āsāṃ bho upādhyāya catuṣṣaṣṭīlipīnāṃ katamāṃ tvaṃ śiṣyāpayiṣyasi?
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking a writing-tablet made of <s>uragasāra</s>-sandalwood, with a divine golden stylus inlaid all around with jewels and gems, addressed the teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s> thus: 'Which script, O preceptor, will you teach me? <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Kharoṣṭī</s>, <s>Puṣkarasārī</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>-script, <s>Vaṅga</s>-script, <s>Magadha</s>-script, <s>Māṅgalya</s>-script, <s>Aṅgulīya</s>-script, <s>Śakāri</s>-script, <s>Brahmavalī</s>-script, <s>Pāruṣya</s>-script, <s>Drāviḍa</s>-script, <s>Kirāta</s>-script, <s>Dākṣiṇya</s>-script, <s>Ugra</s>-script, <s>Saṃkhyā</s>-script, <s>Anuloma</s>-script, <s>Avamūrdha</s>-script, <s>Darada</s>-script, <s>Khāṣya</s>-script, <s>Cīna</s>-script, <s>Lūna</s>-script, <s>Hūṇa</s>-script, <s>Madhyākṣaravistara</s>-script, <s>Puṣpa</s>-script, <s>Deva</s>-script, <s>Nāga</s>-script, <s>Yakṣa</s>-script, <s>Gandharva</s>-script, <s>Kinnara</s>-script, <s>Mahoraga</s>-script, <s>Asura</s>-script, <s>Garuḍa</s>-script, <s>Mṛgacakra</s>-script, <s>Vāyasaruta</s>-script, <s>Bhaumadeva</s>-script, <s>Antarīkṣadeva</s>-script, <s>Uttarakurudvīpa</s>-script, <s>Aparagodānī</s>-script, <s>Pūrvavideha</s>-script, <s>Utkṣepa</s>-script, <s>Nikṣepa</s>-script, <s>Vikṣepa</s>-script, <s>Prakṣepa</s>-script, <s>Sāgara</s>-script, <s>Vajra</s>-script, <s>Lekhapratilekha</s>-script, <s>Anudruta</s>-script, <s>Śāstrāvarta</s>, <s>Gaṇanāvarta</s>-script, <s>Utkṣepāvarta</s>-script, <s>Nikṣepāvarta</s>-script, <s>Pādalikhita</s>-script, <s>Dviruttarapadasaṃdhi</s>-script, up to <s>Daśottarapadasaṃdhi</s>-script, <s>Madhyāhāriṇī</s>-script, <s>Sarvarutasaṃgrahaṇī</s>-script, <s>Vidyānulomāvimiśrita</s>-script, <s>Ṛṣitapastaptā</s>, <s>Rocamānā</s>, <s>Dharaṇīprekṣiṇī</s>-script, <s>Gaganaprekṣiṇī</s>-script, <s>Sarvauṣadhiniṣyandā</s>, <s>Sarvasārasaṃgrahaṇī</s>, <s>Sarvabhūtarutagrahaṇī</s> — of these sixty-four scripts, O preceptor, which one will you teach me?'

body.text: atha viśvāmitro dārakācāryo vismitaḥ prahasitavadano nihatamānamadadarpa imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the boys' teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, astonished, with a smiling face, his pride and arrogance humbled, spoke this verse —

children.text: āścaryaṃ śuddhasattvasya loke lokānuvartino /
children.translated_text: Wonderful [is this] pure being, who follows the ways of the world in the world!

children.text: śikṣitaḥ sarvaśāstreṣu lipiśālāmupāgataḥ // Lal_10.6 //
children.translated_text: Already trained in all sciences, he has come to the writing-school! // Lal_10.6 //

children.text: yeṣāmahaṃ nāmadheyaṃ lipīnāṃ na prajānami /
children.translated_text: Of the scripts whose very names I do not know,

children.text: tatraiṣa śikṣitaḥ santo lipiśālāmupāgataḥ // Lal_10.7 //
children.translated_text: in those this one, already trained, has come to the writing-school! // Lal_10.7 //

children.text: vaktraṃ cāsya na paśyāmi mūrdhānaṃ tasya naiva ca /
children.translated_text: I cannot even look upon his face, nor upon his crown;

children.text: śiṣyayiṣye kathaṃ hyenaṃ lipiprajñāya pāragam // Lal_10.8 //
children.translated_text: how shall I teach one who has reached the far shore of the wisdom of writing? // Lal_10.8 //

children.text: devadevo hyatidevaḥ sarvadevottamo vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: He is indeed the god of gods, surpassing the gods, the highest of all gods, the all-pervading one,

children.text: asamaśca viśiṣṭaśca lokeṣvapratipudgalaḥ // Lal_10.9 //
children.translated_text: the incomparable, the distinguished — in all the worlds there is no one equal to him! // Lal_10.9 //

children.text: asyaiva tvanubhāvena prajñopāye viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: But by his very power, especially in wisdom and skillful means,

children.text: śikṣitaṃ śiṣyayiṣyāmi sarvalokaparāyaṇam // Lal_10.10 //
children.translated_text: I shall teach [him who is already] trained — he who is the refuge of the entire world! // Lal_10.10 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo daśa dārakasahasrāṇi bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ lipiṃ śiṣyante sma / tatra bodhisattvādhisthānena teṣāṃ dārakāṇāṃ mātṛkāṃ vācayatāṃ yadā akāraṃ parikīrtayanti sma, tadā anityaḥ sarvasaṃskāraśabdo niścarati sma / ākāre parikīrtyamāne ātmaparahitaśabdo niścarati sma / ikāre indriyavaikalyaśabdaḥ / īkāre ītibahulaṃ jagaditi / ukāre upadravabahulaṃ jagaditi / ūkāre ūnasattvaṃ jagaditi / ekāre eṣaṇāsamutthānadoṣaśabdaḥ / aikāre airyāpathaḥ śreyāniti / okāre oghottaraśabdaḥ / aukāre aupapādukaśabdaḥ / aṃkāre amoghotpattiśabdaḥ / aḥkāre astaṃgamanaśabdo niścarati sma / kakāre karmavipākāvatāraśabdaḥ / khakāre khasamasarvadharmaśabdaḥ / gakāre gambhīradharmapratītyasamutpādāvatāraśabdaḥ / ghakāre ghanapaṭalāvidyāmohāndhakāravidhamanaśabdaḥ / ṅakāre 'ṅgaviśuddhiśabdaḥ / cakāre caturāryasatyaśabdaḥ / chakāre chandarāgaprahāṇaśabdaḥ / jakāre jarāmaraṇasamatikramaṇaśabdaḥ / jhakāre jhaṣadhvajabalanigrahaṇaśabdaḥ / ñakāre jñāpanaśabdaḥ / ṭakāre paṭopacchedanaśabdaḥ / ṭhakāre ṭhapanīyapraśnaśabdaḥ / ḍakāre ḍamaramāranigrahaṇaśabdaḥ / ḍhakāre mīḍhaviṣayā iti / ṇakāre reṇukleśā iti / takāre tathatāsaṃbhedaśabdaḥ / thakāre thāmabalavegavaiśāradyaśabdaḥ / dakāre dānadamasaṃyamasaurabhyaśabdaḥ / dhakāre dhanamāryāṇāṃ saptavidhamiti / nakāre nāmarūpaparijñāśabdaḥ / pakāre paramārthaśabdaḥ / phakāre phalaprāptisākṣātkriyāśabdaḥ / bakāre bandhanamokṣaśabdaḥ / bhakāre bhavavibhavaśabdaḥ / makāre madamānopaśamanaśabdaḥ / yakāre yathāvaddharmaprativedhaśabdaḥ / rakāre ratyaratiparamārtharatiśabdaḥ / lakāre latāchedanaśabdaḥ / vakāre varayānaśabdaḥ / śakāre śamathavipaśyanāśabdaḥ / ṣakāre ṣaḍāyatananigrahaṇābhijñajñānāvāptiśabdaḥ / sakāre sarvajñajñānābhisaṃbodhanaśabdaḥ / hakāre hatakleśavirāgaśabdaḥ / kṣakāre parikīrtyamāne kṣaṇaparyantābhilāpyasarvadharmaśabdo niścarati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, ten thousand boys were trained in writing together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. There, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s empowerment, when those boys were reciting the alphabet (<s>mātṛkā</s>) — when they pronounced the letter 'a,' the sound 'all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things) are impermanent' issued forth. When 'ā' was pronounced, the sound 'benefit of self and others' issued forth. With 'i,' the sound 'deficiency of the sense-faculties' [issued forth]. With 'ī,' 'the world is full of calamities.' With 'u,' 'the world is full of misfortunes.' With 'ū,' 'the world of beings is deficient.' With 'e,' the sound 'the fault of the arising of craving' [issued forth]. With 'ai,' 'deportment is most excellent.' With 'o,' the sound 'crossing over the flood.' With 'au,' the sound 'spontaneous birth.' With 'aṃ,' the sound 'unfailing arising.' With 'aḥ,' the sound 'setting' issued forth. With 'ka,' the sound 'entering into the ripening of <s>karma</s>.' With 'kha,' the sound 'all <s>dharmas</s> are like space.' With 'ga,' the sound 'entering into the profound <s>dharma</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).' With 'gha,' the sound 'dispelling the darkness of the dense veil of ignorance and delusion.' With 'ṅa,' the sound 'purity of limbs.' With 'ca,' the sound 'the Four Noble Truths.' With 'cha,' the sound 'abandonment of desire and passion.' With 'ja,' the sound 'transcending old age and death.' With 'jha,' the sound 'subduing the forces of <s>Māra</s> with the fish-banner.' With 'ña,' the sound 'making known.' With 'ṭa,' the sound 'cutting the cloth [of delusion].' With 'ṭha,' the sound 'the question to be set aside.' With 'ḍa,' the sound 'subduing the tumult of <s>Māra</s>.' With 'ḍha,' 'the objects are impure.' With 'ṇa,' 'the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are dust.' With 'ta,' the sound 'the indivisibility of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).' With 'tha,' the sound 'strength, power, force, and fearlessness.' With 'da,' the sound 'the fragrance of giving, self-control, and restraint.' With 'dha,' the sound 'the wealth of the Noble Ones is sevenfold.' With 'na,' the sound 'full comprehension of name-and-form.' With 'pa,' the sound 'the ultimate meaning.' With 'pha,' the sound 'realization of the attainment of the fruit.' With 'ba,' the sound 'liberation from bondage.' With 'bha,' the sound 'existence and non-existence.' With 'ma,' the sound 'pacification of intoxication and pride.' With 'ya,' the sound 'penetrating the <s>dharma</s> as it truly is.' With 'ra,' the sound 'delight, non-delight, and supreme delight.' With 'la,' the sound 'cutting the creeper [of craving].' With 'va,' the sound 'the supreme vehicle.' With 'śa,' the sound '<s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).' With 'ṣa,' the sound 'restraint of the six sense-bases and attainment of the knowledge of supernatural powers.' With 'sa,' the sound 'awakening to omniscient knowledge.' With 'ha,' the sound 'afflictions destroyed, dispassion [attained].' When 'kṣa' was pronounced, the sound 'all <s>dharmas</s> are expressible only for a moment's duration' issued forth. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavasteṣāṃ dārakāṇāṃ mātṛkāṃ vācayatāṃ bodhisattvānubhāvenaiva pramukhānyasaṃkhyeyāni dharmamukhaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when those boys were reciting the alphabet, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s very power, innumerable hundreds of thousands of principal gateways to the <s>dharma</s> issued forth. //

body.text: tadānupūrveṇa bodhisattvena lipiśālāsthitena dvātriṃśaddārakasahasrāṇi paripācitānyabhūvan / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpāditāni dvātriṃśaddārikāsahasrāṇi / ayaṃ heturayaṃ pratyayo yacchikṣito 'pi bodhisattvo lipiśālāmupāgacchati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, in due course, while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in the writing-school, thirty-two thousand boys were ripened. In thirty-two thousand girls the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) was aroused. This is the reason, this is the cause why the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though already trained, came to the writing-school. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare lipiśālāsaṃdarśanaparivarto nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the tenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Showing the Writing-School' (<s>Lipiśālāsaṃdarśanaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 11
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 11.

body.text: kṛṣigrāmaparivarta ekādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Eleventh Chapter: On the Farming Village (<s>Kṛṣigrāmaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāvadvivṛddhaḥ kumāraḥ / athāpareṇa samayena kumārastadanyaiḥ kumārairamātyaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ kṛṣigrāmavalokayituṃ gacchati sma / avalokya ca kṛṣikarmāntamanyata udyānabhūmiṃ praviśati sma / saṃvignamanāstatra bodhisattva ekākī advitīyo 'nucaṃkramyamāṇo 'nuvicaran jambuvṛkṣamapaśyat prāsādikaṃ darśanīyam / tatra bodhisattvaśchāyāyāṃ paryaṅkena niṣīdati sma / niṣaṇṇaśca bodhisattvaścittaikāgratāmāsādayati sma / āsādya ca viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma / sa vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotibhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma / sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati sma smṛtimān saṃprajānan / sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayati sma / yattadāryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārī niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamusaṃpadya viharati sma / sa sukhasya ca prahāṇādduḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastaṃgamādaduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the prince had grown up further. Then on another occasion, the prince went to observe a farming village together with other princes and ministers' sons. Having observed the farming activities, he entered another pleasure-ground. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his mind stirred [with spiritual urgency], wandering about alone without a companion, saw a <s>Jambu</s> tree (rose-apple tree), pleasant and beautiful to behold. There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat cross-legged in its shade. And having sat, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attained one-pointedness of mind. Having attained it — secluded from sense-desires, secluded from unwholesome states — he entered and abode in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), which is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, and filled with joy and happiness. By the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, through inner tranquility and one-pointedness of mind, he entered and abode in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without applied thought and sustained thought, born of concentration, and filled with joy and happiness. Through detachment from joy, he abode in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending; and he experienced happiness with the body — that which the Noble Ones declare: 'Equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness' — he entered and abode in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without joy. Through the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering, and through the prior disappearance of mental pleasure and mental pain, he entered and abode in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. //

body.text: tena ca samayena pañca ṛṣayo bāhyāḥ pañcābhijñāḥ ṛddhimanto vihāyasaṃgamā dakṣiṇāyā diśa uttarāṃ diśaṃ gacchanti sma / te tasya vanakhaṇḍasyopari gacchantaḥ pratyāhatā iva na śaknuvanti sma gantum / te saṃvignaromakūpajātā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: And at that time, five external <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) possessing the five supernatural knowledges, endowed with miraculous powers, traversing the sky, were traveling from the southern direction to the northern direction. As they passed above that grove, they were repelled as if struck back and were unable to proceed. With their body-hairs standing on end in awe, they spoke this verse —

children.text: vayamiha maṇivajrakūṭaṃ giriṃ merumabhyudgataṃ tiryagatyarthavaistārikaṃ gaja iva sahakāraśākhākulāṃ vṛkṣavṛndāṃ pradāritva nirdhāvitānekaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: We who have surmounted <s>Meru</s>, the mountain of jewel-and-diamond peaks, rising up, traversing horizontally at will, like elephants that have burst through and charged past multitudes of trees thick with mango branches, time and again —

children.text: vayamiha marūṇāṃ pure cāpyasaktā gatā yakṣagandharvaveśmani cordhvaṃ nabhe niśritā ima puna vanakhaṇḍamāsādya sīdāma bhoḥ kasya lakṣmī nivarteti ṛddherbalam // Lal_11.1 //
children.translated_text: 'We who were unimpeded even in the city of the <s>Maruts</s>, who went to the abodes of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>, and who soared aloft in the sky — here, having reached this grove, we are brought low! Alas, whose glory is this that turns back [our] supernatural power?' // Lal_11.1 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

children.text: atha yā tatra vanakhaṇḍadevatā sā tānṛṣīn gāthayādhyabhāṣat -
children.translated_text: Then the forest deity of that grove addressed those sages in a verse:

children.text: nṛpatipatikuloditaḥ śākyarājātmajo bālasūryaprakāśaprabhaḥ sphuṭitakamalagarbhavarṇaprabhaścārucandrānano lokajyeṣṭho viduḥ /
children.translated_text: Born in a line of lords of kings, the son of the <s>Śākya</s> king, radiant as the newly risen sun, of the hue of a fully opened lotus-womb, with a face lovely as the moon, the foremost of the world, the wise one —

children.text: ayamiha vanamāśrito dhyānacintāparo devagandharvanāgendrayakṣārcito bhavaśataguṇakoṭisaṃvardhitastasya lakṣmī nivarteti ṛddherbalam // Lal_11.2 //
children.translated_text: he has resorted to this forest, absorbed in meditation and contemplation, worshipped by gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāga</s>-lords, and <s>Yakṣas</s>, nurtured by <s>koṭīs</s> of hundreds of qualities through [many] existences — it is his glory that turns back [your] supernatural power! // Lal_11.2 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: tataste 'dhastādavalokayanto 'drākṣuḥ kumāraṃ śriyā tejasā ca jājvalyamānam / teṣāmetadabhūt - ko nvayaṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ? mā haiva vaiśravaṇo dhanādhipatirbhavet / āhosvinmāraḥ kāmādhipatiḥ / atha mahoragendraḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, looking down from above, they saw the prince blazing with glory and splendor. They thought: 'Who is this seated [here]? Could he be <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the lord of wealth? Or <s>Māra</s>, the lord of desires? Or a great <s>Nāga</s>-lord?

body.text: athendro vajradharaḥ / atha rudraḥ kumbhāṇḍādhipatiḥ / atha kṛṣṇo mahotsāhaḥ / uta candro devaputraḥ / uta sūryaḥ sahasraraśmiḥ / uta rājā cakravartī bhaviṣyati? tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Or <s>Indra</s>, the bearer of the <s>vajra</s>? Or <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>? Or <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the greatly vigorous one? Or <s>Candra</s>, the <s>Devaputra</s>? Or <s>Sūrya</s>, the thousand-rayed? Or will he be a <s>Cakravartin</s> king?' And on that occasion they spoke this verse:

children.text: rūpaṃ vaiśravaṇātirekavapuṣaṃ vyaktaṃ kubero hyayaṃ
children.translated_text: His form surpasses <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in body — clearly this must be <s>Kubera</s>!

children.text: āho vajradharasya caiva pratimā candro 'tha sūryo hyayam /
children.translated_text: Or else the likeness of <s>Vajradhara</s>! Or is he <s>Candra</s>, or <s>Sūrya</s>?

children.text: kāmāgrādhipatiśca vā pratikṛtī rūdrasya kṛṣṇasya vā
children.translated_text: Or the supreme lord of desires? Or the image of <s>Rudra</s>, or of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?

children.text: śrīmān lakṣaṇacitritāṅgamanagho buddho 'tha vā syādayam // Lal_11.3 //
children.translated_text: Glorious, his body painted with the [major] marks, faultless — or could this be the <s>Buddha</s>? // Lal_11.3 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: tataḥ sā vanadevatā tānṛṣīn gāthayā pratyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then that forest deity replied to those sages in a verse:

children.text: yā śrī ca vaiśravaṇe ca vai nivasate yā vā sahasrekṣaṇe
children.translated_text: Whatever glory dwells in <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, or in the thousand-eyed [<s>Indra</s>],

children.text: lokānāṃ paripālakeṣu catuṣū yā cāsurendraśriyā /
children.translated_text: or in the four guardians of the world, or the glory of the lord of <s>Asuras</s>,

children.text: brahme yā ca sahāpatau nivasate kṛṣṇe ca yā ca śriyā
children.translated_text: or that which dwells in <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, and the glory that is in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: sā śrī prāpya imaṃ hi śākyatanayaṃ nopaiti kāṃcitkalām // Lal_11.4 //
children.translated_text: that glory, upon reaching this son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, does not equal even a fraction [of his]! // Lal_11.4 //

body.text: atha khalu te ṛṣayastasyā devatāyā vacanamupaśritya dharaṇītale pratiṣṭhante / te paśyanti sma bodhisattvaṃ dhyāyantamāniñjyamānena kāyena tejorāśimiva jvalantam / te bodhisattvamupanidhyāya gāthābhirabhituṣṭuvuḥ / tatraika āha -
body.translated_text: Then those sages, heeding the words of that deity, descended to the surface of the earth. They saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditating, with body motionless, blazing like a mass of fire. They approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and praised him with verses. One among them said:

children.text: loke kleśāgnisaṃtapte prādurbhūto hyayaṃ hradaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this world scorched by the fire of the afflictions, this lake has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagad hlādayiṣyati // Lal_11.5 //
children.translated_text: he will attain that <s>dharma</s> which will refresh the world! // Lal_11.5 //

body.text: aparo 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: Another said:

children.text: ajñānatimire loke prādurbhūtaḥ pradīpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a world [plunged] in the darkness of ignorance, this lamp has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagadbhāsayiṣyati // Lal_11.6 //
children.translated_text: he will attain that <s>dharma</s> which will illuminate the world! // Lal_11.6 //

body.text: aparo 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: Another said:

children.text: śokasāgarakāntāre yānaśreṣṭhamupasthitam /
children.translated_text: In the wilderness of the ocean of sorrow, this foremost vehicle has arrived;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjagattārayiṣyati // Lal_11.7 //
children.translated_text: he will attain that <s>dharma</s> which will ferry the world across! // Lal_11.7 //

body.text: aparo 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: Another said:

children.text: kleśabandhanabaddhānāṃ prādurbhūtaḥ pramocakaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those bound by the fetters of the afflictions, this liberator has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ yajjaganmocayiṣyati // Lal_11.8 //
children.translated_text: he will attain that <s>dharma</s> which will free the world! // Lal_11.8 //

body.text: aparo 'pyāha -
body.translated_text: Another said:

children.text: jarāvyādhikiliṣṭānāṃ prādurbhūto bhiṣagvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For those tormented by old age and disease, this supreme physician has appeared;

children.text: ayaṃ taṃ prāpsyate dharmaṃ jātimṛtyupramocakam // Lal_11.9 //
children.translated_text: he will attain that <s>dharma</s> which liberates from birth and death! // Lal_11.9 //

body.text: atha khalu te ṛṣayo bodhisattvamābhirgāthābhirabhistutvā tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya vihāyasā prakrāntāḥ / rājāpi śuddhodano bodhisattvamapaśyan bodhisattvena vinā na ramate sma / so 'vocat - kumāraḥ kva gataḥ? nainaṃ paśyāmīti / tatra mahājanakāyo nirdhāvito 'bhūt kumāraṃ parigaveṣamāṇaḥ / tato 'nyatama amātyo bodhisattvaṃ paśyati sma jambucchāyāyāṃ paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaṃ dhyāyantam / sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ ca tasmin samaye chāyā parivṛttābhūt / jambucchāyā ca bodhisattvasya kāyaṃ na vijahāti sma / sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ śīghraṃ śīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpo rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramya gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then those sages, having praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with these verses and circumambulated him three times, departed through the sky. And King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, not seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, could not find joy without the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He said: 'Where has the prince gone? I do not see him!' Then a great crowd rushed out searching for the prince. Then a certain minister saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated cross-legged in the shade of a <s>Jambu</s> tree, meditating. And though the shadows of all the trees had turned at that time, the shadow of the <s>Jambu</s> tree did not leave the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body. Seeing this, he was amazed, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with rapture and gladness. Very swiftly, in great haste, he approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and addressed him in two verses:

children.text: paśya deva kumāro 'yaṃ jambucchāyāhi dhyāyati /
children.translated_text: 'See, O lord! This prince meditates in the shade of the <s>Jambu</s> tree;
