children.text: yathā śakro 'thavā brahmā śriyā tejena śobhate // Lal_11.10 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Śakra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s>, he shines with glory and splendor! // Lal_11.10 //

children.text: yasya vṛkṣasya chāyāyāṃ niṣaṇṇo varalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The shadow of the tree beneath which this one of excellent marks is seated

children.text: sainaṃ na jahate chāyā dhyāyantaṃ purūṣottamam // Lal_11.11 //
children.translated_text: does not leave this best of men as he meditates.' // Lal_11.11 //

body.text: atha rājā śuddhodano yena sa jambuvṛkṣastenopasaṃkrāmat / so 'drākṣīdbodhisattvaṃ śriyā tejasā ca jvalantam / dṛṣṭā caimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> approached that <s>Jambu</s> tree. He saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> blazing with glory and splendor. Having seen him, he spoke this verse:

children.text: hutāśano vā girimūrdhni saṃsthitaḥ śaśīva nakṣatragaṇānucīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a fire stationed on a mountain peak, like the moon attended by hosts of stars,

children.text: vepanti gātrāṇi mi paśyato imaṃ dhyāyantu tejo nu pradīpakalpam // Lal_11.12 //
children.translated_text: my limbs tremble as I behold this one meditating — his splendor is like a lamp! // Lal_11.12 //

body.text: sa bodhisattvasya pādāvabhivandyemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Having bowed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, he spoke this verse:

children.text: yadā cāsi mune jāto yadā dhyāyasi cārciman /
children.translated_text: When you were born, O Sage, and now as you meditate, O radiant one,

children.text: ekadvirapi te nātha pādau vande vināyaka // Lal_11.13 //
children.translated_text: once and twice, O Lord, I bow at your feet, O Guide! // Lal_11.13 //

body.text: tatra triphalavāhakā dārakāḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti sma / tānamātyā evamāhuḥ - mā śabdaṃ mā śabdaṃ kārṣṭeti / te 'vocan - kimetaditi / amātyā āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: There some fruit-bearing boys were making noise. The ministers told them: 'Hush! Hush!' They said: 'What is this?' The ministers said:

children.text: vyāvṛtte timiranudasya maṇḍale 'pi vyomābhaṃ śubhavaralakṣaṇāgradhārim /
children.translated_text: Though the disk of the darkness-dispeller [sun] has turned away, the sky-hued one bearing the supreme and beautiful marks,

children.text: dhyāyantaṃ girinicalaṃ narendraputraṃ siddhārthaṃ na jahati saiva vṛkṣachāyā // Lal_11.14 //
children.translated_text: meditating, motionless as a mountain, the son of the king — <s>Siddhārtha</s> — the very shadow of the tree does not leave him! // Lal_11.14 //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: grīṣme vasanta samudāgata jeṣṭhamāse saṃpuṣpite kusumapallavasaṃprakīrṇe /
children.translated_text: In the summer, when spring has arrived in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when [the trees] are in bloom, strewn with flower-buds and blossoms,

children.text: kroñcāmayūraśukasārikasaṃpraghuṣṭe bhūyiṣṭha śākiyasutā abhiniṣkramanti // Lal_11.15 //
children.translated_text: resounding with curlews, peacocks, parrots, and <s>Sārikā</s> birds — the <s>Śākya</s> youths mostly go out [to play]. // Lal_11.15 //

children.text: chando 'bhyuvāca parivāritu dārikebhiḥ hantā kumāra vani gacchama locanārtham /
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, surrounded by the boys, addressed [him]: 'Come, O prince, let us go to the forest for a sight!

children.text: kiṃ te gṛhe nivasato hi yathā dvijasya hanta vrajāma vaya codananārisaṃgham // Lal_11.16 //
children.translated_text: What is the use of staying at home, like a caged bird? Come, let us go together with the companions of <s>Udodana</s> [<s>Śuddhodana</s>]'s son!' // Lal_11.16 //

children.text: madhyāhnakālasamaye suviśuddhasattvaḥ pañcāśataiḥ parivṛtaiḥ saha ceṭakebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: At midday, the one of supremely pure being, surrounded by fifty attendants,

children.text: na ca mātu naiva ca pituḥ prativedayitvā so 'buddha niṣkrāmiti gacchi kṛṣāṇagrāmam // Lal_11.17 //
children.translated_text: without informing either his mother or father, went out unaware, heading to the ploughing village. // Lal_11.17 //

children.text: tasmiṃśca pārthivavarasya kṛṣāṇagrāme jambudrumo 'bhavadanekaviśālaśākhaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in that ploughing village of the king there was a <s>Jambu</s> tree with many widespread branches.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kumāra pratibuddha dukhena cotto dhiksaṃskṛteti bahuduḥkha kṛṣī karoti // Lal_11.18 //
children.translated_text: Seeing it, the prince was awakened and, moved by sorrow, [thought]: 'Shame on the conditioned!' — [seeing] the great suffering [of those who] plough. // Lal_11.18 //

children.text: so jambuchāyamupagamya vinītacitto tṛṇakāni gṛhya svaya saṃstaru saṃstaritvā /
children.translated_text: He approached the <s>Jambu</s> shade with a disciplined mind, and taking grass, he spread a seat himself;

children.text: paryaṅkamābhujiya ujju karitva kāyaṃ catvāri dhyāna śubha dhyāyi sa bodhisattvaḥ // Lal_11.19 //
children.translated_text: sitting cross-legged with body held straight, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditated on the four noble <s>dhyānas</s>. // Lal_11.19 //

children.text: pañcā ṛṣī khagapathena hi gacchamānā jambūya mūrdhni na prabhonti parākrametum /
children.translated_text: Five sages, traveling along the path of the sky, were unable to pass over the top of the <s>Jambu</s> tree;

children.text: te visthitā nihatamānamadāśca bhūtvā sarve samagrasahitā samudīkṣayanto // Lal_11.20 //
children.translated_text: they halted, their pride and intoxication struck down, and all together, united, they looked up. // Lal_11.20 //

children.text: vaya meruparvatavaraṃ tatha cakravālān nirbhidya gacchama javena asajjamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We who split through <s>Meru</s>, the best of mountains, and the <s>Cakravālas</s>, passing swiftly without hindrance —

children.text: te jambuvṛkṣa na prabhoma atikrametuṃ ko nvatra heturayamadya bhaviṣyatīha // Lal_11.21 //
children.translated_text: we are unable to pass over this <s>Jambu</s> tree! What is the cause here? What is happening today?' // Lal_11.21 //

children.text: avatīrya medinitale ca pratiṣṭhihitvā paśyanti śākyatanayaṃ tahi jambumūle /
children.translated_text: Descending to the surface of the earth and standing [there], they saw the son of the <s>Śākyas</s> at the base of the <s>Jambu</s> tree,

children.text: jambunadārcisadṛśaṃ prabhatejaraśmiṃ paryaṅkabandhu tada dhyāyatu bodhisattvam // Lal_11.22 //
children.translated_text: radiant as <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold in his blazing splendor and rays — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> meditating in cross-legged posture. // Lal_11.22 //

children.text: te vismitā daśanakhā kariyāna mūrdhni praṇatā kṛtāñjalipuṭā nipatan krameṣu /
children.translated_text: Amazed, they placed their ten fingers on their heads, bowed with palms joined, and fell at his feet:

children.text: sādho sujāta sumukhaṃ karuṇā jagasya śīghraṃ vibuddha amṛte vinayasva sattvān // Lal_11.23 //
children.translated_text: 'Excellent, O well-born one! O compassionate one toward the world! Swiftly awaken and guide beings to the deathless!' // Lal_11.23 //

children.text: parivṛtta sūrya na jahī sugatasya chāyā olambate drumavaraṃ yatha padmapatram /
children.translated_text: The sun had turned, but the shadow did not leave the <s>Sugata</s>; the finest tree drooped over like a lotus petal;

children.text: devā sahasra bahavaḥ sthita añjalībhiḥ vandanti tasya caraṇau kṛtaniścayasya // Lal_11.24 //
children.translated_text: thousands of gods stood with palms joined, worshipping the feet of him who had made his resolution. // Lal_11.24 //

children.text: śuddhodanaśca svagṛhe parimārgamāṇaḥ saṃpṛcchate kva nu gataḥ sa hi me kumāraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddhodana</s>, searching in his own house, asked: 'Where has my prince gone?'

children.text: mātṛsvasā avaci mārgata no labhāmi saṃpṛcchatā narapate kva gataḥ kumāraḥ // Lal_11.25 //
children.translated_text: The maternal aunt said: 'Though I searched, I could not find him; O lord of men, ask where the prince has gone!' // Lal_11.25 //

children.text: śuddhodanastvaritu pṛcchati kāñcukīyaṃ dauvārikaṃ tathapi cāntajanaṃ samantāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddhodana</s> quickly asked the chamberlain, the doorkeeper, and the inner attendants all around:

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ kumāra mama kenaci niṣkramanto śṛṇute varūpagatu deva kṛṣāṇagrāmam // Lal_11.26 //
children.translated_text: 'Has anyone seen the prince going out?' He heard: 'He has gone to the ploughing village, O lord!' // Lal_11.26 //

children.text: so śīghrameva tvaritaṃ saha śākiyebhiḥ niṣkrāntu prekṣi kṛṣigrāmagiriṃ praviṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Swiftly, in haste, together with the <s>Śākyas</s>, he went out and saw [the prince] who had entered the ploughing-village hill,

children.text: yatha sūryakoṭiniyutāni samudgatāni tatha prekṣate hitakaraṃ śiriyā jvalantam // Lal_11.27 //
children.translated_text: blazing with glory and beneficence, as if <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of suns had risen. // Lal_11.27 //

children.text: mukuṭaṃ ca khaṅga tatha pāduka chorayitvā kṛtvā daśāṅguli śire abhivandite tam /
children.translated_text: Casting aside his crown, sword, and sandals, placing his ten fingers on his head, he bowed to him:

children.text: sādhū subhūtavacanā ṛṣayo mahātmā vyaktaṃ kumāra abhiniṣkrami bodhihetoḥ // Lal_11.28 //
children.translated_text: 'How true are the words of the great-souled sages! Clearly, the prince will go forth for the sake of awakening!' // Lal_11.28 //

children.text: paripūrṇa dvādaśaśatā suprasannadevāḥ paccāśatā upagatā yatha śākiyānām /
children.translated_text: Twelve hundred and fifty well-pleased gods came to the <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca ṛddhi sugate guṇasāgarasya saṃbodhicittu janayaṃ dṛḍhaāśayena // Lal_11.29 //
children.translated_text: and seeing the supernatural display of the <s>Sugata</s>, the ocean of virtues, they generated the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) with firm resolve. // Lal_11.29 //

children.text: so kampayitva trisahasra aśeṣabhūmiṃ smṛtu saṃprajānu pratibuddha tataḥ samādheḥ /
children.translated_text: Having caused the entire trichiliocosm to tremble, mindful and fully aware, he arose from that concentration;

children.text: brahmasvaraḥ pitaramālapate dyutīmān utsṛjya tāta kṛṣigrāmabhato gaveṣa // Lal_11.30 //
children.translated_text: with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, the radiant one addressed his father: 'Dismiss the ploughing-village laborers, O father, and search [for something higher]!' // Lal_11.30 //

children.text: yadi svarṇakāryu ahu svarṇa pravarṣayiṣye yadi vastrakāryu ahameva pradāsyi vastrāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'If gold is needed, I will shower gold; if garments are needed, I myself will give garments;

children.text: atha dhānyakāryu ahameva pravarṣayiṣye samyakprayukta bhava sarvajage narendra // Lal_11.31 //
children.translated_text: if grain is needed, I myself will shower it — be rightly devoted [to dharma], O lord of men, in the whole world!' // Lal_11.31 //

children.text: anuśāsayitva pitaraṃ janapāriṣadyāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe puravaraṃ puna so pravekṣī /
children.translated_text: Having instructed his father and the assembly of the people, at that very moment he entered the best of cities again;

children.text: anuvartamāna jagataḥ sthihate puresmiṃ naiṣmkramyayuktamanasaḥ suviśuddhasattvaḥ // Lal_11.32 //
children.translated_text: conforming to the ways of the world, the one of supremely pure being dwelt in the city, his mind set on renunciation. // Lal_11.32 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare kṛṣigrāmaparivarto nāma ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the eleventh chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Ploughing Village' (<s>Kṛṣigrāmaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 12
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 12.

body.text: śilpasaṃdarśanaparivarto dvādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Twelfth Chapter: On the Display of Skills (<s>Śilpasaṃdarśanaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saṃvṛddhe kumāre rājā śuddhodano 'pareṇa samayena śākyagaṇena sārdhaṃ saṃsthāgāre niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt / tatra te mahallakamahallakāḥ śākyā rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāhuḥ - yatkhalu devo jānīyāt / ayaṃ sarvārthasiddhakumāro naimittikairbrāhmaṇaiḥ kṛtaniścayaiśca devairyadbhūyasaivaṃ nirdiṣṭo yadi kumāro 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati, tathāgato bhaviṣyatyarhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / uta nābhiniṣkramiṣyati rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī caturaṅgo vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ / tasyemāni sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti / tadyathā - cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ aśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnam / evaṃ saptaratnam / saṃpūrṇaṃ cāsya putrasahasraṃ bhaviṣyati śūrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām / sa imaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamadaṇḍenāśastreṇābhinirjityādhyāvasiṣyati saha dharmeṇeti / tasmānniveśanaṃ kumārasya kriyatāmiti / tatra strīgaṇaparivṛto ratiṃ vetsyati, nābhiniṣkramiṣyati / evamasmākaṃ cakravartivaṃśasya cānupacchedo bhaviṣyati / mānitāśca bhaviṣyāmo 'navadyāśca sarvakoṭarājabhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the prince had grown up, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> at a later time was seated together with the <s>Śākya</s> assembly in the council hall. There those most senior <s>Śākya</s> elders said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'May the sovereign please take note. This prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has been declared by the sign-reading <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and by the gods who have ascertained [his destiny] — mostly thus: If the prince goes forth, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. But if he does not go forth, he will become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>, a four-limbed conqueror, a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king, endowed with the seven treasures. These will be his seven treasures: the wheel-treasure, elephant-treasure, horse-treasure, jewel-treasure, woman-treasure, householder-treasure, and general-treasure — thus seven treasures. And he will have a full thousand sons, heroes, of noble form, crushers of enemy armies. He will conquer this circle of the earth without rod and without sword, and rule it by <s>Dharma</s> alone.' 'Therefore let a household be established for the prince. Surrounded by a company of women, he will find delight and will not go forth. Thus the lineage of our <s>Cakravartin</s> dynasty will remain unbroken. And we shall be honored and blameless before all the <s>koṭi</s>-kings.' //

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodana evamāha - yadyevaṃ tena hi vyavalokayata kamatā kanyā kumārasyānurūpā syāt /
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said thus: 'If so, then look about — what maiden would be suitable and fitting for the prince?'

body.text: tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyaśatāni / ekaika evamāha - mama duhitā anurūpā syāt kumārasya / surūpā mama duhiteti /
body.translated_text: There were approximately five hundred <s>Śākya</s> [families]. Each one said: 'My daughter would be fitting for the prince. My daughter is beautiful.'

body.text: rājā prāha - durāsadaḥ kumāraḥ / tat prativedayiṣyāmastāvat kumārasya, katamā te kanyā rocata iti /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'The prince is hard to satisfy. Let us first inform the prince — which maiden pleases you?'

body.text: tataśca te sarve saṃnipatya kumārasyaināṃ prakṛtimārocayanti sma / tān kumāra uvāca - saptame divase prativacanaṃ śroṣyatheti //
body.translated_text: Then all of them, having assembled, reported this matter to the prince. The prince said to them: 'On the seventh day you shall hear my answer.' //

body.text: tato bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat -
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> —

children.text: vidita mama ananta kāmadoṣāḥ saraṇasarvairasaśokaduḥkhamūlāḥ /
children.translated_text: The faults of desires are known to me — boundless, the root of all sorrow, grief, and suffering;

children.text: bhayakara viṣapatrasaṃnikāśāḥ jvalananibhā asidhāratulyarūpāḥ // Lal_12.1 //
children.translated_text: fearsome, like a leaf of poison, like fire, resembling the edge of a sword. // Lal_12.1 //

children.text: kāmaguṇi na me 'sti chandarāgo na ca ahu śobhami istrigāramadhye /
children.translated_text: I have no desire or passion for sensual pleasures, nor do I shine [with joy] in a house with women;

children.text: yannu ahu vane vaseya tūṣṇīṃ dhyānasamādhisukhena śāntacittaḥ // Lal_12.2 //
children.translated_text: rather, let me dwell silently in the forest, my mind pacified by the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>. // Lal_12.2 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: sa punarapi mīmāṃsopāyakauśalyamāmukhīkṛtya sattvaparipākamavekṣamāṇo mahākarūṇāṃ saṃjanayya tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Yet again, applying the skill in means of investigation and observing the ripening of beings, generating great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), at that time he spoke this verse —

children.text: saṃkīrṇi paṅki padumāni vivṛddhimanti ākīrṇa rāja naramadhyi labhāti pūjām /
children.translated_text: In muddy, impure [waters] lotuses grow forth in abundance; in [the midst of] people, a king receives worship.

children.text: yada bodhisattva parivārabalaṃ labhante tada sattvakoṭinayutānyamṛte vinenti // Lal_12.3 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Bodhisattvas</s> obtain a retinue and strength, then they lead <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of beings to the deathless. // Lal_12.3 //

children.text: ye cāpi pūrvaka abhūdvidu bodhisattvāḥ sarvebhi bhārya suta darśita istrigārāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those who were <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of former [times], the knowledgeable ones — all of them showed [life with] wives, sons, and women's quarters.

children.text: na ca rāgarakta na ca dhyānasukhebhi bhraṣṭāḥ hantānuśikṣayi ahaṃ pi guṇeṣu teṣām // Lal_12.4 //
children.translated_text: Yet they were neither stained by passion nor fallen from the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>. Come, I too shall train in those virtues of theirs! // Lal_12.4 //

children.text: na ca prākṛtā mama vadhū anukūla yā syād yasyā na iṣyatu guṇā sada satyavākyam /
children.translated_text: No ordinary [woman] would be a wife suitable for me — one in whom the virtues [I] desire and truthful speech are not found.

children.text: yā cinti mahyamabhirādhayate 'pramattā rūpeṇa janmakulagotratayā suśuddhā // Lal_12.5 //
children.translated_text: She who satisfies my thought, vigilant, pure in form, birth, family, and lineage — // Lal_12.5 //

children.text: so gāthalekha likhite guṇaarthayuktā yā kanya īdṛśa bhave mama tāṃ varethā /
children.translated_text: He wrote a verse-letter endowed with virtues and meaning: 'Whatever maiden is of such [qualities], choose her for me.'

children.text: na mamārthu prākṛtajanena asaṃvṛtena yasyā guṇā kathayamī mama tāṃ varethā // Lal_12.6 //
children.translated_text: 'I have no need of an ordinary, unrestrained person; she whose virtues I shall describe — choose her for me.' // Lal_12.6 //

children.text: yā rūpayauvanavarā na ca rūpamattā mātā svasā va yatha vartati maitracittā /
children.translated_text: She who is excellent in beauty and youth yet not intoxicated by beauty, who conducts herself with a loving mind as toward a mother or sister,

children.text: tyāge ratā śramaṇabrāhmaṇadānaśīlā tāṃ tādṛśāṃ mama vadhūṃ varayasva tāta // Lal_12.7 //
children.translated_text: who delights in generosity, habituated to giving to <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — choose such a one as my bride, O father! // Lal_12.7 //

children.text: yasyā na mānu na khilo na ca doṣamasti na ca śāṭhya īrṣya na ca māya na ujjubhraṣṭā /
children.translated_text: She in whom there is no deceit, no spite, no fault, no cunning, no envy, no guile, and who is not devoid of uprightness,

children.text: svapnāntare 'pi purūṣe na pare 'bhiraktā tuṣṭā svakena patinā śayate 'pramattā // Lal_12.8 //
children.translated_text: who even in dreams is not attached to another man, who is content with her own husband, sleeping vigilantly — // Lal_12.8 //

body.text: na ca garvitā na pi ca uddhata na pragalbhā nirmāna mānavigatāpi ca ceṭibhūtā /
body.translated_text: Neither haughty, nor unruly, nor bold, free from pretense and pride, and servant-like [in humility],

body.text: na ca pānagṛddha na raseṣu na śabdagandhe nirlobhabhidhyavigatā svadhanena tuṣṭā // Lal_12.9 //
body.translated_text: not addicted to drink, nor to tastes, nor to sounds and scents, free from greed and covetousness, content with her own wealth — // Lal_12.9 //

children.text: satye sthitā na pi ca cañcala naiva bhrāntā na ca uddhatonnatasthitā hirivastrachannā /
children.translated_text: Established in truth, not fickle, not confused, not proud and puffed up, covered by the garment of modesty,

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭimaṅgalaratā sada dharmayuktā kāyena vāca manasā sada śuddhabhāvā // Lal_12.10 //
children.translated_text: not devoted to superstitious omens, always endowed with <s>Dharma</s>, pure in thought always — in body, speech, and mind. // Lal_12.10 //

children.text: na ca styānamiddhabahulā na ca mānamūḍhā mīmāṃsayukta sukṛtā sada dharmacārī /
children.translated_text: Not given to sloth and torpor, not deluded by pride, endowed with investigation, virtuous, always walking in <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: śvaśrau ca tasya śvaśure yatha śāstṛpremā dāsī kalatra jani yādṛśamātmaprema // Lal_12.11 //
children.translated_text: who has love for her mother-in-law and father-in-law as for a teacher, [who treats] servants, spouse, and [all] people as if with self-love — // Lal_12.11 //

children.text: śāstre vidhijña kuśalā gaṇikā yathaiva paścāt svapet prathamamutthihate ca śayyāta /
children.translated_text: Skilled and knowledgeable in rules, like a courtesan in [her] art, she sleeps last and rises first from bed,

children.text: maitrānuvarti akuhāpi ca mātṛbhūtā etādṛśīṃ mi nṛpate vadhukāṃ vṛṇīṣva // Lal_12.12 //
children.translated_text: friendly in conduct, without deceit, and like a mother — choose such a bride for me, O king! // Lal_12.12 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodana imā gāthā vācayitvā purohitamāmantrayate sma - gaccha tvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa kapilavastumahānagare / sarvagṛhāṇyanupraviśya kanyā vyavalokaya / yasyā ete guṇāḥ saṃvidyante kṣatriyakanyāyā vā brāhmaṇakanyāyā vā vaiśyakanyāyā vā śūdrakanyāyā vā tāṃ kanyāmasmākaṃ prativedaya / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? na hi kumāraḥ kulārthiko na gotrārthikaḥ / guṇārthika eva kumāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having had these verses read, addressed the chaplain (<s>purohita</s>): 'Go, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, throughout the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Enter all the houses and examine the maidens. She in whom these virtues are found — whether a <s>kṣatriya</s> maiden, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> maiden, a <s>vaiśya</s> maiden, or a <s>śūdra</s> maiden — report that maiden to us. For what reason? The prince does not seek family, nor does he seek lineage. The prince seeks only virtues.' //

body.text: tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: And at that time he spoke this verse —

children.text: brāhmaṇīṃ kṣatriyāṃ kanyāṃ veśyāṃ śūdrīṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maiden, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> maiden, a <s>Vaiśya</s> or a <s>Śūdra</s> maiden likewise —

children.text: yasyā ete guṇāḥ santi tāṃ me kanyāṃ pravedaya // Lal_12.13 //
children.translated_text: she in whom these virtues are found, report that maiden to me. // Lal_12.13 //

children.text: na kulena na gotreṇa kumāro mama vismitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The prince is not amazed by family or lineage;

children.text: guṇe satye ca dharme ca tatrāsya ramate manaḥ // Lal_12.14 //
children.translated_text: in virtue, truth, and <s>Dharma</s> — therein his mind delights. // Lal_12.14 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa purohitastaṃ gāthālekhaṃ gṛhītvā kapilavastuni mahānagare gṛhādgṛhaṃ vyavalokayan gatvā hiṇḍan kanyāṃ paryeṣate sma / evaṃguṇayuktāmapaśyan (na caiva guṇayuktāṃ kanyāṃ) / so 'nupūrveṇa vicaran yena daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / sa taṃ niveśanaṃ praviṣṭo 'drākṣīt kanyāmabhirūpāṃ prāsādikāṃ darśanīyāṃ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgatāṃ nātidīrghāṃ nātihrasvāṃ nātisthūlāṃ nātikṛśāṃ nātigaurāṃ nātikṛṣṇāṃ prathamayauvanāvasthāṃ strīratnamiva khyāyamānām /
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that chaplain, having taken the verse-letter, went from house to house in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, wandering about, examining, and searching for a maiden. He did not see [any] maiden endowed with such virtues. Roaming in due order, he came to the residence of the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>. Having entered that residence, he saw a maiden — beautiful, gracious, lovely, endowed with the supreme excellence of fair complexion, neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout nor too thin, neither too fair nor too dark, in the prime of her first youth, renowned like a woman-jewel.

body.text: atha sā dārikā purohitasya caraṇau gṛhītvā evamāha - kena te mahābrāhmaṇa kāryam?
body.translated_text: Then that maiden, grasping the chaplain's feet, said thus: 'What business brings you, O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>?'

body.text: purohita āha -
body.translated_text: The chaplain said —

children.text: śuddhodanasya tanayaḥ paramābhirūpo dvātriṃśalakṣaṇadharo guṇatejayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, of supreme beauty, bearing the thirty-two marks, endowed with virtue and splendor —

children.text: teneti gātha likhitā guṇaye vadhūnāṃ yasyā guṇāsti hi ime sa hi tasya patnī // Lal_12.15 //
children.translated_text: by him a verse has been written concerning the virtues of brides; she in whom these virtues are found, she shall be his wife. // Lal_12.15 //

body.text: sa tasyāstaṃ lekhamupanāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: He presented that letter to her. //

body.text: atha sā dārikā taṃ gāthālekhaṃ vācayitvā smitamupadarśya taṃ purohitaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then that maiden, having read that verse-letter, displayed a smile and addressed the chaplain with a verse —

children.text: mahyeti brāhmaṇa guṇā anurūpa sarve so me patirbhavatu saumya surūparūpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These virtues, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, are all fitting for me. Let him, the gentle one of supreme beauty, be my husband.

children.text: bhaṇahi kumāru yadi kārya ma hū vilamba mā hīnaprākṛtajanena bhaveya vāsaḥ // Lal_12.16 //
children.translated_text: Tell the prince — if there is business [to be done], let there be no delay, lest I be made to dwell with an inferior, common person!' // Lal_12.16 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha sa khalu purohito rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaiva tamarthamārocayati sma - dṛṣṭā mayā deva kanyā yā kumārasyānurūpā syāt / āha - kasyāsau? āha - daṇḍapāṇerdeva śākyasya duhitā //
body.translated_text: Then that chaplain, approaching King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, reported the matter: 'I have seen, O lord, a maiden who would be fitting for the prince.' He said: 'Whose is she?' He said: 'The daughter of the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, O lord.' //

body.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavat - durāsadaḥ kumāraḥ śubhādhimuktaśca / prāyeṇa ca mātṛgrāmo 'saṃvidyamānaguṇo 'pi guṇānāmātmani prajānīte / yannvahamaśokabhāṇḍakāni kārayeyam, yāni kumāraḥ sarvadārikābhyo 'nuprayacchet / tatra yasyāṃ dārikāyāṃ kumārasya cakṣurabhiniveśyati, tāṃ kumārasya varayiṣyāmīti //
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'The prince is hard to satisfy and inclined toward the pure. And generally, the female sex, even when not possessing virtues, recognizes [such] virtues in themselves. Let me have gifts prepared — auspicious articles — which the prince will distribute to all the maidens. And whichever maiden the prince's eye rests upon, that one I shall choose as bride for the prince.' //

body.text: atha khalu rājā śuddhodano 'śokabhāṇḍāni kārayati sma suvarṇamayāni rūpyamayāni nānāratnamayāni / kārayitvā ca kapilavastuni mahānagare ghaṇṭāghoṣaṇāṃ kārayāmāsa - saptame divase kumāro darśanaṃ dāsyati, aśokabhāṇḍakāni ca dārikābhyo viśrāṇayiṣyati / tatra sarvadārikābhiḥ saṃsthāgāre saṃnipatitavyamiti //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had auspicious articles made — of gold, of silver, of various jewels. Having had them made, he had a bell-announcement proclaimed throughout the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>: 'On the seventh day the prince will grant an audience and will distribute the auspicious articles to the maidens. All maidens are to assemble in the council hall.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ saptame divase bodhisattvaḥ saṃsthāgāramupasaṃkramya bhadrāsane nyaṣīdat / rājāpi śuddhodano 'dṛśyapuruṣān sthāpayati sma - yasyāṃ dārikāyāṃ kumārasya cakṣuḥ saṃniviśet, tāṃ mamārocayadhvamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, on the seventh day the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the council hall and sat upon the auspicious throne. And King <s>Śuddhodana</s> posted hidden observers, [saying]: 'Whichever maiden the prince's eye rests upon, report her to me.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāvantyaḥ kapilavastuni mahānagare dārikāstāḥ sarvā yena saṃsthāgāro yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya darśanāya aśokabhāṇḍakāni ca pratigṛhītum //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, all the maidens in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> approached the council hall and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and to receive the auspicious articles. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo yathāgatābhyastābhyo dārikābhyo 'śokabhāṇḍakānyanuprayacchati sma / tāśca dārikā na śaknuvanti sma bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaśca soḍhum / tā aśokabhāṇḍakāni gṛhītvā śīghraṃ śīghrameva prakrāmanti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> distributed the auspicious articles to the maidens as each arrived. And those maidens were unable to endure the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s radiance and splendor. Having taken the auspicious articles, they departed very quickly. //

body.text: atha daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā, sā dāsīgaṇaparivṛtā puraskṛtā yena saṃsthāgāro yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramyaikānte 'sthāt bodhisattvamanimeṣābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ prekṣamāṇā / tadyadā bodhisattvena sarvāṇyaśokabhāṇḍāni dattāni, tadā sā bodhisattvamupasaṃkramya prahasitavadanā bodhisattvamevamāha - kumāra kiṃ te mayāpanītaṃ yastvaṃ māṃ vimānayasi?
body.translated_text: Then the daughter of the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> maiden named <s>Gopā</s>, surrounded and attended by a company of maidservants, approached the council hall and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, she stood to one side, gazing at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with unblinking eyes. When all the auspicious articles had been given away by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, she then approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and, with a smiling face, said thus to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Prince, what have I done to offend you that you disregard me?'

body.text: āha - nāhaṃ tvāṃ vimānayāmi, api tu khalu punastvamabhipaścādāgateti / sa tasyai cānekaśatasahasramūlyamaṅgulīyakaṃ nirmucya prādāt //
body.translated_text: He said: 'I do not disregard you; rather, you came last.' And he took off a ring worth many hundreds of thousands and gave it to her. //

body.text: sā prāha - idamahaṃ kumāra tavāntikādarhāmi? āha - imāni madīyānyābharaṇāni, gṛhyatām / sā āha - na vayaṃ kumāraṃ vyalaṃkariṣyāmaḥ? alaṃkariṣyāmo vayaṃ kumāram / ityuktvā sā kanyā prakrāmat //
body.translated_text: She said: 'Is this what I deserve from the prince?' He said: 'These are my ornaments — take them.' She said: 'Shall we not adorn the prince? We shall adorn the prince!' Having said this, the maiden departed. //

body.text: tatastairguhyapuruṣai rājānaṃ śuddhodanamupasaṃkramyaiṣa vṛttānto nivedito 'bhūt - deva daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā, tasyāṃ kumārasya cakṣurniviṣṭam, muhūrtaṃ ca tayoḥ saṃlāpo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then those hidden observers approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and reported this account: 'O lord, the daughter of the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> maiden named <s>Gopā</s> — upon her the prince's eye rested, and for a moment there was conversation between the two.' //

body.text: ityetatkhalu vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā śuddhodano daṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasya purohitaṃ dautyena preṣayati sma - yā te duhitā, sā mama kumārasya pradīyatāmiti //
body.translated_text: Having heard this report, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent the chaplain as an envoy to the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>: 'Your daughter — let her be given to my prince.' //

body.text: daṇḍapāṇirāha - ārya kumāro gṛhe sukhasaṃvṛddhaḥ / asmākaṃ cāyaṃ kuladharmaḥ śilpajñasya kanyā dātavyā nāśilpajñasyeti / kumāraśca na śilpajño nāsidhanuṣkalāpayuddhasālambhavidhijñaḥ / tatkathamaśilpajñāyāhaṃ duhitaraṃ dāsyāmi?
body.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> said: 'Noble sir, the prince has grown up comfortably at home. And it is our family custom that a maiden is to be given to one who is skilled in the arts, not to one who is unskilled. The prince is not skilled in arts, nor knowledgeable in the techniques of sword, bow, quiver, combat, wrestling, or ritual procedure. How then shall I give my daughter to one unskilled in the arts?'

body.text: ityetacca rājñaḥ prativeditam / tato rājña etadabhavat - dvirapīdamahaṃ sahadharmeṇa coditaḥ / yadāpi mayoktaṃ kasmācchākyakumārāḥ kumārasyopasthānāya nāgacchantīti tadāpyahamabhihitaḥ - kiṃ vayaṃ maṇḍakasyopasthānaṃ kariṣyāma iti / etarhyapyevamiti pradhyāyanniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: This was reported to the king. Then the king thought: 'For the second time I have been challenged with the rightful custom. When I previously asked why the <s>Śākya</s> youths do not come to attend upon the prince, I was told: "Are we to render service to a weakling (<s>maṇḍaka</s>)?" And now again it is the same.' He sat lost in thought.

body.text: bodhisattvaścainaṃ vṛttāntamaśroṣīt / śrutvā ca yena rājā śuddhodanastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramyaivamāha - deva kimidaṃ dīnamanāstiṣṭhasi?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> heard of this matter. Having heard, he approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having approached, he said: 'Lord, why do you sit so dejected?'

body.text: rājā āha - alaṃ te kumāra anena /
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Enough, prince — this is no concern of yours.'

body.text: kumāra āha - deva sarvathā tāvadavaśyabhevamākhyātavyam / yāvattrirapi bodhisattvo rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ paripṛcchati sma //
body.translated_text: The prince said: 'Lord, in any case this must certainly be told to me.' Three times the <s>Bodhisattva</s> questioned King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvāya tāṃ prakṛtimārocayati sma / tāṃ śrutvā bodhisattva āha - deva asti punariha nagare kaścidyo mayā sārdhaṃ samarthaḥ śilpena śilapamupadarśayitum?
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> informed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the matter. Having heard it, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Lord, is there anyone in this city who is capable of demonstrating his skill in competition with me?'

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ prahasitavadano bodhisattvamevamāha - śakyasi punastvaṃ putra śilpamupadarśayitum? sa āha - bāḍhaṃ śakyāmi deva / tena hi saṃnipātyantāṃ sarvaśilpajñāḥ, yeṣāṃ purataḥ svaṃ śilpamupadarśayiṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with a smiling face, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Are you then able, son, to demonstrate your skill?' He replied: 'Indeed, I am able, Lord.' 'Then let all the skilled artisans be assembled — before whom I shall demonstrate my own skill.'

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ kapilavastuni mahānagaravare ghaṇṭāghoṣaṇāṃ kārayati sma - saptame divase kumāraḥ svaṃ śilpamupadarśayati / tatra sarvaśilpajñaiḥ saṃnipatitavyam //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had a bell-proclamation made in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>: 'On the seventh day, the prince shall demonstrate his skill. All skilled artisans are to assemble there.'

body.text: tatra saptame divase pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni saṃnipatitānyabhūvan / daṇḍapāṇeśca śākyasya duhitā gopā nāma śākyakanyā jayapatākā sthāpitābhūt - yo vā atra asidhanuṣkalāpayuddhasālambheṣu jeṣyati, tasyaiṣā bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: There, on the seventh day, five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths assembled. And a <s>Śākya</s> maiden named <s>Gopā</s>, the daughter of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, was set as the victory-banner [prize] — 'Whoever among them shall be victorious in sword, bow, quiver, combat, and wrestling — she shall be his.'

body.text: tatra sarvapurato devadattaḥ kumāro nagarādabhiniṣkrāmati sma / śvetaśca hastī mahāpramāṇo bodhisattvasyārthe nagaraṃ praveśyate sma / tatra devadattaḥ kumāra īrṣyayā ca śākyabalamadena ca mattaḥ / sa taṃ hastināgaṃ vāmena pāṇinā śuṇḍāyāṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā capeṭayā ekaprahāreṇaiva hato 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: There, before all others, prince <s>Devadatta</s> came forth from the city. A great white elephant was being led into the city for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s sake. <s>Devadatta</s>, out of jealousy and intoxicated by <s>Śākya</s> pride and strength, seized that elephant-lord by the trunk with his left hand and struck it with a slap of his right hand — and with that single blow it was killed.

body.text: tasyānantaraṃ sundaranandakumāro 'bhiniṣkrāmati sma / so 'drākṣīttaṃ hastināgaṃ nagaradvāre hatam / dṛṣṭvā ca paryapṛcchat - kenāyaṃ hata iti / tatra mahājanakāya āha - devadatteneti / sa āha - aśobhanamidaṃ devadattasya / sa taṃ hastināgaṃ lāṅgūle gṛhītvā nagaradvārādapakarṣati sma //
body.translated_text: After him, prince <s>Sundarananda</s> came forth. He saw that elephant-lord lying dead at the city gate. Having seen it, he asked: 'By whom was this killed?' The great crowd said: 'By <s>Devadatta</s>.' He said: 'This is unseemly of <s>Devadatta</s>.' He seized that elephant-lord by the tail and dragged it away from the city gate.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ bodhisattvo rathābhirūḍho 'bhiniṣkrāmati sma / adrākṣīdbodhisattvastaṃ hastinaṃ hatam / dṛṣṭvā ca paryapṛcchat - kenāyaṃ hata iti / āhuḥ - devadatteneti / āha - aśobhanaṃ devadattasya / kena punarasmānnagaradvārādapakarṣita iti / āhuḥ - sundaranandeneti / āha - śobhanamidaṃ sundaranandasya / kiṃ tu mahākāyo 'yaṃ sattvaḥ / so 'yaṃ klinnaḥ sarvanagaraṃ daurgandhena sphuriṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: After that, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> came forth, mounted on a chariot. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw that elephant lying dead. Having seen it, he asked: 'By whom was this killed?' They said: 'By <s>Devadatta</s>.' He said: 'This is unseemly of <s>Devadatta</s>. And by whom was it dragged from the city gate?' They said: 'By <s>Sundarananda</s>.' He said: 'That is commendable of <s>Sundarananda</s>. But this is a great-bodied creature. If it remains wet [decomposing], it will fill the entire city with stench.'

body.text: tataḥ kumāro rathasya evaikaṃ pādaṃ bhūmau prasārya pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ hastināgaṃ lāṅgūle gṛhitvā sapta prākārān sapta ca parikhānatikramya bahirnagarasya krośamātre prakṣipati sma / yatra va pradeśe sa hastī patitastasmin pradeśe mahadbilaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ yatsāṃprataṃ hastigartetyabhidhīyate //
body.translated_text: Then the prince, while still on the chariot, extending one foot to the ground, seized that elephant-lord by the tail with his big toe, and hurled it over seven ramparts and seven moats to the outside of the city, a full <s>krośa</s> away. In the place where that elephant fell, a great pit was formed, which to this day is called '<s>Hastigarta</s>' (the Elephant Pit).

body.text: tatra devamanujāḥ śatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilakilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan / cailavikṣepāṃścākārṣuḥ / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā ime gāthe 'bhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Thereupon, hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of exclamations — 'Aha! Aha!' — shouts of wonder and snapping of fingers. They waved their garments. And the <s>devaputras</s> in the sky uttered these verses:

children.text: yatha mattagajendragatīnāṃ pādāṅguṣṭhatalena gajendram /
children.translated_text: He who has the gait of a lordly rutting elephant — with the tip of his big toe [seizing] a great elephant,

children.text: sapta purāparikhā atikramya kṣiptu bahiḥ svapurātu ayaṃ hi // Lal_12.17 //
children.translated_text: crossing over seven city-walls and moats, hurled it outside his own city! // Lal_12.17 //

children.text: niḥsaṃśayameṣa sumedhā mānabalena samucchritakāyān /
children.translated_text: Without doubt, this wise one, by the power of his strength, those of bodies puffed up with pride —

children.text: saṃsārapurātu bahirdhā eka kṣapiṣyati prajñabalena // Lal_12.18 //
children.translated_text: from the city of <s>saṃsāra</s>, outside, singly he shall destroy them by the power of wisdom! // Lal_12.18 //

body.text: iti hi pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni nagarānniṣkamya yenānyatamaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo yatra śākyakumārāḥ śilpamupadarśayanti sma tenopasaṃkrāman / rājāpi śuddhodano mahallakamahallakāśca śākyā mahāṃśca janakāyo yenāsau pṛthivīpradeśastenopasaṃkrāman bodhisattvasya cānyeṣāṃ ca śākyakumārāṇāṃ śilpaviśeṣaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths came forth from the city and approached a certain place of ground where the <s>Śākya</s> youths were demonstrating their skills. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> also, together with the elder <s>Śākyas</s> and a great crowd of people, approached that place of ground, wishing to see the special skills of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the other <s>Śākya</s> youths.

body.text: tatra ādita eva ye śākyakumārā lipyāṃ paṭuvidhijñāste bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ lipiṃ viśeṣayanti sma / tatra taiḥ śākyairviśvāmitra ācāryaḥ sākṣī sthāpito 'bhūt - sa tvaṃ vyavalokaya katamo 'tra kumāro lipijñāne viśiṣyate yadi vā lekhyato yadi vā bahulipiniryāṇataḥ / atha viśvāmitra ācāryaḥ pratyakṣo bodhisattvasya lipijñāne smitamupadarśayannime gāthe 'bhāṣata -
body.translated_text: There, first of all, those <s>Śākya</s> youths who were skilled in writing competed with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in writing. For this, the <s>Śākyas</s> appointed <s>Viśvāmitra</s> the teacher as judge: 'You observe which youth excels in knowledge of scripts — whether in writing, or in the mastery of many scripts.' Then teacher <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, a direct witness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s knowledge of scripts, displaying a smile, uttered these verses:

children.text: manuṣyaloke 'tha ca devaloke gandharvaloke 'pyasurendraloke /
children.translated_text: 'In the human world, in the divine world, in the <s>Gandharva</s> world, and in the world of <s>Asura</s>-lords —

children.text: yāvanti kecillipi sarvaloke tatraiṣa pāraṃgatu śuddhasattvaḥ // Lal_12.19 //
children.translated_text: whatever scripts exist in all the worlds — in these, this pure being has reached the far shore! // Lal_12.19 //

children.text: nāmāpi yūyaṃ ca ahaṃ ca teṣāṃ lipīna jānāma na cākṣarāṇām /
children.translated_text: You and I do not even know the names of those scripts, nor their characters,

children.text: yānyeṣa jānāti manuṣyacandro ahamatra pratyakṣu vijeṣyate 'yam // Lal_12.20 //
children.translated_text: which this moon among men knows — I bear witness: he shall be victorious here!' // Lal_12.20 //

body.text: śākyā āhuḥ - viśiṣyatāṃ tāvatkumāro lipijñāne / saṃkhyājñāne kumāro viśeṣayitavyo jijñāsyaśca / tatrārjuno nāma śākyagaṇako mahāmātraḥ saṃkhyāgaṇanāsu pāraṃgataḥ, sa sākṣī sthāpito 'bhūt - sa tvaṃ vyavalokaya katamo 'tra kumāro viśiṣyate saṃkhyājñānata iti / tatra bodhisattvaścoddiśati sma, ekaśca śākyakumāro nikṣipati sma, na ca pariprāpayati sma / bodhisattvasyaika dvau trayaścatvāraḥ pañcadaśa viṃśattriṃśaccatvāriṃśatpañcāśacchataṃ yāvatpañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapatkāle nikṣipanti sma, na ca pariprāpayanti sma / tato bodhisattva āha - uddiśata yūyam, ahaṃ nikṣepsyāmīti / tatraikaśākyakumāro bodhisattvasyoddiśati sma, na ca pariprāpayati sma / dvāvapi trayo 'pi pañcāpi daśāpi viṃśatyapi triṃśadapi catvāriṃśadapi pañcāśadapi yāvatpañcāpi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapaduddiśanti sma / na ca pariprāpayanti sma bodhisattvasya nikṣipataḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Śākyas</s> said: 'Let the prince's superiority in knowledge of scripts stand. The prince should be tested and examined in knowledge of numbers.' For this, a <s>Śākya</s> chief accountant named <s>Arjuna</s>, who had reached the far shore in numerical calculation, was appointed as judge: 'You observe which youth excels in knowledge of numbers.' There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would set [problems], and one <s>Śākya</s> youth would calculate, but could not complete [them]. One, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred — up to all five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths would calculate simultaneously, but could not complete [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s problems]. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'You set the problems — I shall calculate.' One <s>Śākya</s> youth set problems for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, but could not exhaust him. Two, three, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty — up to all five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths set problems simultaneously, but could not exhaust the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as he calculated.

body.text: bodhisattva āha - alamalamanena vivādena / sarva idānīmekībhūtvā mamoddiśata, ahaṃ nikṣepsyāmīti / tatra pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatānyekavacanodāhāreṇāpūrvacaritaṃ samuddiśanti sma, bodhisattvaścāsaṃmūḍho nikṣipati sma / evamaparyantāḥ sarvaśākyakumārāḥ, atha paryantaśca bodhisattvaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough, enough of this dispute! Now all of you together set problems for me — I shall calculate.' Then all five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths, with a single simultaneous utterance, set unprecedented problems, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> calculated without confusion. Thus all the <s>Śākya</s> youths were unlimited [in their problems], yet the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [remained] within bounds.

body.text: tato 'rjuno gaṇakamahāmātra āścaryaprāpta ime gāthe 'bhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s> the chief accountant, struck with wonder, uttered these verses:

children.text: jñānasya śīghratā sādhu buddhe saṃparipṛcchatā /
children.translated_text: 'The swiftness of knowledge — excellent! — [is seen] when [many] question the <s>Buddha</s> [simultaneously];

children.text: pañcamātraśatānyete dhiṣṭhitā gaṇanāpathe // Lal_12.21 //
children.translated_text: five hundred are stationed on the path of calculation — // Lal_12.21 //

children.text: īdṛśī ca iyaṃ prajñā buddhirjñānaṃ smṛtirmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: and such is this wisdom, intelligence, knowledge, mindfulness, and intellect —

children.text: adyāpi śikṣate cāyaṃ gaṇitaṃ jñānasāgaraḥ // Lal_12.22 //
children.translated_text: yet even today this ocean of knowledge still studies arithmetic!' // Lal_12.22 //

body.text: tataḥ sarvaśākyagaṇa āścaryaprāptaḥ paramavismayāpanno 'bhūt / ekakaṇṭhāścemāṃ vācamabhāṣanta - jayati jayati bhoḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāraḥ / sarve cāsanebhya utthāya kṛtāñjalipuṭā bhūtvā bodhisattvaṃ namaskṛtya rājānaṃ śuddhodanametadavocan - lābhāste mahārāja paramasulabdhāḥ, yasya te putra evaṃ śīghralaghujavacapalaparipṛcchāpratibhāna iti //
body.translated_text: Then the entire <s>Śākya</s> assembly, struck with wonder and overcome with supreme amazement, spoke with a single voice: 'Victorious! Victorious is Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>!' And all, rising from their seats, with palms joined, having bowed to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Great are your gains, O Great King, supremely well-gained — [you] whose son possesses such quick, light, swift, nimble [powers of] questioning and ready wit!'

body.text: atha sa rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvamevamāha - śakyasi putra arjunena gaṇakamahāmātreṇa sārdhaṃ saṃkhyājñānakauśalyagaṇanāgatimanupraveṣṭum? tena hi gaṇyatām / athārjuno gaṇakamahāmātro bodhisattvamevamāha - jānīṣe tvaṃ kumāra koṭiśatottarāṃ nāma gaṇanāgatim? bodhisattva āha - śakyāmi deva / āha - jānāmyaham / āha - kathaṃ punaḥ koṭiśatottarā gaṇanāgatiranupraveṣṭavyā? bodhisattva āha - śataṃ koṭīnāmayutaṃ nāmocyate / śatamayutānāṃ niyuto nāmocyate / śataṃ niyutānāṃ kaṅkaraṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ kaṅkarāṇāṃ vivaraṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ vivarāṇāmakṣobhyaṃ nāmocyate / śatamakṣobhyāṇāṃ vivāhaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ vivāhānāmutsaṅgaṃ nāmocyate / śatamutsaṅgānāṃ bahulaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ bahulānāṃ nāgabalaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ nāgabalānāṃ tiṭilambhaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ tiṭilambhānāṃ vyavasthānaprajñaptirnāmocyate / śataṃ vyavasthānaprajñaptīnāṃ hetuhilaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ hetuhilānāṃ karakurnāmocyate / śataṃ karakūṇāṃ hetvindriyaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ hetvindriyāṇāṃ samāptalambhaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ samāptalambhānāṃ gaṇanāgatirnāmocyate / śataṃ gaṇanāgatīnāṃ niravadyaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ niravadyānāṃ mudrābalaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ mudrābalānāṃ sarvabalaṃ nāmocyate / śataṃ sarvabalānāṃ visaṃjñāgatī nāmocyate / śataṃ visaṃjñāgatīnāṃ sarvasaṃjñā nāmocyate / śataṃ sarvasaṃjñānāṃ vibhūtaṃgamā nāmocyate / śataṃ vibhūtaṃgamānāṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ nāmocyate / iti hi tallakṣaṇagaṇanayā sumerūparvatarājo lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gacchet / ato 'pyuttari dhvajāgravatī nāma gaṇanā, yasyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ / ato 'pyuttari dhvajāgraniśāmaṇī nāma gaṇanā / ato 'pyuttari vāhanaprajñaptirnāma / ato 'pyuttari iṅgā nāma / ato 'pyuttari kuruṭu nāma / ato 'pyuttari kuruṭāvi nāma / ato 'pyuttari sarvanikṣepā nāma gaṇanā, yasyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ daśa gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepakriyayā parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ / ato 'pyuttari agrasārā nāma gaṇanā, yatra koṭīśataṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamā lakṣanikṣepāḥ parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuḥ / ato 'pyuttari paramāṇurajaḥpraveśānugatānāṃ gaṇanā, yatra tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ ca sarvaṃdharmābhiṣekābhimukhaṃ bodhisattvaṃ nānyaḥ kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate ya etāṃ gaṇanāṃ prajānāti anyatrāhaṃ vā yo vā syānmādṛśaḥ / evaṃ caramabhāviko viniṣkrāntagṛhavāso bodhisattvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Are you able, my son, to enter into the skill of mathematics and numerical progression with <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief minister of mathematics?' Then let him be tested.' Then <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief minister of mathematics, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Do you know, O prince, the numerical progression called 'beyond a hundred <s>koṭīs</s>'?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I am able, O lord.' [<s>Arjuna</s>] said: 'I know it.' He said: 'How then is the numerical progression beyond a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> to be entered?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'A hundred <s>koṭīs</s> is called an <s>ayuta</s>. A hundred <s>ayutas</s> is called a <s>niyuta</s>. A hundred <s>niyutas</s> is called a <s>kaṅkara</s>. A hundred <s>kaṅkaras</s> is called a <s>vivara</s>. A hundred <s>vivaras</s> is called an <s>akṣobhya</s>. A hundred <s>akṣobhyas</s> is called a <s>vivāha</s>. A hundred <s>vivāhas</s> is called an <s>utsaṅga</s>. A hundred <s>utsaṅgas</s> is called a <s>bahula</s>. A hundred <s>bahulas</s> is called a <s>nāgabala</s>. A hundred <s>nāgabalas</s> is called a <s>tiṭilambha</s>. A hundred <s>tiṭilambhas</s> is called a <s>vyavasthānaprajñapti</s>. A hundred <s>vyavasthānaprajñaptis</s> is called a <s>hetuhila</s>. A hundred <s>hetuhilas</s> is called a <s>karakū</s>. A hundred <s>karakūs</s> is called a <s>hetvindriya</s>. A hundred <s>hetvindriyas</s> is called a <s>samāptalambha</s>. A hundred <s>samāptalambhas</s> is called a <s>gaṇanāgati</s>. A hundred <s>gaṇanāgatis</s> is called a <s>niravadya</s>. A hundred <s>niravadyas</s> is called a <s>mudrābala</s>. A hundred <s>mudrābalas</s> is called a <s>sarvabala</s>. A hundred <s>sarvabalas</s> is called a <s>visaṃjñāgatī</s>. A hundred <s>visaṃjñāgatīs</s> is called a <s>sarvasaṃjñā</s>. A hundred <s>sarvasaṃjñās</s> is called a <s>vibhūtaṃgamā</s>. A hundred <s>vibhūtaṃgamās</s> is called a <s>tallakṣaṇa</s>. Now, by the <s>tallakṣaṇa</s> counting, <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, could be exhausted by the operation of placing [counting] marks. Beyond this there is a counting called <s>dhvajāgravatī</s>, by which [the number of] grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> could be exhausted by the operation of placing marks. Beyond this there is a counting called <s>dhvajāgraniśāmaṇī</s>. Beyond this, one called <s>vāhanaprajñapti</s>. Beyond this, one called <s>iṅgā</s>. Beyond this, one called <s>kuruṭu</s>. Beyond this, one called <s>kuruṭāvi</s>. Beyond this there is a counting called <s>sarvanikṣepā</s>, by which ten times the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> could be exhausted by the operation of placing marks. Beyond this there is a counting called <s>agrasārā</s>, by which a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> times the grains of sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> could be exhausted by the operation of placing marks. Beyond this there is the counting of the entry into the atoms of ultimate particles, where — setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has gone to the supreme seat of awakening and a <s>Bodhisattva</s> facing the consecration of all <s>dharmas</s> — no other being in the host of beings comprehends this counting, except myself or one who is like me. Such is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in his final birth who has gone forth from the household life.' //

body.text: arjuno 'vocat - kathaṃ kumāra paramāṇurajaḥpraveśagaṇanānupraveṣṭavyā? bodhisattva āha - sapta paramāṇurajāṃsyaṇuḥ / saptāṇavastrutiḥ / saptatruterekaṃ vātāyanarajaḥ / sapta vātāyanarajāṃsyekaṃ śaśarajaḥ / sapta śaśarajāṃsyekameḍakarajaḥ / saptaiḍakarajāṃsyekaṃ gorajaḥ / sapta gorajāṃsyekaṃ likṣārajaḥ / sapta likṣāḥ sarṣapaḥ / saptasarṣapādyavaḥ / saptayavādaṅgulīparva / dvādaśāṅgulīparvāṇi vitastiḥ / dve vitastī hastaḥ / catvāro hastā dhanuḥ / dhanuḥsahasraṃ mārgadhvajākrośaḥ / catvāraḥ krośā yojanam / tatra ko yuṣmākaṃ yojanapiṇḍaṃ prajānāti? kiyanti tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi bhavanti? arjuno 'vocat - ahameva tāvatkumāra saṃmohamāpannaḥ, kimaṅga punarye cānye 'lpabuddhayaḥ / nirdiśatu kumāro yojanapiṇḍaṃ kiyanti tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi bhavantīti / bodhisattvo 'vocat - tatra yojanapiṇḍaḥ paramāṇurajasāṃ paripūrṇamakṣobhyanayutamekaṃ triṃśacca koṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭiśca koṭīśatāni dvātriṃśatiśca koṭyaḥ pañca ca daśaśatasahasrāṇi dvādaśa ca sahasrāṇi etāvān yojanapiṇḍaḥ paramāṇurajonikṣepasya / anena praveśenāyaṃ jambudvīpaḥ saptayojanasahasrāṇi / godānīyo 'ṣṭau yojanasahasrāṇi / pūrvavideho nava yojanasahasrāṇi / uttarakurudvīpo daśayojanasahasrāṇi / anena praveśenemaṃ cāturdvīpakaṃ lokadhātūṃ pramukhaṃ kṛtvā paripūrṇakoṭīśataṃ cāturdvīpakānāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ yatra koṭīśataṃ mahāsamudrāṇām, koṭīśataṃ cakravālamahācakravālānām, koṭīśataṃ sumerūṇāṃ parvatarajānām, koṭīśataṃ caturmahārājikānāṃ devānām, koṭīśataṃ trayatriṃśānām, koṭīśataṃ yāmānām, koṭīśataṃ tuṣitānām, koṭīśataṃ nirmāṇaratīnām, koṭīśataṃ paranirmitavaśavartīnām, koṭīśataṃ brahmakāyikānām, koṭīśataṃ brahmapurohitānām, koṭīśataṃ brahmapārṣadyānām, koṭīśataṃ mahābrahmāṇām, koṭīśataṃ parīttābhānām, koṭīśataṃ apramāṇābhānām, koṭīśataṃ ābhāsvarāṇām, koṭīśataṃ parīttaśubhānām, koṭīśataṃ apramāṇaśubhānām, koṭīśataṃ śubhakṛtsnānām, koṭīśataṃ anabhrakāṇām, koṭīśataṃ puṇyaprasavānām, koṭīśataṃ bṛhatphalānām, kīṭīśataṃ asaṃjñisattvānām, koṭīśataṃ abṛhānām, koṭīśataṃ atapānām , koṭīśataṃ sudṛśānām, koṭīśataṃ sudarśanānām, koṭīśataṃ akaniṣṭhānāṃ devānām / ayamucyate trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturvipulaśca vistīrṇaśca / sa yāvanti yojanaśatāni (paramāṇurajāṃsi trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau) yāvanti yojanasahasrāṇi, yāvanti yojanakoṭayaḥ, yāvanti yojananayutāni ........peyālaṃ.............yāvadyāvanto yojanāgrasārā gaṇanāḥ / kiyantyetāni paramāṇurajāṃsi ityāha / saṃkhyāgaṇanā vyativṛttā hyeṣāṃ gaṇanānāṃ taducyate 'saṃkhyeyamiti / ato 'saṃkhyeyatamāni paramāṇurajāṃsi yāni trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau bhavanti //
body.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s> said: 'How is the counting of the entry into the atoms of ultimate particles to be entered?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Seven ultimate atoms make one atom (<s>aṇu</s>). Seven atoms make one mote (<s>truti</s>). Seven motes make one mote visible in a sunbeam. Seven sunbeam-motes make one hare-dust. Seven hare-dusts make one ram-dust. Seven ram-dusts make one cow-dust. Seven cow-dusts make one nit-dust (<s>likṣā</s>). Seven nits make one mustard seed. Seven mustard seeds make one barley grain. Seven barley grains make one finger-joint. Twelve finger-joints make one span. Two spans make one cubit. Four cubits make one bow-length. A thousand bow-lengths make one <s>krośa</s> (a quarter-league, the distance-marker of a road). Four <s>krośas</s> make one <s>yojana</s>. Now, who among you can calculate the total of a <s>yojana</s>? How many ultimate atoms does it contain?' <s>Arjuna</s> said: 'I myself, O prince, am utterly bewildered, to say nothing of others of lesser intellect. Let the prince declare the total of a <s>yojana</s> — how many ultimate atoms does it contain?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'The total of a <s>yojana</s> in ultimate atoms is one full <s>akṣobhya</s>-<s>nayuta</s>, plus thirty <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands, plus sixty <s>koṭī</s>-hundreds, plus thirty-two <s>koṭīs</s>, plus five times ten hundred-thousands, plus twelve thousand — such is the total of a <s>yojana</s> in the reckoning of ultimate atoms. By this calculation, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is seven thousand <s>yojanas</s>. <s>Godānīya</s> is eight thousand <s>yojanas</s>. <s>Pūrvavideha</s> is nine thousand <s>yojanas</s>. <s>Uttarakuru</s> is ten thousand <s>yojanas</s>. By this calculation, taking this four-continent world-system as the starting point, there is a full hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of four-continent world-systems, in which there are a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of great oceans, a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Cakravāla</s> and great <s>Cakravāla</s> [mountain ranges], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Meru</s>s, kings of mountains, a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heavens, a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Yāma</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tuṣita</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Brahmapurohita</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Mahābrahmā</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Parīttābha</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Apramāṇābha</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Ābhāsvara</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Parīttaśubha</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Anabhraka</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bṛhatphala</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Abṛha</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Atapa</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Sudṛśa</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Sudarśana</s> [heavens], a hundred <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens. This is called the trichiliocosm — vast and extensive. As many hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> [in ultimate atoms] as there are in the trichiliocosm, as many thousands of <s>yojanas</s>, as many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>yojanas</s>, as many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>yojanas</s> ......[abbreviation]...... as many <s>agrasārā</s> countings of <s>yojanas</s> — how many ultimate atoms are those?' He said: 'The numerical counting has been exceeded for these countings — that is called the incalculable (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>). Thus the ultimate atoms that exist in the trichiliocosm are of the most incalculable [number].' //

body.text: asmin khalu punargaṇanāparivarte bodhisattvena nirdiśyamāne arjuno gaṇakamahāmātraḥ sarvaśca śākyagaṇastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramudita āścaryādbhutaprāpto 'bhūt / te sarva ekaikairvastraiḥ sthitā abhūvan / pariśiṣṭairvastrābharaṇairbodhisattvamabhichādayanti sma //
body.translated_text: When this chapter on counting was being taught by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> the chief minister of mathematics, and the entire <s>Śākya</s> clan, were satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and struck with amazement. They all stood, each divested of a garment. With the remaining garments and ornaments they covered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [in tribute]. //

body.text: atha khalvarjuno gaṇakamahāmātra ime gāthe 'bhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Arjuna</s>, the chief minister of mathematics, spoke these verses:

children.text: koṭīśataṃ ca ayutā nayutāstathaiva niyutānu kaṅkaragatī tatha bimbarāśca /
children.translated_text: Hundred <s>koṭīs</s>, and <s>ayutas</s>, and <s>nayutas</s> likewise, <s>niyutas</s>, the progressions of <s>kaṅkara</s> and <s>bimbara</s>,

children.text: akṣobhiṇī paramajñānu na me 'styato 'rtha - mata uttare gaṇanamapratimasya jñānam // Lal_12.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>akṣobhiṇī</s> — supreme knowledge! I have no understanding beyond this; the knowledge of the incomparable one is beyond [my] comprehension! // Lal_12.23 //

body.text: api ca bhoḥ śākyāḥ -
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Śākyas</s>:

children.text: trisāhasri rajāśrayantakā tṛṇavana oṣadhiyo jalasya bindūn /
children.translated_text: The atoms in the trichiliocosm, the grasses, forests, herbs, and drops of water —

children.text: huṃkāreṇa nyaseya ekinaiṣo ko puni vismayu pañcabhiḥ śatebhiḥ // Lal_12.24 //
children.translated_text: he could reckon them all in a single breath! Who then would wonder at [merely] five hundred [opponents]? // Lal_12.24 //

body.text: tatra devamanujāḥ śatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā imā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of exclamations: 'Aha!' and 'Bravo!' and cries of acclaim. And the <s>Devaputras</s> in the sky spoke these verses:

children.text: yāvanta sattva nikhilena triyadhvayuktāḥ cittāni caitasikasaṃjñi vitarkitāni /
children.translated_text: However many beings there are throughout the entirety of the three times — their minds, mental factors, perceptions, and thoughts,

children.text: hīnāḥ praṇīta tatha saṃkṣipavikṣipā ye ekasmi cittaparivarti prajāni sarvān // Lal_12.25 //
children.translated_text: inferior and superior, contracted and expanded — he knows them all in a single turning of the mind! // Lal_12.25 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'bhibhūtāḥ sarve śākyakumārā abhūvan / bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate / tadanantaraṃ laṅghite plavite javite sarvatra bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, all the <s>Śākya</s> princes were surpassed. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone excelled. Thereafter, in leaping, jumping, and running, everywhere the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone excelled. And the <s>Devaputras</s> in the sky spoke this verse:

children.text: vratatapasaguṇena saṃyamena kṣamadamamaitrabalena kalpakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the power of vows, austerity, virtues, self-restraint, patience, self-control, friendliness, and strength over <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: atha kṛtulaghukāyacittanetā tasya javasya viśeṣatāṃ śṛṇotha // Lal_12.26 //
children.translated_text: having made his body and mind light, [he is] the guide — hear of the excellence of his speed! // Lal_12.26 //

children.text: iha gṛhagata yuṣme paśyathā sattvasāram api ca daśasu dikṣū gacchate 'yaṃ kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: Here, while you householders watch, behold the essence of beings! And in the ten directions he goes in an instant,

children.text: aparimitajinānāṃ pūjanāmeṣa kurvan maṇikanakavicitrairlokadhātuṣvanantā // Lal_12.27 //
children.translated_text: performing worship of limitless <s>Jinas</s>, in world-realms adorned with gems and gold, without end! // Lal_12.27 //

children.text: na ca puna gati āgatiṃ ca asyā yūyaṃ prajānatha tāvadṛddhiprāpto /
children.translated_text: And you cannot perceive his going or his coming — so great is his supernatural attainment!

children.text: ko 'tra javiti vismayo janeyā asadṛśa eṣa karotha gauravo 'smin // Lal_12.28 //
children.translated_text: Who would feel wonder at [mere] speed [when] this one is incomparable? Pay him reverence! // Lal_12.28 //

body.text: evaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> alone excelled in all. //

body.text: tatra śākyā āhuḥ - yuddheṣu tāvatkumāro viśeṣayitavyo jijñāsyaśca / tatra bodhisattva ekānte sthito 'bhūt / tāni ca pañcamātrāṇi śākyakumāraśatāni yugapadyudhyanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Śākyas</s> said: 'The prince should be tested and distinguished in combat as well.' There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stood apart. And those five hundred <s>Śākya</s> princes wrestled all at once. //

body.text: iti hi dvātriṃśacchākyakumārāḥ sālambhāya sthitāḥ / tadā nandaścānandaśca bodhisattvamabhigatau sālambhāya / tau samanantaraṃ spṛṣṭāveva bodhisattvena pāṇinā / tau bodhisattvasya balaṃ tejaścāsahamānau dharaṇītale prapatitāvabhūtām / tadanantaraṃ devadattaḥ kumāro garvitaśca mānī ca balavāneva tabdhaḥ śākyamānena ca tabdho bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ vispardhamānaḥ sarvāvantaṃ raṅgamaṇḍalaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vikrīḍamāno bodhisattvamabhipatati sma / atha bodhisattvo 'saṃbhrānta evātvaran dakṣiṇena pāṇinā salīlaṃ devadattaṃ kumāraṃ gṛhītvā trirgaganatale parivartya mānanigrahārthamavihiṃsābuddhyā maitreṇa cittena dharaṇītale nikṣipati sma / na cāsya kāyaṃ vyābādhate sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, thirty-two <s>Śākya</s> princes stood ready for wrestling. Then <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for wrestling. But the moment they were touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hand, unable to bear the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s strength and splendor, they fell to the ground. Then prince <s>Devadatta</s>, who was proud, arrogant, and indeed strong, puffed up and intoxicated with <s>Śākya</s> pride, competing against the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, circumambulated the entire wrestling arena, played [boastfully], and rushed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, unperturbed and unhurried, with his right hand playfully seized prince <s>Devadatta</s>, whirled him three times through the sky, and — for the purpose of subduing his pride, without any harmful intention, with a mind of friendliness — set him down on the ground. And he did not injure his body. //

body.text: tato bodhisattvo 'pyāha - alamalamanena vivādena / sarva eva ekībhūtvā idānīṃ sālambhāyāgacchateti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> also said: 'Enough, enough of this contention! Let all come together now as one for wrestling!' //

body.text: atha te sarve harṣitā bhūtvā bodhisattvamabhinipatitāḥ / te samanantaraspṛṣṭā bodhisattvena bodhisattvasya śriyaṃ tejaśca kāyabalaṃ sthāmaṃ cāsahamānāḥ spṛṣṭamātrā eva bodhisattvena dharaṇitale prāpatan / tatra marūnmanujaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilakilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇyakārṣuḥ / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā mahāntaṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravṛṣyaikasvareṇemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then all of them, delighted, rushed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. But the moment they were touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, unable to bear the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s glory, splendor, bodily strength, and might, they fell to the ground the instant they were touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of exclamations: 'Hee-hee!' and cries of acclaim. And the <s>Devaputras</s> in the sky, showering a great rain of flowers, spoke this verse in unison:

children.text: yāvanta sattvanayutā daśasū diśāsu te duṣṭamallamahanagnasamā bhaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: However many <s>nayutas</s> of beings there are in the ten directions — even if they were all like fierce wrestlers, great and naked —

children.text: ekakṣaṇena nipateyu nararṣabhasya saṃspṛṣṭamātra nipateyu kṣitītalesmiṃ // Lal_12.29 //
children.translated_text: in a single instant they would fall before this bull among men — they would fall to the surface of the earth at the mere touch [of his hand]! // Lal_12.29 //

children.text: merūḥ sumeru tatha vajrakacakravālāḥ ye cānya parvata kvaciddaśasū diśāsu /
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, likewise the <s>Vajra</s> and <s>Cakravāla</s> [mountains], and whatever other mountains there are in the ten directions —

children.text: pāṇibhya gṛhya masicūrṇanibhāṃ prakuryāt ko vismayo manujaāśrayake asāre // Lal_12.30 //
children.translated_text: with his hands seizing [a man's body] he could reduce it to powder like crushed ink — what wonder concerning this human form, which is without essence? // Lal_12.30 //

children.text: eṣo drumendrapravare mahaduṣṭamallaṃ māraṃ sasainyasabalaṃ sahayaṃ dhvajāgre /
children.translated_text: This one, at the foot of the best of great trees, shall vanquish <s>Māra</s>, the most wicked wrestler, together with his army, forces, and banner-top,

children.text: maitrībalena vinihatya hi kṛṣṇabandhuṃ yāvat spṛśiṣyati anuttarabodhi sāntam // Lal_12.31 //
children.translated_text: having defeated the kinsman of darkness by the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), he shall touch the supreme, peaceful <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)! // Lal_12.31 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: evaṃ kṛtvā bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma //
body.translated_text: Having done all this, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself excelled. //

body.text: atha daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyakumārānetadavocat - jijñāsitamidaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca / hantedānīmiṣukṣepamupadarśayateti / tatra ānandasya dvayoḥ krośayorayasmayī bherī lakṣaṃ sthāpitābhūt / asyānantaraṃ devadattasya caturṣu krośeṣvayasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt / daṇḍapāṇeryojanadvaye 'yasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s> prince said to the <s>Śākya</s> youths: 'This trial is seen and done. Come now, let us demonstrate arrow-shooting!' Thereupon, for <s>Ānanda</s>, an iron drum was set up as a target at a distance of two <s>krośas</s>. Next, for <s>Devadatta</s>, an iron drum was set up at four <s>krośas</s>. For <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, an iron drum was set up at a distance of two <s>yojanas</s>.

body.text: bodhisattvasya daśasu krośeṣvayasmayī bherī sthāpitābhūt / tasyānantaraṃ sapta tālā ayasmayī varāhapratimā yantrayuktā sthāpitābhūt / tatrānandena dvābhyāṃ krośābhyāṃ bheryāhatābhūt, tatottari na śaknoti sma / devadattena catuḥkrośasthā bheryāhatābhūt, nottari śaknoti sma / sundaranandena ṣaṭkrośasthā bheryāhatābhūt, nottari śaknoti sma / daṇḍapāṇinā dviyojanasthā bheryāhatābhūt, nirviddhā ca nottari śaknoti sma / tatra bodhisattvasya yadyadeva dhanurupānamyate sma, tattadeva vicchidyate sma / tato bodhisattva āha - astīha deva nagare kiṃcidanyaddhanuryanmamāropaṇaṃ saheta kāyabalasthāmaṃ ca? rājā āha - asti putra / kumāra āha - kva taddeva? rājā āha - tava putra pitāmahaḥ siṃhahanurnāmābhūt, tasya yaddhanustadeva tarhi devakule gandhamālyairmahīyate / na punastatkaścicchaknoti sma taddhanurāropayituṃ prāgeva pūrayitum / bodhisattva āha - ānīyatāṃ deva taddhanuḥ / jijñāsiṣyāmahe //
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, an iron drum was set up at ten <s>krośas</s>. Beyond that, seven palm trees, an iron boar-figure fitted with mechanisms, were set up. There <s>Ānanda</s> struck the drum at two <s>krośas</s>, but could not [strike] beyond that. <s>Devadatta</s> struck the drum stationed at four <s>krośas</s>, but could not [strike] beyond. <s>Sundarananda</s> struck the drum stationed at six <s>krośas</s>, but could not [strike] beyond. <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> struck the drum stationed at two <s>yojanas</s> and pierced it, but could not [strike] beyond. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whatever bow was offered to him, each one broke. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Is there, O lord, any other bow in the city that could withstand my stringing and bodily strength?' The king replied: 'There is, my son.' The prince said: 'Where is it, O lord?' The king said: 'Your grandfather, my son, was named <s>Siṃhahanu</s>. His bow — that same one is now worshipped with perfume and garlands in the god's temple. But no one can string that bow, let alone draw it.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Let that bow be brought, O lord. We shall test it.' //

body.text: tāvadyāvattaddhanurupanāmitamabhūt / tatra sarve śākyakumārāḥ parameṇāpi prayatnena vyāyacchamānā na śaknuvanti sma taddhanurāropayituṃ prāgeva pūravitum / tatastaddhanurdaṇḍapāṇeḥ śākyasyopanāmitamabhūt / atha daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyaḥ sarvaṃ kāyabalasthāma saṃjanayya taddhanurāropayitumārabdho 'bhūt / na ca śaknoti sma / yāvadbodhisattvasyopanāmitamabhūt / tadbodhisattvo gṛhītvā āsanādanuttiṣṭhannevārdhaparyaṅkaṃ kṛtvā vāmena pāṇinā(gṛhītvā) dakṣiṇena pāṇinā ekāṅgulyagreṇāropitavānabhūt / tasya dhanuṣa āropyamāṇasya sarvaṃ kapilavastu mahānagaraṃ śabdenābhivijñaptamabhūt / sarvanagarajanaśca vihvalībhūto 'nyonyamapṛcchat - kasyāyamevaṃvidhaḥ śabda iti / anye tadavocan - siddhārthena kila kumāreṇa paitāmahadhanurāropitam, tasyāyaṃ śabda iti / tatra devamanujaśatasahasrāṇi hāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then that bow was presented. There all the <s>Śākya</s> youths, though straining with the utmost effort, could not string that bow, let alone draw it. Then that bow was presented to <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>. Then <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, summoning all his bodily strength and power, began to string that bow. But he could not. Then it was presented to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking it, without even rising from his seat, sitting in half cross-legged posture, with his left hand [holding it] and with the tip of a single finger of his right hand, strung it. When that bow was strung, the entire great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was made aware by its sound. And all the city's people, bewildered, asked one another: 'What is this kind of sound?' Others said: 'It is said that the prince <s>Siddhārtha</s> has strung the ancestral bow — this is its sound.' Then hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of exclamations and cries of wonder. And the <s>devaputras</s> stationed in the sky addressed King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great assembly in verse —

children.text: yatha pūrita eṣa dhanurmuninā na ca utthitu āsani no ca bhūmī /
children.translated_text: Just as this bow has been drawn by the Sage, and he has not risen from his seat nor from the ground,

children.text: niḥsaṃśayu pūrṇamabhiprāyu munirlaghu bheṣyati jitva ca māracamūm // Lal_12.32 //
children.translated_text: without doubt, the Sage shall fulfill his purpose and swiftly conquer the army of <s>Māra</s>! // Lal_12.32 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvastaddhanuḥ pūrayitveṣuṃ gṛhītvā tādṛśena balasthāmnā tamiṣuṃ kṣipati sma, yena yā cānandasya bherī yā ca devadattasya yāvatsunddaranandasya yāvaddaṇḍapāṇetāḥ sarvā abhinirbhidya tāṃ ca daśakrośasthāṃ svakāmayasmayīṃ bherīṃ saptatālāṃ yantrayuktavarāhapratimāmabhinirbhidya sa iṣurdharaṇītalaṃ praviśya adarśanābhāso 'bhūt / yatra ca pradeśe sa iṣurbhūmitalaṃ bhittvā praviṣṭastasmin pradeśe kūpaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, yadadyatve 'pi śarakūpa ityabhidhīyate / tatra devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi hīhīkārakilikilāprakṣveḍitaśatasahasrāṇi prāmuñcan / sarvaśca śākyagaṇo vismito 'bhūt āścaryaprāptaḥ -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having drawn that bow and taken an arrow, shot that arrow with such strength and power that it pierced through <s>Ānanda</s>'s drum, and <s>Devadatta</s>'s, and up to <s>Sundarananda</s>'s, and up to <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>'s — piercing through all of them, and [also] his own iron drum stationed at ten <s>krośas</s>, and the seven palm trees, and the mechanically-fitted boar-figure — and that arrow entered the earth and disappeared from sight. And at the spot where that arrow, having split the earth's surface, entered — at that spot a well formed, which even today is called 'The Arrow-Well' (<s>Śarakūpa</s>). Then hundreds of thousands of gods and humans let forth hundreds of thousands of cries of astonishment and wonder. And the entire <s>Śākya</s> clan was amazed and filled with wonder:

body.text: āścaryaṃ bhoḥ / na ca nāma anena yogyā kṛtā, idaṃ cedṛśaṃ śilpakauśalam / gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ taṃ ca mahāntaṃ janakāyamevamāhuḥ - ko 'tra vismayo manujāḥ / tatkasmāt?
body.translated_text: 'How marvelous! He has not even practiced, and yet such is his skill in craftsmanship!' And the <s>devaputras</s> stationed in the sky said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and that great assembly: 'What wonder is there in this, O mortals? Why?'

body.text: eṣa dharaṇimaṇḍe purvabuddhāsanasthaḥ śamathadhanu gṛhītvā śūnyanairātmabāṇaiḥ / kleśaripu nihatvā dṛṣṭijālaṃ ca bhittvā śivavirajamaśokāṃ prāpsyate bodhimagryām // Lal_12.33 //
body.translated_text: This one, seated upon the seat of the former Buddhas on the surface of the earth, taking up the bow of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), with arrows of emptiness and non-self,

body.text: evamuktvā te devaputrā bodhisattvaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpairabhyavakīrya prākrāman //
body.translated_text: having slain the enemy of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and pierced through the net of [wrong] views, shall attain the supreme, auspicious, stainless, and sorrowless <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)! // Lal_12.33 //

body.text: evaṃ laṅghite prāgvallipimudrāgaṇanāsaṃkhyasālambhadhanurvede javite plavite taraṇe iṣvastre hastigrīvāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe dhanuṣkalāpe sthairyasthāmni suśaurye bāhuvyāyāme aṅkuśagrahe pāśagrahe udyāne niryāṇe avayāne muṣṭibandhe padabandhe śikhābandhe chedye bhedye dālane sphālane akṣuṇṇavedhitve marmavedhitve śabdavedhitve dṛḍhaprahāritve akṣakrīḍāyāṃ kāvyakaraṇe granthe citre rūpe rūpakarmaṇi dhīte agnikarmaṇi vīṇāyāṃ vādye nṛtye gīte paṭhite ākhyāne hāsye lāsye nāṭye viḍambite mālyagrathane saṃvāhite maṇirāge vastrarāge māyākṛte svapnādhyāye śakunirute strīlakṣaṇe puruṣalakṣaṇe aśvalakṣaṇe hastilakṣaṇe golakṣaṇe ajalakṣaṇe miśralakṣaṇe kauṭubheśvaralakṣaṇe nirghaṇṭe nigame purāṇe itihāse vede vyākaraṇe nirukte śikṣāyāṃ chandasvinyāṃ yajñakalpe jyotiṣe sāṃkhye yoge kriyākalpe vaiśike vaiśeṣike arthavidyāyāṃ bārhaspatye āmbhirye āsurye mṛgapakṣirute hetuvidyāyāṃ jalayantre madhūcchiṣṭakṛte sūcikarmaṇi vidalakarmaṇi patrachede gandhayuktau - ityevamādyāsu sarvakarmakalāsu laukikādiṣu divyamānuṣyakātikrāntāsu sarvatra bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma //
