body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, those <s>devaputras</s>, having showered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with divine flowers, departed. // Thus, in leaping, and previously in writing, seal-making, arithmetic, computation, financial assessment, archery, swiftness, swimming, crossing, arrow-craft, [riding on] elephant-neck, horse-back, chariot, bow-case, steadiness and power, valiant courage, arm-exercise, goad-wielding, lasso-wielding, going forth, returning, retreat, fist-binding, foot-binding, topknot-binding, cutting, splitting, crushing, striking, unfailing targeting, vital-point targeting, sound targeting, powerful striking, dice-play, poetry composition, book-craft, painting, sculpture, metal-casting, knowledge, fire-craft, the <s>vīṇā</s>, instrumental music, dance, song, recitation, narration, humor, pantomime, drama, mimicry, garland-weaving, massage, gem-dyeing, cloth-dyeing, illusion-craft, dream-interpretation, bird-augury, the science of women's marks, men's marks, horse-marks, elephant-marks, cattle-marks, goat-marks, mixed marks, marks of household lords, lexicography, traditional collections (<s>nigama</s>), <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Vedas</s>, grammar, etymology, phonetics, prosody, ritual procedure, astronomy, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, practical procedure, <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>, dialectics, political science, <s>Bārhaspatya</s> [logic], <s>Āmbhīra</s> [doctrine], <s>Āsura</s> [doctrine], the cries of animals and birds, the science of reasoning, water-machinery, wax-work, needle-craft, leaf-work, leaf-cutting, perfumery — in all these and other arts and crafts, worldly and beyond, surpassing both divine and human [achievements], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself excelled in every one. //

body.text: atha khalu punastena samayena daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyaḥ svāṃ duhitaraṃ gopāṃ śākyakanyāṃ bodhisattvāya prādāt / sā ca rājñā śuddhodanenānupūrveṇa bodhisattvasya vṛtābhūt //
body.translated_text: Then at that time <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s> gave his own daughter <s>Gopā</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> maiden, to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And she was, in due order, chosen by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> as [bride] for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tatra khalvapi bodhisattvaścaturaśītistrīsahasrāṇāṃ madhye prāpto lokānubhavanatayā ramamāṇaṃ krīḍayantaṃ paricārayantamātmānamupadarśayati sma / tāsāṃ caturaśīte strīsahasrāṇāṃ gopā śākyakanyā sarvāsāmagramahiṣyabhiṣiktābhūt //
body.translated_text: There, indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in the midst of eighty-four thousand women, in conformity with worldly experience, displayed himself as one who delighted, played, and enjoyed [their company]. Of those eighty-four thousand women, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden was anointed as the chief queen of them all. //

body.text: tatra khalvapi gopā śākyakanyā na kaṃcid dṛṣṭvā vadanaṃ chādayati sma śvaśrūṃ vā śvaśuraṃ vāntarjanaṃ vā / te tāmupadhyāyanti sma, vicārayanti sma - navavadhūkā hi nāma pratilīnā tiṣṭhati, iyaṃ punarvivṛtaiva sarvadā iti / tato gopā śākyakanyā etāṃ prakṛtiṃ śrutvā sarvasyāntarjanasya purataḥ sthitvā imā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: There, indeed, <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden did not cover her face upon seeing anyone — whether mother-in-law, father-in-law, or inner household attendants. They suspected and discussed her: 'A new bride is supposed to remain concealed, but this one is always uncovered!' Then <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, having heard this opinion, stood before all the inner household and spoke these verses —

children.text: vivṛtaḥ śobhate ārya āsanasthānacaṃkrame /
children.translated_text: The noble one shines when uncovered — whether seated, standing, or walking about —

children.text: maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre vā bhāsamānaṃ prabhāsvaram // Lal_12.34 //
children.translated_text: like a jewel-gem atop a banner, brilliant and radiant! // Lal_12.34 //

children.text: gacchan vai śobhate ārya āgacchannapi śobhate /
children.translated_text: The noble one shines when going, and shines when coming too;

children.text: sthito vātha niṣaṇṇo vā āryaḥ sarvatra śobhate // Lal_12.35 //
children.translated_text: whether standing or seated, the noble one shines everywhere! // Lal_12.35 //

children.text: kathayaṃ śobhate āryastūṣṇībhūto 'pi śobhate /
children.translated_text: The noble one shines when speaking, and shines too when silent,

children.text: kalaviṅko yathā pakṣī darśanena svareṇa vā // Lal_12.36 //
children.translated_text: like the <s>Kalaviṅka</s> bird, [beautiful] whether by sight or by song! // Lal_12.36 //

children.text: kuśacīranivasto vā mandacailaḥ kṛśaṃtanuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even clad in <s>kuśa</s>-grass and bark, with poor garments and an emaciated body,

children.text: śobhate 'sau svatejena guṇavān guṇabhūṣitaḥ // Lal_12.37 //
children.translated_text: such a one shines by his own radiance — the virtuous one is adorned by [his] virtues! // Lal_12.37 //

children.text: sarveṇa śobhate āryo yasya pāpaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: The noble one shines in every way, in whom there is no evil;

children.text: kiyadvibhūṣito bālaḥ pāpacārī na śobhate // Lal_12.38 //
children.translated_text: however much adorned, the fool of evil conduct does not shine! // Lal_12.38 //

children.text: ye kilbiṣāḥ svahṛdaye madhurāsu vācaṃ kumbho viṣasmi pariṣiktu yathāmṛtena /
children.translated_text: Those who harbor sins in their hearts yet [speak] sweet words — like a pot of poison sprinkled with nectar,

children.text: dusparśa śailaśilavat kaṭhināntarātmā sarpasya vā virasu darśana tādṛśānām // Lal_12.39 //
children.translated_text: hard to touch like a rocky cliff, harsh within — the sight of such ones is as loathsome as [that of] a serpent! // Lal_12.39 //

children.text: sarveṣu te namiṣu sarvamupaiti saumyāḥ sarveṣu tirthamiva sarvagopajīvyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those gentle ones [who are virtuous] approach everyone in all forms, accessible to all like a holy ford, a livelihood for all;

children.text: dadhikṣīrapūrṇaghaṭatulya sadaiva āryā śuddhātmadarśanu sumaṅgalu tādṛśānām // Lal_12.40 //
children.translated_text: always like vessels filled with curd and milk — the sight of such noble ones is pure-souled and most auspicious! // Lal_12.40 //

children.text: yaiḥ pāpamitra parivarjita dīrgharātraṃ kalyāṇamitraratanaiśca parigṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have for a long time shunned evil friends and been embraced by the jewel of virtuous friends,

children.text: pāpaṃ vivarjayi niveśayi buddhadharme saphalaṃ sumaṅgalu sudarśanu tādṛśānām // Lal_12.41 //
children.translated_text: who have abandoned evil and established [beings] in the <s>Buddhadharma</s> — the sight of such ones is fruitful and most auspicious! // Lal_12.41 //

children.text: ye kāyasaṃvṛta susaṃvṛtakāyadoṣāḥ ye vācasaṃvṛta sadānavakīrṇavācaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are restrained in body, with bodily faults well-guarded, who are restrained in speech, with words never scattered,

children.text: guptendriyā sunibhṛtāśca manaḥprasannāḥ kiṃ tādṛśāna vadanaṃ pratichādayitvā // Lal_12.42 //
children.translated_text: with senses guarded, composed, and with minds serene — why should such ones cover their faces? // Lal_12.42 //

children.text: vastrā sahasra yadi chādayi ātmabhāvaṃ cittaṃ ca yeṣu vivṛtaṃ na hirī na lajjā /
children.translated_text: Though one may cover one's body with a thousand garments, if the mind is exposed, without shame, without modesty,

children.text: na ca yeṣu īdṛśa guṇā napi satyavākyaṃ nagne vinagnatara te vicaranti loke // Lal_12.43 //
children.translated_text: and if in such ones there are no such virtues, nor truthful speech — they walk about in the world more naked than the naked! // Lal_12.43 //

children.text: yāścittagupta satatendriyasaṃyatāśca na ca anyasattvamanasā svapatīna tuṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those women who are guarded in mind, with senses always restrained, content with their own husbands, not [turning to] the thoughts of other beings,

children.text: ādityacandrasadṛśā vivṛtaprakāśā kiṃ tādṛśāna vadanaṃ pratichādayitvā // Lal_12.44 //
children.translated_text: radiant like the sun and moon, openly luminous — why should such ones cover their faces? // Lal_12.44 //

body.text: api ca -
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: jānanti āśayu mama ṛṣayo mahātmā paracittabuddhikuśalāstatha devasaṃghāḥ /
children.translated_text: The great-souled sages know my disposition, as do the assemblies of gods, skilled in discerning others' minds;

children.text: yatha mahya śīlaguṇasaṃvaru apramādo vadanāvaguṇṭhanamataḥ prakaromi kiṃ me // Lal_12.45 //
children.translated_text: since [they know] my morality, virtue, restraint, and diligence — what purpose then is there for me to veil my face? // Lal_12.45 //

body.text: aśroṣīdbhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano nāma gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyā imāmevaṃrūpāṃ sarvāṃ gāthāṃ pratibhānanirdeśam / śrutvā ca punastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'nekaratnapratyuptena dūṣyayugena koṭīśatasahasramūlyena ca muktāhāreṇābhijātalohitamuktāpratyuptayā ca suvarṇamālayā gopāṃ śākyakanyāmabhicchādyainamudānamudānayati sma -
body.translated_text: O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard all these verses, the inspired discourse of <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden. Having heard, he was satisfied, elated, pleased, delighted, and filled with joy and gladness. He covered <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden with a cloth set with manifold jewels and a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s>, and with a golden garland inlaid with fine rubies and pearls, and uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>) —

children.text: yathā ca putro mama bhūṣito guṇaiḥ tathā ca kanyā svaguṇā prabhāsate /
children.translated_text: Just as my son is adorned with virtues, so too this maiden shines with her own virtues;

children.text: viśuddhasattvau tadubhau samāgatau sameti sarpiryatha sarpimaṇḍe // Lal_12.46 //
children.translated_text: these two beings of pure nature have come together — like clarified butter meeting cream! // Lal_12.46 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: (anupūrveṇa yathāpūrvavadbodhisattvapramukhāḥ svapuraṃ prakrāmanta ) //
body.translated_text: (In due order, as before, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and the others departed to their own city.) //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare śilpasaṃdarśanaparivarto nāma dvādaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the twelfth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Display of Skills' (<s>Śilpasaṃdarśanaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 13
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 13.

body.text: saṃcodanāparivartastrayodaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Thirteenth Chapter: On Exhortation (<s>Saṃcodanāparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣava ātmarutaharṣamudīrayanta āgatā āsan bodhisattvasyāntaḥpuramadhyagatasya anekairdevairnāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālāḥ, ye bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe autsukyamāpatsyante sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, uttering sounds of self-arisen joy, there came — while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was dwelling in the inner palace — many gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians, who were eager for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo apareṇa samayena saṃbahulānāṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālānāmetadabhavat - aticiraṃ batāyaṃ satpuruṣo 'ntaḥpure vilambitaḥ / ye cāsyeme dīrgharātraṃ paripācitāḥ sattvāścaturbhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhirdānena priyavākyenārthakriyayā samānārthatayā, yasya bodhiprāptasya dharmadeśitamājñāsyanti, tatsahaiva ca tāni dharmabhājanāni sarvāṇyantarhitāni bhaviṣyanti / bodhisattvaśca paścādabhiniṣkramyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate //
body.translated_text: There, O monks, at a later time, this thought arose in many gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians: 'Too long indeed has this true person lingered in the inner palace! And those beings whom he has ripened over a long time by the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) — by giving, kind speech, helpful conduct, and impartiality — who, upon his attaining awakening, will understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught, together with those very vessels of the <s>Dharma</s>, all will have disappeared. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going forth only later, will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.' //

body.text: tataste sagauravāḥ sapratīkṣāḥ prāñjalībhūtā bodhisattvaṃ namasyanti sma / evamabhiprāyāścodīkṣamāṇāḥ sthitā abhūvan - kadā ca nāma tadbhaviṣyati yadvayaṃ varapravaraṃ śuddhasattvamabhiniṣkrāmantaṃ paśyema, abhiniṣkramya ca tasmin mahādrumarājamūle 'bhiniṣadya sabalaṃ māraṃ dharṣayitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaṃ daśabhistathāgatabalaiḥ samanvāgataṃ caturbhiśca tathāgatavaiśāradyaiḥ samanvāgatamaṣṭādaśabhiścāveṇikairbuddhadharmaiḥ samanvāgataṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāramanuttaraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayantaṃ mahatā buddhavikrīḍitena sadevamānuṣāsuralokaṃ yathādhimuktyā subhāṣitena saṃtoṣayantamiti //
body.translated_text: Then they, with reverence and expectation, with palms joined, paid homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And they stood looking on with this aspiration: 'When will that time come when we shall see the supreme, the foremost, the pure being going forth, and having gone forth, seated at the foot of that great king of trees, having vanquished <s>Māra</s> together with his army, fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, endowed with the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>Tathāgatabala</s>), endowed with the four fearlessnesses of a <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>Tathāgatavaiśāradya</s>), endowed with the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>), turning the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of three turnings and twelve aspects, satisfying the world with its gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s> with the great display of a <s>Buddha</s>'s sport, with well-spoken [words] according to each one's disposition!' //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvo dīrgharātramasaṃkhyeyān kalpānupādāya satataṃ samitamaparapraṇeyo 'bhūt / sarvalaukikalokottareṣu dharmeṣu svayamevācāryaḥ sarvakuśalamūladharmacaryāsu dīrghakālaṃ ca kālajño velājñaḥ samayajño 'bhūdacyuto 'bhijñaḥ pañcābhijñābhiḥ samanvāgato 'bhūt / ṛddhipādavikrīḍataḥ sarvendriyakuśalaḥ kālākālajñaḥ kālaveṣī mahāsāgara iva prāptāṃ velāṃ nātikrāmati sma / so 'bhijñajñānabalena samanvāgataḥ svayameva sarvaṃ jānāti sma / asyāyaṃ kālaḥ pragrahasya, ayaṃ kālo nigrahasya, ayaṃ kālaḥ saṃgrahasya, ayaṃ kālo 'nugrahasya, ayaṃ kāla upekṣāyāḥ, ayaṃ kālo bhāṣitasya, ayaṃ kālastūṣṇīṃbhāvasya, ayaṃ kālo niṣkramyasya, ayaṃ kālaḥ pravrajyāyāḥ, ayaṃ kālaḥ svādhyāyasya, ayaṃ kālo yoniśomanaskārasya, ayaṃ kālaḥ pravivekasya, ayaṃ kālaḥ kṣatriyaparṣadamupasaṃkramituṃ.............peyālaṃ...............yāvadayaṃ kālo brāhmaṇagṛhapatiparṣadamupasaṃkramitum, ayaṃ kālo devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālabhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāparṣadamupasaṃkramitum, ayaṃ kālo dharmadeśanāyāḥ, ayaṃ kālaḥ pratisaṃlayanasya / sarvatra bodhisattvo nityakālaṃ kālajño bhavati sma kālaveṣī //
body.translated_text: Now, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from the long night of innumerable <s>kalpas</s> onward, had always been continuously self-guided. In all worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s> he himself was the teacher. In all practices of wholesome roots, for a long time he had been a knower of the right time, a knower of the right occasion, a knower of the right moment — unerring, endowed with the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). Playing with the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), skilled in all faculties, a knower of the right and wrong time, a seeker of the right time — like the great ocean, he did not transgress the appropriate limit. Endowed with the power of superknowledge, he himself knew everything: 'This is the time for encouragement; this is the time for restraint; this is the time for gathering; this is the time for assistance; this is the time for equanimity; this is the time for speech; this is the time for silence; this is the time for going forth; this is the time for ordination; this is the time for study; this is the time for careful attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>); this is the time for solitude; this is the time to approach the assembly of <s>kṣatriyas</s>... [abbreviated]... up to: this is the time to approach the assembly of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders; this is the time to approach the assembly of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, world-guardians, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; this is the time for teaching the <s>Dharma</s>; this is the time for meditative retreat.' Everywhere, at all times, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was a knower of the right time, a seeker of the right time. //

body.text: atha ca punarbhikṣavo dharmatāpratilambha eṣa ca caramabhāvikānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yadavaśyaṃ daśadiglokadhātusthitairbuddhairbhagavadbhirantaḥpuramadhyagatāḥ saṃgītitūryanirnāditairebhirevaṃrūpairdharmamukhaiḥ saṃcoditavyā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O monks, this is the natural attainment (<s>dharmatāpratilambha</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their final existence: they must necessarily be urged by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> abiding in the world-systems of the ten directions — while dwelling in the inner palace, amidst music and song — through <s>Dharma</s>-gateways of just this kind. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Hereupon this was said —

children.text: ye sattvāgrā daśadigloke teṣu viśeṣāttatra ratituriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are supreme among beings in the worlds of the ten directions — especially there, with delightful instruments,

children.text: gāthā gītā ima ratimadhurā saṃcodentī naravarapravaram // Lal_13.1 //
children.translated_text: these sweet, delightful verses are sung, urging the foremost among men, the supreme one. // Lal_13.1 //

children.text: pūrvi tubhyaṃ ayu kṛtu praṇidhī dṛṣṭvā sattvān duḥkhaśatabharitān /
children.translated_text: Formerly you made a vow, having seen beings burdened with hundreds of sufferings:

children.text: lenaṃ trāṇaṃ jaganijaśaraṇe bheṣye nāthu hitakaru paramaḥ // Lal_13.2 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall be a shelter, a refuge, a protector for the world, a healer, a leader, the supreme benefactor.' // Lal_13.2 //

children.text: sādho vīrā smara cari purimāṃ yā te āsījjagahitapraṇidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: O virtuous hero, remember your former conduct — your vow for the welfare of the world!

children.text: kālo velā ayu tava samayo niṣkramyāhī ṛṣivarapravarā // Lal_13.3 //
children.translated_text: The time has come, the occasion, your moment — go forth, O foremost among supreme sages! // Lal_13.3 //

children.text: yasyārthe te dhanavara vividhā tyaktā pūrve śirakaracaraṇā /
children.translated_text: For whose sake you formerly gave away various treasures, heads, hands, and feet —

children.text: bheṣye buddho naramarudamako lokasyāgro guṇaśatanicitaḥ // Lal_13.4 //
children.translated_text: [now] be a <s>Buddha</s>, tamer of men and gods, supreme in the world, endowed with hundreds of virtues! // Lal_13.4 //

children.text: tvaṃ śīlena vratatapacaritaḥ tvaṃ kṣāntīye jagahitakaraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: You [practiced] morality, vows, austerities, and conduct; you [practiced] patience for the welfare of the world;

children.text: tvaṃ vīryeṇā śubhaguṇanicito dhyāne prajñe na tu samu tribhave // Lal_13.5 //
children.translated_text: you [are endowed] with vigor, accumulated in wholesome virtues, in <s>dhyāna</s> and wisdom — none in the three realms is your equal! // Lal_13.5 //

children.text: krodhāviṣṭā khilamalabahulā te maitrīye tvayi sphuṭa sugatā /
children.translated_text: Those seized by anger, full of defilement and impurity — your loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward them is manifest and well-gone;

children.text: kāruṇyaṃ te bahuvidhamabudhe mithyātveṣū śubhaguṇarahite // Lal_13.6 //
children.translated_text: your compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) is manifold for those who are foolish, [dwelling] in wrong views, devoid of wholesome virtues. // Lal_13.6 //

children.text: puṇyajñāne śubhānicitātmā dhyānābhijño pratapasi virajo /
children.translated_text: With a self accumulated in merit and knowledge, endowed with <s>dhyāna</s> and superknowledge, blazing, free from dust,

children.text: obhāsesī daśa ima diśato meghā muktaḥ śaśiriva vimalaḥ // Lal_13.7 //
children.translated_text: you illuminate these ten directions — like the moon freed from clouds, stainless! // Lal_13.7 //

children.text: ete cānye bahuvidha rucirā tūryairghoṣāṃ jinarutaravanā /
children.translated_text: These and other manifold, delightful sounds — with instruments, producing the sounds of a <s>Jina</s>'s speech —

children.text: ye codentī suranaramahitaṃ niṣkramyāhī ayu tava samayu // Lal_13.8 //
children.translated_text: urge [him]: 'Go forth! The time has come, your moment!' // Lal_13.8 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarbhikṣavastasmin gṛhavarapradhāne sarvopakaraṇasamṛddhisamudite yathābhiprāyasukhavihārānukūle amarapurabhavanaprakāśe vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādavarapravare sarvaratnavicitrālaṃkāravividhabhaktisuvibhakte ucchritachatradhvajapatākānekaratnakiṅkiṇījālasamalaṃkṛte anekapaṭṭhadāmaśatasahasrābhipralambite nānāratnapratyupte muktāhārābhipralambite vicitrapaṭṭaratnasaṃkramopaśobhite avasaktapaṭṭamālyadāmakalāpe gandhaghaṭikānirdhūpite avaśyāyapaṭavitatavitānesarvartukapuṣpaparamasugandhisurucirābhiprakīrṇapuṣkariṇīpuṇḍarīkanavanalinījāla - saṃsthānaparibhogabahule patraguptaśukasārikakokilahaṃsamayūracakravākakunālakalaviṅkajīvajīvakādinānāvidhadvijagaṇamadhura svaranikūjitenīlavaiḍūryamaye dharaṇītalasaṃsthānaparibhoge sarvarūpapratibhāsasaṃdarśane atṛptanayanābhiramye
body.translated_text: Now, O monks, in that foremost and chief dwelling of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — rich with every furnishing and comfort, conducive to dwelling in happiness as he wished, resplendent like the palace of the immortals, with terraces, projecting balconies, arched gateways, lattice-windows, pinnacled mansions, upper chambers, and supreme palatial towers, variegated with ornaments of all manner of jewels, artfully arranged, raised with parasols, banners, flags, and nets of many jewel-bells adorning it, festooned with hundreds of thousands of silk-garland chains, inlaid with various jewels, hung with strings of pearls, adorned with walkways of variegated silk and gems, draped with festoons of silk garlands, perfumed with incense-vessels, spread with awnings of fine cloth, strewn with supremely fragrant flowers of every season, lovely with pools, white lotuses, fresh water-lily nets —

body.text: paramaprītiprāmodyasaṃjanane tasmin gṛhavarapradhāne 'dhyāvasato bodhisattvasyodāravaraśaraṇabhavananivāsino 'malavimalanirmalāṅgasyāmuktamālyābharaṇasya pravarasurabhigandhānulepanānuliptagātrasya śuklaśubhavimalaviśuddhanirmalavastraprāvṛtaśarīrasya anekadivyadūṣyasūkṣmasuvinyastamṛdukācilindikasukhasaṃsparśavarāṅgaracitaśayanatalābhirūḍhasya amaravadhūbhiriva sarvato anavadyāpratikūladarśanaśubhopacāracaritasya abhirūpāntaḥpuramadhyagatasya śaṅkhabherīmṛdaṅgapaṇavatuṇavavīṇāvallakisaṃpatāḍakipalanakulasughoṣakamadhuraveṇunirnāditaghoṣarutanānātūryasaṃgītisaṃprayogapratibodhitasya ye ca nārīgaṇāḥ snigdhamadhuramanojñasvaraveṇunirnāditanirghoṣarutena bodhisattvaṃ pratisaṃbodhayanti sma, teṣāṃ daśadigavasthitānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmadhisthānena tebhyo veṇutūryaninādanirghoṣarutebhya imā bodhisattvasya saṃcodanā gāthā niścaranti sma -
body.translated_text: abounding in arrangements and furnishings, filled with the sweet warbling of leaf-hidden parrots, <s>sārikā</s>-birds, cuckoos, swans, peacocks, <s>cakravāka</s>-birds, <s>kunāla</s>-birds, <s>kalaviṅka</s>-birds, <s>jīvajīvaka</s>-birds, and many other kinds of birds, set upon a ground-floor of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, reflecting every form, delighting the insatiable eye, generating supreme joy and gladness — in that foremost and chief dwelling, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelt therein, residing in that noble, supreme, auspicious mansion, his body pure, stainless, and spotless, wearing unfading garlands and ornaments, his limbs anointed with supreme fragrant unguents, his body clad in white, pure, stainless, immaculate garments, reclining upon a couch fashioned of many divine silks, fine, well-arranged, soft <s>Kācilinḍika</s> cloth, supremely pleasant to the touch, attended on all sides — as if by celestial brides — with irreproachable, pleasing, and auspicious service, dwelling in the midst of the beautiful inner palace, aroused by the sounds of conch-shells, drums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, <s>tuṇavas</s>, <s>vīṇās</s>, lutes, <s>saṃpatāḍakis</s>, <s>palanakulās</s>, sweet-sounding flutes, and the melodious sounds of various musical ensembles — and as the companies of women awakened the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with the smooth, sweet, enchanting sound of flute-music, by the empowerment of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> abiding in the ten directions, from those sounds of flute and music there issued forth these verses urging the <s>Bodhisattva</s> —

children.text: yā nāryo muditamanāḥ prasannacittā veṇubhyo madhuramanoramaṃ raṇante /
children.translated_text: The women, of delighted minds and clear hearts, play sweetly and charmingly on flutes;

children.text: āveśāddaśadiggatāṃ jinottamānāṃ gāthemā vividhavicitracitrarūpāḥ // Lal_13.9 //
children.translated_text: by the influence of the supreme <s>Jinas</s> of the ten directions, these verses [emerge] — of manifold, variegated, wondrous forms. // Lal_13.9 //

children.text: pūrve te ayu (kṛtu) praṇidhī abhūṣi vīrā dṛṣṭvemāṃ janata sadā anāthabhūtām /
children.translated_text: Formerly, O hero, you made a vow, having seen this world of people always without protectors:

children.text: śociṣye jaramaraṇāttathānyaduḥkhād buddhitvā padamajaraṃ paraṃ aśokam // Lal_13.10 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall relieve [them] from old age, death, and other sufferings; having awakened, [I shall attain] the supreme, ageless, sorrowless state.' // Lal_13.10 //

children.text: tatsādho puravara ita śīghraṃ niṣkramyā purimaṛṣibhi cīrṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O virtuous one, go forth swiftly from this foremost city! Tread the path walked by former sages!

children.text: ākramyā dharaṇitalapradeśaṃ saṃbuddhyā asadṛśajinajñānam // Lal_13.11 //
children.translated_text: Approaching that spot of earth, awaken to the incomparable <s>Jina</s>-knowledge! // Lal_13.11 //

children.text: pūrve te dhanaratana vicitrā tyaktābhūt karacaraṇapriyātmā /
children.translated_text: Formerly, various treasures, wealth, hands, feet, dear ones, and your very self were given away by you.

children.text: eṣo 'dyā tava samayu maharṣe dharmaughaṃ jagi vibhaja anantam // Lal_13.12 //
children.translated_text: This now is your appointed time, O great sage — distribute to the world the boundless flood of <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_13.12 //

children.text: śīlaṃ te śubha vimalakhaṇḍaṃ pūrvānte vara satatamabhūṣī /
children.translated_text: Your morality was pure, stainless, and unbroken — in former times, supreme, it was always yours.

children.text: śīlenānatisadṛśu maharṣe śocehī jagu vividhakileśaiḥ // Lal_13.13 //
children.translated_text: In morality, O great sage, none is your equal — [now] relieve the world [burning] with manifold afflictions! // Lal_13.13 //

children.text: kṣāntīye bhava śatacaritastvaṃ kṣāntāste jagi vividha duruktāḥ /
children.translated_text: In patience you have practiced for hundreds of lifetimes; you have endured the manifold harsh words of the world.

children.text: kṣāntāye kṣamadamaniratātma naiṣkramye mati kuru dvipadendrā // Lal_13.14 //
children.translated_text: O patient one, delighting in forbearance and self-restraint — set your mind upon the going forth, O lord among bipeds! // Lal_13.14 //

children.text: vīryaṃ te dṛḍhamacalamakampyaṃ pūrvānte pṛthu sugata abhūvan /
children.translated_text: Your vigor was firm, immovable, unshakable — in former times, O <s>Sugata</s>, it was abundant.

children.text: dharṣitvā namuci śaṭhaṃ sasainyaṃ śoṣiṣye traya sakalaapāyāt // Lal_13.15 //
children.translated_text: Having vanquished the deceitful <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) with his army, you shall dry up the three [lower] realms entirely of [their suffering]! // Lal_13.15 //

children.text: yasyārthe vratatapa caritastvaṃ dhyāyitvā kalikaluṣakileśāṃ /
children.translated_text: For whose sake you practiced vows and austerities, meditating upon the stain and defilement of afflictions —

children.text: tvaṃ varṣā amṛtajalamoghaṃ tarpehī ciratṛṣita anāthāṃ // Lal_13.16 //
children.translated_text: you shall rain a flood of deathless nectar-water and satisfy the long-thirsty, the unprotected ones! // Lal_13.16 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvāṃ giravaramanucintyā niṣkramyā puravara ita śīghram /
children.translated_text: Recollecting that former mountain-like [vow], go forth swiftly from this foremost city!

children.text: buddhitvā padamamṛtamaśokaṃ tarpiṣye amṛtarasi tṛṣārtāṃ // Lal_13.17 //
children.translated_text: Having awakened to the deathless, sorrowless state, you shall satisfy the thirst-afflicted with the nectar-essence! // Lal_13.17 //

children.text: prajñāyā paricarikuśala tvaṃ jñānaṃ te pṛthu vipulamanantam /
children.translated_text: In the cultivation of wisdom you are skilled; your knowledge is vast, broad, and infinite.

children.text: mūḍhānāṃ vimatipathasthitānāṃ prajñābhāṃ śubharucira kuru tvam // Lal_13.18 //
children.translated_text: For the deluded, those standing on the path of wrong views, produce the light of wisdom, pure and beautiful! // Lal_13.18 //

children.text: maitrāyāṃ bhava śatacaritastvaṃ kārūṇye vara mudita upekṣe /
children.translated_text: In loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) you have practiced for hundreds of lifetimes; supreme in compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), in sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), in equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

children.text: yāmevā varacari caritastvaṃ tāmevā cariṃ vibhaja jagasya // Lal_13.19 //
children.translated_text: That very practice you have followed, O supreme practitioner — distribute that very practice to the world! // Lal_13.19 //

children.text: evaṃ daśa diśa jinatejairgāthā vai guṇakusumavicitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, from the ten directions, by the splendor of the <s>Jinas</s>, verses adorned with flowers of virtues

children.text: tūryebhyo vividhamanuravante codentī śayanagatakumāram // Lal_13.20 //
children.translated_text: resound variously from the instruments, urging the prince as he lies upon his couch. // Lal_13.20 //

body.text: yada puna pramudita ratikara pramadā surucira sumadhura prabhaṇiṣu turiyaiḥ /
body.translated_text: When the delighted, joy-giving women play on their exceedingly beautiful, supremely sweet instruments,

body.text: atha jina daśadiśi suranaradamakāḥ giravaramanuravi tatu ravi turiyaiḥ // Lal_13.21 //
body.translated_text: then the <s>Jinas</s> of the ten directions, tamers of gods and men, cause the mountain-like [words] to resound from those instruments. // Lal_13.21 //

children.text: kṛta tvayi hitakara bahuguṇa janato nijinitu nijaguṇa vicarati gatiṣū /
children.translated_text: Having done much that is beneficial and virtuous for the world, [you shall] lead [beings] by your own virtues through the [various] destinies.

children.text: smara smara purimaka bratatapacaraṇa laghu vraja drumavaru spṛśa padamamṛtam // Lal_13.22 //
children.translated_text: Remember, remember your former vows, austerities, and practices! Go swiftly to the supreme tree and touch the deathless state! // Lal_13.22 //

children.text: sutṛṣita naramaru jinaguṇarahitā tvayi mati pratibalu amṛtarasadadā /
children.translated_text: The thirsty men and gods, devoid of <s>Jina</s>-qualities — you have the capacity to give the nectar-essence to them with your mind fixed on [their welfare].

children.text: daśabalaguṇadhara budhajanamahitaṃ laghu tvayi narapati vibhajahi amṛtam // Lal_13.23 //
children.translated_text: O bearer of the ten powers and virtues, honored by the wise — quickly distribute the nectar, O lord of men! // Lal_13.23 //

children.text: tyaji tvayi puri bhavi dhanamaṇikanakā sakhi priya suta mahi sanagaranigamā /
children.translated_text: You gave up formerly in [past] existences — wealth, jewels, gold, friends, dear ones, sons, the earth with its cities and market-towns;

children.text: śiramapi tyaji svaku karacaranayanā jagati ya hitakaru jinaguṇaniratā // Lal_13.24 //
children.translated_text: you gave up even your own head, hands, feet, and eyes — [you who are] the benefactor of the world, devoted to the qualities of a <s>Jina</s>! // Lal_13.24 //

children.text: puri tuma naravarasutu nṛpu yadabhū naru tava abhimukha ima giramavacī /
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a prince, a king's son, a sovereign, a person approached you and spoke this word:

children.text: dada mama ima mahi sanagaranigamāṃ tyaji tada pramuditu na ca manu kṣubhito // Lal_13.25 //
children.translated_text: 'Give me this earth with its cities and market-towns!' — You gave it then, delighted, with mind unperturbed. // Lal_13.25 //

children.text: puri tuma narapati svaku dvija yadabhū gurujani paricari na ca druhi parato /
children.translated_text: Formerly, when you were a king, [serving] your own <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [devoted] to attending upon your teacher and parents, without harming another —

children.text: sthapayisu dvijavara bahujana kuśale cyutu tatu bhavagatu marupuranilayam // Lal_13.26 //
children.translated_text: you established the multitude of people in wholesome [conduct], and having fallen from there, went to the abode of the divine city. // Lal_13.26 //

children.text: puri tuma nṛpasuta ṛṣivaru yadabhū chini tava tanuruha kalinṛpu ruṣito /
children.translated_text: Formerly you were a king's son, a foremost sage — when the wrathful <s>Kali</s>-king cut your limbs,

children.text: kṛta tvayi kulakriya na ca manu kṣubhito payu tava sravi tada karatalacaraṇaiḥ // Lal_13.27 //
children.translated_text: though such a deed was done to you, your mind was not disturbed; milk flowed then from your hands and feet. // Lal_13.27 //

children.text: syamu puna ṛṣisuta tvayi puri yadabhū vrataratu gurubharu girivaranilaye /
children.translated_text: Again, formerly you were a sage's son — delighting in vows, bearing heavy burdens in a mountain-peak dwelling,

children.text: hata bhava nṛpatina viṣakṛta īṣuṇā kṛpa tava tahi nṛpa na ca manu kṣubhito // Lal_13.28 //
children.translated_text: you were struck by a king with a poisoned arrow; [yet] your compassion [continued], O king, and your mind was not disturbed. // Lal_13.28 //

children.text: puri tuma guṇadhara mṛgapati yadabhū girinadibahujali duyamanu puruṣo /
children.translated_text: Formerly you were a lion, a bearer of virtues, in mountains and rivers and many waters — a man suffering [came to you];

children.text: hita bhava tvayi naru sthalapathi sthapito upanayi tava ari na ca manu kṣubhito // Lal_13.29 //
children.translated_text: you were a benefactor to that man, a way-farer established [in safety]; your enemy approached you, yet your mind was not disturbed. // Lal_13.29 //

children.text: puri tuma naravara tyaji sutu yadabhū maṇi tava prapatitu jaladhari vipule /
children.translated_text: Formerly, O best of men, you abandoned your son — your jewel fell into the vast ocean;

children.text: cyavayitu kṣapayitu tvaya mahaudadhiṃ labhi tada dhanamaṇi dṛḍhabala vaṣabhī // Lal_13.30 //
children.translated_text: to drain and exhaust that great ocean, you obtained then wealth and jewels through firm strength and power. // Lal_13.30 //

children.text: puri tuma supuruṣa ṛṣivaru yadabhū dvija tava upagatu bhava mama śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Formerly you were a most excellent man, a foremost sage — a bird came to you [saying]: 'Be my refuge!';

children.text: bhaṇi ṛṣi dvijavara mama ripuupane tyaji tvaya svaki tanu na ca dvija tyajase // Lal_13.31 //
children.translated_text: the sage said, 'O best of birds, [I am here] for my enemy's approach' — you gave up your own body, yet the bird you did not abandon. // Lal_13.31 //

children.text: syamu ṛṣi upagatu puri drumanilaye ruci bhaṇi taruruha kati ima gaṇaye /
children.translated_text: A sage approached [you] formerly in a tree-dwelling; [one] asked the tree: 'How many are these leaves that I count?'

children.text: suvidita sugaṇita yatha tahi kiśalā tatha tava avitatha samagira racitā // Lal_13.32 //
children.translated_text: Well-known and well-counted were then the leaves — just so were your unfailing words composed. // Lal_13.32 //

children.text: sukula suguṇadhara puri drumi vasato kṣayagatu na ca tyaji kṛtu smari purimam /
children.translated_text: Of good family, bearing good virtues, formerly dwelling in a tree — [when] destruction came, you did not abandon [your vow], remembering what was done before;

children.text: marupati pramuditu tava guṇa smarato śriyakari drumavari yathariva purimā // Lal_13.33 //
children.translated_text: the lord of gods was delighted, remembering your virtues — wealth-bestowing was that best of trees, just as before. // Lal_13.33 //

children.text: iti tava asadṛśa vratatapacaraṇā bahuguṇa guṇadhara guṇapathi carato /
children.translated_text: Thus were your incomparable vows, austerities, and conduct — [you who are] of many virtues, bearer of virtues, walking the path of virtue;

children.text: tyaji mahi sanagari ayu tava samayo laghu jagu sthapayahi jinaguṇacaraṇe // Lal_13.34 //
children.translated_text: abandon the earth with its cities — your time has come! Quickly establish the world in the conduct and virtues of a <s>Jina</s>! // Lal_13.34 //

children.text: yada pramadaratanā śubhavastrā bhūṣitagātrā varapravaru turiyā sumanojñā saṃprabhaṇīṣu /
children.translated_text: When the pleasure-maidens, in beautiful garments, with adorned bodies, with the finest excellent instruments, most delightful, began to sing,

children.text: atha daśasū diśato jinatejairgātha vicitrā iti raviṣū madhurā rutaghoṣā tūryasvarebhyaḥ // Lal_13.35 //
children.translated_text: then from the ten directions, by the power of the <s>Jina</s>, variegated verses — sweet sounds and melodious tones — [issued forth] from the instruments. // Lal_13.35 //

children.text: tava praṇidhī purime bahukalpāṃ lokapradīpā
children.translated_text: Your former aspiration through many <s>kalpas</s>, O Lamp of the World:

children.text: jaramaraṇagrasite ahu loke trāṇu bhaviṣye /
children.translated_text: 'In this world seized by old age and death, I shall become a protector!' —

children.text: smara purimapraṇidhiṃ narasiṃhā yā ti abhūṣī
children.translated_text: remember your former aspiration, O lion among men, that which was yours;

children.text: ayu samayo tvamihā dvipadendrā niṣkramaṇāya // Lal_13.36 //
children.translated_text: the time has come for you here, O lord among bipeds — for the great going-forth! // Lal_13.36 //

children.text: bhavanayute tvamihā bahudānaṃ dattamanekaṃ
children.translated_text: In many myriads of existences you gave abundant, manifold gifts here —

children.text: dhanakanakā ratanā śubhavastrā ratnavicitrā /
children.translated_text: wealth, gold, jewels, fine garments, variegated with gems;

children.text: karacaraṇā nayanā priyaputrā rājya samṛddhaṃ
children.translated_text: hands, feet, eyes, beloved sons, prosperous kingdoms —

children.text: tvayi tyajitaṃ na ca te khiladoṣā yācanakeṣu // Lal_13.37 //
children.translated_text: you relinquished [them all], and there was no fault of meanness in you toward those who asked. // Lal_13.37 //

children.text: śiśunṛpati tvamihā śaśiketo āsi sudaṃṣṭro kṛpa karuṇāmanaso maṇicūḍo candrapradīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: You were here [as] the child-king <s>Śaśiketu</s>, and <s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s>, compassionate and kind of mind, and <s>Maṇicūḍa</s>, and <s>Candrapradīpa</s>;

children.text: iti pramukhā kariyā dṛḍhaśūro rājasunetro bahu nṛpati nayutā rata dāne tvaṃ savikurvan // Lal_13.38 //
children.translated_text: and likewise foremost [among them was] <s>Kariyā</s> [the elephant], <s>Dṛḍhaśūra</s>, <s>Rājasunetra</s> — many <s>nayutas</s> of kings devoted to giving, you manifesting [among them]. // Lal_13.38 //

children.text: tava sugatā carito bahukalpāṃ śīlacarīye maṇiratnā vimalā sadṛśābhūcchīlaviśuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Your well-gone conduct through many <s>kalpas</s> in the practice of morality — like a stainless jewel-gem was your purity of morality;

children.text: tvayi caratā camarī yatha bālaṃ rakṣitu śīlaṃ kṛtu tvamihā jagati vipulārthaṃ śīlaratenā // Lal_13.39 //
children.translated_text: while you practiced [it], like a <s>camarī</s> deer guarding its tail, you guarded your morality — you accomplished vast purpose in the world through delight in morality. // Lal_13.39 //

children.text: gajavaru tvamihā ripulubdhe viddhu iṣūṇā kṛpa karuṇā janiyā atiraudre chāditu śobhe /
children.translated_text: You were here a lordly elephant, struck by arrows of a greedy hunter — [yet] compassion was generated [in you] toward that exceedingly fierce one, concealing [his wrong];

children.text: parityaji te rucirā śubhadantā na ca tyaji śīlaṃ iti pramukhā kariyā bahu tubhyaṃ śīlavikurvī // Lal_13.40 //
children.translated_text: you gave up your beautiful, auspicious tusks, yet did not abandon morality — thus and such were the foremost deeds of your manifold moral displays. // Lal_13.40 //

children.text: tvayi sahitā jagato 'hita anekā duḥkhasahasrā bahukaṭukāvacanaṃ vadhabandhā kṣāntiratenā /
children.translated_text: Together with you, many ills of the world — thousands of sufferings, much harsh speech, beatings, and bondage — [you bore all] through delight in patience;

children.text: paricārita purime nara ye te sarvasukhenā puna vadhakāstava teha abhūvan tacca ti kṣāntam // Lal_13.41 //
children.translated_text: those men who previously attended upon you with all comforts — again, your executioners they became, and that too you endured. // Lal_13.41 //

children.text: giripravarānilaye tuma nāthā ṛkṣu yadāsī
children.translated_text: In the dwelling of a great mountain peak, when you were a lord, a bear —

children.text: himakiraṇā salilā bhayabhītaṃ tvaṃ naru gṛhya /
children.translated_text: a man, snow-cold, [in danger of] water, frightened with fear, you took up;

children.text: paricarasi vividhā phalamūlaiḥ sarvasukhenā
children.translated_text: you served him with various fruits and roots, with all comforts —

children.text: laghu vadhakāṃ sa tavā upanetrī taṃ ca ti kṣāntam // Lal_13.42 //
children.translated_text: swiftly that executioner was brought to you by him, and that too you endured. // Lal_13.42 //

children.text: dṛḍhu saṃsthitamacalamakampyaṃ vīryu tavāsīt
children.translated_text: Firm, steadfast, immovable, unshakable was your vigor,

children.text: vratatapasā vividhā guṇajñānaṃ eṣata bodhim /
children.translated_text: through vows and austerities, various virtues and knowledge, seeking <s>Bodhi</s>;

children.text: kṛtu abalo namucī vaśavartī vīyabalenā
children.translated_text: you made powerless <s>Namuchi</s>, the lord of desires, by the power of vigor —

children.text: ayu samayo tvamihā narasiṃhā niṣkramaṇāya // Lal_13.43 //
children.translated_text: the time has come for you here, O lion among men — for the great going-forth! // Lal_13.43 //

children.text: hayapravarū tvamihā puri āsī hemasuvarṇo
children.translated_text: You were here formerly a supreme horse, golden in color,

children.text: laghu gagane vajrase kṛpajāto rākṣasidvīpam /
children.translated_text: swift in the sky like a thunderbolt, compassion-born, [who flew to] the island of <s>Rākṣasas</s>;

children.text: vyasanagata manujāṃ tada gṛhyā kṣemi thapesī
children.translated_text: men in distress then, having taken them, you placed [them] in safety —

children.text: iti pramukhā kariyā bahu tubhyaṃ vīryavikurvā // Lal_13.44 //
children.translated_text: thus and such were the foremost deeds of your manifold vigor-displays. // Lal_13.44 //

children.text: damaśamatheḥ niyamāhatakleśā dhyāyina agrā
children.translated_text: Through restraint and calm, with afflictions destroyed by discipline, supreme among meditators,

children.text: laghu capalaṃ viṣayai ratilolaṃ cittu damitvā /
children.translated_text: swiftly taming the fickle mind, lustful and attached to sense-objects —

children.text: kṛtu svaguṇo tvamihā jagato 'rthe dhyānaratenā
children.translated_text: you accomplished your own virtues here for the world's sake through delight in meditation;

children.text: ayu samayo tvamihā varasattvā dhyānavikurvā // Lal_13.45 //
children.translated_text: the time has come for you here, O best of beings — for the displays of meditation! // Lal_13.45 //

children.text: tvaṃ purime ṛṣi susthitu āsī dhyānaratīye nṛparahitā manujā tvamu gṛhyā rājyabhiṣiñcī /
children.translated_text: Formerly you were a sage, well-established in delight in meditation — [seeing] men without a king, you took them and anointed [a king];

children.text: daśakuśalī janitā thapitā te brahmapatheṣu cyuta manujā vrajiṣū tada sarve brahmaniketam // Lal_13.46 //
children.translated_text: you generated the ten wholesome courses and established them on the paths of <s>Brahmā</s> — deceased, those men all went then to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>. // Lal_13.46 //

children.text: diśividiśi vividhāgatijñāne tvaṃ suvidhijño paracaritā jagati rutajñāne indriyajñāne /
children.translated_text: In knowledge of the various destinies in all directions, you are well-skilled — in knowing the conduct of others, in knowledge of sounds in the world, in knowledge of faculties;

children.text: nayavinaye vividhāmatidhāre pāragatastvaṃ ayu samayo tvamihā nṛpasūno niṣkramaṇāya // Lal_13.47 //
children.translated_text: in guidance, discipline, and the various streams of intellect, you have gone to the far shore — the time has come for you here, O prince — for the great going-forth! // Lal_13.47 //

children.text: tvayi purimā janatā ima dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭivipannā jaramaraṇā vividhā bahuduḥkhe kṛchragatā hi /
children.translated_text: Formerly, seeing these beings of wrong views — in old age, death, and various great sufferings, fallen into hardship —

children.text: bhavavibhavaṃkaraṇo ṛjumārge svāmanubaddhā hatatamasa tvamihā kṛtu loke arthu mahanto // Lal_13.48 //
children.translated_text: you, the maker of [the distinction between] existence and prosperity, binding [them] to the straight path of your own [teaching], having destroyed darkness, you accomplished great purpose in the world. // Lal_13.48 //

children.text: iti vividhā rucirā guṇayuktā gātha vicitrā
children.translated_text: Thus [these] various, beautiful, virtue-endowed, variegated verses,

children.text: tatu raviṣu turiyebhī jinatejā codayi vīram /
children.translated_text: from those instruments, by the power of the <s>Jina</s>, awakened the hero;

children.text: duḥkhabharitajanate iha dṛṣṭvā mā tvamupekṣā
children.translated_text: 'Seeing beings here filled with suffering, do not be indifferent! —

children.text: ayu samayo tvamihā varabuddhe niṣkramaṇāya // Lal_13.49 //
children.translated_text: the time has come for you here, O supreme <s>Buddha</s> — for the great going-forth!' // Lal_13.49 //

children.text: vicitravastraratnahāragandhamālyabhūṣitā prasannacitta premajāta nāriyo praharṣitā /
children.translated_text: Adorned with variegated garments, jewels, necklaces, fragrances, garlands, and ornaments, with clear minds, love-born, the women were delighted;

children.text: prabodhayanti ye 'grasattva tūryasaṃpravāditaiḥ jinānubhāvi ekarūpa gātha tūrya niścarī // Lal_13.50 //
children.translated_text: they who awaken the foremost being with the playing of instruments — by the <s>Jina</s>'s power, a single form of verse issued forth from the instruments. // Lal_13.50 //

children.text: yasyārthi tubhya kalpa naika tyaktu tyāga dustyajā
children.translated_text: 'For your sake, through not one but many <s>kalpas</s>, you abandoned [things] hard to abandon, [performing] gifts hard to give;

children.text: sucīrṇa śīlu kṣānti vīrya dhyāna prajña bhāvitā /
children.translated_text: well-practiced morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom were cultivated [by you];

children.text: jagaddhitārtha so ti kālu sāṃprataṃ upasthito
children.translated_text: that time for the world's welfare has now arrived —

children.text: naiṣkramyabuddhi cintayāśu mā vilamba nāyaka // Lal_13.51 //
children.translated_text: think quickly of the intention to renounce! Do not delay, O leader! // Lal_13.51 //

children.text: tyuktu pūrvi ratnakośa svarṇarūpyabhūṣaṇā yaṣṭā ti yajña naikarūpa tāsu tāsu jātiṣu /
children.translated_text: Formerly you gave up treasure-stores of gold, silver, and ornaments; you sacrificed great sacrifices of many kinds in those various births;

children.text: tyakta bhārya putra dhīta kāyu rājyu jīvitaṃ bodhiheturaprameya tyaktuḥdustyajā tvayā // Lal_13.52 //
children.translated_text: you gave up wife, son, daughter, body, kingdom, and life — for the sake of <s>Bodhi</s>, immeasurable [things] hard to abandon were abandoned by you! // Lal_13.52 //

children.text: abhūṣi tvaṃ adīnapuṇya rāja viśrutaśriyo
children.translated_text: You were a king of inexhaustible merit, of renowned glory —

children.text: nimiṃdharo nimiśca kṛṣṇa(bandhu) brahmadatta kesarī /
children.translated_text: <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>, <s>Nimi</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇabandhu</s>, <s>Brahmadatta</s>, <s>Kesarī</s>,

children.text: sahasrayajña dharmacinti arcimān dṛḍhadhanu
children.translated_text: <s>Sahasrayajña</s>, <s>Dharmacintī</s>, <s>Arcimān</s>, <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>,

children.text: sucintitārtha dīnasattva yeḥti tyakta dustyajā // Lal_13.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sucintitārtha</s>, <s>Dīnasattva</s> — by whom things hard to abandon were abandoned! // Lal_13.53 //

children.text: sutasoma dīptavīrya puṇyaraśmi yo so 'bhū
children.translated_text: <s>Sutasoma</s>, <s>Dīptavīrya</s>, <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> — that is who you were;

children.text: mahatyāgavantu sthāmavantu yaḥ kṛtajña tvaṃ abhūḥ /
children.translated_text: one of great generosity, of great strength, grateful — that is who you were;

children.text: rājarṣi candrarūpavantu śūra satyavardhano
children.translated_text: a royal sage, <s>Candrarūpavantu</s>, <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Satyavardhana</s>,

children.text: subhāṣitaṃgaveṣi rāji asi sumatiṃ ca sūrato // Lal_13.54 //
children.translated_text: a seeker of well-spoken [words], a king — you were <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Sūrata</s>. // Lal_13.54 //

children.text: candraprabho viśeṣagāmi reṇubhū diśāṃpati pradānaśūra kāśirāju ratnacūḍa śāntagaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Candraprabha</s>, <s>Viśeṣagāmī</s>, <s>Reṇu</s>, lord of the directions, <s>Pradānaśūra</s>, king of <s>Kāśī</s>, <s>Ratnacūḍa</s>, <s>Śāntaga</s>;

children.text: eti cānyi pārthivendra yebhi tyakta dustyajā yathā ti vṛṣṭa tyāgavṛṣṭi eṣa dharma varṣahī // Lal_13.55 //
children.translated_text: and other lords of kings by whom things hard to abandon were abandoned — as they rained a rain of generosity, so this one shall rain the <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_13.55 //

children.text: dṛṣṭā ti pūrviṃ sattvasāra gaṅgavālukopamā kṛtā ti teṣa buddhapūja aprameyacintiyā /
children.translated_text: Seen in the past — [those] jewels among beings, [numerous] as the sands of the Ganges — inconceivable was the <s>Buddha</s>-worship performed for them;

children.text: varāgrabodhi eṣamāṇa sattvamokṣakāraṇādū ayaṃ sa kālu prāptu sūru niṣkramā purottamāt // Lal_13.56 //
children.translated_text: seeking supreme <s>Bodhi</s> for the sake of liberating beings — that time has arrived! O hero, go forth from this best of cities! // Lal_13.56 //

children.text: prathamena te amoghadarśi śālapuṣpapūjito virocanaḥ prasannacitta prekṣitaḥ kṣaṇāntaram /
children.translated_text: The first [<s>Buddha</s>] by you [worshiped was] <s>Amoghadarśī</s> — with <s>śāla</s>-flower worship; <s>Virocana</s>, beheld with a clear mind for just a moment;

children.text: harītakī ca eka datta dundubhisvarāya te tṛṇottha gṛhya dhāritā ti dṛṣṭa candanaṃ gṛham // Lal_13.57 //
children.translated_text: a single <s>harītakī</s> [fruit] given to <s>Dundubhisvara</s>; a grass-born [offering] grasped and held — and the candana-house was seen. // Lal_13.57 //

children.text: purapraveśi reṇu dṛṣṭa kṣiptu cūrṇamuṣṭikā dharmeśvarāya sādhukāru dattu dharma bhāṣato /
children.translated_text: At [<s>Buddha</s>] <s>Reṇu</s>'s city-entry, dust was seen, [and you] threw a handful of powder; to <s>Dharmeśvara</s>, a cry of 'Well done!' was given as he preached the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: namo namaḥ samantadarśi dṛṣṭa vāca bhāṣitā mahārciskandhi svarṇamāla kṣipta harṣitena te // Lal_13.58 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Namo namaḥ</s>!' was the word spoken upon seeing <s>Samantadarśī</s>; a golden garland was joyfully thrown to <s>Mahārciskandhi</s>. // Lal_13.58 //

children.text: dharmadhvajo daśāpradāni rodhu muṅga muṣṭinā aśokapuṣpi jñānaketu yvāgupāna sārathiḥ /
children.translated_text: To <s>Dharmadhvaja</s>, ten <s>apradānis</s>; blocking [a stream] with a handful of <s>muṅga</s> [grass]; <s>aśoka</s>-flowers to <s>Jñānaketu</s>; a gruel-offering to <s>Sārathi</s>;

children.text: ratnaśikhī ca dīpadāni padmayoni oṣadhī sarvābhibhūśca muktahāri padmadāni sāgaro // Lal_13.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> — lamp-offerings; <s>Padmayoni</s> — herbs; <s>Sarvābhibhū</s> — a released pearl-necklace; <s>Sāgara</s> — lotus-offerings. // Lal_13.59 //

children.text: vitānadāni padmagarbhi siṃhu varṣasaṃstare śālendrarāja sarpidāni kṣīratyāgi puṣpitī /
children.translated_text: Canopy-offerings to <s>Padmagarbhī</s>; <s>Siṃhu</s> — a rain-garment spread; <s>Śālendrarāja</s> — clarified butter offerings; <s>Kṣīratyāgī</s> — <s>Puṣpitī</s>;

children.text: yaśodattu kuruṇṭapuṣpi satyadarśi bhojane kāyu praṇāmi jñānameru nāgadattu cīvare // Lal_13.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodatta</s> — <s>kuruṇṭa</s>-flowers; <s>Satyadarśī</s> — food; body-prostration to <s>Jñānameru</s>; <s>Nāgadatta</s> — robes. // Lal_13.60 //

children.text: atyuccagāmi candanāgri tīkṣṇalohamuṣṭinā mahāviyūha padmadāni raśmirāja ratnabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Atyuccagāmī</s> — sandalwood supreme; <s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s> — a fistful; <s>Mahāviyūha</s> — lotus-offerings; <s>Raśmirāja</s> — with jewels;

children.text: śākyamuni ca suvarṇamuṣṭi indraketu saṃstuto sūryānano vataṃsake hi svarṇapaṭṭi sūmatī // Lal_13.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śākyamuni</s> — a fistful of gold; <s>Indraketu</s> — praised; <s>Sūryānana</s> — with a chaplet; <s>Suvarṇapaṭṭī</s> — <s>Sumatī</s>. // Lal_13.61 //

children.text: nāgābhibhū maṇipradāni puṣya dūṣyasaṃstare bhaiṣajyarāju ratnachatri siṃhaketu āsane /
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgābhibhū</s> — jewel-offerings; <s>Puṣya</s> — a spread of <s>dūṣya</s>-cloth; <s>Bhaiṣajyarāju</s> — a jewel-parasol; <s>Siṃhaketu</s> — a seat;

children.text: guṇāgradhāri ratnajāli sarvavādi kāśyapo gandhāgri cūrṇi mukta arciketu puṣpacaityake // Lal_13.62 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guṇāgradhārī</s> — a jewel-net; <s>Sarvavādī</s> — <s>Kāśyapa</s>; fragrance-supreme — powders; <s>Mukta</s> — <s>Arciketu</s> — a flower-shrine. // Lal_13.62 //

children.text: akṣobhyarāja kūṭāgāri mālya lokapūjito tagaraśikhi ca rājyatyāgi sarvagandhi durjayo /
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣobhyarāja</s> — a mansion; garlands to <s>Lokapūjita</s>; <s>Tagaraśikhī</s> — kingdom-renunciation; <s>Sarvagandhi</s> — <s>Durjaya</s>;

children.text: mahāpradīpa ātmatyāgi bhūṣaṇe padmottaro vicitrapuṣpi dharmaketu dīpakāri utpalaiḥ // Lal_13.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāpradīpa</s> — self-sacrifice; ornaments to <s>Padmottara</s>; <s>Vicitrapuṣpī</s> — <s>Dharmaketu</s>; lamp-offerings with lotuses. // Lal_13.63 //

children.text: eti cānyi sattvasāra ye ti pūrva pūjitā nānārūpa vicitra pūja anyajanyakurvatā /
children.translated_text: And other jewels among beings who were worshiped in the past — with various, variegated worship performed in other births;

children.text: smarāhi te atīta buddha tā ca pūja śāstunāṃ anāthasattva śokapūrṇa mā upekṣi niṣkramā // Lal_13.64 //
children.translated_text: remember those past <s>Buddhas</s> and those worships of the Teachers! Do not disregard the helpless, sorrow-filled beings — go forth! // Lal_13.64 //

children.text: dīpaṃkareti dṛṣṭamātri labdha kṣānti uttamā abhijña pañca acyutā ti labdha ānulomikā /
children.translated_text: Upon merely seeing <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, you obtained the supreme patience; the five <s>abhijñās</s> [were obtained], the unfailing; and the <s>ānulomikī</s> [acceptance was] attained;

children.text: atottareṇa ekameka buddha pūjacintiyā pravartitā asaṃkhyakalpa sarvalokadhātuṣū // Lal_13.65 //
children.translated_text: from that point onward, each and every <s>Buddha</s> — inconceivable worship — was set in motion through innumerable <s>kalpas</s> in all world-systems. // Lal_13.65 //

children.text: kṣīṇā ti kalpa aprameya te ca buddha nirvṛtā tavāpi sarva ātmabhāvi te ca nāma kva gatā /
children.translated_text: Exhausted are those immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, and those <s>Buddhas</s> have attained <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; your own self-existences too — they and their names, where have they gone?

children.text: kṣayāntadharmi sarvi bhāvu nāsti nityu saṃskṛte anitya kāma rājyabhoga niṣkramā purottamāt // Lal_13.66 //
children.translated_text: All conditioned things are of the nature of ending — there is nothing permanent in the compounded; impermanent are pleasures, kingdoms, enjoyments — go forth from this best of cities! // Lal_13.66 //

children.text: jarā ca vyādhi mṛtyu enti dāruṇā mahābhayā
children.translated_text: Old age, disease, and death come — dreadful, of great terror,

children.text: hutāśano va ugrateja bhīma kalpasaṃkṣaye /
children.translated_text: like a raging fire of fierce energy, terrifying, at the <s>kalpa</s>'s destruction;

children.text: kṣayāntadharmi sarvi bhāvu nāsti nityu saṃskṛte
children.translated_text: all conditioned things are of the nature of ending — there is nothing permanent in the compounded;

children.text: sukṛcchra prāpta sattva* * niṣkramā guṇaṃdharā // Lal_13.67 //
children.translated_text: beings have reached great difficulty * * — go forth, O bearer of virtues! // Lal_13.67 //

children.text: yada nārigaṇastuṇaveṇuravaiḥ vividhaisturiyaiḥ pratibodhayiṣu /
children.translated_text: When the groups of women with <s>tuṇa</s>-drums, flutes, and diverse instruments sought to awaken

children.text: sukhaśayanagataṃ manujādhipatiṃ tada tūryaravo ayu niścarate // Lal_13.68 //
children.translated_text: the lord of men lying on his comfortable bed — then from the instruments this sound issued forth: // Lal_13.68 //

children.text: jvalitaṃ tribhavaṃ jaravyādhidukhaiḥ maraṇāgnipradīptamanāthamidam /
children.translated_text: 'Blazing is the triple world with old age, disease, and suffering; ablaze with the fire of death is this protectorless [world];

children.text: bhavani śaraṇe sada mūḍha jagat bhramatī bhramaro yatha kumbhagato // Lal_13.69 //
children.translated_text: deluded beings always take refuge in [worldly] existence — they wander like a bee trapped in a pot!' // Lal_13.69 //

children.text: adhruvaṃ tribhavaṃ śaradabhranibhaṃ naṭaraṅgasamā jagi rūrmicutī /
children.translated_text: The three realms are impermanent, like autumn clouds; the rising and falling of beings in the world is like the play of a dancer.

children.text: girinadyasamaṃ laghuśīghrajavaṃ vrajatāyu jage yatha vidyu nabhe // Lal_13.70 //
children.translated_text: life passes swiftly like a mountain torrent, and the lifespan in the world is like lightning in the sky. // Lal_13.70 //

children.text: bhuvi devapure triapāyapathe bhavatṛṣṇaavidyavaśā janatā /
children.translated_text: On earth, in the abodes of gods, and in the three lower paths, beings are under the power of craving and ignorance of existence;

children.text: parivartiṣu pañcagatiṣvabudhāḥ yatha kumbhakarasya hi cakrabhramī // Lal_13.71 //
children.translated_text: the unawakened revolve in the five destinies, like the turning of a potter's wheel. // Lal_13.71 //

children.text: priyarūpavaraiḥ saha snigdharutaiḥ śubhagandharasai varasparśasukhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With pleasing forms and beautiful sounds, with fine fragrances, tastes, and the pleasure of excellent touches,

children.text: pariṣiktamidaṃ kalipāśa jagat mṛgalubdhakapāśi yathaiva kapi // Lal_13.72 //
children.translated_text: this world is ensnared by the noose of strife — like a monkey in the snare of a deer-hunter. // Lal_13.72 //

children.text: sabhayā saraṇāḥ sada vairakarāḥ bahuśoka upadrava kāmaguṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Full of fear, refugeless, always producing enmity — the qualities of sensual pleasure bring much grief and calamity;

children.text: asidhārasamā viṣapatranibhā jahitāryajanairyatha mīḍhaghaṭāḥ // Lal_13.73 //
children.translated_text: they are like the edge of a sword, like leaves of poison — they are abandoned by the noble, like pots of filth. // Lal_13.73 //

children.text: smṛtiśokakarāstamasīkaraṇāḥ bhayahetukarā dukhamūla sadā /
children.translated_text: They produce sorrow and remembrance, they bring darkness, they are a cause of fear, always the root of suffering;

children.text: bhavatṛṣṇalatāya vivṛddhikarāḥ sabhayā saraṇā sada kāmaguṇāḥ // Lal_13.74 //
children.translated_text: they nourish the creeper of craving for existence — the qualities of sensual pleasure are full of fear, refugeless, always. // Lal_13.74 //

children.text: yatha agnikhadā jvalitā sabhayā tatha kāma ime viditāryajanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a blazing pit of fire, full of danger — so are these sensual pleasures, as known by the noble;

children.text: mahapaṅkasamā asisundhusamāḥ madhudigdha iva kṣuradhāra yathā // Lal_13.75 //
children.translated_text: like a great swamp, like a river of swords, like honey smeared on a razor's edge. // Lal_13.75 //

children.text: yatha sarpisaro yatha mīḍhaghaṭāḥ tatha kāma ime viditā viduṣām /
children.translated_text: Like a pit of serpents, like pots of filth — so are these sensual pleasures, as known by the wise;

children.text: tatha śūlasamā dvijapeśisamāḥ yatha śvāna karaṅka savairamukhāḥ // Lal_13.76 //
children.translated_text: like stakes, like pieces of flesh for birds, like bones that dogs [fight over] with hostile faces. // Lal_13.76 //

children.text: udacandrasamā imi kāmaguṇāḥ pratibimba iva girighoṣa yathā /
children.translated_text: These qualities of sensual pleasure are like the moon reflected in water, like a reflection, like a mountain echo;

children.text: pratibhāsasamā naṭaraṅgasamāḥ tatha svapnasamā viditāryajanaiḥ // Lal_13.77 //
children.translated_text: like an illusion, like a dancer's play — and like a dream, as known by the noble. // Lal_13.77 //

children.text: kṣaṇikā vaśikā imi kāmaguṇāḥ tatha māyamarīcisamā alikāḥ /
children.translated_text: These qualities of sensual pleasure are momentary, subjugating, illusory like magic and mirages;

children.text: udabudbudaphenasamā vitathā parikalpasamuchita buddha budhaiḥ // Lal_13.78 //
children.translated_text: like bubbles and foam on water, false — conceived by mental construction, as understood by the awakened. // Lal_13.78 //

children.text: prathame vayase vararūpadharaḥ priya iṣṭa mato iya bālacarī /
children.translated_text: In the prime of youth, bearing a beautiful form, dear, pleasing, and esteemed — such is this childish behavior;

children.text: jaravyādhidukhai hatatejavapuṃ vijahanti mṛgā iva śuṣkanadīm // Lal_13.79 //
children.translated_text: [but when] struck down by old age, disease, and suffering, with splendor and body destroyed — they abandon [one] like animals [abandon] a dried-up river. // Lal_13.79 //

children.text: dhanadhānyavaro bahudravyabalī priya iṣṭa mato iya bālacarī /
children.translated_text: Rich in wealth, grain, and great possessions, strong — dear, pleasing, and esteemed — such is this childish behavior;

children.text: parihīnadhanaṃ puna kṛcchragataṃ vijahanti narā iva śūnyaṭavīm // Lal_13.80 //
children.translated_text: [but when one is] impoverished and fallen into misery, people abandon [him] like an empty wilderness. // Lal_13.80 //

children.text: yatha puṣpadrumo saphaleva drumo naru dānaratastatha prītikaro /
children.translated_text: Just as a flowering tree or a fruit-bearing tree — so is a man delighting in generosity, a bringer of joy;

children.text: dhanahīna jarārtitu yācanako bhavate tada apriyu gṛdhrasamaḥ // Lal_13.81 //
children.translated_text: [but when] impoverished, afflicted by old age, and begging, he then becomes disliked, like a vulture. // Lal_13.81 //

children.text: prabhu dravyabalī vararūpadharaḥ priyasaṃgamanendriyaprītikaro /
children.translated_text: Powerful, rich in possessions, bearing a beautiful form, bringing pleasure to the senses through the company of loved ones —

children.text: jaravyādhidukhārditu kṣīṇadhano bhavate tada apriyu mṛtyusamaḥ // Lal_13.82 //
children.translated_text: [but when] afflicted by old age, disease, and suffering, with wealth exhausted, he then becomes disliked, like death itself. // Lal_13.82 //

children.text: jarayā jaritaḥ samatītavayo druma vidyuhateva yathā bhavati /
children.translated_text: Consumed by old age, with youth gone by, one becomes like a tree struck by lightning;

children.text: jarajīrṇa agāru yathā sabhayo jaraniḥsaraṇaṃ laghu brūhi mune // Lal_13.83 //
children.translated_text: like a house decayed by old age, full of danger — tell us quickly, O Sage, of the escape from old age! // Lal_13.83 //

children.text: jara śoṣayate naranārigaṇaṃ yatha mālulatā ghanaśālavanam /
children.translated_text: Old age withers the company of men and women, as the <s>Mālu</s> creeper [withers] a dense <s>Śāla</s> forest;

children.text: jara vīryaparākramavegaharī jara paṅkanimagna yathā puruṣo // Lal_13.84 //
children.translated_text: old age robs [one of] vigor, valor, and speed — old age is like a man sunk in mud. // Lal_13.84 //

body.text: jara rūpasurūpavirūpakarī jara tejaharī balasthāmaharī /
body.translated_text: Old age makes the beautiful ugly, old age robs splendor, robs strength and firmness;

body.text: sada saukhyaharī paribhāvakarī jara mṛtyukarī jara ojaharī // Lal_13.85 //
body.translated_text: old age always robs happiness and brings contempt; old age brings death, old age robs vitality. // Lal_13.85 //

children.text: bahurogaśatai ghanavyādhidukhaiḥ upasṛṣṭa jagajjvalateva mṛgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beset by hundreds of diseases, by dense suffering of illness, the world blazes like animals [in a forest fire];

children.text: jaravyādhigataṃ prasamīkṣva jagat dukhaniḥsaraṇaṃ laghu deśayahī // Lal_13.86 //
children.translated_text: behold the world overtaken by old age and disease — teach quickly the escape from suffering! // Lal_13.86 //

children.text: śiśire hi yathā himadhātu mahān tṛṇagulmavanauṣadhiojaharo /
children.translated_text: Just as in winter the great element of frost robs the vitality of grass, shrubs, forests, and herbs,

children.text: tatha ojaharo ahu vyādhijaro parihīyati indriya rūpa balam // Lal_13.87 //
children.translated_text: so old age and disease rob vitality — the senses, form, and strength decline. // Lal_13.87 //

children.text: dhanadhānyamahārthakṣayāntakaro paritāpakaraḥ sahavyādhijaro /
children.translated_text: Old age and disease bring the destruction of wealth, grain, and great treasures, and produce torment;

children.text: pratighātakaraḥ priyu dveṣakaraḥ paridāhakaro yatha sūrya nabhe // Lal_13.88 //
children.translated_text: they bring adversity, turn the dear into the hateful, and cause burning — like the sun in the sky. // Lal_13.88 //

children.text: maraṇaṃ cavanaṃ cuti kālakriyā priyadravyajanena viyogu sadā /
children.translated_text: Death, passing away, decease, the end of time — always separation from dear possessions and people;

children.text: apunāgamanaṃ ca asaṃgamanaṃ drumapatraphalā nadisrota yathā // Lal_13.89 //
children.translated_text: no return, no reunion — like leaves, fruit from a tree, like the current of a river. // Lal_13.89 //

children.text: maraṇaṃ vaśitāmavaśīkurute maraṇaṃ harate nadi dāru yathā /
children.translated_text: Death subjugates [even] the powerful, making them powerless; death carries [one] away like a river carries timber;

children.text: asahāyu naro vrajate 'dvitiyo svakakarmaphalānugato vivaśaḥ // Lal_13.90 //
children.translated_text: a man goes helpless and alone, without a companion, following the fruits of his own actions, powerless. // Lal_13.90 //

children.text: maraṇo grasate bahuprāṇiśataṃ makareva jalā hari bhūtagaṇam /
children.translated_text: Death devours hundreds of living beings — like a sea-monster [swallows] water-creatures, a lion the herds of animals,

children.text: garuḍo uragaṃ mṛgarāju gajaṃ jvalaneva tṛṇoṣadhibhūtagaṇam // Lal_13.91 //
children.translated_text: a <s>Garuḍa</s> the serpent, a lord of beasts the elephant — like fire [consumes] grass, herbs, and all living things. // Lal_13.91 //

children.text: ima īdṛśakai bahudoṣaśataiḥ jagu mocayituṃ kṛta yā praṇidhi /
children.translated_text: To liberate the world from these and such hundreds of faults — [remember] the vow you made;

children.text: smara tāṃ purimāṃ praṇidhānacarīṃ ayu kālu tavā abhiniṣkramitum // Lal_13.92 //
children.translated_text: remember that former vow-practice — the time of your life [here] has come; it is time to go forth! // Lal_13.92 //

children.text: yada nārigaṇaḥ praharṣito bodhayatī turiyairmahāmunim /
children.translated_text: When the company of women, delighted, awakens the great Sage with music,

children.text: tada gātha vicitra niścarī tūryaśabdāt sugatānubhāvataḥ // Lal_13.93 //
children.translated_text: then wondrous verses issued forth from the sound of the instruments, by the power of the <s>Sugata</s>: // Lal_13.93 //

children.text: laghu tadbhañjati sarvasaṃskṛtaṃ acirasthāyi nabheva vidyataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Swiftly it breaks — all that is conditioned, impermanent, like lightning in the sky;

children.text: ayu kālu tavā upasthitaḥ samayo niṣkramaṇāya suvrata // Lal_13.94 //
children.translated_text: the time of your life has arrived — it is the moment for going forth, O one of excellent vows! // Lal_13.94 //

children.text: saṃskāra anitya adhruvāḥ āmakumbhopama bhedanātmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Conditioned things are impermanent, unstable, like unfired pots, having the nature of breaking;

children.text: parakeraka yācitopamāḥ pāṃśunagaropama tāvakālikāḥ // Lal_13.95 //
children.translated_text: like another's thing on loan, like a city of sand — they are temporary. // Lal_13.95 //

children.text: saṃskāra pralopadharmime varṣakāli calitaṃ ca lepanam /
children.translated_text: Conditioned things are subject to decay — like plaster during the rainy season,

children.text: nadikūla ivā savālukaṃ pratyayādhīna svabhāvadurbalāḥ // Lal_13.96 //
children.translated_text: like a river bank with [loose] sand — dependent on conditions, weak by nature. // Lal_13.96 //

children.text: saṃskāra pradīpaacivat kṣiprautpattinirodhadharmikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Conditioned things, like a lamp, are of the nature of swift arising and cessation;

children.text: anavasthita mārutopamāḥ phenapiṇḍave asāra durbalāḥ // Lal_13.97 //
children.translated_text: unstable, like the wind — like a ball of foam, essenceless and weak. // Lal_13.97 //

children.text: saṃskāra nirīha śūnyakāḥ kadalīskandhasamā nirīkṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Conditioned things are inert and empty — like the trunk of a plantain tree, upon examination;

children.text: māyopama cittamohanā bālaullāpana ukta muṣṭivat // Lal_13.98 //
children.translated_text: like an illusion, they delude the mind — like the talk of fools, said to be [empty] like a fist. // Lal_13.98 //

children.text: hetūbhi ca pratyayebhi cā sarvasaṃskāragataṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: By causes and by conditions, everything in the realm of conditioned things proceeds;

children.text: anyonya pratītya hetutaḥ tadidaṃ bālajano na budhyate // Lal_13.99 //
children.translated_text: arising dependently from mutual causes — this the foolish do not understand. // Lal_13.99 //

body.text: yatha muñja pratītya balvajaṃ rajju vyāyāmabalena vartitā /
body.translated_text: Just as, depending on <s>muñja</s> grass and <s>balbaja</s> [reeds], a rope is turned by the effort of the hands,

body.text: ghaṭiyantra sacakra vartate eṣa ekaikaśa nāsti vartanā // Lal_13.100 //
body.translated_text: and the wheel-mechanism with its wheel turns — [yet] each one singly has no [independent] turning — // Lal_13.100 //

children.text: tatha sarvabhavāṅgavartinī anyamanyopacayena niśritā /
children.translated_text: so all the links of existence turn, depending on one another's accumulation;

children.text: ekaikaśa teṣu vartinī pūrvaparāntata nopalabhyate // Lal_13.101 //
children.translated_text: the turning of each singly among them is not found from beginning to end. // Lal_13.101 //

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīja sa caiva aṅkuro /
children.translated_text: Just as, when the seed exists, there is the sprout — yet that which is the seed is not itself the sprout,

children.text: na ca tato na caiva tat evamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā // Lal_13.102 //
children.translated_text: and [the sprout] is neither other than [the seed] nor identical with it — such is the nature of things: neither annihilation nor eternality. // Lal_13.102 //

children.text: saṃskāra avidyapratyayāḥ te saṃskāre na santi tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Formations are conditioned by ignorance — [yet] in those formations they do not truly exist;

children.text: saṃskāra avidya caiva hi śūnya eke prakṛtīnirīhakāḥ // Lal_13.103 //
children.translated_text: both formations and ignorance are empty, each inert by nature. // Lal_13.103 //

children.text: mudrātpratimudra dṛśyate mudrasaṃkrānti na copalabhyate /
children.translated_text: From a seal, a counter-impression is seen, yet no transference of the seal is found;

children.text: na ca tatra na caiva śāśvato eva saṃskārānucchedaśāśvatāḥ // Lal_13.104 //
children.translated_text: it is neither other [than the seal] nor eternal — so too, formations are neither annihilated nor eternal. // Lal_13.104 //

children.text: cakṣuśca pratītya rūpataḥ cakṣuvijñānamihopajāyate /
children.translated_text: Depending on the eye and on form, eye-consciousness arises here;

children.text: na ca cakṣuṣi rūpa niśrita rūpasaṃkrānti na caiva cakṣuṣi // Lal_13.105 //
children.translated_text: form does not reside in the eye, nor is there a transference of form into the eye. // Lal_13.105 //

children.text: nairātmyaśubhāśca dharmime punarātmeti śubhāśca kalpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: These phenomena are [in truth] selfless and impure, yet they are imagined as having a self and as pure;

children.text: viparītamasadvikalpitaṃ cakṣuvijñāna tatopajāyate // Lal_13.106 //
children.translated_text: being perverted, falsely imagined as [what they are] not — from that, eye-consciousness arises. // Lal_13.106 //

children.text: vijñānanirodhasaṃbhavaṃ vijñānotpādavyayaṃ vipaśyati /
children.translated_text: The yogin sees the arising and cessation of consciousness, the origination and decay of consciousness;

children.text: akahiṃ ca gataṃ anāgataṃ śūnya māyopama yogi paśyati // Lal_13.107 //
children.translated_text: gone nowhere, come from nowhere — the yogin sees [it as] empty, like an illusion. // Lal_13.107 //

children.text: araṇiṃ yatha cottarāraṇiṃ hastavyāyāma trayebhi saṃgati /
children.translated_text: Just as [with] the lower fire-stick and the upper fire-stick, through the conjunction of three — the effort of the hand —

children.text: iti pratyayato 'gni jāyate jātu kṛtārthu laghu nirudhyate // Lal_13.108 //
children.translated_text: fire is born from conditions, and having served its purpose, it quickly ceases. // Lal_13.108 //

children.text: atha paṇḍitu kaści mārgate kutayaṃ āgatu kutra yāti vā /
children.translated_text: Then a wise person may search: 'Whence did it come? Where does it go?'

children.text: vidiśo diśi sarvi mārgato nāgati nāsya gatiśca labhyate // Lal_13.109 //
children.translated_text: Searching in every quarter and direction, neither its coming nor its going is found. // Lal_13.109 //

children.text: skandhadhātvāyatanāni dhātavaḥ tṛṣṇa avidyā iti karmapratyayā /
children.translated_text: Aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — the constituents; craving, ignorance — the conditions of action;

children.text: sāmagri tu sattvasūcanā sa ca paramārthatu nopalabhyate // Lal_13.110 //
children.translated_text: their combination is the designation 'being' — but that [being] is not found in the ultimate sense. // Lal_13.110 //

children.text: kaṇṭhoṣṭha pratītya tālukaṃ jihvāparivarti akṣarā /
children.translated_text: Depending on the throat, lips, palate, and the turning of the tongue, syllables [arise];

children.text: na ca kaṇṭhagatā na tāluke akṣaraikaika tu nopalabhyate // Lal_13.111 //
children.translated_text: they are not in the throat, nor in the palate — each syllable singly is not found. // Lal_13.111 //

children.text: sāmagri pratītyataśca sā vācamanabuddhivaśena niścarī /
children.translated_text: Depending on the combination, speech issues forth through the power of mind and intellect;

children.text: mana vāca adṛśyarūpiṇī bāhyato 'bhyantara nopalabhyate // Lal_13.112 //
children.translated_text: mind and speech are of invisible form — they are found neither externally nor internally. // Lal_13.112 //

children.text: utpādavyayaṃ vipaśyato vāca rutaghoṣasvarasya paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise person who sees the arising and decay of speech, sound, tone, and voice

children.text: kṣaṇikāṃ vaśikāṃ tadā dṛśī sarvā vāca pratiśrutakopamām // Lal_13.113 //
children.translated_text: then sees all speech as momentary, subjugating — like an echo. // Lal_13.113 //

children.text: yatha tantri pratītya dārū ca hastavyāyāma trayebhi saṃgati /
children.translated_text: Just as, depending on strings and wood, through the conjunction of three — the effort of the hands —

children.text: tuṇavīṇasughoṣakādibhiḥ śabdo niścarate tadudbhavaḥ // Lal_13.114 //
children.translated_text: from flutes, <s>vīṇās</s>, and other sweet-sounding [instruments], sound issues forth, born from them. // Lal_13.114 //

body.text: atha paṇḍitu kaści mārgate kutayaṃ āgatu kutra yāti vā /
body.translated_text: Then a wise person may search: 'Whence did it come? Where does it go?'

body.text: vidiśo diśi sarvi mārgataḥ śabdagamanāgamanaṃ na labhyate // Lal_13.115 //
body.translated_text: Searching in every quarter and direction — the coming and going of sound is not found. // Lal_13.115 //

children.text: tatha hetubhi pratyayebhi ca sarvasaṃskāragataṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: So too, by causes and conditions, everything in the realm of conditioned things proceeds;

children.text: yogī puna bhūtadaśanāt śūnya saṃskāra nirīha paśyati // Lal_13.116 //
