children.translated_text: but the yogin, through seeing things as they are, sees formations as empty and inert. // Lal_13.116 //

children.text: skandhāyatanāni dhātavaḥ śūnya adhyātmika śūnya bāhyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Aggregates, sense-bases, and elements — empty internally, empty externally;

children.text: sattvātmaviviktamanālayā dharmākāśasvabhāvalakṣaṇāḥ // Lal_13.117 //
children.translated_text: devoid of a being or self, without abode — having the nature and characteristic of space. // Lal_13.117 //

children.text: iya īdṛśa dharmalakṣaṇā buddha dīpaṃkara darśane tvayā /
children.translated_text: This very nature of phenomena you awakened to in the presence of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>,

children.text: anubuddha svayaṃ yathātmanā tatha bodhehi sadevamānuṣāṃ // Lal_13.118 //
children.translated_text: [realizing it] yourself — now likewise awaken the world with its gods and humans! // Lal_13.118 //

children.text: viparītaabhūtakalpitaiḥ rāgadoṣaiḥ paridahyate jagat /
children.translated_text: By perverted, unreal imaginations, the world is burned by the fires of passion and fault;

children.text: kṛpameghasamāmbuśītalāṃ muñca dhārāmamṛtasya nāyakā // Lal_13.119 //
children.translated_text: release a shower of the deathless, cool as water from a cloud of compassion, O Leader! // Lal_13.119 //

children.text: tvayi yasya kṛtena paṇḍitā dattu dānaṃ bahukalpakoṭiṣu /
children.translated_text: For whose sake wise ones gave you charity over many koṭis of kalpas —

children.text: saṃprāpya hi bodhimuttamāṃ āryadhanasaṃgraha kariṣya prāṇinām // Lal_13.120 //
children.translated_text: having attained supreme awakening, gather the noble treasure for living beings! // Lal_13.120 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā nārya dhanahīna daridra duḥkhitām /
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice — [beings are] without noble treasure, destitute, impoverished, and suffering;

children.text: mā upekṣahi sattvasārathe āryadhanasaṃgrahi teṣu kurvahi // Lal_13.121 //
children.translated_text: do not disregard [them], O charioteer of beings — gather the noble treasure for them! // Lal_13.121 //

children.text: tvayi śīla sadā surakṣitaṃ pithanārthāya apāyabhūminām /
children.translated_text: In you, moral conduct was always well-guarded, for the purpose of closing off the lower realms;

children.text: svargāmṛtadvāramuttamāṃ darśayiṣye bahusattvakoṭinām // Lal_13.122 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall show the supreme gate of heaven and the deathless to many koṭis of beings.' // Lal_13.122 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā baddhvā dvāra nirayāya bhūminām /
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice — having closed the gate to the grounds of hell,

children.text: svargāmṛtadvāra muñcahī ṛddhyahi śīlavato vicintitam // Lal_13.123 //
children.translated_text: open the gate of heaven and the deathless! Fulfill the aspiration of the morally virtuous! // Lal_13.123 //

children.text: tvayi kṣānti sadā surakṣitā pratighakrodhaśamārtha dehinām /
children.translated_text: In you, patience was always well-guarded, for the sake of pacifying aversion and anger in beings;

children.text: bhāvārṇava sattva tāriyā sthāpayiṣye śivi kṣemi nirjvale // Lal_13.124 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall ferry beings across the ocean of existence and establish them in safety, peace, and freedom from fire.' // Lal_13.124 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā vairavyāpādavihiṃsaākulām /
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice — [the world is] overwhelmed by enmity, ill-will, and harmfulness;

children.text: mā upekṣa vihiṃsacāriṇaḥ kṣāntibhūmīya sthape imaṃ jagat // Lal_13.125 //
children.translated_text: do not disregard those who practice harmfulness — establish this world on the ground of patience! // Lal_13.125 //

children.text: tvayi vīrya yadartha sevitaṃ dharmanāvaṃ samudānayitvanā /
children.translated_text: In you, vigor was cultivated for the purpose of preparing the ship of Dharma;

children.text: uttārya jagadbhavārṇavāt thapayiṣye śivi kṣemi nirjvale // Lal_13.126 //
children.translated_text: 'Having ferried the world across the ocean of existence, I shall establish [them] in safety, peace, and freedom from fire.' // Lal_13.126 //

body.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā caturoghairiva muhyate jagat //
body.translated_text: Remember that former practice — the world is bewildered as if by the four floods;

body.text: laghu vīryabalaṃ parākramā sattva saṃtārayahī anāyakāṃ // Lal_13.127 //
body.translated_text: quickly exert the power of vigor and valor — ferry across the leaderless beings! // Lal_13.127 //

children.text: tvaya dhyānakileśadhyeṣaṇā bhāvitā yasya kṛtena sūratā /
children.translated_text: By you, meditation was cultivated for the purpose of seeking the destruction of afflictions, for the sake of those who are heroes [in practice];

children.text: bhrāntendriya prākṛtendriyāṃ kvapi cittāryapathe sthapeṣyaham // Lal_13.128 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall establish those with deluded and untrained faculties somewhere on the noble path of mind.' // Lal_13.128 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā kleśajālairihamākulaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: Remember that former practice — the world is entangled in the net of afflictions;

children.text: mā upekṣahi kleśupadrutāṃ dhyānaikāgri sthapehimāṃ prajām // Lal_13.129 //
children.translated_text: do not disregard those beset by afflictions — establish these beings in one-pointed meditation! // Lal_13.129 //

children.text: tvayi prajña purā subhāvitā mohavidyāndhatamovṛte jage /
children.translated_text: In you, wisdom was formerly well-cultivated — in a world enveloped by the darkness and blindness of delusion and ignorance,

children.text: bahudharmaśatābhilokane dāsye cakṣuṣi tattvadarśanam // Lal_13.130 //
children.translated_text: to behold many hundreds of <s>dharmas</s>, I shall give the eye of truth-seeing! // Lal_13.130 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvacarīmanusmarā mohavidyāndhatamovṛte jage /
children.translated_text: Remember that former conduct! In a world shrouded in the darkness and gloom of delusion and ignorance,

children.text: dadahī varaprajña suprabhā dharmacakṣuṃ vimalaṃ nirañjanam // Lal_13.131 //
children.translated_text: give, O one of supreme wisdom, the radiant, stainless, spotless eye of <s>dharma</s>! // Lal_13.131 //

children.text: iyamīdṛśa gātha niścarī tūryasaṃgītiravātu nāriṇām /
children.translated_text: Such verses as these issued forth from the instrumental music and songs of the women;

children.text: yaṃ śrutva middhaṃ vivarjiyā cittu preṣeti varāgrabodhaye // Lal_13.132 //
children.translated_text: hearing which, having cast off torpor, the mind is sent toward supreme, foremost awakening! // Lal_13.132 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'ntaḥpuramadhyagato bodhisattvo 'virahito 'bhūddharmaśravaṇena, avirahito 'bhūddharmamanasikāreṇa / takasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo dīrgharātraṃ sagauravo 'bhūt / dharmeṣu dharmabhāṇakeṣu cādhyāśayena dharmārthiko dharmakāmo dharmaratirato 'bhūt / dharmaparyeṣṭyatṛpto yathāśrutadharmasaṃprakāśakaḥ, anuttaro mahādharmadānapatiḥ, nirāmiṣadharmadeśako dharmadānenāmatsaraḥ, ācāryamuṣṭivigato dharmānudharmapratipanno dharmapratipattiśūraḥ, dharmalayano dharmatrāṇo dharmaśaraṇo dharmapratiśaraṇo dharmaparāyaṇaḥ dharmanidhyāptiḥ kṣāntiniryātaḥ prajñāpāramitācarita upāyakauśalyagatiṃ gataḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while dwelling in the midst of the inner palace, was never separated from hearing the <s>dharma</s>, was never separated from attending to the <s>dharma</s> in his mind. And for what reason? Because, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had long been reverential toward <s>dharmas</s> and toward teachers of <s>dharma</s>, with deep intention; he was desirous of <s>dharma</s>, longing for <s>dharma</s>, delighting in <s>dharma</s>; unsatisfied in seeking <s>dharma</s>, proclaiming whatever <s>dharma</s> he heard; the unsurpassed great master of the gift of <s>dharma</s>; a teacher of <s>dharma</s> without worldly motives, ungrudging in the gift of <s>dharma</s>; free from the teacher's closed fist, one who practiced <s>dharma</s> in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, a hero of <s>dharma</s>-practice; whose shelter was <s>dharma</s>, whose protection was <s>dharma</s>, whose refuge was <s>dharma</s>, who took recourse in <s>dharma</s>, whose goal was <s>dharma</s>; who had penetrated <s>dharma</s>, who had emerged through patience, who had practiced the perfection of wisdom, who had gone to the course of skill in means. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvo mahopāyakauśalyavikrīḍitena sarvāntaḥpurasya yathādhimuktyā īryāpathamupadarśya, paurvikāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ lokaviṣayasamatikrāntānāṃ lokānuvartanakriyādharmatāmanuvartya, dīrgharātraṃ suviditakāmadoṣaḥ sattvaparipākavaśādakāmātkāmopabhogaṃ saṃdarśya, aparimitakuśalamūlopacayapuṇyasaṃbhārabalaviśeṣaṇāsadṛśīṃ lokādhipateyatāṃ saṃdarśya, devamanuṣyātikrāntaṃ sārodāravividhavicitrarūpaśabdagandharasasparśaparamaratiramaṇīyaṃ kāmaratirasaukhyamupadarśya, sarvakāmaratisvaviṣayeṣvaparyantatvāt svacittavaśavartitāṃ saṃdarśya, pūrvapraṇidhānabalasahāyakuśalamūlopacitān sattvān samānasaṃvāsatayā paripācya, sarvalokasaṃkleśamalāsaṃkliṣṭacittatayāntaḥpuramadhyagato yathābhinimantritasya sattvadhātoḥ paripākakālamavekṣamāṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā bodhisattvastasmin samaye pūrvapratijñāmanusmarati sma, buddhadharmāṃścāmukhīkaroti sma, praṇidhānabalaṃ cābhinirharati sma / sattveṣu ca mahākaruṇāmavakrāmati sma / sattvapramokṣaṃ ca cintayati sma / sarvasaṃpado vipattiparyavasānā iti pratyavekṣate sma / anekopadravabhayabahulaṃ ca saṃsāramupaparīkṣate
body.translated_text: There, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the sport of great skill in means, displayed modes of conduct to the entire inner palace according to their dispositions; and following the conduct of former <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had transcended the domains of the world yet followed the practices of worldly convention, having long known the faults of sensual pleasures, and for the sake of maturing beings, reluctantly displayed the enjoyment of sensual pleasures; displaying the unrivaled lordship over the world through the excellence of his vast accumulation of wholesome roots and the power of his accumulation of merit; displaying the enjoyment of pleasure and delight in sensual happiness — supreme, delightful, varied, beautiful — in forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and touches surpassing gods and humans; displaying the subjection of all pleasures and sensory objects to his own will, since [they were] without limit; and having matured beings — who had been nurtured by the accumulation of wholesome roots with the aid of the power of his former vows — through dwelling together with them, with a mind unstained by the defilements and impurities of the entire world, while dwelling in the midst of the inner palace, looking for the time of maturation of the realm of beings who were, as it were, invited [to awakening] — all the more at that time did the <s>Bodhisattva</s> recollect his former vow, and made the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> manifest, and brought forth the power of his vow. And he brought great compassion to bear upon beings. And he contemplated the liberation of beings. He reflected: 'All acquisitions end in ruin.' And he examined <s>saṃsāra</s>, filled with manifold calamities and dangers

body.text: sma / mārakalipāśāṃśca saṃchinatti sma / saṃsāraprabandhāccātmānamuccārayati sma / nirvāṇe ca cittaṃ saṃpreṣayati sma //
body.translated_text: . He cut through the snares and fetters of <s>Māra</s>. He raised himself up from the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>. And he directed his mind toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pūrvāntata eva suviditasaṃsāradoṣaḥ saṃskṛtenādhyāśayenānarthikaḥ sarvopādānaparigrahairanarthiko buddhadharmanirvāṇābhimukhaḥ saṃsāraparāṅmukhastathāgatagocarābhirataḥ māraviṣayagocarāsaṃsṛṣṭaḥ ādīptabhavadoṣadarśī traidhātukānniḥśaraṇābhiprāyaḥ saṃsāradoṣādīnavaniḥsaraṇakuśalaḥ pravrajyābhilāṣī niṣkramaṇābhiprāyo vivekanimno vivekapravaṇo vivekaprāgbhāraḥ āraṇyaprāraṇyābhimukhaḥ pravivekapraśamābhikāṅkṣī ātmaparahitapratipannaḥ anuttarapratipattiśūro lokasyārthakāmo hitakāmaḥ sukhakāmo yogakṣemakāmo lokānukampako hitaiṣī maitrīvihārī mahākāruṇikaḥ saṃgrahavastukuśalaḥ satatasamitamaparikhinnamānasaḥ sattvaparipākavinayakuśalaḥ sarvasattveṣvekaputrakapremānugatamanasikāraḥ sarvavastunirapekṣaparityāgī dānasaṃvibhāgarataḥ prayuktatyāgaḥ prayatapāṇiḥ tyāgaśūro yaṣṭayajñaḥ susamṛddhapuṇyaḥ susaṃgṛhītapuṇyaḥ pariṣkāravigatamalāmātsaryasunigṛhītacitto 'nuttaro mahādānapatirdattvā ca vipākāpratikāṅkṣī pradānaśūraḥ icchāmahecchālobhadveṣamadamānamohamātsaryapramukhasarvārikleśagaṇapratyarthikanigrahāyābhyutthitaḥ sarvajñatācittotpādaprabandhāccalitaḥ mahātyāgacittasaṃnāhasusaṃnaddhaḥ lokānukampako hitaiṣīva varmitakavacitavīryaḥ sattvapramokṣālambanamahākaruṇābalavikramaparākramaḥ avaivartikasarvasattvasamacittatyāgapraharaṇo yathābhiprāyasattvāśayasaṃtoṣaṇo bodhibhājanībhūtaḥ kālākṣuṇṇadharmavedhī bodhipariṇāmapraṇidhiḥ anavanāmitadhvajastrimaṇḍalapariśodhanadānaparityāgī jñānavaravajradṛḍhapraharaṇaḥ sunigṛhītakleśapratyarthikaḥ śīlaguṇacāritrapratipannaḥ svārakṣitakāyavāṅbhanaskarmānto 'ṇumātrāvadyabhayadarśī supariśuddhaśīlaḥ amalavimalanirmalacittaḥ sarvaduruktadurāgatavacanapathākrośaparibhāṣaṇakutsanatāḍanatarjanavadhabandhanāvarodhanaparikleśāluḍitacitto 'kṣubhitacittaḥ kṣāntisaurabhyasaṃpannaḥ akṣato 'nupahato 'vyāpannacittaḥ sarvasattvahitārthāyottaptavīryārambhī dṛḍhasamādānasarvakuśalamūladharmasamudānayanāpratyudāvartyasmṛtimān susaṃprajñāsusamāhito 'vikṣiptacitto dhyānaikāgramanasikāro dharmapravicayakuśalo labdhāloko vigatatamondhakāraḥ anityaduḥkhātmāśubhākāraparibhāvitacetāḥ smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇaṛddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgārya satyasarvabodhipakṣadharmasuparikarmakṛtamanasikāraḥ śamathavipaśyanāsuparyavadātabuddhiḥ pratītyasamutpādasatyadarśī satyānubodhādaparapratyayastrivimokṣasukhavikrīḍito māyāmarīcisvapnodakacandrapratiśrutkāpratibhāsopamasarvadharmanayāvatīrṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: There, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who from the very beginning had well understood the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>, was, by his conditioned deep intention, without desire; without desire for all attachments and possessions; facing the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; turned away from <s>saṃsāra</s>; delighting in the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; unentangled with the domain of <s>Māra</s>; seeing the faults of the burning house [of existence]; intent on escape from the three realms; skilled in emerging from the faults and dangers of <s>saṃsāra</s>; desirous of renunciation; intent on going forth; inclined toward seclusion, leaning toward seclusion, directed toward seclusion; facing the forest wilderness; longing for the peace of solitude; pursuing the welfare of self and others; a hero of unsurpassed practice; desiring the welfare of the world, its benefit, its happiness, its security; compassionate toward the world; benevolent, abiding in friendliness, greatly compassionate; skilled in the means of attraction; with a mind ever unwearied; skilled in the discipline and maturation of beings; with a mind that followed the love of an only child toward all beings; one who relinquished all possessions without regard; delighting in generous distribution; devoted to generosity, with a ready hand; a hero of giving; offering worship and sacrifice; with merit well-established and well-gathered; with a mind well-restrained, free from the stain of miserliness, the unsurpassed great master of giving; and having given, without expectation of its result; a hero of offering; one who had arisen to subdue the host of adversarial afflictions headed by desire, great desire, greed, hatred, pride, arrogance, delusion, and miserliness; unfailing in his continuous generation of the mind of omniscience; well-armored with the armor of the mind of great renunciation; compassionate toward the world, benevolent, clad in the armor of vigor; of the power and valor of great compassion whose support was the liberation of beings; one whose weapon of equal-minded and irreversible renunciation was cast toward all beings; one who satisfied beings according to their intentions and dispositions; who had become a vessel of awakening; who pierced the <s>dharma</s> at its timely points; whose vow was the dedication toward awakening; whose banner was unfurled, whose giving and renunciation purified the three spheres; whose firm weapon was the supreme <s>vajra</s> of knowledge; who had well-restrained the adversary of the afflictions; who had practiced the path of morality, virtue, and conduct; whose deeds of body, speech, and mind were well-guarded; who saw danger even in the slightest fault; whose morality was supremely pure; whose mind was spotless, stainless, and immaculate; whose mind was undisturbed and unshaken by all abuse, ill-treatment, verbal assault, reproach, reviling, criticism, striking, threatening, killing, imprisonment, and affliction; endowed with the fragrance of patience; unhurt, uninjured, with mind unharmed; one who had undertaken ardent vigor for the benefit of all beings; with firm undertaking, one who brought together all wholesome root-<s>dharmas</s> without turning back; mindful, well-comprehending, well-concentrated, with undistracted mind; with one-pointed attention to meditation; skilled in the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>; having attained illumination, free from darkness and obscuration; with a mind cultivated in the aspects of impermanence, suffering, self, and the unattractive; with a mind well-prepared in the practice of the establishments of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, the path, the noble truths, and all factors conducive to awakening; with understanding well-purified through calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>); a seer of the truth of dependent origination; not dependent on others for the awakening to truth; sporting in the bliss of the three liberations; one who had entered the approach of all <s>dharmas</s> as being like illusion, a mirage, a dream, the reflection of the moon in water, an echo, and a reflection. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaivaṃ bhavati pratikṛtiḥ - evaṃ dharmavihārī evaṃ guṇamāhātmyavihārī evaṃ sattvārthābhiyuktavihārī abhūt / bhūyasyā mātrayā ābhirdaśadigbuddhādhiṣṭhānatūryasaṃgītiviniḥsṛtābhirgāthābhiḥ saṃcoditaḥ sa tasyāṃ velāyāṃ pūrveṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ caramabhavopagatānāmantaḥpuraparipācitāni
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, such was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s manner — such was his abiding in <s>dharma</s>, such was his abiding in the greatness of virtues, such was his abiding devoted to the welfare of beings. All the more was he exhorted by these verses that issued forth from the musical exhortations empowered by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions, and on that occasion he made manifest the four <s>dharma</s>-gates that had been matured in the inner palace by former <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had reached their final birth

body.text: catvāri dharmamukhānyāmukhīkaroti sma / katamāni catvāri? yadidaṃ dānaṃ priyavacanamarthakriyāṃ samānārthatāṃ ca / catuḥsaṃgrahavastuprayoganirhāraviśuddhiṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma / triratnavaṃśasādhāraṇābhiprāyo vipraṇāśasarvajñatācittapraṇidhānabalādhānāvaivartyaviṣayaṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma / sarvasattvāparityāgādhyāśayamahākaruṇāvatāratāṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma / sarvabodhipakṣadharmapade prabhedārthābhiniścayajñānasaṃsārabalaviśeṣasamudānayamahāvyūhaṃ ca nāma dharmamukhamāmukhīkaroti sma / imāni catvāri dharmamukhānyāmukhīkṛtya bodhisattvaḥ sarvasyāntaḥpurasya paripācanārthaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisaṃskaroti sma, yathārūpeṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena tebhyaḥ saṃgītirutebhyo bodhisattvānubhāvenemānyevaṃrūpāṇi dharmamukhaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma / tadyathā -
body.translated_text: . What were the four? Namely: giving, kind speech, beneficial action, and impartiality. He made manifest the <s>dharma</s>-gate called 'the purification of the practice and accomplishment of the four means of attraction.' He made manifest the <s>dharma</s>-gate called 'the domain of irreversibility through the power of the vow of omniscient mind, [sharing] the common purpose of the lineage of the Three Jewels and [its] non-destruction.' He made manifest the <s>dharma</s>-gate called 'the entry into great compassion with the deep intention of never abandoning any being.' He made manifest the <s>dharma</s>-gate called 'the great array of accomplishing the special powers of <s>saṃsāra</s> through the knowledge of definitive meaning in the analysis of the factors of all <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening.' Having made manifest these four <s>dharma</s>-gates, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of maturing the entire inner palace, at that time performed such a miraculous transformation that, by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, from those musical sounds there issued forth hundreds of thousands of <s>dharma</s>-gates of this kind. Namely:

children.text: udārachandena ca āśayena adhyāśayenā karuṇāya prāṇiṣu /
children.translated_text: Through noble intention, deep resolve, superior intention, and compassion for beings,

children.text: utpadyate cittu varāgrabodhaye śabde ca rūpasturiyebhi niścarī // Lal_13.133 //
children.translated_text: the mind arises toward supreme, foremost awakening — this sound issues forth from the forms and instruments! // Lal_13.133 //

children.text: śraddhā prasādo adhimukti gauravaṃ nirmānatā onamanā gurūṇām /
children.translated_text: Faith, serene confidence, conviction, reverence, freedom from pride, humility toward teachers,

children.text: paripṛcchanā kiṃkuśalaṃgaveṣaṇā anusmṛtībhāvanu śabda niścarī // Lal_13.134 //
children.translated_text: inquiry, seeking what is wholesome, recollection and cultivation — this sound issues forth! // Lal_13.134 //

children.text: dāne dabhe saṃyamaśīlaśabdaḥ kṣāntīya śabdastatha vīryaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sound of giving, self-restraint, discipline, and morality; the sound of patience; likewise the sound of vigor;

children.text: dhyānābhinirhārasamādhiśabdaḥ prajñā upāyasya ca śabda niścarī // Lal_13.135 //
children.translated_text: the sound of meditation, accomplishment, and concentration; the sound of wisdom and of skillful means issues forth! // Lal_13.135 //

children.text: maitrāya śabdaḥ karuṇāya śabdo muditāupekṣāya abhijñaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sound of friendliness, the sound of compassion, the sound of joy and equanimity and superknowledge;

children.text: catusaṃgrahāvastuviniścayena sattvāna paripācanaśabda niścarī // Lal_13.136 //
children.translated_text: through the definitive understanding of the four means of attraction — the sound of maturing beings issues forth! // Lal_13.136 //

children.text: smṛterupasthānaprabhedaśabdaḥ samyakprahāṇāstatha ṛddhipādā /
children.translated_text: The sound of the analysis of the establishments of mindfulness; the right exertions and the bases of supernatural power;

children.text: pañcedriyā pañcabalaprabhedā bodhyaṅgaśabdasturiyebhi niścarī // Lal_13.137 //
children.translated_text: the five faculties and the five powers in their divisions — the sound of the factors of awakening issues forth from the instruments! // Lal_13.137 //

children.text: aṣṭāṅgiko mārgabalaprabhedaḥ śamathasya śabdo 'tha vipaśyanāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The eightfold path in its divisions of power; the sound of calm abiding and of insight;

children.text: anityaduḥkhārtianātmaśabdaḥ aśubhārtiśabdo turiyebhi niścarī // Lal_13.138 //
children.translated_text: the sound of impermanence, suffering-affliction, and non-self; the sound of the unattractive and affliction issues forth from the instruments! // Lal_13.138 //

children.text: virāgaśabdaśca vivekaśabdaḥ kṣayajñānaśabdo anutpādaśabdaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sound of dispassion and the sound of seclusion; the sound of the knowledge of destruction and the sound of non-arising;

children.text: anirodhaśabdaśca anālayaṃ ca nirvāṇaśabdasturiyebhi niścarī // Lal_13.139 //
children.translated_text: the sound of non-cessation and of non-attachment; the sound of <s>nirvāṇa</s> issues forth from the instruments! // Lal_13.139 //

children.text: ima evarūpāsturiyebhi śabdāḥ saṃbodhiśabdaścanubhāva niścarī /
children.translated_text: Such sounds as these issue forth from the instruments, and the sound of awakening issues forth by [his] power;

children.text: yaṃ śrutva sarvā pramadā nu śikṣitā varāgrasattve praṇidhenti bodhaye // Lal_13.140 //
children.translated_text: hearing which, all the women were well-instructed, and they aspired to awakening toward the supreme, foremost being! // Lal_13.140 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo antaḥpuramadhyagatena bodhisattvena tāni caturaśītistrīsahasrāṇi paripācitānyabhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bahūni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi ye tatra saṃprāptā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in the midst of the inner palace, those eighty-four thousand women were matured toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, as well as many hundreds of thousands of divinities who had assembled there. //

body.text:
tathā abhiniṣkramaṇakāle tasmin samaye bodhisattvasya hrīdevo nāma tuṣitakāyiko devaputro 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ sa rātrau praśāntāyāṃ dvātriṃśatā devaputrasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhisattvasyopasthānaprāsādastenopasaṃkrāmat /
upasaṃkramya gaganatalagata eva bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, at the time of the great going forth, at that time a <s>Devaputra</s> of the <s>Tuṣita</s> host named <s>Hrīdeva</s>, [who had urged] the unsurpassed perfect awakening, in the quiet of the night, surrounded and preceded by thirty-two thousand <s>Devaputras</s>, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s attendant's palace. Having approached, standing in the sky, he addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in verses:

children.text: cyuti darśitā atiyaśā janma ca saṃdarśitaṃ puruṣasiṃha /
children.translated_text: You have displayed the descent, O one of surpassing glory, and you have displayed the birth, O lion among men!

children.text: antaḥpuraṃ vidarśitu kṛtānuvṛttistvayā loke // Lal_13.141 //
children.translated_text: You have displayed the inner palace life, acting in conformity with the world. // Lal_13.141 //

children.text: paripācitā ti bahavo deva manuja loki dharmamanuprāpya /
children.translated_text: You have matured many gods and humans in the world, having attained <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: ayamadya kālasamayo niṣkramye mati vicintehi // Lal_13.142 //
children.translated_text: now is the proper time — contemplate the resolve for the going forth! // Lal_13.142 //

children.text: na hi baddha mocayātī na cāndhapuruṣena darśiyati mārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: A bound one does not liberate [others]; nor is the path shown by a blind man;

children.text: muktastu mocayātī sacakṣuṣā darśayati mārgaḥ // Lal_13.143 //
children.translated_text: but a free one liberates, and one with eyes shows the path! // Lal_13.143 //

children.text: ye sattva kāmadāsā gṛhe dhane putrabhāryapariśraddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings who are slaves to desire, at home, devoted to wealth, sons, and wives —

children.text: te tubhya śiṣyamāṇā naiṣkramyamatau spṛhāṃ kuryuḥ // Lal_13.144 //
children.translated_text: being instructed by you, they would desire the resolve of renunciation! // Lal_13.144 //

children.text: aiśvarya kāmakrīḍā catudvīpā sapta ratna vijahitvā /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned sovereignty, sensual pleasures, the four continents, and the seven jewels,

children.text: niṣkrānta tvāṃ viditvā spṛhayetsanarāmaro lokaḥ // Lal_13.145 //
children.translated_text: knowing that you have gone forth, the world with its gods and humans would aspire [to follow]! // Lal_13.145 //

children.text: kiṃ cāpi dhyānasaukhyairviharasi dharmairna cāsi kāmarataḥ /
children.translated_text: Even now you dwell in the happiness of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>dharmas</s>, and you do not delight in sensual pleasures;

children.text: atha puna ciraprasuptāṃ bodhaya marumānuṣaśatāni // Lal_13.146 //
children.translated_text: Now awaken the hundreds of <s>Māra</s>'s [hosts] and humans who have long been asleep! // Lal_13.146 //

children.text: atipatita yauvanamidaṃ girinadi yatha cañcalapracalavegā /
children.translated_text: This youth has passed like a mountain stream, swift and unsteady in its rushing force;

children.text: gatayauvanasya bhavato naiṣkramyamatirna śobhete // Lal_13.147 //
children.translated_text: for one whose youth has departed, the intention to renounce does not shine [as brightly]! // Lal_13.147 //

children.text: tatsādhu taruṇarūpe prathame varayāvane 'bhiniṣkramya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, well in [your] youthful form, in the prime of the supreme vehicle, go forth!

children.text: uttāraya pratijñāṃ kuruṣva cārthaṃ suragaṇānām // Lal_13.148 //
children.translated_text: Fulfill [your] promise and accomplish the purpose of the hosts of gods! // Lal_13.148 //

children.text: na ca kāmaguṇaratībhistṛptirlavaṇodadheryathāmbhobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no satisfaction from pleasures of the senses, as there is none from the waters of the salt ocean;

children.text: te tṛpta yeṣa prajñā āryā lokottarā virajā // Lal_13.149 //
children.translated_text: those are [truly] satisfied who possess the noble, supramundane, stainless wisdom! // Lal_13.149 //

children.text: tvamiha priyo manāpo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya rāṣṭrasya /
children.translated_text: You here are dear and pleasing to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and [his] kingdom;

children.text: śatapatrasadṛśavadanā naiṣkramyamatiṃ vicintehi // Lal_13.150 //
children.translated_text: O lotus-faced one, contemplate the intention to renounce! // Lal_13.150 //

children.text: ādīpta kleśatāpairaniḥśaraṇairgāḍhabandhanairbaddhāṃ /
children.translated_text: Beings burning with the heat of afflictions, without refuge, bound by tight bonds —

children.text: śīghraṃ pramokṣamārge sthāpaya śānte asamavīrā // Lal_13.151 //
children.translated_text: swiftly establish them on the path of liberation, in peace, O incomparable hero! // Lal_13.151 //

children.text: tvaṃ vaidya dhātukuśalaścirāturāṃ sattvarogasaṃspṛṣṭāṃ /
children.translated_text: You are a physician, skilled in the elements; beings long sick, afflicted with the disease of [existence] —

children.text: bhaiṣajyadharmayogairnirvāṇasukhe sthapaya śīghram // Lal_13.152 //
children.translated_text: with the remedies of the <s>dharma</s>, establish them swiftly in the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s>! // Lal_13.152 //

children.text: andhātamā anayanā mohākuladṛṣṭijālabaddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Blinded, in darkness, without eyes, bewildered, bound by the net of [wrong] views —

children.text: prajñāpradīpacakṣuḥ śodhaya śīghraṃ naramarūṇām // Lal_13.153 //
children.translated_text: with the lamp of wisdom, swiftly purify the eyes of humans and gods! // Lal_13.153 //

children.text: samudīkṣante bahavo devāsuranāgayakṣagandharvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> gaze expectantly:

children.text: drakṣyāma bodhiprāptaṃ niruttaraṃ dharma śroṣyāmaḥ // Lal_13.154 //
children.translated_text: 'We shall see [him] having attained <s>bodhi</s>! We shall hear the unsurpassed <s>dharma</s>!' // Lal_13.154 //

children.text: drakṣyati ca bhujagarājo bhavanaṃ avabhāsitaṃ tava śirīye /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Nāga</s> king shall see his dwelling illuminated by your glory;

children.text: kariyati anantapūjā pūrehi vratāśayastasya // Lal_13.155 //
children.translated_text: he shall make infinite worship — fulfill the aspirations of his vows! // Lal_13.155 //

children.text: catvāri lokapālāḥ sasainyakāste tava pradīkṣante /
children.translated_text: The four <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians) with their armies await you;

children.text: dāsyāma caturi pātrāṃ bodhidhvaji pūrṇamanasasya // Lal_13.156 //
children.translated_text: 'We shall offer the four bowls to the one whose banner is <s>bodhi</s>, whose mind is full [of compassion]!' // Lal_13.156 //

children.text: brahma praśāntacārī udīkṣate maitravākvaruṇalābhī /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> of peaceful conduct awaits, having attained kindly and gentle speech;

children.text: adhyoṣiṣye narendraṃ vartenti niruttaraṃ cakram // Lal_13.157 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall invite the Lord of Men — [may he] turn the unsurpassed wheel [of <s>dharma</s>]!' // Lal_13.157 //

children.text: bodhiparipācikāpi ca devata abhivusta bodhimaṇḍesmiṃ /
children.translated_text: And the deity who ripens <s>bodhi</s>, established at this <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening),

children.text: utpatsye 'yaṃ satya ti drakṣyāmyabhibudhyato bodhim // Lal_13.158 //
children.translated_text: [says]: 'This one shall truly arise!' — 'I shall behold his awakening to <s>bodhi</s>!' // Lal_13.158 //

children.text: satyaṃ hi bodhisattvā antaḥpuriye kriyā vidarśenti /
children.translated_text: Truly, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> display their activities in the inner palace;

children.text: pūrvaṃgamo bhava tvaṃ mā bheṣyasi paścimasteṣām // Lal_13.159 //
children.translated_text: be you the forerunner! Do not be the last among them! // Lal_13.159 //

children.text: mañjuruta mañjughoṣā smarāhi dīpaṃkarasya vyākaraṇam /
children.translated_text: O one of sweet voice and melodious speech, remember the prophecy of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>!

children.text: bhūtaṃ tathā avitathā jinaghoṣarutaṃ udīrehi // Lal_13.160 //
children.translated_text: It is true, not false — proclaim the sound of the <s>Jina</s>'s (Victor's) voice! // Lal_13.160 //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare saṃcodanāparivarto nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the thirteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Exhortation' (<s>Saṃcodanāparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 14
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 14.

body.text: svapnaparivartaścaturdaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Fourteenth Chapter: On Dreams (<s>Svapnaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ saṃcoditaḥ san tena devaputreṇa rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyemaṃ svapnamupadarśayati sma - yadrājā śuddhodanaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragato 'drākṣīt bodhisattvaṃ rātrau praśāntāyāmabhiniṣkramantaṃ devagaṇaparivṛtam / abhiniṣkramya pravrajitaṃ cādrākṣīt kāṣāyavastraprāvṛtam / sa pratibuddhaḥ tvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ kāñcukīyaṃ paripṛcchati sma - kaccit kumāro 'ntaḥpure 'sti? so 'vocat - asti deveti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having been exhorted by that <s>devaputra</s>, showed this dream to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> — namely, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having fallen asleep and entered a dream, saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> going forth in the stillness of the night, surrounded by hosts of gods. He saw him, having gone forth, as a renunciant clad in saffron robes. He, having awoken, quickly and anxiously asked the chamberlain: 'Is the prince still in the inner palace?' He replied: 'He is, O lord.' //

body.text: tato rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāntaḥpure śokaśalyo hṛdaye 'nupraviṣṭo 'bhūt - abhiniṣkramiṣyati avaśyaṃ kumāro 'yam / yaccemāni pūrvanimittāni saṃdṛśyante sma //
body.translated_text: Then in King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s heart, within the inner palace, a dart of grief entered: 'This prince will certainly go forth! For these portents have been seen!' //

body.text: tasyaidabhavat - na khalvavyayaṃ kumāreṇa kadācidudyānabhūmimabhinirgantavyam / strīgaṇamadhye 'bhirataḥ ihaiva ramyate, nābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: This thought occurred to him: 'Under no circumstances shall the prince ever go out to the garden grounds. Let him delight, surrounded by the company of women, enjoying himself right here — then he will not go forth!' //

body.text: tato rājñā śuddhodanena kumārasya paribhogārthaṃ trayo yathartukāḥ prāsādāḥ kāritā abhūvan graiṣmiko vārṣiko haimantikaśca / tatra yo graiṣmikaḥ sa ekāntaśītalaḥ / yo vārṣikaḥ sa sādhāraṇaḥ / yo haimantikaḥ sa svabhāvoṣṇaḥ / ekaikasya ca prāsādasya sopānāni pañca pañca puruṣaśatānyutkṣipanti sma, nikṣipanti sma / teṣāṃ tathotkṣipyamāṇānāṃ nikṣipyamāṇānāṃ ca śabdo 'rdhayojane śrūyate sma - mā khalu kumāro 'nabhijñāta evābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti / naimittikairvaipañcikaiśca vyākṛtamabhūt - maṅgaladvāreṇa kumāro 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti / tato rājā maṅgaladvārasya mahānti kapāṭāni kārayati sma / ekaikaṃ ca kapāṭaṃ pañca pañca puruṣaśatānyuddhāṭayanti sma, apaghāṭayanti sma / teṣāṃ cārdhayojanaṃ śabdo gacchati sma / pañca cāsya kāmaguṇān sadṛśānupasaṃharati sma / gītavāditanṛtyaiścainaṃ sadaiva yuvataya upatasthuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had three seasonal palaces built for the prince's enjoyment — one for summer, one for the rains, and one for winter. The summer palace was entirely cool. The rainy-season one was temperate. The winter one was naturally warm. The stairs of each palace were raised and lowered by five hundred men each. And when they were thus raised and lowered, the sound was heard for half a <s>yojana</s> — [thinking:] 'Lest the prince go forth undetected!' And the soothsayers and astrologers had declared: 'The prince will go forth through the Auspicious Gate.' Therefore the king had great doors made for the Auspicious Gate. Each door required five hundred men to open and close it. And its sound carried for half a <s>yojana</s>. He gathered the five strands of sensual pleasure [for the prince]. Young women attended him constantly with song, music, and dance. //

body.text: atha bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ sārathiṃ prāha - śīghraṃ sārathe rathaṃ yojaya / udyānabhūmiṃ gamiṣyāmīti / tataḥ sārathī rājānaṃ śuddhoddhanamupasaṃkramyaivamāha - deva kumāra udyānabhūmimabhiniryāsyatīti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to the charioteer: 'Quickly, charioteer, harness the chariot! I shall go to the garden grounds.' Then the charioteer approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and said: 'O lord, the prince wishes to go forth to the garden grounds.' //

body.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyaitadabhavat - na kadācinmayā kumāra udyānabhūmimabhiniṣkramitaḥ / subhūmidarśanāya / yannvahaṃ kumāramudyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāmayeyam / tataḥ kumāraḥ strīgaṇaparivṛto ratiṃ vetsyate, nābhiniṣkramiṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'The prince has never once gone out to the garden grounds. Let me send the prince to the garden grounds for [him to see] the beauty of the land. Then the prince, surrounded by the company of women, will find pleasure and will not go forth!' //

body.text: tato rājā śuddhodanaḥ snehabahumānābhyāṃ bodhisattvasya nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇāṃ kārayati sma saptame divase kumāra udyānabhūmiṃ niṣkramiṣyatīti (subhūmidarśanāya) / tatra bhavadbhiḥ sarvāmanāpāni cāpanayitavyāni - mā kumāraḥ pratikūlaṃ paśyet / sarvamanāpāni copasaṃhartavyāni viṣayābhiramyāṇi //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, out of affection and respect, had a bell-proclamation made throughout the city for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'On the seventh day, the prince will go forth to the garden grounds [to see the beauty of the land]. You must all remove all unpleasant things — lest the prince see anything disagreeable. And all pleasant and sense-delighting things must be arranged!' //

body.text: tataḥ saptame divase sarvaṃ nagaramalaṃkṛtamabhūt udyānabhūmimupaśobhitaṃ nānāraṅgadūṣyavitānīkṛtaṃ chatradhvajapatākāsamalaṃkṛtam / yena ca mārgeṇa bodhisattvo 'bhinirgacchati sma, sa mārgaḥ siktaḥ saṃmṛṣṭo gandhodakapariṣikto muktakusumāvakīrṇo nānāgandhaghaṭikānirdhūpitaḥ pūrṇakumbhopaśobhitaḥ kadalīvṛkṣocchrito nānāvicitrapaṭavitānavitato ratnakiṅkiṇījālahārārdhahārābhipralambito 'bhūt / caturaṅgasainyavyūhitaḥ parivāraścodyukto 'bhūt kumārasyāntaḥpuraṃ pratimaṇḍayitum / atha śuddhāvāsakāyikā devā nidhyāpayanti sma bodhisattvamāharitum, tatra bodhisattvasya pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāmato mahatā vyūhena atha bodhisattvasyānubhāvena śuddhavāsakāyikairdevaputraistasmin mārge puruṣo jīrṇo vṛddho mahallako dhamanīsaṃtatagātraḥ khaṇḍadanto valīnicitakāyaḥ palitakeśaḥ kubjo gopānasīvakro vibhagno daṇḍaparāyaṇa āturo gatayauvanaḥ kharakharāvasaktakaṇṭhaḥ prāgbhāreṇa kāyena daṇḍamavaṣṭabhya pravepayamānaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgaiḥ purato mārgasyopadarśito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then on the seventh day, the entire city was adorned and the garden grounds were beautified — hung with various colored silken canopies, decorated with parasols, banners, and pennants. The road along which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> would go forth was sprinkled, swept, perfumed with scented water, strewn with loose flowers, fumigated with various fragrance-pots, beautified with full vases, planted with plantain trees, stretched with various colorful cloth canopies, hung with nets of jeweled bells, necklaces, and half-necklaces. The four-fold army was arrayed, and the entourage was deployed to adorn the prince's inner quarters. Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) gods caused the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to be brought forth. There, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was going forth through the eastern city-gate to the garden grounds with a great procession, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika devaputras</s> displayed on that road, before [him], a man — decrepit, old, aged, his body covered with veins, broken-toothed, his body wrinkled, grey-haired, hunched, bent like a roof-rafter, broken, dependent on a staff, infirm, past his youth, with a harsh rattling in his throat, his body leaning forward, trembling in all his limbs and members, walking supported on a staff. //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though already knowing, said to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa durbala alpasthāmo ucchuṣkamāṃsarudhiratvacasnāyunaddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is this, charioteer? A man, weak and of little strength, his flesh, blood, skin, and sinews dried up,

children.text: śvetaṃśiro viraladanta kṛśāṅgarūpo ālambya daṇḍa vrajate asukhaṃ skhalantaḥ // Lal_14.1 //
children.translated_text: white-haired, sparse-toothed, emaciated in form — walking supported on a staff, unhappily stumbling?' // Lal_14.1 //

body.text: sārathirāha -
body.translated_text: The charioteer replied:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo jarayābhibhūtaḥ kṣīṇendriyaḥ sudukhito balavīryahīnaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This, O lord, is a man overcome by old age, with faculties declined, greatly suffering, bereft of strength and vigor,

children.text: bandhūjanena paribhūta anāthabhūtaḥ kāryāsamartha apaviddhu vaneva dāru // Lal_14.2 //
children.translated_text: despised by his relatives, become helpless, incapable of action — cast aside like a log of wood in the forest!' // Lal_14.2 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kuladharma eṣa ayamasya hitaṃ bhaṇāhi athavāpi sarvajagato 'sya iyaṃ hyavasthā /
children.translated_text: 'Tell me — is this the nature of his family alone, or is this indeed the condition of the entire world?

children.text: śīghraṃ bhaṇāhi vacanaṃ yathabhūtametat śrutvā tathārthamiha yoniśa cintayiṣye // Lal_14.3 //
children.translated_text: Speak quickly, tell the truth as it is! Hearing it, I shall reflect on this matter wisely!' // Lal_14.3 //

body.text: sārathirāha -
body.translated_text: The charioteer replied:

children.text: naitasya deva kuladharma na rāṣṭradharmaḥ sarve jagasya jara yauvanu dharṣayāti /
children.translated_text: 'This is not, O lord, his family's nature nor his country's custom; old age overwhelms the youth of all the world!

children.text: tubhyaṃ pi mātṛpitṛbāndhavajñātisaṃgho jarayā amukta na hi anya gatirjanasya // Lal_14.4 //
children.translated_text: For you too, and for your assembly of mother, father, relatives, and kinsmen — from old age there is no escape; there is no other destiny for people!' // Lal_14.4 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: dhiksārathe abudha bālajanasya buddhiḥ yadyauvanena madamatta jarāṃ na paśyet /
children.translated_text: 'Shame, O charioteer, on the understanding of ignorant, foolish people, who, intoxicated with youth, do not see old age!

children.text: āvartayāśu mi rathaṃ punarahaṃ pravekṣye kiṃ mahya krīḍaratibhirjarayāśritasya // Lal_14.5 //
children.translated_text: Turn back my chariot at once! I shall go back again. What use are sports and pleasures for one subject to old age?' // Lal_14.5 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ pratinirvatya rathavaraṃ punarapi puraṃ prāviśat //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, turning back the excellent chariot, entered the city again. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'pareṇa kālasamayena dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkraman mahatā vyūhena so 'drākṣīnmārge puruṣaṃ vyādhispṛṣṭaṃ dagdhodarābhibhūtaṃ durbalakāyaṃ svake mūtrapurīṣe nimagnamatrāṇamapratiśaraṇaṃ kṛcchreṇocchvasantaṃ praśvasantam / dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on another occasion, going forth through the southern city-gate to the garden grounds with a great procession, saw on the road a man afflicted with disease — overcome by burning in his belly, with a feeble body, submerged in his own urine and excrement, without protection, without refuge, breathing in and out with great difficulty. Having seen [him], the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though already knowing, said to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa ruṣyavivarṇagātraḥ sarvendriyebhi vikalo guru praśvasantaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What is this, charioteer? A man with a changed and discolored body, impaired in all his faculties, breathing heavily,

children.text: sarvāṅgaśuṣka udarākula kṛcchraprāpto mūtre purīṣi svaki tiṣṭhati kutsanīye // Lal_14.6 //
children.translated_text: dried up in all his limbs, his belly distressed, in dire straits — lying in his own urine and excrement, loathsome?' // Lal_14.6 //

body.text: sārathirāha -
body.translated_text: The charioteer replied:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo paramaṃ gilāno vyādhībhayaṃ upagato maraṇāntaprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This, O lord, is a man extremely ill; the fear of disease has come upon him, he has reached the brink of death,

children.text: ārogyatejarahito balaviprahīno atrāṇadvīpaśaraṇo hyaparāyaṇaśca // Lal_14.7 //
children.translated_text: bereft of the vigor of health, deprived of strength — without protection, island, or refuge, and without recourse!' // Lal_14.7 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: ārogyatā ca bhavate yatha svapnakrīḍā vyādhībhayaṃ ca imamīdṛśu ghorarūpam /
children.translated_text: 'Good health is but a dream at play, and the fear of disease is of such terrible form!

children.text: ko nāma vijñapuruṣo ima dṛṣṭvavasthāṃ krīḍāratiṃ ca janayecchubhasaṃjñatāṃ vā // Lal_14.8 //
children.translated_text: What wise person, having seen this condition, would generate delight in play or a perception of auspiciousness?' // Lal_14.8 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya rathavaraṃ punarapi puravaraṃ prāvikṣat //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, turning back the excellent chariot, entered the excellent city again. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'pareṇa kālasamayena paścimena nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkraman mahatā vyūhena so 'drākṣīt puruṣaṃ mṛtaṃ kālagataṃ mañce samāropitaṃ cailavitānīkṛtaṃ jñātisaṃghaparivṛtaṃ sarvai rudadbhiḥ krandadbhiḥ paridevamānaiḥ prakīrṇakeśaiḥ pāṃśvavakīrṇaśirobhirurāṃsi tāḍayadbhirutkrośadbhiḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchadbhiḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on another occasion, going forth through the western city-gate to the garden grounds with a great procession, saw a dead man — deceased, mounted on a bier, covered with a cloth canopy, surrounded by the assembly of relatives — all weeping, crying, lamenting, with disheveled hair, casting dust upon their heads, beating their chests, wailing, following behind. Having seen [him], the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though already knowing, said to the charioteer:

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa mañcapari gṛhīto uddhūtakeśanakha pāṃśu śire kṣipanti /
children.translated_text: 'What is this, charioteer? A man borne on a bier, [while others] with loosened hair and nails cast dust on their heads,

children.text: paricārayitva viharantyurastāḍayanto nānāvilāpavacanāni udīrayantaḥ // Lal_14.9 //
children.translated_text: attending him they go about beating their chests, uttering various words of lamentation?' // Lal_14.9 //

body.text: sārathirāha -
body.translated_text: The charioteer replied:

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo mṛtu jambudvīpe nahi bhūyu mātṛpitṛ drakṣyati putradārāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'This, O lord, is a man who has died here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; he shall never again see mother, father, sons, or wife;

children.text: apahāya bhogagṛha (mātṛpitṛ) mitrajñātisaṃghaṃ paralokaprāptu na hi drakṣyati bhūyu jñātīṃ // Lal_14.10 //
children.translated_text: leaving behind wealth, home, mother, father, friends, and the assembly of kinsmen, he has gone to the next world — he shall never again see his relatives!' // Lal_14.10 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: dhigyauvanena jarayā samabhidrutena ārogya dhigvividhavyādhiparāhatena /
children.translated_text: 'Shame on youth, assailed by old age! Shame on health, struck down by manifold disease!

children.text: dhigjīvitena viduṣā nacirasthitena dhikpaṇḍitasya puruṣasya ratiprasaṅgaiḥ // Lal_14.11 //
children.translated_text: Shame on life, [which is] not long-lasting for the wise! Shame on the wise man's attachment to pleasures!' // Lal_14.11 //

children.text: yadi jara na bhaveyā naiva vyādhirna mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: If there were no old age, nor disease, nor death,

children.text: tathapi ca mahaduḥkhaṃ pañcaskandhaṃ dharanto /
children.translated_text: Yet bearing the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), which are great suffering —

children.text: kiṃ puna jaravyādhirmṛtyu nityānubaddhāḥ
children.translated_text: how much more [so when] old age, disease, and death are ever in pursuit!

children.text: sādhu pratinivartyā cintayiṣye pramokṣam // Lal_14.12 //
children.translated_text: It is good to turn back — I shall contemplate liberation. // Lal_14.12 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya taṃ rathavaraṃ punarapi puraṃ prāvikṣat //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned back that excellent chariot, once again entered the city. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyāpareṇa kālasamayenottareṇa nagaradvāreṇodyānabhūmimabhiniṣkrāmatastaireva devaputrairbodhisattvasyānubhāvenaiva tasminmārge bhikṣurabhinirmito 'bhūt / adrākṣīdbodhisattvastaṃ bhikṣuṃ śāntaṃ dāntaṃ saṃyataṃ brahmacāriṇamavikṣiptacakṣuṣaṃ yugamātraprekṣiṇaṃ prāsādikenairyāpathena saṃpannaṃ prāsādikenābhikramapratikrameṇa saṃpannaṃ prāsādikenāvalokitavyavalokitena prāsādikena samiñjitaprasāritena prāsādikena saṃghāṭīpātracīvaradhāraṇena mārge sthitam / dṛṣṭvā ca punarbodhisattvo jānanneva sārathimidamavocat -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, at a later time, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was going out through the northern city gate toward the park, by those very <s>devaputras</s> and by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own power, a monk was manifested on that road. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw that monk — tranquil, restrained, controlled, a celibate (<s>brahmacārin</s>), with unscattered gaze, looking only a yoke's length ahead, endowed with a serene deportment, endowed with serene approaching and departing, endowed with serene looking forward and looking around, serene in bending and stretching, serene in wearing his patchwork robe, bowl, and robes — standing on the road. Having seen him, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though knowing [already], said this to the charioteer —

children.text: kiṃ sārathe puruṣa śāntapraśāntacitto notkṣiptacakṣu vrajate yugamātradarśī /
children.translated_text: Who is this man, O charioteer, of peaceful, supremely tranquil mind, who walks without raised gaze, looking only a yoke's length ahead?

children.text: kāṣāyavastravasano supraśāntacārī pātraṃ gṛhītva na ca uddhatu unnato vā // Lal_14.13 //
children.translated_text: Clad in saffron robes, of supremely peaceful conduct, carrying a bowl — neither agitated nor haughty? // Lal_14.13 //

body.text: sārathirāha -
body.translated_text: The charioteer said —

children.text: eṣo hi deva puruṣo iti bhikṣunāmā apahāya kāmaratayaḥ suvinītacārī /
children.translated_text: This, O lord, is a person called a '<s>bhikṣu</s>' (monk) — having abandoned the delights of sensual pleasures, of well-disciplined conduct,

children.text: pravajyaprāptu śamamātmana eṣamāṇo saṃrāgadveṣavigato 'nveti piṇḍacaryā // Lal_14.14 //
children.translated_text: having attained the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), seeking tranquility for himself, free from passion and hatred, he follows the alms-round (<s>piṇḍacaryā</s>). // Lal_14.14 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: sādhū subhāṣitamidaṃ mama rocate ca pravrajya nāma vidubhiḥ satataṃ praśastā /
children.translated_text: Excellent! Well-spoken is this, and it pleases me. The going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) is always praised by the wise.

children.text: hitamātmanaśca parasattvahitaṃ ca yatra sukhajīvitaṃ sumadhuraṃ amṛtaṃ phalaṃ ca // Lal_14.15 //
children.translated_text: Where there is benefit for oneself and benefit for other beings — a happy life, supremely sweet, with the deathless as its fruit! // Lal_14.15 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratinivartya taṃ rathavaraṃ punarapi puravaraṃ prāvikṣat //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having turned back that excellent chariot, once again entered the foremost city. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodano bodhisattvasyemāmevaṃrūpāṃ saṃcodanāṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca bhūyasyā mātrayā bodhisattvasya parirakṣaṇārthaṃ prākārān māpayate sma, parikhāḥ khānayati sma, dvārāṇi ca gāḍhāni kārayati sma / ārakṣān sthāpayati sma / śūrāṃścodayati sma / vāhanāni yojayati sma / varmāṇi grāhayati sma / caturṣu nagaradvāraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu caturo mahāsenāvyūhān sthāpayati sma bodhisattvasya parirakṣaṇārtham / ya enaṃ rātriṃdivaṃ rakṣanti sma - mā bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti / antaḥpure cājñāṃ dadāti sma - mā sma kadācitsaṃgītiṃ vicchetsyatha / sarvaratikrīḍāścopasaṃhartavyāḥ, strīmāyāścopadarśayata, nirbandhata kumāraṃ yathānuraktacitto na nirgacchetpravrajyāyai //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having seen and heard this kind of urging of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, to an even greater degree, for the purpose of guarding the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, had ramparts constructed, had moats dug, had gates made strong, posted guards, mustered warriors, yoked chariots, had armor taken up, and at the four city-gate intersections stationed four great army formations for the purpose of guarding the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — [all of these] to guard him day and night: 'Let the <s>Bodhisattva</s> not go forth!' And in the inner palace he gave the command: 'Never let the music be interrupted! And all amusements and recreations are to be arranged; display your feminine wiles; bind the prince so that, with his mind attached, he will not depart for the going-forth!' //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Hereupon this was said —

children.text: dvāre sthāpita yuddhaśauṇḍapuruṣāḥ khaḍgāyudhāpāṇayo
children.translated_text: At the gates were posted men fierce in battle, with swords and weapons in their hands,

children.text: hastīaśvarathāśca varmitanarā ārūḍha nāgāvalī /
children.translated_text: elephants, horses, chariots, and armored men, rows of elephants mounted;

children.text: parikhā khoṭakatoraṇāśca mahatā prākāra ucchrāpitā
children.translated_text: moats, drawbridges, and arched gateways, and a great rampart raised high,

children.text: dvārā baddha sugāḍhabandhanakṛtāḥ krośasvarāmuñcanāḥ // Lal_14.16 //
children.translated_text: gates bound with strong fastenings, emitting the sound of a <s>krośa</s>. // Lal_14.16 //

children.text: sarve śākyagaṇā viṣaṇṇamanaso rakṣanti rātriṃdivaṃ
children.translated_text: All the <s>Śākya</s> assembly, their minds anxious, guard [him] day and night;

children.text: nirghoṣaśca balasya tasya mahataḥ śabdo mahā śrūyate /
children.translated_text: and the loud clamor of that great army is heard.

children.text: nagaraṃ vyākulu bhītatrastamanaso mā smād vrajetsūrato
children.translated_text: 'Let the city be vigilant, the people fearful and on alert — may the hero not depart!

children.text: mā bhūcchākyakuloditasya gamane chidyeta vaṃśo hyayam // Lal_14.17 //
children.translated_text: May it not be that, by the departure of this scion of the <s>Śākya</s> lineage, this dynasty shall be cut off!' // Lal_14.17 //

body.text:
ājñapto yuvatījanaśca satataṃ saṃgīti mā chetsyathā
vasthānaṃ prakarotha krīḍaratibhirnirbandhathā mānasam /
body.translated_text: The company of young women was commanded: 'Never let the music cease! Make yourselves established with amusements and recreations — bind his mind!

body.text: ye vā istriyamāya nekavividhā darśetha ceṣṭāṃ bahuṃ
body.translated_text: Whatever manifold feminine wiles and stratagems exist — display them!

body.text: ārakṣāṃ prakarotha vighna kuruthā mā khu vrajetsūrataḥ // Lal_14.18 //
body.translated_text: Set up guards, create obstacles — may the hero not depart!' // Lal_14.18 //

children.text: tasyā niṣkramikāli sārathivare pūrve nimittā ime
children.translated_text: At the time of his going forth, these were the omens for the foremost charioteer:

children.text: haṃsā kroñca mayūra sārika śukā no te ravaṃ muñciṣu /
children.translated_text: the swans, cranes, peacocks, <s>sārikā</s>-birds, and parrots released no sounds.

children.text: prāsādeṣu gavākṣatoraṇavareṣvātālamañceṣu ca
children.translated_text: In the palaces, at the lattice-windows, arched gateways, platforms, and couches,

children.text: jihmājihva sudurmanā asukhitā dhyāyantyadhomūrdhakāḥ // Lal_14.19 //
children.translated_text: [all were] silent, dejected, ill-at-ease, brooding, with downcast heads. // Lal_14.19 //

children.text: puḍinīpuṣkariṇīṣu padma rucirā mlānāni mlāyanti ca
children.translated_text: In the lily-ponds and lotus-pools, the beautiful lotuses were wilted and fading;

children.text: vṛkṣāḥ śuṣkapalāśa puṣparahitāḥ puṣpanti bhūyo na ca /
children.translated_text: the trees, with dried leaves, bereft of flowers, did not bloom again.

children.text: vīṇāvallakivaṃśatantriracitā chidyantyakasmāttadā
children.translated_text: The <s>vīṇās</s>, lutes, flutes, and stringed instruments broke of their own accord;

children.text: bherīścaiva mṛdaṅga pāṇyabhihatā bhidyanti no vādyiṣu // Lal_14.20 //
children.translated_text: and the drums and <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, though struck with the hand, would not sound. // Lal_14.20 //

children.text: sarvaṃ vyākulamāsi tacca nagaraṃ nidrābhibhūtaṃ bhṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: The entire city was in turmoil, deeply overcome by sleep;

children.text: no nṛtte na ca gāyite na ramite bhūyo manaḥ kasyacit /
children.translated_text: no one's mind was any longer in dancing, singing, or rejoicing.

children.text: rājāpī paramaṃ sudīnamanasaḥ cintāparo dhyāyate
children.translated_text: Even the king, of supremely dejected mind, sat absorbed in anxious thought:

children.text: hā dhikśākyakulasya ṛddhi vipulā mā haiva saṃdhakṣyate // Lal_14.21 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas for the <s>Śākya</s> lineage! May this vast prosperity not be consumed [by flames]!' // Lal_14.21 //

children.text: ekasmiṃ śayane sthite sthitamabhūdgopā tathā pārthivo
children.translated_text: Upon one bed lay <s>Gopā</s>, and there lay the prince.

children.text: gopā rātriyi ardharātrasamaye svapnānimāṃ paśyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Gopā</s>, in the night, at the hour of midnight, saw these dreams:

children.text: sarveyaṃ pṛthivī prakampitamabhūcchailā sakūṭāvaṭī
children.translated_text: The entire earth trembled and shook; mountains with their peaks and hollows

children.text: vṛkṣā mārutaeritā kṣiti patī utpāṭya mūloddhṛtāḥ // Lal_14.22 //
children.translated_text: and trees tossed by the wind fell to the ground, uprooted. // Lal_14.22 //

children.text: candrāsūrya nabhātu bhūmipatitau sajyotiṣālaṃkṛtau
children.translated_text: The moon and sun fell from the sky to the ground, together with their luminous ornaments;

children.text: keśānadṛśi lūna dakṣiṇi bhuje mukuṭaṃ ca vidhvaṃsitam /
children.translated_text: she saw her hair shorn on the right arm, and her crown shattered.

children.text: hastau chinna tathaiva chinna caraṇau nagnā dṛśī ātmanaṃ
children.translated_text: Her hands were severed, and likewise her feet severed; she saw herself naked.

children.text: muktāhāra tathaiva mekhalamaṇī chinnā dṛśī ātmanaḥ // Lal_14.23 //
children.translated_text: The pearl necklace and likewise the girdle-jewels were severed — she saw [it all]. // Lal_14.23 //

children.text: śayanasyā dṛśi chinna pāda caturo dharaṇītalesmiṃ chayī
children.translated_text: She saw the four legs of the bed broken, lying upon the ground;

children.text: chatre daṇḍu sucitru śrīma ruciraṃ chinnā dṛśī pārthive /
children.translated_text: the staff of the parasol — beautifully variegated, splendid, and lovely — she saw broken, O prince.

children.text: sarve ābharaṇā vikīrṇa patitā muhyanti te vāriṇā
children.translated_text: All the ornaments were scattered and fallen, carried away by the waters;

children.text: bhartuścābharaṇā savastramukuṭā śayyāgatā vyākulā // Lal_14.24 //
children.translated_text: and the husband's ornaments, garments, and crown lay upon the bed, disordered. // Lal_14.24 //

body.text:
ulkāṃ paśyati niṣkramanta nagarāttamasābhibhūtaṃ puraṃ
chinnāṃ jālikamadṛśāti supine ratanāmikāṃ śobhanāṃ /
body.translated_text: She saw a torch departing from the city, the city overcome by darkness; she saw the beautiful jeweled net severed in her dream.

body.text: muktāhāru pralambamānu patitaḥ kṣubhito mahāsāgaraṃ
body.translated_text: The hanging pearl necklace fell; the great ocean was agitated.

body.text: meruṃ parvatarājamadṛśi tadā sthānātu saṃkampitam // Lal_14.25 //
body.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, she saw at that time trembling from its base. // Lal_14.25 //

children.text: etānīdṛśa śākyakanya supināṃ supināntare adṛśī
children.translated_text: Such dreams as these did the <s>Śākya</s> maiden see in her sleep;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā sā pratibuddha ruṇṇanayanā svaṃ svāminaṃ abravīt /
children.translated_text: having seen [them], she awoke with tearful eyes and said to her lord:

children.text: devā kiṃ mi bhaviṣyate khalu bhaṇā supināntarāṇīdṛśā
children.translated_text: 'O lord, what will become of me? Tell me — with such dreams!

children.text: bhrāntā me smṛti no ca paśyami punaḥ śokārditaṃ me manaḥ // Lal_14.26 //
children.translated_text: My awareness is confused, and I cannot see [clearly] — my mind is tormented by grief.' // Lal_14.26 //

children.text: śrutvāsau kalaviṅkadundubhiruto brahmasvaraḥ susvaro
children.translated_text: Having heard [her], he of the voice like a <s>kalaviṅka</s>-bird, like a <s>dundubhi</s>-drum, like <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice, of sweet tone, [said]:

children.text: gopāmālapate bhava pramuditā pāpaṃ na te vidyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Gopā</s>, my beloved, be joyful! There is no evil for you.

children.text: ye sattvā kṛtapuṇyapūrvacaritā teṣeti svapnā
children.translated_text: Those beings who have performed meritorious deeds in former lives — theirs are such dreams.

children.text: ime ko 'nyaḥ paśyati naikaduḥkhavihitaḥ svapnāntarāṇīdṛśā // Lal_14.27 //
children.translated_text: Who else, beset by many sufferings, sees such dreams? // Lal_14.27 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā medinī kampamānā kūṭā śailā medinīye patantā /
children.translated_text: That you saw the earth trembling, the mountain peaks falling to the earth —

children.text: devā nāgā rākṣasā bhūtasaṃghāḥ sarve tubhyaṃ pūjyaśreṣṭhāṃ karonti // Lal_14.28 //
children.translated_text: gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and hosts of <s>Bhūtas</s> shall all render the highest worship to you! // Lal_14.28 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā vṛkṣamūloddhṛtāni keśāṃ lūnāṃ dakṣiṇenādṛśāsi /
children.translated_text: That you saw trees uprooted, your hair shorn on the right [arm] —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśajālaṃ chinitvā dṛṣṭījālaṃ uddharī saṃskṛtātaḥ // Lal_14.29 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, having cut through the net of afflictions, [I] shall pull out the net of [wrong] views from the conditioned! // Lal_14.29 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭau candrasūryau patantau dṛṣṭā nakṣatrā jyotiṣā nīpatantaḥ /
children.translated_text: That you saw the moon and sun falling, the stars and luminaries plummeting —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśaśatrū nihatvā pūjyā loke bhāvinī tvaṃ praśasyā // Lal_14.30 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, having slain the enemy of afflictions, you shall be worshipped in the world, honored and praised! // Lal_14.30 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā muktahāraṃ viśīrṇaṃ nagnaṃ bhagnaṃ sarvakāyādṛśāsi /
children.translated_text: That you saw the pearl necklace shattered, [yourself] naked, broken, your whole body [so] seen —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope istrikāyaṃ jahitvā puruṣastvaṃ vai bheṣyase nocireṇa // Lal_14.31 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, having abandoned the female body, you shall become a man before long! // Lal_14.31 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭaṃ mañcakaṃ chinnapādaṃ chatre daṇḍaṃ ratnacitraṃ prabhagnam /
children.translated_text: That you saw the bed with its legs broken, the parasol-staff variegated with jewels shattered —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope ogha catvāri tīrtvā māṃ draṣṭāsī ekachatraṃ triloke // Lal_14.32 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, having crossed the four floods (<s>ogha</s>), you shall see me as the single sovereign of the three worlds! // Lal_14.32 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā bhūṣaṇā uhyamānā cūḍā vastrā mahya mañce 'dṛśāsi /
children.translated_text: That you saw the ornaments being carried away, the crown and garments upon my bed —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope lakṣaṇairbhūṣitāṅgaṃ māṃ saṃpaśyī sarvalokaiḥ stuvantam // Lal_14.33 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, you shall behold me with limbs adorned by the [auspicious] marks, praised by all the worlds! // Lal_14.33 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭā dīpakoṭīśatāni nagarānniṣkrāntā tatpuraṃ cāndhakāram /
children.translated_text: That you saw hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of lamps departing from the city, and that city in darkness —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope mohavidyāndhakāre prajñāloke kurvamī sarvalokam // Lal_14.34 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, in the darkness of delusion and ignorance, I shall make all the world [bright] with the light of wisdom! // Lal_14.34 //

children.text: yatte dṛṣṭaṃ muktahāraṃ prabhagnaṃ chinnaṃ caiva svarṇasūtraṃ vicitram /
children.translated_text: That you saw the pearl necklace broken, the variegated golden thread severed —

children.text: kṣipraṃ gope kleśajālaṃ chinitvā saṃjñā sūtraṃ uddharī saṃskṛtātaḥ // Lal_14.35 //
children.translated_text: swiftly, O <s>Gopā</s>, having cut through the net of afflictions, [I] shall pull out the thread of perception (<s>saṃjñā-sūtra</s>) from the conditioned! // Lal_14.35 //

children.text: yatte gope cittikāraṃ karoṣī nityaṃ pūjāṃ gauraveṇottamena /
children.translated_text: That you, O <s>Gopā</s>, have shown me reverence, always worshipping with the highest respect —

children.text: nāstī tubhyaṃ durgatī naiva śokaḥ kṣipraṃ bhohī prītiprāmodyalabdhā // Lal_14.36 //
children.translated_text: there is no evil destiny for you, nor grief. Swiftly you shall attain joy and gladness! // Lal_14.36 //

children.text: pūrve mahyaṃ dānu dattaṃ praṇītaṃ śīlaṃ cīrṇaṃ bhāvitā nityakṣānti /
children.translated_text: Formerly, excellent giving was given by me; morality was practiced, patience was cultivated constantly.

children.text: tasmānmahyaṃ ye prasādaṃ labhante sarve bhontī prītiprāmodyalābhāḥ // Lal_14.37 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who gain faith in me — all of them shall gain joy and gladness! // Lal_14.37 //

children.text: kalpā koṭī saṃskṛtā me anantā bodhīmārgo śodhito me praṇītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Countless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> have been prepared by me; the path to awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>) has been purified by me, supreme.

children.text: tasmānmahyaṃ ye prasādaṃ karonti sarve chinnā teṣu trīṇyapyapāyāḥ // Lal_14.38 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, those who pay reverence to me — for all of them the three lower realms are cut off! // Lal_14.38 //

children.text: harṣaṃ vindā mā ca khedaṃ janehi tuṣṭiṃ vindā saṃjanehī ca prītim /
children.translated_text: Find joy! Do not generate sorrow! Find contentment! Generate gladness!

children.text: kṣipraṃ bheṣye prītiprāmodyalābhī sehī gope bhadrakā te nimittā // Lal_14.39 //
children.translated_text: Swiftly I shall become one who has gained joy and gladness — endure, O <s>Gopā</s>; auspicious are your omens! // Lal_14.39 //

body.text: so puṇyatejabharito siritejagarbho pūrve nimittasupine imi adṛśāsi /
body.translated_text: That one, filled with the splendor of merit, radiance, and glory — these former dreams of auspicious, beautiful vows were seen in his sleep,

body.text: ye bhonti pūrvaśubhakarmasamuccayānāṃ naiṣkramyakālasamaye narapuṃgavānām // Lal_14.40 //
body.translated_text: which occur at the time of going forth for those bulls among men who have accumulated past wholesome deeds. // Lal_14.40 //

children.text: so adṛśāsi ca karāccaraṇāddhatānā mahasāgarebhi catubhirjala lolayantā /
children.translated_text: He was seen [in a dream] — his hands and feet agitating the waters of the four great oceans,

children.text: sarvāmimāṃ vasumatīṃ śayanaṃ vicitraṃ meruṃ ca parvatavaraṃ śirasopadhānam // Lal_14.41 //
children.translated_text: this entire earth [spread as] a variegated bed, and <s>Meru</s>, the supreme mountain, as his pillow. // Lal_14.41 //

children.text: ābhā pramukta supine tada adṛśāsi loke vilokitu mahātamasāndhakāram /
children.translated_text: A radiance was released [in the dream] — he was seen illuminating the great darkness of the world;

children.text: chatrodgataṃ dharaṇiye spharate trilokaṃ ābhāya spṛṣṭa vinipātadukhā praśāntā // Lal_14.42 //
children.translated_text: a parasol arose from the earth and pervaded the three worlds — by that radiance touched, the suffering of the lower realms was pacified. // Lal_14.42 //

children.text: kṛṣṇā śubhā caturi prāṇaka pāda lekhī catuvarṇa etva śakunādbhuta ekavarṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: A dark, auspicious animal with four legs [and] feet marked — of four colors, [yet] those wondrous birds of one color;

children.text: mīḍhaṃgirī paramahīna jugupsanīyā abhibhūya caṃkramati tatra ca nopalipto // Lal_14.43 //
children.translated_text: a heap of filth, supremely low and loathsome — [yet] he walked upon it and was not stained. // Lal_14.43 //

children.text: bhūyo 'dṛśī supini nadya jalaprapūrṇā bahusattvakoṭinayutāni ca uhyamānā /
children.translated_text: Again [she] saw in the dream a river full of water, with many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of beings carried away;

children.text: so nāva kṛtva prataritva parāṃ pratārya sthāpeti so sthalavare abhaye aśoke // Lal_14.44 //
children.translated_text: he, having made a boat, having crossed over and ferrying [them] to the far shore, established them on the firm ground — safe and sorrowless. // Lal_14.44 //

children.text: bhūyo 'dṛśāti bahu ātura rogaspṛṣṭāṃ ārogyatejarahitāṃ balaviprahīnāṃ /
children.translated_text: Again [she] saw many sick and diseased, deprived of health, splendor, and strength;

children.text: so vaidya bhūtva bahu oṣadha saṃprayacchā moceti sattvanayutāṃ bahurogaspṛṣṭāṃ // Lal_14.45 //
children.translated_text: he, having become a physician, gave them many medicines and freed <s>nayutas</s> of beings afflicted by many diseases. // Lal_14.45 //

children.text: siṃhāsane va hi niṣaṇṇa sumerupṛṣṭhe śiṣyāṃ kṛtāñjalipuṭānamarānnamantāṃ /
children.translated_text: Seated on a lion-throne upon the peak of <s>Meru</s>, with his disciples, palms joined, and the immortals bowing —

children.text: saṃgrāmamadhyi jayu adṛśi ātmanaśca ānandaśabdamamarāṃ gagane bruvantaḥ // Lal_14.46 //
children.translated_text: victory in the midst of battle she saw for him, and the immortals uttering sounds of joy in the sky. // Lal_14.46 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā supini adṛśi bodhisattvo maṅgalya śobhanavratasya ca pāripūrim /
children.translated_text: Such dreams the <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw — the fulfillment of auspicious, beautiful vows.

children.text: yāṃ śrutva devamanujā abhavanprahṛṣṭā na cirādbhaviṣyati ayaṃ naradevadevaḥ // Lal_14.47 //
children.translated_text: Having heard [of them], gods and humans were delighted: 'Before long, this one shall become the god of gods among men!' // Lal_14.47 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare svapnaparivarto nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Dreams' (<s>Svapnaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 15
body.translated_text: [START Chapter 15]

body.text: abhiniṣkramaṇaparivartaḥ pañcadaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Fifteenth Chapter: On the Going Forth (<s>Abhiniṣkramaṇaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - ayuktametanmama syādakṛtajñatā ca yadahamaprativedya mahārājñaḥ śuddhodanasya ananujñātaśca pitrā niṣkrameyam / sa rātrau praśāntāyāṃ svakādupasthānaprāsādādavatīrya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya prāsādatale pratiṣṭhito 'bhūt / pratiṣṭhitamātrasya ca punarbodhisattvasya sarvo 'sau prāsāda ābhayā sphuṭo 'bhūt / tatra rājā prativibuddhastāṃ prabhāmadrākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca punastvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ kāñcukiyamāmantrayāmāsa - kiṃ bhoḥ kāñcukīya sūryo 'bhyudgato yeneyaṃ prabhā virājate? kāñcukīya āha - adyāpi tāvadeva rajanyā upārdhaṃ nātikrāntam / api ca deva -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'It would be improper of me and an act of ingratitude if I were to go forth without informing the great King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and without receiving my father's permission.' In the stillness of the night, having descended from his own attendant's palace, he stationed himself at the base of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s palace. The moment the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stationed himself there, that entire palace was pervaded by radiance. There the king, having awakened, saw that radiance. And having seen it, he quickly, quickly addressed the chamberlain: 'What is this, chamberlain — has the sun risen, that this radiance shines?' The chamberlain said: 'Even now, not even the first half of the night has passed. But, O lord —

children.text: sūryaprabhāya bhavate drumakuḍyachāyā saṃtāpayāti ca tanuṃ prakaroti dharmam /
children.translated_text: 'Where the sun's radiance falls, there are shadows of trees and walls; it heats the body and produces sweat.

children.text: haṃsā mayūraśukakokilacakravākāḥ pratyūṣakālasamaye svarutāṃ ravanti // Lal_15.1 //
children.translated_text: Swans, peacocks, parrots, cuckoos, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds sing their calls at the time of dawn. // Lal_15.1 //

children.text: ābhā iyaṃ tu naradeva sukhā manojñā prahlādanī śubhakarī na karoti dāham /
children.translated_text: But this radiance, O lord of men, is pleasant, delightful, refreshing, auspicious, and does not burn.

children.text: kuḍyā ca vṛkṣa abhibhūya na cāsti chāyā niḥsaṃśayaṃ guṇadharo iha adya prāptaḥ // Lal_15.2 //
children.translated_text: It pervades walls and trees, and there are no shadows — without doubt, one endowed with virtues has arrived here today!' // Lal_15.2 //

children.text: so prekṣate daśadiśo nṛpatī viṣaṇṇo dṛṣṭaśca so kamalalocana śuddhasattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king, dismayed, gazes in the ten directions — and he saw that lotus-eyed one of pure being.

children.text: so 'bhyutthituṃ śayani icchati na prabhoti pitṛgauravaṃ janayate varaśuddhabuddhiḥ // Lal_15.3 //
children.translated_text: He wishes to rise from the bed but is unable — that one of supremely pure intellect generates reverence for his father. // Lal_15.3 //

children.text: so ca sthihitva purato nṛpatiṃ avocat mā bhūyu vighna prakarohi ma caiva khedam /
children.translated_text: Standing before [him], he said to the king: 'Do not make obstacles any longer, nor [cause] grief.

children.text: naiṣkramyakālasamayo mama deva yukto hanta kṣamasva nṛpate sajanaḥ sarāṣṭraḥ // Lal_15.4 //
children.translated_text: The time and moment for my going forth is fitting, O lord — have patience, O king, with your people and your kingdom!' // Lal_15.4 //

children.text: taṃ aśrupūrṇanayano nṛpatī babhāṣe kiṃcitprayojanu bhavedvinivartane te /
children.translated_text: The king, his eyes filled with tears, spoke: 'Is there anything at all that would cause you to turn back?

children.text: kiṃ yācase mama varaṃ vada sarva dāsye anugṛhṇa rājakulu māṃ ca idaṃ ca rāṣṭram // Lal_15.5 //
children.translated_text: What boon do you ask? Speak — I shall give all! Show grace to the royal family, to me, and to this kingdom!' // Lal_15.5 //

children.text: tada bodhisattva avacī madhurapralāpī icchāmi deva caturo vara tān mi dehi /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, speaking sweetly, said: 'I wish, O lord, for four boons — give them to me!

children.text: yadi śakyase daditu mahya vase ti tatra tad drakṣyase sada gṛhe na ca niṣkramiṣye // Lal_15.6 //
children.translated_text: If you are able to give them and they remain in [your] power, then you shall always see [me] at home, and I shall not go forth. // Lal_15.6 //

children.text: icchāmi deva jara mahya na ākrameyyā
children.translated_text: I wish, O lord, that old age would not assail me,

children.text: śubhavarṇa yauvanasthito bhavi nityakālam /
children.translated_text: that I may remain forever in my prime, with beautiful complexion and youth;

children.text: ārogyaprāptu bhavi no ca bhaveta vyādhiḥ
children.translated_text: that I may attain [perpetual] health and that disease would not arise;

children.text: amitāyuṣaśca bhavi no ca bhaveta mṛtyuḥ (saṃpattitaśca vipulā nu bhavedvipattiḥ) // Lal_15.7 //
children.translated_text: and that I may be of immeasurable lifespan and that death would not occur (and that vast prosperity would not [turn to] misfortune)! // Lal_15.7 //

children.text: rājā śruṇitva vacanaṃ paramaṃ dukhārto asthānu yācasi kumāra na me 'tra śaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: The king, having heard [these] words, greatly distressed, [said:] 'You ask for what is unattainable, O prince — this is not within my power!

children.text: jaravyādhimṛtyubhayataśca vipattitaśca kalpasthitīya ṛṣayo 'pi na jātu muktāḥ // Lal_15.8 //
