children.translated_text: From old age, disease, death, fear, and misfortune — even the sages, [though they endure] for the duration of a <s>kalpa</s>, are never freed!' // Lal_15.8 //

children.text: yadidāni deva caturo vara no dadāsi jaravyādhimṛtyubhayataśca vipattitaśca /
children.translated_text: 'If you cannot give [me] these four boons, O lord — freedom from old age, disease, death, fear, and misfortune —

children.text: hanta śṛṇuṣva nṛpate aparaṃ varaikaṃ asmāccyutasya pratisaṃdhi na me bhaveyā // Lal_15.9 //
children.translated_text: then listen, O king, to one other boon: that upon departing from this [life], I may have no further rebirth!' // Lal_15.9 //

children.text: śrutvaiva cema vacanaṃ narapuṃgavasya tṛṣṇā tanuṃ ca kari chindati putrasneham /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of the bull among men, [the king's] craving for the body was cut, as was his son's affection:

children.text: anumodamī hitakarā jagati pramokṣaṃ abhiprāyu tubhya paripūryatu yanmataṃ te // Lal_15.10 //
children.translated_text: 'I approve — you bring benefit to the world and liberation! May your intention and aspiration be fulfilled!' // Lal_15.10 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ pratikramya svake prāsāde 'bhiruhya śayane niṣasāda / na cāsya kaścidgamanaṃ vā āgamanaṃ vā saṃjānīte sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having taken his leave, ascended his own palace and sat upon his couch. And no one perceived his going or coming. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo rājā śuddhodanastasyā rātryā atyayena sarvaṃ śākyagaṇaṃ saṃnipātyaināṃ prakṛtimārocayati sma - abhiniṣkramiṣyati kumāraḥ / tatkiṃ kariṣyāmaḥ? śākyā āhuḥ - rakṣāṃ deva kariṣyāmaḥ / tatkasmāt? ayaṃ ca mahāñśākyagaṇaḥ, sa caikākī / tatkā tasya śaktirasti balādabhiniṣkramitum?
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, after the passing of that night, assembled the entire <s>Śākya</s> clan and reported this matter: 'The prince will go forth! What shall we do?' The <s>Śākyas</s> said: 'We shall set a guard, O lord! And why? This great <s>Śākya</s> clan is many, and he is alone. What power does he have to go forth by force?'

body.text: tatra taiḥ śākyai rājñā śuddhodanena ca pañca śākyakumāraśatāni kṛtāstrāṇi kṛtayogyāni iṣvastraśikṣitāni mahānagnabalopetāni pūrve nagaradvāre sthāpitānyabhūvan bodhisattvasya rakṣaṇārtham / ekaikaśca śākyakumāraḥ pañcarathaśataparivāraḥ, ekaikaṃ ca rathaṃ pañcapattiśataparivāraṃ sthāpitamabhūt
body.translated_text: There, by those <s>Śākyas</s> and King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths — skilled in arms, trained, instructed in the bow and weapons, endowed with great naked strength — were posted at the eastern city gate for the protection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Each <s>Śākya</s> youth was accompanied by five hundred chariots, and each chariot was accompanied by five hundred foot-soldiers, posted

body.text: bodhisattvasya rakṣaṇārtham / evaṃ dakṣiṇe paścime uttare nagaradvāre pañca pañca śākyakumāraśatāni kṛtāstrāṇi kṛtayogyāni iṣvastraśikṣitāni mahānagnabalopetāni / ekaikaśca śākyakumāraḥ pañcarathaśataparivāraḥ, ekaikaṃ ca rathaṃ pañcapattiśataparivāraṃ sthāpitamabhūta bodhisattvasya rakṣārtham / mahallakamahallikāśca śākyāḥ sarvacatvaraśṛṅgāṭakapūgarathyāsvārakṣārthaṃ sthitā abhavan / rājā ca śuddhodanaḥ pañcabhiḥ śākyakumāraśataiḥ sārdhaṃ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ svake gṛhadvāre hayeṣu ca gajeṣu ca samabhiruhya jāgarti sma / mahāprajāpatī ca gotamī ceṭīvargamāmantrayate sma -
body.translated_text: for the protection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Likewise, at the southern, western, and northern city gates, five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths each — skilled in arms, trained, instructed in the bow and weapons, endowed with great naked strength. Each <s>Śākya</s> youth accompanied by five hundred chariots, and each chariot accompanied by five hundred foot-soldiers, were posted for the protection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The elder <s>Śākya</s> men and women stood in all the squares, crossroads, market-halls, and carriage-ways for the purpose of guarding. And King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, surrounded and attended by five hundred <s>Śākya</s> youths, having mounted upon horses and elephants at his own house-gate, kept vigil. And <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> addressed the company of maidservants —

children.text: jvāletha dīpa vimalāṃ dhvajāgri maṇiratna sarvi sthāpethā /
children.translated_text: 'Light the lamps brightly! Set up jeweled and gem banners everywhere!

children.text: olambayātha hārāṃ prabhāṃ kuruta sarvi gehesmin // Lal_15.11 //
children.translated_text: Hang necklaces! Make radiance throughout this house! // Lal_15.11 //

children.text: saṃgīti yojayethā jāgaratha atandritā imāṃ rajanīm /
children.translated_text: Arrange the music! Keep vigil, unwearied, through this night!

children.text: pratirakṣathā kumāraṃ yathā avidito na gaccheyā // Lal_15.12 //
children.translated_text: Guard the prince, lest he depart undetected! // Lal_15.12 //

children.text: varmitakalāpahastā asidhanuśaraśaktitomaragṛhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: With armor, quivers in hand, seizing swords, bows, arrows, spears, and lances —

children.text: priyatanayarakṣaṇārthaṃ karotha sarve mahāyatnam // Lal_15.13 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of guarding the dear son, all of you make the greatest effort! // Lal_15.13 //

children.text: dvārāṃ pithetha sarvāṃ suyantritāṃ nirgaḍāṃ dṛḍhakapāṭāṃ /
children.translated_text: Close all the doors — well-bolted, with strong bars and firm panels!

children.text: muñcatha mā ca akāle mā agrasattva itu na vrajeyā // Lal_15.14 //
children.translated_text: Do not open them untimely, lest the foremost of beings should depart! // Lal_15.14 //

children.text: maṇihāramuktahārāṃ mukhapuṣpake ardhacandra saśṛṅkhalāḥ /
children.translated_text: Fasten jeweled necklaces, pearl necklaces, lip-ornaments, half-moons with chains,

children.text: mekhalakarṇikamudrika sunibaddhāṃ nūpurāṃ kuruta // Lal_15.15 //
children.translated_text: girdles, earrings, and rings — bind on the anklets tightly! // Lal_15.15 //

children.text: yadi sahasa niṣkrameyā naramaruhita mattavāraṇavicārī /
children.translated_text: If he should suddenly go forth — that man-god who roams like a rutting elephant —

children.text: tatha tatha parākramathā yathā vighātaṃ na vindeyā // Lal_15.16 //
children.translated_text: then exert yourselves in every way so that he may not find an opening! // Lal_15.16 //

children.text: yā nāri śaktidhārī śayanaṃ parivārayantu vimalasya /
children.translated_text: Let the women who bear weapons surround the couch of the stainless one!

children.text: ma ca bhavatha middhavihatāḥ pataṃga iva rakṣathā netraiḥ // Lal_15.17 //
children.translated_text: Do not be overcome by drowsiness — guard [him] with your eyes like moths [watching a flame]! // Lal_15.17 //

children.text: chādetha ratanajālai idaṃ gṛhaṃ pārthivasya rakṣārtham /
children.translated_text: Cover this house with nets of jewels, for the protection of the prince!

children.text: veṇūravāṃśca ravathā imāṃ rajani rakṣathā virajām // Lal_15.18 //
children.translated_text: Play flutes and music — guard this stainless night! // Lal_15.18 //

children.text: anyonya bodhayethā ma vasayathā rakṣathā imāṃ rajanīm /
children.translated_text: Awaken one another! Do not sleep! Guard this night!

children.text: mā hu abhiniṣkramethā vijahya rāṣṭraṃ ca rājyaṃ ca // Lal_15.19 //
children.translated_text: Lest he go forth, abandoning the kingdom and the realm! // Lal_15.19 //

body.text:
etasya nirgatasyā rājakulaṃ sarvimaṃ nirabhiramyam /
ucchinnaśca bhaveyā pārthivavaṃśaściranubaddhaḥ // Lal_15.20 // Lal_15.iti
body.translated_text: If he goes forth, this entire royal family will be joyless, and the long-established royal lineage will be cut off!' // Lal_15.20 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo 'ṣṭāviṃśatimahāyakṣasenāpatayaḥ pāñcikayajñasenāpatipūrvaṃgamāni ca pañcahāritīputraśatānyekasmin saṃnipātyaivaṃ mataṃ vicārayanti sma - adya mārṣā bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati / tasya yuṣmābhiḥ pūjākarmaṇe autsukyamāpattavyam //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the twenty-eight great <s>Yakṣa</s> generals, led by the general <s>Pāñcika</s>, and the five hundred sons of <s>Hārītī</s>, having assembled together, considered this opinion: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth! You must show eagerness for the act of worshipping him.' //

body.text: catvāraśca mahārājāno alakavatīṃ rājadhānīṃ praviśya tāṃ mahatīṃ yakṣaparṣadamāmantrayate sma - adya mārṣā bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati / sa yuṣmābhirha yavaracaraṇaparigṛhīto niṣkrāmayitavyaḥ / sā ca yakṣaparṣadāha -
body.translated_text: And the four great kings, entering the royal capital <s>Alakavatī</s>, addressed that great <s>Yakṣa</s> assembly: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth! He must be brought forth by you with reverent service.' And that <s>Yakṣa</s> assembly said —

children.text: vajradṛḍha abhedya nārāyaṇo ātmabhāvo guru vīryabalaupetu so 'kampito sarvasattvottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His body is adamantine, unbreakable, like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, heavy, endowed with the power of vigor, unshakable — the foremost of all beings!

children.text: girivara mahameru utpāṭya śakyaṃ nabhe dhārituṃ kenacit na tu jinaguṇameru śailairguruḥ puṇyajñānāśritaḥ śakya netuṃ kvacit // Lal_15.21 //
children.translated_text: One might uproot <s>Meru</s>, the great mountain, and hold it in the sky — but the mountain of the <s>Jina</s>'s qualities, heavy with merit and knowledge, cannot be led anywhere [by force]!' // Lal_15.21 //

body.text: vaiśravaṇa āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> said —

children.text: ye mānagarvita narā guru teṣu śāstā ye premagauravasthitā laghu te vijāni /
children.translated_text: 'Those men who are prideful and arrogant — the teacher is heavy [i.e. difficult] for them; those who are established in love and respect — they will know him easily.',

children.text: adhyāśayena abhiyujyatha gauraveṇa laghu taṃ hi vetsyatha khagā iva tūlapeśim // Lal_15.22 //
children.translated_text: 'Apply yourselves with earnest intention and reverence — you will know him quickly, like birds [know] a tuft of cotton! // Lal_15.22 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca purato yāsye yūyaṃ ca vahathā hayam /
children.translated_text: I shall go before [him], and you shall carry the horse!

children.text: naiṣkramye bodhisattvasya puṇyamārjayāmo bahum // Lal_15.23 //
children.translated_text: In the going forth of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, let us accumulate much merit!' // Lal_15.23 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindro devāṃstrāyatriṃśānāmantrayate sma - adya mārṣā bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati / tatra yuṣmābhiḥ sarvaiḥ pūjākarmaṇe autsukyena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, addressed the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth! There, all of you must be eager for the act of worship!' //

body.text: tatra śāntamatirnāma devaputraḥ sa evamāha - ahaṃ tāvatkapilavastuni mahānagare sarvastrīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāṃ prasvāpanaṃ kariṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: There, a <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Śāntamati</s> said: 'I shall put to sleep all the women, men, boys, and girls in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>.'

body.text: lalitavyūho nāma devaputraḥ sa evamāha - ahamapi sarvahayagajakharoṣṭragomahiṣastrīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāṃ śabdamantardhāpayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: A <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Lalitavyūha</s> said: 'I too shall cause the sound of all horses, elephants, donkeys, camels, cattle, buffalo, women, men, boys, and girls to disappear.'

body.text: vyūhamatirnāma devaputraḥ sa evamāha - ahaṃ gaganatale saptarathavistārapramāṇaṃ ratnavedikāparivṛtaṃ sūryakāntamaṇiratnaprabhojjvalitamuchritachatradhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇaṃ nānāgandhaghaṭikānidhūpitaṃ mārgavyūhaṃ kariṣyāmi, yena mārgeṇa bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyati /
body.translated_text: A <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Vyūhamati</s> said: 'I shall create in the sky a path-array seven chariot-widths in extent, surrounded by a railing of jewels, blazing with the radiance of sun-stone gems, with raised parasols, banners, and pennants, strewn with various flowers, fumigated with various fragrance-pots — along the path by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth.'

body.text: airāvaṇo nāma nāgarājā sa evamāha - ahamapi ca svasyāṃ śuṇḍāyāṃ dvātriṃśadyojanapramāṇaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ māpayiṣyāmi / yatrāpsaraso 'bhiruhya tūryasaṃgītisaṃprabhaṇitena mahatā gītavāditena bodhisattvasyopasthānaparicaryāṃ kurvantyo gamiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: A <s>Nāga</s>-king named <s>Airāvaṇa</s> said: 'I too shall construct on my own trunk a palace three hundred and twenty <s>yojanas</s> in extent, where <s>Apsarases</s>, having ascended, will serve and attend the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with great singing and music as they proceed.'

body.text: svayaṃ ca śakro devānāmindra evamāha - ahaṃ dvārāṇi vivariṣyāmi / mārgaṃ ca saṃdarśayāmi /
body.translated_text: And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, himself said: 'I shall open the gates and show the way.'

body.text: dharmacārī devaputra āha - ahaṃ vikṛtamantaḥpuramupadarśayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: A <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Dharmacārī</s> said: 'I shall display the altered [i.e. repulsive] state of the inner palace [women].'

body.text: saṃcodako devaputra āha - ahaṃ bodhisattvaṃ śayanādutthāpayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: A <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Saṃcodaka</s> said: 'I shall rouse the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from his couch.'

body.text: tatra varuṇaśca nāma nāgarājo manasvī ca nāgarājaḥ sāgaraśca nāgarājo 'navataptaśca nāgarājo nandopanandau nāgarājāvevamāhuḥ - vayamapi bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe kālānusārimeghamabhinirmāya uragasāracandanacūrṇavarṣamabhivarṣayiṣyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: There, <s>Nāga</s>-kings — <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Manasvī</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Anavatapta</s>, and <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> — said: 'We too, for the act of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, shall create a timely cloud and rain down a shower of powdered <s>Uraga-sāra</s> sandalwood!' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo devanāgayakṣagandharvaiścāyamevaṃrūpo niścayābhiprāyaścintito 'bhūd vyavasitaśca / bodhisattvasyaivaṃ dharmacintānupraviṣṭasya saṃgītiprāsādeṣu sukhaśayanagatasya antaḥpuramadhyagatasya pūrvabuddhacarita vicintayataḥ sarvasattvahitamanucintayataścatvāri pūrvapraṇidhānapadānyāmukhībhavanti sma / katamāni catvāri? pūrvaṃ mayā svayaṃbhuvāmādhipateyatāmabhilaṣatā sarvajñatāṃ prārthayamānenaivaṃ saṃnāhaḥ saṃnaddho 'bhūt - sattvān duḥkhitān dṛṣṭā aho batāhaṃ saṃsāramahācārakabandhanaprakṣiptasya lokasaṃniveśasya saṃsāracārakaṃ bhittvā bandhanapramokṣaśabdaṃ codīrayeyaṃ tṛṣṇayā sanigaḍagāḍhabandhanabaddhāṃśca sattvān pramocayeyam / idaṃ prathamaṃ pūrvapraṇidhānapadamāmukhībhavati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, by the gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, such a resolve and intention was conceived and determined. As the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, absorbed in contemplation of the <s>Dharma</s>, resting comfortably in the music-palace, situated within the inner quarters, reflected upon the deeds of the former <s>Buddhas</s> and contemplated the welfare of all beings, four former vow-resolutions arose before him. What four? 'Formerly, when I aspired to self-sovereignty and sought omniscience, I girded myself with this armor: Having seen beings in suffering — alas! — may I break open the prison of the great <s>saṃsāra</s> into which the world-assembly has been cast, and may I raise the cry of liberation from bondage! May I liberate beings bound with the stocks and fetters of craving!' This was the first former vow-resolution that arose before him. //

body.text: aho batāhaṃ saṃsāramahāvidyāndhakāragahanaprakṣiptasya lokasyājñānapaṭalatimirāvṛtanayanasya prajñācakṣurvirahitasyāvidyāmohāndhakārasya mahāntaṃ dharmālokaṃ kuryām / jñānapradīpaṃ copasaṃhareyam / trivimokṣasukhajñānavatauṣadhisaṃprayogeṇa copāyaprajñājñānasaṃprayuktena sarvāvidyāndhakāratamohataṃ mahattimirapaṭalakāluṣyamapanīya prajñācakṣurviśodhayeyam / idaṃ dvitīyaṃ pūrvapraṇidhānapadamāmukhībhavati sma //
body.translated_text: 'Alas! May I create for the world — cast into the dense darkness of the great ignorance of <s>saṃsāra</s>, its eyes covered by the film of nescience, deprived of the eye of wisdom, [plunged] in the darkness of ignorance and delusion — a great light of <s>Dharma</s>! May I bring forth the lamp of knowledge! By the application of the medicine of the three liberations (<s>trivimokṣa</s>) — bliss, knowledge, and tranquility — conjoined with skillful means, wisdom, and knowledge, having dispelled the thick film of darkness, the impurity of all the darkness of ignorance and delusion, may I purify the eye of wisdom!' This second clause of the former aspiration became manifest.

body.text: aho batāhaṃ mānadhvajocchritasya lokasyāhaṃkāramamakārābhiniviṣṭasyātmanīyagrāhānugamānasasya saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsaviparyastasyāsaṃgrahagṛhītasyāryamārgopadeśenāsmimānadhvajaprapātanaṃ kuryām / itīdaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pūrvapraṇidhānapadamāmukhībhavati sma /
body.translated_text: 'Alas! May I, for the world whose banner of pride is raised aloft, engrossed in the concepts of "I" and "mine," whose minds pursue the grasping of a self, perverted by the perversions of perception, thought, and view, seized by non-comprehension — may I by the instruction of the Noble Path bring about the casting down of the banner of self-conceit!' This third clause of the former aspiration became manifest.

body.text: aho batāhaṃ vyupaśāntasya lokasya tandrākulajātasya guṇāvaguṇṭhitabhūtasyājavaṃjavasamāpannasyāsmāllokāt paraṃ lokaṃ paralokādimaṃ lokaṃ saṃghāvataḥ saṃsarataḥ saṃsārādabhinivṛttasyālātacakrasamārūḍhasyopaśamikaṃ prajñātṛptikaraṃ dharmaṃ saṃprakāśayeyam / itīdaṃ caturthaṃ pūrvapraṇidhānapadamāmukhībhavati sma / imāni catvāri pūrvapraṇidhānapadānyāmukhībhavanti sma //
body.translated_text: 'Alas! May I, for the world that is [seemingly] tranquil [yet] born of sloth and torpor, whose virtues are veiled, rushing headlong, wandering from this world to the next, from the next world to this — whirling in <s>saṃsāra</s> without turning back, mounted upon a wheel of fire — proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> that brings calm and satisfaction through wisdom!' This fourth clause of the former aspiration became manifest. These four clauses of the former aspiration became manifest.

body.text: tasmiṃśca kṣaṇe dharmacāriṇā devaputreṇa śuddhāvāsakāyikaiśca devaputrairvikṛtavigalitamantaḥ - puramupadarśitamabhūt / visaṃsthitaṃ bībhatsarūpamupadarśya ca gaganatalasthāste bodhisattvaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: At that moment, <s>Dharmacārī</s> <s>devaputra</s> and the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s> displayed the inner palace in a distorted, decomposed state. And having displayed [it] in this disordered, loathsome form, standing in the sky, they addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in verses:

children.text: athābruvan devasutā maharddhayo vibuddhapadmāyatalocanaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>devaputras</s> of great supernatural power spoke to him whose lotus-eyes were wide-awakened:

children.text: kathaṃ tavāsminnupajāyate ratiḥ śmaśānamadhye samavasthitasya // Lal_15.24 //
children.translated_text: 'How does delight arise in you — one who is stationed in the midst of a charnel ground?' // Lal_15.24 //

body.text: saṃcoditaḥ so 'tha sureśvarebhiḥ nirīkṣate 'ntaḥpura taṃ muhūrtam /
body.translated_text: Prompted thus by the lords of gods, he gazed upon that inner palace for a moment;

body.text: saṃpreṣate paśyati tāṃ bibhatsāṃ śmaśānamadhye vasito 'smi bhūtam // Lal_15.25 //
body.translated_text: he looked about and saw that loathsomeness: 'Truly I am dwelling in the midst of a charnel ground!' // Lal_15.25 //

body.text: adrākṣīt khalvapi bodhisattvaḥ sarvāvantaṃ nārīgaṇam / vyavalokayan paśyati / tatra kāścidvayapakṛṣṭavastrāḥ kāścidvidhūtakeśyaḥ kāścidvikīrṇābharaṇāḥ kāścidvibhraṣṭamukuṭāḥ kāścidvihatairaṃsaiḥ kāścidvigopitagātryaḥ kāścidvisaṃsthitamukhāḥ kāścidviparivartitanayanāḥ kāścitprasravantī lālābhiḥ kāścicchvasantyaḥ kāścitprahasantyaḥ kāścitkāśantyaḥ kāścitpralapantyaḥ kāściddantān kaṭakaṭāyantyaḥ kāścidvivarṇavadanāḥ kāścidvisaṃsthitarūpāḥ kāścitpralambitabāhavaḥ kāścidvikṣiptacaraṇāḥ kāściduddhāṭitaśīrṣāḥ kāścidavaguṇṭhitaśīrṣāḥ kāścidviparivartitamukhamaṇḍalāḥ kāścitpradhvastaśarīrāḥ kāścidvibhugnagātryaḥ kāścinnikubjāḥ khurakhurāyamāṇāḥ kāścinmṛdaṅgamupaguhya parivartitaśīrṣaśarīrāḥ kāścidvīṇāvallakyādyaparibaddhapāṇayaḥ kāścidveṇuṃ dantaiḥ kaṭakaṭāyantyaḥ kāścitkimpalanakulasaṃpatāḍāpakarṣitavādyabhāṇḍāḥ kāścinnimeṣonmeṣaparivṛttanayanāḥ kāścidvivṛtāsyāḥ / evaṃ tadvikṛtaṃ dharaṇītalagatamantaḥpuraṃ nirīkṣamāṇo bodhisattvaḥ śmaśānasaṃjñāmutpādayati sma //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> indeed saw the entire company of women. Surveying them, he beheld: some with garments pulled away; some with disheveled hair; some with ornaments scattered; some with diadems fallen off; some with shoulders uncovered; some with bodies exposed; some with distorted mouths; some with eyes rolled back; some drooling with saliva; some snoring; some laughing [in sleep]; some coughing; some babbling; some gnashing their teeth; some with discolored faces; some of disordered appearance; some with arms hanging loose; some with legs flung apart; some with heads thrown back; some with heads covered; some with faces twisted around; some with bodies collapsed; some with limbs bent; some hunched over, making snorting sounds; some embracing drums with heads and bodies twisted; some with hands still clutching <s>vīṇās</s> and lutes; some gnashing their teeth upon flutes; some with percussion instruments pulled away and scattered; some with eyes flickering open and shut; some with mouths gaping open. Thus beholding that distorted inner palace strewn upon the ground, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> generated the perception of a charnel ground.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭva udvigna sa lokanāthaḥ karuṇaṃ viniśvasya idaṃ jagāda /
children.translated_text: Seeing that, the Lord of the World, distressed, heaving a compassionate sigh, said this:

children.text: aho batā kṛcchragatā vrajeyaṃ kathaṃ ratiṃ vindati rākṣasīgaṇe // Lal_15.26 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, those gone to wretchedness! How could I find delight among a host of <s>Rākṣasīs</s>?' // Lal_15.26 //

children.text: atimohatamāvṛta durmati kāmaguṇairniguṇairguṇasaṃjñinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Enveloped in the extreme darkness of delusion, of impaired intellect, perceiving virtues in the virtueless sense-pleasures —

children.text: vihaga pañjaramadhyagatā yathā na hi labhanti kadāci viniḥsṛtim // Lal_15.27 //
children.translated_text: like birds trapped inside a cage, they never find release! // Lal_15.27 //

body.text: atha bodhasattvo 'nena punarapi dharmālokamukhenāntaḥpuraṃ pratyavekṣamāṇo mahākaruṇāparidevitena sattvān paridevate sma - iha te bālā hanyante āghātana iva vadhyāḥ / iha te bālā rajyante citraghaṭeṣvivāmedhyaparipūrṇeṣvavidvāṃsaḥ / iha te bālā majjanti gajā iva vārimadhye / iha te bālā rudhyante caurā iva cārakamadhye / iha te bālā abhiratā varāhā ivāśucimadhye / iha te bālā adhyavasitāḥ kukkurā ivāsthikaraṅkamadhye / iha te bālāḥ prapatitā dīpaśikhāsviva pataṃgāḥ / iha te bālā badhyante kapaya iva lepena / iha te bālāḥ paridahyante jālotkṣiptā iva jalajāḥ / iha te bālāḥ parikrūḍyante sūnākāṣṭheṣvivorabhrāḥ / iha te bālā avasajjante kilbiṣakāriṇa iva śūlāgre / iha te bālāḥ saṃsīdanti jīrṇagajā iva paṅke / iha te bālā vipadyante bhinnayānapātra iva mahāsamudre / iha te bālāḥ prapatante mahāprapāta iva jātyandhāḥ / iha te bālāḥ paryādānaṃ gacchanti pātālasaṃdhigatamiva vāri / iha te bālā dhūmāyante kalpasaṃkṣaya iva mahāpṛthivī / ābhirbālā bhrāmyante kumbhakārakacakramivāviddham / iha te bālāḥ paribhramanti śailāntargatā
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, again surveying the inner palace with this illumination of <s>Dharma</s>, lamented over beings with the lamentation of great compassion: 'Here these fools are slaughtered like victims in a slaughterhouse. Here these fools are enamored, like the ignorant [attracted] to painted pots filled with filth. Here these fools are drowning like elephants in the midst of water. Here these fools are trapped like thieves among spies. Here these fools delight like pigs in the midst of impurity. Here these fools are attached like dogs among bone-carcasses. Here these fools have fallen like moths into lamp-flames. Here these fools are bound like monkeys by bird-lime. Here these fools are scorched like water-creatures cast into a net. Here these fools are sport like lambs upon butcher-blocks. Here these fools are impaled like sinners upon the tip of a stake. Here these fools are sinking like aged elephants in mud. Here these fools are perishing like [those in] broken vessels in the great ocean. Here these fools are falling like the congenitally blind into a great precipice. Here these fools are being consumed like water that has entered a subterranean chasm. Here these fools are smoldering like the great earth at the <s>kalpa</s>'s destruction. By these [sense-pleasures] fools are whirled like a potter's wheel set spinning. Here these fools are wandering like the congenitally blind among

body.text: iva jātyandhāḥ / iha te bālā viparivartante kurkurā iva śardūlabaddhāḥ / iha te bālā mlāyante grīṣmakāla iva tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ / iha te bālāḥ parihīyante śaśīva kṛṣṇapakṣe / ābhirbālā bhakṣyante garuḍeneva pannagāḥ / ābhirbālā grasyante mahāmakareṇeva potaḥ / ābhirbālā lupyante corasaṃgheneva sārthaḥ / ābhirbālā bhidyante māruteneva śālāḥ / ābhirbālā hanyante dṛṣṭīviṣairiva jantavaḥ / āsvādasaṃjñino bālāḥ kṣaṇyante madhudigdhābhiriva kṣuradhārābhirbālajātīyāḥ / ābhirbālā uhyante dāruskandhā iva jalaughaiḥ / ābhirbālāḥ krīḍanti dārakā iva svamūtrapurīṣaiḥ / ābhirbālā āvartyante 'ṅkuśeneva gajāḥ / ābhirbālā badhyante dhūrtakairiva bālajātīyāḥ / iha te bālāḥ kuśalamūlāni kṣapayanti dyatābhiratā iva dhanam / ābhirbālā bhakṣyante rākṣasībhiriva vaṇijāḥ / ityebhirdvātriṃśatākārairbodhisattvo 'ntaḥpuraṃ paritulayitvā kāye 'śubhasaṃjñāṃ vicārayan pratikūlasaṃjñāmupasaṃharan jugupsasaṃjñāmutpādayan svakāyaṃ prativibhāvayan kāyasyādīnavaṃ saṃpaśyan kāyātkāyābhiniveśamuccārayan śubhasaṃjñāṃ vibhāvayan aśubhasaṃjñāmavakrāmayan adhaḥ pādatalābhyāṃ yāvadūrdhvaṃ mastakaparyantaṃ paśyati sma aśucisamutthitamaśucisaṃbhavamaśucisravaṃ nityam / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: mountains. Here these fools are tossed about like dogs bound by a leopard. Here these fools wither like grass and trees in the hot season. Here these fools wane like the moon in the dark fortnight. By these [sense-pleasures] fools are devoured like serpents by <s>Garuḍa</s>. By these, fools are swallowed like a boat by a great <s>makara</s>. By these, fools are robbed like a caravan by a band of thieves. By these, fools are shattered like halls by the wind. By these, fools are slain like creatures by venomous glances. Perceiving sweetness, fools are cut like the childish by razor-edges smeared with honey. By these, fools are swept away like logs by floods of water. By these, fools play like children in their own urine and excrement. By these, fools are driven like elephants by goads. By these, fools are ensnared like the childish by rogues. Here these fools exhaust their wholesome roots like those addicted to gambling [exhaust their] wealth. By these, fools are devoured like merchants by <s>Rākṣasīs</s>.' Thus, having evaluated the inner palace with these thirty-two similes, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, contemplating the perception of the unlovely in the body, bringing to bear the perception of repulsiveness, generating the perception of disgust, analyzing his own body, seeing the danger of the body, extracting the attachment to body from the body, dispelling the perception of beauty, introducing the perception of the unlovely — from the soles of his feet below to the crown of his head above, he beheld [it as] always arisen from impurity, born from impurity, streaming with impurity. And at that time he spoke this verse:

children.text: karmakṣetraruhaṃ tṛṣāsalilajaṃ satkāyasaṃjñīkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Sprung from the field of <s>karma</s>, born from the water of craving, made into the conception of a self-body,

children.text: aśrusvedakaphārdramūtravikṛtaṃ śoṇītabindvākulam /
children.translated_text: moist with tears, sweat, and phlegm, defiled with urine, agitated with drops of blood,

children.text: bastīpūyavasāsamastakarasaiḥ pūrṇaṃ tathā kilbiṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: filled with the juices of bladder, pus, fat, and brain, and likewise with impurities,

children.text: nityaprasravitaṃ hyamedhya sakalaṃ durgandha nānāvidham // Lal_15.28 //
children.translated_text: constantly oozing, entirely unclean, foul-smelling in many ways — // Lal_15.28 //

body.text:
asthīdantasakeśaromavikṛtaṃ carmāvṛtaṃ lomaśaṃ
antaḥplīhayakṛdvapoṣṇarasanairebhiścitaṃ durbalaiḥ /

children.text: majjāsnāyunibaddhayantrasadṛśaṃ māṃsena śobhīkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: like a machine bound with marrow and sinews, made to appear beautiful by flesh,

children.text: nānāvyādhiprakīrṇaśokakalilaṃ kṣuttarṣasaṃpīḍitam /
children.translated_text: strewn with various diseases, beset with grief, afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: jantūnāṃ nilayaṃ anekasuṣiraṃ mṛtyuṃ jarāṃ cāśritaṃ
children.translated_text: a dwelling of creatures, full of many cavities, subject to death and old age —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ko hi vicakṣaṇo ripunibhaṃ manye śarīraṃ svakam // Lal_15.29 //
children.translated_text: what discerning person, having seen [this], would consider his own body as anything but an enemy?' // Lal_15.29 //

body.translated_text: deformed with bones, teeth, hair [of head and body], covered with skin, hairy, filled within by spleen, liver, entrails, hot humors, and feeble [constituents],

body.text: evaṃ ca bodhisattvaḥ kāye kāyānugatayā smṛtyā viharati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelt with mindfulness directed to the body within the body.

body.text: gaganatalagatāśca devaputrā dharmacāriṇaṃ devaputramevamāhuḥ - kimidaṃ mārṣāḥ? siddhārtho vilambate 'ntaḥpuraṃ cāvalokayati sma / taṃ codaparśayati cittaṃ codvejayati / bhūyaścakṣurniveśayati / athavā javajalanidhigambhīro 'yam, na śakyamasya pramāṇaṃ grahītum / athavā asaṅgasya mā khalu viṣaye sajjate manaḥ / mā khalvamarairasaṃcodito vismarati pūrvapratijñāmiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>devaputras</s> in the sky said to <s>Dharmacārī</s> <s>devaputra</s>: 'What is this, sirs? <s>Siddhārtha</s> delays and gazes upon the inner palace! Who shall now show him [the way] and arouse urgency in his mind? Again he casts his gaze! Perhaps he is as deep as a swift ocean — his measure cannot be grasped! Perhaps his mind, being non-attached, does not cling to [sense] objects! Perhaps, unexhorted by the immortals, he may forget his former vow!'

body.text: dharmacāryāha - kimevaṃ kathayata? nanu yūyamasya pratyakṣapūvemava bodhāya caratastathāvidhā niḥsaṅgatābhūt / naiṣkramyatyāge ca kimaṅga punaretarhi caramabhavāvasthitasya saṅgo bhaviṣyati?
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmacārī</s> said: 'Why do you speak thus? Were you not direct witnesses of his non-attachment while he practiced for awakening through [countless births of] such a kind? If, in the great renunciation, [there was no attachment then], how much less will there be attachment now, when he stands in his final existence?'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ kṛtaniścayaḥ saṃvejitamānaso vyavasitabuddhiḥ salīlamavilambitaṃ paryaṅkādavatīrya saṅgītiprāsāde pūrvābhimukhaḥ sthitvā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā ratnajālikāmavanāmya prāsādakoṭīgato daśanakhakṛtakarapuṭo bhūtvā sarvabuddhān samanvāhṛtya sarvabuddhebhyaśca namaskāraṃ kṛtvā gaganatalamavalokayati sma / so 'drākṣīd gaganatalagatamamarādhipatiṃ daśaśatanayanaṃ devaśatasahasraparivṛtaṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvarachatradhvajapatākāvataṃsakaratna - hāradāmaparigṛhītamavanatakāyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānaṃ sthitam / caturaśca lokapālān yakṣarākṣasagandharvabhujagagaṇasaṃparivṛtān saṃnaddhadṛḍhavarmitakavacitān asidhanuśaraśaktitomaratriśūlahastān salīlaṃ maṇimukuṭavilambitacūḍān bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānān sthitān paśyati sma / candrasūryāvati devaputrau vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ pārśvayoḥ sthitāvapaśyat / puṣyaśca nakṣatrādhipatirupasthito 'bhūt / ardharātriṃ ca samayaṃ saṃprāptam / dṛṣṭvā ca bodhisattvaśchandakamāmantrayate sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his resolve made firm, his mind filled with urgency, his determination set, gracefully and without delay descended from his couch. Standing in the concert-hall facing east, he pressed down the jeweled lattice with his right hand, and reaching the pinnacle of the palace, forming a cup with his ten fingernails, he called to mind all the <s>Buddhas</s>, made salutation to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, and gazed at the sky. He saw, stationed in the sky, the lord of the immortals, thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of gods, holding flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, chaplets, jewel-necklaces, and garlands — bowing his body, standing in worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He saw the four world-guardians, surrounded by hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>, well-armored with firm mail and cuirass, bearing swords, bows, arrows, spears, lances, and tridents in hand, with gem-crested diadems gracefully hanging — standing in worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He saw <s>Candra</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>, the two <s>devaputras</s>, standing on his left and right sides. And <s>Puṣya</s>, the lord of the asterisms, had drawn near. And midnight had arrived. Having seen [all this], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> summoned <s>Chandaka</s>:

children.text: chandakā capalu mā vilambahe aśvarāja dada me alaṃkṛtam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Chandaka</s>! Be swift, do not delay! Give me the king of horses, well-adorned!

children.text: sarvasiddhi mama eti maṅgalā arthasiddhi dhruvamadya bheṣyate // Lal_15.30 //
children.translated_text: All success and good fortune is mine — the accomplishment of purpose shall certainly be today!' // Lal_15.30 //

body.text: atha chandaka idaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā udvignamanā evamāha -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Chandaka</s>, hearing these words, his mind distressed, spoke thus:

body.text: kva gamiṣyase vikasitabhrū kamaladala śubhalocana

children.text: nṛpasiṃha śaradindupūrṇa kumudaśaśāṅkamuditā // Lal_15.31 //
children.translated_text: O lion among men, [radiant as] the full autumn moon, delighting the night-lilies like the moon? // Lal_15.31 //

body.translated_text: 'Where will you go, O one of arched brows, with lotus-petal auspicious eyes,

body.text: navanalinakomalavibuddhapadmavadanā

children.text: hāṭakasudhāntaravitaruṇavimalaśaśiteja /
children.translated_text: [whose radiance is] like pure stainless youthful moonlight within a golden temple,

children.text: dhṛtahutārciragnimaṇividyutatprabhojjvalitatejo /
children.translated_text: [whose] splendor blazes like a kindled fire-flame, a jewel, or lightning,

children.text: vāraṇamattalīlagajagāmi /
children.translated_text: [who has] the graceful gait of a lordly rutting elephant,

children.text: govṛṣamṛgendrahaṃsakrama sukramā sucaraṇā // Lal_15.32 //
children.translated_text: the step of a bull, a lion-king, a swan — of beautiful stride, of lovely feet!' // Lal_15.32 //

body.translated_text: [You] whose face is like a fresh lotus, soft, an awakened <s>padma</s>,

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: chandaka yasya arthiṃ mayi pūrva tyakta karacaraṇanayana /
children.translated_text: '<s>Chandaka</s>! He for whose sake I formerly gave up hands, feet, and eyes,

children.text: tatha uttamāṅga tanaya bhārya priyāśca rājyadhanakanakavasana /
children.translated_text: likewise head, sons, wife, and beloved ones, kingdom, wealth, gold, and garments,

children.text: ratnapūrṇa gaja turagānilajavavega vikramabalāḥ // Lal_15.34 //
children.translated_text: jewel-laden elephants and horses swift as the wind — by valor and strength — // Lal_15.34 //

children.text: śīlu mi rakṣi kṣānti paribhāvi
children.translated_text: I guarded morality, cultivated patience,

children.text: vīryabaladhyānaprajñānirataścāsmi bahukalpakoṭinayutā /
children.translated_text: and [was] devoted to vigor, strength, meditation, and wisdom for many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: kiṃ tu spṛśitva bodhiśivaśāntim
children.translated_text: but now, having touched the peace and tranquility of <s>Bodhi</s> —'

children.text: jarāmaraṇapañjaraniraṣṭasattvaparimocanasya samayo 'dyupasthitu mama // Lal_15.35 //
children.translated_text: The time has now arrived for me to liberate beings thrust into the cage of old age and death! // Lal_15.35 //

body.text: chandaka āha - śrutaṃ mayā āryaputra yathā tvaṃ jātamātra eva naimittikānāṃ brāhmaṇānāmupanāmito darśanāya / taiścāsi rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāgrato vyākṛtaḥ - deva vṛddhiste rājakulasya / āha - kimiti? te āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s> said: 'I have heard, O noble son, that when you were just born you were presented to the soothsayer <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> for examination. And they declared before King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: "O lord, good fortune has increased for your royal house!" He asked: "Why?" They said:"

children.text: ayaṃ kumāraḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇo jātastavā ātmaja puṇyatejitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "This prince, bearing the marks of a hundred merits, born as your son, empowered by merit,

children.text: ca cakravartī catudvīpaīśvaro bhaviṣyati saptadhanairupetaḥ // Lal_15.36 //
children.translated_text: shall either become a <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Monarch), lord of the four continents, endowed with the seven treasures, // Lal_15.36 //

children.text: sa cetpunarlokamavekṣya duḥkhitaṃ vijahyamāntaḥpuri niṣkramiṣyati /
children.translated_text: or if, seeing the world as suffering, he abandons the inner palace and goes forth,

children.text: avāpya bodhiṃ ajarāmaraṃ padaṃ tarpeṣyate dharmajalairimāṃ prajām // Lal_15.37 //
children.translated_text: having attained <s>bodhi</s> — the state free from old age and death — he shall satisfy this multitude with the waters of the <s>dharma</s>!" // Lal_15.37 //

body.text: hanta āryaputra asti tāvadeva tadvyākaraṇaṃ nedaṃ nāsti / kiṃ tu śṛṇu tāvanmamārthakāmasya vacanam / āha - kimiti / aha - deva yasyārthe iha kecidanekavidhāni vratatapāṃsyārabhante 'jinajaṭāmakuṭacīvaravalkaladharā dīrghanakhakeśasmaśru ca, anekavidhāni kāyasyātāpanaparitāpanāni samutsahante / tīvraṃ ca vratatapamārabhante / kimiti? vayaṃ devamanuṣyasaṃpattiṃ pratilabhemahīti / sā ca saṃpattvayāryaputra pratilabdhā / idaṃ ca rājyamṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ramaṇīyamākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyam / imāni codyānāni varapravarāṇi nānāvidhapuṣpaphalamaṇḍitāni nānāśakunigaṇanikūjitāni / puṣkariṇyaścotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkopaśobhitā haṃsamayūrakokilacakravākakroñcasārasanikūjitāḥ puṣpitasahakārāśokacampakakurabakatilakakeśarādinānādrumatīroparibaddhā nānāratnavṛkṣavāṭikāsamalaṃkṛtā aṣṭāpadavinibaddhā ratnavedikāparivṛtā ratnajālasaṃchannā yathartukālaparibhogā grīṣmavarṣāśaraddhemantasukhasaṃvāsāḥ / ime ca śaradabhranibhāḥ kailāsaparvatasadṛśā mahāprāsādā vaijayantasamā dharmasudharmakṣemasamā śokavigataprabhṛtayo vitardiniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaharmyakūṭāgāraprāsādatalasamalaṃkṛtā ratnakiṅkiṇījālasamīritāḥ / idaṃ cāryaputra antaḥpuraṃ tuṇavapaṇavavīṇāveṇusaṃpatāḍāvacarākimpalanakulasughoṣakamṛdaṅgapaṭahanṛtyagītavāditrasaṃgītisaṃprayogasuśikṣitaṃ hāsyalāsyakrīḍitaramitasukhilamadhuropacāram / tvaṃ ca deva yuvā anabhikrāntayauvano navo daharastaruṇaḥ komalaśarīraḥ śiśuḥ kṛṣṇakeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Come, O noble son, that prophecy still stands — it is not that it does not exist! But hear the words of one who desires your welfare.' He asked: 'What?' [<s>Chandaka</s>] said: 'O lord, for the sake of which [goal] some people here undertake various austerities and observances — wearing deer-skin, matted hair, diadems, bark-garments, and robes, with long nails, hair, and beards, enduring various forms of bodily torment and mortification, undertaking severe observances and austerities — why? [Thinking:] "May we obtain the prosperity of gods and humans!" But that prosperity, O noble son, has already been obtained by you! This kingdom is rich, prosperous, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, teeming with many people. Here are these supreme and excellent parks, adorned with manifold flowers and fruits, resounding with various flocks of birds. Lotus-pools beautified with blue lotuses, red lotuses, night-lotuses, and white lotuses, resounding with geese, peacocks, cuckoos, <s>cakravāka</s> ducks, herons, and cranes — their banks adorned with blossoming mango, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>kurabaka</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, and <s>keśara</s> trees and other diverse trees, adorned with various jewel-tree gardens, inlaid with the eight-square pattern, surrounded by jeweled railings, covered with nets of gems, with seasonal enjoyments for summer, rains, autumn, and winter. And these great palaces — like autumn clouds, resembling Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, equal to [<s>Indra</s>'s] <s>Vaijayanta</s>, comparable to [the gods'] <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Sudharmā</s>, and <s>Kṣema</s> [halls] — [the palace] named <s>Śokavigata</s> (Grief-Gone) and the rest, adorned with balconies, projecting galleries, arched gateways, windows, mansions, upper stories, and palace terraces, resounding with nets of jeweled bells. And this inner palace, O noble son — well-trained in the arts of <s>tūṇava</s>, <s>paṇava</s>, <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, percussion-play, <s>avacarā</s>, <s>kimpala</s>, <s>nakula</s>, <s>sughoṣaka</s>, <s>mṛdaṅga</s>, <s>paṭaha</s>, dance, song, instrumental music, and ensemble performance — with laughter, pantomime, sport, delight, and sweet, gentle service. And you, O lord, are young, your youth not yet passed, fresh, tender, of delicate body, a youth with dark hair.

body.text: avikrīḍitaḥ kāmaiḥ / abhiramasva tāvadamarādhipatiriva daśaśatanayanastridaśādhipatiḥ / tataḥ paścād vṛddhībhūtā abhiniṣkramiṣyāmaḥ / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: You have not yet enjoyed sensual pleasures! Delight [in them] for now, like the thousand-eyed lord of the immortals, <s>Indra</s>, ruler of the Thirty-Three! Then later, when old, we shall go forth!' And at that moment he spoke this verse —

children.text: ramatāṃ ca ratividhijñāṃ amarādhipatiryathā tridaśaloke /
children.translated_text: 'Let him delight, skilled in the arts of pleasure, as the lord of the immortals in the heaven of the Thirty-Three;

children.text: paścādvṛddhībhūtā vratatapasaṃ ārabhiṣyāmaḥ // Lal_15.39 //
children.translated_text: later, when old, we shall undertake observances and austerities!' // Lal_15.39 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha - alaṃ chandaka / anityāḥ khalvete kāmā adhruvā aśāśvatā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ pradrutāścapalā girinadīvegatulyāḥ / avaśyāyabinduvadacirasthāyina ullāpanā riktamuṣṭivadasārāḥ kadalīskandhavaddurbalā āmabhājanavadbhedanātmakāḥ śaradabhranibhāḥ kṣaṇādbhūtvā na bhavanti / acirasthāyino vidyuta iva nabhasi saviṣabhojanamiva pariṇāmaduḥkhā mālutālatevāsukhadā abhilikhitā bālabuddhibhirudakabudbudopamāḥ kṣipraṃ vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ / māyāmarīcisadṛśāḥ saṃjñāviparyāsasamutthitāḥ / māyāsadṛśāścittaviparyāsavidhāpitāḥ / svapnasadṛśā dṛṣṭiviparyāsaparigrahayogenātṛptikarāḥ / sāgara iva duṣpūrā lavaṇodaka iva tṛṣākarāḥ / sarpaśirovadduḥsparśanīyā mahāprapātavatparivarjitāḥ paṇḍitaiḥ / sabhayāḥ saraṇāḥ sādīnavaḥ sadoṣāḥ iti jñātvā vivarjitāḥ prājñairvigarhitā vidvadbhirjugupsitā āryairvivarjitāḥ budhaiḥ parigṛhītā abudhairniṣevitā bālaiḥ / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enough, <s>Chandaka</s>! These sense-pleasures are indeed impermanent, unstable, not everlasting, subject to change, fleeting, fickle, equal in speed to a mountain torrent. They are as short-lived as a dewdrop, deceiving, as empty of substance as a hollow fist, as fragile as a plantain trunk, as breakable as an unfired vessel, like autumn clouds — existing for a moment, then ceasing to be. They are as momentary as lightning in the sky, as painful in their aftereffect as poisoned food, as joyless as a wind-tossed palm tree, painted [only] by foolish minds, like water-bubbles, quickly subject to change. Like mirages, they arise from the distortion of perception. Like illusions, they are produced by the distortion of mind. Like dreams, through attachment to the distortion of views, they never bring satisfaction. Like the ocean, they are impossible to fill; like salt water, they [only] increase thirst. Hard to touch, like a serpent's head; to be avoided by the wise, like a great precipice. Knowing them to be fearful, full of calamity, full of danger, full of fault — they are shunned by the intelligent, condemned by the learned, loathed by the knowing, avoided by the noble, wise ones, [yet] seized upon by the foolish, resorted to by the ignorant.' And at that moment he spoke this verse —

children.text: vivarjitā sarpaśiro yathā budhaiḥ vigarhitā mīḍhaghaṭo yathāśuciḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Shunned by the wise like a serpent's head, condemned like an impure vessel of filth,

children.text: vināśakā sarvaśubhasya chandakā jñātvā hi kāmānna mi jāyate rati // Lal_15.40 //
children.translated_text: destroyers of everything auspicious, O <s>Chandaka</s> — knowing sense-pleasures thus, no delight arises in me!' // Lal_15.40 //

body.text: tadā chandakaḥ śalyaviddho yathā krandamānastato 'śrunetro duḥkhī evaṃ vākyamavravīt -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Chandaka</s>, as if pierced by an arrow, weeping, with tear-filled eyes, spoke these words in grief:

children.text: devā yasyārthi kecidihā tīvra nekavidhā ārabhante vratān
children.translated_text: 'O lord, for the sake of which [goal] some here undertake various severe observances —

children.text: ajinajaṭādhara sudīrghakeśānakhā śmaśrucīrāstathā /
children.translated_text: wearing deer-skin, matted hair, with exceedingly long hair and nails, beards, and bark —

children.text: valkalādhāra śuṣkāṅga neke vratānāśritā
children.translated_text: wearing bark-garments, with dried-up bodies, resorting to various vows,

children.text: śākasyāmākagardūlabhakṣāśca omūrdhakāścāpare govratāṃ saṃśritāḥ // Lal_15.41 //
children.translated_text: eating vegetables, wild rice, and mustard, some standing on their heads, others following the cow-vow — // Lal_15.41 //

body.text:
kiṃ tu vaya bhavema śreṣṭhā viśiṣṭā jage cakravartivarā lokapālāstathā /
śakra vajraṃdharā yāma devādhipā nirmitā / brahmaloke ca dhyānāsukhākāṅkṣiṇaḥ // Lal_15.42 //
body.translated_text: But may we rather become the best, the most distinguished in the world — supreme <s>Cakravartins</s>, or <s>Lokapālas</s>, or <s>Śakra</s> the <s>Vajra</s>-bearer, or lord of the <s>Yāma</s> gods, or a <s>Nirmita</s> [god], or in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, desiring the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>! // Lal_15.42 //

body.text: tadida naravariṣṭha rājyaṃ tava sphītamṛddhaṃ subhikṣaṃ tathā ārāmodyānaprāsādaucchrepitaṃ vaijayantāsamam /
body.translated_text: This kingdom of yours, O best of men, is prosperous, rich, well-provisioned, with gardens, parks, and towering palaces equal to <s>Vaijayanta</s>;

body.text: istrigārasvayaṃ veṇuvīṇāravai gītavādyai ratī nṛtyasaṃgīti saṃyogi saṃśikṣitaṃ
body.translated_text: the women's quarters [resound] with <s>veṇu</s> (flutes), <s>vīṇā</s>, songs, and music — well-trained in the arts of dance and musical ensemble —

body.text: bhuñja kāmānimān mā vrajā sūratā // Lal_15.43 //
body.translated_text: enjoy these pleasures! Do not go forth, O hero!' // Lal_15.43 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: chandaka śṛṇu yāni duḥkhāśatāmarpitā pūrvi janmāntare
children.translated_text: '<s>Chandaka</s>, listen! The hundreds of sufferings I endured in former births —

children.text: bandhanā rundhanā tāḍanā tarjanā kāmahetormayā /
children.translated_text: bonds, imprisonment, beatings, and threats — all for the sake of sense-desires!

children.text: no ca nirviṇṇabhūt saṃskṛte mānasam // Lal_15.44 //
children.translated_text: Yet my mind has not become [finally] wearied of the conditioned! // Lal_15.44 //

children.text: pramadavaśagataṃ ca mohākulaṃ dṛṣṭijālāvṛtaṃ andhabhūtaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: Formerly, subject to intoxication, bewildered by delusion, enveloped by the net of [wrong] views, blinded —

children.text: ātmasaṃjñāgrahākārakā vedanāvītivṛttā ime dharma ajñānataḥ // Lal_15.45 //
children.translated_text: [driven by] the grasping of self-perception, these feelings passed by — these <s>dharmas</s>, through ignorance! // Lal_15.45 //

children.text: saṃbhūtā capalacala 'nitya meghaiḥ samā vidyubhiḥ sadṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Arisen, fickle, unstable, impermanent, like clouds, like lightning,

children.text: osabindūpamā riktatucchā asārā anātmā ca śūnyasvabhāvā ime sarvaśaḥ // Lal_15.46 //
children.translated_text: like dewdrops, empty, void, without substance, without self, empty by nature — all these, in every way! // Lal_15.46 //

children.text: na ca mama viṣayeṣu saṃrajyate mānasaṃ
children.translated_text: My mind does not delight in sense-objects!

children.text: dehi me chandakā kaṇṭhakālaṃkṛtaṃ aśvarājottamam /
children.translated_text: Give me, <s>Chandaka</s>, <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, the supreme king of horses, adorned!

children.text: pūrṇa me maṅgalā ye purā cintitā
children.translated_text: My auspicious [vows] that were conceived long ago are [now] fulfilled —

children.text: bheṣyi sarvābhibhū sarvadharmeśvaro dharmarājo muniḥ // Lal_15.46 //
children.translated_text: I shall become the All-Conqueror, the Lord of All <s>Dharmas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> King, the Sage! // Lal_15.46 //

body.text: chandaka āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s> said:

children.text: imāṃ vibuddhāmbujapatralocanāṃ vicitrahārāṃ maṇiratnabhūṣitām /
children.translated_text: 'These [women] with eyes [beautiful] like awakened lotus petals, adorned with variegated necklaces and jewel ornaments,

children.text: ghanapramuktāmiva vidyutāṃ nabhe nopekṣase śayanagatāṃ virocatīm // Lal_15.48 //
children.translated_text: shining like lightning released from dense clouds in the sky — will you not regard them, [beautiful] as they lie on their couches? // Lal_15.48 //

children.text: imāṃśca veṇūn paṇavāṃ sughoṣakāṃ mṛdaṅgavaṃśāṃśca saṃgītavāditām /
children.translated_text: These flutes, drums, <s>sughoṣakas</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, bamboo flutes, and instrumental music,

children.text: cakorasorāṃ kalaviṅkanāditāṃ yathālayaṃ kinnariṇāṃ vihāsyase // Lal_15.49 //
children.translated_text: [sweet as] <s>cakora</s> and <s>sārasa</s> birds, resounding like <s>kalaviṅkas</s> — will you abandon [them] like the dwelling of <s>Kinnarīs</s>? // Lal_15.49 //

children.text: sumanotpalāṃ vārṣikacampakāṃstathā sugandhamālāṃ guṇapuṣpasaṃcayām /
children.translated_text: These <s>sumanas</s>, blue lotuses, <s>vārṣika</s>, and <s>campaka</s> [flowers], and fragrant garlands — collections of virtuous flowers,

children.text: kālāgurūnuttamagandhadhūpanāṃ nopekṣase tānanulepanān varān // Lal_15.50 //
children.translated_text: and the finest perfumery of <s>kālāguru</s> (black aloe) incense — will you not regard these excellent unguents? // Lal_15.50 //

body.text: sugandhagandhāṃśca rasāṃ praṇītāṃ susādhitāṃ vyañjanabhojanāṃstathā /
body.translated_text: Fine fragrances, exquisite flavors, well-prepared condiments and foods,

body.text: saśarkarāṃ pānarasāṃ susaṃskṛtāṃ nopekṣase deva kahiṃ gamiṣyasi // Lal_15.51 //
body.translated_text: drink-preparations with sugar, well-made — will you not regard [them], O lord? Where will you go? // Lal_15.51 //

children.text: śīte ca uṣṇānanulepanāmbarāṃ uṣṇe ca tānuragasāracandanāṃ /
children.translated_text: In cold, warm unguents and garments; in heat, [cooling] <s>uragasāra</s>-sandalwood;

children.text: tāṃ kāśikāvastravarāmbarāṃ śubhāṃ nopekṣase deva kahiṃ gamiṣyasi // Lal_15.52 //
children.translated_text: those fine <s>Kāśī</s> silks and excellent garments, beautiful — will you not regard [them], O lord? Where will you go? // Lal_15.52 //

children.text: ime ca te (deva) kāmaguṇā hi pañca samṛddha deveṣviva devatānām /
children.translated_text: These five strands of sensual pleasure of yours, O lord, are as prosperous as those of the gods among the deities;

children.text: ramasva tāvadratisaukhyaanvitaḥ tato vanaṃ yāsyati śākyapuṅgavaḥ // Lal_15.53 //
children.translated_text: delight for now, endowed with the pleasure of enjoyment — later shall the bull of the <s>Śākyas</s> go to the forest!' // Lal_15.53 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

body.text: aparimitānanta kalpā mayā chandakā bhukta kāmāni rūpāśca śabdāśca gandhā rasā sparśa nānāvidhā /
body.translated_text: 'For immeasurable and infinite <s>kalpas</s>, O <s>Chandaka</s>, I have enjoyed sense-pleasures — forms, sounds, scents, tastes, touches of various kinds,

body.text: divya ye mānuṣā no ca tṛptīrabhūt /
body.translated_text: both divine and human — yet satisfaction never arose!

body.text:
nṛpativarasutena aiśvarya kārāpitaṃ cātudvīpe yadā rāja bhūccakravartī samanvāgataḥ saptabhī ratnabhiḥ istrigārasya madhye gataḥ /
tridaśapatisuyāmadevādhipatyaṃ ca kārāpitaṃ yebhyaścāhaṃ cyavitvā ihābhyāgato nirmito nirmiteṣu māno ātmikā ca śriyā uttamā / bhukta pūrve mayā /

children.text: surapuri vaśavarti māreśvatvaṃ ca kārāpitaṃ
children.translated_text: Sovereignty over [the heaven of] <s>Vaśavartin</s> and the lordship of <s>Māra</s> in the city of the gods was exercised;

children.text: bhukta kāmāḥ samṛddhā varā no ca tṛptībhūt /
children.translated_text: I enjoyed prosperous and supreme sense-pleasures — yet satisfaction never arose!

children.text: kiṃ puno adya māṃ hīnasaṃsevatastṛpti gacchedahaṃ sthānametanna saṃvidyate // Lal_15.54 //
children.translated_text: How then could satisfaction come to me today from resort to these inferior [pleasures]? Such a state does not exist!' // Lal_15.54 //

body.translated_text: As a prince and heir, sovereignty was exercised over the four continents when I was a <s>Cakravartin</s> king endowed with the seven treasures, in the midst of the women's quarters. Lordship over <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Suyāma</s> gods was exercised — from which I fell and came here — and over the <s>Nirmita</s> and <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> [heavens], with supreme personal glory — [all] enjoyed by me in the past!

body.text: api ca -
body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text:
imu jaṃga apekṣāmyahaṃ chandakā duḥkhitaṃ śokakāntārasaṃsāramadhye sthitam / kleśavyālākule uhyamānaṃ sadā /
aśaraṇamaparāyaṇaṃ mohavidyāndhakāre jarāvyādhimṛtyūbhayaiḥ pīḍitam /
janmaduḥkhaiḥ samabhyāhataṃ vyāhataṃ śatrubhiḥ /
ahamiha samudāniyā dharmanāvaṃ mahātyāgaśīlavratakṣāntivīryābalāṃ dārusaṃbhārasaṃghātitāṃ sāramadhyāśayairvajrakaiḥ saṃgṛhītāṃ dṛḍhām / svayamahamabhiruhya nāvāmimātmāno 'vatīrya saṃsāraoghe ahaṃ tārayiṣye anantaṃ jagat /
śokasaṃsārakāntāraroṣormirāgagrahāvartavairākule dustare / eva cittaṃ mama // Lal_15.55 //
body.translated_text: 'I look upon this world, O <s>Chandaka</s> — suffering, standing in the wilderness of grief and <s>saṃsāra</s>, tossed about constantly in [the thicket] swarming with the serpents of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), without refuge, without recourse, in the darkness of delusion and ignorance, tormented by the terrors of old age, disease, and death, struck and beaten by the sufferings of birth, assailed by enemies! I shall here construct the great ship of <s>dharma</s> — made strong with the timber of great generosity, morality, observances, patience, and vigor, held together by firm vajra-like resolves of essential intent — and I myself, having boarded this ship and descended into the flood of <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall ferry across the infinite world — [across this flood] difficult to cross, turbulent with waves of anger, [infested with] the whirlpools and crocodiles of passion, the wilderness of grief and <s>saṃsāra</s> and enmity! Such is my intention! // Lal_15.55 //

children.text: tadātmanottīrya idaṃ bhavārṇavaṃ savairadṛṣṭigrahakleśarākṣasam /
children.translated_text: Having myself crossed this ocean of existence — with its sharks of enmity, wrong views, <s>kleśas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> —

children.text: svayaṃ taritvā ca anantakaṃ jagat sthale sthapeṣye ajarāmare śive // Lal_15.56 //
children.translated_text: having crossed, [I shall ferry] the infinite world and establish it on the shore — in the auspicious [state] free from old age and death! // Lal_15.56 //

body.text: tadā chandako bhūyasyā mātrayā prarudannevamāha - deva eṣa vyavasāyasya niścayaḥ?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Chandaka</s>, weeping yet more profusely, said: 'O lord, is this your firm resolve and determination?'

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu chandaka mahya niścayaṃ mokṣasattvārtha hitārthamudyatam /
children.translated_text: 'Hear, <s>Chandaka</s>, my determination — [I am] devoted to liberation, to the welfare of beings, to their benefit;

children.text: acalācalamavyayaṃ dṛḍhaṃ merurājeva yathā suduścalam // Lal_15.57 //
children.translated_text: immovable, unwavering, imperishable, firm — like the king of mountains, <s>Meru</s>, most difficult to shake! // Lal_15.57 //

body.text: chandaka āha - kīdṛśa āryaputrasya niścayaḥ?
body.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s> said: 'Of what nature is the noble son's determination?'

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: vajrāśaniḥ paraśuśaktiśarāśca varṣe vidyutpratānajvalitaḥ kvathitaṃ ca loham /
children.translated_text: 'Even if thunderbolts, axes, lances, arrows were to rain down, or blazing lightning-streaks, or molten metal,

children.text: ādīptaśailaśikharā prapateyu mūrdhni naivā ahaṃ puna janeya gṛhābhilāṣam // Lal_15.58 //
children.translated_text: or burning mountain-peaks were to fall upon my head — I would never again generate desire for household life! // Lal_15.58 //

children.text: tadā amara nabhagatāḥ kilakilā muñciṣu kusumavṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the gods, stationed in the sky, let forth cries of wonder and rained down flowers:

children.text: jaya he paramamatidharā jagati abhayadāyakā nātha // Lal_15.59 //
children.translated_text: 'Victory! O one of supreme and firm resolve, giver of fearlessness to the world, O Lord!' // Lal_15.59 //

children.text: na rajyate puruṣavarasya mānasaṃ nabho yathā tamarajadhūmaketubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The mind of the best of men is not stained [by passions], just as the sky is not [stained] by dust, particles, or smoke;

children.text: na lipyate viṣayasukheṣu nirmalo jale yathā navanalinaṃ samudbhavam // Lal_15.59 //
children.translated_text: the stainless one is not defiled by the pleasures of sense-objects, just as a newly-born lotus [is not defiled] by water! // Lal_15.59 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya niścayaṃ viditvā śāntamatiśca devaputro lalitavyūhaśca devaputraḥ kapilavastuni mahānagare sarvastrīpuruṣadārakadārikānāmapasvāpanamakurutām, sarvaśabdāṃścāntardhāpayāmāsatuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, having learned the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s determination, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Śāntamati</s> and the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Lalitavyūha</s> put all the men, women, boys, and girls of the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> to sleep, and caused all sounds to disappear. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ sarvaṃ nagarajanaṃ prasuptaṃ viditvā ardharātrisamayaṃ copasthitaṃ jñātvā puṣyaṃ ca nakṣatrādhipatiṃ yuktaṃ jñātvā sāṃprataṃ niṣkramaṇakāla iti jñātvā chandakamāmantrayate sma - chandaka māṃ medānīṃ khedaya / prayaccha me kaṇṭhakaṃ samalaṃkṛtya, mā ca vilambiṣṭhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, knowing that all the people of the city were fast asleep, and knowing that the midnight hour had arrived, and knowing that the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation was in conjunction, and knowing 'Now is the time for going forth,' addressed <s>Chandaka</s>: '<s>Chandaka</s>, do not make me weary now! Give me <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, fully adorned, and do not delay!' //

body.text: samanantarodāhṛtā ca bodhisattveneyaṃ vāk / atha tatkṣaṇameva catvāro lokapālā bodhisattvasya vacanamupaśrutya svakasvakāni ca bhavanāni gatvā bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe svaiḥ svairvyūhaistvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ punarapi kapilavastumahānagaramāgacchanti sma //
body.translated_text: No sooner had the <s>Bodhisattva</s> uttered these words than, at that very instant, the four <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians), hearing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s words, went to their respective abodes and quickly, quickly returned again to the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> with their respective arrays, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tatra dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo gandharvādhipatiḥ pūrvasyā diśa āgato 'bhūt sārdhamanekairgandharvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairnānātūryasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena / āgatya ca kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathāgataḥ pūrvāṃ diśamupaniśrityāsthāt bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: There <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the great king, lord of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, came from the eastern direction, together with many <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s>, with various instruments of music playing. Having come, he circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and, as he had come, stationed himself to the east, paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: dakṣiṇasyā diśo virūḍhako mahārājo 'bhyāgato 'bhūt sārdhamanekaiḥ kumbhāṇḍakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairnānāmuktāhārapāṇipralambitairnānāmaṇiratnaparigṛhītairvividha - gandhodakapūrṇaghaṭaparigṛhītaiḥ / āgatya ca kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathāgata eva dakṣiṇāṃ diśamupaniśrityāsthāt bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the southern direction, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the great king, came together with many <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, with various pearl necklaces dangling from their hands, holding various gem-jewels, holding pitchers filled with various fragrant water. Having come, he circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and, as he had come, stationed himself to the south, paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: paścimāyā diśo virūpākṣo mahārāja āgato 'bhūt sārdhamanekairnāgakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairnānāmuktāhārapāṇipralambitairnānāmaṇiratnaparigṛhītairgandha - cūrṇapuṣpavarṣameghasamutthitaiśca mṛdubhiḥ sugandhibhirnānāvātaiḥ pravāyadbhiḥ / āgatya ca kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathāgata eva paścimāṃ diśamupaniśrityāsthāt bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the western direction, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the great king, came together with many <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Nāgas</s>, with various pearl necklaces dangling from their hands, holding various gem-jewels, with clouds of incense-powder and flower-rain arisen, with gentle, fragrant, various winds blowing. Having come, he circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and, as he had come, stationed himself to the west, paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: uttarasyā diśaḥ kubero mahārāja āgato 'bhūt sārdhamanekairyakṣakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairjyotīrasamaṇiratnaparigṛhītairdīpikāpāṇiparigṛhītaiśca jvalitolkāpāṇiparigṛhītairdhanurasiśaraśaktitomaratriśūlacakrakaṇayabhindipālādinānāpraharaṇaparigṛhītairdṛḍha - saṃnaddhavarbhitakavacitaiḥ / āgatya kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathāgata evottarāṃ diśamupaniśrityāsthāt bodhisattvaṃ namasyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the northern direction, <s>Kubera</s>, the great king, came together with many <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, holding gem-jewels radiant as fireflies, holding lamps in their hands, holding blazing torches in their hands, bearing various weapons — bows, swords, arrows, spears, lances, tridents, discuses, iron clubs, slings, and other [arms] — firmly armored and clad in cuirasses. Having come, he circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and, as he had come, stationed himself to the north, paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: śakraśca devānāmindraḥ sārdhaṃ trāyatriṃśadevairāgato 'bhūt divyapuṣpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvarachatradhvajapatākāvataṃsakābharaṇaparigṛhītaiḥ / āgatya kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathāgata eva saparivāra uparyantarikṣe 'sthāt bodhisattvaṃ namaskurvan //
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, came together with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, bearing divine flowers, incense, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, pennants, wreaths, and ornaments. Having come, he circumambulated the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and, as he had come, with his retinue, stood above in the sky, paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaśchandako bodhisattvasya vacanamupaśrutyāśrupūrṇanayano bodhisattvamevamāha - āryaputra tvaṃ ca kālajño velajñaśca samayajñaḥ / ayaṃ ca akālo 'samayo gantum / tatkimājñāpayasi iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Chandaka</s>, hearing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s words, his eyes filled with tears, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'O noble son, you are one who knows the time, knows the occasion, and knows the season. But this is an improper time and occasion for going. What then do you command?' //

body.text: bodhisattva āha - chandaka, ayaṃ sa kālaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: '<s>Chandaka</s>, this is the [right] time.'

body.text: chandaka āha - kasyāryaputra kālaḥ?
body.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s> said: 'The time for what, O noble son?'

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: yattanmayā prārthitu dīrgharātraṃ sattvānamarthaṃ parimārgatā hi /
children.translated_text: That which I have sought for a long time — the welfare of beings I have pursued;

children.text: avāpya bodhiṃ ajarāmaraṃ padaṃ moce jagattasya kṣaṇo upasthitaḥ // Lal_15.60 //
children.translated_text: having attained awakening, the state free from aging and death, I shall liberate the world — that moment has arrived! // Lal_15.60 //

body.text: iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: Such is the nature of things here. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: bhaumāntarīkṣāśca tathaiva pālāḥ śakraśca devādhipatiḥ sayakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The guardians of the earth and the sky, and <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, with the <s>Yakṣas</s>,

children.text: yāmāśca devāstuṣitāśca nirmitāḥ paranirmitodyukta tathaiva devāḥ // Lal_15.61 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Yāma</s> gods, and the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, and the <s>Nirmita</s> [gods], and the <s>Paranirmita</s> gods likewise — // Lal_15.61 //

body.text: varuṇo manasvī api nāgarājā anāvataptaśca tathaiva māgaraḥ

children.text: abhiyukta te cāpyabhipūjanārthaṃ naiṣkramyakāle narapuṃgavasya // Lal_15.62 //
children.translated_text: they all applied themselves for the worship at the time of the great going forth of the bull among men. // Lal_15.62 //

body.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> the wise, and the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Anāvatapta</s>, and likewise <s>Sāgara</s> —

children.text: ye cāpi rūpāvacareṣu devāḥ praśāntacārī saha dhyānagocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those gods who dwell in the <s>Rūpāvacara</s> (Form Realm) heavens, of peaceful conduct, with the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> —

children.text: abhiyukta te cāpyabhipūjanārthaṃ trailokyapūjyasya narottamasya // Lal_15.63 //
children.translated_text: they too applied themselves for the worship of the best of men, worthy of worship by the three worlds. // Lal_15.63 //

children.text: daśādiśo 'bhyāgata śuddhasattvāḥ sahāyakāḥ pūrvacariṃ carantaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the ten directions came beings of pure nature, companions who had practiced the former conduct:

children.text: drakṣyāmahe niṣkramaṇaṃ jinasya pūjāṃ kariṣyāmi tathānurūpām // Lal_15.64 //
children.translated_text: 'We shall behold the going forth of the <s>Jina</s> and perform worship befitting him!' // Lal_15.64 //

children.text: sa cāpi guhyādhipatirmahātmā pradīptavajro nabhasi pratisthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that great-souled lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret ones), with blazing <s>vajra</s>, standing in the sky,

children.text: saṃnaddhagātro balavīryavikramaḥ kareṇa guhya jvalamānu vajram // Lal_15.65 //
children.translated_text: with armored body, of the valor and might of strength, holding in his hand the flaming <s>vajra</s> — // Lal_15.65 //

children.text: candraśca sūryo ubhi devaputrau pradakṣiṇaṃ vāmaku supratisthitau /
children.translated_text: And <s>Candra</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>, both <s>Devaputras</s>, stationed to the right and left, well-positioned,

children.text: daśāṅgulī añjalibhirgṛhītvā naiṣkramyaśabdo 'nuvicārayanti // Lal_15.66 //
children.translated_text: with ten fingers held in palms-joined [salute], they proclaim the word of going forth. // Lal_15.66 //

children.text: puṣyaśca nakṣatra sapāriṣadyo audārikaṃ nirmiṇi ātmabhāvam /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation, with its retinue, manifested a large form,

children.text: sthitvāgratastasya narottamasya manojñaghoṣābhirutaṃ pramuñcat // Lal_15.67 //
children.translated_text: and standing before that best of men, it released a melodious and beautiful sound: // Lal_15.67 //

body.text: sarve 'dya siddhāḥ śubha tubhya maṅgalāḥ puṣyaśca yuktaḥ samayaśca gantum /
body.translated_text: 'All auspicious signs are fulfilled for you today! <s>Puṣya</s> is in conjunction and the season for going has come!

body.text: ahaṃ pi yāsyāmi tvayaiva sārdhaṃ / anuttarāyo bhava rāgasūdanaḥ // Lal_15.68 //
body.translated_text: I too shall go together with you! Be the unsurpassed one, the destroyer of passion!' // Lal_15.68 //

children.text: saṃcodakaścodayi devaputra uttiṣṭha śīghraṃ balavīryaudgataḥ /
children.translated_text: The exhorting <s>Devaputra</s> exhorted: 'Arise quickly, arisen in strength and vigor!

children.text: duḥkhairhatāṃstāraya sarvasattvān naiṣkramyakālaḥ samupasthitaste // Lal_15.69 //
children.translated_text: Ferry across all beings struck by sufferings! The time of going forth has arrived for you!' // Lal_15.69 //

children.text: samāgatā devasahasrakoṭyaḥ pravarṣamāṇā kusumān manojñān /
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of gods have assembled, showering beautiful flowers;

children.text: sa cāpi paryaṅkavare niṣaṇṇo devairvṛto bhrājati dīptatejaḥ // Lal_15.70 //
children.translated_text: and he, seated on the excellent cross-legged [seat], surrounded by gods, shines with blazing splendor. // Lal_15.70 //

children.text: nagare istrika dārakāśca puruṣā yāścābhavan dārikāḥ
children.translated_text: In the city, women and boys, men and girls —

children.text: sarve te śayitā kilāntamanaso īryāpathebhyaścyutāḥ /
children.translated_text: all of them were asleep, their minds wearied, fallen from [their normal] postures.

children.text: hasti aśvagavāśca sārikaśukāḥ kroñcā mayūrāstathā
children.translated_text: Elephants, horses, cows, <s>Sārikā</s> birds, parrots, curlews, and peacocks likewise —

children.text: sarve te śayitā kilāntamanasaḥ paśyanti rūpaṃ na te // Lal_15.71 //
children.translated_text: all of them were asleep, their minds wearied; they perceive no form. // Lal_15.71 //

children.text: ye cā te dṛḍhavajratomaradharā śākyaiḥ sutāḥ sthāpitāḥ
children.translated_text: And those who bore firm <s>vajras</s> and lances, stationed by the <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: hastiaśvaratheṣu toraṇavare te cāpyavasvāpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: on elephants, horses, chariots, and at the finest gateways — they too had been put to sleep.

children.text: rājā rājakumāra pārthivajanaḥ sarve prasuptā bhavan
children.translated_text: The king, princes, courtly folk — all were fast asleep;

children.text: api cā nārigaṇā vinagnavasanā suptā na te buddhiṣū // Lal_15.72 //
children.translated_text: and also the company of women, their garments disheveled, asleep — they were not in their senses. // Lal_15.72 //

children.text: so ca brahmaruto manojñavasanaḥ kalaviṅkaghoṣasvaro
children.translated_text: He, with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, in lovely garments, with a voice like the <s>Kalaviṅka</s> bird,

children.text: rātrau nirgata ardharātrasamaye taṃ chandakaṃ abravīt /
children.translated_text: went out in the night, at the midnight hour, and said to <s>Chandaka</s>:

children.text: sādhū chandaka dehi kaṇṭhaku mama svālaṃkṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Good <s>Chandaka</s>, give me <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, well-adorned and beautiful!

children.text: mā vighnaṃ kuru me dadāhi capalaṃ yadi me priyaṃ manyase // Lal_15.73 //
children.translated_text: Do not obstruct me — give him quickly, if you regard me with affection!' // Lal_15.73 //

body.text:
kva tvaṃ yāsyasi sattvasārathivarā kiṃ aśvakāryaṃ ca te
kālajñaḥ samayajña dharmacaraṇo kālo na gantu kvacit /
dvārāste pithitā dṛḍhārgalakṛtā ko dāsyate tāṃ tava /

children.text: śakreṇā manasātha cetanavaśātte dvāra muktā kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'By <s>Śakra</s>'s will and the power of intention, those gates have been opened!'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā chandaka harṣito puna dukhī aśrūṇi so 'vartayī /
children.translated_text: Seeing this, <s>Chandaka</s>, delighted and yet sorrowful, shed tears:

children.text: hā dhikko mi sahāyu kiṃ tu kurumī dhāvāmi kāṃ vā diśaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Alas, woe is me, the companion! What shall I do? Where shall I run, to which direction?

children.text: ugraṃtejadhareṇa vākyu bhaṇitaṃ śakyaṃ na saṃdhāritum // Lal_15.74 //
children.translated_text: The word spoken by the one who bears fierce splendor cannot be defied!' // Lal_15.74 //

body.translated_text: 'Where will you go, O best charioteer of beings? What use is a horse? You who know the time and season, one of <s>dharma</s>-conduct — this is no time to go anywhere! Your gates are shut and firmly barred — who will open them for you?'

children.text: sā senā caturaṅginī balavatī kiṃ bhū karotīha hā
children.translated_text: 'That mighty four-fold army — what use is it now? Alas!

children.text: rājā rājakumāra pārthiva jano nemaṃ hi budhyanti te /
children.translated_text: The king, the princes, the courtly folk — they are not aware of this!

children.text: strīsaṃghaḥ śayitastathā yaśavatī osvāpitā devataiḥ
children.translated_text: The company of women lies asleep, and <s>Yaśovatī</s> [too] has been put to sleep by the gods.

children.text: hā dhiggacchati sidhyate 'sya praṇidhiryaścintitaḥ pūrvaśaḥ // Lal_15.75 //
children.translated_text: Alas! He goes, and that vow contemplated long ago is being fulfilled!' // Lal_15.75 //

children.text: devāḥ koṭisahasra hṛṣṭamanasastaṃ chandakaṃ abruvan
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of gods, with delighted minds, said to <s>Chandaka</s>:

children.text: sādhu chandaka dehi kaṇṭhakavaraṃ mā khedayī nāyakam /
children.translated_text: 'Good <s>Chandaka</s>, give the excellent <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>! Do not make the leader weary!

children.text: bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgatūryanayutā devāsurairvāditā
children.translated_text: Kettledrums, conches, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>nayutas</s> of instruments have been sounded by gods and <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: naivedaṃ pratibudhyate puravaraṃ osvāpitaṃ devataiḥ // Lal_15.76 //
children.translated_text: yet the best of cities does not awaken — it has been put to sleep by the gods!' // Lal_15.76 //

children.text: paśya chandaka antarīkṣa vimalaṃ divyā prabhā śobhate
children.translated_text: 'See, <s>Chandaka</s>, the clear sky — divine radiance shines!

children.text: paśya tvaṃ bahubodhisattvanayutāṃ ye pūjanāyāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: See the many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have come for worship!

children.text: śakraṃ paśya śacīpatiṃ balavṛtaṃ dvārasthitaṃ bhrājate
children.translated_text: See <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of <s>Śacī</s>, standing at the gate, surrounded by his forces, shining!

children.text: devāṃścāpyasurāṃśca kinnaragaṇāṃ ye pūjanārthāgatāḥ // Lal_15.77 //
children.translated_text: And [see] the gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and hosts of <s>Kinnaras</s> who have come for worship!' // Lal_15.77 //

children.text: śrutvā chandaka devatāna vacanaṃ taṃ kaṇṭhakaṃ ālapī
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the gods, <s>Chandaka</s> addressed <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>:

children.text: eṣvāgacchati sattvasārathivaraḥ tvaṃ tāva heṣiṣyase /
children.translated_text: 'The best charioteer of beings is coming — now is the time for you to neigh!'

children.text: so taṃ varṣikuvarṇa kāñcanakhuraṃ svālaṃkṛtaṃ kṛtvanā
children.translated_text: And he brought that rain-cloud-colored one with golden hooves, well-adorned,

children.text: upanetī guṇasāgarasya vahanaṃ rodantako durmanā // Lal_15.78 //
children.translated_text: the mount of the ocean of virtues — weeping, heavy-hearted. // Lal_15.78 //

children.text: eṣā te varalakṣaṇā hitakarā aśvaḥ sujātaḥ śubho
children.translated_text: 'Here is your well-marked, beneficent horse, well-born and auspicious;

children.text: gaccha sidhyatu tubhya eva praṇidhiryaścintitaḥ pūrvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: go — may that vow contemplated long ago be fulfilled for you!

children.text: ye te vighnakarā vrajantu praśamaṃ āsāṃ vrataṃ sidhyatāṃ
children.translated_text: May those who obstruct you go to peace! May your vow be accomplished!

children.text: bhavahī sarvajagasya saukhyadadanaḥ svargasya śāntyāstathā // Lal_15.79 //
children.translated_text: Be the giver of happiness to all the world, and of heaven and peace!' // Lal_15.79 //

children.text: sarvā kampita ṣaḍvikāra dharaṇī śayanādyadā sotthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The entire earth trembled in six ways when he arose from his bed;

children.text: ārūḍhaḥ śaśipūrṇamaṇḍalanibhaṃ taṃ aśvarājottamam /
children.translated_text: he mounted that king of horses, bright as the full moon's orb.

children.text: pālā pāṇiviśuddhapadmavimalā nyasayiṃsu aśvottame
children.translated_text: The guardians, with pure lotus-like hands, placed [their hands] on the excellent horse;

children.text: śakro brahma ubhau ca tasya purato darśyanti mārgo hyayam // Lal_15.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, both before him, pointed out: 'This is the way!' // Lal_15.80 //

children.text: ābhā tena pramukta acchavimalā obhāsitā medinī
children.translated_text: The radiance released by him, clear and stainless, illuminated the earth;

children.text: sarve śānta apāya sattva sukhitā kleśairna bādhyī tadā /
children.translated_text: all the lower realms were calmed, beings were made happy — afflictions did not torment [them] then.

children.text: puṣpā varṣiṣu tūryakoṭi raṇiṣū devāsurāstuṣṭuvuḥ
children.translated_text: Flowers rained, <s>koṭīs</s> of instruments resounded, gods and <s>Asuras</s> praised him;

children.text: sarve kṛtva pradakṣiṇaṃ puravaraṃ gacchanti harṣānvitāḥ // Lal_15.81 //
children.translated_text: all, having circumambulated the best of cities, departed, filled with joy! // Lal_15.81 //

children.text: puravarottami devata dīnamanā upagamya gacchati mahāpuruṣe /
