children.translated_text: The deity of the best of cities, sorrowful in mind, approached as the great person was departing;

children.text: purataḥ sthitā karuṇadīnamanā girayā samālapati padmamukham // Lal_15.82 //
children.translated_text: standing before him, sorrowful with compassion, she addressed the lotus-faced one in a verse: // Lal_15.82 //

children.text: tamasākulaṃ bhuvimu sarvapuraṃ nagaraṃ na śobhati tvaya rahitam /
children.translated_text: 'This entire city on earth is enveloped in darkness; the city does not shine without you;

children.text: na mamātra kāci rati prītikarī tyaktaṃ tvayā ca yadidaṃ bhavanam // Lal_15.83 //
children.translated_text: there is no delight or joy for me here — and you have abandoned this dwelling! // Lal_15.83 //

children.text: na punaḥ śruṇiṣyi rutu pakṣigaṇe antaḥpure madhuraveṇuravam /
children.translated_text: No longer shall I hear the sounds and songs of birds in the inner palace, the sweet flute-melody,

children.text: maṅgalyaśabda tatha gītaravaṃ pratibodhanaṃ tava anantayaśaḥ // Lal_15.84 //
children.translated_text: the auspicious sounds and the singing that awakened you, O one of infinite glory! // Lal_15.84 //

children.text: darśe na bhūyu surasiddhagaṇāṃ kurvantu pūja tava rātridivam /
children.translated_text: No longer shall I see the hosts of gods and <s>Siddhas</s> performing worship for you day and night;

children.text: ghrāyiṣyi gandha na ca divya punaḥ tvayi nirgate nihatakleśagaṇe // Lal_15.85 //
children.translated_text: no longer shall I smell the divine fragrances — now that you have departed, O destroyer of the hosts of afflictions! // Lal_15.85 //

children.text: nirbhuktamālyamiva paryuṣitaṃ tyaktaṃ tvayādya bhavanaṃ hi tathā /
children.translated_text: Like a discarded, withered garland, you have now abandoned this dwelling;

children.text: naṭaraṅgakalpa pratibhāyati me tvayi nirgate na bhuyu tejaśiri // Lal_15.86 //
children.translated_text: it appears to me like a stage-set — now that you have departed, there is no longer splendor and glory! // Lal_15.86 //

children.text: ojo balaṃ harasi sarvapure na ca śobhate aṭavitulyamidam /
children.translated_text: You take away the vigor and strength of the entire city; it does not shine and appears like a wilderness!

children.text: vitathaṃ ṛṣīṇa vacanādya bhutaṃ yehī viyākṛtu bhuvi cakrabalo // Lal_15.87 //
children.translated_text: The words of the sages have today become true — those who prophesied that [you would be] the powerful wheel-turner on earth! // Lal_15.87 //

children.text: abalaṃ balaṃ bhuvimu śākyabalaṃ ucchinna vaṃśa iha rājakule /
children.translated_text: Powerless now is the power of the <s>Śākyas</s> on earth; the lineage is cut off here in the royal family!

children.text: āśā pranaṣṭa iha śākyagaṇe tvayi nirgate mahati puṇyadrume // Lal_15.88 //
children.translated_text: Hope has perished here for the <s>Śākya</s> clan — now that you have departed, O great tree of merit! // Lal_15.88 //

body.text: ahameva tubhya gati gacchayamī yatha tvaṃ prayāsi amalā vimalā /
body.translated_text: I myself shall go with you, wherever you go, O stainless and spotless one!

body.text: api cā kṛpā karuṇa saṃjaniya vyavalokayasva bhavanaṃ tvamidam // Lal_15.89 //
body.translated_text: But generate compassion and mercy, and look upon this dwelling!' // Lal_15.89 //

children.text: vyavalokya caiva bhavanaṃ matimān madhurasvaro giramudīritavān /
children.translated_text: Having looked upon the dwelling, the wise one, with a sweet voice, uttered this word:

children.text: nāhaṃ pravekṣi kapilasya puraṃ aprāpya jātimaraṇāntakaram // Lal_15.90 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall not enter the city of <s>Kapila</s> again until I have attained the destroyer of birth and death!' // Lal_15.90 //

children.text: sthānāsanaṃ śayanacaṃkramaṇaṃ na kariṣyahaṃ kapilavastumukham /
children.translated_text: I shall not sit, stand, lie down, or walk [here again], facing <s>Kapilavastu</s>,

children.text: yāvanna labdha varabodhi mayā ajarāmaraṃ padavaraṃ hyamṛtam // Lal_15.91 //
children.translated_text: until I have attained the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>, the ageless, deathless, supreme, immortal state! // Lal_15.91 //

children.text: yadasau jagatpradhāno niṣkrāntu bodhisattvo tasyā nabhe vrajanto stavayiṃsu apsarāṇām /
children.translated_text: When that foremost of the world, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, had gone forth, as he traveled through the sky, the <s>Apsarases</s> praised him:

children.text: eṣa maha dakṣiṇīyo eṣa maha puṇyakṣetraṃ puṇyarthikāna kṣetraṃ amṛtāphalasya dātā // Lal_15.92 //
children.translated_text: 'This one is greatly worthy of offerings! This one is a great field of merit, a field for those who seek merit, a giver of the fruit of the deathless! // Lal_15.92 //

children.text: ena bahukalpakoṭī dānadamasaṃyamenā samudānitāsya bodhiḥ sattvakaruṇāyamānā /
children.translated_text: By him, over many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through giving, self-restraint, and discipline, his <s>Bodhi</s> has been accumulated, with compassion for beings.

children.text: eṣa pariśuddhaśīlo suvrata akhaṇḍacārī na ca kāma naiva bhogāṃ prārthentu śīlarakṣī // Lal_15.93 //
children.translated_text: This one is of purified morality, observing excellent and unbroken vows — he desires neither pleasures nor enjoyments, a guardian of morality! // Lal_15.93 //

children.text: eṣa sada kṣāntivādī chidyanti aṅgamaṅge na ca krodhu naiva roṣaḥ sattvaparitrāyaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: This one is always an advocate of patience — even when his limbs and sub-limbs are cut, there is neither anger nor rage, for the sake of protecting beings.

children.text: eṣa sada vīryavanto avikhinna kalpakoṭyaḥ samudānitāsya bodhiryaṣṭā ca yakṣakoṭīḥ // Lal_15.94 //
children.translated_text: This one is always endowed with vigor, unwearied over <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; his <s>Bodhi</s> has been accumulated, and he has worshipped <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Yakṣas</s> [and Buddhas]. // Lal_15.94 //

children.text: eṣa sada dhyānadhyāyī śāntapraśāntacitto dhyāyitva sarvakleśāṃ moceṣyi sattvakoṭīḥ /
children.translated_text: This one is always a meditator, of peaceful, supremely tranquil mind; having meditated upon all afflictions, he shall liberate <s>koṭis</s> of beings.

children.text: eṣo asaṅga prājñaḥ kalpairvikalpamukto kalpairvimuktacitto jinu bheṣyate svayaṃbhūḥ // Lal_15.95 //
children.translated_text: This one is unattached, wise, freed from conceptualization over [many] <s>kalpas</s>, his mind liberated over [many] <s>kalpas</s> — he shall become a <s>Jina</s>, a <s>Svayambhū</s> (Self-Arisen One)! // Lal_15.95 //

children.text: eṣa sada maitracitto karuṇāya pāraprāpto mudito upekṣadhyāyī brāhme pathi vidhijñaḥ /
children.translated_text: This one is always of loving mind, who has reached the far shore of compassion, joyful, a meditator on equanimity, skilled in the path of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: eṣo 'tidevadevo devebhi pūjanīyo śubhavimalaśuddhacitto guṇaniyutapāraprāptaḥ // Lal_15.96 //
children.translated_text: This one is a god beyond gods, worthy of worship by the gods, of pure, stainless, purified mind, who has reached the far shore of <s>nayutas</s> of virtues! // Lal_15.96 //

children.text: śaraṇaṃ bhayārditānāṃ dīpo acakṣuṣāṇāṃ layano upadrutānāṃ vaidyaścirāturāṇām /
children.translated_text: A refuge for the terror-stricken, a lamp for the sightless, a shelter for the afflicted, a physician for the long-ailing!

children.text: rājeva dharmarājo indraḥ sahasranetro brahmasvayaṃbhubhūtaḥ kāyapraśabdhacitto // Lal_15.97 //
children.translated_text: Like a <s>Dharma</s>-king among kings, like <s>Indra</s> of the thousand eyes, like <s>Brahmā</s> the Self-Arisen, with body and mind at peace! // Lal_15.97 //

children.text: dhīraḥ prabhūtaprajño vīro viviktacittaḥ śūraḥ kileśaghātī ajitaṃjayo jitāriḥ /
children.translated_text: Steadfast, of abundant wisdom, a hero of secluded mind, a champion who slays the afflictions, unconquered, victorious, having conquered his enemies!

children.text: siṃho bhayaprahīṇo nāgaḥ sudāntacitto ṛṣabho gaṇapradhānaḥ kṣāntaḥ prahīṇakopaḥ // Lal_15.98 //
children.translated_text: A lion who has abandoned fear, an elephant of well-tamed mind, a bull foremost among assemblies, patient, who has abandoned anger! // Lal_15.98 //

body.text:
candraḥ prabhāsayantaḥ sūryo 'vabhāsakārī
ulkā pradyotakārī sarvatamovimuktaḥ /

children.text: padmaṃ anopaliptaṃ puṣpaṃ suśīlapatraṃ
children.translated_text: A lotus unstained, a flower with leaves of good morality,

children.text: merūrakampi śāstā pṛthivī yathopajīvyo
children.translated_text: an unshaking <s>Meru</s>, a teacher, like the earth sustaining [all],

children.text: ratanākaro akṣobhyaḥ // Lal_15.99 //
children.translated_text: a mine of jewels, unshakable! // Lal_15.99 //

body.translated_text: A moon illuminating, a sun giving light, a torch giving radiance, freed from all darkness!

children.text: ena jitu kleśamāro ena jitu skandhamāro ena jitu mṛtyumāro nihato 'sya deva(putra)māro /
children.translated_text: By him the <s>Māra</s> of afflictions shall be conquered, by him the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates shall be conquered, by him the <s>Māra</s> of death shall be conquered, and the <s>Māra</s> of the <s>devaputras</s> shall be slain!

children.text: eṣa maha sārthavāho kupathapratisthitānāṃ aṣṭāṅgamārgaśreṣṭhaṃ deśeṣyate nacireṇā // Lal_15.100 //
children.translated_text: This one is a great caravan-leader for those established on wrong paths — he shall teach the supreme Noble Eightfold Path before long! // Lal_15.100 //

children.text: jaramaraṇakleśaghātī tamatimiravipramukto
children.translated_text: Slayer of old age, death, and affliction, freed from the darkness of ignorance,

children.text: bhuvi divi ca saṃpraghuṣṭo jinu bheṣyate svayaṃbhūḥ /
children.translated_text: proclaimed on earth and in heaven, he shall become a <s>Jina</s>, a Self-Arisen One!

children.text: stuta stavitu aprameyo varapuruṣarūpadhārī
children.translated_text: Praised, to be praised, immeasurable, bearing the form of the supreme person —

children.text: yatpuṇya tvāṃ stavitvā bhoma yatha vādisiṃhaḥ // Lal_15.101 //
children.translated_text: whatever merit [we gain] by praising you, may we become like lions among speakers! // Lal_15.101 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'bhiniṣkrānto bodhisattvo 'tikramya śākyānatikramya kroḍyānatikramya mallān maineyānāmanuvaineye niga me ṣaṭsu yojaneṣu / tatra bodhisattvasya rātriprabhāto 'bhūt / tato bodhisattvo kaṇṭhakādavatīrya dharaṇītale sthitvā taṃ mahāntaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragasaṃghaṃ visarjayati sma / visarjya cāsyaitadabhūt -imānyābharaṇāni kaṇṭhakaṃ ca chandakasya haste visarjayāmīti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> went forth. Crossing beyond the <s>Śākyas</s>, crossing beyond the <s>Kroḍyas</s>, crossing beyond the <s>Mallas</s>, in the <s>Maineya</s> domain, in the <s>Anuvaineya</s> town, at six <s>yojanas</s> [distance]. There, dawn broke for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having dismounted from <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, standing on the ground, dismissed that great assembly of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. Having dismissed them, he thought: 'I shall place these ornaments and <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> into <s>Chandaka</s>'s hands and send them back.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvaśchandakamāmantryaitadavocat - gaccha tvaṃ chandaka, imānyābharaṇāni kaṇṭhakaṃ ca gṛhītvā nivartayasva / yatra ca pradeśe chandako nivṛttastatra caityaṃ sthāpitamabhūt / adyāpi taccaityaṃ chandakanivartanamiti jñāyate //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, addressing <s>Chandaka</s>, said this: 'Go, <s>Chandaka</s>! Take these ornaments and <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> and turn back.' And at the spot where <s>Chandaka</s> turned back, a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) was established. To this day, that <s>caitya</s> is known as '<s>Chandakanivartana</s>' (Chandaka's Turning Back). //

body.text: punaśca bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - kathaṃ ca nāma cūḍā ca pravrajyā ceti / sa khaḍgena cūḍāṃ chittvā antarikṣe kṣipati sma / sā ca trāyatriṃśatā devaiḥ parigṛhītābhūt pūjārtham / adyāpi ca trāyatriṃśatsu deveṣu cūḍāmaho vartate / tatrāpi caityaṃ sthāpitamabhūt / adyāpi ca taccūḍāpratigrahaṇamiti jñāyate //
body.translated_text: Then again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'How can a topknot and the going-forth go together?' With his sword he cut off his topknot and threw it into the sky. It was received by the <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> gods for worship. To this day, among the <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> gods, the 'Festival of the Topknot' (<s>Cūḍāmaha</s>) takes place. And there too a <s>caitya</s> was established. To this day, that [caitya] is known as 'The Receiving of the Topknot' (<s>Cūḍāpratigrahana</s>). //

body.text: punarapi bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - kathaṃ hi nāma pravrajyā ca kāśikāni vastrāṇi / sacedvanavāsānurūpāṇi kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi labheyam, śobhanaṃ syāt / atha śuddhavāsakāyikānāṃ devānāmetadabhūt - kāṣāyairbodhisattvasya kāryamiti / tatraiko devaputro divyaṃ rūpamantardhāpya lubdhakarūpeṇa kāṣāyavastraprāvṛto bodhisattvasya purato 'sthāt / atha bodhisattvastametadavocat - sacenme tvaṃ mārṣā kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dadyāḥ, imāni te 'haṃ kāśikāni vastrāṇi dadyām / so 'vocat - etāni vastrāṇi tava śobhante / imāni mama / bodhisattva āha - ahaṃ tvāṃ yācāmi / tatastena lubdhakarūpiṇā devaputreṇa bodhisattvāya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dattānyabhūvan / kāśikāni gṛhṇīte sma / atha sa devaputro gauravajātastāni vastrāṇi ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śirasi kṛtvā tata eva devalokamagamat teṣāṃ pūjārtham / tacchandakena dṛṣṭamabhūt / tatrāpi caityaṃ sthāpitam / adyāpi taccaityaṃ kāṣāyagrahaṇamityevaṃ jñāyate //
body.translated_text: Then again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'How can the going-forth and <s>Kāśika</s> garments go together? If I could obtain saffron robes suitable for forest-dwelling, that would be excellent.' Then the <s>Śuddhavāsakāyika</s> gods had this thought: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> needs saffron robes.' There, one <s>devaputra</s>, hiding his divine form and appearing in the guise of a hunter, clad in saffron garments, stood before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to him: 'If you, good sir, would give me saffron garments, I would give you these <s>Kāśika</s> garments.' He said: 'These garments suit you. These [saffron ones] are mine.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I am asking you.' Then that <s>devaputra</s> in the guise of a hunter gave the saffron garments to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and took the <s>Kāśika</s> garments. Then that <s>devaputra</s>, seized with reverence, placing those garments on his head with both hands, departed immediately to the world of the gods — for the worship of those [garments]. This was witnessed by <s>Chandaka</s>. There too a <s>caitya</s> was established. To this day, that <s>caitya</s> is known as 'The Receiving of the Saffron Robes' (<s>Kāṣāyagrahaṇa</s>). //

body.text: yadā ca bodhisattvena cūḍāṃ chittvā kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi prāvṛtāni, tasmin samaye devaputraśatasahasrā hṛṣṭāstuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ paramapramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā hīhīkārakilikilāprakṣveḍitānirnādanirghoṣaśabdamakārṣuḥ / siddhārtho bho mārṣāḥ kumāraḥ pravrajitaḥ / so 'yamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartayiṣyati / asaṃkhyeyāñjātidharmāṇaḥ sattvān jātyā parimocayiṣyati / yāvajjarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimocya saṃsārasāgarāt pāramuttāryānuttare kṣeme 'bhaye 'śoke nirūpadrave śive virajase 'mṛte dharmadhātau pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyatīti / sa ca śabdaḥ śabdaparaṃparayā yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanamabhyudgato 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: And when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had cut off his topknot and put on the saffron garments, at that time hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s>, thrilled, satisfied, elated, delighted, supremely joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, raised a great clamor of 'Hīhī!' and 'Kilikili!' sounds, exclaiming: '<s>Siddhārtha</s>, the noble prince, has gone forth! He, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, shall turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel! He shall liberate innumerable beings subject to birth from birth — up to liberating them from old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, distress, and despair, and having ferried them across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall establish them in the supreme, secure, fearless, sorrowless, untroubled, auspicious, dustless, immortal realm of <s>Dharma</s>!' And that sound, through a succession of echoes, ascended up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven. //

body.text: tato 'ntaḥpurikābhiḥ kumāramapaśyantībhiḥ grīṣmikavārṣikahaimantikeṣu prāsādeṣvāsaneṣu ca gṛheṣu parimāgamāṇā yadā na paśyanti sma, tadā ekībhūtābhiḥ kurarībhirivotkrṛṣṭamabhūt / tatra kāścitstriyaḥ paramaśokārtā hā tātehi krandanti sma / kāścidbhrātaḥ kāścidbharta iti krandanti sma / kāściddhā nātheti krandanti sma / kāściddhā svāminniti / kāścinnānāpriyavacanapralāpaiḥ, kāścinnānākāyaparisarpikayā rudanti sma / kāścicchīrṣopakarṣikayā, kāścidanyonyamukhāvalokitayā rudanti sma / kāściccakṣuḥparivartikayā, kāścitsvavadanāni vastrairucchādya rudanti sma / kāścidūrū pāṇibhiḥ prasphoṭayantyaḥ, kāściddhṛdayaḥ, pāṇibhistāḍayantyaḥ, kāścidbāhūn pāṇibhiḥ prasphoṭayantyaḥ, kāścicchirāṃsi, kāścicchiraḥ pāṃśubhiravakirantyo rudanti sma / kāścidvikṣiptakeśyaḥ, kāścitkeśaṃ viluñcantyaḥ, kāścidūrdhvabāhavaḥ uccairutkrośanti sma / kāścinmṛgya iva digdhaviddhāḥ sahasā pradhāvantyo
body.translated_text: Then, when the women of the inner palace did not see the prince — searching for him in the summer, rainy-season, and winter palaces, on the seats, and in the chambers — when they could not find him, they all together raised a wail like <s>kurarī</s>-birds. There, some women, overcome by extreme grief, cried out 'O father!' Some cried 'O brother!' Some cried 'O husband!' Some cried 'O protector!' Some cried 'O lord!' Some wept with various lamentations of endearing words; some wept with various writhings of the body. Some wept pulling at their heads; some wept gazing into each other's faces. Some wept rolling their eyes; some wept covering their own faces with garments. Some wept slapping their thighs with their hands; some striking their breasts with their hands; some slapping their arms with their hands; some [striking] their heads; some wept scattering dust upon their heads. Some had disheveled hair; some tore out their hair; some raised their arms high and cried aloud. Some, like does struck by a poisoned [arrow], suddenly ran about,

body.text: rudanti sma / kāścinmārutakampitā iva kadalyaḥ pravikampyamānā rudanti sma / kāściddharaṇītale vinipatitāḥ kiṃcitprāṇāḥ, kāścijjālotkṣiptamatsyā iva pṛthivyāṃ parivartyamānā rudanti sma / kāścinmūlachinnā iva vṛkṣāḥ sahasā dharaṇītale nipatya rudanti sma //
body.translated_text: weeping. Some, like plantain trees shaken by the wind, trembled and wept. Some fell upon the ground with barely a breath; some, like fish thrown from a net, rolled about on the earth weeping. Some, like trees cut at the root, suddenly fell to the ground and wept. //

body.text: taṃ ca śabdaṃ rājā śrutvā śākyānāmantrayate sma - kimetaduccairantaḥpure śabdaḥ śrūyate? śākyā vijñāya kathayanti sma - kumāraḥ kila mahārāja antaḥpure na dṛśyate / rājā āha - kṣipraṃ nagaradvārāṇi pithayata / kumāramabhyantare mṛgayāmaḥ / te sāntarbahirmṛgayante sma / sāntarbahirmṛgayamānā na paśyanti sma //
body.translated_text: The king, hearing that sound, addressed the <s>Śākyas</s>: 'What is this loud sound heard in the inner palace?' The <s>Śākyas</s>, having learned, reported: 'The prince, O great king, is not seen in the inner palace.' The king said: 'Quickly, close the city gates! We shall search for the prince within!' They searched inside and outside. Searching inside and outside, they could not find [him]. //

body.text: mahāprajāpatyapi gautamī paridevamānā mahītale parivartate sma / rājānaṃ śuddhodanamevamāha kṣipraṃ māṃ mahārāja putreṇa samaṅginīṃ kuruṣveti //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> too, lamenting, rolled about on the ground. She said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Quickly, O great king, reunite me with my son!' //

body.text: tato rājā caturdiśamaśvadūtān preṣayati sma / gacchata, yāvatkumāraṃ na paśyatha, tāvanmā nivartayatha //
body.translated_text: Then the king sent horseback messengers in the four directions: 'Go! Do not turn back until you have found the prince!' //

body.text: naimittikairvaipañcikaiśca vyākṛtamabhūt - maṅgaladvāreṇa bodhisattvo 'bhiniṣkramiṣyatīti / te maṅgaladvāreṇa gacchantaḥ paśyanti sma antarāpathi puṣpavarṣaṃ prapatitam / teṣāmetadabhūt - anena pathā kumāro 'bhinirgata iti //
body.translated_text: The sign-readers and diviners had declared: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth through the Auspicious Gate.' Those going through the Auspicious Gate saw, on the road along the way, a shower of flowers that had fallen. They thought: 'The prince has departed by this road.' //

body.text: te svalpamantaraṃ gatvā taṃ devaputraṃ paśyanti sma bodhisattvasya kāśikavastrāṇi śirasi kṛtvā āgacchantam / teṣāmetadabhūt - imāni khalu kumārasya kāśikavastrāṇi / mā khalvanenaiṣāṃ vastrāṇāmarthe kumāro jīvitādvyaparopitaḥ syāt / gṛhṇītainamiti / bhūyaḥ paśyanti sma / tasya pṛṣṭhataścchandakaṃ kaṇṭhakamābharaṇāni cādāyāgacchantam / tataste parasparamūcuḥ - mā tāvadbhoḥ sāhasaṃ mā kārṣṭa / eṣa chandako 'bhyāgacchati kaṇṭhakamādāya, yāvadenaṃ prakṣyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having gone a short distance, they saw that <s>devaputra</s> coming [toward them] with the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Kāśika</s> garments on his head. They thought: 'These are certainly the prince's <s>Kāśika</s> garments. Could the prince have been deprived of his life for the sake of these garments? Seize this [person]!' Then they saw further: behind him, <s>Chandaka</s> was coming, bringing <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> and the ornaments. Then they said to each other: 'Wait, sirs, do not act rashly! Here comes <s>Chandaka</s> bringing <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> — let us first question him.' //

body.text: te chandakaṃ paripṛcchanti sma - he chandaka, mā khalvanenaiva puruṣeṇa kāśikānāṃ vastrāṇāmarthāya kumāro jīvitādvyaparopitaḥ syāt / chandaka āha - na hyetat / api tu anena kumārāya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dattāni / kumāreṇa cāsyaitāni kāśikāni vastrāṇi dattāni / atha sa devaputrastāni vastrāṇyubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śirasi kṛtvā tata eva devalokamagamat teṣāṃ pūjārtham //
body.translated_text: They questioned <s>Chandaka</s>: 'O <s>Chandaka</s>, the prince has not been deprived of his life by this very person for the sake of the <s>Kāśika</s> garments, has he?' <s>Chandaka</s> said: 'No indeed! Rather, this [person] gave saffron garments to the prince, and the prince gave him these <s>Kāśika</s> garments. Then that <s>devaputra</s>, placing those garments on his head with both hands, departed immediately to the world of the gods for their worship.' //

body.text: evaṃ ca te bhūyaśchandakaṃ paripṛcchanti sma - tatkiṃ manyase chandaka gacchāmo vayam? śakyaḥ kumāraḥ pratinivartayitum? sa āha - mā khalu / anivartyaḥ kumāro dṛḍhavīryaparākramaḥ / evaṃ ca tenoktam - na tāvadahaṃ punarapi kapilavastumahānagaraṃ pravekṣyāmi, yāvanme nānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeti / yathā ca kumāreṇoktaṃ tathaiva tadbhaviṣyati / tatkasmāt? anivartyaḥ kumāro dṛḍhavīryaparākramaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus they questioned <s>Chandaka</s> further: 'What do you think, <s>Chandaka</s> — shall we go? Can the prince be turned back?' He said: 'By no means! The prince is irreversible, of firm vigor and valor. And thus he has declared: "I shall not enter the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> again until I have attained unsurpassed perfect awakening." And as the prince has declared, so it shall be. Why? The prince is irreversible, of firm vigor and valor.' //

body.text: tataśchandakaḥ kaṇṭhakamābharaṇāni cādāyāntaḥpuraṃ prāvikṣat / tatastānyābharaṇāni cireṇa kālena bhadrikasya śākyakumārasya mahānāmno 'niruddhasya cābadhyanta sma / tāni mahānārāyaṇasaṃghaṭanakāyārthamanye
body.translated_text: Then <s>Chandaka</s>, taking <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> and the ornaments, entered the inner palace. And those ornaments, after a long time, were worn by the <s>Śākya</s> princes <s>Bhadrika</s>, <s>Mahānāma</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>. Others [say] those [ornaments were] for the purposes of the great <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> assembly.

body.text: nārāyaṇasaṃhananā na śaknuvanti sma dhārayitum / yadā na kaścittāni dhārayituṃ śaknoti sma, tadā mahāprajāpatyā gautamyā cintitamabhūt - yāvadahamimānyābharaṇāni paśyāmi, tāvanmama hṛdaye śoko bhaviṣyati / yannvahamimānyābharaṇāni puṣkariṇyāṃ prakṣipeyamiti / tato mahāprajāpatī gautamī tānyābharaṇāni puṣkariṇyāṃ prakṣipati sma / adyāpi sā ābharaṇapuṣkariṇītyevaṃ saṃjñāyate //
body.translated_text: of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-like constitution — were unable to hold them. When no one was able to hold them, <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> thought: 'As long as I see these ornaments, so long will there be grief in my heart. Let me cast these ornaments into the lotus-pond.' Then <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s> cast those ornaments into the lotus-pond. To this day, it is known by the name 'Ornament Lotus-Pond' (<s>Ābharaṇapuṣkariṇī</s>). //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Thereupon this was said —

children.text: niṣkrāntu śūro yada vidu bodhisattvo nagaraṃ vibuddhaṃ kapilapuraṃ samagram /
children.translated_text: When the hero, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, had departed, the city of <s>Kapila</s> awoke, every part of it;

children.text: manyanti sarve śayanagato kumāro anyonya hṛṣṭāḥ pramudita ālabhante // Lal_15.102 //
children.translated_text: they all believe the prince is still asleep — joyfully, happily they greet one another. // Lal_15.102 //

children.text: gopā vibuddhā tatha api istrigārā śayanaṃ nirīkṣī na ca dṛśi bodhisattvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gopā</s> too awoke in the women's quarters; she looked at the bed but did not see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>;

children.text: utkrośu mukto narapatino agāre hā vañcitāḥ smaḥ kahi gatu bodhisattvo // Lal_15.103 //
children.translated_text: a shriek was released in the king's house: 'Alas, we have been deceived! Where has the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gone?' // Lal_15.103 //

children.text: rājā śruṇitvā dharaṇitale nirasto utkrośu kṛtvā aho mama ekaputro /
children.translated_text: The king, hearing, fell to the ground, uttering a cry: 'Alas, my only son!'

children.text: so stemito hi jalaghaṭasaṃprasikto āśvāsayantī bahuśata śākiyānām // Lal_15.104 //
children.translated_text: He fainted and was revived with pitchers of water; hundreds of <s>Śākyas</s> consoled [him]. // Lal_15.104 //

children.text: gopā śayāto dharaṇitale nipatya keśāṃ lunātī avaśiri bhūṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: <s>Gopā</s>, falling from the bed to the ground, tears at her hair and casts off her ornaments:

children.text: aho subhāṣṭaṃ mama puri nāyakenā sarvapriyebhirnaciratu viprayogaḥ // Lal_15.105 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, how well-spoken was the word of the leader in my presence: "Separation from all that is dear comes before long!"' // Lal_15.105 //

children.text: rūpā surūpā vimalavicitritāṅgā acchā viśuddhā jagati priyā manāpā /
children.translated_text: 'Beautiful, most beautiful, with stainless and wondrously adorned limbs, bright, pure, dear and pleasing in the world,

children.text: dhanyā praśastā divi bhuvi pūjanīyā kva tvaṃ gato 'si mama śayi chorayitvā // Lal_15.106 //
children.translated_text: blessed, praiseworthy, worthy of worship in heaven and on earth — where have you gone, leaving me sleeping? // Lal_15.106 //

children.text: na pāsyi pānaṃ na ca madhu na pramādaṃ bhūmau śayiṣye jaṭamakuṭaṃ dhariṣye /
children.translated_text: I shall not look at drink, nor honey, nor pleasures; I shall lie on the ground, I shall wear matted hair and a topknot;

children.text: snānaṃ jahitvā vratatapa ācariṣye yāvanna drakṣye guṇadharu bodhisattvam // Lal_15.107 //
children.translated_text: abandoning bathing, I shall practice austerity and vows — until I see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the bearer of virtues! // Lal_15.107 //

children.text: udyāna sarve aphala apatrapuṣpā hārā viśuddhā tamarajapāṃśutulyāḥ /
children.translated_text: All the gardens are fruitless, leafless, and flowerless; the pure necklaces are [now] equal to dirt, dust, and grime;

children.text: veśmaṃ na śobhī aṭavi puraṃ prakāśaṃ yattena tyaktaṃ naravarapuṃgavena // Lal_15.108 //
children.translated_text: the house no longer shines — the city appears as a wilderness — since it has been abandoned by that bull, the best of men! // Lal_15.108 //

children.text: hā gītavādyāḥ sumadhura mañjughoṣāḥ hā istrigārā vigalita bhūṣaṇābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas, the songs and music, sweet and melodious! Alas, the women's quarters, with ornaments fallen loose!

children.text: hā hemajālaiḥ parisphuṭamantarikṣaṃ na bhūyu drakṣye guṇadharaviprahīṇā // Lal_15.109 //
children.translated_text: Alas, the sky pervaded with golden nets! Deprived of the bearer of virtues, I shall see [them] no more!' // Lal_15.109 //

children.text: mātṛsvasā cā paramasukṛcchraprāptā āśvāsayāti ma rudahi śākyakanye /
children.translated_text: The maternal aunt, having come in supreme distress, consoled [her]: 'Do not weep, O <s>Śākya</s> maiden!

children.text: pūrve ca uktaṃ naravarapuṃgavena kartāsmi loke jaramaraṇātpramokṣam // Lal_15.110 //
children.translated_text: For it was formerly declared by that bull, the best of men: "I shall bring about liberation from old age and death in the world!"' // Lal_15.110 //

children.text: so cā maharṣī kuśalasahasra cīrṇaḥ ṣaḍ yojanāni pratigatu rātriśeṣe /
children.translated_text: 'And that great sage, who has performed thousands of meritorious deeds, has gone six <s>yojanas</s> in what remains of the night.

children.text: chandasya detī hayavaru bhūṣaṇāni chandā gṛhītvā kapilapuraṃ prayāhi // Lal_15.111 //
children.translated_text: He gives <s>Chandaka</s> the excellent horse and the ornaments: "Take them, <s>Chandaka</s>, and return to <s>Kapilavastu</s>!"' // Lal_15.111 //

children.text: mātāpitaṇāṃ mama vacanena pṛcche gataḥ kumāro na ca puna śocayethā /
children.translated_text: '"Ask my mother and father on my behalf — the prince has departed, and you should not grieve any longer.

children.text: buddhitva bodhiṃ punarihamāgamiṣye dharmaṃ śruṇitvā bhaviṣyatha śāntacittāḥ // Lal_15.112 //
children.translated_text: Having awakened to awakening, I shall come back here again; having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, you will become peaceful in mind."' // Lal_15.112 //

children.text: chando rudanto pratibhaṇi nāyakasya na me 'sti śaktirbalata parākramo vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, weeping, replied to the leader: 'I have neither strength, nor force, nor valor;

children.text: haneyu mahyaṃ naravarajñātisaṃghāḥ chandā kva nīto guṇadharu bodhisattvo // Lal_15.113 //
children.translated_text: the kinsmen of the lord of men will kill me! "<s>Chandaka</s>, where have you taken the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the bearer of virtues?"' // Lal_15.113 //

children.text: mā tāhi chandā pratibhaṇi bodhisattvo tuṣṭā bhavitvā api mama jñātisaṃghāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do not fear, <s>Chandaka</s>,' replied the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'My kinsmen will be pleased;

children.text: śāstārasaṃjñā tvayi sada bhāviṣyanti premeṇa mahyaṃ tvayamapi vartiṣyante // Lal_15.114 //
children.translated_text: they will always regard you as a teacher, and out of affection for me, they will treat you well.' // Lal_15.114 //

body.text: chando gṛhītvā hayavaru bhūṣaṇāni udyānaprāpto naravarapuṃgavasya /
body.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, having taken the excellent horse and the ornaments of the bull, the best of men, arrived at the garden.

body.text: udyānapālaḥ pramuditu vegajāto ānandaśabdaṃ pratibhaṇi śākiyānām // Lal_15.115 //
body.translated_text: The garden-keeper, overjoyed and filled with excitement, proclaimed the joyful news to the <s>Śākyas</s>: // Lal_15.115 //

children.text: ayaṃ kumāro hayavaru chandakaśca udyānaprāpto na ca puna śocitavyo /
children.translated_text: 'The prince, the excellent horse, and <s>Chandaka</s> have arrived at the garden — grieve no more!'

children.text: rājā śraṇitvā parivṛtu śākiyebhiḥ udyānaprāpto pramuditu vegajāto // Lal_15.116 //
children.translated_text: The king, hearing, surrounded by <s>Śākyas</s>, arrived at the garden, overjoyed and filled with excitement. // Lal_15.116 //

children.text: gopā viditvā dṛḍhamati bodhisattvaṃ no cāpi harṣī na ca gira śraddadhāti /
children.translated_text: But <s>Gopā</s>, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s firm resolve, was neither joyful nor did she believe the words:

children.text: asthānametadvinigatu yatkumāro aprāpya bodhiṃ punariha āgameyā // Lal_15.117 //
children.translated_text: 'It is impossible that the prince has returned — unless he first attains awakening, he will not come back here!' // Lal_15.117 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu rājā hayavaru chandakaṃ ca utkrośu kṛtvā dharaṇitale nirasto /
children.translated_text: But the king, seeing the excellent horse and <s>Chandaka</s>, uttered a cry and fell to the ground:

children.text: hā mahya putrā sukuśalagītavādyā kva tvaṃ gato 'si vijahiya sarvarājyam // Lal_15.118 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my son — skilled in beautiful songs and music! Where have you gone, abandoning the entire kingdom?' // Lal_15.118 //

children.text: sādhū bhaṇāhi vacana mameha chandā kiṃ vā prayogaḥ kva ca gatu bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Come, tell me the news here, <s>Chandaka</s> — what was the method? Where has the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gone?

children.text: kenātha nīto vivarita kena dvārā pūjā ca tasyā katha kṛta devasaṃghaiḥ // Lal_15.119 //
children.translated_text: By whom was he taken? By whom were the gates opened? And how was worship performed by the hosts of gods?' // Lal_15.119 //

children.text: chando bhaṇātī śṛṇu mama pārthivendrā rātrau prasupte nagari sabālavṛddhe /
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s> replied: 'Hear me, O lord of kings! In the night, when the city was asleep — young and old alike —

children.text: so mañjughoṣo mama bhaṇi bodhisattvo chandā dadāhi mama laghu aśvarājam // Lal_15.120 //
children.translated_text: that sweet-voiced one said to me: "<s>Chandaka</s>, give me quickly the king of horses!"' // Lal_15.120 //

children.text: so bodhayāmi naragaṇi nārisaṃghaṃ suptā prasuptā na ca gira te śruṇanti /
children.translated_text: 'I tried to awaken the men and the company of women — but asleep, deeply asleep, they did not hear my voice;

children.text: so rodamāno dadi ahu aśvarājaṃ hanta vrajāhī hitakara yena kāmam // Lal_15.121 //
children.translated_text: and so, weeping, I gave him the king of horses: "Go then, O benefactor, wherever you wish!"' // Lal_15.121 //

children.text: śakreṇa dvārā vivarita yantrayuktāḥ pālāścatasro hayacaraṇe śiliṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By <s>Śakra</s> the bolted doors were opened; the four guardians clung to the horse's hooves;

children.text: ārūḍhi śūre pracalita trisahasrāḥ mārgo nabhe 'smin suvipula yena krānto // Lal_15.122 //
children.translated_text: the hero mounted, the trichiliocosm trembled — along this vast path in the sky he passed!' // Lal_15.122 //

children.text: ābhā pramuktā vihatatamondhakārā puṣpā patiṃsū turiyaśatā raṇiṃṣū /
children.translated_text: 'Radiance was emitted, dispelling the darkness; flowers fell, hundreds of instruments sounded;

children.text: devāḥ staviṃsū tathapi hi cāpsarāṇi nabhasā prayāto parivṛtu devasaṃghaiḥ // Lal_15.123 //
children.translated_text: gods praised [him], and <s>Apsarases</s> too — he departed through the sky, surrounded by hosts of gods!' // Lal_15.123 //

children.text: chando gṛhītvā hayavaru bhūṣaṇāni antaḥpure so upagatu rodamāno /
children.translated_text: '<s>Chandaka</s>, having taken the excellent horse and the ornaments, entered the inner palace, weeping.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu gopā hayavaru chandakaṃ ca saṃmūrchayitvā dharaṇitale nirastā // Lal_15.124 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Gopā</s>, seeing the excellent horse and <s>Chandaka</s>, fainted and fell to the ground.' // Lal_15.124 //

children.text: udyukta sarvā suvipula nārisaṃghāḥ vāriṃ gṛhītvā snapayiṣu śākyakanyām /
children.translated_text: 'The entire vast company of women sprang up; taking water, they bathed the <s>Śākya</s> maiden:

children.text: mā haiva kālaṃ kariṣyati śokaprāptā dvābhyāṃ priyābhyāṃ bahu bhavi viprayogo // Lal_15.125 //
children.translated_text: "Lest she, stricken with grief, should die! From two beloved ones, great is the separation!"' // Lal_15.125 //

children.text: sthāmaṃ janitvā suduḥkhita śākyakanyā kaṇṭhe 'valambyā hayavaraaśvarāje /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Śākya</s> maiden, having gathered her strength, greatly suffering, clinging to the neck of the excellent horse-king,

children.text: anusmaritvā purimaka kāmakrīḍāṃ nānāpralāpī pralapati śokaprāptā // Lal_15.126 //
children.translated_text: recalling the former pleasures of love, stricken with grief, laments with various cries:' // Lal_15.126 //

children.text: hā mahya prītijananā hā mama narapuṃgavā vimalacandramukhā /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my joy-bringer! Alas, my bull among men, with face like a stainless moon!

children.text: hā mama surūparūpā hā mama varalakṣaṇā vimalatejadharā // Lal_15.127 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of supremely beautiful form! Alas, my one of excellent marks, bearer of stainless splendor! // Lal_15.127 //

children.text: hā mama aninditāṅgā sujāta anupūrvaudgatā asamā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of unblemished limbs, well-born, with limbs harmoniously proportioned, incomparable!

children.text: hā mama guṇāgradhāriṃ naramarūbhiḥ pūjitā paramakārūṇikā // Lal_15.128 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my foremost bearer of virtues, worshipped by gods and men, supremely compassionate! // Lal_15.128 //

children.text: hā mama balopapetā narāyaṇasthāmavannihataśatrugaṇā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one endowed with strength, with the firmness of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, crusher of enemy hosts!

children.text: hā mama sumāñjaghoṣā kalaviṅkarutasvarā madhurabrahmarutā // Lal_15.129 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of sweet, melodious voice, with the song of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, with a sweet <s>Brahmā</s>-voice! // Lal_15.129 //

children.text: hā mama anantakīrte śatapuṇyasamudgatā vimalapuṇyadharā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of boundless fame, arisen from a hundred merits, bearer of stainless merit!

children.text: hā mama anantavarṇā guṇagaṇapratimaṇḍitā ṛṣigaṇaprītikarā // Lal_15.130 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of boundless praise, adorned with multitudes of virtues, bringer of joy to assemblies of sages! // Lal_15.130 //

children.text: hā mama sujātajātā lumbinivana uttame bhramaragītarute /
children.translated_text: Alas, my nobly-born one, [born] in the excellent <s>Lumbinī</s> grove to the song of bees!

children.text: hā mama vighuṣṭaśabdā divi bhuvi abhipūjitā vipulajñānadrumā // Lal_15.131 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of proclaimed fame, worshipped in heaven and on earth, a tree of vast knowledge! // Lal_15.131 //

children.text: hā mama rasārasāgrā bimboṣṭhā kamalalocanā kanakanibhā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one supreme in essence and flavor, with <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips, lotus eyes, golden-hued!

children.text: hā mama suśuddhadantā gokṣīratuṣārasaṃnibhasahitadantā // Lal_15.132 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of brilliant white teeth, teeth like the luster of cow's milk and frost! // Lal_15.132 //

children.text: hā mama sunāsa subhrū ūrṇābhru mukhāntare sthitā vimalā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of beautiful nose and brows, with the <s>ūrṇā</s> between the brows, stainless!

children.text: hā mama suvṛttaskandhā cāpodara eṇeyajaṅghavṛttakaṭī // Lal_15.133 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my one of well-rounded shoulders, with a bow-shaped belly, with thighs like a deer, with rounded hips! // Lal_15.133 //

children.text: hā mama gajahastorū karacaraṇaviśuddhaśobhanā tāmranakhā /
children.translated_text: Alas, my one with thighs like an elephant's trunk, with pure and beautiful hands and feet, with copper-colored nails!'

children.text: iti tasya bhūṣaṇāni puṇyehi kṛtāni pārthive prītikarā // Lal_15.134 //
children.translated_text: 'These ornaments of his were made by merit, bringing joy to the king.' // Lal_15.134 //

children.text: ha mahya gītavādyā varapuṣpavilepanā śubhaṛtupravare /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my songs and music, with excellent flowers and ointments in the best of seasons!

children.text: hā mahya puṣpagandhā antaḥpuri gītavāditairharṣakarā // Lal_15.135 //
children.translated_text: Alas, my flower-fragrances in the inner palace, bringing joy with songs and music!' // Lal_15.135 //

children.text: hā kaṇṭhakā sujātā mama bhartu sahāyakastvayā kva nīto /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, nobly born, companion of my husband — where have you taken him?

children.text: hā chandakā nikaruṇā na bodhayasi gacchamānake naravariṣṭhe // Lal_15.136 //
children.translated_text: Alas, <s>Chandaka</s>, merciless one — why did you not awaken me when the foremost of men was departing?' // Lal_15.136 //

children.text: gacchatyayaṃ hitakaro ekā gira tasminnantari na bhasi kasmāt /
children.translated_text: 'This benefactor departs — and in that moment you do not speak a single word? Why?

children.text: itu adya puravarāto gacchati naradamyasārathiḥ kāruṇikaḥ // Lal_15.137 //
children.translated_text: Today, from this best of cities, the charioteer of men departs — the compassionate one!' // Lal_15.137 //

children.text: katha vā gato hitakaro kena ca niṣkramito itu sa rājakulāt /
children.translated_text: 'How indeed did the benefactor go? By whom was he brought forth from the royal house?

children.text: katamāṃ diśāmanugato dhanyā vanagulmadevatā yāsya sakhī // Lal_15.138 //
children.translated_text: In which direction did he proceed? Fortunate are the forest and grove deities who are his companions!' // Lal_15.138 //

children.text: atiduḥkha mahya chandā nidhidarśiya netrauddhṛtā cakṣudadā /
children.translated_text: 'Supreme is my suffering, O <s>Chandaka</s> — having shown me the treasure, the giver of eyes has plucked out [my] eyes!

children.text: sarvairjanaiśca chandā mātāpitṛnityavarṇitā pūjaniyāḥ // Lal_15.139 //
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, always praised and honored by all people, by mother and father —' // Lal_15.139 //

children.text: tānapi jahitva nirgatu kiṃ punarima istrikāmaratim /
children.translated_text: 'Even them he has abandoned and departed — how much more these pleasures of women!

children.text: hā dhik priyairviyogo naṭaraṅgasvabhāvasaṃnibhā anityā // Lal_15.140 //
children.translated_text: Alas, shame on separation from the beloved — impermanent, like the play of a dancer!' // Lal_15.140 //

children.text: saṃjñāgraheṇa bālā dṛṣṭiviparyāsaniśritā janmacyuti /
children.translated_text: 'Fools, through the grasping of perception, dependent on the perversion of views — birth and death [continue];

children.text: prāgeva tena bhaṇitaṃ nāsti jarāmaraṇasaṃskṛte kāści sakhā // Lal_15.141 //
children.translated_text: as he himself declared before: "In the conditioned realm of old age and death, there is no companion!"' // Lal_15.141 //

children.text: paripūryato 'sya āśā spṛśatū varabodhisamuttamāṃ drumavariṣṭhe /
children.translated_text: 'May his aspiration be fulfilled — may he touch the supreme, excellent <s>Bodhi</s> at the best of trees!

children.text: buddhitva bodhivirajāṃ punarapi etū ihā puravareṃ asmin // Lal_15.142 //
children.translated_text: Having awakened to the stainless awakening, may he come back again here to this best of cities!' // Lal_15.142 //

children.text: chandakaḥ paramadīnamānaso gopikāya vacanaṃ śruṇitvanā /
children.translated_text: <s>Chandaka</s>, his mind supremely wretched, hearing the words of <s>Gopikā</s>,

children.text: sāśrukaṇṭha gira saṃprabhāṣate sādhu gopi niśṛṇohi me vacaḥ // Lal_15.143 //
children.translated_text: speaks with a voice choked with tears: 'Well then, O <s>Gopī</s>, hear my words: // Lal_15.143 //

children.text: rātriye rahasi yāmi madhyame sarvanārigaṇi saṃprasuptake /
children.translated_text: 'In the middle of the night, privately, when the entire company of women was fast asleep,

children.text: so tadā ca śatapuṇyaudgato ālapeti mama dehi kaṇṭhakam // Lal_15.144 //
children.translated_text: that one arisen from a hundred merits said to me: "Give me <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>!"' // Lal_15.144 //

children.text: taṃ niśāmya vacanaṃ tadantaraṃ tubhya prekṣami śayāni suptikām /
children.translated_text: 'Hearing those words, at that moment I looked upon you sleeping on your bed;

children.text: uccaghoṣu ahu tatra muñcamī utthi gopi ayu yāti te priyo // Lal_15.145 //
children.translated_text: I let out a loud cry: "Rise, O <s>Gopī</s>! Your beloved is departing!"' // Lal_15.145 //

children.text: devatā vacanu taṃ nirodhayi eka istri napi kāci budhyate /
children.translated_text: 'The deities suppressed those words — not a single woman awoke;

children.text: rodamāna samalaṃkaritvanā aśvarāju dadamī narottame // Lal_15.146 //
children.translated_text: weeping, having adorned [him], I gave the king of horses to the foremost of men.' // Lal_15.146 //

children.text: kaṇṭhako hiṣati ugratejasvī krośamātru svaru tasya gacchatī /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> neighed, fiercely splendid — his voice carried a <s>krośa</s>;

children.text: no ca kaści śṛṇute purottame devatābhi osvāpanaṃ kṛtam // Lal_15.147 //
children.translated_text: yet no one in the best of cities heard — for the deities had put [all] to sleep.' // Lal_15.147 //

children.text: svarṇarūpyamaṇikoṭitā mahī kaṇṭhakasya caraṇaiḥ parāhatā /
children.translated_text: 'The earth, inlaid with gold, silver, and jewels, was struck by <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>'s hooves;

children.text: sā raṇī madhurabhīṣmaśobhanā no ca keci śṛṇuvanti mānuṣāḥ // Lal_15.148 //
children.translated_text: that sound was sweet, awesome, and beautiful — yet no humans heard it.' // Lal_15.148 //

children.text: puṣyayuktu abhu tasmi antare candrajyotiṣa nabhe pratisthitā /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Puṣya</s> constellation was in conjunction at that moment; the moonlight was established in the sky;

children.text: devakoṭi gagane kṛtāñjalī onamanti śirasābhivandiṣū // Lal_15.149 //
children.translated_text: <s>koṭis</s> of gods in the sky, with palms joined, bowed their heads in worship.' // Lal_15.149 //

children.text: yakṣarākṣasagaṇairupasthitā lokapāla caturo maharddhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Attended by hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, the four world-guardians of great supernatural power

children.text: kaṇṭhakasya caraṇāṃ kare nyasī padmakeśaraviśuddhanirmalam // Lal_15.150 //
children.translated_text: placed in their hands [lotuses] pure and stainless as lotus-filaments, [receiving] <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>'s hooves.' // Lal_15.150 //

children.text: so ca puṇyaśatatejaudgato āruhī kumudavarṣikopamam /
children.translated_text: 'That one, arisen from the splendor of a hundred merits, mounted [the horse] like a shower of water-lilies;

children.text: ṣaḍvikāra dharaṇī prakampitā buddhakṣetra sphuṭa ābhanirmalā // Lal_15.151 //
children.translated_text: the earth trembled with the six kinds of shaking; the Buddha-fields shone with stainless radiance.' // Lal_15.151 //

children.text: śakra devaguruḥ śacīpatiḥ svāma dvāra vivarī tadantare /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śakra</s>, guru of the gods, lord of <s>Śacī</s>, himself opened the gates at that moment;

children.text: devakoṭinayutaiḥ puraskṛto so vrajī amaranāgapūjito // Lal_15.152 //
children.translated_text: attended by <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of gods, he departed, worshipped by immortals and <s>Nāgas</s>.' // Lal_15.152 //

body.text: saṃjñamātra iha jāti kaṇṭhako lokanāthu vahatī nabho 'ntare /
body.translated_text: '<s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, [though but] a designation, bore the Lord of the World through mid-air;

body.text: devadānavagaṇā saindrikāḥ ye vahanti sugatasya gacchataḥ // Lal_15.153 //
body.translated_text: hosts of gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, together with <s>Indra</s>, bore the <s>Sugata</s> as he went.' // Lal_15.153 //

children.text: apsarā kuśalagītavādite bodhisattvaguṇabhāṣamānikāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Apsarases</s>, with skillful songs and music, praising the virtues of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: kaṇṭhakasya balu te dadantikāḥ muñci ghoṣu madhuraṃ manoramam // Lal_15.154 //
children.translated_text: giving strength to <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> — released a sound sweet and captivating.' // Lal_15.154 //

children.text: kaṇṭhakā vahahi lokanāyakaṃ śīghra śīghra ma janehi khedatām /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, carry the Lord of the World! Quickly, quickly — do not cause him weariness!

children.text: nāsti me bhayamapāyadurgatiṃ lokanāthamabhidhārayitvanā // Lal_15.155 //
children.translated_text: I have no fear of the lower realms or evil destinies — having carried the Lord of the World! // Lal_15.155 //

children.text: ekameka abhinandate suro vāhanaṃ smi ahu lokanāyake /
children.translated_text: Each god rejoices: "I am the mount of the Lord of the World!"

children.text: no ca kiṃcidapi deśu vidyate devakoṭicaraṇairna marditam // Lal_15.156 //
children.translated_text: There is not a single place not pressed by the feet of <s>koṭis</s> of gods! // Lal_15.156 //

children.text: paśya kaṇṭhaka nabhontare imaṃ mārgu saṃsthitu vicitraśobhanam /
children.translated_text: See, <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, in the midst of the sky, this path, beautifully established, of wondrous splendor,

children.text: ratnavedikavicitramaṇḍitaṃ divyasāravaragandhadhūpitam // Lal_15.157 //
children.translated_text: adorned with variegated jeweled railings, perfumed with divine, supreme fragrances! // Lal_15.157 //

children.text: ena kaṇṭhaka śubhena karmaṇā trāyatriṃśabhavane sunirmito /
children.translated_text: By this auspicious deed, <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, you shall be well-fashioned in the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven;

children.text: apsarai parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto divyakāmaratibhī ramiṣyase // Lal_15.158 //
children.translated_text: surrounded and preceded by <s>Apsarases</s>, you shall enjoy divine pleasures of desire! // Lal_15.158 //

children.text: sādhu gopi ma khu bhūyu rodahī tuṣṭa bhohi paramapraharṣitā /
children.translated_text: Good <s>Gopī</s>, do not weep any more! Be content and supremely delighted!

children.text: drakṣase nacirato narottamaṃ bodhiprāptamamaraiḥ puraskṛtam // Lal_15.159 //
children.translated_text: Before long you shall see the foremost of men, having attained <s>Bodhi</s>, preceded by the immortals! // Lal_15.159 //

children.text: ye narāḥ sukṛtakarmakārakāḥ te na gopi sada roditavyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those men who perform meritorious deeds — they are not to be wept for, O <s>Gopī</s>!

children.text: so ca puṇyaśatatejaudgato harṣitavya na sa roditavyakaḥ // Lal_15.160 //
children.translated_text: He who has risen in the splendor of a hundred merits — he is to be rejoiced for, not wept for! // Lal_15.160 //

children.text: saptarātra bhaṇabhānu gopike sā viyūha napi śakya kṣepitum /
children.translated_text: In seven nights, O <s>Gopikā</s>, tell [her] — that splendid array cannot be cast aside;

children.text: yā viyūha abhu tatra pārthive niṣkramanti naradevapūjite // Lal_15.161 //
children.translated_text: that splendid array which was in the king's [palace] — the one worshiped by gods and men goes forth [from it]! // Lal_15.161 //

children.text: lābha tubhya paramā acintiyā yaṃ tyupasthitu jage hitaṃkaro /
children.translated_text: Great and inconceivable is your gain — that the benefactor of the world has attended upon you!

children.text: mahya saṃjñi svakameva vartate tvaṃ hi bheṣyasi yathā narottamaḥ // Lal_15.162 //
children.translated_text: What is mine shall go according to its own [destiny] — and you shall become as the foremost of men!' // Lal_15.162 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare 'bhiniṣkramaṇaparivarto nāma pañcadaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Great Going-Forth' (<s>Abhiniṣkramaṇaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 16
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 16.

body.text: bimbisāropasaṃkramaṇaparivartaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Sixteenth Chapter: On the Approach to <s>Bimbisāra</s> (<s>Bimbisāropasaṃkramaṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaśchandako bodhisattvādhisthānena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gopāyāḥ śākyakanyāyāśca sarvasya cāntaḥpurasya sarvasya ca śākyagaṇasya śokavinodakathāmakārṣīt //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, <s>Chandaka</s>, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s empowerment, dispelled the grief of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, of <s>Gopā</s> the <s>Śākya</s> maiden, of the entire inner palace, and of the entire <s>Śākya</s> clan with a narrative of consolation.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo lubdhakarūpāya devaputrāya kāśikāni vastrāṇi dattvā tasya sakāśātkāṣāyāni vastrāṇi gṛhītvā svayameva pravajyāṃ lokānuvartanāmupādāya sattvānukampāyai sattvaparipācanārtham //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having given his <s>Kāśika</s> garments to a <s>devaputra</s> in the form of a hunter, and having received saffron robes from him, himself went forth into homelessness — following the ways of the world, out of compassion for beings, for the sake of ripening beings.

body.text: atha bodhisattvo yenaiva śākyā brāhmaṇyā āśramastenopasaṃkrāmat / sā bodhisattvaṃ vāsena bhaktena copanimantrayate sma / tato bodhisattvaḥ padmāyā brāhmaṇyā āśramaṃ gacchati sma / tayāpi bodhisattvo vāsena bhaktena copanimantrito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the hermitage of a <s>Śākya</s> <s>brāhmaṇī</s>. She invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with lodging and food. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> went to the hermitage of the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> <s>Padmā</s>. She too invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with lodging and food.

body.text: tato raivatasya brahmarṣerāśramamagamat / asāvapi bodhisattvaṃ tathaivopanimantrayate sma / tathaiva rājako 'pi datṛmadaṇḍikaputro bodhisattvamupanimantrayate sma //
body.translated_text: Then he went to the hermitage of the brahma-sage <s>Raivata</s>. He too invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the same way. Likewise, <s>Rājaka</s>, the son of <s>Datṛmadaṇḍika</s>, also invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'nupūrveṇa vaiśālīṃ mahānagarīmanuprāpto 'bhut //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, proceeding step by step, arrived at the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenārāḍaḥ kālāpo vaiśālīmupanisṛtya prativasati sma mahatā śrāvakasaṃghena sārdhaṃ tribhiḥ śiṣyaśataiḥ / sa śiṣyebhya ākiṃcanyāyatanasahavratāyai dharmaṃ deśayati sma / sa bodhisattvaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptaḥ śiṣyānāmantrayate sma - paśyata paśyata bho rūpamasyeti / te 'bruvan - evaṃ hyetatpaśyāmaḥ / enamativismayanīyam //
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s> was dwelling near <s>Vaiśālī</s> with a great assembly of disciples — three hundred students. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to his disciples for the attainment of the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). He, seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> coming from afar, was struck with wonder and addressed his disciples: 'Look! Look at the form of this one!' They said: 'Indeed, we see it. This is most astonishing!'

body.text: tato 'haṃ bhikṣavo yenārāḍaḥ kālāpastenopasaṃkramyārāḍa kālāpametadavocat - careyamahaṃ bho ārāḍe kālāpe brahmacaryam / so 'vocat - cara bho gautama tathārūpeṇa dharmākhyāne yasmin śrāddhaḥ kulaputro 'lpakṛcchreṇājñāmārādhayati //
body.translated_text: Then I, O monks, approaching <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s>, said to him: 'I would practice the holy life under you, O <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s>.' He said: 'Practice [it], O <s>Gautama</s>, with such a teaching of <s>Dharma</s> that a faithful son of good family, with little difficulty, accomplishes the goal.'

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - asti me chando 'sti vīryamasti smṛtirasti samādhirasti prajñā, yannvahameko 'pramatta ātāpī vyapakṛṣṭo vihareyaṃ tasyaiva dharmasya prāptaye sākṣātkriyāyai //
body.translated_text: This thought occurred to me, O monks: 'I have desire, I have vigor, I have mindfulness, I have concentration, I have wisdom — suppose I were to dwell alone, heedful, ardent, secluded, for the attainment and realization of that very <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: atha khalvahaṃ bhikṣavo eko 'pramatta ātāpī vyapakṛṣṭo viharannalpakṛcchreṇaivaṃ taṃ dharmamadhyavagacchan sākṣādakārṣam //
body.translated_text: Then I, O monks, dwelling alone, heedful, ardent, secluded, with little difficulty indeed comprehended that <s>Dharma</s> and realized it directly.

body.text: atha khalvahaṃ bhikṣavo yenārāḍaḥ kālāpastenopasaṃkramyaitadavocat - etāvadbho tvayā ārāḍa dharmo 'dhigataḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ? so 'vocat - evametadbho gautama / tamahamavocat - mayāpi bho eṣa dharmaḥ sākṣātkṛto 'dhigataḥ / so 'vocat - tena hi bho gautama yadahaṃ dharma jānāmi, bhavānapi taṃ jānāti, yaṃ bhavān jānāti, ahamapi taṃ jānāmi / tena hyāvāmubhāvapīmaṃ śiṣyagaṇaṃ pariharāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then I, O monks, approaching <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s>, said this: 'Is it to this extent, O <s>Ārāḍa</s>, that the <s>Dharma</s> has been attained and realized by you?' He said: 'To this extent, O <s>Gautama</s>.' I said to him: 'This <s>Dharma</s> has been realized and attained by me as well.' He said: 'Then, O <s>Gautama</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> that I know, you also know; what you know, I also know. Therefore let us both together guide this assembly of disciples.'

body.text: iti hi bhikṣava ārāḍaḥ kālāpaḥ paramayā pūjayā māṃ pūjayati sma / antevāsiṣu ca māṃ samānārthatayā sthāpayati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s> honored me with supreme worship and placed me on equal standing among his disciples.

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - ayaṃ khalvārāḍasya dharmo na nairyāṇiko na niryāti, tatkatarasya samyagduḥkhakṣayāya? yannvahamata uttari paryeṣamāṇaścareyam //
body.translated_text: This thought occurred to me, O monks: 'This <s>Dharma</s> of <s>Ārāḍa</s> does not lead to deliverance, does not lead out — to what then would it [lead] for the complete destruction of suffering? Suppose I were to continue seeking further beyond this.'

body.text: atha khalvahaṃ bhikṣavo yathābhirāmaṃ vaiśālyāṃ vihṛtya magadheṣu ca prakrānto 'bhūt / so 'haṃ magadheṣu caryāṃ caran yena māgadhakānāṃ rājagṛhaṃ nagaraṃ tadanusṛto yena ca pāṇḍavaḥ parvatarājastenopasaṃkrānto 'bhūvam / tatrāhaṃ pāṇḍave parvatarājapārśve vyāhārṣamekākyadvitīyo 'sahāyo 'nekairdevakoṭinayutaśatasahasraiḥ saṃrakṣitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then I, O monks, having dwelt at <s>Vaiśālī</s> as long as I wished, set forth to <s>Magadha</s>. I, wandering in <s>Magadha</s>, followed [the path] to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the city of the <s>Magadhans</s>, and approached <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, the king of mountains. There, at the slope of <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, the king of mountains, I dwelt — alone, without a second, without a companion, [yet] protected by many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of gods.

body.text: tato 'haṃ kalyameva saṃnivāsya pātracīvaramādāya tapodadvāreṇa rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat prāsādikenābhikrāntena pratikrāntena vyavalokitena saṃmiñjitena prasāritena prāsādikena saṃghāṭīpaṭapātracīvaradhāraṇenāvikṣiptairindriyairabahirgatena mānasena nirmitavattailapātradharavadyugamātraṃ paśyan / tatra māṃ rājagṛhakā manuṣyā dṛṣṭvā vismitā abhūvan - kiṃ svidayaṃ brahmā bhaviṣyati śakro devānāmindra āhosvidvaiśravaṇo āhosvitkiṃcidgiridaivatam //
body.translated_text: Then, in the early morning, I dressed, took my bowl and robe, and entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms through the Gate of Austerity — with a pleasing gait going forward and returning, looking about, bending, and stretching; with a pleasing manner of wearing the double robe, robes, and bowl; with senses unscattered, with mind not straying outward, as if carrying a full oil-bowl, looking only a yoke's distance ahead. There, the people of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having seen me, were amazed: 'Could this be <s>Brahmā</s>? <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods? Or <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>? Or some mountain deity?'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: atha vimaladharo hyanantatejo svayamiha pravrajiyāna bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the stainless one of infinite splendor, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having himself gone forth here,

children.text: śāntamanu dānta īryavanto viharati pāṇḍavaśailarājapārśve // Lal_16.1 //
children.translated_text: of peaceful mind, restrained, of stately bearing, dwelt at the slope of <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, king of mountains. // Lal_16.1 //

children.text: rajani vigatu jñātva bodhisattvaḥ paramasudarśaniyaṃ nivāsayitvā /
children.translated_text: Knowing the night had passed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having donned his supremely beautiful robe,

children.text: pātra pratigṛhīya nīcamāno praviśati rājagṛhaṃ sapiṇḍapātram // Lal_16.2 //
children.translated_text: taking his bowl, with humility, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for his alms-round. // Lal_16.2 //

children.text: kanakamiva sudhātujātarūpaṃ kavacitu lakṣaṇatriṃśatā dvibhiśca /
children.translated_text: Like refined gold of pure alloy, armored with the thirty-two marks and [eighty minor] signs,

children.text: naragaṇa tatha nāri prekṣamāṇo na ca bhavate kvaci tṛpti darśanena // Lal_16.3 //
children.translated_text: crowds of men and women gazing [at him] — yet there is no satiation anywhere from [just] seeing him! // Lal_16.3 //

children.text: vīthi racita ratnavastradhāryai avaśiriyā janu yāti pṛṣṭhato 'sya /
children.translated_text: In the streets, [women] adorned with jeweled garments let their knees fall and follow behind him:

children.text: ko nu ayu adṛṣṭapūrvasattvo yasya prabhāya puraṃ vibhāti sarvam // Lal_16.4 //
children.translated_text: 'Who is this being, never seen before, by whose radiance the entire city shines?' // Lal_16.4 //

body.text: upari sthihiya nāriṇāṃ sahasrā tathariva dvāri tathaiva vātayāne /
body.translated_text: Thousands of women [stood] above [on rooftops], and likewise at the doors and windows;

body.text: rathya bharita gehi śūnya kṛtvā naravaru prekṣiṣu te ananyakarmāḥ // Lal_16.5 //
body.translated_text: filling the streets, making their houses empty — they gazed at the best of men, engaged in nothing else. // Lal_16.5 //

children.text: na ca bhuyu krayavikrayaṃ karontī na ca puna sauṇḍa pibanti madyapānam /
children.translated_text: No more do they conduct buying and selling; no longer do the tavern-keepers drink their wine;

children.text: na ca gṛhi na ca vīthiye ramante puruṣavarasya nirīkṣamāṇa rūpam // Lal_16.6 //
children.translated_text: none remain at home, none delight in the streets — gazing at the form of the best of men. // Lal_16.6 //

children.text: puruṣa tvaritu gacchi rājagehaṃ avaciṣu rāja sa bimbisāra tuṣṭo /
children.translated_text: A man ran quickly to the royal palace; they informed King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, who was delighted:

children.text: deva parama tubhya labdha lābhā svayamiha brahma pure carāti piṇḍam // Lal_16.7 //
children.translated_text: 'Lord, supreme are the gains obtained by you! <s>Brahmā</s> himself here wanders for alms in the city!' // Lal_16.7 //

children.text: keci avaci śakra devarājo apari bhaṇanti suyāma devaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: Some said: '<s>Śakra</s>, king of gods!' Others declared: '<s>Suyāma</s> <s>devaputra</s>!

children.text: tatha api saṃtuṣitaṃ va nirmitaśca apari bhaṇanti sunirmiteṣu devaḥ // Lal_16.8 //
children.translated_text: Or one from <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> [<s>Tuṣita</s>], or from <s>Nirmita</s>!' — others declared: 'A god from the <s>Sunirmita</s> [heaven]!' // Lal_16.8 //

children.text: keci puna bhaṇanti candrasūryau tathapi ca rāhu baliśca vemacitrī /
children.translated_text: Some again declared: 'It is <s>Candra</s> or <s>Sūrya</s>!' — and others: '<s>Rāhu</s> or <s>Bali</s> or <s>Vemacitri</s>!'

children.text: keci puna bhaṇanti vācamevaṃ ayu so pāṇḍavaśailarājavāsī // Lal_16.9 //
children.translated_text: But some uttered this word: 'He is the one dwelling at <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, king of mountains!' // Lal_16.9 //

children.text: vacanamimu śruṇitva pārthivo 'sau paramaudagramanā sthito gavākṣe /
children.translated_text: Having heard these words, that king, his mind supremely elated, stood at the window

children.text: prekṣati varasattva bodhisattvaṃ jvalatu śirīya sudhātukāñcanaṃ vā // Lal_16.10 //
children.translated_text: and beheld the supreme being, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — blazing with glory like refined gold! // Lal_16.10 //

children.text: piṇḍa dadiya rāja bimbisāraḥ puruṣamavocannirīkṣa kva prayātī /
children.translated_text: King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, having given alms, said to a man: 'Watch where he goes!'

children.text: dṛṣṭva girivaraṃ sa gacchamāno avaciṣu deva gataḥ sa śailapārśvam // Lal_16.11 //
children.translated_text: Seeing him going toward the great mountain, they reported: 'Lord, he has gone to the mountain-slope.' // Lal_16.11 //

children.text: rajani vigatu jñātva bimbisāro mahata janaiḥ parivārito narendraḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing the night had passed, <s>Bimbisāra</s>, the lord of men, surrounded by a great retinue,

children.text: upagami pāṇḍavaśailarājamūle śiriya jvalantu tamadṛśāti śailam // Lal_16.12 //
children.translated_text: approached the foot of <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, king of mountains — [which] blazed with glory, beholding that mountain! // Lal_16.12 //

children.text: dharaṇi vrajitu yāni oruhitvā paramasugaurava prekṣi bodhisattvam /
children.translated_text: Descending from his vehicle, going on foot, with supreme respect he beheld the <s>Bodhisattva</s> —

children.text: meruriva yathā hyakampamāno nyasiya tṛṇāni niṣaṇṇa sostikena // Lal_16.13 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Meru</s>, indeed, unshaking — who had spread grass and sat with a blessed [seat]. // Lal_16.13 //

children.text: śirasi caraṇi vandayitva rājā vividhakathāṃ samudāharitva vocat /
children.translated_text: Having bowed at his feet, the king, having conversed with various words, said:

children.text: dadami tava upārdhu sarvarājyād rama iha kāmaguṇairahaṃ ca piṇḍam // Lal_16.14 //
children.translated_text: 'I give you half of my entire kingdom — enjoy here with the pleasures of the senses, and I [shall provide] alms!' // Lal_16.14 //

children.text: prabhaṇati giri bodhisattva ślakṣṇaṃ dharaṇipate ciramāyu pālayasva /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> spoke gently upon the mountain: 'O lord of the earth, may you long protect your life!

children.text: ahamapi pravijahya rājyamiṣṭaṃ pravrajito nirapekṣi śāntihetoḥ // Lal_16.15 //
children.translated_text: I too, having abandoned the desired kingdom, have gone forth, free from attachment, for the sake of peace.' // Lal_16.15 //

children.text: daharu taruṇayauvanairupetaḥ śubhatanuvarṇanibho 'si vegaprāptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are young, endowed with the bloom of youthful vigor, of beautiful complexion and form, having arrived with speed;

children.text: vipula dhana pratīccha nārisaṃghaṃ iha mama rājyi vasāhi bhuṅkṣva kāmāṃ // Lal_16.16 //
children.translated_text: accept vast wealth and a company of women — dwell here in my kingdom and enjoy pleasures!' // Lal_16.16 //

children.text: paramapramudito 'smi daśanātte avaciṣu sa māgadharāja bodhisattvam /
children.translated_text: 'I am supremely delighted upon seeing you!' — said the king of <s>Magadha</s> to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>;

children.text: bhavahi mama sahāyu sarvarājyaṃ ahu tava dāsyi prabhūta bhuṅkṣva kāmāṃ // Lal_16.17 //
children.translated_text: 'Be my companion — the entire kingdom! I shall be your servant! Enjoy abundant pleasures!' // Lal_16.17 //

children.text: mā ca puna vane vasāhi śūnye ma bhuyu tṛṇeṣu vasāhi bhūmivāsam /
children.translated_text: 'Do not dwell again in the empty forest! No more dwell on grass upon the bare ground!

children.text: paramasukumāru tubhya kāyo iha mama rājyi vasāhi bhuṅkṣva kāmāṃ // Lal_16.18 //
children.translated_text: Your body is supremely delicate — dwell here in my kingdom and enjoy pleasures!' // Lal_16.18 //

children.text: prabhaṇati giri bodhisattva ślakṣṇaṃ akuṭila premaṇiyā hitānukampī /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> spoke gently upon the mountain — straightforward, lovable, compassionate, and benevolent:

children.text: svasti dharaṇipāla te 'stu nityaṃ na ca ahu kāmaguṇebhirarthiko 'smi // Lal_16.19 //
children.translated_text: 'Blessings to you always, O protector of the earth! I do not desire the pleasures of the senses. // Lal_16.19 //

children.text: kāma viṣasamā anantadoṣā narakaprapātana pretatiryagyonau /
children.translated_text: Sense-pleasures are like poison, of endless faults, causing beings to fall into hell, the <s>preta</s>-realm, and animal births;

children.text: vidubhi vigarhita cāpyanārya kāmā jahita mayā yathā pakvakheṭapiṇḍam // Lal_16.20 //
children.translated_text: despised by the wise and ignoble are sense-pleasures — abandoned by me like a ball of spittle! // Lal_16.20 //

children.text: kāma drumaphalā yathā patantī yathamiva abhrabalāhakā vrajanti /
children.translated_text: Pleasures [fall] like fruits from a tree; they pass like cloud-masses;

children.text: adhruva capalagāmi mārutaṃ vā vikiraṇa sarvaśubhasya vañcanīyā // Lal_16.21 //
children.translated_text: unstable, swift-moving like the wind — they scatter all good [and are] deceptive! // Lal_16.21 //

children.text: kāma alabhamāna dahyayante tatha api labdha na tṛpti vindayantī /
children.translated_text: When pleasures are not obtained, [people] burn; and when obtained, they bring no satisfaction;

children.text: yada puna avaśasya bhakṣayante tada mahaduḥkha janenti ghora kāmāḥ // Lal_16.22 //
children.translated_text: and when they are consumed against one's will, then terrible pleasures generate great suffering! // Lal_16.22 //

children.text: kāma dharaṇipāla ye ca divyā tatha api mānuṣa kāma ye praṇītā /
children.translated_text: Whatever pleasures exist, O lord of the earth — divine or the refined human pleasures —

children.text: eku naru labheta sarvakāmāṃ na ca so tṛpti labheta bhūyu eṣan // Lal_16.23 //
children.translated_text: if one man obtained all pleasures, he would find no satisfaction, [but only] further seeking! // Lal_16.23 //

children.text: ye tu dharaṇipāla śāntadāntā ārya anāśrava dharmapūrṇasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: But those who are peaceful and restrained, O lord of the earth — noble, free from outflows, of the perception of fullness in <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: prajñaviduṣa tṛpta te sutṛptā na ca puna kāmaguṇeṣu kāci tṛptiḥ // Lal_16.24 //
children.translated_text: those wise in wisdom are satisfied, well-satisfied — and in the strands of pleasure there is no satisfaction [at all]! // Lal_16.24 //

children.text: kāma dharaṇipāla sevamānā purima na vidyati koṭi saṃskṛtasya /
children.translated_text: Pleasures, O lord of the earth, when indulged in — there is no prior limit to the conditioned [realm] found;

children.text: lavaṇajala yathā hi nārū pītvā bhuyu tṛṣa vardhati kāma sevamāne // Lal_16.25 //
children.translated_text: like a man who has drunk salt water — the more one indulges in pleasures, the more thirst increases! // Lal_16.25 //

children.text: api ca dharaṇipāla paśya kāyaṃ adhruvamasāraku duḥkhayantrametat /
children.translated_text: Moreover, O protector of the earth, look at this body — impermanent, without essence, a machine of suffering!

children.text: navabhi vraṇamukhaiḥ sadā sravantaṃ na mama narādhipa kāmachandarāgaḥ // Lal_16.26 //
children.translated_text: Constantly oozing from nine wound-openings — I have no desire, attraction, or passion for pleasures, O lord of men! // Lal_16.26 //

children.text: ahamapi vipulāṃ vijahya kāmāṃ tathapi ca istrisahasra darśanīyāṃ /
children.translated_text: I too have abandoned vast pleasures, and [the company of] thousands of beautiful women;

children.text: anabhiratu bhaveṣu nirgato 'haṃ paramaśivāṃ varabodhi prāptukāmaḥ // Lal_16.27 //
children.translated_text: without delight in [worldly] existence, I have gone forth, wishing to attain the supreme, auspicious awakening! // Lal_16.27 //

body.text: rājā āha -
body.translated_text: The king said:

body.text: katama diśi kuto gato 'si bhikṣo kva ca tava janma kva te pitā kva mātā /
body.translated_text: 'In which direction, whence have you come, O monk? Where is your birthplace? Where is your father? Where is your mother?

body.text: kṣatriya atha brāhmaṇo 'tha rājā parikatha bhikṣu yadī na bhārasaṃjñā // Lal_16.28 //
body.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s>, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or a king? Tell me, O monk, if it is not burdensome to you.' // Lal_16.28 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: śratu ti dharaṇipāla śākiyānāṃ kapilapuraṃ paramaṃ suṛddhisphītam /
children.translated_text: 'Hear, O protector of the earth: there is a city of the <s>Śākyas</s> called <s>Kapilapura</s>, supreme and abundantly prosperous;

children.text: pitu mama śuddhodaneti nāmnā tanu ahu pravrajito guṇābhilāṣī // Lal_16.29 //
children.translated_text: my father is known by the name <s>Śuddhodana</s>. I have gone forth, seeking virtues.' // Lal_16.29 //

body.text: rājā āha -
body.translated_text: The king said:

children.text: sādhu tava sudṛṣṭadarśanaṃ te yanu tava janma vayaṃ pi tasya śiṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Excellent! Good is the sight of seeing you! As for your birth — we too shall be his disciples!

children.text: api ca mama kṣamasva āśayenā yamapi nimantritu kāmavītarāgo // Lal_16.30 //
children.translated_text: Please bear with me in my intention: I would invite one who is free from the passion of desires! // Lal_16.30 //

children.text: yadi tvaya anuprāptu bhoti bodhiḥ tada mama seti bhoti dharmasvāmim /
children.translated_text: If awakening is attained by you, then let my [kingdom] be yours, O lord of <s>dharma</s>!

children.text: api ca mama purā sulabdha lābhā mama vijite vasasīha yatsvayaṃbho // Lal_16.31 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, I have gained an excellent gain — dwell here in my dominion, O self-arisen one!' // Lal_16.31 //

children.text: punarapi caraṇāni vandayitvā kṛtva pradakṣiṇu gauraveṇa rājā /
children.translated_text: Then, having bowed once more at his feet, the king circumambulated him with reverence;

children.text: svakajanaparivārito narendraḥ punarapi rājagṛhaṃ anupraviṣṭaḥ // Lal_16.32 //
children.translated_text: and the lord of men, surrounded by his attendants, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> again. // Lal_16.32 //

children.text: magadhapuri praveśi lokanātho vihariya śāntamanā yathābhiprāyam /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the World entered the city of <s>Magadha</s>, dwelling with a tranquil mind as he wished;

children.text: arthu kariya devamānuṣāṇāṃ upagami tīru nirañjanā narendraḥ // Lal_16.33 //
children.translated_text: having accomplished the purpose of gods and humans, the lord approached the bank of the <s>Nirañjanā</s> [river]. // Lal_16.33 //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare bimbisāropasaṃkramaṇaparivarto nāma ṣoḍaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the sixteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Visit to <s>Bimbisāra</s>' (<s>Bimbisāropasaṃkramaṇaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 17
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 17.

body.text: duṣkaracaryāparivartaḥ saptadaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Seventeenth Chapter: On Difficult Practices (<s>Duṣkaracaryāparivarta</s>).

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena rudrako nāma rāmaputro rājagṛhaṃ nāma mahānagaramupanisṛtya viharati sma mahatā śiṣyagaṇena sārdhaṃ saptabhiḥ śiṣyaśataiḥ / sa tebhyo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasahavratāyai dharmaṃ deśayati sma / adrākṣīt khalvapi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo rudrakaṃ rāmaputraṃ saṃghegaṇinaṃ gaṇācāryaṃ jñātamabhīpsitaṃ bahujanapūjitaṃ paṇḍitasaṃmatam / dṛṣṭvā cāsyaitadabhūt - ayaṃ khalvapi rudrako rāmaputraḥ saṃghegaṇī gaṇācāryaḥ jñāto 'bhīpsito bahujanapūjitaḥ paṇḍitasaṃmataḥ / sacedahamasyāntikamupasaṃkramya vratatapamārabheyam, naiṣa mamāntike viśiṣṭasaṃjño bhavennāpi pratyakṣajñānena jñāto bhavennāpi saṃskṛtānāṃ sāśravānāṃ sopādānānāṃ dhyānasamādhisamāpattīnāṃ doṣo datto bhavet / yannvahaṃ tathārupamupāyamupasaṃdarśayeyaṃ yenaite ca pratyakṣā bhaveyuḥ / dhyānagocarāṇāṃ ca samāpattyārambaṇānāṃ laukikasamādhīnāmaniḥsaraṇatā darśitā bhavet / yannvahaṃ rudrakasya rāmaputrasya sakāśamupasaṃkramya svasamādhiguṇaviśeṣodbhāvanārthaṃ śiṣyatvamabhyupagamya saṃskṛtasamādhīnāmasāratāmupadarśayeyamiti //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, one named <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, dwelt near the great city called <s>Rājagṛha</s>, together with a great company of disciples — seven hundred disciples. He was teaching them the <s>dharma</s> for the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O monks, saw that <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, was a leader of a community, a teacher of a group, well-known, sought after, honored by many people, esteemed by the learned. Having seen [this], he thought: 'This <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, is a leader of a community, a teacher of a group, well-known, sought after, honored by many people, esteemed by the learned. If I were to approach him and undertake vows and austerities, he would not consider himself superior in my presence, nor would he know me through direct knowledge. Nor would the fault of the conditioned, contaminated, and attachment-based <s>dhyānas</s>, concentrations, and attainments be pointed out. Let me demonstrate such a skillful means by which these [flaws] would become manifest, and the inability to escape through worldly concentrations — which are within the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> and have attainment as their support — would be shown. Let me therefore approach <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, accept the role of a disciple for the purpose of demonstrating the special excellence of my own concentration-qualities, and show the essencelessness of conditioned concentrations.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattva idamarthavaśamadhikṛtya yena rudrako rāmaputrastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya rudrakaṃ rāmaputrametadavocat - kaste mārṣa śāstā, kasya vā dharmaṃ deśitamājānāsi?
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with this purpose in mind, approached <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>: 'Who, O noble one, is your teacher? Or whose <s>dharma</s> do you acknowledge as having been taught [to you]?'

body.text: ityevamukte rudrako rāmaputro bodhisattvamevamāha - na me mārṣa kaścicchāstā / api tu khalu punaḥ svayameva mayedaṃ samyagadhigatamiti / bodhisattva āha - kiṃ bhavatādhigatam? āha - naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattermārgaḥ / bodhisattva āha - labhemahi vayaṃ bhavataḥ sakāśādavavādānuśāsanīyasya samādhermārgam? āha - vāḍhamastviti / yāvaddatto 'vavādo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'I have no teacher, O noble one. Rather, this was well-realized by myself.'
