The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'What have you realized?' He said: 'The path to the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'May I obtain from you the instruction and guidance on the path of this concentration?' He said: 'Certainly, so be it.' And thereupon instruction was given. //

body.text: tato bodhisattva ekāntaṃ gatvā paryaṅkamābhujyopaviśati sma / samanantaropaviṣṭasya ca bodhisattvasya puṇyaviśeṣeṇa ca jñānaviśeṣeṇa ca pūrvasucaritacaryāphalaviśeṣeṇa ca sarvasamādhiparicayaviśeṣeṇa ca dhyānapramukhāni sarvāṇi laukikāni lokottarāṇi samāpattiśatānyāmukhībhavanti sma sākārāṇi soddeśāni yathāpi taccittavaśavartitvāt / atha ca bodhisattvaḥ smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan utthāyāsanādyena rudrako rāmaputrastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya rudrakaṃ rāmaputramevamāha astyanyo 'pi mārṣa kaściduttare naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattermārgaḥ? so 'bravīt - nāstīti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going aside, sat cross-legged. No sooner had the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat down than, by the distinction of his merit, the distinction of his knowledge, the distinction of the fruit of his former well-practiced conduct, and the distinction of his complete familiarity with all concentrations, hundreds of attainments — both worldly and supramundane, beginning with <s>dhyāna</s> — became manifest to him, with their aspects and descriptions, inasmuch as they were subject to his will. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, mindful and fully aware, rose from his seat and approached <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>: 'Is there, O noble one, any other path beyond the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?' He said: 'There is not.' //

body.text: tato bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - na khalu rudrakasyaivāsti śraddhā vīryaṃ smṛtiḥ prajñā / mamāpyasti śraddhā vīryaṃ smṛtiḥ samādhiḥ prajñā /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'It is not the case that <s>Rudraka</s> alone has faith, vigor, mindfulness, and wisdom. I too have faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvo rudrakaṃ rāmaputramevamāha - mayāpyeṣa mārṣa dharmo 'dhigato yatra tvaṃ niryātaḥ / so 'vocat - tena hyāgaccha, tvaṃ cāhaṃ cemaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharāva iti / samānārthe ca bodhisattvaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>: 'I too, O noble one, have realized this <s>dharma</s> in which you have trained [your disciples].' He said: 'Then come — you and I shall together lead this community.' And he placed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in equal standing

body.text: sthāpayati sma ācāryasthāne ca / bodhisattva āha - naiṣa mārṣa mārgo nirvṛtaye na virāgāya na nirodhāya nopaśamāya nābhijñāyai na saṃbodhaye na śrāmaṇāya na brāhmaṇāya na nirvāṇāya saṃvartate //
body.translated_text: and in the teacher's seat. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'This is not the path, O noble one. It does not lead to cessation, nor to dispassion, nor to stopping, nor to peace, nor to higher knowledge, nor to awakening, nor to the state of a <s>Śramaṇa</s>, nor to the state of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor to <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo rudrakasya rāmaputrasya saśiṣyasyāvarjanīkṛtva yāvadalamiti kṛtvā prakrāmat - alaṃ mamāneneti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having attracted the attention of <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, and his disciples, having concluded 'Enough!' departed — [thinking:] 'Enough of this for me.' //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena pañcakā bhadravargīyā rudrake rāmaputre brahmacaryaṃ caranti sma / teṣāmetadabhūt - yasya khalu vayamarthāya dīrgharātraṃ ghaṭāmahe udyujyāmahe, na ca śaknumo 'ntaṃ vā paryantaṃ cādhigantum, tacchramaṇena gautamenālpakakṛcchaṇādhigantuṃ sākṣātkṛtam / taccāsya na rocate / tathā cottari paryeṣate / niḥsaṃśayameṣa śāstā loke bhaviṣyati / yaccaiṣa sākṣātkariṣyati, tadasmabhyaṃ saṃvibhakṣyatīti / evaṃ vimṛṣya pañcakā bhadravargīyā rudrakarāmaputrasakāśādapakramya bodhisattvamanvabadhnan //
body.translated_text: At that time, five [ascetics] of the <s>Bhadravargīya</s> group were living the holy life under <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>. They thought: 'The purpose for which we have striven and exerted ourselves for a long time — and yet cannot reach its end or limit — that has been realized and directly witnessed by the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s> with but little effort. Yet he is not satisfied with it. He seeks still further. Without doubt, he will become the teacher of the world. Whatever he directly realizes, he will share with us.' Having reflected thus, the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, departing from the presence of <s>Rudraka</s>, son of <s>Rāma</s>, followed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo yathābhipretaṃ rājagṛhe vihṛtya magadheṣu cārikāṃ prakrāmat sārdhaṃ pañcakairbhadravargīyaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having dwelt in <s>Rājagṛha</s> as he wished, set out on a journey through <s>Magadha</s> together with the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>. //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenāntarācca rājagṛhasya antarācca gayāyā yo 'nyatamo gaṇa utsavaṃ karoti sma, tena ca gaṇena bodhisattvo 'bhinimantrito 'bhūt vāsena bhaktena ca sārdhaṃ pañcakairbhadravargīyaiḥ //
body.translated_text: At that time, between <s>Rājagṛha</s> and <s>Gayā</s>, a certain group was holding a festival, and that group had invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with lodging and food, together with the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvo magadheṣu caryāṃ caran yena māgadhakānāṃ gayā tāmanusṛtya tāmanuprāpto 'bhūt / tatra khalvapi bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ prahāṇārthī viharati sma gayāśīrṣe parvate / tatrāsya viharatastisra upamāḥ pratibhānti sma aśrutapūrvā anabhijñātapūrvāḥ / katamāstisraḥ? ye kecitte khalvapi śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ kāmebhyo 'navakṛṣṭakāyā viharanti sma / kāmebhyo 'navakṛṣṭacittāśca viharanti sma / yāpi caiṣāṃ kāmeṣu nandiḥ kāmeṣu rāgaḥ kāmeṣu chandaḥ kāmeṣu tṛṣṇā kāmeṣu pipāsā kāmeṣu mūrchā kāmeṣu paridāhaḥ kāmeṣvadhyavasānatā, sāpyanupaśāntā / kiṃ cāpi te ātmopakramikāṃ śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayante / atha tarhi abhavyā eva te uttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / tadyathāpi nāma puruṣo 'gnyarthī jyotirgaveṣī jyotiṃ paryeṣamāṇaḥ sa ārdraṃ kāṣṭhamādāya ārdrāṃ cottarāraṇīmudake prakṣipya mathnīyāt, abhavyo 'sāvagnimutpādayituṃ tejaḥ prāduṣkartum / evameva ya ime śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ kāmebhyo 'navakṛṣṭakāyā anavakṛṣṭacittāśca viharanti, yāpyeṣāṃ kāmeṣu nandiḥ kāmeṣu rāgaḥ kāmeṣu chandaḥ kāmeṣu tṛṣṇā kāmeṣu pipāsā kāmeṣu mūrchā kāmeṣu paridāhaḥ kāmeṣvadhyavasānaṃ tadapyanupaśāntam / kiṃ cāpi te ātmopakramikāṃ śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayante / atha tarhi abhavyā evottarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / iyaṃ bodhisattvasya prathamā upamā pratibhāti sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, journeying through <s>Magadha</s>, reached <s>Gayā</s> of the <s>Magadhans</s>, following along it and arriving there. There, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, intent on striving, dwelt on Mount <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>. While he dwelt there, three similes — never before heard, never before known — arose in his mind. What were the three? 'Those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who dwell with bodies not withdrawn from pleasures and with minds not withdrawn from pleasures — and in whom the delight in pleasures, the passion for pleasures, the desire for pleasures, the craving for pleasures, the thirst for pleasures, the infatuation with pleasures, the burning for pleasures, and the attachment to pleasures are not pacified — even if they experience painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings that are self-inflicted and bodily-tormenting, they are nevertheless incapable of directly realizing the distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>. Just as, for example, a man desiring fire, seeking flame, searching for flame, were to take a piece of wet wood and a wet upper fire-stick, throw them into water, and rub them — he would be incapable of producing fire or manifesting heat. Even so, those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who dwell with bodies and minds not withdrawn from pleasures, and in whom the delight in pleasures ... [and so on as before] ... attachment to pleasures is not pacified — even if they experience painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings — they are nevertheless incapable of directly realizing the distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>.' This was the first simile that arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind. //

body.text: bhūyaścāsyaitadabhūt - ya ime śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ kāmebhyo vyapakṛṣṭakāyacittā viharanti, yāpi teṣāṃ kāmeṣu nandīti sarvaṃ kartavyaṃ yāvajjyotiṃ paryeṣata iti / sa ārdraṃ kāṣṭhamādāya sthale sthāpayitvā ārdrāṃ cottarāraṇiṃ mathnīyāt, abhavyo 'sāvagnimutpādayitum / evameva ye ime śramaṇabrāhmaṇā iti sarvaṃ pūrvavatkāryaṃ yāvadabhavyā uttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / iyaṃ dvitīyā upamā pratibhāti sma pūrvamaśrutā cāvijñātā ca //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, he thought: 'Those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who dwell with bodies and minds withdrawn from pleasures — but in whom the delight in pleasures' ... [and so on, all to be done as before, up to] ... 'searching for flame' — 'were to take a piece of wet wood, set it on dry ground, and take a wet upper fire-stick and rub — he would be incapable of producing fire. Even so, those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>' ... [and so on, everything as before, up to] ... 'are incapable of directly realizing the distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>.' This was the second simile that arose in [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s] mind — never before heard and never before known. //

body.text: punaraparaṃ ya ime śramaṇabrāhmaṇā bhavantaḥ kāmebhyo vyapakṛṣṭakāyacittā viharanti, yāpi teṣāṃ kāmeṣu nandiḥ / iti sarvaṃ peyālam / tadapyeṣāmupaśāntam / kiṃ cāpi te ātmopakramikāṃ śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayante / atha khalu punarbhavyā eva te uttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / tadyathāpi nāma iha syātpuruṣo 'gnyarthī jyotirgaveṣī jyotiḥ paryeṣamāṇaḥ, sa śuṣkaṃ kāṣṭhamādāya śuṣkāṃ cottarāraṇiṃ sthale pratiṣṭhāpya mathnīyāt, sa bhavyo 'gnimabhinirvartayituṃ tejaḥ prāduṣkartum / evameva ya ime bhavantaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇā iti sarvaṃ yāvadvedanāṃ vedayanta iti / atha ca punarbhavyā eva te uttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / iyaṃ tṛtīyā upamā pratibhāti sma aśrutapūrvā ca avijñātapūrvā ca //
body.translated_text: And further: 'Those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who dwell with bodies and minds withdrawn from pleasures, and in whom the delight in pleasures' ... [and so on, all abbreviated] ... 'has been pacified — even if they experience painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter feelings that are self-inflicted and bodily-tormenting — they are indeed capable of directly realizing the distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>. Just as, for example, a man desiring fire, seeking flame, searching for flame, were to take a piece of dry wood and a dry upper fire-stick, set [them] on dry ground, and rub — he would be capable of producing fire and manifesting heat. Even so, those <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>' ... [and so on, everything up to] ... 'experience feelings — they are indeed capable of directly realizing the distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>.' This was the third simile that arose in [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s] mind — never before heard and never before known. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - ahaṃ khalvetarhi kāmebhyo vyapakṛṣṭakāyo viharāmi vyapakṛṣṭacittaśca / yāpi me kāmeṣu nandīti sarvaṃ yāvattadapi me upaśāntam / kiṃ cāpi ahamātmopakramikāṃ śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāmiti peyālaṃ yāvadvedanāṃ vedmi / atha khalvahaṃ bhavya evottarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'I now dwell with body withdrawn from sense-pleasures, and with mind withdrawn. Whatever delight I had in sense-pleasures — all that too has been pacified in me. Yet I experience a feeling that is self-afflicting, body-tormenting, and painful' — abbreviated — 'But surely I am capable of realizing, beyond the human condition, a distinction in noble knowledge and vision.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo yathābhipretaṃ gayāyāṃ vihṛtya gayāśīrṣe parvate jaṅgāvihāramanucaṃkramyamāṇo yenorubilvā senāpatigrāmakastadanusṛtastadanuprāpto 'bhūt / tatrādrākṣīnnadīṃ nairañjanāmacchodakāṃ sūpatīrthāṃ prāsādikaiśca drumagulmairalaṃkṛtāṃ samantataśca gocaragrāmām / tatra khalvapi bodhisattvasya mano 'tīva prasannamabhūt - samo batāyaṃ bhūmipradeśo ramaṇīyaḥ pratisaṃlayanānurūpaḥ / paryāptamidaṃ prahāṇārthikakulaputrasya / ahaṃ ca prahāṇārthī / yannvahamihaiva tiṣṭheyam //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having stayed at <s>Gayā</s> as he wished, wandering on foot on <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s> Mountain, traveled toward and reached the village of <s>Senāpati</s> at <s>Urubilvā</s>. There he saw the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> — with clear water, with good fords, adorned with pleasing trees and shrubs, and with villages for alms-gathering all around. There the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind became exceedingly serene [thinking]: 'Indeed, this spot of ground is level, delightful, suited for meditative retreat. It is sufficient for a son of good family seeking spiritual exertion. And I am one who seeks spiritual exertion. Let me remain right here.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - pañcakaṣāyakāle 'hamiha jambudvīpe 'vatīrṇo hīnādhimuktikeṣu sattveṣvākīrṇatīrthyavargeṣu nānādṛṣṭipraskanneṣu kāyapiṇḍagrāhābhiniviṣṭeṣu nānāvidhaiścātāpanaparitāpanaiḥ kāyaśuddhiṃ paryeṣante, prajñāpayanti ca saṃmūḍhāḥ / tadyathā - mantravicārakairhastapralehakairnayācanakairanāmantraṇakairanekamūlikairamatsyamāṃsakairavārṣikaiḥ surātuṣodakarvajanairekatripañcasaptakulabhikṣāgrahaṇairmūlaphalaśaivālakakuśapatragomayagomūtrapāyasadadhisarpiḥ phāṇitāmapiṣṭakamabhakṣaṇapānaiḥ sārasikāpotakasaṃdaṃśikotsṛṣṭasaṃprakṣālakaiḥ / grāmyāraṇyābhiśca vṛttibhiḥ / govratamṛgaśvavarāhavānarahastivrataiśca sthānamaunavīrāsanaiśca ekālāpakairyāvatsaptālāpakaiḥ / ekabhaktā ekāhorātracāturthyapañcaṣaṭkālāntarāśca
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'In the time of the five degenerations, I have descended here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, among beings of inferior disposition, among whom heretical groups are widespread, who have gone astray into various [wrong] views, who are attached to grasping at the physical body, and who seek bodily purification through various kinds of self-mortification and torment, and who, deluded, proclaim [such practices]. That is to say — those who practice: [examining] mantras, licking the hand, not asking, not being invited, [subsisting on] various roots, abstaining from fish and meat, abstaining from seasonal [food], [drinking] water from rice-husks and chaff, taking alms from one, three, five, or seven families, [eating] roots, fruits, moss, <s>kuśa</s>-grass shoots, cow-dung, cow-urine, milk-rice, curd, ghee, molasses, ground flour, [or] abstaining from food and drink; [practicing] the crane-chick [vow], the pincers [vow], the discarding [vow], the washing [vow]; subsisting on village or forest alms; the cow-vow, deer-vow, dog-vow, boar-vow, monkey-vow, elephant-vow; standing, silence, the heroic posture; one meal [a day] up to seven meals; eating once a day, once every two days, every fourth, fifth, or sixth day;

body.text: pakṣakṣapaṇamāsakṣapaṇacāndrāyaṇaiśca gṛdhrolūkapakṣadhāraṇaiśca phalamuñjāsanavalkaladarbhabalbajoṣṭrakambalājakambalakeśakambalacarmaniveśanaiśca ārdrapaṭāstopakajālaśayanaiśca bhasmaśarkarāpāṣāṇaphalakakaṇṭakatṛṇamusalaśayanāvākchirotkuṭukasthaṇḍilaśayanaiśca ekavāsadvitricatuṣpañcaṣaṭsaptabahuvāsobhirnagnabhāvaiśca sthānāsthānavidhibhiśca dīrghakeśanakhaśmaśrujaṭāmakuṭadhāraṇaiśca ekakolatilataṇḍulāhāraiśca bhasmamasinirmālyoddhṛtatamorajapāṃśupaṅkaparimrakṣaṇaiśca lomamuñjakeśanakhacīvarapañjarakaraṅkadhāraṇaiśca uṣṇodakataṇḍulodakaparisrāvitakāmbalikasthālīpānīyapānaiśca aṅgāradhātukaṣāyatridaṇḍamuṇḍikakuṇḍikakapālakhaṭvāṅgadhāraṇaiśca śuddhiṃ pratyavagacchanti saṃmūḍhāḥ / dhūmapānāgnipānādityanirīkṣaṇapañcatapaikapādordhvabāhusthānaikacaraṇaiśca tapaḥ saṃcinvanti / tuṣādyaṅgāradāhanikumbhasādhanapakvaśilāpacanāgnijalapraveśanamarutīrthagamanamaraṇaiśceṣṭāṃ gatiṃ mṛgayante / oṃkāravaṣaṭkārasvadhākārasvāhākārāśīrvacanastuticayanāvāhanajapyamantrādhyayanadhāraṇakaraṇaiśca śuddhiṃ pratyavagacchanti / śuddhaṃ cātmānaṃ manyamānā imānāśrayante / tadyathā - brahmendrarudraviṣṇudevīkumāramātṛkātyāyanīcandrādityavaiśravaṇavaruṇavāsavāśvinaunāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragarākṣasapretabhūtakumbhāṇḍapārṣadagaṇapatipiśācāṃśca devarṣirājarṣibrahmarṣīśca namasyanti, teṣu ca sārasaṃjñino bhavanti / pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśaṃ cāśrayante / girīnadīnadyutsasarohradataḍāgasāgarasaraḥpalvalapuṣkariṇīkūpavṛkṣagulmalatātṛṇasthāṇugoṣṭhaśmaśāna - catvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇamukhāni cāśrayante / gṛhastambhopalamusalāsidhanuparaśuśaraśaktitriśūlāṃśca namasyanti / dadhighṛtasarṣapayavapratisarādūrvāmaṇikanakarajatādibhiśca maṅgalaṃ pratyavagacchanti / evaṃvidhāni ime tīrthyāḥ kurvante, āśrayante ca saṃsārabhayabhītāḥ //
body.translated_text: fasting for a fortnight or a month, the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar fast); wearing vulture or owl feathers; wearing garments of fruit, <s>muñja</s>-grass, bark, <s>darbha</s>-grass, <s>balbaja</s>-grass, camel-hair, goat-hair, human-hair, or leather; sleeping on wet cloth, swaddling, or nets; sleeping on ashes, gravel, stone-slabs, thorns, grass, pestles; sleeping head-down, squatting, or on bare ground; wearing one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, or many garments; [or] nudity; various rules about proper and improper times and places; wearing long hair, nails, beards, and matted-hair crowns; eating one berry, one sesame seed, or one rice-grain; smearing [the body] with ashes, soot, discarded garlands, darkness, dust, or mud; wearing hair, <s>muñja</s>-grass, nails, bark, cage-frames, or skulls; drinking hot water, rice-water, filtered <s>kāmbalika</s>-water, or pot-water; carrying embers, relics, astringents, the triple-staff, [being a] shaven-headed one, carrying a water-pot, skull, bed-frame, or <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> — through such [practices] they, deluded, imagine purification. Through smoke-drinking, fire-drinking, gazing at the sun, the five-fire penance, standing on one foot, [keeping] arms raised, and standing on one leg, they accumulate 'austerity.' Through [practices like] burning with husks, fire, immersion in heated pots, cooking on hot stones, entering fire or water, going to water-fords, and dying — they seek the desired destiny. Through [reciting] <s>Oṃ</s>, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, <s>svāhā</s>, blessings, praises, accumulations, invocations, repetitive chanting, studying mantras, and memorizing [them] — they imagine purification. And thinking themselves purified, they resort to these [deities]: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Goddess, <s>Kumāra</s>, the [Divine] Mothers, <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, the moon, the sun, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, attendants, <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and <s>Devarṣis</s>, <s>Rājarṣis</s>, and <s>Brahmarṣis</s> — these they worship, and in these they perceive essence. They resort to earth, water, fire, wind, and space. They resort to mountains, rivers, streams, springs, ponds, lakes, pools, seas, reservoirs, puddles, lotus-pools, wells, trees, shrubs, creepers, grass, stumps, cow-pens, cremation-grounds, squares, crossroads, and market-fronts. They worship house-pillars, stones, pestles, swords, bows, axes, arrows, lances, and tridents. And through curd, ghee, mustard, barley, amulets, <s>dūrvā</s>-grass, jewels, gold, silver, and the like, they imagine auspiciousness. Such things do these heretics perform and resort to, [being] afraid of the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>! //

body.text: iha ca kecitparatra manyante svargāpavargāvasmākametebhyo nirvartsyeta iti mithyāmārgaprayātā aśaraṇe śaraṇasaṃjñino 'maṅgalye maṅgalasaṃjñino 'śuddhyā śuddhiṃ manyatoyannvahaṃ tādṛśaṃ vratatapoviśeṣamālabheyaṃ yathā sarvaparapravādinaśca nigṛhītāḥ syuḥ, karmakriyāpraṇaṣṭānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ karmakriyāvipraṇāśamādarśayeyam / dhyānagocarāṇāṃ ca rūpāvacarāṇāṃ ca devānāṃ dhyānaviśeṣopadarśanādāvarjanaṃ kuryāmiti //
body.translated_text: And some here think of the hereafter: 'Heaven and liberation will be attained by us through these [practices]' — thus they have gone astray on wrong paths, perceiving refuge where there is no refuge, perceiving auspiciousness where there is no auspiciousness, thinking there is purification where there is no purification. [The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought:] 'Let me undertake such a distinction in observances and austerities that all opposing teachers will be subdued, and I may demonstrate the functioning of <s>karma</s> to beings in whom [faith in] the functioning of <s>karma</s> has been lost; and through displaying the distinction of meditative attainments, I may attract the gods of the Form Realm who dwell in the range of meditation.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattva evaṃ cintayitvā ṣaḍvarṣikaṃ mahāghoraṃ vratatapaḥsuduṣkarātsuduṣkarāṃ duṣkaracaryāmālabhate sma / kena kāraṇenocyate duṣkaracaryeti? duṣkarakārikaiṣā, tenocyate duṣkaracaryeti / na sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā, yaḥ samarthastathārūpaṃ duṣkaraṃ caritum, anyatra caramabhavikādbodhisattvāt, ya āsphānakadhyānaṃ samāpadyate sma / kena kāraṇenocyate āsphānakamiti? sa caturthadhyānamādita eva samāpadyamāna āśvāsapraśvāsānuparodhayati saṃnirodhayati / akalpaṃ tad dhyānamavikalpamaniñjanamapanītamaspandanaṃ sarvatrānugataṃ ca sarvatra cāniśritam / na ca tad dhyānaṃ jātu kenacitsamāpannaṃ pūrvaṃ śaiṣyeṇa vā aśaiṣyeṇa vā pratyekabuddhena
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having reflected thus, undertook for six years the great and terrible observances and austerities — the most difficult of difficult, the hard-to-practice austerity. Why is it called 'hard-to-practice' (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>)? Because it is hard to perform — therefore it is called 'hard-to-practice.' There is no being in the realm of beings, whether human or non-human, who is capable of practicing such difficult practice — except the final-birth <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who entered the <s>āsphānaka</s> meditation. Why is it called <s>āsphānaka</s>? Entering the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> from the very beginning, he blocked and completely stopped the in-breath and out-breath. That meditation is without conceptual construction, without discrimination, without movement, withdrawn, without vibration, pervading everywhere, and everywhere unsupported. And that meditation was never attained previously by anyone — neither by a learner, nor by one beyond learning, nor by a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>,

body.text: vā caryāpratipannena vā bodhisattvena / ataścāsphānakaṃ nāmocyate / ākāśamaspharaṇamakaraṇamavikaraṇaṃ tacca sarvaṃ spharatīti hyākāśasamaṃ tad dhyānam / tenocyate āsphānakamiti //
body.translated_text: nor by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the path of practice. Therefore it is called <s>āsphānaka</s>. It is like space — non-extending, non-doing, non-modifying — yet it pervades everything; that meditation is like space. Therefore it is called <s>āsphānaka</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvo lokasyāścaryasaṃdarśanārthaṃ tīrthikānāṃ ca darpanirghātanārthaṃ parapravādināṃ ca nigrahārthaṃ devānāṃ cāvarjanārthamucchedaśāśvatavādināṃ ca sattvānāṃ krarmakriyāpraṇaṣṭānāṃ karmakriyāvatāraṇārthaṃ puṇyaphalodbhāvanārthaṃ jñānaphalasaṃdarśanārthaṃ dhyānāṅgavibhajanārtha kāyabalasthāmasaṃdarśanārthaṃ cittaśauryasaṃjananārthaṃ ca asaṃskṛtāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ paryaṅkamābhujya niṣīdati sma / niṣadya ca svakāyaṃ cetasā nigṛhṇīte sma, niṣpīḍayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of showing the world a marvel, for the purpose of crushing the pride of heretics, for the purpose of subduing opposing teachers, for the purpose of attracting the gods, for the purpose of demonstrating the functioning of <s>karma</s> to beings in whom [faith in] <s>karma</s> had been lost, for the purpose of revealing the fruit of merit, for the purpose of showing the fruit of knowledge, for the purpose of analyzing the factors of <s>dhyāna</s>, for the purpose of displaying bodily strength and power, and for the purpose of generating courage of mind — sat cross-legged on the uncultivated ground. Having sat, he restrained and compressed his own body with [his] mind. //

body.text: tato me bhikṣavo haimantikāsvaṣṭakarātriṣu tathā kāyaṃ nigṛhṇato niṣpīḍayataḥ kakṣābhyāmapi svedāḥ praśravanti sma / lalāṭādapi svedāḥ praśravanti sma / bhūmau nipatanti sma avaśyāyanta ūṣmāyanto bāṣpāyantaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma balavān puruṣo durbalataraṃ puruṣaṃ grīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā niṣpīḍayet, evameva bhikṣava imaṃ kāyaṃ cetasā nigṛhṇato niṣpīḍayataḥ kakṣābhyāmapi svedāḥ praśravanti sma / lalāṭādapi svedāḥ praśravanti sma / bhūbhau nipatanti sma avaśyāyanta ūṣmāyanto bāṣpāyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, during the eight cold nights of winter, as I thus restrained and compressed the body, sweat flowed from [my] armpits, sweat flowed from [my] forehead, and fell to the ground — dripping, steaming, and evaporating. Just as a strong man, seizing a weaker man by the neck, would squeeze [him], even so, O monks, as I thus restrained and compressed this body with [my] mind, sweat flowed from the armpits, sweat flowed from the forehead, and fell to the ground — dripping, steaming, and evaporating. //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - yannvahamāsphānakaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyāyeyam / tato me bhikṣava āsphānakaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyāyato mukhato nāsikātaścāśvāsapraśvāsā upaniruddhāvabhūtām / karṇachidrābhyāmuccaśabdā mahāśabdā niścaranti sma / tadyathāpi nāma karmāragagayā mathyamānāyāmuccaśabdo mahāśabdo niścarati, evameva me bhikṣavo mukhanāsikābhyāmāśvāsapraśvāsāvuparuddhāvabhūtāṃ śrotachidrābhyāmuccaśabdo mahāśabdo niścarati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, I thought: 'Let me now meditate the <s>āsphānaka</s> meditation.' Then, O monks, as I meditated the <s>āsphānaka</s> meditation, the in-breath and out-breath through mouth and nostrils were blocked. Loud, great sounds issued forth from [my] ear-openings. Just as loud, great sounds issue from a blacksmith's bellows when being pumped — even so, O monks, when the in-breath and out-breath through mouth and nostrils were blocked, loud, great sounds issued from [my] ear-openings. //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - yannvahaṃ bhūya āsphānakaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyāyeyamiti / tato me bhikṣavo mukhanāsikāśrotrāṇyuparuddhāni cābhūvan / teṣūparuddheṣu vāyururdhvaṃ śiraḥkapālamupanihanti sma / tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavaḥ puruṣaḥ kuṇḍayā śaktyā śiraḥkapālamupahanyād, evameva me bhikṣavo mukhanāsikāśrotreṣūparuddheṣu āśvāsapraśvāsā urdhvaṃ śiraḥkapālamupanighnanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, I thought: 'Let me meditate the <s>āsphānaka</s> meditation further.' Then, O monks, [the passages of] mouth, nostrils, and ears were blocked. When these were blocked, wind-currents struck upward against the skull. Just as, O monks, a man might strike the skull with a sharp lance — even so, O monks, when the [passages of] mouth, nostrils, and ears were blocked, the in-breath and out-breath struck upward against the skull. //

body.text: tāṃ cāvasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā bodhisattvasya tatra keciddevā evamāhu - kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ kālagato batāyaṃ siddhārthaḥ kumāraḥ / apare evamāhuḥ - nāyaṃ kālagataḥ / api tudhyānavihāra eṣo 'rhatāmevaṃvidha iti / tasyāṃ ca velāyamimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: And seeing this condition of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, some gods there said: 'Alas! This prince <s>Siddhārtha</s> has died!' Others said: 'He has not died — rather, this is the meditative practice of <s>Arhats</s>, which is of this nature.' And at that moment they spoke this verse —

children.text: mā khalvayaṃ śākyanarendragarbho hyapūrṇasaṃkalpa ihaiva raṇye /
children.translated_text: 'May this scion of the <s>Śākya</s> king not, with unfulfilled aspirations, right here in the forest,

children.text: kṛtvā trilokaṃ dukhitaṃ hyanāthaṃ kālaṃ kariṣyatyakṛtārtha eva // Lal_17.1 //
children.translated_text: having made the three worlds suffering and helpless, pass away with his purpose unaccomplished!' // Lal_17.1 //

body.text: hā sattvasārā sadṛḍhapratijñā saddharmayajñena nimantritābhūt /
body.translated_text: 'O essence of beings, of firm resolve! He was invited by the sacrifice of the true <s>dharma</s>!

body.text: vayaṃ purā te tuṣiteṣu nāthā kva sā pratijñā tava śuddhasattva // Lal_17.2 //
body.translated_text: We, formerly in <s>Tuṣita</s>, [heard your vow], O Lord — where is that promise of yours, O pure being?' // Lal_17.2 //

body.text: atha te devaputrāstrāyatriṃśeṣu deveṣu gatvā māyādevyā evamarthaṃ śrāvayanti - kālagataḥ kumāraḥ / atha māyādevī apsarāgaṇaparivṛtā ardharātrasamaye nairañjanāyāstīre yena bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāntā / sā paśyati sma bodhisattvaṃ śuṣkagātram / kālagatamiva dṛṣṭvā bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhā roditumārabdhā / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputras</s>, having gone to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, announced to <s>Māyādevī</s>: 'The prince has died!' Then <s>Māyādevī</s>, surrounded by hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, at midnight, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s>. She saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with his body emaciated. Seeing [him] as if dead, with a voice choked with tears, she began to weep. And at that moment she spoke this verse —

children.text: yadā jāto 'si me putra vane lumbinisāhvaye /
children.translated_text: 'When you were born, my son, in the grove called <s>Lumbinī</s>,

children.text: siṃhavaccāgṛhītastvaṃ prakrāntaḥ sapta padā svayam // Lal_17.3 //
children.translated_text: you stood up boldly like a lion and strode seven steps by yourself! // Lal_17.3 //

children.text: diśāṃ cālokya cature vācā te pravyāhṛtā śubhā /
children.translated_text: Having looked upon the four directions, you uttered this auspicious speech:

children.text: iyaṃ me paścimā jātiḥ sā te na paripūritā // Lal_17.4 //
children.translated_text: "This is my final birth!" — but that [vow] of yours has not been fulfilled! // Lal_17.4 //

children.text: asitenābhinirdiṣṭo buddho loke bhaviṣyasi /
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s> declared: "He shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world!"

children.text: kṣuṇṇaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ tasya na dṛṣṭā tena nityatā // Lal_17.5 //
children.translated_text: His prophecy has been brought to naught — but constancy was never seen in it! // Lal_17.5 //

children.text: cakravartiśriyaṃ putra napi bhuktā manoramā /
children.translated_text: Neither have you enjoyed, my son, the delightful glory of a <s>Cakravartin</s>,

children.text: na ca bodhimanuprāpto yāto 'si nidhanaṃ vane // Lal_17.6 //
children.translated_text: nor have you attained <s>bodhi</s> — [and now] you have gone to destruction in the forest! // Lal_17.6 //

children.text: putrārthe kaṃ prapadyāmi kaṃ va krandāmi duḥkhitā /
children.translated_text: For the sake of [my] son, to whom shall I turn? To whom shall I cry out in grief?

children.text: ko me dadyekaputrasya kiṃcitprāṇasya jīvitam // Lal_17.7 //
children.translated_text: Who will give me some [portion of] life-breath for [my] only son?' // Lal_17.7 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kaiṣā ati tvāṃ karuṇaṃ rudāsi prakīrṇakeśā vinivṛttaśobhā /
children.translated_text: 'Who is this that weeps so piteously, with disheveled hair, her beauty faded,

children.text: putraṃ hyatīvā paridevayantī viceṣṭamānā dharaṇītalasthā // Lal_17.8 //
children.translated_text: lamenting exceedingly for [her] son, writhing upon the ground?' // Lal_17.8 //

body.text: māyādevī āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māyādevī</s> said:

children.text: mayā tu daśamāsāṃ vai kukṣau vajra ivā dhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I who bore [you] in my womb for ten months, like a <s>vajra</s> (diamond) —'

children.text: sā te 'haṃ putrakā mātā vilapāmi suduḥkhitā // Lal_17.9 //
children.translated_text: I, who am your mother, O dear son, lament, deeply grieved. // Lal_17.9 //

body.text: atha bodhisattva āśvāsayannuvāca - na bhetavyaṃ putralālase, śramaṃ te saphalaṃ kariṣyasi / amoghaṃ buddhaparityāgam / asitanirdeśaṃ ca vyaktaṃ kariṣyāmi / dīpaṃkarasya vyākaraṇaṃ vyaktīkariṣyāmi ca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, consoling her, said: 'Do not be afraid, O fond mother. Your labor shall I make fruitful. Not in vain is the renunciation of a <s>Buddha</s>. And I shall make manifest the prophecy of <s>Asita</s>. I shall fulfill the prediction of <s>Dīpaṅkara</s>.'

body.text:
api śatadhā vasudhā vikīryeta meruḥ plave cāmbhasi ratnaśṛṅgaḥ /
candrārkatārāgaṇa bhū pateta pṛthajano naiva ahaṃ mriyeyam /
body.translated_text: 'Even if the earth were scattered into a hundred pieces, even if <s>Meru</s> with its jewel-peaks were to float upon the waters, even if the moon, sun, and host of stars were to fall to the earth — I, who am no ordinary being, shall not die.

body.text: yasmānna śoko tvayi atra kāryo na vai cirād drakṣyasi buddhabodhim // Lal_17.10 //
body.translated_text: Therefore no grief should be made on your account — before long you shall see the <s>Buddha</s>'s awakening!' // Lal_17.10 //

body.text: sahaśravaṇādeva devī māyā saṃpraharṣitaromakūpajātā bodhisattvaṃ māndāravapuṣpairabhyavakirya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtvā divyatūryaiḥ saṃpravādyamānairyena svabhavanaṃ tenopajagāma //
body.translated_text: Immediately upon hearing [this], the goddess <s>Māyā</s>, her hair standing on end with joy, having scattered <s>māndārava</s> flowers upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and circumambulated him three times, with divine instruments being played, went to her own abode. //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - santyeke śramaṇabrāhmaṇā ye alpāhāratayā śuddhiṃ manyante / yannvahamalpāhāratayā pratipadyeyamiti / abhijānāmyahaṃ bhikṣava ekamevādvitīyaṃ kolamāhāramāhartum / syātkhalu punarbhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ eṣā buddhiḥ - mahattaraṃ tatra kāle kolamāsīditi / na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / atha khalviyadeva tatra kāle kolamabhūt / tasya me bhikṣava ekameva kolamāhāramāharato 'dvitīyaṃ kāyo 'tyarthaṃ karśito 'bhūddurbalaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣava āsītakīparvāṇi vā kālāparvāṇi vā, evameva me 'ṅgapratyaṅgānyabhūvan / tadyathāpi nāma karkaṭapārśukā, evameva me pārśukā abhūvan / tadyathāpi nāma vāhanakāraśālāyāṃ vā hastiśālāyāṃ vā jīrṇāyāmubhayato vivṛtāyāṃ gopānasyāntarikāśca virājante vyavabhāsante, evameva me pārśukā antaḥkāye ubhayato virājante sma vyavabhāsante sma / tadyathāpi nāma vartanyā veṇī unnatāvanatā bhavati samaviṣamā, evaṃ me pṛṣṭhīkaṇṭako 'bhūdunnatāvanataḥ samaviṣamaḥ / tadyathā tiktakālābustaruṇo lūna āmlāno bhavati saṃmlānaḥ samutpuṭakajātaḥ evameva śira āmlānamabhūtsaṃmlānaṃ samutpuṭakajātam / tadyathāpi nāma grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse kūpatārakā dūragatā bhavanti, kṛcchreṇa saṃprakāśyante, evameva me 'kṣitārakau duragatāvabhūtāṃ kṛcchreṇa saṃprakāśyete sma / tadyathāpi nāmājapadaṃ voṣṭrapadaṃ vā, evameva me kakṣākukṣivakṣādīnyabhūvan / tato yadāhaṃ bhikṣavaḥ pāṇinā kukṣiṃ spṛśāmīti pṛṣṭhikaṇṭakamevāsprākṣam / uttiṣṭhāmīti cābhisaṃskurvaṃstathaivāvakubjaḥ prayāmeṇa prāpatam / tataḥ kṛcchreṇotthito 'pi pāṃśukṛtāni gātrāṇi pāṇinā pramṛjato me pūtiromāṇi kāyācchīryante sma / yāpi me 'bhūtpaurāṇī śubhavarṇatanuḥ sāpyantaradhādyathāpīdaṃ rūkṣapradhānaṃ prahitātmanaḥ / sāmantāśca me gocaragrāmavāsina evaṃ saṃjānante sma - kālako bata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / śyāmako bata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / madguracchavirbata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / yāpyasyābhūtpaurāṇī śubhavarṇā nibhā, sāpyantarhitā //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'There are some <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who believe that purity comes through eating little food. Let me undertake the practice of eating little food.' I recall, O monks, taking as food only a single <s>kola</s>-berry, without a second. Now, O monks, you might think: 'The <s>kola</s>-berry must have been very large at that time.' But it should not be seen thus. The <s>kola</s>-berry at that time was just as it is [now]. As I, O monks, took only a single <s>kola</s>-berry as food without a second, my body became extremely emaciated and weak. Just as, O monks, <s>āsītakī</s> knots or <s>kāla</s>-reed knots [are], so were my limbs and sub-limbs. Just as the ribs of a crab [are], so were my ribs. Just as in an old, dilapidated chariot-shed or elephant-stable, open on both sides, the rafters are visible and gleam, so too my ribs were visible and gleamed within my body on both sides. Just as the curve of a spindle is raised and lowered, uneven, so was my spinal column — raised and lowered, uneven. Just as a bitter gourd, young, cut, becomes withered, shriveled, and puckered, so too my head became withered, shriveled, and puckered. Just as in the last month of summer, the stars of a well are far withdrawn and barely visible, so too my eye-sockets were far withdrawn and barely visible. Just as the footprint of a goat or camel [appears], so were my armpits, belly, and chest. Then, O monks, when I tried to touch my belly with my hand, I grasped the very spinal column. When I intended to stand up, I fell over stooped just as I was. Then, having risen with great difficulty, when I rubbed my dust-covered limbs with my hand, my putrid hairs fell from my body. Whatever had been my former fair and beautiful complexion — that too had vanished, as one whose chief food is harsh [and] who is given to self-mortification. And the neighboring villagers in my alms-round territory recognized me thus: 'Alas, how dark is the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s>! How swarthy is the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s>! His skin is the color of a <s>madgura</s>-fish! Whatever was his former beautiful fair complexion — that too has vanished.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - yannvahaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayālpāhāratayā pratipadyeyamiti / abhijānāmyahaṃ bhikṣava ekameva taṇḍulamadvitīyamāhāramāhartum / syādbhikṣavo yuṣmākamevaṃ mahattaraṃ taṇḍulaṃ tasmin kāle 'bhūditi / na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam / athaitāvāneva tasmin kāle taṇḍulo 'bhūt / tasya me bhikṣava ekaṃ taṇḍulamāharataḥ kṣipraṃ kāyo 'bhūditi pūrvavadyāvanmadguracchavirbata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautama iti / yāpyasya sābhūtpaurāṇī śubhavarṇatanuḥ sāpyantarhiteti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'Let me undertake to an even greater degree the practice of eating little food.' I recall, O monks, taking as food only a single grain of rice without a second. Now, monks, you might think: 'The grain of rice must have been very large at that time.' But it should not be seen thus. The grain of rice at that time was just as it is [now]. As I, O monks, took a single grain of rice as food, quickly my body became [emaciated]' — as before, up to: 'His skin is the color of a <s>madgura</s>-fish! Whatever was his former beautiful fair complexion — that too has vanished.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - yannvahaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayālpāhāratāyai pratipadyeyamiti / abhijānāmyahaṃ bhikṣava ekameva tilamadvitīyamāhāramāhārayitum / peyālaṃ / yāvatsāpyasya śubhavarṇatanurantarhiteti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'Let me undertake to an even greater degree the practice of eating little food.' I recall, O monks, taking as food only a single sesame seed without a second. [Abbreviated.] Up to: 'Whatever was his beautiful fair complexion — that too has vanished.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - santyeke śramaṇabrāhmaṇā ye 'nāhāratayā śuddhiṃ manyante / yannvahaṃ sarveṇa sarvamanāhāratāyai pratipadyeyamiti / tato 'haṃ bhikṣavo 'nāhārasthito 'bhūvan / tasya me bhikṣavo 'nāhārasya kāyo 'tīva śuṣko 'bhūt kṛśo durbalaḥ, tadyathāpi nāma āsitakīparvāṇi vā kālāparvāṇi vā / tato dviguṇatriguṇacaturguṇapañcaguṇadaśaguṇaṃ me kṛśānyaṅgapratyaṅgānyabhūvan / tadyathā karkaṭakapārśukā vāhanaśālāyāṃ vā gopānasī (pārśve) dviparivartanā veṇīvatpṛṣṭhīkaṇṭakaḥ / tiktālābuvacchiraḥkapālam, kūpatārakā ivākṣitārake / so 'haṃ bhikṣavaḥ sādhukamuttiṣṭhāmīti gātrāṇyabhisaṃskurvannavakubjaḥ prāpatam / kṛcchreṇāpi cotthitaḥ pāṃśukṛtāni me gātrāṇi pramṛjataḥ pūtimūlāni romāṇyaśīryanta / yāpi me sābhūcchubhavarṇatanunibhā, sāpyantaradhāt / tadyathāpi tadrūkṣapradhānaprahitātmakatvāt / sāmantāśca me gocaragrāmavāsino janā evaṃ saṃjānante sma - kālako bata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / śyāmako bata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / madguracchavirbata bhoḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / yāpyasya sābhūtpaurāṇī śubhavarṇanibhā sāpyantarhiteti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'There are some <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who believe that purity comes through not eating at all. Let me undertake the complete abstention from food.' Then, O monks, I stood without food. As I, O monks, stood without food, my body became extremely dried up, emaciated, and weak — just as <s>āsītakī</s> knots or <s>kāla</s>-reed knots [are]. Then my limbs and sub-limbs became two-, three-, four-, five-, ten-fold more emaciated. As the ribs of a crab; as [the rafters of] a chariot-stable, the rafters of a stable (on the side); the spinal column like a spindle's curve bent in two turns; the skull like a bitter gourd; the eye-sockets like stars of a well. I, O monks, intending to stand up properly, making an effort with my limbs, fell over stooped. Having risen with great difficulty, as I rubbed my dust-covered limbs, my hair fell from its very roots, putrid. Whatever had been my beautiful, fair complexion — that too had vanished, on account of my dedication to harsh food and self-mortification. And the neighboring villagers recognized me: 'Alas, how dark is the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s>! How swarthy is the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s>! His skin is the color of a <s>madgura</s>-fish! Whatever was his former beautiful, fair complexion — that too has vanished.' //

body.text: rājāpi tadā śuddhodanaḥ pratipratidivasaṃ bodhisattvasyāntike dūtaṃ preṣayati sma //
body.translated_text: And King <s>Śuddhodana</s> at that time sent a messenger day after day to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo lokasyādbhutakriyāsaṃdarśanārthaṃ pūrvavadyāvatkarmakriyāpraṇaṣṭānāṃ sattvānāṃ karmakriyāvatāraṇārthaṃ puṇyasaṃcayānāṃ codbhāvanārthaṃ mahājñānasya ca guṇasaṃdarśanārthaṃ dhyānāṅgānāṃ ca vibhajanārthamekatilakolataṇḍulena ṣaḍvarṣāṇi duṣkaracaryāmanuvartayantamupadarśayati sma / adīnamānasaḥ ṣaḍvarṣā bodhisattvo yathā niṣaṇṇa evāsthāt paryaṅkena / na ca īryāpathāccyavate sma / nātapācchāyāmagamanna chāyāyā ātapam / na ca vātātapavṛṣṭiparitrāṇamakaronna ca daṃśamaśakasarīsṛpānapanayati sma / na coccārapraśrāvaśleṣmasiṃhāṇakānutsṛjati sma / na ca samiñjanaprasāraṇamakarot / na ca pārśvodarapṛṣṭhasthānenāsthāt / ye 'pi ca te mahāmeghā durdinavarṣāśaniśaradgrīṣmahaimantikāḥ, te 'pi bodhisattvasya kāye nipatanti sma / na cāntato bodhisattvaḥ pāṇināpi pracchādanamakarot / na cendriyāṇi pithayati sma / na cendriyārthān gṛhṇite sma / ye ca tatrāgaman grāmakumārakā vā grāmakumārikā vā gopālakā vā paśupālakā vā tṛṇahārikā vā kāṣṭhahārikā vā gomayahārikā vā, te bodhisattvaṃ pāṃśupiśācamiti manyante sma / tena ca krīḍanti sma / pāṃśubhiścainaṃ mrakṣayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of displaying his wondrous deeds to the world — as before, up to: for the purpose of establishing beings who had lost faith in the efficacy of action in the efficacy of action, and for the purpose of generating accumulations of merit, and for the purpose of displaying the virtues of great knowledge, and for the purpose of distinguishing the constituents of <s>dhyāna</s> — displayed the practice of austerities (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>) for six years on [a diet of] one sesame seed, one <s>kola</s>-berry, one grain of rice. With undaunted mind, for six years, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained just as he had sat down, cross-legged. He did not deviate from his posture. He did not move from sun to shade, nor from shade to sun. He did not seek shelter from wind, sun, or rain. He did not brush away gadflies, mosquitoes, or creeping things. He did not relieve himself of feces, urine, phlegm, or mucus. He did not bend or stretch [his limbs]. He did not stand upon his side, belly, or back. And even the great clouds — those of the rainy season, of thunderstorms, of hailstorms, of autumn, of summer, and of winter — even these fell upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> did not so much as cover himself even with his hand. He did not close his sense-organs, nor did he grasp at sense-objects. And whoever came there — village boys, village girls, cowherds, goatherds, grass-gatherers, wood-gatherers, dung-gatherers — they thought the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was a dust-demon. And they played with him, and smeared him with dust. //

body.text: tatra bodhisattvastaiḥ ṣaḍbhirvarṣaistāvallūhanyūnadurbalakāyaḥ saṃvṛtto 'bhūt, yadasya karṇaśrotābhyāṃ tṛṇatūlakaṃ prakṣipya nāsāśrotābhyāṃ niṣkāsyate sma / nāsāśrotābhyāṃ prakṣipya karṇaśrotābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: There, over those six years, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body became so emaciated, reduced, and weak that if a tuft of grass-cotton were inserted through his ear-openings, it would come out through his nose-openings; if inserted through his nose-openings, it would

body.text: niṣkāsyate sma / karṇaśrotābhyāṃ prakṣipya mukhadvāreṇa niṣkāsyate sma / mukhadvāreṇa prakṣipya karṇanāsikāśrotābhyo niṣkāsyate sma / nāsāyāṃ prakṣipya karṇanāsikāmukhadvāreṇa niṣkāsyate sma //
body.translated_text: come out through his ear-openings; if inserted through his ear-openings, it would come out through his mouth; if inserted through his mouth, it would come out through his ear and nose openings; if inserted through his nose, it would come out through the openings of his ears, nose, and mouth. //

body.text: ye ca te devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā manuṣyāmanuṣyā bodhisattvasya guṇeṣu pratyakṣāḥ, te rātriṃdivaṃ samadhiṣṭhā bodhisattvasya pūjāṃ kurvanti sma / praṇidhānāni ca kurvanti sma //
body.translated_text: And those gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans who had directly witnessed the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s virtues — they day and night stood in attendance, performing worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and making aspirations. //

body.text: tatra bodhisattvena tai ṣaḍbhirvarṣairduṣkaracaryāṃ saṃdarśayatā paripūrṇāni dvādaśanayutāni devamanuṣyāṇāṃ tribhiryānaiḥ paripācitānyabhūvan //
body.translated_text: There, during those six years of displaying the practice of austerities, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> ripened a full twelve <s>nayutas</s> of gods and humans by means of the three vehicles. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Hereupon this was said —

children.text: tasya ca guṇānvitasya purādviniṣkramya bodhisattvasya /
children.translated_text: Having gone forth from the city, that virtue-endowed <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s

children.text: cintā upāyayuktā sattvārthahitāya utpannā // Lal_17.11 //
children.translated_text: skillful reflections arose for the welfare and benefit of beings. // Lal_17.11 //

children.text: pañcasu kaṣāyakāle hīne 'dharmādhimuktike loke /
children.translated_text: In the time of the five defilements (<s>kaṣāya</s>), in a debased world inclined to unrighteousness,

children.text: jāto 'smi jambudvipe dharmakriyauddhure loke // Lal_17.12 //
children.translated_text: I have been born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in a world that has abandoned the practice of <s>Dharma</s>. // Lal_17.12 //

children.text: ākīrṇa tīrthikagaṇaiḥ kautūhalamaṅgalairime yuktā /
children.translated_text: Overrun by hordes of <s>tīrthikas</s>, these [people] are devoted to curious rituals and auspicious rites;

children.text: kāyopakramakaraṇairmanyante bāliśāḥ śuddhim // Lal_17.13 //
children.translated_text: through bodily mortifications and treatments, the foolish believe [they attain] purity. // Lal_17.13 //

children.text: agnipraveśamaruprapātapāṃśubhasmādimakṣitā nagnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Entering fire, leaping from cliffs, smeared with dust and ashes, naked,

children.text: kāyaparitāpanārthaṃ pañcātapayogamanuyuktāḥ // Lal_17.14 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of tormenting the body, [they are] devoted to the practice of the five fires (<s>pañcātapa</s>). // Lal_17.14 //

children.text: mantrāvicārakaraṇā keciddhastāvalehakā abudhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some are devoted to mantras and divination; some are hand-lickers (eating from the hand alone), foolish;

children.text: na ca kumbhamukhakaroṭānna dhārakuśalāntarācca gṛhṇanti // Lal_17.15 //
children.translated_text: they do not accept [food] from a pot-mouth or a bowl, nor do they accept what is offered skillfully between [meals]. // Lal_17.15 //

children.text: na ca yatra svānubhavatī na cāhitaṃ tena tiṣṭhavākyasya /
children.translated_text: Nor do they remain where one experiences [ease]; nor [does one] abide by the word of [one whose food is] not harmful.

children.text: kulabhikṣa eka gṛhyā śuddhaṃ manyantihātmānam // Lal_17.16 //
children.translated_text: Taking alms from a single family, a single house, they consider themselves pure. // Lal_17.16 //

children.text: varjenti sarpitailaṃ phāṇitadadhidugdhamatsyamāṃsāni /
children.translated_text: They avoid ghee, oil, molasses, curds, milk, fish, and meat;

children.text: śyāmākaśākabhakṣā mṛṇālagarḍulakaṇābhakṣāḥ // Lal_17.17 //
children.translated_text: they eat millet, greens, lotus-stalks, <s>garḍula</s>-seeds, and grain. // Lal_17.17 //

children.text: mūlaphalapatrabhakṣāḥ kuśacīvaracarmakambaladharāśca /
children.translated_text: They eat roots, fruits, and leaves; they wear [garments of] <s>kuśa</s>-grass, bark, skins, and blankets.

children.text: apare bhramanti nagnāḥ satyamidaṃ mohamanyaditi mūḍhāḥ // Lal_17.18 //
children.translated_text: Others wander about naked — 'This is truth, all else is delusion!' — such are the deluded. // Lal_17.18 //

children.text: dhārenti ūrdhvahastā urdhvaṃkeśā jaṭāśca dhārenti /
children.translated_text: They hold their arms upraised, their hair standing upward, and they wear matted locks.

children.text: mārgānatipranaṣṭā amārgasaṃsthāḥ sugatigamanakāmāḥ // Lal_17.19 //
children.translated_text: Lost from the [true] path, established on the wrong path, [yet] desiring to go to a good destination! // Lal_17.19 //

children.text: tṛṇamusalabhasmaśayanāḥ kaṇṭakaśayanāśca utkuṭadhyāyi /
children.translated_text: Sleeping on grass, pestles, ashes, or thorns, squatting in meditation,

children.text: sthita kecidekapāde ūrdhvamukhāścandrasūrya paśyantaḥ // Lal_17.20 //
children.translated_text: some standing on one foot, facing upward, gazing at the moon and sun. // Lal_17.20 //

children.text: utsāṃ sarasataḍāgāṃ sāgarasaritaśca candrasūryau ca /
children.translated_text: They worship springs, lakes, ponds, oceans, rivers, the moon, the sun,

children.text: vṛkṣagiriśailaśikharāṃ kumbhaṃ dharaṇīṃ namasyante // Lal_17.21 //
children.translated_text: trees, mountains, mountain-peaks, water-jars, and the earth. // Lal_17.21 //

children.text: vividhaiśca kāraṇaiste kāyaṃ pariśodhayanti saṃmūḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: By various such means, the deluded purify [only] the body;

children.text: mithyādṛṣṭiparītāḥ kṣipraṃ prapatantyapāyeṣu // Lal_17.22 //
children.translated_text: pervaded by wrong views, they quickly fall into the lower realms. // Lal_17.22 //

children.text: yannūnamahaṃ vratatapa duṣkaracaryāṃ samārabhe ghorām /
children.translated_text: 'What if I were to undertake a fierce austerity (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>) of vows and <s>tapas</s>,

children.text: yaṃ duṣkaraṃ na śakyaṃ carituṃ devairmanuṣyairvā // Lal_17.23 //
children.translated_text: which is impossible for gods or humans to practice — // Lal_17.23 //

children.text: āsphānakaṃ ca dhyānaṃ dhyāyeyaṃ vajrakalpadṛḍhasthānam /
children.translated_text: 'and meditate the <s>āsphānaka</s> meditation, immovable, firm as diamond,

children.text: yaṃ dhyānaṃ na samarthāḥ pratyekajināpi darśayitum // Lal_17.24 //
children.translated_text: a meditation that even <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are unable to display! // Lal_17.24 //

children.text: santīha devamanujāḥ tīrthika lūhavratena hṛṣyante /
children.translated_text: 'There are here gods and humans and <s>tīrthikas</s> who rejoice in emaciated vows;

children.text: teṣa paripākaheto duṣkaravratatapa rabheya sūtīvram // Lal_17.25 //
children.translated_text: for their ripening, let me undertake exceedingly intense vows and <s>tapas</s> of austerity.' // Lal_17.25 //

children.text: paryaṅkamābhujitvā upaviṣṭo 'bhūtsthale asaṃstīrṇe /
children.translated_text: Having crossed his legs, he sat down upon the bare ground, unsoftened,

children.text: kolatilataṇḍulenā āhāravidhiṃ vidarśayati // Lal_17.26 //
children.translated_text: and displayed the manner of eating with [only] a <s>kola</s>-berry, a sesame seed, and a grain of rice. // Lal_17.26 //

children.text: āśvāsaviprahīnaḥ praśvāsavarjitu na ceñjate bālavān /
children.translated_text: devoid of inhalation, deprived of exhalation, without any movement, yet powerful —

children.text: ṣaḍvarṣāṇi pravaraṃ dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.27 //
children.translated_text: for six supreme years, he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.27 //

children.text: kalpaṃ no na vikalpaṃ na ceñjanaṃ nāpimanyena pracāram /
children.translated_text: Without conceptualization, without discrimination, without movement, without any other activity —

children.text: ākāśadhātuspharaṇaṃ dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.28 //
children.translated_text: pervading the element of space, he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.28 //

children.text: na ca ātapātu chāyāṃ chāyāyā nātapaṃ gataścāsau /
children.translated_text: He has not gone from sunlight to shade, nor from shade to sunlight —

children.text: meruriva niṣprakampyo dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.29 //
children.translated_text: immovable like <s>Meru</s>, he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.29 //

children.text: na ca vātavṛṣṭichadanaṃ na daṃśamaśakāsarīsṛpātrāṇam /
children.translated_text: Without shelter from wind and rain, without protection from gadflies, mosquitoes, and serpents —

children.text: avikopitayā caryā dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.30 //
children.translated_text: with undisturbed practice, he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.30 //

children.text: na ca kevalamātmārthaṃ dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam /
children.translated_text: Not merely for his own benefit does he meditate the unshakable meditation,

children.text: anyatra karuṇacitto bhāvī lokasya vipulārtham // Lal_17.31 //
children.translated_text: but with a mind of compassion, for the vast benefit of the world in the future. // Lal_17.31 //

children.text: ye grāmadārakāśca gopālāḥ kāṣṭhahāratṛṇahārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Village children, cowherds, and gatherers of wood and grass

children.text: pāṃśupiśācakamiti taṃ manyante pāṃśunā ca mrakṣanti // Lal_17.32 //
children.translated_text: think him a 'dust-demon' and smear him with dust. // Lal_17.32 //

children.text: aśucīnā ca kirante vividhāste kāraṇāśca kārenti /
children.translated_text: They cast impurities upon him and subject him to various provocations,

children.text: na ca iñjate bhramati vā dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.33 //
children.translated_text: yet he neither stirs nor wavers — he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.33 //

children.text: na ca namati no vinamate na kāyaparirakṣaṇā spṛśati /
children.translated_text: He neither bends nor stoops; no care for the body's protection touches him;

children.text: kiṃcinnoccāraprasravaṃ śabdeṣu na saṃtrasī na paraprekṣī // Lal_17.34 //
children.translated_text: no excretion or urination whatsoever; he is not startled by sounds, nor does he glance at others. // Lal_17.34 //

children.text: saṃśuṣkamāṃsarudhiraṃ carmasnāyvasthikāśca avaśiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: His flesh and blood dried up, only skin, sinews, and bones remaining,

children.text: udarācca pṛṣṭhivaṃśo vidṛśyate vartitā yathā veṇī // Lal_17.35 //
children.translated_text: his backbone visible through his belly — twisted like a braided cord. // Lal_17.35 //

children.text: ye te kṛtādhikārā devāḥ suranāgayakṣagandharvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> who have accumulated merit

children.text: pratyakṣaguṇadharasyā karonti pūjāṃ divārātrau // Lal_17.36 //
children.translated_text: worship the one whose virtues are manifest, day and night. // Lal_17.36 //

children.text: praṇidhiṃ ca kurvate te vayamapi tādṛśa bhavāmahe kṣipram /
children.translated_text: They make the vow: 'May we too quickly become like this one,

children.text: yatha eṣa gaganacitto dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.37 //
children.translated_text: who, with mind [vast] as space, meditates the unshakable meditation.' // Lal_17.37 //

children.text: na ca kevalamātmārthaṃ na dhyānasvādanānna sukhabuddhyā /
children.translated_text: Not merely for his own benefit, not for the taste of meditation, not with the idea of happiness —

children.text: anyatra karuṇabuddhyā kariṣyatyarthaṃ vipula loke // Lal_17.38 //
children.translated_text: but with the mind of compassion, he will accomplish vast benefit in the world. // Lal_17.38 //

children.text: nihatāḥ parapravādā dhyāmīkṛta tīrthikā mativihīnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Rival teachers are defeated, the <s>tīrthikas</s> are humbled, bereft of understanding;

children.text: karmakriyā ca darśita yā proktā kāśyape vācā // Lal_17.39 //
children.translated_text: the deeds of ritual action are shown — as was proclaimed in the words of <s>Kāśyapa</s>. // Lal_17.39 //

children.text: krakucchandakasya bodhi bodhiriha sudurlabhā bahubhi kalpaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The awakening of <s>Krakucchanda</s> — such awakening is exceedingly rare, [attained only] over many <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: janatāyā ityarthaṃ dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.40 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of all people, he meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.40 //

children.text: dvādaśanayutā pūrṇā vinīta marumānuṣāstribhiryānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>nayutas</s> in full — gods and humans — were trained through the three vehicles;

children.text: etadadhikṛtya sumati dhyāyatyāsphānakaṃ dhyānam // Lal_17.41 //
children.translated_text: with this in mind, <s>Sumati</s> meditates the unshakable meditation. // Lal_17.41 //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare duṣkaracaryāparivarto nāma saptadaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventeenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Difficult Practices' (<s>Duṣkaracaryāparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 18
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 18.

body.text: nairañjanāparivarto 'ṣṭādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Eighteenth Chapter: On the <s>Nairañjanā</s> (<s>Nairañjanāparivarta</s>).

body.text: māraśca bhikṣavaḥ pāpīyān bodhisattvasya ṣaḍvarṣāṇi duṣkaracaryāṃ carataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddho 'bhūt avatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī / na ca kadācitkiṃcidavatāramadhyagacchat / so 'vatāramanadhigacchannirviṇṇo vipratisārī prākrāmat //
body.translated_text: And <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, O monks, had followed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> for six years as he practiced difficult austerities, looking for an opportunity, seeking an opening. But he never found any opening whatsoever. Not finding an opening, he departed, frustrated and filled with regret. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Thereupon this was said —

children.text: ramaṇīyānyaraṇyāni vanagulmāśca vīrudhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Delightful are the forests, the groves, shrubs, and creepers

children.text: prācīnamurubilvāyāṃ yatra nairañjanā nadī // Lal_18.1 //
children.translated_text: in eastern <s>Urubilvā</s>, where the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> flows. // Lal_18.1 //

children.text: prahāṇāyodyataṃ tatra satataṃ dṛḍhavikramam /
children.translated_text: There [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], risen for exertion, of unwavering resolve,

children.text: parākramantaṃ vīryeṇa yogakṣemasya prāptaye // Lal_18.2 //
children.translated_text: striving constantly with vigor for the attainment of the state of peace (<s>yogakṣema</s>) — // Lal_18.2 //

children.text: namucirmadhurāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣamāṇo upāgamat /
children.translated_text: <s>Namuci</s>, speaking in a sweet voice, approached:

children.text: śākyaputrā samuttiṣṭha kāyakhedena kiṃ tava // Lal_18.3 //
children.translated_text: 'Rise, O son of the <s>Śākyas</s>! What use is this bodily torment to you? // Lal_18.3 //

children.text: jīvato jīvitaṃ śreyo jīvan dharmaṃ cariṣyasi /
children.translated_text: Life is better for the living; living, you will practice <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: jīvaṃ hi tāni kurute yāni kṛtvā na śocati // Lal_18.4 //
children.translated_text: the living man does those deeds which, having done, he does not grieve. // Lal_18.4 //

children.text: kṛśo vivarṇo dīnastvaṃ antike maraṇaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: You are emaciated, discolored, pitiable — death is near to you;

children.text: sahasrabhāge maraṇaṃ ekabhāge ca jīvitam // Lal_18.5 //
children.translated_text: a thousand parts belong to death, one part to life. // Lal_18.5 //

children.text: dadataḥ satataṃ dānaṃ agnihotraṃ ca juhvataḥ /
children.translated_text: By constantly giving gifts and offering the <s>Agnihotra</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyati mahatpuṇyaṃ kiṃ prahāṇe kariṣyasi // Lal_18.6 //
children.translated_text: great merit will arise — what will you accomplish by striving?' // Lal_18.6 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ mārgaṃ prahāṇasya duṣkaraṃ cittanigraham /
children.translated_text: 'The path of striving is difficult; restraint of the mind is hard to accomplish' —

children.text: imāṃ vācaṃ tadā māro bodhisattvamathābravīt // Lal_18.7 //
children.translated_text: these words <s>Māra</s> then spoke to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // Lal_18.7 //

children.text: taṃ tathāvādinaṃ māraṃ bodhisattvastato 'bravīt /
children.translated_text: To <s>Māra</s>, who spoke thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied:

children.text: pramattabandho pāpīya svenārthena tvamāgataḥ // Lal_18.8 //
children.translated_text: 'O kinsman of the heedless, Evil One! You have come for your own purpose! // Lal_18.8 //

children.text: aṇumātraṃ hi me puṇyairartho māra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: I have not the slightest need for merit, O <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: artho yeṣāṃ tu puṇyena tānevaṃ vaktumarhasi // Lal_18.9 //
children.translated_text: those who have need of merit — to them you should speak thus! // Lal_18.9 //

children.text: naivāhaṃ maraṇaṃ manye maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam /
children.translated_text: I do not even think of death, for life ends in death;

children.text: anivartī bhaviṣyāmi brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ // Lal_18.10 //
children.translated_text: I shall be irreversible, devoted to the holy life! // Lal_18.10 //

children.text: srotāṃsyapi nadīnāṃ hi vāyureṣa viśoṣayet /
children.translated_text: This wind could dry up even the streams of rivers;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ śoṣayetkāyaṃ śoṇitaṃ prahitātmanām // Lal_18.11 //
children.translated_text: how much more could it dry up the blood of one whose self is devoted [to striving]! // Lal_18.11 //

children.text: śoṇite tu viśuṣke vai tato māṃsaṃ viśuṣyati /
children.translated_text: When the blood has dried up, then the flesh dries up;

children.text: māṃseṣu kṣīyamāṇeṣu bhūyaścittaṃ prasīdati /
children.translated_text: when the flesh wastes away, the mind becomes all the more clear,

children.text: bhūyaśchandaśca vīryaṃ ca samādhiścāvatiṣṭhate // Lal_18.12 //
children.translated_text: and aspiration, vigor, and concentration become all the more established! // Lal_18.12 //

children.text: tasyaiva me viharataḥ prāptasyottamacetanām /
children.translated_text: While I thus dwell, having attained the supreme state of mind,

children.text: cittaṃ nāvekṣate kāyaṃ paśya sattvasya śuddhatām // Lal_18.13 //
children.translated_text: the mind does not look to the body — behold the purity of [this] being! // Lal_18.13 //

children.text: asti chandaṃ tathā vīryaṃ prajñāpi mama vidyate /
children.translated_text: I have aspiration, likewise vigor, and wisdom too is present in me;

children.text: taṃ na paśyāmyahaṃ loke vīryādyo māṃ vicālayet // Lal_18.14 //
children.translated_text: I do not see anyone in this world who could shake me from [my] vigor! // Lal_18.14 //

children.text: varaṃ mṛtyuḥ prāṇaharo dhiggrāmyaṃ nopajīvitam /
children.translated_text: Better is death that takes life away — shame on a base, ignoble livelihood!

children.text: saṃgrāme maraṇaṃ śreyo yacca jīvetparājitaḥ // Lal_18.15 //
children.translated_text: Death in battle is better than living defeated! // Lal_18.15 //

children.text: nāśūro jayate senāṃ jitvā caināṃ na manyate /
children.translated_text: A coward does not conquer an army, and having conquered it, does not esteem [the victory];

children.text: śūrastu jayate senāṃ laghu māra jayāmi te // Lal_18.16 //
children.translated_text: but a hero conquers an army — quickly, O <s>Māra</s>, I shall conquer you! // Lal_18.16 //

children.text: kāmāste prathamā senā dvitīyā aratistathā /
children.translated_text: Sensual pleasures are your first army; discontent is your second;

children.text: tṛtīyā kṣutpipāsā te tṛṣṇā senā caturthikā // Lal_18.17 //
children.translated_text: hunger and thirst are your third; craving is your fourth army. // Lal_18.17 //

children.text: pañcamī styānamiddhaṃ te bhayaṃ ṣaṣṭī nirucyate /
children.translated_text: Sloth and torpor are your fifth; fear is declared as your sixth;

children.text: saptamī vicikitsā te krodhamrakṣau tathāṣṭamī // Lal_18.18 //
children.translated_text: doubt is your seventh; anger and hypocrisy your eighth. // Lal_18.18 //

children.text: lobhaślokau ca saṃskārau mithyālabdhaṃ ca yadyaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Greed and [desire for] praise, false accomplishments, and whatever fame is wrongly obtained,

children.text: ātmānaṃ yaśca utkarṣedyaśca vai dhvaṃsayetparāṃ // Lal_18.19 //
children.translated_text: and whoever exalts himself and whoever disparages others — // Lal_18.19 //

children.text: eṣā hi namuceḥ senā kṛṣṇabandhoḥ pratāpinaḥ /
children.translated_text: this indeed is the army of <s>Namuci</s>, the kinsman of darkness, the tormenter;

children.text: atrāvagāḍhā dṛśyante ete śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ // Lal_18.20 //
children.translated_text: plunged into it, these <s>Śramaṇas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are seen [to be stuck]. // Lal_18.20 //

children.text: yā te senā dharṣayati lokamenaṃ sadevakam /
children.translated_text: That army of yours which overwhelms this world with its gods —

children.text: bhetsyāmi prajñayā tāṃ te āmapātramivāmbunā // Lal_18.21 //
children.translated_text: I shall shatter it with wisdom, as [one shatters] an unfired pot with water! // Lal_18.21 //

children.text: smṛtiṃ sūpasthitāṃ kṛtvā prajñāṃ caiva subhāvitām /
children.translated_text: Having well-established mindfulness, and having well-cultivated wisdom,

children.text: saṃprajānaṃ cariṣyāmi kiṃ kariṣyasi durmate // Lal_18.22 //
children.translated_text: I shall live with full awareness — what will you do, O evil-minded one?' // Lal_18.22 //

body.text: evamukte māraḥ pāpīyān duḥkhī durmanā anāttamanā vipratisārī tatraivāntaradhāt //
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, pained, disheartened, dejected, and filled with regret, vanished right there. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - ye kecicchramaṇā brāhmaṇā vā atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasvātmopakramikāṃ śarīropatāpikāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti etāvatparamaṃ te duḥkhamanubhavanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Whatever <s>Śramaṇas</s> or <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the past, future, or present experience painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and unpleasant feelings that are self-inflicted and bodily-tormenting — this is the utmost suffering they endure.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - anayāpi khalu mayā caryayā anayāpi pratipadā na kaściduttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ / nāyaṃ mārgo bodheḥ / nāyaṃ mārga āyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇasaṃbhavānāmastaṃgamāya / syāttadanyo mārgo bodherāyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasamudayānāmastaṃgamāyeti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'Even by this practice, even by this path, no distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s> has been directly realized by me. This is not the path to awakening. This is not the path to the future cessation of the arising of birth, old age, and death. Perhaps there is another path to awakening, to the future cessation of the arising of birth, old age, death, and suffering.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhavat - yadahaṃ piturudyāne jambucchāyāyāṃ niṣaṇṇo viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya vyāhārṣaṃ yāvaccaturthadhyānamupasaṃpadya vyāhārṣam, syātsa mārgo bodherjātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasamudāyānāmasaṃbhavāyāstaṃgamāyeti / tadanusāri ca me vijñānamabhūt / sa mārgo bodheriti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'When I was seated in the shade of the <s>Jambu</s> tree in my father's garden, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered upon and dwelt in the first <s>dhyāna</s> — with thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion — up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. Perhaps that is the path to awakening, to the non-arising and cessation of birth, old age, death, and the origin of suffering.' And knowledge arose in me, following upon [that insight]: 'That is the path to awakening.' //

body.text: tasya mamaitadabhūt - nāsau mārgaḥ śakyaḥ evaṃ daurbalyaprāptenābhisaṃboddhum / sacetpunarahamabhijñājñānabalenaiva lūhaṃ durbalakāya eva bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkrameyam, na me paścimā janatā anukampitā syāt / na caiṣa mārgo bodheḥ / yannvahamaudārikamāhāramāhṛtya kāyabalasthāmaṃ saṃjanayya paścādbodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkrameyam //
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in me: 'That path cannot be realized by one who has reached such a state of debility. What if I were to approach the seat of awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>) in this emaciated, weak body, relying on the power of higher knowledge alone? Then my future generations would not be looked upon with compassion. Nor is this the path to awakening. Let me rather take substantial food, generate bodily strength and firmness, and afterward approach the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>.' //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo ye te lūhādhimuktā devaputrāste mama cetasaścetasaiva parivitarkamājñāya yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya māmevamāhuḥ - mā sma tvaṃ satpuruṣa audārikamāhāramāhareḥ / vayaṃ te romakūpairojaḥ prakṣepsyāma iti //
body.translated_text: There, O monks, those <s>Devaputras</s> who were inclined to austerity, knowing the thought and deliberation of my mind, approached me and said: 'Do not, good sir, take substantial food! We shall infuse nourishment through your pores.' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - ahaṃ khalvanaśana ityātmānaṃ pratijāne, sāmantāśca me gocaragrāmavāsino janā evaṃ saṃjānante sma yathānaśanaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ / itīva me khalu lūhādhimuktā devaputrā romakūpairojaḥ prakṣipanti / sa mama paramo mṛṣāvādaḥ syāt / tato bodhisattvo mṛṣāvādaparihārārthaṃ tān devaputrān pratikṣipyaudārikamāhāramāhartu cittaṃ nāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in me: 'I have proclaimed myself as one who fasts, and the people of the surrounding villages in my begging-territory know me thus: "The <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s> is one who fasts." Yet these <s>Devaputras</s> inclined to austerity would infuse nourishment through my pores — that would be a supreme falsehood on my part.' Therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of avoiding falsehood, rejected those <s>Devaputras</s> and inclined his mind to taking substantial food. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ṣaḍvarṣavratatapaḥsamuttīrṇo bodhisattvo 'smādāsanādutthāyaudārikamāhāramāhariṣyāmīti vācaṃ niścārayati sma / tadyathā phāṇīkṛtaṃ mudgayūṣaṃ hareṇukayūṣaṃ mathyodanakulmāṣamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having completed the six years of vows and austerities, rising from his seat, uttered the declaration: 'I shall take substantial food!' — namely, [foods such as] sugar-cane juice, mung-bean broth, <s>hareṇukā</s>-bean broth, churned rice, and pulse-porridge. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ pañcānāṃ bhadravargīyānāmetadabhūt - tayāpi tāvaccaryayā tayāpi tāvatpratipadā śramaṇena gautamena na śakitaṃ kiṃciduttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum, kiṃ punaretarhi audārikamāhāramāharan sukhallikānuyogamanuyukto viharan / avyakto bālo 'yamiti ca manyamānā bodhisattvasyāntikātprakrāman / te vārāṇasīṃ gatvā ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve vyāhārṣuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in the five of the <s>Bhadravargīya</s> group: 'Even by that practice, even by that path, the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s> was unable to directly realize any distinction of noble knowledge and vision beyond human <s>dharmas</s>. How much less now, when he takes substantial food and lives devoted to the practice of comfort!' And regarding him as undeveloped and foolish, they departed from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s presence. Having gone to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, they dwelt at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. //

body.text: tatra bodhisattvamādita eva duṣkaracaryāṃ carantaṃ daśa grāmikaduhitaraḥ kumārya upagacchan darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya ca / tairapi pañcakairbhadravargīyairupasthito 'bhūt / ekakolatilataṇḍulapradānena
body.translated_text: There, O monks, from the very beginning when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was practicing the difficult austerities, ten daughters of the village-chief — maidens — would come to see him, to pay homage, and to attend upon him. He was also attended by those five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, and was provided with one grain of sesame, one grain of rice each. //

body.text: ca pratipādito 'bhūt / balā ca nāma dārikā balaguptā ca supriyā ca vijayasenā ca atimuktakamalā ca sundarī ca kumbhakārī ca uluvillikā ca jaṭilikā ca sujātā ca nāma grāmikaduhitāḥ / ābhiḥ kumārikābhirbodhisattvāya sarvāstā yūṣavidhāḥ kṛtvopanāmitā abhūvan / tāścābhyavahṛtya bodhisattvaḥ krameṇa gocaragrāme piṇḍāya caran varṇarūpabalavānabhūt / tadagreṇa bodhisattvaḥ sundaraḥ śramaṇo mahāśramaṇa ityācakṣate //
body.translated_text: And a maiden named <s>Balā</s>, and <s>Balaguptā</s>, <s>Supriyā</s>, <s>Vijayasenā</s>, <s>Atimuktakamalā</s>, <s>Sundarī</s>, <s>Kumbhakārī</s>, <s>Uluvillikā</s>, <s>Jaṭilikā</s>, and <s>Sujātā</s> — these were the daughters of the village-chief. By these maidens, all those varieties of broth were prepared and offered to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And having eaten them, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gradually, while going about for alms in the begging-village, regained his color, form, and strength. From that time onward, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was called 'the handsome <s>Śramaṇa</s>, the great <s>Śramaṇa</s>.' //

body.text: tatra ca bhikṣavaḥ sujātā grāmikaduhitā bodhisattvasya duṣkaracaryāṃ carataḥ ādita eva bodhisattvasya vratatapaḥsamuttāraṇārthaṃ śarīrasyāpyāyanahetośca pratidivasamaṣṭaśataṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhojayati sma / evaṃ ca praṇidadhāti sma - mama bhojanaṃ bhuktvā bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeteti //
body.translated_text: There, O monks, <s>Sujātā</s>, a daughter of the village-chief, from the very beginning when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was practicing difficult austerities, for the purpose of assisting the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s emergence from the vows and austerities and for the nourishment of his body, fed eight hundred <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> daily. And she made this vow: 'May the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having eaten my food, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening!' //

body.text: tasya me bhikṣavaḥ ṣaḍvarṣavyativṛttasya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi parijīrṇānyabhūvan / tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - sacedahaṃ kaupīnapracchādanaṃ labheyam, śobhanaṃ syāt //
body.translated_text: After six years, O monks, my saffron robes had become worn out. Then this thought occurred to me: 'If I could obtain a covering for my loincloth, that would be good.' //

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena sujātāyā grāmikaduhiturdāsī rādhā nāma kālagatābhūt / sā śāṇakaiḥ pariveṣṭya śmaśānamapakṛṣya parityaktābhut / tadahamevādrākṣīt pāṃśukūlam / tato 'haṃ tatpāṃśukūlaṃ vāmena pādenākramya dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ prasāryāvanato 'bhūttadrahītum /
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, a slave-woman named <s>Rādhā</s>, belonging to <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter, had died. She had been wrapped in hemp cloth, dragged to the cremation ground, and abandoned. I myself saw this rag-cloth (<s>pāṃśukūla</s>). Then I, pressing on the left edge of that rag-cloth with my left foot, extended my right hand and bent down to take it.

body.text: atha bhaumā devā antarīkṣāṇāṃ devānāṃ ghoṣamanuśrāvayanti sma - āścaryaṃ mārṣā adbhutamidaṃ mārṣāḥ / yatra hi nāmaivaṃ mahārājakulaprasūtasya cakravartirājyaparityāginaḥ pāṃśukūle cittaṃ natamiti / antarīkṣā devā bhaumānāṃ devānāṃ śabdaṃ śratvā cāturmahārājikānāṃ devānāṃ ghoṣamudīrayanti sma / cāturmahārājikā devāstrāyatriṃśataḥ / trāyatriṃśā yāmānām / yāmāstuṣitānām / tuṣitā nirmāṇaratīnām / nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartinām / paranirmitavaśavartino yāvad brahmakāyikānām / iti hi bhikṣavastatkṣaṇaṃ tallavaṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhuvanādekaghoṣa ekasaṃnirnādo 'bhyudgato 'bhūt āścaryamidaṃ mārṣā adbhutamidam / yatra hi nāmaivaṃ mahārājakulaprasūtasya cakravartirājyaparityāginaḥ pāṃśukūle cittaṃ natamiti //
body.translated_text: Then the earth-dwelling gods proclaimed to the gods of the sky: 'A marvel, O noble ones! A wonder, O noble ones! That one born of such a great royal family, who has renounced a <s>Cakravartin</s>'s kingdom — his mind has turned to a rag-cloth!' The sky-dwelling gods, hearing the sound of the earth-dwelling gods, proclaimed to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods. The <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>. The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> to the <s>Yāma</s>. The <s>Yāma</s> to the <s>Tuṣita</s>. The <s>Tuṣita</s> to the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>. The <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> to the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>. The <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> up to the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [gods]. Thus, O monks, at that instant, that moment, that second, from the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven down, a single cry, a single resounding proclamation arose: 'A marvel, O noble ones! A wonder! That one born of such a great royal family, who has renounced a <s>Cakravartin</s>'s kingdom — his mind has turned to a rag-cloth!' //
