body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punarapyetadabhavat - labdhaṃ mayā pāṃśukūlam / sacedudakaṃ labheyam, śobhanaṃ syāditi / tatastatraiva devatā pāṇinā mahīṃ parāhanti sma / tatra puṣkariṇī prādurabhūt / adyāpi sā pāṇihateti puṣkariṇī saṃjñāyate //
body.translated_text: Then again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'I have obtained the rag-cloth. If I could obtain water, that would be good.' Then the deity of that very place struck the earth with her hand. There a pool appeared. Even today that pool is known as the 'Hand-Struck' pool. //

body.text: punarapi bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - labdhaṃ mayā pānīyam / sacecchilāṃ labheyam, yatredaṃ pāṃśukūlaṃ prakṣālayeyam, śobhanaṃ syāt / atha tatraiva śakreṇa śilā tatkṣaṇamevopanikṣiptābhūt / tato bodhisattvastatpāṃśukūlaṃ prakṣālayati sma //
body.translated_text: Again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'I have obtained water. If I could obtain a stone upon which to wash this rag-cloth, that would be good.' Then <s>Śakra</s> immediately deposited a stone at that very spot. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> washed that rag-cloth. //

body.text: atha śakro devarājo bodhisattvamevamāha - dadasvedaṃ satpuruṣa mahyam / ahaṃ prakṣālayiṣyāmīti / tato bodhisattvaḥ svayaṃkāritāṃ pravrajyāyāḥ saṃdarśayituṃ tatpāṃśukūlaṃ śakrasyādatvā svayameva prakṣālayati sma / sa śrāntaḥ klāntakāyo 'vatīrya puṣkariṇīmuttariṣyāmīti / māreṇa ca pāpīyasā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the king of the gods, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Give it to me, O noble one. I will wash it.' But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in order to demonstrate the self-reliance of the renunciant life, did not give the rag-cloth to <s>Śakra</s> and washed it himself. Wearied, with an exhausted body, he descended into the pool [thinking:] 'I shall climb out.' But <s>Māra</s>, the evil one

body.text: īrṣyādharmaparītena puṣkariṇyā atyucchritāni taṭāni nirmitānyabhūvan / tasyāśca puṣkariṇyāstīre mahān kukubhapādapaḥ / tatra devatāṃ bodhisattvo lokānuvṛttyā devatānugrahārthaṃ cābravīt - āhara devate vṛkṣaśākhāmiti / tayā vṛkṣaśākhāvanāmitābhūt / tāṃ bodhisattvo 'balambyottarati sma / uttīrya ca tasya kakubhapādapasyādhastāttatpāṃśukūlaṃ saṃghāṭīkṛtya āsīvyati sma / adyāpi tat pāṃśukūlaṃ sīvanamityevaṃ saṃjñāyate sma //
body.translated_text: , overcome by the vice of jealousy, had made the banks of the pool exceedingly high. And on the bank of that pool stood a great <s>Kakubha</s> tree. There the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, out of conformity with the world and for the sake of honoring the deity, said: 'Bring down a branch of the tree, O deity.' The branch of the tree was bent down by her. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, grasping it, climbed out. Having climbed out, beneath that <s>Kakubha</s> tree, he fashioned that rag-cloth into a robe and stitched it. Even today that rag-cloth is known as the 'Stitching.' //

body.text: atha vimalaprabho nāma śuddhāvāsakāyiko devaputraḥ, sa divyāni cīvarāṇi kāṣāyaraṅgaraktāni kalpikāni śramaṇasārūpyāṇi bodhisattvāyopanāmayati sma / bodhisattvaśca tāni gṛhītvā pūrvāhṇe nivāsya saṃghāṭīprāvṛtya gocaragrāmābhimukho 'bhut //
body.translated_text: Then a <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Vimalaprabha</s> presented to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> divine robes, dyed in saffron color, proper and suitable for a renunciant. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having accepted and put them on in the forenoon, covered with the outer robe, set out toward the village for alms. //

body.text: tatra devatābhirurubilvāsenāpatigrāmake nandikagrāmikaduhituḥ sujātāyā ārocitamabhūdardharātrasamaye - yadarthaṃ tvaṃ mahāyajñaṃ yajase tasmādvratāduttīrṇaḥ saḥ / subhagamaudārikamāhāramāhariṣyati / tvayā ca pūrve praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam - mama bhojanaṃ bhuktvā bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeta iti / yatte karaṇīyaṃ tatkuruṣveti //
body.translated_text: There, the deities informed <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter of <s>Urubilvā</s>, at midnight: 'The one for whose sake you perform the great sacrifice — he has completed his vow. He will accept a fine, substantial meal. And your former vow was made: "May the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having eaten my food, fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening." Do what needs to be done.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sujātā nandikagrāmaduhitā teṣāṃ devatānāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śīghraṃ gosahasrasya kṣīrātsaptakṛtsāroddhṛtādagryamojomaṇḍaṃ gṛhṇīte sma / gṛhītvā ca sā tatkṣīra(mabhinavama)bhinavaistaṇḍulairabhinavāyāṃ sthālyāmabhinavāṃ cullīmupalipya tadbhojanaṃ sādhayati sma / tasmiṃśca sādhyamāne imāni pūrvanimittāni saṃdṛśyante sma - tasmin khalvapi kṣīre śrīvatsasvastikanandyāvartapadmavardhamānādīni maṅgalyāni saṃdṛśyante sma / tatastasyā etadabhūt - yādṛśānīmāni pūrvanimittāni saṃdṛśyante, niḥsaṃśayamidaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuktvā bodhisattvo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prāpsyati / sāmudrajñānavidhijñaśca naimittikastaṃ pradeśaṃ prāpto 'bhūt / so 'pi tathaivāmṛtādhigamanameva vyākṛtavān / tataḥ sujātā taṃ pāyasaṃ pakvaṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya puṣpairavakīrya gandhodakenābhyukṣya āsanaṃ prajñāpya satkṛtyottarāṃ nāma ceṭīmāmantrayate sma - gacchottare brāhmaṇamānaya / ahamidaṃ madhupāyasamavalokayāmi / sādhvārya iti pratiśrutya uttarā pūrvāṃ diśamagamat / sā tatra bodhisattvaṃ paśyati sma / tathaiva dakṣiṇām / bodhisattvameva paśyati sma / evaṃ paścimāmuttarāmeva diśaṃ gacchati sma, tatra tatra bodhisattvamevādrākṣīt / tena khalu punaḥ samayena śuddhāvāsakāyikairdevaputraiḥ sarve 'nyatīrthikā nigṛhītā abhūvan / na kaścit saṃdṛśyate sma / tataḥ sā āgatvā svāminīmevamāha - na khalvārye anyaḥ kaścid dṛśyate śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā, anyatra yato yata eva gacchāmi, tatra tatra śramaṇameva sundaraṃ paśyāmi / sujātā āha - gacchottare sa eva brāhmaṇaḥ, sa eva śramaṇaḥ / tasyaivārthe 'yamārambhaḥ / tamevānayeti / sādhvārye ityuttarā gatvā bodhisattvasya caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya sujātāyā
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter of <s>Nandika</s>, hearing the words of those deities, quickly took from the milk of a thousand cows — from the cream extracted seven times [by successive reduction] — the finest essence of vitality. Having taken it, she cooked that food with fresh rice grains, in a fresh pot, on a fresh oven freshly plastered. And while it was being cooked, these portents were seen: in that milk appeared the auspicious marks — <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Svastika</s>, <s>Nandyāvarta</s>, lotus, <s>Vardhamāna</s>, and others. Then she thought: 'Since such portents as these are seen, without doubt, having eaten this food, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening!' And a soothsayer skilled in the science of ocean-knowledge came to that place. He too prophesied the same — the attainment of the deathless. Then <s>Sujātā</s>, having cooked that <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice), plastered a clean surface, strewed it with flowers, sprinkled it with scented water, prepared a seat, and with due reverence addressed a maidservant named <s>Uttarā</s>: 'Go, <s>Uttarā</s>, bring a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. I will keep watch over this honey-<s>pāyasa</s>.' 'Yes, my lady,' assented <s>Uttarā</s> and went to the east. There she saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Likewise to the south — she saw only the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Similarly going west and north, everywhere she saw only the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. At that time, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika Devaputras</s> had caused all the other <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox ascetics) to disappear. Not a single one was visible. Then, having returned, she said to her mistress: 'Indeed, O lady, no other <s>Śramaṇa</s> or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is visible anywhere, except that wherever I go, I see only that same beautiful renunciant.' <s>Sujātā</s> said: 'Go, <s>Uttarā</s>! He is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he is the <s>Śramaṇa</s>. This preparation is for his sake alone. Bring him!' 'Yes, my lady!' <s>Uttarā</s> went, prostrated at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, and invited him in <s>Sujātā</s>'s

body.text: nāmnopanimantrayate sma / tato bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ sujātāyā grāmikaduhiturniveśanaṃ gatvā prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat / atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sujātā grāmikaduhitā suvarṇamayīṃ pātrīṃ madhupāyasapūrṇāṃ bodhisattvasyopanāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: name. Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going to the dwelling of <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter, sat down on the prepared seat. Then, O monks, <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter, presented to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a golden bowl filled with honey-<s>pāyasa</s>. //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - yādṛśamidaṃ sujātayā bhojanamupanāmitam, niḥsaṃśayamahamadyainaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuktvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'Since <s>Sujātā</s> has presented such food as this, without doubt, having eaten this food today, I shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastadbhojanaṃ pratigṛhya sujātāṃ grāmikaduhitarametadavocat - iyaṃ bhagini suvarṇapātrī / kiṃ kriyatām? sā āha - tavaiva bhavatviti / bodhisattva āha - na mamedṛśena bhājanena prayojanam / sujātā āha - yatheṣṭaṃ kriyatām / nāhaṃ vinā bhājanena kasyacidbhojanaṃ prayacchāmi //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having accepted that food, said to <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter: 'This, sister, is a golden bowl. What shall be done with it?' She said: 'Let it be yours.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I have no use for such a vessel.' <s>Sujātā</s> said: 'Do as you wish with it. I never give food to anyone without its vessel.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastaṃ piṇḍapātramādāyorubilvāyā niṣkramya nāganadīṃ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nadīṃ nairañjanāmupasaṃkramya taṃ piṇḍapātraṃ cīvarāṇi caikānte nikṣipya nadīṃ nairañjanāmavatarati sma gātrāṇi śītalīkartum //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking that almsfood, departed from <s>Urubilvā</s> and, in the forenoon, approached the <s>Nāga</s> river, the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. He set down the almsfood and robes to one side and descended into the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> to cool his limbs. //

body.text: bodhisattvasya khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ snāyato 'nekāni devaputraśatasahasrāṇi divyāgurucandanacūrṇavilepanairnadīmāloḍayanti sma / divyāni ca nānāvarṇāni kusumāni jale kṣipanti sma yaduta bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe //
body.translated_text: And while the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was bathing, O monks, many hundreds of thousands of <s>Devaputras</s> stirred the river with divine aloe and sandalwood powder and unguents. And they cast various divine flowers of many colors into the water — for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena nairañjanā nadī divyairgandhaiḥ puṣpaiśca samākulā vahati sma / yena ca gandhodakena bodhisattvaḥ snāto 'bhūt, taṃ devaputrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhyutkṣipya svakasvakāni bhavanāni nayanti sma caityārthaṃ pūjārthaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Nairañjanā</s> river flowed full of divine fragrances and flowers. And the scented water in which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had bathed — <s>koṭī</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Devaputras</s> scooped it up and carried it to their respective abodes as a relic and for worship. //

body.text: yāni ca bodhisattvasya keśaśmaśrūṇyabhūvan, tāni sarvāṇi sujātā grāmikaduhitā maṅgalyānīti kṛtvā caityārthaṃ pūjārthaṃ ca parigṛhṇīte sma //
body.translated_text: And whatever hair from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s head and beard there was — all of that <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter, gathered up, considering it auspicious, as a relic and for worship. //

body.text: nadyuttīrṇaśca bodhisattvaḥ pulinaṃ nirīkṣate sma upaveṣṭukāmaḥ / atha yā nairañjanāyāṃ nadyāṃ nāgakanyā sā dharaṇitalādabhyudgabhya maṇimayaṃ (manoramaṃ) bhadrāsanaṃ bodhisattvāyopanāmayati sma / tatra bodhisattvo niṣadya yāvadarthaṃ taṃ madhupāyasaṃ paribhuṅkte sma sujātāyā grāmikaduhituranukampāmupādāya / paribhujya ca tāṃ suvarṇapātrīmanapekṣo vāriṇi prākṣipati sma / kṣiptamātrāṃ ca tāṃ sāgaro nāgarājaścittikārabahumānajāto gṛhītvā svabhavanābhimukhaḥ prasthito 'bhut pūjārheti kṛtvā / atha daśaśatanayanaḥ puraṃdaro garuḍarūpamabhinirmāya vajratuṇḍo bhūtvā sāgarasya nāgarājasyāntikāttāṃ suvarṇapātrīṃ hartumārabdhaḥ / yadā na śaknoti sma, tadā svarūpeṇādareṇa yācitvā trāyatriṃśadbhavanaṃ nītavān pūjārthaṃ caityārthaṃ ca / nītvā pātrīyātrāṃ nāma parvaṇi pravartitavān / adyāpi ca trāyatriṃśeṣu deveṣu pratisaṃvatsaraṃ pātrīmaho vartate / tacca bhadrāsanaṃ tayaiva nāgakanyayā parigṛhītaṃ caityārthaṃ pūjārthaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having crossed the river, surveyed the bank, wishing to sit down. Then a <s>Nāga</s> maiden who dwelt in the <s>Nairañjanā</s> river rose up from the surface of the earth and presented to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a beautiful gem-studded seat. There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat and ate the honey-<s>pāyasa</s> to his satisfaction — out of compassion for <s>Sujātā</s>, the village-chief's daughter. Having eaten, he cast the golden bowl into the water without regard. No sooner was it cast than <s>Sāgara</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king, with devotion and great respect, took it and set out toward his own abode, considering it worthy of worship. Then <s>Indra</s> of the thousand eyes, having manifested the form of a <s>Garuḍa</s> and become <s>Vajra</s>-beaked, began to seize that golden bowl from the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Sāgara</s>. When he could not [take it by force], he reverently entreated [him] in his own form and brought it to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven as a relic and for worship. Having brought it, he instituted a festival called 'The Bowl Festival.' And even today, among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, every year the Bowl Festival (<s>Pātrīmaha</s>) takes place. And that seat was taken by the very same <s>Nāga</s> maiden as a relic and for worship. //

body.text: samantaparibhuktaśca bhikṣavo bodhisattvenaudārika āhāraḥ / atha tatkṣaṇameva bodhisattvasya puṇyabalena prajñābalena pūrvikā kāye śubhavarṇapuṣkaratā prādurabhūt / dvātriṃśacca mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni aśītiścānuvyañjanāni vyāmaprabhatā ca / tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: And, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fully consumed the substantial food. Then at that very instant, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power of merit and power of wisdom, his former beautiful complexion and lotus-like [radiance] reappeared in his body. And the thirty-two marks of a great person, and the eighty minor characteristics, and the fathom-wide aura [appeared]. Concerning this, it was said:

body.text: ṣaḍvarṣa vrata uttaritva bhagavān evaṃ matiṃ cintayan so 'haṃ dhyānaabhijñajñānabalavānevaṃ kṛśāṅgo 'pi san / gaccheyaṃ drumarājamūlaviṭapaṃ sarvajñatāṃ buddhituṃ no me syādanukampitā hi janatā evaṃ bhavet paścimā // Lal_18.23 //
body.translated_text: Having completed his six-year vow, the <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected thus: 'I, endowed with the strength of <s>dhyāna</s>, superknowledges, and knowledge, even being thus emaciated — shall I go to the base of the king of trees to awaken to omniscience? But then compassion for people would not arise, and this would be the last [opportunity].' // Lal_18.23 //

body.text: yattvaudārika bhuktva bhojanavaraṃ kāye balaṃ kṛtvanā gaccheyaṃ drumarājamūlaviṭapaṃ sarvajñatāṃ budhyitum / mā haivetvarapuṇya devamanujā lūhena jñānekṣiṇo no śaktā siya budhyanāya amṛtaṃ kāyena te durbalāḥ // Lal_18.24 //
body.translated_text: 'Having eaten substantial, excellent food and generated strength in the body, I shall go to the base of the king of trees to awaken to omniscience. Let not the gods and humans of hastily-earned merit, looking with [worldly] knowledge at the emaciated one, be unable to awaken to the deathless — their bodies being weak!' // Lal_18.24 //

children.text: sā ca grāmikadhīta pūrvacaritā nāmnā sujātā iti
children.translated_text: And that village-chief's daughter, known by former conduct, named <s>Sujātā</s> —

children.text: yajñā nityu yajāti evamanasā siddhe vrataṃ nāyake /
children.translated_text: she constantly offered worship with this intention: 'May the vow of the leader be accomplished!'

children.text: sā devāna niśāmya codana tadā gṛhyā madhūpāyasaṃ
children.translated_text: She, hearing the exhortation of the gods, then taking the honey-<s>pāyasa</s>,

children.text: upagamyā naditīri hṛṣṭamanasā nairañjanāyāḥ sthitā // Lal_18.25 //
children.translated_text: approached the bank of the <s>Nairañjanā</s> river and stood there, with joyful mind. // Lal_18.25 //

children.text: so cākalpasahasracīrṇacarito śāntapraśāntendriyo
children.translated_text: He, whose conduct had been practiced for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, with senses calm and tranquil,

children.text: devairnāgagaṇairṛṣī parivṛto āgatya nairañjanām /
children.translated_text: surrounded by gods, hosts of <s>Nāgas</s>, and sages, having come to the <s>Nairañjanā</s> —

children.text: tīrṇastāraku pārasattva matimāṃ snāne matiṃ cintayan
children.translated_text: The wise one, having crossed [<s>saṃsāra</s>], a deliverer of beings, contemplating the thought of bathing,

children.text: oruhyā nadi snāpi śuddhavimalo lokānukampī muniḥ // Lal_18.26 //
children.translated_text: descended into the river and bathed — the pure, stainless Sage, compassionate toward the world! // Lal_18.26 //

children.text: devā koṭisahasra hṛṣṭamanasā gandhāmbu cūrṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of gods, with joyful minds, [bringing] scented waters and powders,

children.text: oruhyā nadi loḍayanti salilaṃ snānārtha sattvottame /
children.translated_text: descended into the river and churned the water, for the bathing of the Supreme Being.

children.text: snānā snātvana bodhisattva vimalastīre sthitaḥ sūrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having bathed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, stainless, stood on the bank, heroic;

children.text: harṣurdevasahasra snānasalilaṃ pūjārtha sattvottame // Lal_18.27 //
children.translated_text: thousands of gods joyfully [took] the bathing water for the worship of the Supreme Being. // Lal_18.27 //

children.text: kāṣāyāni ca vastra nirmala śubhā tā devaputro dade
children.translated_text: A <s>devaputra</s> gave him saffron robes, clean and auspicious;

children.text: kalpīyāni ca saṃnivāsya bhagavāṃstīre hi nadyāḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: having donned the ritual garments, the Blessed One stood on the bank of the river.

children.text: nāgākanya udagra hṛṣṭamanasā bhadrāsanaṃ sā nyaṣīt
children.translated_text: A <s>Nāga</s> maiden, elated and joyful in mind, placed a fine seat

children.text: yatrāsau niṣasāda śāntamanaso lokasya cakṣuṣkaraḥ // Lal_18.28 //
children.translated_text: where he of tranquil mind, the maker of sight for the world, sat down. // Lal_18.28 //

children.text: dattvā bhojanu sā sujāta matimāṃ svarṇāmaye bhājane
children.translated_text: The wise <s>Sujātā</s>, having given food in a golden vessel,

children.text: vanditvā caraṇāni sā pramuditā paribhuṅkṣva me sārathe /
children.translated_text: bowed at his feet, delighted: 'Partake of my [offering], O Charioteer [of beings]!'

children.text: bhuktvā bhojanu yāvadartha matimān pātrīṃ jale prākṣipat
children.translated_text: Having eaten the food sufficient for his purpose, the wise one cast the bowl into the water;

children.text: tāṃ jagrāha puraṃdaraḥ suraguruḥ pūjāṃ kariṣyāmyaham // Lal_18.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puraṃdara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the teacher of the gods, seized it: 'I shall perform worship [with this]!' // Lal_18.29 //

children.text: yada bhuktaṃ ca jinena bhojanavaraṃ odārikaṃ tatkṣaṇe
children.translated_text: When the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) had eaten that excellent, substantial food, at that very moment

children.text: tasyā kāyabalaṃ ca tejaśiriyā pūrvaṃ yathā saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: his bodily strength, splendor, and glory were restored as before.

children.text: dharmā kṛtva kathā sujāta maruṇāṃ kṛtvā ca arthaṃ bahuṃ
children.translated_text: Having given a <s>dharma</s>-discourse to the wise <s>Sujātā</s> and the gods, accomplishing great benefit,

children.text: siṃho haṃsagatirgajendragamano bodhidrumaṃ saṃsthitaḥ // Lal_18.30 //
children.translated_text: with the gait of a lion, the walk of a goose, the stride of the lord of elephants, he proceeded to the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree. // Lal_18.30 //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare nairañjanāparivarto nāmāṣṭādaśamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the eighteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on [the River] <s>Nairañjanā</s>.' //

body.text: START Parivarta 19
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 19.

body.text: bodhimaṇḍagamanaparivarta ekonaviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Nineteenth Chapter: On Going to the Seat of Awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍagamanaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo nadyāṃ nairañjanāyāṃ snātvā ca bhuktvā kāyabalasthāma saṃjanayya yena ṣoḍaśākārasaṃpannapṛthivipradeśe mahābodhidrumarājamūlaṃ tena pratasthe vijayayā tayā ca gatyā, yāsau mahāpuruṣāṇāṃ gatiranuccalitagatirindriyeṣṭigatiḥ susaṃsthitagatiḥ merurājagatirajihmagatirakuṭilagatiranupadrutagatiravilambitagatiraluḍitagatiraskhalitagatirasaṃghaṭitagatiralīnagatiracapalagatiḥ salīlagatiḥ vimalagatiḥ śubhagatiradoṣagatiramohagatiraraktagatiḥ siṃhagatiḥ haṃsarājagatirnāgarājagatirnārāyaṇagatiḥ dharaṇitalāsaṃsṛṣṭagatiḥ sahasrāracakradharaṇītalacitragatiḥ jālāṅgulitāmranakhagatiḥ dharaṇītalanirnādagatiḥ śailarājasaṃghaṭanagatiḥ utkūlanikūlasamakaracaraṇagatiḥ jālāntarābhāraśmyutsarjanasattvasaṃspṛśanasugatigamanagatiḥ vimalapadmakramanikṣipaṇagatiḥ pūrvaśubhasucaritagamanagatiḥ pūrvabuddhasiṃhābhigamanagatiḥ vajradṛḍhābhedyāśayagatiḥ (sarvopāyagatiḥ) sarvāpāyadurgatipithitagatiḥ sarvasattvasukhasaṃjananagatiḥ mokṣapathasaṃdarśanagatiḥ mārabalābalakaraṇagatiḥ kugaṇigaṇaparapravādisahadharmanigrahaṇagatiḥ / tamaḥpaṭalakleśavidhamanagatiḥ saṃsārapakṣāpakṣakaraṇagatiḥ śakrabrahmamaheśvaralokapālābhibhavagatiḥ / trisāhasramahāsāhasraikaśūragatiḥ svayaṃbhvanabhibhūtagatiḥ sarvajñajñānābhigamanagatiḥ smṛtimatigatiḥ sugatigamanagatiḥ jarāmaraṇapraśamanagatiḥ śivavirajāmalābhayanirvāṇapuragamanagatiḥ / īdṛśyā gatyā bodhisattvo bodhimaṇḍaṃ saṃprasthito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having bathed in the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> and eaten, generating bodily strength and power, proceeded toward the root of the great king of <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, on a spot of earth endowed with sixteen qualities, with that victorious gait — the gait of great beings: the unwavering gait, the sense-directed gait, the well-established gait, the gait [steady as] King <s>Meru</s>, the straight gait, the uncrooked gait. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāvacca nadyā nairañjanāyā yāvacca bodhimaṇḍādestasminnantare vātabalāhakairdevaputraiḥ saṃmṛṣṭamabhūt / varṣabalāhakairdevaputrairgandhodakena siktamabhūt puṣpaiścāvakīrṇamabhūt / yāvadeva trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau vṛkṣāste sarve yena bodhimaṇḍastenābhinatāgrā abhūvan / ye 'pi ca tadahojātā bāladārikāste 'pi bodhimaṇḍaśīrṣakāḥ svapanti sma / ye 'pi ceha trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau sumerupramukhāḥ parvatāste 'pi sarve yena bodhimaṇḍastena praṇatā abhūvan / nadīṃ ca nairañjanāmupādāya yāvadbodhimaṇḍo 'sminnantare kāmāvacarairdevaputraiḥ krośavistāraikapramāṇo mārgo 'bhivyūhito 'bhūt / tasya ca mārgasya vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ pārśvayoḥ saptaratnamayī vedikā abhinirmitā 'bhūt / saptatālānuccaistvena upariṣṭādratnajālasaṃchannā divyachatradhvajapatākāsamalaṃkṛtā iṣukṣepe saptaratnamayāstālā abhinirmitā abhūvan tasyā vedikāyā abhyudgatāḥ / sarvasmācca tālādratnasūtrā dvitīye tālamavasaktamabhūt / dvayośca tālayormadhye puṣkariṇī māpitābhūt gandhodakaparipūrṇā suvarṇavālikrāsaṃstṛtā utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannā ratnavedikāparivṛtā vaidūryamaṇiratnasopānapratyuptā
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, in the interval between the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> and the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (Seat of Awakening), the <s>devaputras</s> of the wind-clouds swept [the path]; the <s>devaputras</s> of the rain-clouds sprinkled it with scented water and strewed it with flowers. Throughout the entire trichiliocosm, all the trees bent their tops toward the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. And those that //

body.text: āḍibalākāhaṃsacakravākamayūropakūjitā / taṃ ca mārgamaśītyapsaraḥsahasrāṇi gandhodakena siñcanti sma / aśītyapsaraḥsahasrāṇi muktakusumairabhyavakiranti sma divyairgandhavadbhiḥ / sarvasya ca tālavṛkṣasya purato ratnavyomakaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt / sarvasmiṃśca ratnavyomake aśītyapsaraḥ sahasrāṇi candanāgurucūrṇakapuṭāparigṛhītāni kārānusāridhūpaghaṭikāparigṛhītāni sthitānyabhūvan / sarvasmiṃśca ratnavyomake pañcapañcāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi divyasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena sthitānyabhūvan //
body.translated_text: [The path was] resounded with <s>āḍi</s>-birds, herons, geese, <s>cakravāka</s> ducks, and peacocks. And eighty thousand <s>Apsarases</s> sprinkled that road with scented water. Eighty thousand <s>Apsarases</s> scattered loose flowers, divine and fragrant. Before every palm tree a jeweled canopy was set up. And in every jeweled canopy, eighty thousand <s>Apsarases</s> [held] sandal—

body.text:
iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvaḥ prakampyamānaiḥ kṣetrai raśmikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi niścārayaṃstūryaśatasahasraiḥ pravādyamānaiḥ, mahatā puṣpāḍhyena pravarṣatā, ambaraśatasahasrairbhrāmyamānaiḥ, dundubhiśatasahasraiḥ parāhanyamānaiḥ, garjadbhiḥ pragarjadbhiḥ hayagajavṛṣabhaiḥ, pradakṣiṇīkurvadbhiḥ śukasārikākokilakalaviṅkajīvaṃjīvakahaṃsakroñcamayuracakravākaśatasahasraiḥ, upanāmyamānaiḥ maṅgalyaśatasahasraiḥ / anenaivaṃrūpeṇa mārgavyūhena bodhisattvo bodhimaṇḍaṃ gacchati sma / yāṃ ca rātriṃ bodhisattvo bodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmo 'bhūt, tāmeva rātriṃ vaśavartī nāma trisāhasramahāsāhasrādhipatirbrahmā sahāpatirbrahmaparṣadamāmantryaivamāha - yatkhalu mārṣā jānīyāḥ / eṣa sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāsaṃnāhasaṃnaddho mahāpratijñānutsṛṣṭo dṛḍhasaṃnāhasaṃnaddho 'parikhinnamānasaḥ sarvabodhisattvacaryāsu nirjātaḥ sarvapāramitāsu pāraṃgataḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmiṣu vaśitāprāptaḥ sarvabodhisattvāśayasuviśuddhaḥ sarvasattvendriyeṣvanugataḥ sarvatathāgataguhyasthāneṣu supraviṣṭaḥ sarvamārakarmapathasamatikrāntaḥ sarvakuśalamūleṣvaparapratyayaḥ sarvatathāgatairadhiṣṭhitaḥ sarvasattveṣu pramokṣamārgadeśayitā mahāsārthavāhaḥ / sarvamāramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanakaraḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasraikaśūraḥ / sarvadharmabhaiṣajyasamudānītaḥ mahāvaidyarājaḥ / vimuktipaṭṭābaddho mahādharmarājaḥ / mahāprajñāprabhotsarjanakaraḥ mahāketurājaḥ aṣṭalokadharmānupaliptaḥ mahāpadmabhūtaḥ sarvadharmadhāraṇyasaṃpramuṣitaḥ mahāsāgarabhūtaḥ anunayapratighāpagataḥ acalo 'prakampī mahāsumerūbhūtaḥ / sunirmalaḥ supariśuddhaḥ svavadarpitavimalabuddhirmahāmaṇiratnabhūtaḥ sarvadharmavaśavartī sarvakarmaṇyacitto mahābrahmabhūto bodhisattvo bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkramati mārasainyapradharṣaṇārthamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmaḥ / daśabalavaiśāradyāṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmaparipuraṇārthaṃ mahādharmacakrapravartanārthaṃ mahāsiṃhanādanādanārthaṃ sarvasattvān dharmadānena saṃtarpaṇārthaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ dharmacakṣurviśodhanārthaṃ sarvaparapravādīnāṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahārthaṃ pūrvapratijñāpāripūrisaṃdarśanārthaṃ sarvadharmaiśvaryavaśitāprāptyartham / tatra yuṣmābhirmārṣā sarvaireva bodhisattvasya pūjopasthānakarmaṇyutsukairbhavitavyam /
atha khalu vaśavartī mahābrahmā tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the realms trembling, emitting hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of rays of light, with hundreds of thousands of instruments being played, with a great rain of flowers pouring down, with hundreds of thousands of garments being waved, with hundreds of thousands of kettledrums being struck, with horses, elephants, and bulls roaring and trumpeting, with parrots circumambulating —

body.text: yasyā tejatu puṇyataśca śiriye brāhmaḥ patho jñāyate maitrī vā karuṇā upekṣa muditā dhyānānyabhijñāstathā /
body.translated_text: He whose splendor and merit and glory reveal the path of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), <s>dhyānas</s>, and <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges) [are perfected] —

body.text: so 'yaṃ kalpasahasracīrṇacarito bodhidrumaṃ prasthitaḥ

children.text: pūjāṃ sādhu karotha tasya munino āśivrate sādhanām // Lal_19.1 //
children.translated_text: Perform worship well for that Sage, [aiding] the accomplishment of his auspicious vow! // Lal_19.1 //

body.translated_text: he, whose conduct has been practiced for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, has set out for the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree!

children.text: yaṃ gatvā śaraṇaṃ na durgatibhayaṃ prāpnoti naivākṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Going to whom as refuge, one does not attain the fear of lower rebirths, nor unfortunate circumstances,

children.text: deveṣviṣṭasukhaṃ ca prāpya vipulaṃ brahmālayaṃ gacchati /
children.translated_text: and having obtained abundant desired happiness among the gods, one goes to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s> —

children.text: ṣaḍvaṣāṇi caritva duṣkaracariṃ yātyeṣa bodhidrumaṃ
children.translated_text: he who has practiced the hard-to-practice conduct for six years now goes to the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree!

children.text: sādhū sarvi udagrahṛṣṭamanasaḥ pūjāsya kurvāmahe // Lal_19.2 //
children.translated_text: Well then! Let us all, elated and joyful in mind, perform worship for him! // Lal_19.2 //

children.text: rājāsau trisahasri īśvaravaro dharmeśvaraḥ pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the king of the trichiliocosm, the supreme lord, the lord of <s>dharma</s>, the sovereign;

children.text: śakrābrahmapure ca candrasuriye nāstyasya kaścit samaḥ /
children.translated_text: in the cities of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, in [the realms of] the moon and sun — there is none equal to him!

children.text: yasyā jāyata kṣetrakoṭinayutā saṃkampitā ṣaḍvidhā
children.translated_text: At whose birth <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> of world-realms trembled in six ways —

children.text: saiṣo 'dya vrajate mahādrumavaraṃ mārasya jetuṃ camūn // Lal_19.3 //
children.translated_text: that very one today proceeds to the great, supreme tree, to conquer the armies of <s>Māra</s>! // Lal_19.3 //

children.text: mūrdhnaṃ yasya na śakyamīkṣitumiha brahmālaye 'pi sthitaiḥ
children.translated_text: His head cannot be seen even by those stationed in the <s>Brahma</s>-world;

children.text: kāyo yasya varāgralakṣaṇadharo dvātriṃśatālaṃkṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: his body bears the supreme, excellent marks — adorned with the thirty-two [signs];

children.text: vāgyasyeha manojñavalgumadhurā brahmasvarā susvarā
children.translated_text: his speech here is lovely, charming, sweet — the <s>Brahma</s>-voice, beautifully voiced;

children.text: cittaṃ yasya praśānta doṣarahitaṃ gacchāma tatpūjane // Lal_19.4 //
children.translated_text: his mind is tranquil, free from faults — let us go to worship him! // Lal_19.4 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ vā mati brahmaśakrabhavane nityaṃ sukha kṣepituṃ
children.translated_text: Whether one's intention is to enjoy eternal happiness in the abodes of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: athavā sarvakileśabandhanalatāṃ chettuṃ hi tāṃ jālinīm /
children.translated_text: or to cut the creeping vine of all the bonds of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), that net,

children.text: aśrutvā parataḥ spṛśeyamamṛtaṃ pratyekabodhiṃ śivāṃ
children.translated_text: or to touch without hearing from another the auspicious, deathless <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening),

children.text: buddhatvaṃ yadi vepsitaṃ tribhuvane pūjetvasau nāyakam // Lal_19.5 //
children.translated_text: or if <s>Buddhahood</s> is desired in the three worlds — worship this Leader! // Lal_19.5 //

children.text: tyaktā yena sasāgarā vasumatī ratnānyanantānyatho
children.translated_text: He by whom the earth with its oceans was relinquished, and infinite treasures,

children.text: prāsādāśca gavākṣaharmyakalikā yugyāni yānāni ca /
children.translated_text: and palaces with windows, mansions, and turrets, yoked vehicles and conveyances,

children.text: bhūmyālaṃkṛta puṣpadāma rucirā udyānakūpāsarāḥ
children.translated_text: and lands adorned with beautiful flower-garlands, and parks, wells, and lakes,

children.text: hastā pādaśirottamāṅganayanā so bodhimaṇḍonmukhaḥ // Lal_19.6 //
children.translated_text: and hands, feet, head, and eyes — he now faces toward the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>! // Lal_19.6 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastrisāhasramahāsāhasriko mahābrahmā imaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ tatkṣaṇaṃ samamadhyatiṣṭhat / pāṇitalajātamapagataśarkarakaṭhallamutsadamaṇimuktivaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpyaṃ nīlamṛdukuṇḍalajātapradakṣiṇanandyāvartakācilindikasukhasaṃsparśaiśca tṛṇairimaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃchāditamadhyatiṣṭhat / sarve ca tadā mahāsamudrā dharaṇītalasaṃsthitā abhūvan / na ca jalacarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ kācidviheṭhābhūt / imaṃ caiva lokadhātumalaṃkṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca daśasu dikṣu śakrabrahmalokapālairbodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe buddhakṣetraśatasahasrāṇi samalaṃkṛtānyabhūvan / bodhisattvaiśca divyamānuṣyakātikrāntaiḥ pūjāvyūhairdaśasu dikṣvaprameyāṇi buddhakṣetrāṇi pratimaṇḍitānyabhūvan
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, the great <s>Brahmā</s> of the trichiliocosm at that instant established this trichiliocosmic world-system [in splendor] — level as the palm of a hand, free from pebbles and rubble, raised up with gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch, crystal, coral, silver, and gold, and covered this trichiliocosmic world-system with grass — blue, soft, curling rightward in auspicious spirals, pleasant to touch like <s>Kācilinḍika</s> cloth. And at that time all the great oceans stood at the level of the earth's surface, and no harm came to any water-dwelling beings. And having seen this world-system adorned, in the ten directions, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians adorned hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with worship-arrays surpassing divine and human [offerings] beautified immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions

body.text: bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe / sarvāṇi ca tāni buddhakṣetrāṇyekamiva buddhakṣetraṃ saṃdṛśyante sma, nānāvyūhālaṃkārālaṃkṛtāni ca / na ca bhūyo lokāntarikā na ca kālaparvatā na ca cakravālamahācakravālāḥ prajñāyante sma / sarvāṇi ca tāni buddhakṣetrāṇi bodhisattvasyābhayā sphuṭāni saṃdṛśyante sma / ṣoḍaśa ca bodhimaṇḍaparipālikā devaputrāḥ / tadyathā - utkhalī ca nāma devaputraḥ sūtkhalī ca nāma prajāpatiśca śūrabalaśca keyūrabalaśca supratisthitaśca mahiṃdharaśca avabhāsakaraśca vimalaśca dharmeśvaraśca dharmaketuśca siddhapātraśca apratihatanetraśca mahāvyūhaśca śīlaviśuddhanetraśca padmaprabhaśca / itīme ṣoḍaśa bodhimaṇḍapratipālakā devaputrāḥ sarve 'vaivartyakṣāntipratilabdhāste bodhisattvasya pūjārthaṃ bodhimaṇḍaṃ maṇḍayanti sma / samantādaśītiyojanāni saptabhī ratnavedikābhiḥ parivṛtaṃ saptabhistālapaṅktibhiḥ saptabhī ratnakiṅkiṇījālaiḥ saptabhī ratnasūtraiḥ parivṛtam, saptaratnapratyuptaiśca jāmbūnadasuvarṇapaṭaiḥ suvarṇasūtrairjāmbūnadasuvarṇapadmaiścāvakīrṇaṃ sāravaragandhanirdhūpitaṃ ratnajālasaṃchannam / ye ca daśasu dikṣu nānālokadhātuṣu vividhā vṛkṣāḥ santyabhijātā abhipūjitā divyamānuṣyakāste 'pi sarve tatra bodhimaṇḍe saṃdṛśyante sma / yāśca daśasu dikṣu nānāprakārā jalasthalajāḥ puṣpajātayastā api sarvāstatra bodhimaṇḍe saṃdṛśyante sma / ye 'pi ca daśasu dikṣu nānālokadhātuṣu bodhisattvā bodhimaṇḍālaṃkurvantyapramāṇapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāravyūhaiste 'pi tatra bodhimaṇḍe saṃdṛśyante sma //
body.translated_text: for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And all those <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared as if a single <s>Buddha</s>-field, adorned with various arrays of ornaments. No longer were the inter-world spaces, the dark mountains, the <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> [ranges] perceived. All those <s>Buddha</s>-fields appeared clearly, pervaded by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s fearlessness. And there were sixteen <s>devaputras</s> who guarded the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, namely: <s>Utkhalī</s>, <s>Sūtkhalī</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Śūrabala</s>, <s>Keyūrabala</s>, <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>, <s>Mahiṃdhara</s>, <s>Avabhāsakara</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Dharmeśvara</s>, <s>Dharmaketu</s>, <s>Siddhapātra</s>, <s>Apratihatanetra</s>, <s>Mahāvyūha</s>, <s>Śīlaviśuddhanetra</s>, and <s>Padmaprabha</s>. These sixteen <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-guardian <s>devaputras</s>, all having attained the patience of irreversibility, adorned the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — surrounded on all sides for eighty <s>yojanas</s> by seven jeweled railings, seven rows of palm trees, seven jeweled bell-nets, seven jeweled strings; overlaid with cloths of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold set with the seven jewels, strewn with golden strings and <s>Jāmbūnada</s> golden lotuses, perfumed with supreme fragrances, canopied by jeweled nets. And whatever various trees exist in the various world-systems in the ten directions — noble, highly honored, divine and human — all of them appeared there at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. And whatever various kinds of flowers, water-born and land-born, exist in the ten directions — all of those too appeared there at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. And whatever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the various world-systems of the ten directions adorn the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> with immeasurable arrays of merit and knowledge — they too appeared there at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhimaṇḍaparipālakairdevaputraistādṛśā vyūhā bodhimaṇḍe abhinirmitā abhūvan, yān dṛṣṭvā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsurāḥ svabhavanāni śmaśānasaṃjñāmutpādayāmāsuḥ / tāṃśca vyūhān dṛṣṭvātyarthaṃ citrīkāramutpādayāmāsuḥ / evamudānaṃ codānayāmāsuḥ - sādhvaho 'cintyaḥ puṇyavipākaniṣyanda iti / catvāraśca bodhivṛkṣadevatāḥ / tadyathā - veṇuśca valguśca sumanaśca ojāpatiśca / ete catvāro bodhivṛkṣadevatā bodhisattvasya pūjārthaṃ bodhivṛkṣaṃ māpayanti sma mūlasaṃpannaṃ skandhasaṃpannaṃ śākhāpatrapuṣpaphalasaṃpannaṃ ārohapariṇāhasaṃpannaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ vistīrṇamaśītistālānuccaistvena tadanurūpeṇa pariṇāhena citraṃ darśanīyaṃ manoramaṃ saptabhī ratnavedikābhiḥ parivṛtaṃ saptabhī ratnatālapaṅktibhiḥ saptabhī ratnakiṅkiṇījālaiḥ saptabhī ratnasūtraiḥ samantādanuparivṛtairanuparikṣiptaṃ pārijātakakovidāraprakāśamatṛptacakṣurdarśanam / sa ca pṛthivīpradeśastrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuvajreṇābhidṛḍhaḥ sāro 'bhedyavajramayaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt yatra bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇo 'bhūdbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, such arrays were magically created at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> by the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>-guardian <s>devaputras</s> that, upon seeing them, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Asuras</s> generated the perception of a charnel ground toward their own abodes. Having seen those arrays, they generated the utmost wonder and exclaimed this <s>udāna</s>: 'Excellent! Inconceivable is the outpouring of the ripening of merit!' And there were four deities of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, namely: <s>Veṇu</s>, <s>Valgu</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, and <s>Ojāpati</s>. These four <s>Bodhi</s>-tree deities, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, fashioned the <s>Bodhi</s> tree — perfect in roots, perfect in trunk, perfect in branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit, perfect in height and girth, pleasing, beautiful to behold, broad, eighty palm-trees in height with proportional girth, wondrous, beautiful, delightful, surrounded by seven jeweled railings, seven rows of jeweled palms, seven jeweled bell-nets, seven jeweled strings encompassing it on all sides; of the splendor of a <s>Pārijātaka</s> or <s>Kovidāra</s> [tree], unsating to the eye. And that place of earth was made diamond-firm with the diamond of the trichiliocosmic world-system — solid, indestructible, made of <s>vajra</s> — where the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat, wishing to fully awaken to <s>Bodhi</s>.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvena bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkramatā tathārūpā kāyātprabhā muktābhūt, yayā prabhayā sarve 'pāyāḥ śāntā abhūvan / sarvāṇyakṣaṇāni pithitānyabhūvan / sarvadurgativedanāścopaśoṣitā anubhavan / ye ca sattvā vikalendriyā abhūvan, te sarve paripūrṇendriyatāmanuprāpnuvan / vyādhitāśca vyādhibhyo vyamucyanta / bhayārditāścāśvāsaprāptā abhūvan / bandhanabaddhāśca bandhanebhyo vyamucyanta / daridrāśca sattvā bhogavanto 'bhūvan / kleśasaṃtaptāśca niṣparidāhā abhūvan /
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, such a radiance was released from his body that by that radiance all the lower realms were pacified; all the unfavorable states were blocked; all the sufferings of the evil destinies were dried up. All beings with impaired faculties attained complete faculties. The diseased were freed from disease. Those afflicted by fear gained reassurance. Those bound in chains were freed from their bonds. Poor beings became wealthy. Those tormented by afflictions became free from burning.

body.text: bubhukṣitāśca sattvāḥ pūrṇodarā abhūvan / pipāsitāśca tṛṣāpagatā abhūvan / gurviṇyaśca sukhena prasūyante sma / jīrṇadurbalāśca balasaṃpannā abhūvan / na ca kasyacitsattvasya tasmin samaye rāgo bādhate dveṣo va moho vā krodho vā lobho vā khilo vā vyāpādo vā īrṣyā vā mātsaryo vā / na kaścitsattvastasmin samaye mriyate sma, na cyavate sma, nopapadyate sma / sarvasattvāśca tasmin samaye maitracittā hitacittāḥ parasparaṃ mātāpitṛsaṃjñino 'bhūvan //
body.translated_text: Hungry beings became full-bellied. Thirsty beings had their thirst removed. Pregnant women gave birth with ease. The old and feeble became endowed with strength. No being's passion afflicted [them] at that time, nor hatred, nor delusion, nor anger, nor greed, nor malice, nor ill-will, nor envy, nor miserliness. No being died at that time, nor was reborn, nor was conceived. All beings at that time were of loving minds, benevolent minds — regarding each other with the perception of mother and father.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: yāvaccāvīciparyantaṃ narakā ghoradarśanāḥ /
children.translated_text: As far as <s>Avīci</s>, the hells of terrible appearance —

children.text: duḥkhaṃ praśāntaṃ sattvānāṃ sukhaṃ vindanti vedanām // Lal_19.7 //
children.translated_text: the suffering of beings was pacified; they experienced happy feeling. // Lal_19.7 //

children.text: tiryagyoniṣu yāvantaḥ sattvā anyonyaghātakāḥ /
children.translated_text: However many beings in the animal realms destroyed one another —

children.text: maitracittā hite jātāḥ spṛṣṭā bhābhirmahāmune // Lal_19.8 //
children.translated_text: they became of loving mind, born in benevolence, touched by the radiance of the Great Sage. // Lal_19.8 //

children.text: pretalokeṣu yāvantaḥ pretāḥ kṣuttarṣapīḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: However many <s>pretas</s> in the <s>preta</s>-worlds, afflicted by hunger and thirst —

children.text: prāpnuvantyannapānāni bodhisattvasya tejasā // Lal_19.9 //
children.translated_text: they obtained food and drink by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s splendor. // Lal_19.9 //

children.text: akṣaṇāḥ pithitāḥ sarve durgatiścopaśoṣitā /
children.translated_text: All the unfavorable states were blocked, the evil destinies dried up;

children.text: sukhitāḥ sarvasattvāśca divyasaukhyasamarpitāḥ // Lal_19.10 //
children.translated_text: all beings were made happy, established in divine bliss. // Lal_19.10 //

children.text: cakṣuśrotravihīnāśca ye cānye vikalendriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those deprived of sight or hearing, and others with impaired faculties —

children.text: sarvendriyaiḥ susaṃpūrṇā jātāḥ sarvāṅgaśobhanāḥ // Lal_19.11 //
children.translated_text: all became complete in every faculty, beautiful in all their limbs. // Lal_19.11 //

children.text: rāgadveṣādibhiḥ kleśaiḥ sattvā bādhyanta ye sadā /
children.translated_text: Beings always afflicted by passion, hatred, and other defilements —

children.text: śāntakleśāstadā sarve jātāḥ sukhasamarpitāḥ // Lal_19.12 //
children.translated_text: all then had their afflictions pacified, established in happiness. // Lal_19.12 //

children.text: unmattāḥ smṛtimantaśca daridrā dhaninastathā /
children.translated_text: The mad regained mindfulness; the poor became wealthy;

children.text: vyādhitā roganirmuktā muktā bandhanabaddhakāḥ // Lal_19.13 //
children.translated_text: the diseased were freed from illness; those bound in chains were freed. // Lal_19.13 //

children.text: na khilaṃ na ca mātsaryaṃ vyāpādo na ca vigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: No malice, no miserliness, no ill-will, and no conflict —

children.text: anyonyaṃ saṃprakurvanti maitracittāḥ sthitāstadā // Lal_19.14 //
children.translated_text: they treated each other [well], abiding in loving-kindness at that time. // Lal_19.14 //

children.text: mātuḥ pituścaikaputre yathā prema pravartate /
children.translated_text: As the love of a mother and father toward an only son arises,

children.text: tathānyonyena sattvānāṃ putraprema tadābhavat // Lal_19.15 //
children.translated_text: so was the parental love of beings toward each other at that time. // Lal_19.15 //

children.text: bodhisattvaprabhājālaiḥ sphuṭāḥ kṣetrā hyacintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Pervaded by the net of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s radiance — inconceivable fields,

children.text: gaṅgāvālikasaṃkhyātāḥ samantādvai diśo daśaḥ // Lal_19.16 //
children.translated_text: numbered as the sands of the Ganges, in all ten directions! // Lal_19.16 //

children.text: na bhūyaścakravālāśca dṛśyante kālaparvatāḥ /
children.translated_text: No longer were <s>Cakravāla</s> [ranges] or dark mountains seen;

children.text: sarve te vipulāḥ kṣetrāḥ dṛśyantyekaṃ yathā tathā // Lal_19.17 //
children.translated_text: all those vast fields appeared as one. // Lal_19.17 //

children.text: pāṇitalaprakāśāśca dṛśyante sarvaratnikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Clear as the palm of a hand, they appeared, all made of jewels;

children.text: bodhisattvasya pūjārthaṃ sarvakṣetrā alaṃkṛtāḥ // Lal_19.18 //
children.translated_text: all fields were adorned for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // Lal_19.18 //

children.text: devāśca ṣoḍaśa tathā bodhimaṇḍopacārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: And sixteen gods, attendants of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>,

children.text: alaṃcakrurbodhimaṇḍaṃ aśītiryojanāvṛtam // Lal_19.19 //
children.translated_text: adorned the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, encompassed for eighty <s>yojanas</s>. // Lal_19.19 //

children.text: ye ca kecinmahāvyūhāḥ kṣetrakoṭīṣvanantakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever great arrays exist in endless <s>koṭis</s> of fields —

children.text: te sarve tatra dṛśyante bodhisattvasya tejasā // Lal_19.20 //
children.translated_text: all are seen there, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s splendor. // Lal_19.20 //

children.text: devā nāgāstathā yakṣāḥ kinnarāśca mahoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> —

children.text: svāni svāni vimānāni śmaśānānīva menire // Lal_19.21 //
children.translated_text: they regarded their own palaces as charnel grounds! // Lal_19.21 //

children.text: tān vyūhān saṃnirīkṣyeha vismitāḥ suramānuṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beholding those arrays, amazed were gods and humans:

children.text: sādhuḥ puṇyasya nisyandaḥ saṃpadyasyeyamīdṛśī // Lal_19.22 //
children.translated_text: 'Excellent is the outpouring of merit! Such is this prosperity!' // Lal_19.22 //

children.text: karoti naiva codyogaṃ kāyavāṅbhanasā tathā /
children.translated_text: He makes no effort whatsoever with body, speech, or mind;

children.text: sarvārthāścāsya sidhyanti ye 'bhipretā manorathāḥ // Lal_19.23 //
children.translated_text: yet all purposes are accomplished — whatever wishes he has in mind. // Lal_19.23 //

children.text: abhiprāyā yathānyeṣāṃ pūritāścaratā purā /
children.translated_text: As formerly, while practicing, he fulfilled the wishes of others —

children.text: vipākāḥ karmaṇastasya saṃpadyāteyamīdṛśī // Lal_19.24 //
children.translated_text: such is the ripening of that <s>karma</s>: this prosperity [now] manifests! // Lal_19.24 //

children.text: alaṃkṛto bodhimaṇḍaścaturbhirbodhidevataiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> was adorned by the four <s>Bodhi</s>-tree deities;

children.text: pārijāto divi yathā tasmādapi viśiṣyate // Lal_19.25 //
children.translated_text: like the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree in heaven — yet it surpasses even that! // Lal_19.25 //

children.text: guṇāḥ śakyā na te vācā sarve saṃparikīrtitum /
children.translated_text: These virtues cannot all be proclaimed by speech —

children.text: ye vyūhā bodhimaṇḍasya devatairabhisaṃskṛtāḥ // Lal_19.26 //
children.translated_text: the arrays of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> fashioned by the deities! // Lal_19.26 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastayā bodhisattvasya kāyapramuktayā prabhayā kālikasya nāgarājasya bhavanamavabhāsitamabhūt viśuddhayā vimalayā kāyacittaprahlādaudvilyajananyā sarvakleśāpakarṣiṇyā sarvasattvasukhaprītiprasādaprāmodyajananyā / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ kāliko nāgarājastasyāṃ velāyāṃ svasya parivārasya purataḥ sthitvemā gāthā abhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, by that radiance released from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body, the abode of <s>Kālika</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king was illuminated — pure, stainless, generating bodily and mental joy and exhilaration, removing all afflictions, generating happiness, delight, serenity, and gladness for all beings. Having seen [this], <s>Kālika</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, at that time standing before his retinue, spoke these verses:

children.text: krakuchande yatha ābha dṛṣṭa rucirā dṛṣṭā ca kanakāhvaye
children.translated_text: 'Such radiance as was seen when <s>Krakucchanda</s> [came], beautiful, and was seen with <s>Kanakāhvaya</s> [<s>Konāgamana</s>],

children.text: yadvatkāśyapi dharmarājamanaghe dṛṣṭā prabhā nirmalā /
children.translated_text: and such as was seen — stainless — with <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the faultless <s>Dharma</s>-king —

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ varalakṣaṇo hitakaro utpanna jñānaprabho
children.translated_text: without doubt, one bearing supreme marks, a benefactor, born as a light of knowledge,

children.text: yenedaṃ bhavanaṃ virocati hi me svarṇaprabhālaṃkṛtam // Lal_19.27 //
children.translated_text: by whom this dwelling of mine shines, adorned with golden radiance! // Lal_19.27 //

children.text: nāsmiṃ candraraviprabhā suvipulā saṃdṛśyate veśmani
children.translated_text: In this dwelling, the vast radiance of moon and sun is not seen,

children.text: no cāgnerna maṇerna vidyudamalā no ca prabhā jyotiṣām /
children.translated_text: nor of fire, nor of jewels, nor the stainless [light of] lightning, nor the radiance of stars,

children.text: no vā śakraprabhā na brahmaṇa prabhā no ca prabhā āsurī
children.translated_text: nor the radiance of <s>Śakra</s>, nor of <s>Brahmā</s>, nor the radiance of <s>Asuras</s> —

children.text: ekāntaṃ tamasākulaṃ mama gṛhaṃ prāgduṣkṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ // Lal_19.28 //
children.translated_text: utterly pervaded with darkness was my abode, due to prior evil deeds! // Lal_19.28 //

children.text: adyedaṃ bhavanaṃ virājati śubhaṃ madhye raviṃdīptivat
children.translated_text: Today this dwelling shines beautifully, like the radiance of the sun at midday;

children.text: cittaṃ prīti janeti kāyu sukhito gātrādbhutā śītalā /
children.translated_text: the mind generates joy, the body is blissful, and a wondrous coolness [pervades] the limbs!

children.text: taptā vālika yā śarīri nipatī jātā sa me śītalā
children.translated_text: The hot sand that falls upon [my] body has now become cool for me —

children.text: suvyaktaṃ bahukalpakoṭicarito bodhidramaṃ gacchati // Lal_19.29 //
children.translated_text: clearly, one who has practiced for many <s>kalpa</s>-<s>koṭis</s> approaches the <s>Bodhi</s> tree! // Lal_19.29 //

children.text: śīghraṃ gṛhṇata nāgapuṣpa rucirā vastrāṃ sugandhāṃ śubhāṃ
children.translated_text: Quickly take beautiful <s>Nāga</s>-flowers, garments, fragrances, and auspicious things —

children.text: muktāhārapinaddhatāṃśca valayāṃścūrṇāni dhūpottamā /
children.translated_text: pearl necklaces, bracelets, powders, and supreme incense!

children.text: saṃgītiṃ prakṛrudhva vādya vividhā bherīmṛdaṅgaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Strike up the music, play various instruments — the auspicious drums and <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>!

children.text: hantā gacchatha pūjanā hitakaraṃ pūjārha sarve jage // Lal_19.30 //
children.translated_text: Come, go for worship of the benefactor — the one worthy of worship from all the world!' // Lal_19.30 //

children.text: so 'bhyutthāya ca nāgakanyasahitaścaturo diśaḥ prekṣate
children.translated_text: He rose up, together with the <s>Nāga</s> maidens, and gazed in the four directions;

children.text: adrākṣīdatha meruparvatanibhaṃ svālaṃkṛtaṃ tejasā /
children.translated_text: he then beheld [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], like <s>Meru</s> mountain, well-adorned with splendor,

children.text: devairdānavakoṭibhiḥ parivṛtaṃ brahmendrayakṣaistathā
children.translated_text: surrounded by gods, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Dānavas</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s> —

children.text: pūjāṃ tasya karonti hṛṣṭamanaso darśenti mārgo hyayam // Lal_19.31 //
children.translated_text: they perform worship with delighted minds and point out: 'This is the way!' // Lal_19.31 //

children.text: saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa hi nāgarāṭ sumuditaścābhyarcya lokottamaṃ
children.translated_text: That <s>Nāga</s> king, delighted and supremely joyful, having worshiped the foremost in the world,

children.text: vanditvā caraṇau ca gauravakṛtastasthau muneragrataḥ /
children.translated_text: bowing at his feet with reverence, stood before the sage.

children.text: nāgākanya udagra hṛṣṭamanasaḥ kurvanti pūjāṃ muneḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Nāga</s> maidens, elated and delighted, perform worship of the sage,

children.text: puṣpaṃ gandhavilepanā ca kṣipiṣustūryāṇi nirnādayan // Lal_19.32 //
children.translated_text: scattering flowers, fragrances, and ointments, sounding instruments! // Lal_19.32 //

children.text: kṛtvā cāñjali nāgarāṭ sumuditastuṣṭāva tathyairguṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: With palms joined, the <s>Nāga</s> king, supremely joyful, praised [him] with truthful virtues:

children.text: sādhurdarśitu pūrṇacandravadane lokottame nāyake /
children.translated_text: Excellent! The display, O full-moon-faced one, supreme in the world, O leader —

children.text: yatha me dṛṣṭa nimitta pūrvaṛṣiṇāṃ paśyāmi tāneva te
children.translated_text: just as I saw the omens of the former sages, I see those same [omens] in you.

children.text: adya tvaṃ vinihatya mārabalavāniṣṭaṃ padaṃ lapsyase // Lal_19.33 //
children.translated_text: Today you, having destroyed the forces of <s>Māra</s>, shall attain the desired state! // Lal_19.33 //

children.text: yasyārthe damadānasaṃyama pure sarvā ti tyāgī abhūt
children.translated_text: For whose sake you formerly gave up all — restraint, giving, discipline, in the city;

children.text: yasyārthe damaśīlamaitrakaruṇākṣāntibalaṃ bhāvitam /
children.translated_text: for whose sake you cultivated restraint, morality, loving-kindness, compassion, and the power of patience;

children.text: yasyārthe damavīryadhyānanirataḥ prajñāpradīpaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: for whose sake, devoted to restraint, vigor, and <s>dhyāna</s>, you kindled the lamp of wisdom —

children.text: saiṣā te paripūrṇa sarva praṇidhī adyā jino bheṣyase // Lal_19.34 //
children.translated_text: that vow of yours is now completely fulfilled — today you shall become a <s>Jina</s>! // Lal_19.34 //

body.text:
yadvadvṛkṣa sapatrapuṣpa saphalā bodhidrumaṃ saṃnatāḥ
yadvatkumbhasahasra pūrṇasalilā kurvanti prādakṣiṇam /

children.text: yadvaccāpsaragaṇāśca saṃpramuditā snigdhaṃ rutaṃ kurvate
children.translated_text: just as the hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, delighted, utter sweet sounds;

children.text: haṃsā kroñcagaṇā yathā ca gagane gacchanti līlānvitaṃ
children.translated_text: just as swans and flocks of cranes move gracefully through the sky, and joyfully circumambulate the sage —

children.text: kurvante sumanāḥ pradakṣiṇamṛṣiṃ bhāvi tvamadyārhavān // Lal_19.35 //
children.translated_text: you shall become today an <s>Arhat</s>! // Lal_19.35 //

body.translated_text: Just as trees with leaves, flowers, and fruits bow down toward the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree; just as thousands of vessels full of water circumambulate [you];

children.text: yatha vā kāñcanavarṇa ābha rucirā kṣatrāśatā gacchate
children.translated_text: Just as a beautiful golden radiance spreads over hundreds of lands;

children.text: śāntāścāpi yathā apāya nikhilā duḥkhairvimuktā prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: just as the lower realms are pacified and beings are freed from all sufferings;

children.text: yadvadvṛṣṭita candrasūryabhavanā vāyurmṛdurvāyate
children.translated_text: just as from the rain the abodes of the moon and sun [are refreshed] and a gentle breeze blows —

children.text: adyā bheṣyasi sārthavāhu tribhave jātījarāmocako // Lal_19.36 //
children.translated_text: today you shall become the caravan-leader of the three realms, the liberator from birth and old age! // Lal_19.36 //

children.text: yadvatkāmaratī vihāya ca surāstvatpūjane 'bhyāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as gods have come to worship you, having abandoned the pleasures of desire-realm;

children.text: brahmā brahmapurohitāśca amarā utsṛjya dhyānaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: just as <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, and the immortals have come, having given up the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>;

children.text: ye kecittribhave tathaiva ca pure sarve ihābhyāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: just as all who exist anywhere in the three realms and in cities have come here —

children.text: adyā bheṣyasi vaidyarāju tribhave jāṭījaramocako // Lal_19.37 //
children.translated_text: today you shall become the physician-king of the three realms, the liberator from birth and old age! // Lal_19.37 //

children.text: mārgaścāpi yathā viśodhitu surairyenādya tvaṃ gacchase
children.translated_text: And just as the path by which you travel today has been purified by the gods —

children.text: etenāgatu krakucchandu bhagavān kanakāhvayaḥ kāśyapaḥ /
children.translated_text: by this [path] came the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, <s>Kanakāhvaya</s> [Kanakamuni], and <s>Kāśyapa</s>.

children.text: yatha vā padma viśuddha nirmala śubhā bhittvā mahīmudgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as pure, stainless, beautiful lotuses have burst through the earth and risen forth

children.text: yasmiṃ nikṣipase kramānatibalāṃ bhāvi tvamadyārhavān // Lal_19.38 //
children.translated_text: wherever you set down your step with incomparable power — you shall today become an <s>Arhat</s>! // Lal_19.38 //

children.text: mārāḥ koṭisahasra nekanayutā gaṅgā yathā vālikāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Māras</s> in <s>koṭi</s>-thousands and countless <s>nayutas</s>, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: te tubhyaṃ na samartha bodhiviṭapāccāletu kampetu vā /
children.translated_text: they are unable to shake or cause you to tremble from the branch of the <s>Bodhi</s> [tree]!

children.text: yajñā naikavidhāḥ sahasranayutā gaṅgā yathā vālikāḥ
children.translated_text: Sacrifices of countless kinds, thousands of <s>nayutas</s>, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: yaṣṭāste caratā hitāya jagatasteneha vibhrājase // Lal_19.39 //
children.translated_text: those you worshipped while wandering for the welfare of the world — by that [merit] you shine here! // Lal_19.39 //

children.text: nakṣatrā saśaśī satārakaravī bhūmau patedambarāt
children.translated_text: Even if the stars with the moon, the sun with its rays, were to fall from the sky to the earth;

children.text: svasthānācca calenmahāgirivaraḥ śuṣyedatho sāgaraḥ /
children.translated_text: even if the great mountain-king were to move from its place, and the ocean were to dry up;

children.text: caturo dhātava kaści vijñapuruṣo darśeya ekaikaśaḥ
children.translated_text: even if some wise person could display the four elements one by one —

children.text: naiva tvaṃ drumarājamūlupagato aprāpya bodhyutthihet // Lal_19.40 //
children.translated_text: even so, you, having approached the foot of the king of trees, shall not rise without attaining <s>Bodhi</s>! // Lal_19.40 //

children.text: lābhā mahya sulabdha vṛddhi vipulā dṛṣṭo 'si yatsārathe
children.translated_text: Great is our gain, well-gained, vast — that you have been seen, O charioteer [of beings]!

children.text: pūjā caiva kṛtā guṇāśca kathitā bodhāya cotsāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worship has been offered, virtues have been recounted, and you have been urged toward awakening.

children.text: sarvā nāgavadhū ahaṃ ca sasutā mucyemito yonitaḥ
children.translated_text: May all <s>Nāga</s> brides, I, and [our] children be freed from [this animal] birth!

children.text: tvaṃ yāsī yatha mattavāraṇagate gacchema evaṃ vayam // Lal_19.41 //
children.translated_text: As you go with the gait of a rutting elephant — may we go likewise! // Lal_19.41 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavaḥ kālikasya nāgarājasyāgramahiṣī suvarṇaprabhāsā nāma, sā saṃbahulābhirnāgakanyābhiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā nānāratnachatraparigṛhītābhiḥ nānādūṣyaparigṛhītābhirnānāmuktāhāraparigṛhītābhiḥ nānāmaṇiratnaparigṛhītābhiḥ divyamānuṣyakamālyavilepanaguṇṭhaparigṛhītābhiḥ nānāgandhaghaṭikāparigṛhītābhiḥ nānātūryasaṃgītisaṃpravāditairnānāratnapuṣpavarṣairbodhisattvaṃ gacchantamabhyavakiranti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the chief queen of the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Kālika</s>, named <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsā</s>, surrounded and attended by many <s>Nāga</s> maidens — bearing various jeweled parasols, bearing various silk [banners], bearing various pearl necklaces, bearing various gem-jewels, bearing divine and human garlands, ointments, and shawls, bearing various incense-vessels — with various musical ensembles being played, showered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as he walked with showers of various jewel-flowers. //

body.text: ābhiśca gāthābhistuṣṭuvuḥ -
body.translated_text: And with these verses they praised [him] —

children.text: abhrāntā atrastā abhīrū achambhī alīnā adīnā prahṛṣṭā dudharṣā /
children.translated_text: Unwavering, unafraid, fearless, unshaken, unshrunken, undaunted, delighted, unassailable,

children.text: araktā aduṣṭā amūḍhā alubdhā viraktā vimuktā namaste maharṣe // Lal_19.42 //
children.translated_text: unattached, uncorrupted, undeluded, ungreedy, dispassionate, liberated — homage to you, O great sage! // Lal_19.42 //

children.text: bhiṣaṅkā viśalyā vineyā vineṣī suvaidyā jagasyā dukhebhyaḥ pramocī /
children.translated_text: A physician, a remover of darts, a trainer, one who guides, a supreme healer, a liberator of the world from sufferings!

children.text: alenā atrāṇā ahīnā viditvā bhavā lenu trāṇo trilokesmi jātaḥ // Lal_19.43 //
children.translated_text: Having known [beings to be] without shelter, without refuge, without protector — [you are] born as a shelter, a refuge in the three worlds! // Lal_19.43 //

children.text: prasannā prahṛṣṭā yathā devasaṃghāḥ pravarṣī nabhasthā mahatpuṣpavarṣam /
children.translated_text: Just as serene and joyful divine hosts rain down a great shower of flowers from the sky,

children.text: mahācailakṣepaṃ karontī yatheme jino bheṣyase 'dyā kuruṣva praharṣam // Lal_19.44 //
children.translated_text: and wave their garments aloft — you shall today become a <s>Jina</s>! Rejoice! // Lal_19.44 //

children.text: upehi drumendraṃ niṣīdā achambhī jinā mārasenāṃ dhuna kleśajālam /
children.translated_text: Approach the king of trees! Sit down, unshaken! O <s>Jina</s>, shake off <s>Māra</s>'s army, the net of afflictions!

children.text: vibuddhya praśāntāṃ varāmagrabodhiṃ yathā paurvakaistairvibuddhā jinendraiḥ // Lal_19.45 //
children.translated_text: Awaken to the supreme, foremost, peaceful <s>Bodhi</s>, just as those former <s>Jina</s>-lords awakened! // Lal_19.45 //

children.text: tvayā yasya arthe bahūkalpakoṭyaḥ kṛtā duṣkarāṇī jaganmocanārtham /
children.translated_text: For whose sake you performed austerities over many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, for the liberation of the world —

children.text: prapūrṇā ti āśā ayaṃ prāptu kālo upehi drumendraṃ spṛśasvāgrabodhim // Lal_19.46 //
children.translated_text: that aspiration is fully complete; this time has arrived! Approach the king of trees and touch the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>! // Lal_19.46 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

children.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - kutra niṣaṇṇaistaiḥ pūrvakaistathāgatairanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā iti /
children.translated_text: Then, O monks, this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Where did the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, seated, attain unsurpassed perfect awakening?'

children.text: tato 'syaitadabhūt - tṛṇasaṃstare niṣaṇṇairiti //
children.translated_text: Then he thought: 'Seated upon a grass-seat.' //

body.text: atha khalvantarīkṣagatāni śuddhāvāsakāyikadevaśatasahasrāṇi bodhisattvasya cetobhireva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāyaivaṃ vāco bhāṣante sma - evametat satpuruṣa, evametat / tṛṇasaṃstare satpuruṣa niṣadya taiḥ pūrvakaistathāgatairanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā iti //
body.translated_text: Then hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> gods in the sky, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mental reflection with their own minds, spoke these words: 'Just so, O true person, just so! Seated upon a grass-seat, O true person, the former <s>Tathāgatas</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.' //

body.text: adrākṣītkhalvapi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo mārgasya dakṣiṇe pārśve svastikaṃ yāvasikam tṛṇāni lūnāti sma nīlāni mṛdukāni sukumārāṇi ramaṇīyāni kuṇḍalajātāni pradakṣiṇāvartāni / mayūragrīvasaṃnibhāni kācilindikasukhasaṃsparśāni sugandhīni varṇavanti manoramāṇi / dṛṣṭvā ca
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O monks, saw on the right side of the road a [man named] <s>Svastika</s>, a grass-cutter (<s>yāvasika</s>), who was cutting grass — green, soft, delicate, lovely, curling, turning to the right, like a peacock's neck in color, pleasant to touch like <s>Kācilinḍika</s> cloth, fragrant, colorful, and delightful. Having seen [him],

body.text: punarbodhisattvo mārgādapakramya yena svastiko yāvasikastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya svastikaṃ yāvasikaṃ madhurayā vācā samālapati sma / yāsau vāgājñāpanī vijñāpanī vispaṣṭā anekalokaikavarṇasukhā valguḥ śravaṇīyā snigdhā smaraṇīyā codanī toṣaṇī premaṇī akarkaśā agadgadā aparuṣā acapalā ślakṣṇā madhurā karṇasukhā kāyacittodbilyakaraṇī rāgadoṣamohakalikaluṣavinodanī kalaviṅkarutasvarā kuṇālajīvaṃjīvakābhinaditaghoṣā dundubhisaṃgītirutaravitanirghoṣavatī anapahatā satyā acchā bhūtā brahmasvarutaravitanirghoṣā samudrasvaraveganibhā śailasaṃghaṭṭanavatī devendrāsurendrābhiṣṭutā gambhīrā duravagāhā namucibalābalakaraṇī parapravādamathanī siṃhasvaravegā hayagajagarjitaghoṣā nāganirnādanī meghastanitābhigarjitasvarā daśadiksarvabuddhakṣetraspharaṇī vineyasattvasaṃcodanī adrutā anupahatā avilambitā sahitā yuktā kālavādinī samayānatikramaṇī dharmaśatasahasrasugrathitā saumyā asaktā adhiṣṭhitapratibhānā ekarutā sarvarutaracanī sarvābhiprāyajñāpanī sarvasukhasaṃjananī mokṣapathasaṃdarśikā mārgasaṃbhāravādinī parṣadanatikramaṇī sarvaparṣatsaṃtoṣaṇī sarvabuddhabhāṣitānukūlā / īdṛśyā vācā bodhisattvaḥ svastikaṃ yāvasikaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, stepping off the road, approached <s>Svastika</s> the grass-cutter. Having approached, he addressed <s>Svastika</s> the grass-cutter in a sweet voice — a voice that was commanding, informing, clear, of a single tone [yet] pleasing to many worlds, charming, worthy of hearing, smooth, memorable, encouraging, satisfying, endearing, not harsh, not stammering, not rough, not fickle, gentle, sweet, pleasant to the ear, generating joy of body and mind, dispelling the stain of passion, hatred, and delusion, like the voice of a <s>kalaviṅka</s>-bird, like the cry of a <s>kunāla</s>-bird or <s>jīvajīvaka</s>-bird, resonating like a <s>dundubhi</s>-drum concert, unobstructed, true, clear, real, resonating like the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, like the force of the ocean's roar, like the crashing of mountains, praised by the lords of gods and <s>Asuras</s>, deep, unfathomable, enfeebling the forces of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>), crushing the doctrines of opponents, forceful like a lion's voice, roaring like horses and elephants, thundering like a <s>Nāga</s>, like the rumbling thunder of a storm-cloud, pervading all <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the ten directions, urging beings to be trained, neither hurried nor impeded, neither slow, coherent, well-composed, timely in speech, not transgressing the proper occasion, well-woven with hundreds of thousands of <s>dharmas</s>, gentle, unattached, endowed with inspired eloquence, a single sound comprehending all sounds, making known all intentions, generating all happiness, displaying the path to liberation, speaking of the provisions of the path, not transgressing the assembly, satisfying all assemblies, in accord with all <s>Buddha</s>-speech — with such a voice the <s>Bodhisattva</s> addressed <s>Svastika</s> the grass-cutter with verses —

children.text: tṛṇu dehi mi svastika śīghraṃ adya mamārthu tṛṇaiḥ sumahāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Give me grass quickly, O <s>Svastika</s>! Today my need for grass is supremely great.

children.text: sabalaṃ namuciṃ nihanitvā bodhimanuttaraśānti spṛśiṣye // Lal_19.47 //
children.translated_text: Having vanquished <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) with his army, I shall touch the <s>Bodhi</s>, the unsurpassed peace! // Lal_19.47 //

children.text: yasya kṛte mayi kalpasahasrā dānu damo 'pi ca saṃyama tyāgo /
children.translated_text: 'For whose sake over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> I [practiced] giving, restraint, discipline, and renunciation,

children.text: śīlavrataṃ ca tapaśca sucīrṇā tasya mi niṣpadi bheṣyati adya // Lal_19.48 //
children.translated_text: morality, vows, and well-practiced <s>tapas</s> — the fruition of that shall be mine today! // Lal_19.48 //

children.text: kṣāntibalaṃ tatha vīryabalaṃ ca dhyānabalaṃ tatha jñānabalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'The power of patience, the power of vigor, the power of <s>dhyāna</s>, the power of knowledge,

children.text: puṇyaabhijñavimokṣabalaṃ ca tasya mi niṣpadi bheṣyati adya // Lal_19.49 //
children.translated_text: the power of merit, superknowledge, and liberation — the fruition of that shall be mine today! // Lal_19.49 //

children.text: prajñabalaṃ ca upāyabalaṃ ca ṛddhima saṃgatamaitrabalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'The power of wisdom, the power of skillful means, the power of supernatural power, combined with the power of loving-kindness,

children.text: pratisaṃvidaparisatyabalaṃ ca teṣa mi niṣpadi bheṣyati adya // Lal_19.50 //
children.translated_text: the power of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>) and the power of truth — the fruition of those shall be mine today! // Lal_19.50 //

children.text: puṇyabalaṃ ca tavāpi anantaṃ yanmama dāsyasi adya tṛṇāni /
children.translated_text: 'Boundless too is your power of merit, in that you give me grass today;

children.text: na hyaparaṃ tava etu nimittaṃ tvaṃ pi anuttaru bheṣyasi śāstā // Lal_19.51 //
children.translated_text: for there is no other omen for you [but this] — you too shall become an unsurpassed teacher!' // Lal_19.51 //

children.text: śrutvā svastiku vāca nāyake suruciramadhurāṃ
children.translated_text: Having heard the leader's exceedingly beautiful and sweet voice,

children.text: tuṣṭo āttamanāśca harṣitaḥ pramuditamanasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Svastika</s> was satisfied, delighted, joyful, of glad mind.

children.text: gṛhṇītvā tṛṇamuṣṭi sparśanavatī mṛdutaruṇaśubhāṃ
children.translated_text: Taking a handful of grass — palpable, soft, tender, and beautiful —

children.text: purataḥ sthitvana vāca bhāṣate pramuditahṛdayaḥ // Lal_19.52 //
children.translated_text: standing before [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], he spoke with a delighted heart: // Lal_19.52 //

children.text: yadi tāva ṇṛkebhi labhyate padavaramamṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: 'If the supreme, deathless state can be attained by humans,

children.text: bodhī uttama śānta durdṛśā purimajinapathaḥ /
children.translated_text: the supreme, peaceful <s>Bodhi</s>, hard to see, the path of the former <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: tiṣṭhatu tāva mahāguṇodadhe aparimitayaśā
children.translated_text: then wait, O ocean of great virtues, of immeasurable fame!

children.text: ahameva prathame nu budhyami padavaramṛtam // Lal_19.53 //
children.translated_text: Let me be the very first to awaken to the supreme, deathless state!' // Lal_19.53 //

children.text: naiṣā svastika bodhi labhyate tṛṇavaraśayanaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Bodhi</s>, O <s>Svastika</s>, is not attained by [merely lying on] excellent grass-beds,

children.text: acaritvā bahukalpa duṣkarī vratatapa vividhā /
children.translated_text: without having practiced for many <s>kalpas</s> various severe vows and <s>tapas</s>.

children.text: prajñāpuṇyaupāyaudgato yada bhavi matimāṃ
children.translated_text: When one becomes wise, endowed with the resources of wisdom, merit, and skillful means —

children.text: tada paścājjina vyākaronti munayo bhaviṣyasi virajaḥ // Lal_19.54 //
children.translated_text: then afterward the <s>Jinas</s>, the sages, prophecy: "You shall become the dustless one!"' // Lal_19.54 //

children.text: yadi bodhi iya śakyu svastikā parajani dadituṃ
children.translated_text: 'If this <s>Bodhi</s> could be given by [one like] <s>Svastika</s> in another birth,

children.text: piṇḍīkṛtya dadeya prāṇināṃ ma bhavatu vimatiḥ /
children.translated_text: I would make it into a lump and give it to beings — let there be no doubt!

children.text: yada bodhī maya prāpta jānasī vibhajami amṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: When <s>Bodhi</s> is attained by me — as you shall know — I shall distribute the deathless.

children.text: āgatvā śṛṇu dharmayukta tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi virajaḥ // Lal_19.55 //
children.translated_text: Having come, hear the <s>Dharma</s>-endowed [teaching] — you shall become the dustless one!' // Lal_19.55 //

children.text: gṛhṇītvā tṛṇamuṣṭi nāyakaḥ paramasumṛdukāṃ
children.translated_text: Taking the supremely soft handful of grass, the leader,

children.text: siṃhāhaṃsagatiśca prasthitaḥ pracalita dharaṇī /
children.translated_text: with the gait of a lion and a swan, set forth — the earth trembled!

children.text: devā nāgagaṇāḥ kṛtāñjalī pramuditamanasaḥ
children.translated_text: Gods and hosts of <s>Nāgas</s>, with palms joined, of delighted minds [exclaimed]:

children.text: adyā mārabalaṃ nihatyayaṃ spṛśiṣyati amṛtam // Lal_19.56 //
children.translated_text: 'Today, having destroyed the forces of <s>Māra</s>, this one shall touch the deathless!' // Lal_19.56 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya bodhivṛkṣamupasaṃkrāmato 'śītibodhivṛkṣasahasrāṇi devaputraiśca bodhisattvaiśca maṇḍitānyabhūvan - iha niṣadya bodhisattvo bodhiṃ prāpsyatyabhisaṃbhotsyata iti / santi tatra kecidbodhivṛkṣāḥ puṣpamayā yojanaśatasahasrodviddhāḥ / kecid bodhivṛkṣā
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, eighty thousand <s>Bodhi</s>-trees had been adorned by <s>devaputras</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [each thinking]: 'Here, seated, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> shall attain and realize <s>Bodhi</s>!' Some of those <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of flowers, hundreds of thousands of <s>yojanas</s> in height. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees

body.text: gandhamayā dviyojanaśatasahasrodviddhāḥ / kecidbodhivṛkṣāścandanamayāstriyojanaśatasahasrodviddhāḥ / kecidbodhivṛkṣā vastramayāḥ pañcayojanaśatasahasrāṇyuccaistvena / kecidbodhivṛkṣā ratnamayā daśayojanaśatasahasrāṇyuccaistvena / kecidbodhivṛkṣāḥ sarvaratnamayā daśayojanakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇyuccaistvena / kecidbodhivṛkṣā ratnamayāḥ koṭinayutaśatasahasramudviddhāḥ / sarveṣu teṣu bodhivṛkṣamūleṣu yathānurūpāṇi siṃhāsanāni prajñaptānyabhūvan nānādivyadūṣyasaṃstṛtāni / kvacidbodhivṛkṣe padmāsanaṃ prajñaptamabhūt, kvacidgandhāsanam, kvacinnānāvidharatnāsanam / bodhisattvaśca lalitavyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma / samanantarasamāpannasya ca bodhisattvasyemaṃ lalitavyūhaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhim, atha tatkṣaṇameva bodhisattvaḥ sarveṣu ca teṣu bodhivṛkṣamūleṣu siṃhāsane saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamalaṃkṛtena kāyena / ekaikaśca bodhisattvo devaputraiścaivaṃ saṃjānīte sma - mamaiva siṃhāsane bodhisattvo niṣaṇṇo nānyeṣāmiti / yathā ca te saṃjānate sma - tathāsyaiva lalitavyūhasya bodhisattvasamādheranubhāvena sarvanirayatiryagyoniyamalokikāḥ sarve devamanuṣyāśca sarve gatyupapannāḥ sarvasattvā bodhisattvaṃ paśyanti sma bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇam //
body.translated_text: [Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were] made of fragrance, rising two hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of sandalwood, rising three hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of cloth, five hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of jewels, ten hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of all jewels, ten <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height. Some <s>Bodhi</s>-trees were made of jewels, rising <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> hundred thousands. At the root of all those <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, appropriately proportioned lion-thrones were prepared, spread with various divine silk cloths. Somewhere at a <s>Bodhi</s>-tree a lotus-seat was prepared, somewhere a fragrance-seat, somewhere a seat of various jewels. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Lalitavyūha</s> (Graceful Array). And immediately upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s entering this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s> called <s>Lalitavyūha</s>, at that very instant the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was seen seated on the lion-throne at the root of every one of those <s>Bodhi</s>-trees, with a body adorned with the [major] marks and [minor] characteristics. And each [group of] <s>devaputras</s> perceived: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is seated on my lion-throne alone, and not on those of others.' And just as they perceived, so by the power of this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s> called <s>Lalitavyūha</s>, all beings in the hells, animal realms, and <s>Yama</s>'s world, all gods and humans, all beings born in every destiny — [all] saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated on the lion-throne at the root of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree. //

body.text: atha ca punarhīnādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ matiparitoṣaṇārthaṃ bodhisattvastṛṇamuṣṭimādāya yena bodhivṛkṣastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhivṛkṣaṃ saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svayamevābhyantarāgraṃ bahirmūlaṃ samantabhadraṃ tṛṇasaṃstaraṇaṃ saṃstīrya siṃhavacchūravadbalavaddṛḍhavīryavatsthāmavannāgavadaiśvaryavatsvayaṃbhūvajjñānivadanuttaravadviśeṣavadabhyudratavadyaśovatkīrtivaddānavacchīlavatkṣāntivadvīryavaddhyānavatprajñāvajjñānavatpuṇyavannihatamārapratyarthikavatsaṃbhāravatparyaṅkamābhujya tasmiṃstṛṇasaṃstare nyaṣīdat prāṅmukha ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya abhimukhāṃ smṛtimupasthāpya / īdṛśaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ samādānamakarot -
body.translated_text: And further, for the purpose of satisfying the minds of beings of inferior disposition, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, taking a handful of grass, approached the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree.
