Having approached, he circumambulated the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree seven times, then himself spread a grass-mat — with its inner [ends] facing in, its roots outward, auspicious all around — and with the valor of a lion, the courage of a hero, the strength of the powerful, the firm vigor of the resolute, the power of the mighty, the sovereignty of the self-existent, the wisdom of the knowing, the supreme quality of the unsurpassed, the distinction of the distinguished, the excellence of the glorious, the fame of the renowned, the generosity of the giving, the morality of the virtuous, the patience of the patient, the vigor of the vigorous, the meditation of the meditative, the wisdom of the wise, the knowledge of the knowing, the merit of the meritorious, [and the confidence of] one who has conquered the adversary <s>Māra</s>, with complete accumulations — he sat cross-legged on that grass-mat, facing east, holding his body upright, establishing mindfulness before him. And he made this firm resolution:

children.text: ihāsane śuṣyatu me śarīraṃ tvagasthimāṃsaṃ pralayaṃ ca yātu /
children.translated_text: 'Let my body dry up on this seat! Let skin, bones, and flesh go to dissolution!

children.text: aprāpya bodhiṃ bahukalpadurlabhāṃ naivāsanātkāyamataścaliṣyate // Lal_19.57 //
children.translated_text: Without attaining <s>bodhi</s>, which is difficult to obtain in many <s>kalpas</s>, this body shall never be moved from this seat!' // Lal_19.57 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare bodhimaṇḍagamanaparivarto nāma ekonaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the nineteenth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on Going to the Seat of Awakening' (<s>Bodhimaṇḍagamanaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 20
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 20.

body.text: bodhimaṇḍavyūhaparivarto viṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Twentieth Chapter: On the Array of the Seat of Awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍavyūhaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇasyaṃ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ṣaṭ kāmāvacarā devāḥ sthitā abhūvan - mā bodhisattvasya kaścidantarāyaṃ kārṣīditi / evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottarā diśo devaiḥ parigṛhītā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, in the eastern direction, the six <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (Desire Realm) gods stood guard — [thinking:] 'Let no one create an obstacle for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>!' Likewise, the southern, western, and northern directions were guarded by gods. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bodhisattvasaṃcodanīṃ nāma raśmiṃ prāmuñcat, yayā raśmyā samantāddaśasu dikṣvaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni dharmadhātuparamāṇyākāśadhātuparyavasānāni sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyavabhāsitānyabhūvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, at that time emitted a ray of light called <s>Bodhisattvasaṃcodanī</s> (Exhortation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>), by which ray, in all ten directions, immeasurable, innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields, extending to the ultimate atoms of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and to the limits of the space-element, were illuminated. //

body.text: atha khalu pūrvasyāṃ diśi vimalāyāṃ lokadhātau vimalaprabhāsasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāllalitavyūho nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya ca tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe tathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramabhisamakarod yenaddharyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena daśasu dikṣvākāśadhātuparyavasānāni sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇyekaṃ maṇḍalamātramādarśayati sma śuddhasya nīlavaiḍūryasya / pañcagatyupapannānāṃ sarvasattvānāṃ purato bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇaṃ bodhisattvamupadarśayati sma / te ca sattvāḥ parasparamekāṅgulikābhirbodhisattvamupadarśayanti sma - ko 'yamevaṃrūpaḥ sattvo lalitaḥ, ko 'yamevaṃrūpaḥ sattvo virājata iti / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ purato bodhisattvo bodhisattvānnirmimīte sma / tatra te bodhisattvavigrahā imā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, from the eastern direction, from the world-system called <s>Vimalā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalaprabhāsa</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Lalitavyūha</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he performed such a miraculous transformation that, by that miraculous transformation, all <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions up to the limits of the space-element were displayed as a single mirror-like disk of pure blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). Before all beings born in the five destinies, he displayed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. And those beings pointed out the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to one another with their fingers: 'Who is this being of such graceful form? Who is this being that shines so?' And before those beings, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> emanated <s>Bodhisattva</s>-forms. Those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-forms spoke these verses —

children.text: yasyā kiṃcana rāgadoṣakaluṣā sā vāsanā uddhṛtā
children.translated_text: He in whom every stain of passion, hatred, and defilement has been uprooted, along with its latent impressions;

children.text: yasyā kāyaprabhākṛtā daśadiśe sarve prabhā niṣprabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: he whose bodily radiance renders all [other] radiances in the ten directions lightless;

children.text: yasyā puṇyasamādhijñānanicayaḥ kalpaughasaṃvardhiṃtaḥ
children.translated_text: he whose accumulation of merit, <s>samādhi</s>, and knowledge has been increased through floods of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: so 'yaṃ śākyamunirmahāmunivaraḥ sarvā diśo bhrājate // Lal_20.1 //
children.translated_text: this is <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the supreme Great Sage, who illuminates all directions! // Lal_20.1 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi ratnavyūhāyā lokadhāto ratnārciṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādratnacchatrakūṭasaṃdarśano nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe ekaratnachatreṇa taṃ sarvāvantaṃ maṇḍalamātraṃ saṃchādayati sma / tatra śakrabrahmalokapālāḥ parasparametadavocan - kasyedaṃ phalam, kenāyamevaṃrūpo ratnachatravyūhaḥ saṃdṛśyata iti / atha tasmādratnachatrādiyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, from the southern direction, from the world-system called <s>Ratnavyūhā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnārciṣa</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnacchatrakūṭasaṃdarśana</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he covered that entire mirror-like disk with a single jeweled parasol. Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s> said to one another: 'Whose is this fruit? By whom is this kind of jeweled parasol array seen?' Then from that jeweled parasol this verse issued forth —

body.text:
yena cchatrasahasrakoṭinayutā gandhāna ratnāna ca
dattā apratimeṣu maitramanasā tiṣṭhanti ke nirvṛte /
body.translated_text: He by whom thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of parasols of fragrance and jewels were given to the incomparable ones with loving minds, [those who] abide in <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

body.text: so eṣo varalakṣaṇo hitakaro nārāyaṇasthāmavān
body.translated_text: this very one, bearing the excellent marks, a benefactor, possessed of the strength of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

body.text: bodhermūlamupāgato guṇadharastasyaiṣa pūjā kṛtā // Lal_20.2 //
body.translated_text: has come to the root of awakening, a bearer of virtues — this worship has been performed for him! // Lal_20.2 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu paścimāyā diśaścampakavarṇāyā lokadhātoḥ puṣpāvalivanarājikusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādindrajālī nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopajagāma / upetya ca bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe sarvāvantaṃ maṇḍalamātramekaratnajālena saṃchādayati sma / tatra daśasu dikṣu devanāgayakṣagandharvāḥ parasparamevamāhuḥ - kasyāyamevaṃrūpo prabhāvyūha iti / atha tasmādratnajālādiyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, from the western direction, from the world-system called <s>Campakavarṇā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Puṣpāvalivanarājikusumitābhijña</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Indrajālī</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he covered the entire mirror-like disk with a single jeweled net. Then the <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> in the ten directions said to one another: 'Whose is this kind of radiant array?' Then from that jeweled net this verse issued forth —

children.text: ratnākaro ratanaketu ratistriloke ratnottamo ratanakīrti rataḥ sudharme /
children.translated_text: He who is a mine of jewels, a jewel-banner, the joy of the three worlds, the supreme jewel, jewel-fame, delighting in the true <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: ratnāni trīṇi na ca chetsyati vīryaprāptaḥ so bodhi prāpsyati varāmiya tasya pūjā // Lal_20.3 //
children.translated_text: who shall not abandon the Three Jewels, endowed with vigor — he shall attain <s>bodhi</s>! This is the supreme worship for him! // Lal_20.3 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalūttarasyāṃ diśi sūryāvartāyā lokadhātoścandrasūryajihmīkaraprabhasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādvyūharājo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe yāvanto daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāstān sarvāṃstasmin maṇḍalamātre saṃdarśayati sma / tatra kecidbodhisattvā evamāhuḥ - kasyema evaṃrūpā vyūhāḥ? atha tebhyaḥ sarvavyūhebhya iyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, from the northern direction, from the world-system called <s>Sūryāvartā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryajihmīkaraprabha</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vyūharāja</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he displayed within that mirror-like disk all the qualities and arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-fields in all world-systems of the ten directions. Then some <s>Bodhisattvas</s> said: 'Whose are these kinds of arrays?' Then from all those arrays this verse issued forth —

children.text: kāyo yena viśodhitaḥ subahuśaḥ puṇyena jñānena ca
children.translated_text: He by whom the body was purified many times through merit and knowledge;

children.text: yenā vāca viśodhitā vratatapaiḥ satyena dharmeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: he by whom speech was purified through observances, austerities, truth, and <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: cittaṃ yena viśodhitaṃ hiridhṛtī kāruṇyamaitryā tathā
children.translated_text: he by whom the mind was purified through modesty, steadfastness, compassion, and loving-kindness —

children.text: so eṣo drumarājamūlupagataḥ śākyarṣabhaḥ pūjyate // Lal_20.4 //
children.translated_text: this very one, the Bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, having come to the root of the king of trees, is worshipped! // Lal_20.4 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu pūrvadakṣiṇasyā diśo guṇākarāyā lokadhātorguṇarājaprabhāsasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādruṇamatirnāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe sarvaguṇavyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ tasmin maṇḍalamātre 'bhinirmimīte sma / tasya te parivārā evamāhuḥ - kasyāyamevaṃrūpaḥ kūṭāgāravyūhaḥ? tataśca kūṭāgārādiyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, from the southeastern direction, from the world-system called <s>Guṇākarā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Guṇarājaprabhāsa</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ruṇamati</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he created within that mirror-like disk a palace adorned with all virtues. His attendants said: 'Whose is this kind of palace array?' Then from that palace this verse issued forth —

body.text: yasya guṇaiḥ satataṃ guṇagandhikā bhonti surāsura yakṣa mahoragāḥ /
body.translated_text: He whose virtues constantly make gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> fragrant with virtue;

body.text: so guṇavān guṇarājakulodito bodhiviṭape upaviṣṭu guṇodadhiḥ // Lal_20.5 //
body.translated_text: that virtuous one, arisen from the lineage of the king of virtues, seated at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree — an ocean of virtues! // Lal_20.5 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu dakṣiṇapaścimāyā diśo ratnasaṃbhavāyā lokadhāto ratnayaṣṭestathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādratnasaṃbhavo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe aprameyāsaṃkhyeyān ratnavyomakāṃstasminmaṇḍalamātre 'bhinirmimīte sma / tebhyaśca ratnavyomakebhya iyaṃ gāthā niścacāra -
body.translated_text: Then, from the southwestern direction, from the world-system called <s>Ratnasaṃbhavā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnayaṣṭi</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he created immeasurable, innumerable jeweled canopies within that mirror-like disk. And from those jeweled canopies this verse issued forth —

children.text: tyaktā yena sasāgarā vasumatī ratnānyatho 'nekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: He by whom the earth with its oceans was relinquished, and manifold treasures,

children.text: prāsādāśca gavākṣaharmikavarā yugyāni yānāni ca /
children.translated_text: and palaces with windows and finest mansions, yoked vehicles and conveyances,

children.text: vyomālaṃkṛta puṣpadāma rucirā udyāna kūpā sabhā
children.translated_text: and sky-adorned beautiful flower-garlands, parks, wells, and assembly halls,

children.text: hastā pāda śirottamāṅganayanāḥ so bodhimaṇḍe sthitaḥ // Lal_20.6 //
children.translated_text: and hands, feet, head, and eyes — he stands at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>! // Lal_20.6 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu paścimottarasyā diśo meghavatyā lokadhātormegharājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrānmeghakūṭābhigarjitasvaro nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe kālānusāryagurumeghamabhinirmāyoragasāracandanacūrṇavarṣaṃ tasmin maṇḍalamātre 'bhipravarṣati sma / tasmācca kālānusārimeghamaṇḍalamātrādiyaṃ gāthā niścarati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, from the northwestern direction, from the world-system called <s>Meghavatī</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Megharāja</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Meghakūṭābhigarjitasvara</s>, exhorted by that radiance, surrounded and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> beyond enumeration, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having created a cloud of <s>kālānusāri</s> (finest black aloe), he rained down a shower of <s>uragasāra</s>-sandalwood powder within that mirror-like disk. And from that cloud-disk of <s>kālānusāri</s>, this verse issued forth —

children.text: dharmāmegha sphuritva sarvatribhave vidyādhimuktaprabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having spread the <s>dharma</s>-cloud throughout all the three worlds, with the radiance of knowledge and aspiration,

children.text: saddharmaṃ ca virāga varṣiṃ amṛtaṃ nirvāṇasaṃprāpakam /
children.translated_text: and raining down the true <s>dharma</s>, dispassionate, deathless, leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: sarvā rāgakileśabandhanalatā so vāsanā chetsyati
children.translated_text: he shall cut all the creeping vines of passion, <s>kleśas</s>, and bondage, together with their latent impressions,

children.text: dhyānarddhībalaindriyaiḥ kusumitaḥ śraddhākaraṃ dāsyate // Lal_20.7 //
children.translated_text: blossoming with <s>dhyāna</s>, supernatural powers, [spiritual] strengths, and faculties — he shall give the mine of faith! // Lal_20.7 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalūttarapūrvasyā diśo hemajālapratichannāyā lokadhāto ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrāddhemajālālaṃkṛto nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayāprabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe sarveṣu teṣu kūṭāgāreṣu ratnavyomakeṣu dvātriṃśallakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtān bodhisattvavigrahānabhinirmimīte sma / sarve ca te bodhisattvavigrahā divyamānuṣyakapuṣpadāmaparigṛhītā yena bodhisattvastenābhinatakāyāstāni puṣpadāmānyabhipralambayanti sma / te imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then from the northeast direction, from the world-system called 'Covered with a Golden Net,' from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsa</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Hemajālālaṃkṛta</s>, roused by that radiance, surrounded and preceded by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> past counting, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in all those upper-storied palaces and jewel-canopied spaces, he manifested forms of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> adorned with the thirty-two marks. And all those <s>Bodhisattva</s>-forms, holding garlands of divine and human flowers, with bodies bowed toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, hung down those flower-garlands. They spoke this verse:

children.text: yena buddhanayutā stavita pūrva gauraveṇa mahatā janiya śraddhām /
children.translated_text: He by whom <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were praised before, with great reverence, generating faith,

children.text: brahmaghoṣavacanaṃ madhuravāṇiṃ bodhimaṇḍopagataṃ śirasi vande // Lal_20.8 //
children.translated_text: with a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, with sweet speech — I bow at the head of him who has gone to the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>! // Lal_20.8 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalvadhastāddiśaḥ samantavilokitāyā lokadhātoḥ samantadarśinastathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādratnagarbho nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe tasmin vaidūryamayamaṇḍalamātre jāmbūnadasuvarṇapadmānyabhyudgatānyupadarśayati sma / teṣāṃ ca padmānāṃ karṇikāsvardhakāyikā nāryo varṇarūpasaṃpannāḥ sarvālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitā upadarśayati sma / vāmadakṣiṇe pāṇibhirharṣakaṭakakeyūrasuvarṇasūtramuktāhārādivividhābharaṇaparigṛhītāḥ puṣpapaṭṭadāmāni cābhipralambayantyo yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenoparyabhinatakāyāḥ / tāścemāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then from the direction below, from the world-system called <s>Samantavilokitā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantadarśin</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, roused by that radiance, surrounded and preceded by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> past counting, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on that circular area made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, he made to appear golden lotuses of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold risen up. And on the pistils of those lotuses, he made to appear half-bodied women, endowed with beauty of complexion and form, adorned with all ornaments, holding in their left and right hands various ornaments — bracelets, armlets, golden strings, pearl necklaces, and the like — and hanging down garlands of flower-cloth, with bodies bowed upward toward the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And they spoke this verse:

children.text: yo onamiṣṭa sadā gurūṇāṃ buddhaśrāvakapratyekajinānām /
children.translated_text: He who always bowed to his teachers — <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> —

children.text: nirmāṇasuśīla sadojju praṣṭho tasyā onamathā guṇadharasya // Lal_20.9 //
children.translated_text: of pure good conduct by his manifestations, always upright and foremost — bow down to that bearer of virtues! // Lal_20.9 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalūpariṣṭāddiśo varagaganāyā lokadhātorgaṇendrasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādgaganagañjo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastayā prabhayā saṃcoditaḥ san gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe gaganatalastha eva yāvanto daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣvadṛṣṭāśrutapūrvāḥ santi puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaravastrālaṃkārachatradhvajapatākāvaijayantiratn - amaṇikanakarajatamuktāhārahayagajarathapattivāhanapuṣpavṛkṣapatrapuṣpaphaladārakadārikā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālamānuṣyāmānuṣyāṇāṃ sarvā gaganatalānmahāntaṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravarṣanti sma sarvasattvaprītisukhasaṃjananaṃ ca / na ca kasyacitsattvasya bhayaṃ cotpīḍāṃ vā karoti sma //
body.translated_text: Then from the direction above, from the world-system called <s>Varagaganā</s>, from the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gaṇendra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Gaganagañja</s>, roused by that radiance, surrounded and preceded by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> past counting, approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, standing in the sky, [he produced] all that had never before been seen or heard in all the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the ten directions — flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, garments, ornaments, parasols, banners, pennants, victory-standards, jewels, gems, gold, silver, pearl necklaces, horses, elephants, chariots, infantry, vehicles, flower-trees, leaves, flowers, fruits, boys, girls, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Lokapālas</s>, humans, and non-humans — all of these rained down a great rain of flowers from the sky, generating joy and happiness for all beings. And it did not cause fear or distress to any being. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: peyālameṣa diśatāsu jinaurasā ye saṃpūjituṃ hitakaraṃ anuprāpta bodhim /
children.translated_text: In abbreviated form: those sons of the <s>Jinas</s> in [all] the ten directions, who came to worship the beneficent one who had reached awakening —

children.text: teṣāṃ viyūhakramavikramasukramāṇāṃ opamyamātra niśṛṇotha jinaurasānām // Lal_20.10 //
children.translated_text: hear but a portion [likened to] the arrays, sequences, and displays of those sons of the <s>Jinas</s>! // Lal_20.10 //

children.text: ke cāgatā nabhasi megha iva stananto hārā sahasranayutāni pralambayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came thundering in the sky like clouds, hanging down thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of necklaces;

children.text: ke cāgatā makuṭaratnavilambacūḍāḥ pauṣpaṃ vimāna gagane upadarśayantaḥ // Lal_20.11 //
children.translated_text: some came with crests of jewels dangling from their crowns, displaying floral palaces in the sky. // Lal_20.11 //

children.text: ke cāgatā dharaṇisiṃha ivā nadantaḥ śūnyānimittapraṇidhīravamuñcamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came roaring like lions on the earth, releasing the sounds of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;

children.text: ke cāgatā yatha vṛṣā abhinandamānāḥ na ca dṛṣṭapūrva rucirāṇi kṣipanti puṣpāṃ // Lal_20.12 //
children.translated_text: some came rejoicing like bulls, casting beautiful flowers never before seen. // Lal_20.12 //

children.text: ke cāgatā nabhasi sāra ivā ravanto varṇāsahasra svaki ātmani darśayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came resounding in the sky like <s>Sāras</s> [cranes], displaying a thousand colors in their own forms;

children.text: ke cāgatā śaśirivā gagane supūrṇāḥ sugatātmajasya guṇamālamudīrayantaḥ // Lal_20.13 //
children.translated_text: some came like the full moon in the sky, proclaiming garlands of the <s>Sugata</s>'s son's virtues. // Lal_20.13 //

children.text: ke cāgatā raviriva prabha muñcamānāḥ sarvāṇi mārabhavanāni karonti jihmā /
children.translated_text: Some came releasing radiance like the sun, making all of <s>Māra</s>'s abodes crooked;

children.text: ke cāgatā vimalaketu yathendrayaṣṭyaḥ saṃbhārapuṇyanicitāstahi bodhimaṇḍe // Lal_20.14 //
children.translated_text: some came like stainless banners, like <s>Indra</s>'s flagpoles, their accumulations of merit heaped at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. // Lal_20.14 //

children.text: kecitkṣipanti gaganānmaṇiratnajālā candrā sucandra tatha bāla virocamānā /
children.translated_text: Some cast from the sky nets of gem-jewels, moons, splendid moons, and shining crescents;

children.text: māndāravā sumanavārṣikacampadāmā saṃbodhisattva drumarājasthite kṣipanti // Lal_20.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, <s>Sumanā</s>, <s>Vārṣika</s>, and <s>Campaka</s> garlands — they cast them upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established at the king of trees. // Lal_20.15 //

children.text: ke cāgatā dharaṇi kampayamāna padbhyāṃ saṃkampitā vasudha prītikarī janasya /
children.translated_text: Some came causing the earth to tremble with their feet — the earth trembled, bringing joy to people;

children.text: ke cāgatā grahiya meru karetalebhiḥ utsṛṣṭapuṣpapuṭa saṃsthita antarīkṣe // Lal_20.16 //
children.translated_text: some came grasping <s>Meru</s> in the palms of their hands, casting flower-cups, standing in mid-air. // Lal_20.16 //

children.text: ke cāgatāścaturi sāgara gṛhya mūrdhnā utsṛṣṭa siñci vasudhāṃ varagandhatoyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came bearing the four oceans on their heads, casting and sprinkling the earth with finest scented water;

children.text: ke cāgatā ratanayaṣṭi gṛhītva citraṃ saṃbodhisattvamupadarśaya sthitva dūre // Lal_20.17 //
children.translated_text: some came holding variegated jeweled staffs, displaying them to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, standing at a distance. // Lal_20.17 //

children.text: ke cāgatā bhaviya brahma praśāntarūpāḥ śāntā praśāntamanasaḥ sthita dhyānadhyāyī /
children.translated_text: Some came in the form of <s>Brahmās</s>, of peaceful appearance, tranquil, of serene minds, standing in meditative absorption;

children.text: romebhi teṣa svaru niścarate manojña maitrīupekṣakaruṇāmuditāpramāṇā // Lal_20.18 //
children.translated_text: from their pores issued beautiful sounds — of boundless <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), and <s>muditā</s> (joy). // Lal_20.18 //

body.text: ke cāgatā maruta śakra ivā yathaiva devaiḥ sahasranayutaiśca purākṛtāste /
body.translated_text: Some came like <s>Śakra</s> among the <s>Maruts</s>, preceded by thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of gods;

body.text: upagamya bodhivaṭu gṛhya kṛtāñjalībhiḥ śakrābhilagna maṇiratna kṣipanti citrā // Lal_20.19 //
body.translated_text: approaching the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, holding palms joined, they cast variegated gem-jewels clinging to <s>Śakra</s> [in homage]. // Lal_20.19 //

children.text: ke cāgatāścatudiśā ca yathaiva pālā gandharvarākṣasaparīvṛta kinnarebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came like the guardians of the four directions, surrounded by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>;

children.text: vidyutsphuṭānta kusumāni pravarṣamāṇāḥ gandharvakinnararūtena stuvanti vīram // Lal_20.20 //
children.translated_text: raining flowers with lightning flashing, they praised the hero with the songs of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Kinnaras</s>. // Lal_20.20 //

children.text: ke cāgatāḥ kusumitāṃ pragṛhītva vṛkṣān saphalāṃ sapuṣpavaragandha pramuñcamānāṃ /
children.translated_text: Some came holding flowering trees, with fruits and flowers, releasing the finest fragrances;

children.text: jāteṣu teṣu sthita buddha śuddhakāyāḥ avalambamāna pratimaṇḍi kṣipanti puṣpā // Lal_20.21 //
children.translated_text: in those [trees] stood <s>Buddhas</s> of pure body, hanging down and adorning, casting flowers. // Lal_20.21 //

children.text: ke cāgatāḥ kusumitāḥ puḍinī gṛhītvā padmotpalaiḥ kusumitaistatha puṇḍarīkaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came holding flowering lotus-pools, blooming with lotuses, water-lilies, and white lotuses;

children.text: dvātriṃśalakṣaṇadharāḥ sthita padmagarbhe staviṣṭa aliptamanasaṃ vidu bodhisattvam // Lal_20.22 //
children.translated_text: bearing the thirty-two marks, standing in the lotus-wombs, they praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the wise one of unstained mind. // Lal_20.22 //

children.text: ke cāgatā vipulakāya tatheva meru sthitvāntarīkṣa svakamātmanamutsṛjanti /
children.translated_text: Some came with bodies vast as <s>Meru</s> itself, standing in mid-air they released their own forms;

children.text: utsṛjyamātra bhaviyā navapuṣpadāmāḥ saṃchādayanti trisahasri jinasya kṣetram // Lal_20.23 //
children.translated_text: the moment they were released, becoming fresh flower-garlands, they covered the trichiliocosm — the <s>Jina</s>'s field. // Lal_20.23 //

children.text: ke cāgatā ubhayacakṣuṣi kalpadāhaṃ saṃdarśayanta vibhavaṃ tatha saṃbhavaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Some came displaying in both eyes the <s>kalpa</s>-conflagration, and showing destruction and creation alike;

children.text: teṣāṃ śarīri bahudharmasukhā raṇanti tāṃ śrutva sattvanayutā prajahanti tṛṣṇām // Lal_20.24 //
children.translated_text: from their bodies resounded many <s>dharma</s>-joys, hearing which <s>nayutas</s> of beings abandoned craving. // Lal_20.24 //

children.text: ke cāgatā ravitakinnaratulyaghoṣāḥ bimboṣṭhacāruvadanāḥ paripūrṇavaktrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came with voices like the sound of <s>Kinnara</s>-birds, with lovely red lips, with full, beautiful faces;

children.text: kanyā yathaiva sualaṃkṛta citrahārāḥ prekṣanta yāṃ suragaṇā na labhanti tṛptim // Lal_20.25 //
children.translated_text: adorned like maidens with variegated necklaces — a sight at which even the hosts of gods could not find satisfaction. // Lal_20.25 //

body.text: ke cāgatā vajirakāya ivā abhedyāḥ heṣṭhā paskandhacaraṇaiḥ pratigrāhyamāṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: Some came with bodies impenetrable as <s>vajra</s>, received below on their shoulders and feet;

body.text: ke cāgatā ravirivā śaśipūrṇavaktrāḥ jyotsnākarāḥ prabhakarā hatakleśadoṣāḥ // Lal_20.26 //
body.translated_text: some came like the sun, with faces full as the moon, makers of radiance, light-makers, with afflictions and faults destroyed. // Lal_20.26 //

children.text: ke cāgatā ratanamaṇḍita ratnapāṇī saṃchādayitva bahukṣetrasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came with jewel-adorned hands, covering many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of fields;

children.text: varṣanti ratnavara puṣpa sugandhagandhā saṃtoṣaṇārthaṃ bahusattvahitaṃ sukhārtham // Lal_20.27 //
children.translated_text: they rained supreme jewels, flowers, and fine fragrances — for the satisfaction and welfare and happiness of many beings. // Lal_20.27 //

children.text: ke cāgatā mahati dhāraṇi ratnakośāḥ romebhi sūtranayutāni prabhāṣamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some came as great <s>dhāraṇī</s>-jewel-treasuries, from whose pores <s>nayutas</s> of <s>sūtras</s> were proclaimed;

children.text: pratibhānavanta mativanta subuddhivanto mattapramattajanatāṃ pratibodhayantaḥ // Lal_20.28 //
children.translated_text: eloquent, wise, of supreme understanding — awakening the intoxicated and heedless multitudes. // Lal_20.28 //

children.text: ke cāgatā grahiya bheri yathaiva meru ākoṭyamānu gagane sumanojñaghoṣām /
children.translated_text: Some came holding a drum like <s>Meru</s>, struck in the sky with a most beautiful sound;

children.text: yasyā ravaṃ daśadiśe vraji kṣetrakoṭyā adyāvaboddhumamataṃ anubuddhi śāstā // Lal_20.29 //
children.translated_text: its sound traversed <s>koṭīs</s> of fields in the ten directions — 'Today the Teacher shall awaken to the deathless, incomparable [truth]!' // Lal_20.29 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare bodhimaṇḍavyūhaparivarto nāma viṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus [ends] the twentieth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Array of the Seat of Awakening' (<s>Bodhimaṇḍavyūhaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 21
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 21.

body.text: māragharṣaṇaparivarta ekaviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Twenty-First Chapter: On the Defeat of <s>Māra</s> (<s>Māragharṣaṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvaiścema evaṃrūpā vyūhā bodhisattvasya pūjākarmaṇe bodhimaṇḍe 'bhisaṃkṛtā abhūvan / svayaṃ ca bodhisattvo yāvanto daśasu dikṣvatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāravyūhāstān sarvāṃstasmin bodhimaṇḍe saṃdarśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, these kinds of arrays were created by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the worship of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself displayed at that <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> all the arrays and ornamental arrangements of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍas</s> of all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — past, future, and present — in all the <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the ten directions. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇasya bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - iha khalu kāmadhātau māraḥ pāpīyānadhipatirīśvaro vaśavartī / naitanmama pratirūpaṃ bhavedyadahaṃ tenāvidito 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam / yannvahaṃ mārasya pāpīyasaḥ saṃcodanaṃ kuryām / tasmin vijite sarve kāmāvacarā devādayo nigṛhītā bhaviṣyanti / tataśca māraparṣadaḥ pūrvāvaropitakuśalamūlā mārakāyikā devaputrāste mama siṃhavikrīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayiṣyanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sat at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, this thought arose in him: 'Here in the desire realm, <s>Māra</s>, the evil one, is the sovereign lord, the ruler, the one who holds sway. It would not be fitting for me to fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening unknown to him. Let me rather provoke <s>Māra</s>, the evil one. When he is conquered, all the gods of the desire realm and the rest will be subdued. And from <s>Māra</s>'s own retinue, those <s>Mārakāyika</s> (belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s host) <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly planted roots of merit, upon seeing my lion-sport, will generate the mind of unsurpassed perfect awakening.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattva evamanuvicintya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhrūvivarāntarādūrṇākośāt sarvamāramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanakarīṃ nāmaikāṃ raśmimudasṛjat / yayā raśmyā sarvasmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau sarvamārabhavanānyavabhāsya jihmīkṛtāni saṃprakampitāni cābhūvan / sarvaścāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturmahatāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt / tasyāśca prabhāyā māraḥ pāpīyānidamevaṃ rūpaṃ śabdamaśrauṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having thus reflected, at that moment released from between his brows, from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (the circle of hair), a single ray of light called 'Destroyer of All <s>Māra</s>'s Hosts.' By that ray, all of <s>Māra</s>'s abodes in the entire trichiliocosm were illuminated, made crooked, and shaken. And this entire trichiliocosm was pervaded by a great radiance. And <s>Māra</s>, the evil one, heard from that radiance a sound of this kind:

body.text: kalpaughacīrṇacarito hyabhiśuddhasattvaḥ śuddhodanasya tanayaḥ pravijahya rājyam / so nirgato hitakaro hyamṛtābhilāṣī bodhidrumaṃ hyupagato 'dya kuru prayatnam // Lal_21.1 //
body.translated_text: He whose conduct has been practiced through floods of <s>kalpas</s>, of supremely pure being, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having abandoned the kingdom,

children.text: so tīrṇa ātmana parānapi tārayeyā moceṣyate sa ca parāṃ svayameva muktaḥ /
children.translated_text: he has gone forth, the beneficent one, longing for the deathless — having reached the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree today, make your effort! // Lal_21.1 //

children.text: āśvāsaprāpta sa parānapi cāśvaseyā nirvāpayiṣyati parāṃ parinirvṛtaśca // Lal_21.2 //
children.translated_text: He, having crossed over himself, will ferry others across too; he, himself freed, will liberate others;

children.text: śūnyāṃ kariṣyati āpāyatrayo 'pyaśeṣāṃ pūrṇāṃ kariṣyati purāṃ suramānuṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: he, having found reassurance, will reassure others too; himself having attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he will extinguish [the fires of suffering] in others. // Lal_21.2 //

children.text: dhyānānabhijña paramaṃ amṛtaṃ sukhaṃ ca dāsyatyasau hitakaro amṛtaṃ spṛśitvā // Lal_21.3 //
children.translated_text: He will empty the three lower realms completely; he will fill the cities of gods and humans;

body.text: śūnyaṃ kariṣyati puraṃ tava kṛṣṇabandho abalo balo balavihīnu apakṣyapakṣyo /
body.translated_text: <s>dhyānas</s>, superknowledges, the supreme deathless happiness — he, the beneficent one, will give, having touched the deathless! // Lal_21.3 //

body.text: na jñāsyase kva nu vrajāmi karomi kiṃ vā yada dharmavarṣamabhivarṣi svayaṃ svayaṃbhūḥ // Lal_21.4 //
body.translated_text: He will make your city empty, O friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (Darkness)! Powerless, you who [think yourself] powerful, bereft of strength, your faction diminished!

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: You will not know where to go or what to do when the Self-Arisen One himself rains the rain of <s>dharma</s>! // Lal_21.4 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo māraḥ pāpīyānābhiḥ saṃcodanābhirgāthābhiḥ saṃcoditaḥ san dvātriṃśadākāraṃ svapnamapaśyat / katamad dvātriṃśadākāram? tadyathā - tamasākulaṃ ca svabhavanamapaśyat / rajasākulaṃ cākīrṇaśarkarakaṭhalyaṃ ca svabhavanamapaśyat / bhītatrastodvignaṃ diśo daśa prapalāyamānaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / vibhraṣṭamakuṭamapaviddhakuṇḍalaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / śuṣkoṣṭhagalatālukaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / saṃtaptahṛdayaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / śīrṇapatrapuṣpaphalāni codyānānyapaśyat / apagatajalāḥ pariśuṣkāśca puṣkariṇīrapaśyat / haṃsakroñcamayūrakalaviṅkakuṇālajīvaṃjīvakādīṃśca pakṣigaṇātrchīrṇapakṣānapaśyat / bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgapaṭahatuṇavavīṇāvallakītāḍasampādīṃśca vādyabhāṇḍāṃśchinnavichinnān bhūmau nipatitānapaśyat / priyajanaparivārāśca māramutsṛjya dīnamukhā ekānte gatvā pradhyāyantamapaśyat / agramahiṣīṃ ca māriṇīṃ śayanabhraṣṭāṃ dharaṇyāmubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śīrṣamabhipīḍayantīmapaśyat / ye ca te māraputrā vīryavattamāśca balavattamāśca tejavattamāśca prajñāvattamāśca taṃ bodhisattvaṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ namasyanta evamapaśyat / ātmanīyāśca duhitrīrhā tāta hā tāteti krandantyo 'paśyat / malinacailagātraṃ cātmānamapaśyat / avakīrṇapāṃśuśiraskaṃ ca pāṇḍudurvarṇamojopahṛtaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / harmyakūṭāgāragavākṣatoraṇāṃśca rajasāvakīrṇān patato 'paśyat / ye cāsya te senāpatayo yakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍagandharvādhipatayaḥ, tān sarvān hastāñśirasi kṛtvā rodantaḥ krandantaḥ palāyamānāṃścāpaśyat / ye ca te kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu devādhipatayaḥ, tadyathā - dhṛtarāṣṭravirūḍhakavirūpākṣavaiśravaṇaśakrasuyāmasaṃtuṣitasunirmitavaśavartiprabhṛtayaḥ, tān sarvāñśuśruṣamāṇān māraḥ pāpīyān sabodhisattvābhimukhānapaśyat / raṇamadhye cāsyāsirvikośo na bhavati sma / vikrośantamaśivaṃ cātmānamapaśyat / svena ca parivāreṇātmānaṃ parityaktamapaśyat / maṅgalapūrṇakumbhāṃśca patitān dvāre 'paśyat / nāradaṃ ca brāhmaṇamamaṅgalyaśabdaṃ śrāvayantamapaśyat / ānanditaṃ ca dauvārikamanānandaśabdaṃ śrāvayantamapaśyat / tamasākulaṃ ca gaganatalamapaśyat / kāmabhavananivāsinīṃ ca śriyaṃ rudantīmapaśyat / svamaiśvaryaṃ cānaiśvaryamapaśyat / svapakṣaṃ cāpakṣamapaśyat / maṇimuktājālāni ca tūṣṇībhūtāni chinnabhinnapatitānyapaśyat / sarvaṃ ca mārabhavanaṃ pracalitamapaśyat / vṛkṣāñchidyamānānniryūhāṃśca patato 'drākṣīt / sarvaṃ ca mārasenāvyūhamabhimukhaṃ pātyamānamapaśyat //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, urged by these exhortatory verses, beheld a dream of thirty-two aspects. What were the thirty-two aspects? He saw his own abode filled with darkness. He saw his own abode filled with dust, strewn with pebbles and gravel. He saw himself frightened, terrified, agitated, fleeing in all ten directions. He saw himself with his crown fallen and his earrings cast off. He saw himself with dried-up lips, throat, and palate. He saw himself with a scorched heart. He saw the gardens with their leaves, flowers, and fruits withered. He saw the lotus-ponds with their water gone, dried up. He saw the flocks of birds — swans, herons, peacocks, <s>kalaviṅkas</s>, <s>kuṇālas</s>, <s>jīvaṃjīvakas</s>, and others — with broken wings. He saw the musical instruments — drums, conches, kettledrums, tabors, flutes, <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>vallakīs</s>, hand-cymbals, and clappers — broken and shattered, fallen upon the ground. He saw the company of dear ones abandoning <s>Māra</s> and going aside with dejected faces, sitting in brooding meditation. He saw his chief queen <s>Māriṇī</s>, fallen from the bed, pressing her head with both hands upon the ground. He saw those sons of <s>Māra</s> who were the most vigorous, the most powerful, the most splendid, and the most wise — bowing to that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who had reached the supreme seat of awakening. He saw his own daughters crying: 'Alas, father! Alas, father!' He saw himself with soiled garments and body. He saw himself with head covered in dust, pallid, discolored, with vitality drained away. He saw the pavilions, palaces, lattice-windows, and arched gateways covered with dust, falling. He saw all his generals — lords of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> — with hands placed on their heads, weeping, crying, and fleeing. He saw all the lords of the gods in the Desire Realm — namely, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, <s>Sunirmita</s>, <s>Vaśavartin</s>, and others — all facing toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in devoted service. He saw that in the midst of battle, his sword would not come out of its scabbard. He saw himself crying out inauspicious sounds. He saw himself abandoned by his own retinue. He saw the auspicious full pitchers fallen at the gate. He saw a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Nārada</s> proclaiming inauspicious words. He saw the doorkeeper <s>Ānandita</s> proclaiming words of non-joy. He saw the sky filled with darkness. He saw <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), who dwelt in the pleasure-palace, weeping. He saw his own sovereignty become non-sovereignty. He saw his own partisans become non-partisans. He saw the nets of gems and pearls fallen silent, broken, shattered, and fallen. He saw his entire abode trembling. He saw trees being cut down and pinnacles falling. He saw his entire army-array being toppled face-forward. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣava evaṃ dvātriṃśadākāraṃ māraḥ pāpīyān svapnamapaśyat / sa pratibuddhaḥ san bhītastrastaḥ saṃvignaḥ sarvamantarjanaṃ saṃnipātya sabalapārṣadyasenāpatidauvārikasaṃnipatitāṃśca tān viditvā ābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One beheld this dream of thirty-two aspects. Having awakened, frightened, terrified, and agitated, he assembled all his inner people. And knowing that his troops, retinue, generals, and doorkeepers had assembled, he addressed them with these verses —

children.text: dṛṣṭvāna tāṃ sa supināṃ namucī dukhārto āmantrayāti suta ye 'pi ca pāriṣadyā /
children.translated_text: Having seen those dreams, <s>Namuci</s>, greatly distressed, addresses his sons and his courtiers:

children.text: senāpatiṃ namuci siṃhahanuśca nāmnā sarveṣa teṣa paripṛcchati kṛṣṇabandhuḥ // Lal_21.5 //
children.translated_text: the general named <s>Siṃhahanu</s> — of all of them the kinsman of darkness inquires. // Lal_21.5 //

children.text: gāthābhi gītaracito 'dya śruto 'ntarīkṣācchākyeṣu jātu varalakṣaṇacitritāṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Today verses composed in song have been heard from the sky: "Born among the <s>Śākyas</s>, his limbs adorned with the excellent marks,

children.text: ṣaḍvarṣa duṣkaravratāni caritva ghorā bodhidrumaṃ hyupagataḥ prakuruṣva yatnam // Lal_21.6 //
children.translated_text: having practiced dreadful difficult austerities for six years, he has approached the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree — make your effort!"' // Lal_21.6 //

children.text: so cedvibuddha svayameva hi bodhisattvo bahusattvakoṭinayutāni vibodhayeta /
children.translated_text: 'If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> awakens by himself, he will awaken many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of beings;

children.text: śūnyaṃ kariṣyati sa me bhavanaṃ hyaśeṣaṃ yada lapsyate hyamṛtu sparśanaśītibhāvam // Lal_21.7 //
children.translated_text: he will make my abode entirely empty, when he attains the touch of the deathless, the state of peace.' // Lal_21.7 //

children.text: hanta vrajāma sahitā mahatā balena ghātema taṃ śramaṇu eku drumendramūle /
children.translated_text: 'Come, let us go together with a great force! Let us slay that <s>Śramaṇa</s>, alone at the root of the king of trees!

children.text: udyojayadhva caturaṅgiṇi śīghra senāṃ yadi icchathā mama priyaṃ ma ciraṃ karotha // Lal_21.8 //
children.translated_text: Muster the fourfold army quickly — if you desire what is dear to me, do not delay!' // Lal_21.8 //

children.text: pratyekabuddhabhi ca arhabhiḥ pūrṇa loko nirvāyamāṇu na balaṃ mama durbalaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: 'Even when the world was filled with <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Arhats</s>, my power did not become feeble, and was not weakened;

children.text: so bhūyu eku jinu bheṣyati dharmarājo gaṇanātivṛttu jinavaṃśu na jātu chidyet // Lal_21.9 //
children.translated_text: but this one shall become a single <s>Jina</s>, a <s>Dharma</s>-king — [his] lineage of victors, surpassing count, shall never be cut off!' // Lal_21.9 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sārthavāho nāma māraputraḥ, sa māraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, a son of <s>Māra</s> named <s>Sārthavāha</s> addressed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One in verses —

children.text: kiṃ tāt bhinnavadano 'si vivarṇavaktro hṛdayaṃ samutplavati vedhati te 'ṅgamaṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Why, father, is your face broken, your countenance discolored? Your heart leaps up, your every limb trembles.

children.text: kiṃ te śrutaṃ athava dṛṣṭu bhaṇāhi śīghraṃ jñāsyāma tattvatu vicintya tathā prayogam // Lal_21.10 //
children.translated_text: What have you heard or seen? Speak quickly! We shall know the truth and, having reflected, [devise] the right course of action.' // Lal_21.10 //

children.text: nirmāṇu māru avacī śṛṇu mahya vatsa pāpaṃ mi dṛṣṭu supinaṃ paramaṃ sughoram /
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> the creator said: 'Hear, my son — I have seen an evil dream, supremely terrible;

children.text: bhāṣeya sarvamiha parṣadi adya śeṣaṃ saṃmūrchitā kṣititale prapateyu yūyam // Lal_21.11 //
children.translated_text: were I to relate all of it here in the assembly now, you would all faint and fall to the ground!' // Lal_21.11 //

body.text: sārthavāha āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Sārthavāha</s> said —

children.text: raṇakāli prāpti yadi nāma jayo na doṣaḥ tatraiva yastu nihato bhavate sa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If, having arrived at the time of battle, there is victory, that is no fault; the fault lies in being slain there.

children.text: svapnāntare tu yadi īdṛśa te nimittā śreyo upekṣa ma raṇe paribhāvu gacchet // Lal_21.12 //
children.translated_text: But if in a dream such omens [appear] for you, it is better to desist — lest you meet with humiliation in battle!' // Lal_21.12 //

body.text: māro 'bravīt -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said —

children.text: vyavasāyabuddhi puruṣasya raṇe prasiddhi avalambya dhairya sukṛtaṃ yadi no jayaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: 'When a man has the determination and courage [to fight], his fame in battle is established; relying on firmness — [even] if there is no victory, meritorious [is the effort].

children.text: kā tasya śakti mama dṛṣṭi sapāriṣadyaṃ notthātu mahya caraṇe śirasā prapattum // Lal_21.13 //
children.translated_text: Who has the power, in my sight, together with my retinue, not to rise and fall at my feet with [their] head?' // Lal_21.13 //

body.text: sārthavāha āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Sārthavāha</s> said —

children.text: vistīrṇamasti hi balaṃ ca sudurbalaṃ ca astyeka śūru balavāṃśca raṇaṃjahaśca /
children.translated_text: 'There is a vast army, and there is also a very feeble one; there is one who is a hero, powerful, and also one who abandons the battle.

children.text: khadyotakairyadi bhavettrisahasra pūrṇā eko ravirgrasati niṣprabhatāṃ karoti // Lal_21.14 //
children.translated_text: Even if the trichiliocosm were filled with fireflies, a single sun swallows them and makes them lightless. // Lal_21.14 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yasya mānaśca mohaśca mīmāṃsā ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'One in whom there is no pride, no delusion, and no doubt —

children.text: viloma yadi vidvāṃso nāsau śakyaścikitsitum // Lal_21.15 //
children.translated_text: if wise ones [go] against him, he cannot be treated [i.e. defeated].' // Lal_21.15 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo māraḥ pāpīyān sārthavāhasya vacanamakṛtvā mahatīṃ caturaṅginīṃ senāmudyojayati sma mahābalaraṇaśauṇḍāṃ bhīṣaṇāṃ romaharṣaṇīmadṛṣṭāśrutapūrvāṃ devamanuṣyairbahuvidhamukhavikārakoṭinayutaśatasahasravikāraprakārāṃ bhujagaśatasahasrakaracaraṇakuṭilapariveṣṭitaśarīrāṃ asidhanuśaraśaktitomarakuṭhārapaṭṭisabhuśuṇḍimusaladaṇḍapāśagadācakravajrakaṇayadharāṃ varavarmakavacavarmitaśarīrāṃ viparītaśiraḥkaracaraṇanayanāṃ jvalitaśironayanavadanāṃ duḥsaṃsthitodarapāṇipādamugratejovadanāṃ paramavikṛtavadanadarśanāṃ vikarālavikṛtadaṃṣṭrāṃ ghanabahuvipulapralambajihvāṃ suṇḍikakiliñjasadṛśajihvāṃ jvalanasadṛśakṛṣṇasarpaviṣapūrṇaraktanetrām / keciddhi tatrāśīviṣān vamanti sma / kecitkaratalairāśīviṣān parigṛhya bhakṣayanti sma / garuḍā iva sāgarādabhyutkṣipya kecinnaramāṃsarudhirakaracaraṇaśiroyakṛdantrapurīṣādīṃśca bhakṣayanti sma / kecijjvalitapiṅgalakṛṣṇanīlaraktakadrukarālavicitrarūpāḥ / kecidvikṛtakūpaprajvalitotpāṭitavikṛtakaṭākṣāḥ / kecitparivṛttajvalitavikṛtanayanāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, disregarding the words of <s>Sārthavāha</s>, mustered a great fourfold army — mighty in strength, fierce in battle, terrifying, hair-raising, never before seen or heard of by gods or humans — with <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of various kinds of facial transformations; with bodies entwined by hundreds of thousands of serpents [as] hands and feet; bearing swords, bows, arrows, spears, lances, axes, <s>paṭṭisas</s>, <s>bhuśuṇḍīs</s>, clubs, staffs, nooses, maces, wheels, and thunderbolts; with bodies armored in excellent armor and mail; with heads, hands, feet, and eyes reversed; with heads, eyes, and mouths ablaze; with bellies, hands, and feet grotesquely formed, and faces of fierce splendor; of supremely distorted and hideous appearance; with fearsome, deformed fangs; with thick, vast, and hanging tongues; with tongues like the trunks of elephants or like reeds; with blazing red eyes filled with the venom of black serpents. Some there vomited venomous serpents. Some seized venomous serpents in their palms and devoured them. Like <s>Garuḍas</s> snatching from the ocean, some devoured human flesh, blood, hands, feet, heads, livers, entrails, and excrement. Some were of blazing tawny, black, blue, red, brown, terrifying, and variegated forms. Some had distorted, blazing, gouged-out, deformed, squinting eyes. Some had rolling, blazing, distorted eyes.

body.text: kecijjvalitān parvatān parigṛhya salīlamapareṣu parvateṣu abhirūḍhā āgacchanti sma / kecitsamūlān vṛkṣānutpāṭya bodhisattvābhimukhā abhidhāvanti sma / kecidajakaṇaśūrpakarṇahastikarṇalambakarṇavarāhakarṇāḥ / kecid vṛkakarṇāḥ / keciddakodariṇo durbalakāyā asthikaṅkālasaṃghāṭamabhinirmāya bhagnanāsāḥ kumbhodarāḥ karoṭapādā ucchuṣkatvagmāṃsarudhirāḥ chinnakarṇanāsākaracaraṇanayanottamāṅgāḥ / kecidrudhirapipāsayā śirāṃsi parasparaṃ nikṛntanti sma / keciddhrinnavikṛtabhairavarūkṣasvarāḥ phutphutkārapicutkāraphuluphuluprakṣveḍitāni kurvanti sma / kecidāhuḥ - āharata haratābhihanata hanata bandhata gṛhṇata chindata bhindata mathayatotkṣipata nāśayatemaṃ śramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ sārdhaṃ drameṇeti bruvanti sma / kecidbheruṇḍakaśṛgālasūkaragardabhagohastyaśvoṣṭrakharamahiṣaśaśacamarakhaḍgaśarabhanānāpratibha - yaraudravikṛtavaktrāḥ / kecitsiṃhavyāghraṛkṣavarāhavānaradvīpibiḍālachāgalorabhrasarpanakulamatsyamakaraśiśumārakūrmakāka - gṛghrolūkagaruḍādisadṛśātmabhāvāḥ / kecidvirūparūpāḥ / kecidekaśīrṣā dviśīrṣā yāvacchatasahasraśīrṣāḥ / kecidaśīrṣāḥ / kecidekabhujā yāvacchatasahasrabhujāḥ / kecidabhujāḥ / kecidekapādakāḥ / kecidyāvacchatasahasrapādāḥ / kecidapādakāḥ / kecitkarṇamukhanāsikākṣinābhisrotobhirāśīviṣānniścārayanti sma / kecidasidhanuśaraśaktipaṭṭiśaparaśucakratomarakaṇayavajrabhuśuṇḍibhindipālādīni nānāpraharaṇāni bhrāmayanto nṛtyanto bodhisattvaṃ saṃtarjayanti sma / kecinnarāṅgulīśchitvā mālāguṇān kṛtvā dhārayanti sma / kecicchirobhirasthikarakāñchīrṣakaṭāhakāṃśca mālāguṇamiva kṛtvā dhārayanti sma / kecidāśiviṣapariveṣṭitaśarīrāḥ / kecicchīrṣakaṭāhakān parigṛhya hastyaśvoṣṭragogardabhamahiṣārūḍhāḥ / kecidadhaḥśirasa ūrdhvapādāḥ / kecitsūcīromāṇaḥ / kecidgogardabhavarāhanakulachāgalorabhrabiḍālakapivṛkaśṛgālaromāṇaḥ āśīviṣān vamanto 'yoguḍāni nirgaranto dhūmaketūnutsṛjanto jvalitatāmralohavarṣaṃ pravarṣanto vidyudvarṣān kṣipanto vajrāśaniṃ pramuñcantastaptāmayovālikāṃ pravarṣantaḥ kālameghān saṃjanayanto vātavṛṣṭimutpādayantaḥ śarameghavarṣānutsṛjantaḥ kālarātriṃ darśayanto rāvaṃ saṃjanayanto bodhisattvamabhidhāvanti sma / kecitpāśān bhrāmayanto mahāparvatān prapātayanto mahāsāgarān kṣobhayanto laṅghayanto mahāparvatāṃścālayanto meruṃ parvatarājaṃ vidhāvantaḥ palāyamānā vikṣipanto 'ṅgapratyaṅgāni bhrāmayantaḥ śarīrāṇi hasanto mahāhāsyāni urāṃsi prasphoṭayantaḥ urāṃsi tāḍayantaḥ keśāṃsi dhunvantaḥ pītamukhāni ca nīlaśarīrā jvalitaśirasa ūrdhvakeśā itastato vegena paridhāvanto bherūṇḍākṣāśca bodhisattvaṃ vibhīṣayanti sma / jīrṇāḥ striyaśca rudantyo bodhisattvamupasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadanti sma - aho putra, hā mama putra, uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha, śīghraṃ prapalāyasva / rākṣasarūpāḥ piśācarūpāḥ kāṇakhañjadurbalāśca pretāḥ kṣutkṣāmākṣā urdhvabāhavo vikṛtāsyāḥ krandanto bhayamupadarśayantastrāsaṃ saṃjanayanto bodhisattvasya purato 'bhidhāvanti sma / tayā caivarūpayā mārasenayā samuditayā samantādaśītiryojanānyāyāmena vistāreṇa sphuṭamabhūt / yathā caikasya mārasyaivaṃ koṭīśatānāṃ trisāhasraparyāpannānāṃ mārāṇāṃ pāpīyasāṃ senābhistiryagūrdhvaṃ ca parisphuṭamabhūt //
body.translated_text: some, seizing blazing mountains, playfully mounted upon other mountains and came; some, uprooting trees with their roots, rushed toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; some had goat-ears, <s>śūrpa</s>-ears, elephant-ears, drooping ears, pig-ears; some had wolf-ears; some had swollen bellies and feeble bodies, having created [forms like] skeleton-assemblages — with broken noses, pot-bellied, with bowl-shaped feet, with dried-up skin, flesh, and blood, with severed ears, noses, hands, feet, eyes, and heads; some, thirsting for blood, were cutting off each other's heads; some, with split, distorted, terrible, harsh voices, made sounds — 'phut-phut,' 'picut-picut,' 'phulu-phulu,' and snapping of fingers; some said: 'Bring [him]! Seize [him]! Strike! Kill! Bind! Grab! Cut! Split! Crush! Hurl! Destroy this <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s> together with his tree!' Some had faces resembling those of <s>bheruṇḍas</s>, jackals, pigs, donkeys, cows, elephants, horses, camels, mules, buffaloes, hares, <s>camaras</s>, rhinoceroses, <s>śarabhas</s>, and various other [creatures] — terrible, ferocious, distorted faces; some had bodies resembling lions, tigers, bears, boars, monkeys, leopards, cats, goats, sheep, serpents, mongooses, fish, <s>makaras</s>, <s>śiśumāras</s> (dolphins), tortoises, crows, vultures, owls, <s>Garuḍas</s>, and the like; some were of deformed appearance; some had one head, two heads, up to a hundred thousand heads; some were headless; some had one arm, up to a hundred thousand arms; some were armless; some had one foot, up to a hundred thousand feet; some were footless; some emitted deadly serpents from their ears, mouths, noses, eyes, and navel-openings; some, brandishing swords, bows, arrows, spears, <s>paṭṭiśas</s>, axes, discuses, lances, clubs, <s>vajras</s>, clubs, and <s>bhindipālas</s> and various weapons, dancing, threatened the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; some, cutting off human fingers, made them into garland-strings and wore them; some, making garland-strings of heads, bones, and skull-bowls, wore them; some had bodies encircled by deadly serpents; some, holding skull-bowls, were mounted on elephants, horses, camels, cows, donkeys, and buffaloes; some were head-downward with feet upward; some had needle-hairs; some had the fur of cows, donkeys, boars, mongooses, cats, sheep, cats, monkeys, wolves, and jackals; vomiting deadly serpents, belching iron balls, emitting fire-meteors, raining down blazing molten copper, hurling lightning-rains, releasing <s>vajra</s>-thunderbolts, raining hot iron sand, generating black storm-clouds, producing wind-and-rain, releasing cloud-showers of arrows, displaying the night of destruction, creating roars — they rushed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; some, whirling lassos, toppling great mountains, churning the great oceans, leaping over and shaking great mountains, running at <s>Meru</s> the king of mountains, fleeing and hurling, whirling their limbs and bodies, laughing great laughs, striking their chests, beating their breasts, shaking their hair — with yellow faces, blue bodies, blazing heads, hair standing upward — running about in every direction with great speed, with terrible eyes, they sought to terrify the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And aged women, weeping, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and said thus: 'O son! Alas, my son! Rise up! Rise up! Flee quickly!' <s>Rākṣasa</s>-formed, <s>Piśāca</s>-formed, one-eyed, lame, feeble, and <s>preta</s>-like — emaciated, with hollow eyes, arms raised, with distorted mouths — screaming, displaying terror, generating fright, they rushed before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And with <s>Māra</s>'s army thus assembled, it was spread out eighty <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth on all sides. And just as one <s>Māra</s> [had such an army], so did hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of evil <s>Māras</s> belonging to the trichiliocosm — their armies were spread out sideways and upward.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: yakṣakumbhāṇḍamahoragarūpāḥ rākṣasapretapiśācakarūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the forms of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s> —

children.text: yattaka loki virūpa suraudrāḥ sarvi ta nirmita tatra śaṭhebhiḥ // Lal_21.16 //
children.translated_text: whatever deformed and fierce [beings] exist in the world — all were created there by those deceivers! // Lal_21.16 //

children.text: ekaśirā dviśirā triśirāśca yāvatsahasraśirā bahuvaktrāḥ /
children.translated_text: One-headed, two-headed, three-headed, up to thousand-headed, many-faced;

children.text: ekabhujā dvibhujā tribhujāśca yāvatsahasrabhujā bahubhujāḥ /
children.translated_text: one-armed, two-armed, three-armed, up to thousand-armed, many-armed;

children.text: ekapadā dvipadā tripadāśca yāvatsahasrapadā bahu anye // Lal_21.17 //
children.translated_text: one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, up to thousand-footed — and many others! // Lal_21.17 //

children.text: nīlamukhāni ca pītaśarīrā pītamukhāni ca nīlaśarīrā /
children.translated_text: Blue-faced with yellow bodies, yellow-faced with blue bodies,

children.text: anyamukhāni ca anyaśarīrāḥ ekamupāgatu kiṃkarasainyam // Lal_21.18 //
children.translated_text: of different faces and different bodies — together they came as one servant-army! // Lal_21.18 //

children.text: vātu pravāyati varṣati varṣaṃ vidyusahasraśatāni patanti /
children.translated_text: Wind blows, rain pours down, hundreds of thousands of lightning-bolts fall;

children.text: deva guḍāyati vṛkṣa luḍanti bodhivaṭasya na īryati patram // Lal_21.19 //
children.translated_text: the sky is shrouded, trees are uprooted — yet not a leaf of the <s>Bodhi</s> fig-tree stirs! // Lal_21.19 //

children.text: varṣati deva pravarṣati varṣaṃ ogha vahanti jalākulabhūmim /
children.translated_text: The sky rains, downpour upon downpour, floods carry away the water-deluged earth;

children.text: īdṛśa bhīṣaṇikā bahurāśī yatra acetana vṛkṣa patanti // Lal_21.20 //
children.translated_text: such terrifying [forces come] in great masses — [storms] by which even insensible trees fall! // Lal_21.20 //

children.text: dṛṣṭva ca tānatibhīṣaṇarūpāṃ sarvi visaṃsthita rūpavirūpāṃ /
children.translated_text: Seeing those exceedingly terrifying forms — all disordered, [both] form and formless —

children.text: śrīguṇalakṣaṇatejadharasyā cittu na kampati meru yathaiva // Lal_21.21 //
children.translated_text: the mind of him who bears glory, virtue, marks, and splendor does not tremble — just as <s>Meru</s> [does not tremble]! // Lal_21.21 //

children.text: māyasamāṃstatha svapnasamāṃśca abhranibhāṃ samudīkṣati dharmāṃ /
children.translated_text: He perceives all phenomena as like illusions, like dreams, like clouds;

children.text: īdṛśa dharmanayaṃ vimṛṣanto susthitu dhyāyati saṃsthitu dharme // Lal_21.22 //
children.translated_text: reflecting thus on the nature of <s>Dharma</s>, well-established, he meditates, established in <s>Dharma</s>. // Lal_21.22 //

children.text: yasya bhaveta ahaṃ ti mameti bhāva samucchrayi tattvaniviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: He who has the notion of 'I' and 'mine,' established in the arising of entities and fixed in [false] essence —

children.text: so bibhiyādabuddheḥ sthitu grāhe ātmani saṃbhrami gaccha nirīkṣya // Lal_21.23 //
children.translated_text: he would fear, standing in the grasp of non-awakening, confused about the self — seeing [this], go [away]! // Lal_21.23 //

children.text: śākyasutastu svabhāvamabhāvaṃ dharma pratītya samutthita buddhā /
children.translated_text: But the son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, awakened to the naturelessness and non-existence of phenomena, arisen through dependent origination —

children.text: gaganopamacittu suyukto na bhramate sabalaṃ śaḍha dṛṣṭvā // Lal_21.24 //
children.translated_text: with a mind like space, well-concentrated — he is not confused upon seeing the deceitful one with his army! // Lal_21.24 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo mārasya pāpīyasaḥ putrasahasram / tatra ye māraputrā bodhisattve 'bhiprasannāḥ sārthavāhapūrvaṃgamāḥ, te mārasya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthitā abhūvan / ye mārapākṣikāḥ, te vāme pārśve sthitā abhuvan mārasya pāpīyasaḥ / tatra māraḥ pāpīyāṃstān svān putrānāmantrayate sma - kīdṛśena balena vayaṃ bodhisattvaṃ dharṣayiṣyāmaḥ? tatra dakṣiṇe pārśve sārthavāho nāma māraputraḥ / sa pitaraṃ gāthayā pratyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, <s>Māra</s> Pāpīyas had a thousand sons. Among them, those sons of <s>Māra</s> who were well-disposed toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, led by <s>Sārthavāha</s>, stood on <s>Māra</s>'s right side. Those who were on <s>Māra</s>'s side stood on the left side of <s>Māra</s> Pāpīyas. There, <s>Māra</s> Pāpīyas addressed his sons: 'With what kind of force shall we overcome the <s>Bodhisattva</s>?' Then on the right side, a son of <s>Māra</s> named <s>Sārthavāha</s> replied to his father in verse:

children.text: suptaṃ prabodhayitumicchati pannagendraṃ suptaṃ prabodhayitumicchati yo gajendram /
children.translated_text: 'He who wishes to awaken a sleeping lord of serpents; he who wishes to awaken a sleeping lord of elephants;

children.text: suptaṃ prabodhayitumicchati yo mṛgendraṃ suptaṃ prabodhayitumicchati so narendram // Lal_21.25 //
children.translated_text: he who wishes to awaken a sleeping lord of beasts [lions] — he [is one who] wishes to awaken a sleeping lord of men!' // Lal_21.25 //

body.text: vāme pārśve durmatirnāma māraputraḥ sa evamāha -
body.translated_text: On the left side, a son of <s>Māra</s> named <s>Durmati</s> (Evil-minded) said thus:

children.text: saṃprekṣaṇena hṛdayānyabhisaṃsphuṭanti lokeṣu sāra mahatāmapi pādapānām /
children.translated_text: 'By [my] gaze, the heartwood of even great trees in the world splits asunder!

children.text: kā śaktirasti mama dṛṣṭihatasya tasya saṃjīvituṃ jagati mṛtyuhatasya vāstu // Lal_21.26 //
children.translated_text: What power does he have who has been struck by [my] gaze to survive in the world — like one struck by death!' // Lal_21.26 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe madhuranirghoṣo nāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, [one] named <s>Madhuranirghoṣa</s> (Sweet-voiced) said:

children.text: vṛkṣeṣu sāra ka ihāsti tato bravīṣi dṛṣṭvā bhinanmi manujeṣvatha kā avasthā /
children.translated_text: 'What heartwood is there in trees? Yet you say: "Seeing [them], I split!" What then is the condition among men?

children.text: meruṃ giriṃ yadi bhinatsi nirīkṣaṇena naivāsya tubhya nayanebhi hatonmiṣeran // Lal_21.27 //
children.translated_text: If you could split even <s>Meru</s> mountain by your gaze — even so, by your eyes, his would not so much as blink!' // Lal_21.27 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: yaḥ sāgaraṃ taritumicchati vai bhujābhyāṃ toyaṃ ca tasya pibituṃ manujeṣvasantu /
children.translated_text: 'If someone wished to cross the ocean with his arms alone, and to drink its water — among humans, let it be;

children.text: śakyaṃ bhavedidamatastu vadāmi duḥkhaṃ yastasya vaktramabhito 'pyamalaṃ nirīkṣet // Lal_21.28 //
children.translated_text: that might be possible — but this I say is harder: to gaze upon his stainless face and [still prevail]!' // Lal_21.28 //

body.text: vāme śatabāhurnāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, [one] named <s>Śatabāhu</s> (Hundred-armed) said:

children.text: mameha dehesmi śataṃ bhujānāṃ kṣipāmi caikena śataṃ śarāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'I have a hundred arms on this body of mine; with each one I hurl a hundred arrows!

children.text: bhinanmi kāyaṃ śramaṇasya tāta sukhī bhava tvaṃ vraja mā vilamba // Lal_21.29 //
children.translated_text: I shall split the body of the <s>Śramaṇa</s>, father! Be happy — go [forth]! Do not delay!' // Lal_21.29 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe subuddhirāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Subuddhi</s> (Good-minded) said:

children.text: śataṃ bhujānāṃ yadi ko viśeṣo bhujā kimarthaṃ na bhavanti romāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If you have a hundred arms, what distinction is that? Why are not the arms like mere hairs?

children.text: bhujaikamekena tathaiva śūlāḥ taiścāpi kuryānna hi tasya kiṃcit // Lal_21.30 //
children.translated_text: Even if arms were each a trident — even with those, you could do nothing to him! // Lal_21.30 //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇam?
body.translated_text: Why?

children.text: maitrāvatastasya muneḥ śarīre viṣaṃ na śastraṃ kramate na cāgniḥ /
children.translated_text: 'On the body of that sage, endowed with loving-kindness — neither poison penetrates, nor weapons, nor fire;

children.text: kṣiptāni śastrāṇi vrajanti puṣpatāṃ maitrī hi lokottarabhāvi tasya // Lal_21.31 //
children.translated_text: weapons hurled [at him] become flowers — for his loving-kindness is supramundane in nature!' // Lal_21.31 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: divi bhuvi ca jale ca ye balāḍhyāḥ asiparaśugharāśca guhyakā narā vā /
children.translated_text: 'Those in heaven, on earth, and in water who are mighty — <s>Guhyakas</s> bearing swords and axes, or men —

children.text: kṣamabalamimu prāpya te narendraṃ prabalabalālpabalā bhavanti sarve // Lal_21.32 //
children.translated_text: having encountered the power of patience of this lord of men, the very powerful all become weak!' // Lal_21.32 //

body.text: vāme ugratejā āha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Ugratejā</s> (Fierce-splendor) said:

children.text: antargato 'haṃ dhakṣyāmi praviśyāsya tanuṃ śubhām /
children.translated_text: 'Entering inside, I shall burn his beautiful body,

children.text: vṛkṣaṃ sakoṭaraṃ śuṣkaṃ dāvāgniriva sūkṣmataḥ // Lal_21.33 //
children.translated_text: as a forest fire [burns] a dry, hollow tree — subtly!' // Lal_21.33 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe sunetra āha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Sunetra</s> (Good-eyed) said:

children.text: meruṃ dahestvaṃ yadi vāpi kṛtsnaṃ praviśya cāntargatu medinīṃ vā /
children.translated_text: 'Even if you could burn all of <s>Meru</s>, or enter inside the earth and [burn it] —

children.text: dagdhuṃ na śakyaḥ sa hi vajrabuddhiḥ tvatsaṃnibhairvālikagaṅgatulyaiḥ // Lal_21.34 //
children.translated_text: he whose mind is [like] diamond cannot be burned — not by ones like you, [even if] equal to the sands of the Ganges!' // Lal_21.34 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: caleyurgirayaḥ sarve kṣayaṃ gacchenmahodadhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'All mountains may tremble; the great ocean may reach destruction;

children.text: candrasūryau patedbhūmau mahī ca vilayaṃ vrajet // Lal_21.35 //
children.translated_text: moon and sun may fall to earth, and the earth itself may dissolve —

children.text: lokasyārthe kṛtārambhaḥ pratijñākṛtaniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: but this one, who has set out for the sake of the world, whose resolve is firm in his vow,

children.text: aprāpyaiṣa varāṃ bodhiṃ notthāsyati mahādrumāt // Lal_21.36 //
children.translated_text: without attaining the supreme <s>Bodhi</s>, shall not rise from the great tree!' // Lal_21.35-36 //

body.text: vāme dīrghabāhurgarvita āha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Dīrghabāhu</s> (Long-armed), arrogant, said:

children.text: ālayaṃ candrasūryāṇāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The abode of moon, sun, and all the stars —

children.text: pāṇināhaṃ pramardāmi taveha bhavane sthitaḥ // Lal_21.37 //
children.translated_text: I shall crush them with my hand, standing in your domain! // Lal_21.37 //

children.text: caturbhyaḥ sāgarebhyaśca jalaṃ gṛhṇāmi līlayā /
children.translated_text: From the four oceans I shall playfully take the water;

children.text: taṃ gṛhya śramaṇaṃ tāta sāgarasya paraṃ kṣipe // Lal_21.38 //
children.translated_text: seizing that <s>Śramaṇa</s>, father, I shall hurl him beyond the ocean! // Lal_21.38 //

children.text: tiṣṭhatāṃ tāta seneyaṃ mā tvaṃ śokārdito bhava /
children.translated_text: Let this army stand, father! Do not be afflicted by grief!

children.text: sabodhivṛkṣamutpāṭya kṣepsye pāṇyā diśo daśa // Lal_21.39 //
children.translated_text: I shall uproot the <s>Bodhi</s> tree and hurl it with my hand in the ten directions!' // Lal_21.39 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe prasādapratilabdha āha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Prasādapratilabdha</s> (One who has gained faith) said:

children.text: sadevāsuragandharvāṃ sasāgaranagāṃ mahīm /
children.translated_text: 'The earth with its gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, its oceans and mountains —

children.text: tvaṃ marditāṃ prakuryāśca pāṇibhyāṃ madagarvitaḥ // Lal_21.40 //
children.translated_text: you might crush it with your hands, intoxicated with pride; // Lal_21.40 //

children.text: tvadvidhānāṃ sahasrāṇi gaṅgāvālikayā samāḥ /
children.translated_text: but thousands like you, equal to the sands of the Ganges,

children.text: romaṃ tasya na cāleyurbodhisattvasya dhīmataḥ // Lal_21.41 //
children.translated_text: could not move a single hair of the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>!' // Lal_21.41 //

body.text: vāme bhayaṃkara āha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Bhayaṃkara</s> (Terror-maker) said:

children.text: bhayaṃ hi te tāta bhṛśaṃ kimarthaṃ senāya madhye kimavasthitasya /
children.translated_text: 'Why, father, is your fear so great? What [troubles you] standing in the midst of your army?

children.text: senā na tasyāsti kutaḥ sahāyāḥ kasmādbhayaṃ te bhavatīha tasmāt // Lal_21.42 //
children.translated_text: He has no army, and whence [would he have] allies? Why then does fear arise in you?' // Lal_21.42 //

body.text: dakṣiṇa ekāgramatirāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Ekāgramati</s> (Single-minded) said:

children.text: yūthaṃ na loke 'sti śaśīravīnāṃ na cakravartī na ca kesarīṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Hares in the world do not have a pack; nor do <s>cakravartins</s>; nor do lions;

children.text: na bodhisattvāniha tāta yūthaṃ ekaḥ samartho namuciṃ nihantum // Lal_21.43 //
children.translated_text: nor, father, do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have a pack — alone he is able to destroy <s>Namuci</s>!' // Lal_21.43 //

body.text: vāme 'vatāraprekṣyāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Avatāraprekṣī</s> (Opportunity-seeker) said:

children.text: na śaktiśūlā na gadā na khaṅgāḥ na hastino 'śvā na rathā na pattiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He has no spears, no tridents, no maces, no swords, no elephants, horses, chariots, or infantry;

children.text: taṃ śauṇḍamekaṃ śramaṇaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ hansye 'dya mā saṃbhrama tāta kiṃci // Lal_21.44 //
children.translated_text: I shall today strike that lone, bold <s>Śramaṇa</s> seated [there] — have no agitation, father!' // Lal_21.44 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe puṇyālaṃkāra āha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Puṇyālaṃkāra</s> (Merit-adorned) said:

children.text: nārāyaṇasya yatha kāya achedyabhedyo kṣāntibalaiḥ kavacito dṛḍhavīryakhaṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His body is as indestructible and impenetrable as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s; armored with the power of patience, with the sword of firm vigor;

children.text: trivimokṣavāhanasi prajñadhanuḥ sa tāta puṇyābalena sa hi jeṣyati mārasenām // Lal_21.45 //
children.translated_text: mounted on the three liberations, with the bow of wisdom — father, by the power of merit he shall conquer <s>Māra</s>'s army!' // Lal_21.45 //

body.text: vāme 'nivartyāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Anivartya</s> (Unstoppable) said —

children.text: na nivartate tṛṇagataḥ pradahan davāgniḥ kṣiptaṃ śaro na ca nivartati śikṣitena /
children.translated_text: A forest fire, having entered the grass, does not turn back; an arrow shot by a trained [archer] does not turn back.

children.text: vajraṃ nabhe nipatitaṃ na nivartate ca na sthānamasti mama śākyasutaṃ hyajitvā // Lal_21.46 //
children.translated_text: A thunderbolt fallen from the sky does not turn back — there is no position for me except to conquer the <s>Śākya</s>'s son! // Lal_21.46 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe dharmakāma āha -
body.translated_text: On the right, [the son named] <s>Dharmakāma</s> said —

children.text: ārdraṃ tṛṇaṃ prāpya nivartate 'gniḥ girikūṭamāsādya nivartate śaraḥ /
children.translated_text: A fire turns back upon reaching moist grass; an arrow turns back upon reaching a mountain peak.

children.text: vajraṃ mahīṃ prāpya adhaḥ prayāti aprāpya śāntamamṛtaṃ na nivartate ayam // Lal_21.47 //
children.translated_text: A thunderbolt, reaching the earth, goes downward — [but] this one will not turn back without attaining the peaceful, deathless [state]! // Lal_21.47 //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇam?
body.translated_text: For what reason?

children.text: śakya tāt antarīkṣe lekhyacitra citrituṃ yāvanti keci sarva sattva ekacitta sthāpitum /
children.translated_text: It is possible to paint pictures in the sky; it is possible to set all beings to a single mind.

children.text: candrāsūrya mārutaṃ ca śakya pāśa bandhituṃ na bodhisattva śakya tāta bodhimaṇḍi cālitum // Lal_21.48 //
children.translated_text: It is possible to bind the moon, sun, and wind in a noose — [but] it is not possible, O father, to shake the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from the <s>Bodhi</s>-seat! // Lal_21.48 //

body.text: vāme 'nupaśānta āha -
body.translated_text: On the left, [the son named] <s>Anupaśānta</s> said —

children.text: dṛṣṭīviṣeṇa mahatā pradahāmi meruṃ bhasmīkaromi salilaṃ ca mahodadhīnām /
children.translated_text: With the great poison of my gaze I burn <s>Meru</s>; I reduce to ashes the waters of the great oceans.

children.text: bodhiṃ ca paśya śramaṇaṃ ca ahaṃ hi tāta dṛṣṭyā yathādya ubhayaṃ hi karomi bhasmam // Lal_21.49 //
children.translated_text: Behold! O father, the <s>Bodhi</s> [seat] and the <s>Śramaṇa</s> — with my gaze today I shall reduce both to ashes! // Lal_21.49 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe siddhārtha āha -
body.translated_text: On the right, [the son named] <s>Siddhārtha</s> said —

children.text: viṣeṇa pūrṇo yadi vaiṣa sarvo bhavettrisāhasravaraḥ pradīptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if this entire <s>trisāhasra</s> (billion-fold) world-system were filled with poison and ablaze,

children.text: nirīkṣaṇādeva guṇākarasya sunirviṣatvaṃ viṣamabhyupeyāt // Lal_21.50 //
children.translated_text: by merely being looked upon by this mine of virtues, the poison would become completely non-poisonous. // Lal_21.50 //

children.text: viṣāṇamugraṃ tribhaveha yacca rāgaśca doṣaśca tathaiva mohaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fierce poison in the three realms — passion, hatred, and likewise delusion —

children.text: te tasya kāye ca tathaiva citte nabhe yathā paṅkarajo na santi // Lal_21.51 //
children.translated_text: these do not exist in his body nor in his mind, just as mud-dust [does not exist] in the sky. // Lal_21.51 //

body.text: * * * * tasmānnivartāmaha tāta sarve // Lal_21.52 //
body.translated_text: [...] Therefore let us all turn back, O father! // Lal_21.52 //

body.text: vāme ratilolo nāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, [the son named] <s>Ratilola</s> said —

children.text: ahu tūryasahasra pravāditaiḥ apsarakoṭisahasra alaṃkṛtaiḥ /
children.translated_text: I, with thousands of instruments played, with <s>koṭi</s>-thousands of <s>Apsarases</s> adorned,

children.text: lobhayitvana neṣyi purottamaṃ kāmaratiṃ hi karomi vaśe tava // Lal_21.53 //
