children.translated_text: having tempted [him], shall lead that foremost of men [away] — for I shall bring the pleasure of desire under your power! // Lal_21.53 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe dharmaratirāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, [the son named] <s>Dharmarati</s> said —

children.text: dharmaratī sada tasya ratīhā dhyānaratī amṛtārtharatiśca /
children.translated_text: His delight is always in the <s>Dharma</s>; his delight is in <s>dhyāna</s>; his delight is in the deathless goal;

children.text: sattvapramokṣaṇa maitraratiśca rāgaratiṃ sa ratiṃ na karoti // Lal_21.54 //
children.translated_text: his delight is in the liberation of beings through loving-kindness — he does not take delight in the pleasure of passion. // Lal_21.54 //

body.text: vāme vātajavo nāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, [the son named] <s>Vātajava</s> (Swift-as-Wind) said —

children.text: javenahaṃ candraravī graseyaṃ pravāyamānaṃ gagane ca vāyum /
children.translated_text: With my speed I could swallow the moon and sun, and the wind blowing in the sky!

children.text: adyaiva tāta śramaṇaṃ gṛhītvā prāsasya muṣṭiṃ vikirāmi vāyum // Lal_21.55 //
children.translated_text: Today, O father, having seized the <s>Śramaṇa</s>, I shall scatter him to the wind with a single blow of my fist! // Lal_21.55 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe 'calamatirnāma māraputraḥ, sa evamāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, the <s>Māra</s>-son named <s>Acalamati</s> (Unshakable Mind) said —

children.text: yathā tavaiṣo javavega ugraḥ tadvadyadi syātsuramānuṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: Even if such fierce speed and force as yours were possessed by all gods and humans,

children.text: sarve samagrāpi na te samarthāḥ kartuṃ rujāmapratipudgalasya // Lal_21.56 //
children.translated_text: all of them together would not be able to cause even a scratch to this peerless one. // Lal_21.56 //

body.text: vāme brahmamatirāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, <s>Brahmamati</s> said —

children.text: syāttādṛśānāmapi vṛndamugraṃ kuryānna kiṃcittava mānaghātam /
children.translated_text: Even a fierce multitude of such [warriors] as you could not cause the slightest injury to his pride.

children.text: prāgeva saikaḥ prakaroti kiṃ te vṛndena sādhyanti hi sarvakāryā // Lal_21.57 //
children.translated_text: Much less can one alone do anything to him — [for] it is by multitudes that all tasks are accomplished. // Lal_21.57 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe siṃhamatirāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, <s>Siṃhamati</s> (Lion-Mind) said —

children.text: na siṃhavṛndaṃ bhuvi dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ dṛṣṭīviṣāṇāṃ api nāsti vṛndam /
children.translated_text: A pack of lions has never been seen on earth; nor is there a pack of those with poison in their gaze.

children.text: tejasvināṃ satyaparākramāṇāṃ puruṣarṣabhāṇāṃ api nāsti vṛndam // Lal_21.58 //
children.translated_text: There is no pack among the splendid, those of true valor — [nor among] bulls among men. // Lal_21.58 //

body.text: vāme sarvacaṇḍālo nāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the left, [the son named] <s>Sarvacaṇḍāla</s> (All-Fierce) said —

children.text: na te śrutā tāta giro 'bhidīptā yathā nadante tanayāstaveme /
children.translated_text: Have you not heard, O father, the blazing words that these sons of yours utter?

children.text: vīryeṇa vegena balena yuktā vrajāma śīghraṃ śramaṇaṃ nihantum // Lal_21.59 //
children.translated_text: Endowed with vigor, speed, and strength — let us go quickly to slay the <s>Śramaṇa</s>! // Lal_21.59 //

body.text: dakṣiṇe siṃhanādī nāmāha -
body.translated_text: On the right, [the son named] <s>Siṃhanādī</s> (Lion-Roarer) said —

children.text: bahavaḥ śṛgālā hi vanāntareṣu nadanti nādānna satīha siṃhe /
children.translated_text: Many jackals howl in the forest depths when the lion is not present.

children.text: te siṃhanādaṃ tu niśāmya bhīmaṃ trastā palāyanti diśo daśāsu // Lal_21.60 //
children.translated_text: But hearing the lion's fearsome roar, they flee in terror to the ten directions. // Lal_21.60 //

children.text: māraurasāstadvadamī apaṇḍitāḥ aśrutva nādaṃ puruṣottamasya /
children.translated_text: These unwise sons of <s>Māra</s>, likewise — not having heard the roar of the foremost among men,

children.text: nadanti tāvatsvamatā 'tighṛṣṭā manuṣyasiṃhe nadite na santi // Lal_21.61 //
children.translated_text: they roar thus far, proud of their own opinions; when the lion among men roars, they shall be no more. // Lal_21.61 //

body.text: vāmātpārśvādduścintitacintyāha -
body.translated_text: From the left side, [the son named] <s>Duścintitacintya</s> (Ill-Conceived Thought) said —

children.text: yaccintayāmi tadihāśu bhoti kathaṃ na eṣo ima vīkṣate ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever I think, that swiftly comes to pass here! Why then does this one not even look [at us]?

children.text: mūḍho na eṣo anabhijña kiṃ vā yadutthihitvā na palāyate laghum // Lal_21.62 //
children.translated_text: Is this one deluded? Is he without superknowledge? Why does he not rise up and flee quickly? // Lal_21.62 //

body.text: dakṣiṇātpārśvātsucintitārtho nāmāha -
body.translated_text: From the right side, the <s>Māra</s>-son named <s>Sucintitārtha</s> (Well-Conceived Purpose) said —

children.text: mūḍho na vāyaṃ aparākramo vā yuṣmaiva mūḍhāśca asaṃyatāśca /
children.translated_text: This one is neither deluded nor lacking in valor — rather, you yourselves are the deluded and unrestrained ones!

children.text: na yuṣmi jānātha imasya vīryaṃ prajñābalenāsya jitāḥ stha sarve // Lal_21.63 //
children.translated_text: You do not know his vigor — by the power of his wisdom, you are all already conquered! // Lal_21.63 //

body.text: mārātmajānāṃ yatha gaṅgavālikā etena vīryeṇa yathaiva yūyam /
body.translated_text: Even if <s>Māra</s>'s sons were as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with such vigor as yours,

body.text: romasya ekaṃ na samartha cālituṃ prāgeva yaścintayi ghātayiṣye // Lal_21.64 //
body.translated_text: you would not be able to move even a single hair [of his] — much less one who thinks 'I shall slay [him]!' // Lal_21.64 //

children.text: mā yūyamatra kṣiṇuyāta mānasaṃ prasannacitā bhavathā sagauravāḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not waste your minds here! Be of serene minds, with reverence!

children.text: nivartayā mā prakarotha vigrahaṃ bhaviṣyate 'sau tribhavesmi rājā // Lal_21.65 //
children.translated_text: Turn back! Do not make war! This one shall become the sovereign of the three realms! // Lal_21.65 //

body.text: peyālam / evaṃ te sarve māraputrāḥ paripurṇaṃ putrasahasraṃ śuklapākṣikāśca kṛṣṇapākṣikāśca māraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ pṛthakpṛthaggāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta //
body.translated_text: [Abbreviated.] Thus all those <s>Māra</s>-sons — a full thousand sons, those of the white party and those of the dark party — addressed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, each separately, with verses. //

body.text: atha khalu bhadraseno nāma mārasya pāpīyasaḥ senāpatiḥ, sa māraṃ pāpīyasaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhadrasena</s>, the general of <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, addressed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One with verses —

children.text: ye te tavānuyātrāḥ śakro lokapālāśca kinnaragaṇāśca /
children.translated_text: Those who are your followers — <s>Śakra</s>, the world-guardians, the <s>Kinnara</s> hosts,

children.text: asurendrā garuḍendrāḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ praṇata tasmai // Lal_21.66 //
children.translated_text: <s>Asura</s>-lords, <s>Garuḍa</s>-lords — [all stand] with palms joined, bowing to him. // Lal_21.66 //

children.text: kiṃ punaranānuyātrā brahmā ābhāsvarāśca suraputrāḥ /
children.translated_text: How much more those who are not your followers — <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>devaputras</s>,

children.text: devāśca śuddhāvāsakāste 'pi ca sarve praṇata tasmai // Lal_21.67 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods — they too, all of them, bow to him! // Lal_21.67 //

children.text: ye ca taveme putrāḥ prajñāmeghāvinaśca balinaśca /
children.translated_text: And those sons of yours who are wise, endowed with <s>prajñā</s>-clouds, and powerful —

children.text: te bodhisattvahṛdayaṃ anupraviṣṭā namasyanti // Lal_21.68 //
children.translated_text: they have entered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s heart and pay homage. // Lal_21.68 //

children.text: yāpyeṣa mārasenā aśīti sphuṭa yojanāni yakṣādyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And this army of <s>Māra</s>, spread over eighty <s>yojanas</s> with <s>Yakṣas</s> and others —

children.text: bhūyiṣṭha sarvaprekṣī prasannamanaso hi nirdoṣam // Lal_21.69 //
children.translated_text: for the most part, they all look upon [him] with serene minds, free from fault. // Lal_21.69 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yathā subhīmāṃ raudrāṃ vikṛtāṃ camūmimāṃ ghorām /
children.translated_text: Having seen this fearsome, terrible, deformed, and dreadful army,

children.text: na ca vismito na calito dhruvamasya jayo bhavatyadya // Lal_21.70 //
children.translated_text: [yet] he is neither astonished nor shaken — certainly his shall be the victory today! // Lal_21.70 //

children.text: sthita yatra ca seneyaṃ tatra ulūkāḥ śivāśca viruvanti /
children.translated_text: Where this army stands, there owls and jackals howl;

children.text: vāyasagardabharuditaṃ nivartitavyaṃ kṣamaṃ śīghram // Lal_21.71 //
children.translated_text: the cries of crows and donkeys [are heard] — it is fitting to turn back quickly! // Lal_21.71 //

children.text: vīkṣasva bodhimaṇḍe paṭukroñcā haṃsa kokīla mayūrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Look at the <s>Bodhi</s>-seat — sharp-voiced cranes, swans, cuckoos, and peacocks

children.text: abhidakṣiṇaṃ karonti dhruvamasya jayo bhavatyadya // Lal_21.72 //
children.translated_text: circumambulate [it] to the right — certainly his shall be the victory today! // Lal_21.72 //

children.text: yatra sthita seneyaṃ tatra masiḥ pāṃśavaśca varṣanti /
children.translated_text: Where this army stands, there ink and dust rain down;

children.text: mahimaṇḍi kusumavṛṣṭiḥ kuruṣva vacanaṃ nivartasva // Lal_21.73 //
children.translated_text: [but] on the earth-<s>maṇḍala</s> [of the <s>Bodhi</s>-seat], a rain of flowers [falls] — heed these words and turn back! // Lal_21.73 //

children.text: yatra sthita seneyaṃ utkūlanikūla śalyakaṇṭakākīrṇam /
children.translated_text: Where this army stands, [the ground is] uneven, full of stakes and thorns;

children.text: mahimaṇḍa kanakanirmalu nivartitavyaṃ kṣamaṃ prājñaiḥ // Lal_21.74 //
children.translated_text: [but] the earth-<s>maṇḍala</s> [of the <s>Bodhi</s>-seat is] pure as gold — it is fitting for the wise to turn back! // Lal_21.74 //

children.text: dṛṣṭā ti supini pūrve bheṣyasi pratyakṣu yadi na gacchāsi /
children.translated_text: Seen formerly in dreams, it shall become reality — if you do not retreat,

children.text: bhasmaṃ camūṃ ca kariṣyati ṛṣibhirdeśā kṛtā yathā bhasmam // Lal_21.75 //
children.translated_text: he shall reduce this army to ashes, just as the sages reduced realms to ashes! // Lal_21.75 //

children.text: rājā yato ṛṣivaro roṣitu āsīt sa brahmadattena /
children.translated_text: The king, that supreme sage, was once enraged by <s>Brahmadatta</s>;

children.text: uddagdhadaṇḍakavanaṃ varṣairbahubhistṛṇa na jātā // Lal_21.76 //
children.translated_text: [he] burned the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, and for many years not even grass grew [there]. // Lal_21.76 //

children.text: ye keci sarvaloke ṛṣayo vratacāriṇastapoyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever sages exist in all the world — those who observe vows and are devoted to <s>tapas</s> —

children.text: teṣāmayaṃ pradhāno hyahiṃsakaḥ sarvabhūtānām // Lal_21.77 //
children.translated_text: this one is their chief, a non-harmer of all beings. // Lal_21.77 //

children.text: kiṃ te na śrutapūrvaṃ kāye dīptā sulakṣaṇā yasya /
children.translated_text: Have you not heard before? He on whose body the auspicious marks blaze,

children.text: niṣkrāmati cāgārātsa bhavati buddho jitakleśaḥ // Lal_21.78 //
children.translated_text: who goes forth from the household — he becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, a conqueror of afflictions. // Lal_21.78 //

children.text: ima īdṛśī vibhūtiṃ pūjārthaṃ nirmitā jinasutebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Such splendor as this, created by the <s>Jina</s>'s sons for the purpose of worship —

children.text: taṃ nūnamagrasattvo hyagrāhutisaṃpratigrāhī // Lal_21.79 //
children.translated_text: surely this one is the foremost of beings, the recipient of the foremost offering! // Lal_21.79 //

children.text: ūrṇā yathā suvimalā virājate kṣetrakoṭinayuteṣu /
children.translated_text: Just as his supremely pure <s>ūrṇā</s> radiates over <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> of fields —

children.text: jihmīkṛtāḥ sma ca tayā nisaṃśayaṃ eṣa mārabalahantā // Lal_21.80 //
children.translated_text: we have been humbled by it; without doubt, this one is the destroyer of <s>Māra</s>'s forces! // Lal_21.80 //

children.text: mūrdhnaṃ yathāsya devairdraṣṭu na śakyaṃ na vai bhavāgrasthaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as his crown is not able to be seen by the gods, not even by those at the summit of existence —

children.text: nūnaṃ sarvajñatvaṃ prāpsyatyanyairanupadiṣṭam // Lal_21.81 //
children.translated_text: surely he shall attain omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>), untaught by others! // Lal_21.81 //

children.text: yatha merucakravālāścandrāsūryaśca śakrabrahmāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Meru</s>, the <s>Cakravāla</s> [mountains], the moon and sun, <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: vṛkṣāśca parvatavarāḥ praṇate sarve mahīmaṇḍam // Lal_21.82 //
children.translated_text: the trees and the supreme mountains — all bow down, and the earth-circle [trembles] — // Lal_21.82 //

children.text: niḥsaṃśayu puṇyabalī prajñābalavāṃśca jñānabalavāṃśca /
children.translated_text: without doubt, he is powerful in merit, powerful in wisdom, powerful in knowledge,

children.text: kṣāntibalavāṃśca vīryabalavānabalaṃkartā namucipakṣāṃ // Lal_21.83 //
children.translated_text: powerful in patience, powerful in vigor — he shall render the hosts of <s>Namuci</s> powerless! // Lal_21.83 //

children.text: hastī yathāmabhāṇḍaṃ pramardate kroṣṭukān yathā siṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as an elephant crushes a clay vessel, as a lion [scatters] jackals,

children.text: khadyotaṃ vādityo bhetsyati sugatastathā senām // Lal_21.84 //
children.translated_text: as the sun [extinguishes] a firefly — so shall the <s>Sugata</s> shatter [this] army! // Lal_21.84 //

body.text: etacchutvā paro māraputro 'tīva roṣātsaṃraktanayano 'bravīt -
body.translated_text: Hearing this, another <s>Māra</s>-son, his eyes red with extreme anger, said —

children.text: ekasya varṇānatiapremayāṃ prabhāṣase tasya tvamekakasya /
children.translated_text: You speak praising the qualities of just this one alone, of this single person!

children.text: eko hi kartuṃ khalu kiṃ samartho mahābalā paśyasi kiṃ na bhīmā // Lal_21.85 //
children.translated_text: What can one alone accomplish? Do you not see [these] mighty and fearsome [forces]? // Lal_21.85 //

body.text: atha dakṣiṇātpārśvānmārapramardako nāma māraputra āha -
body.translated_text: Then from the right side, the <s>Māra</s>-son named <s>Mārapramardaka</s> (Crusher of <s>Māra</s>) said —

children.text: sūryasya loke na sahāyakṛtyaṃ candrasya siṃhasya na cakravartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun has no need of allies in the world; nor the moon, nor the lion, nor the <s>Cakravartin</s>.

children.text: bodhau niṣaṇṇasya ca niścitasya na bodhisattvasya sahāyakṛtyam // Lal_21.86 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seated in <s>Bodhi</s> with firm resolve — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has no need of allies! // Lal_21.86 //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo mārasya durbalīkaraṇahetorvikasitaśatapatranibhaṃ vadanaṃ saṃcārayati sma / yaṃ dṛṣṭvā māraḥ pāpīyān prapalāyāno 'bhūt / mama camū bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ pratiṣṭheti
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the purpose of weakening <s>Māra</s>, displayed a countenance like a blooming hundred-petaled [lotus]. Seeing it, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One began to flee. Thinking 'My army is [rushing] toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s face,'

body.text: manyamānaḥ prapalānaḥ punareva pratinivṛtya saparivāro vividhāni praharaṇāni bodhisattvasyoparyutsṛjati sma sumerumātrāṃśca parvatān / te ca bodhisattvasyopari prakṣiptāḥ puṣpavitāne vimānāni saṃtiṣṭhante sma / ye ca dṛṣṭiviṣā āśīviṣāḥ śvāsaviṣāścāgnijvālānutsṛjanti sma, taccāgnimaṇḍalaṃ bodhisattvasya prabhāmaṇḍalamiva saṃtiṣṭhate sma //
body.translated_text: he turned back again, and together with his retinue hurled various weapons upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and mountains the size of <s>Meru</s>. But those, when hurled upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, stood [transformed into] flower-canopies and celestial palaces. And the poison-eyed, poison-fanged, and poison-breathed [serpents] released flames of fire — but that fire-circle stood like the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s halo of radiance. //

body.text: atha punareva bodhisattvo dakṣiṇena pāṇinā śīrṣaṃ pramārṣṭi sma / māraśca paśyati sma / bodhisattvasya haste khaṅga iti dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ prapalāyate sma / na kiṃciditi punareva pratinivartate sma / nivṛtya ca bodhisattvasyopari nānāvidhāni praharaṇānyutsṛjati sma asidhanuśaraśaktitomaraparaśvadhabhuśuṇḍimusalakaṇayagadācakravajramudgarapādapaśilāpāśāyoguḍānatibhayānakān / te cotkṣiptamātrā nānāvidhāni puṣpadāmāni puṣpavitānāni iva saṃtiṣṭhante sma / muktasukusumāni ca mahīmavakiranto mālyadāmāni cāvalambamānāni bodhivṛkṣaṃ vibhūṣayanti sma / tāṃśca vyūhān vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā bodhisattvasya māraḥ pāpīyānīrṣyāmātsaryopahatacetā bodhisattvamabravīt - uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha he rājakumāra, rājyaṃ bhuṅkṣva, tāvattava puṇyam, kutaste mokṣaprāptiḥ?
body.translated_text: Then once again the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wiped his head with his right hand. <s>Māra</s> saw [this] and, [thinking] 'a sword is in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hand!' fled facing south. [Seeing] 'it is nothing' — he turned back again. Having returned, he hurled upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s> various weapons — swords, bows, arrows, spears, javelins, axes, clubs, pestles, iron bars, maces, discs, <s>vajras</s>, hammers, trees, rocks, nooses, iron balls — terrifying beyond measure. But the moment they were hurled, they stood [transformed into] various flower-garlands and flower-canopies. And the released flowers, scattering upon the earth, and the hanging garland-chains adorned the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree. Having seen those arrays and that splendor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, his mind overcome by jealousy and miserliness, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Rise! Rise, O prince! Enjoy your kingdom! That is the extent of your merit — whence comes the attainment of liberation for you?'

body.text: atha bodhisattvo dhīragambhīrodāraślakṣṇamadhurayā vācā māraṃ pāpīyasametadavocat - tvayā tāvatpāpīyannekena nirgaḍena yajñena kāmeśvaratvaṃ prāptam / mayā tvanekāni yajñakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi nirgaḍāni yaṣṭāni / karacaraṇanayanottamāṅgāni ca nikṛtya nikṛtyārthibhyo dattāni / gṛhadhanadhānyaśayanavasanaṃ caṃkramodyānāni cānekaśo yācanakebhyo nisṛṣṭāni sattvānāṃ mokṣārthinā /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with a voice steady, deep, noble, gentle, and sweet, said to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'You, Evil One, by a single unrestricted sacrifice, have attained the lordship of the Desire Realm. But I have performed many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred thousands of unrestricted sacrifices. And I have cut off and given away my hands, feet, eyes, and head repeatedly to supplicants. Houses, wealth, grain, beds, garments, promenades, and gardens — I have many times relinquished [these] to those who ask, desiring the liberation of beings.'

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān bodhisattvaṃ gāthayā pratyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with a verse —

children.text: yajño mayeṣṭastvamihātra sākṣī nirargaḍaḥ pūrvabhave 'navadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sacrifice I performed — you are my witness here — unrestricted, blameless in a former existence.

children.text: taveha sākṣī na tu kaścidasti kiṃcitpralāpena parājitastvam // Lal_21.87 //
children.translated_text: But as for you, there is no witness here. By empty words you are defeated!' // Lal_21.87 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha - iyaṃ pāpīyan mama bhūtadhātrī pramāṇamiti //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'This, O Evil One, is my witness — the earth, the supporter of beings!' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo māraṃ māraparṣadaṃ ca maitrīkaruṇāpūrvaṃgamena cittena sphuritvā siṃhavadabhīto 'nuttrasto 'stambhī adīno 'līnaḥ asaṃkṣubhito 'lulito vigatabhayalomaharṣaḥ śaṅkhadhvajamīnakalaśasvastikāṅkuśacakrāṅkamadhyena jālāvitānāvanaddhena suruciratāmranakhālaṃkṛtena mṛdutaruṇasukumāreṇānantakalpāparimitakuśalamūlasaṃbhāropacitena dakṣiṇena pāṇinā sarvakāyaṃ parimārjya salīlaṃ mahīṃ parāhanati sma / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having pervaded <s>Māra</s> and <s>Māra</s>'s retinue with a mind preceded by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), fearless like a lion, unalarmed, unwavering, undiscouraged, undepressed, unperturbed, unshaken, his hair not standing on end from fear — with his right hand marked in the center with the signs of a conch, banner, fish, vase, <s>svastika</s>, goad, and wheel, covered by the net-canopy [of webbed fingers], adorned with beautifully lustrous copper-colored nails, soft, young, and tender, accumulated through the amassing of roots of merit through immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> — having stroked his entire body, he gracefully struck the earth. And at that moment he spoke this verse —

body.text: iyaṃ mahī sarva jagatpratiṣṭhā apakṣapātā sacarācare samā /
body.translated_text: 'This great earth is the support of all the world, impartial, equal toward all that moves and does not move;

body.text: iyaṃ pramāṇā mama nāsti me mṛṣā sākṣitvamasmiṃ mama saṃprayacchatu // Lal_21.88 //
body.translated_text: she is my witness — there is no falsehood in me — let her grant me testimony in this!' // Lal_21.88 //

body.text: saṃspṛṣṭamātrā ceyaṃ mahāpṛthivī bodhisattvena ṣaḍvikāramakampat prākampat saṃprākampat / araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat / tadyathāpi nāma māgadhikānāṃ kāṃsapātrī kāṣṭhenābhyāhatā raṇatyanuraṇati, evameveyaṃ mahāpṛthivī bodhisattvena pāṇitāḍitā raṇatyanuraṇati sma //
body.translated_text: And this great earth, merely touched by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, trembled in six ways — it shook, greatly shook, and thoroughly shook; it resounded, greatly resounded, and thoroughly resounded. Just as a bronze bowl of the <s>Magadhans</s>, when struck with a stick, rings and reverberates — even so this great earth, struck by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hand, rang and reverberated. //

body.text: atha khalu yasyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau sthāvarā nāma mahāpṛthivīdevatā sā koṭiśatapṛthivīdevatāparivārā sarvāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ saṃprakampya nātidūre bodhisattvasya pṛthivītalaṃ bhittvārdhakāyābhyunnāmya sarvālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitā yena bodhisattvastenāvanatakāyā prāñjalīkṛtā bodhisattvametadavocat - evametanmahāpuruṣa evametat yathā tvayābhihitam / vayamatra pratyakṣāḥ / api tu bhagavaṃstvameva sadevakasya lokasya paramasākṣībhūtaḥ pramāṇabhūtaśceti / evamuktvā sthāvarā mahāpṛthivīdevatā māraṃ pāpīyāṃsamanekaprakāraṃ nirbhartsya bodhisattvaṃ cābhyabhistutya vividhaṃ ca svakaṃ prabhāvaṃ saṃdarśya saparivārā tatraivāntaradhāt //
body.translated_text: Then the great earth deity named <s>Sthāvarā</s> in that trichiliocosm, attended by hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of earth deities, having caused the entire great earth to tremble, not far from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, splitting open the earth's surface, rising up with half her body, fully adorned with all ornaments, with body bowed toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with palms joined, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'It is so, O Great Being! It is so, just as you have declared! We are here as eyewitnesses! Moreover, O Blessed One, you yourself are the supreme witness and authority for the world with its gods.' Having spoken thus, <s>Sthāvarā</s>, the great earth deity, having rebuked <s>Māra</s> the Evil One in many ways, having praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and having displayed her own manifold power, vanished right there with her retinue. //

children.text: taṃ śrutva mediniravaṃ sa śaṭhaḥ sasainyaḥ uttrasta bhinnahṛdayo prapalāna sarve /
children.translated_text: Hearing that sound of the earth, the deceitful one with his army — terrified, their hearts shattered — all fled!

children.text: śrutveva siṃhanaditaṃ hi vane śṛgālāḥ kākā va loṣṭupatane sahasā praṇaṣṭāḥ // Lal_21.89 //
children.translated_text: Like jackals hearing the lion's roar in the forest, or like crows suddenly scattering at the fall of a clod! // Lal_21.89 //

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān duḥkhito durmanā anāttamanā apatrapamāṇarūpo mānābhibhavānna gacchati sma / na nivartate sma / na palāyate sma / paścānmukhaṃ sthitvā uttari senāmāmantrayate sma - sahitāḥ samagrāstāvadbhavantastiṣṭhantu muhurtaṃ yāvadvayaṃ jñāsyāmo yadi tāvacchakyetāyamanunayenotthāpayitum / mā khalvevaṃrūpasya sattvaratnasya sahasā vināśo bhūditi //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, grieving, dejected, displeased, ashamed, overcome by pride, did not go away; he did not turn back; he did not flee. Standing with his back [to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], he addressed the remaining army: 'Let your forces stand together and united for a moment while we determine whether this one can be raised [from his seat] by persuasion. Let not such a jewel among beings be destroyed abruptly!' //

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān svā duhitṝrāmantrayate sma - gacchadhvaṃ yūyaṃ kanyakāḥ, bodhimaṇḍamupasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya jijñāsanāṃ kuruta - kiṃ sarāgo 'tha vītarāgaḥ / kiṃ mūko 'tha prajñaḥ / kimandho 'tha deśajño 'rthaparāyaṇaḥ / dīno vā dhīro veti / idaṃ khalu vacanaṃ śrutvā tā apsaraso yena bodhimaṇḍo yena ca bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramya bodhisattvasya purataḥ sthitvā dvātriṃśadākārāṃ strīmāyāmupadarśayanti sma / tadyathā / katamā dvātriṃśadākārā? kāścittatrārdhavadanaṃ chādayanti sma / kāścidunnatān kaṭhinān payodharān darśayanti sma / kāścidardhavihasitairdantāvaliṃ darśayanti sma / kāścidbāhūnutkṣipya vijṛmbhamāṇān kākṣān darśayanti sma / kāścidbimbaphalopamānoṣṭhān darśayanti sma / kāścidardhanimīlitairnayanairbodhisattvaṃ nirīkṣante sma, dṛṣṭvā ca śīghraṃ nimīlayanti sma / kāścidardhaprāvṛtān payodharān darśayanti sma / kāścicchithilāmbarāṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One summoned his daughters: 'Go, you maidens! Approach the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and test the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — whether he is passionate or dispassionate, whether dull or wise, whether blind or one who knows the terrain and is devoted to purpose, whether timid or steadfast!' Having heard these words, those <s>Apsarases</s> approached the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, standing before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, they displayed the thirty-two forms of feminine enchantment. What were the thirty-two forms? Some there covered half their faces. Some displayed high, firm breasts. Some displayed their row of teeth with half-smiles. Some raised their arms, yawning, displaying their underarms. Some displayed lips resembling <s>bimba</s>-fruit. Some gazed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with half-closed eyes, and having looked, quickly closed them. Some displayed half-covered breasts. Some displayed loosely-clad

body.text: samekhalāṃ śroṇīṃ darśayanti sma / kāścitsamekhalāṃ tanudukūlanivāsitāṃ śroṇīṃ darśayanti sma / kāścijjhaṇajhaṇāśadbānnūpuraiḥ kurvanti sma / kāścidekāvalīṃ stanāntareṣūpadarśayanti sma / kāścidvinagnānarghorūnupadarśayanti sma / kāścicchiraḥsvaṃseṣu ca patraguptāñśukaśārikāṃścopaviṣṭānupadarśayanti sma / kāścidardhakaṭākṣairbodhisattvaṃ nirīkṣante sma / kāścitsunivastā api durnivastāḥ kurvanti sma / kāścijjaghanarasanāḥ kampayanti sma / kāścitsaṃbhrāntā iva savilāsamitastataścaṃkramyante sma / kāścinnṛtyanti sma / kāścidrāyanti sma / kāścidvilasanti sma, lajjante ca / kāścitkadalya iva vāyuvidhūtā urū kampayanti sma / kāścidgambhīrāḥ stananti sma / kāścidaṃśukaprāvṛtāḥ saghaṇṭārasanā vihasyantyaścaṃkramyante sma / kāścidvastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca pṛthivyāṃ chorayanti sma / kāścidguhyaprakāśāni sarvābharaṇānyupadarśayanti sma / kāścidgandhānuliptān bāhūnupadarśayanti sma / kāścidgandhānulepanakuṇḍalānyupadarśayanti sma / kāścidavaguṇṭhikayā vadanāni chādayanti sma, kṣaṇekṣaṇā copadarśayanti sma / kāścitpūrvahasitaramitakrīḍitā anyonyaṃ smārayanti sma / punarapi lajjitā iva tiṣṭhanti sma / kāścitkumārīrūpāṇyaprasūtirūpāṇi madhyastrīrūpāṇi copadarśayanti sma / kāścitkāmopahitena bodhisattvaṃ nimantrayante sma / kāścinmuktakusumairbodhisattvamavakiranti sma / purataśca sthitvā bodhisattvasyāśayaṃ mīmāṃsante sma / vadanaṃ ca nirīkṣante sma - kimayaṃ raktendriyaiḥ paśyatyāhosviddūrīkaroti, nayane īryate vā na veti / tāḥ paśyanti bodhisattvasya vadanaṃ śuddhaṃ vimalaṃ candramaṇḍalamiva rāhuvinirmuktaṃ sūryamiva prodayamānaṃ yūpamiva kanakamayaṃ vikasitamiva sahasrapatraṃ havyāvasiktamivānalaṃ merumivācalaṃ cakravālamivābhyudrataṃ gupteindriyaṃ nāgamiva sudāntacittam //
body.translated_text: belted hips. Some displayed belted hips draped in thin silk garments. Some made jingling sounds with their anklets. Some displayed a single strand of pearls between their breasts. Some displayed their completely bare thighs. Some displayed parrots and <s>śārikā</s> birds perched on their heads and shoulders, hidden in cloth. Some gazed at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with sidelong glances. Some, though well-dressed, made themselves appear poorly dressed. Some swayed their hip-girdles. Some walked about here and there with agitation, as if playfully. Some danced. Some sang. Some flirted, and blushed. Some, like plantain trees shaken by the wind, made their thighs tremble. Some sighed deeply. Some, covered in garments with girdles of bells, walked about laughing. Some cast their garments and ornaments upon the ground. Some displayed all their ornaments that reveal the intimate parts. Some displayed arms anointed with perfume. Some displayed earrings [shaped like] perfume-pots. Some veiled their faces with scarves, displaying them for an instant and then [covering again]. Some reminded each other of former laughter, sport, and play; and then again stood as if bashful. Some displayed the forms of maidens, forms of those who have not yet given birth, and forms of women in their prime. Some invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with words laden with desire. Some showered the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with loose flowers. And standing before him, they examined the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s disposition, gazing at his face — [asking:] 'Does he look with inflamed senses, or does he turn away? Do his eyes move or not?' They beheld the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s face — pure, stainless, like the disk of the moon freed from <s>Rāhu</s>, like the rising sun, like a golden sacrificial post, like a blossoming thousand-petaled [lotus], like a fire upon which oblations have been poured, immovable like <s>Meru</s>, exalted like <s>Cakravāla</s>, with guarded senses, like a well-tamed elephant with tranquil mind. //

body.text: atha tā māraduhitaro bhūyasyā mātrayā bodhisattvasya saṃlobhanārthamimā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those daughters of <s>Māra</s>, yet more profusely, for the purpose of tempting the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, spoke these verses —

children.text: suvasantake ṛtuvara āgatake ramimo priya phullitapādapake /
children.translated_text: 'In the most beautiful of seasons, when spring has arrived, we delight, O beloved, among the blossoming trees,

children.text: tava rūpa surūpa suśobhanake vaśavartisulakṣaṇacitritake // Lal_21.90 //
children.translated_text: with your form so beautiful, so splendid, enchanting, painted with excellent marks of [one who is] sovereign! // Lal_21.90 //

children.text: vaya jāta sujāta susaṃsthitikāḥ sukhakāraṇa devanarāṇa susaṃtutikāḥ /
children.translated_text: We are well-born, well-formed, well-established — givers of happiness and delight to gods and men!

children.text: utthi laghuṃ paribhuñja suyauvanikaṃ durlabha bodhi nivartaya mānasakam // Lal_21.91 //
children.translated_text: Arise quickly! Enjoy the bloom of youth! <s>Bodhi</s> is hard to attain — turn your mind [away from it]! // Lal_21.91 //

body.text: prekṣasi tāva imā marukanya sulaṃkṛtikā tava kāraṇa sajjita bhūṣita āgatikā /
body.translated_text: Look upon these divine maidens, well-adorned, prepared and ornamented and come for your sake!

body.text: ko rūpamimaṃ samavekṣya na rajyati rāgarato api jarjara kāṣṭha va śoṣitajīvitako // Lal_21.92 //
body.translated_text: Who, seeing such beauty, is not inflamed? Even one devoted to passion, dried up like withered wood with spent life-force! // Lal_21.92 //

children.text: keṣa mṛdū surabhī varagandhinikā makuṭākuṇḍalapatravibodhitaānanikā /
children.translated_text: [See our] soft, fragrant, and sweetly-scented hair, with crowns, earrings, and leaf-ornaments adorning [our] faces,

children.text: sulalāṭa sulepanaānanikā padmaviśuddhaviśālasulocanikā // Lal_21.93 //
children.translated_text: beautiful foreheads, lovely unguent-adorned faces, wide lotus-pure beautiful eyes! // Lal_21.93 //

children.text: paripūritacandranibhānanikā bimbasupakvanibhādharikā /
children.translated_text: Full moon-like faces, lower lips like ripe <s>bimba</s>-fruit,

children.text: śaṅkhakundahimaśuklasudantinikā prekṣa kānta ratilālasikām // Lal_21.94 //
children.translated_text: teeth white as conches, <s>kunda</s>-flowers, and snow — behold, beloved, [us] eager for the pleasure of love! // Lal_21.94 //

children.text: kaṭhinapīnapayodhara udgatikāṃ trivalīkṛtamadhyasusundarikām /
children.translated_text: Firm, full, upraised breasts, beautiful waists with three folds,

children.text: jaghanāṅgaṇacārusuvittharikāṃ prekṣasu nātha sukāminikām // Lal_21.95 //
children.translated_text: with lovely, broad hips and flanks — behold, O Lord, these desirous women! // Lal_21.95 //

children.text: gajabhujasaṃnibhaūruṇikāṃ valayanirantarabāhanikām /
children.translated_text: Thighs like elephant trunks, arms continuously adorned with bracelets,

children.text: kāñcīvaraśroṇisamaṇḍitikāṃ prekṣahi nātha imā tava dāsinikām // Lal_21.96 //
children.translated_text: hips adorned with finest girdles — behold, O Lord, these who are your servants! // Lal_21.96 //

children.text: haṃsagatīsuvilambitagāminikāṃ maññumanojñasumanmathabhāṣiṇikām /
children.translated_text: [Women with] the gait of geese, walking with graceful languor, speaking charming, pleasing, and passion-arousing words,

children.text: īdṛśarūpasubhūṣiṇikāṃ divyaratīṣu supaṇḍitikām // Lal_21.97 //
children.translated_text: adorned with such beautiful ornaments, expert in divine pleasures! // Lal_21.97 //

children.text: gītakavāditanṛtyasuśikṣitikāṃ ratikāraṇajātisurūpiṇikām /
children.translated_text: Well-trained in song, music, and dance, born with beautiful forms for the sake of love's pleasure —

children.text: yadi necchasi kāmasulālasikāṃ suṣṭu suvañcitako 'si bhṛśaṃ khalu loke // Lal_21.98 //
children.translated_text: if you do not desire [us], eager for love's delight, you are truly well-deceived indeed in this world! // Lal_21.98 //

children.text: nidhi dṛṣṭa yathā hi palāyati ko ci naro dhanasaukhyamajānaku mūḍhamano /
children.translated_text: Like a man who, having found a treasure, runs away — a fool of deluded mind, not knowing the happiness of wealth —

children.text: tvamapi tathaiva hi rāgamajānanako yaḥ svayamāgatikāṃ na hi bhuñjasi kāminikām // Lal_21.99 //
children.translated_text: even so are you, not knowing passion: one who does not enjoy a loving woman who has come of her own accord!' // Lal_21.99 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvo 'nimiṣanayanaḥ prahasitavadanaḥ smitamukho 'vikopitairindriyairanabhisaṃskṛtairgātrairajihmo 'rakto 'duṣṭo 'mūḍhaḥ śailendravadaprakampyo 'navalīno 'navadīrṇo 'saṃpīḍitaḥ susaṃsthitayā buddhyā svādhīnena jñānamukhenātyantasuprahīṇatvātkleśānāṃ ślakṣṇayā madhurayā vācā brahmātirekeṇa ghopeṇa karaviṅkarutena svareṇa valgunā manojñena tāṃ māraduhitṝn gāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with unblinking eyes, with a laughing face, with a smiling countenance, with unperturbed senses, with unaffected limbs, straight, unattached, un-angered, undeluded, unshakable like the king of mountains, neither contracted nor distended, unoppressed, with well-established wisdom, with autonomous knowledge-faculty, through having perfectly abandoned the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — with smooth, sweet speech, with a voice surpassing <s>Brahmā</s>'s, melodious, [sounding] like a <s>karaviṅka</s> bird, charming, pleasing — he addressed those daughters of <s>Māra</s> in verses —

children.text: kāmā bho bahuduḥkhasaṃcayā duḥkhamūlā dhyānarddhītapasaṃ ca bhraṃsanī abudhānām /
children.translated_text: 'Sense-pleasures are a great accumulation of suffering, the root of suffering, and they destroy the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditations), supernatural powers, and austerities of the foolish!

children.text: na strīkāmaguṇebhi tṛptitāṃ vidumāhuḥ prajñātṛptikaro bhaviṣyahaṃ abudhānām // Lal_21.100 //
children.translated_text: The wise say there is never satisfaction from the pleasures of women — [but] I shall become the giver of the satisfaction of wisdom to the foolish! // Lal_21.100 //

children.text: kāmāṃ sevayato vivardhate puna tṛṣṇā pītvā vai lavaṇodakaṃ yathā naru kaści /
children.translated_text: For one who indulges in sense-pleasures, thirst only increases further — like a person who has drunk salt water;

children.text: nātmārthe ca parārthi bhotihā pratipanno ātmārthe ca parārtha utsuko bhavitāham // Lal_21.101 //
children.translated_text: nor is [such a one] devoted to others' welfare for his own sake — but I, devoted to my own welfare and that of others, shall [give both]! // Lal_21.101 //

children.text: phenābudbudatulyasaṃnibhaṃ tava rūpaṃ māyāraṅgamivā vithāpitaṃ svamatena /
children.translated_text: Your forms are similar to foam and bubbles, like a stage-play of illusion, created by your own minds;

children.text: krīḍā vai supineva adhruvā apinityā bālānāṃ sada cittamohanā abudhānām // Lal_21.102 //
children.translated_text: these sports are as impermanent and unstable as dreams — ever deluding the minds of the foolish and ignorant! // Lal_21.102 //

children.text: netrā budbudatulyasādṛśā tvacanaddhāḥ kaṭhinaṃ śoṇitapiṇḍamudrataṃ yatha gaṇḍam /
children.translated_text: The eyes are like bubbles, bound with skin; the cheeks are merely a sealed lump of blood, hard;

children.text: udaro mūtrapurīṣasaṃcayo asucokṣaḥ karmakleśasamutthito dukhayantraḥ // Lal_21.103 //
children.translated_text: the belly is a collection of urine and excrement, impure — a machine of suffering arisen from <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>! // Lal_21.103 //

children.text: saṃmūḍhā yahi bālabuddhayo na tu vijñāḥ śubhato kalpayamāna āśrayaṃ vitathena /
children.translated_text: Let the deluded ones of foolish understanding go — not the wise! — who imagine [this body] to be beautiful, grasping at [their] basis through what is false;

children.text: saṃsāre bahukāla saṃsarī duḥkhamūle anubhoktā nirayeṣu vedanā bahuduḥkhā // Lal_21.104 //
children.translated_text: wandering long in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the root of suffering, [they shall] experience extremely painful sensations in the hells! // Lal_21.104 //

children.text: śroṇi prasravate vigandhikā pratikūlā urūjaṅghakramāśca saṃsthitā yatha yantram /
children.translated_text: The hips emit putrid discharge, repulsive; the thighs, shanks, and feet are constructed like a machine;

children.text: bhūtaṃ yuṣmi ahaṃ nirīkṣamī yatha māyā hetupratyayataḥ pravartathā vitathena // Lal_21.105 //
children.translated_text: I look upon the truth in you — as upon an illusion — you proceed from causes and conditions through what is false! // Lal_21.105 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā kāmaguṇāṃśca nirguṇāṃ guṇahīnāṃ āryajñānapathasya utpathāṃ vipathāṃśca /
children.translated_text: Having seen that the strands of sense-pleasure are virtueless, devoid of virtue, off the path of noble knowledge, wrong paths,

children.text: viṣapatrāgnisamāṃ mahoragāṃ yatha kruddhāṃ bālā atra hi mūrchitā sukhasaṃjñāḥ // Lal_21.106 //
children.translated_text: like poison-leaves, fire, and an angry great serpent — fools here are intoxicated, perceiving [them as] pleasant! // Lal_21.106 //

children.text: kāmādāsu bhavīti yo nara pramadānāṃ śīle utpathi dhyāyi utpathi matihīno /
children.translated_text: A man who becomes [a slave] to desires among women — he is off the path of morality, off the path of meditation, bereft of wisdom;

children.text: jñāne so hi sudūri tiṣṭhate ratilolo yo 'sau dharmaratiṃ jahitvanā rami kāmaiḥ // Lal_21.107 //
children.translated_text: he stands far from knowledge — that pleasure-seeker who, having abandoned delight in <s>dharma</s>, delights in sense-pleasures! // Lal_21.107 //

children.text: no rāgeṇa sahī vasāmyahaṃ na ca doṣaiḥ no nairnityaaśubhaanātmabhirvasi sārdham /
children.translated_text: I do not dwell together with passion, nor with hatred; nor do I dwell with impermanence, impurity, and non-self —

children.text: ārātīyaratīyasaṃvaśena ca sārdhaṃ nirmuktaṃ mama cittu māruto gagane vā // Lal_21.108 //
children.translated_text: Released is my mind from the sway of <s>Ārātī</s> and <s>Ratī</s>, like the wind in the sky! // Lal_21.108 //

children.text: pūrṇaṃ sarvajagattvamīdṛśairyadiha syāt kalpaṃ tābhi sahā samosṛto vihareyam /
children.translated_text: Even if the whole world were filled with such women as these, and I were to dwell with them for a <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: no vā mahya khilaṃ na rajyanā na ca moho ākāśaḥsamatulyamānasā jina bhonti // Lal_21.109 //
children.translated_text: there would be no attachment in me, no passion, and no delusion — the <s>Jinas</s> are those whose minds are equal to space! // Lal_21.109 //

children.text: yadyapīha rudhirāsthivarjitāḥ devaapsara sunirmalāḥ śubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even though these divine <s>apsaras</s> are free of blood and bone, immaculate and beautiful,

children.text: te 'pi sarvi sumahadbhaye sthitāḥ nityabhāvarahitā aśāśvatāḥ // Lal_21.110 //
children.translated_text: they too are all subject to the great fear, devoid of permanent nature, impermanent! // Lal_21.110 //

body.text: atha khalu tā māraduhitaraḥ suśikṣitāḥ strīmāyāsu bhūyasyā mātrayā rāgamadadarpaṃ saṃjanayya ceṣṭāmupadarśya gātrāṇi vibhūṣayitvā strīmāyāmupadarśya bodhisattvaṃ pralobhayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then those daughters of <s>Māra</s>, well-trained in feminine wiles, generating pride of passion and arrogance to an even greater degree, displaying coquettish gestures, adorning their limbs, and exhibiting feminine allurements, tempted the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this was said —

children.text: tṛṣṇaratī ratiśca sahitā pramadavara madhurā
children.translated_text: <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (Craving), <s>Ratī</s> (Delight), and <s>Rati</s> (Pleasure), together — foremost among lovely women, sweet-voiced,

children.text: mārasamīritāḥ sulalitā tvaritamupagatāḥ /
children.translated_text: sent forth by <s>Māra</s>, graceful, approached swiftly.

children.text: vāyusamīhitā kisalayāstaruṇatarulatā
children.translated_text: Like young creepers and tender tree-branches stirred by the wind,

children.text: nṛttata lobhayaṃ nṛpasutaṃ drumaviṭapagatam // Lal_21.111 //
children.translated_text: they danced, tempting the prince who sat at the tree-trunk. // Lal_21.111 //

body.text:
eṣa vasantakālasamayaḥ pravara ṛtuvaro
nārinarāṇa harṣaṇakaro nihatatamarajaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the springtime season, the finest of seasons, bringing joy to women and men, with darkness dispelled;

body.text: kokilahaṃsamoraraviśā dvijagaṇakalilaḥ
body.translated_text: teeming with flocks of birds — cuckoos, swans, peacocks, and warblers —

body.text: kāla upasthito 'nubhavituṃ madanaguṇaratim // Lal_21.112 //
body.translated_text: the time has come to enjoy the pleasures of love! // Lal_21.112 //

children.text: kalpasahasraśīlanirato vratatapacarito
children.translated_text: Devoted to morality for a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, practicing vows and austerities,

children.text: niścala śailarājasadṛśastaruṇaravivapuḥ /
children.translated_text: unshakable like the king of mountains, with a body radiant as the young sun,

children.text: meghaninādavalguvacano mṛgapatininado
children.translated_text: with a voice melodious as thunder, with a roar like the lord of beasts,

children.text: vacanamuvāca so 'rthasahitaṃ jagati hitakaraḥ // Lal_21.113 //
children.translated_text: he spoke words full of meaning, beneficial to the world: // Lal_21.113 //

children.text: kāmavivāda vaira kalahā maraṇabhayakarā
children.translated_text: Sensual pleasures bring disputes, enmity, quarrels, and the fear of death;

children.text: bālajanopasevita sadā budhajanarahitā /
children.translated_text: they are always frequented by the foolish, avoided by the wise.

children.text: prāptayu kālu yatra sugatairamṛtamadhigataṃ
children.translated_text: The time has come when the <s>Sugatas</s> attained the deathless;

children.text: adya bhaviṣya māru jiniyā daśabalu arahān // Lal_21.114 //
children.translated_text: today <s>Māra</s> shall be conquered, and I shall become a <s>Daśabala</s> (One of Ten Powers), an <s>Arhat</s>! // Lal_21.114 //

children.text: māya nidarśayantiya vadaṃ śṛṇu kamalamukhā
children.translated_text: [They replied:] "Displaying illusions, we say — listen, O lotus-faced one!

children.text: rāju bhaviṣyaseśvaravaraḥ kṣitipati balavān /
children.translated_text: You shall become a king, a supreme sovereign, a mighty lord of the earth!

children.text: tūryasahasrasaṃprabhaṇite pramadavaragaṇe
children.translated_text: Amidst thousands of musical instruments and troupes of beautiful women,

children.text: kiṃ muniveṣakena bhavato virama rati bhajā // Lal_21.115 //
children.translated_text: what is the use of this ascetic garb? Desist! Enjoy pleasures!" // Lal_21.115 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: bheṣyi ahaṃ hi rāju tribhave divi bhuvi mahito
children.translated_text: "I shall indeed be a king in the three realms, honored in heaven and on earth,

children.text: īśvaru dharmacakracaraṇo daśabalu balavān /
children.translated_text: a sovereign, a turner of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, a <s>Daśabala</s>, mighty in power!

children.text: śaikṣyaaśaikṣyaputranayutaiḥ satatasamitamabhinato
children.translated_text: Constantly and perpetually bowed to by tens of thousands of sons both in training and beyond training,

children.text: dharmaratī ramiṣyi viṣayairna rami ramati manaḥ // Lal_21.116 //
children.translated_text: I shall delight in the joy of <s>Dharma</s>; my mind does not delight in sense-objects, nor does it take pleasure [in them]." // Lal_21.116 //

body.text: tā āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: They said —

children.text: yāva ca yauvanaṃ na galitaṃ prathamavayadharo
children.translated_text: "As long as your youth has not faded, while you are in the prime of life,

children.text: yāva ca vyādhi nākramati te na ca jara asitā /
children.translated_text: as long as disease does not assail you and old age has not come with its dark hair,

children.text: yāva ca rūpayauvanadharo vayamapi ca sukhī
children.translated_text: as long as you possess beauty and youth, and we too are joyful —

children.text: tāva nu bhuṅkṣva kāmaratayaḥ prahasitavadanaḥ // Lal_21.117 //
children.translated_text: so long, enjoy the pleasures of love with a smiling face!" // Lal_21.117 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: yāva ca durlabho 'dya labhitaḥ kṣaṇavara amṛto
children.translated_text: "As long as this rare, supreme, deathless moment has been obtained today,

children.text: yāva ca varjitā kṣaṇadukhā asurasurapure /
children.translated_text: as long as the sufferings of unfavorable births in the realms of <s>asuras</s> and gods have been avoided,

children.text: yāva jarā ca vyādhimaraṇaṃ na kupitarūpavaṃ
children.translated_text: as long as old age, disease, and death have not assumed their wrathful forms,

children.text: tāvahu bhāvayiṣyi supathaṃ abhayapuragamam // Lal_21.118 //
children.translated_text: so long shall I cultivate the good path leading to the city of fearlessness!" // Lal_21.118 //

body.text: tā āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: They said —

children.text: devapurālaye 'psaravṛtastridaśapatirivā yāmasuyāmasaṃtuṣitake amaravarastuto /
children.translated_text: "Like <s>Tridaśapati</s> (Indra) surrounded by <s>apsaras</s> in the divine palace, in the <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, and <s>Tuṣita</s> [heavens], praised by the foremost immortals,

children.text: mārapure ca kāmaratayaḥ pramadavaśagataḥ krīḍyanubhuṅkṣva asmabhi sahā vipularatikaraḥ // Lal_21.119 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>Māra</s>'s abode with sensual delights, subject to lovely women — play and enjoy with us, bestowers of abundant pleasure!" // Lal_21.119 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: kāma tṛṇosabinducapalā śaradaghanasamā pannagakanyaroṣasadṛśā bhṛśabhayakaraṇā /
children.translated_text: "Sensual pleasures are fickle as dewdrops on grass, like autumn clouds, like the anger of serpent maidens — causing extreme fear!

children.text: śakrasuyāmadevatuṣitā namucivaśagatāḥ ko 'tra rameta naryabhilaṣite vyasanaparigate // Lal_21.120 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Suyāma</s>, and the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods are all under <s>Namuci</s>'s sway — who would delight in that which is desired by women, beset by calamity?" // Lal_21.120 //

body.text: tā āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: They said —

children.text: puṣpita paśyimāṃ taruvarāṃ taruṇakisalayāṃ kokilajīvajīvakarutā madhukaravirutā /
children.translated_text: "Behold these flowering trees with tender shoots, resounding with the cries of cuckoos and <s>jīvaṃjīvakas</s>, humming with bees!

children.text: snigdhasunīlakuñcitamṛduṃ dharaṇitalaruhe kiṃ narasiṃha sevita vane ramasu yuvatibhiḥ // Lal_21.121 //
children.translated_text: On this smooth, dark-green, curly, soft ground-growing [grass] — why, O lion among men, do you dwell in the forest? Take delight with young women!" // Lal_21.121 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: kālavaśātpuṣpita ime kisalaya taravo bhukṣapipāsitā madhukarāḥ kusumamabhigatāḥ /
children.translated_text: "By the power of time these trees and shoots blossom; the bees, afflicted by hunger and thirst, approach the flowers.

children.text: bhāskaru śoṣayiṣyati yadā dharaṇitalaruhāṃ pūrvajinopabhuktamamṛtaṃ vyavasitamiha me // Lal_21.122 //
children.translated_text: When the sun dries up these ground-growing [plants] — the deathless [nectar] enjoyed by former <s>Jinas</s> is what I have resolved upon here!" // Lal_21.122 //

body.text: māraduhitara āhuḥ -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>'s daughters said —

children.text: prekṣahi tāva candravadanā navanalininibhā vāca manojña ślakṣṇa daśanā himarajatanibhā /
children.translated_text: "Behold moon-faced ones with lotus-like [eyes], sweet-voiced, with smooth teeth, white as snow and silver!

children.text: īdṛśa durlabhā surapure kuta manujapure te tvaya labdha ye suravarairabhilaṣita sadā // Lal_21.123 //
children.translated_text: Such women are rare even in the divine realm, how much more in the human realm — you have obtained those who are always desired by the chief gods!" // Lal_21.123 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said —

children.text: paśyami kāyamedhyamaśuciṃ kṛmikulabharitaṃ
children.translated_text: "I see this body as impure, unclean, filled with colonies of worms,

children.text: jarjaramitvaraṃ ca bhiduraṃ asukhaparigatam /
children.translated_text: decrepit, perishable, fragile, and beset by suffering.

children.text: yatsacarācarasya jagataḥ paramasukhakaraṃ
children.translated_text: That which brings supreme happiness to the world of moving and unmoving beings —

children.text: tatpadamacyutaṃ pratilabhe budhajanamahitam // Lal_21.124 //
children.translated_text: that imperishable state I shall attain, honored by the wise!" // Lal_21.124 //

children.text: tā catuṣaṣṭikāmalalitāni camanubhaviyā
children.translated_text: [They], having displayed sixty-four erotic arts,

children.text: nūpuramekhalā abhihanī vigalitavasanā /
children.translated_text: striking their anklets and girdles, with garments loosened,

children.text: kāmaśarāhatāḥ samadanāḥ prahasitavadanāḥ
children.translated_text: struck by the arrows of love, intoxicated, with smiling faces, [said:]

children.text: kiṃ tava āryaputra vikṛtaṃ yadi na bhajase // Lal_21.125 //
children.translated_text: "What defect do you see in us, O noble son, that you do not enjoy [us]?" // Lal_21.125 //

children.text: sarvabhaveṣu doṣa vidito 'vaci vidhutarajā
children.translated_text: "The faults in all existences are known to me — I am one whose dust has been shaken off, free from stain.

children.text: kāmasiśaktiśūlasadṛśāḥ samadhukṣurasamāḥ /
children.translated_text: Sensual pleasures are like spears, pikes, and tridents, like honey on razors!

children.text: sarpaśirognikarṣusadṛśāḥ suvidita iha me
children.translated_text: They are like serpent-heads and burning embers — this is well-known to me.

children.text: tenahu nārisaṃgha tyajamī guṇahara pramadāḥ // Lal_21.126 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I abandon the company of women — [those] thieves of virtue, beguiling women!" // Lal_21.126 //

children.text: tā bahubhiḥ prakāranayutaiḥ pramadaguṇakaraiḥ
children.translated_text: They, with many thousands of devices and womanly charms,

children.text: lobhayituṃ na śeku sugataṃ gajakarabhagatim /
children.translated_text: were unable to tempt the <s>Sugata</s>, who moved with the gait of a bull elephant.

children.text: lajjihirotrapāttu munina prapatiṣu caraṇe
children.translated_text: Overcome by shame and modesty, falling at the feet of the sage,

children.text: gauravu tuṣṭa prema janiyā staviṣu hitakaram // Lal_21.127 //
children.translated_text: generating reverence, satisfaction, and affection, they praised the benefactor: // Lal_21.127 //

children.text: nirmalapadmagarbhasadṛśā śaradiśaśimukhā
children.translated_text: "O you whose purity is like the heart of a lotus, whose face is like the moon in autumn,

children.text: sarpihutārcitejasadṛśā kanakagirinibhā /
children.translated_text: whose splendor is like a fire fed with clarified butter, resembling a golden mountain —

children.text: sidhyatu cintitā ti praṇidhi bhavaśatacaritā
children.translated_text: may your aspiration, practiced through hundreds of existences, be fulfilled!

children.text: svāmupatīrya tāraya jagadvyasanaparigatam // Lal_21.128 //
children.translated_text: Having crossed over yourself, ferry across the world beset by calamity!" // Lal_21.128 //

children.text: tā karṇikāracampakanibhaṃ staviya bahuvidhaṃ
children.translated_text: Having praised him who was like a <s>karṇikāra</s> and <s>campaka</s> flower in many ways,

children.text: kṛtva pradakṣiṇaṃ atiśayaṃ giririva acalam /
children.translated_text: and having circumambulated that supreme one, immovable like a mountain,

children.text: gatva piturnipatya śirasā idamavaci giraṃ
children.translated_text: they went and fell at their father's head, and spoke these words:

children.text: sādhvasa naṃ hi tāta pratighaṃ amaranaraguroḥ // Lal_21.129 //
children.translated_text: "Do not, O father, harbor hostility against the teacher of gods and men!" // Lal_21.129 //

children.text: paśyati padmapatranayanaḥ prahasitavadano
children.translated_text: "He gazes with lotus-petal eyes, with a smiling face;

children.text: nāpi saraktu prekṣati janaṃ na pi ca sabhṛkuṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: he looks at people without attachment and without frowning.

children.text: meru caleya śuṣya udadhiḥ śaśiravi prapate
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s> may tremble, the ocean may dry up, the sun and moon may fall,

children.text: naiva sa doṣadarśi tribhave pramadavaśa gamiyā // Lal_21.130 //
children.translated_text: but never shall that seer of faults in the three realms come under the sway of women!" // Lal_21.130 //

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyānidaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā bhūyasyā mātrayā duḥkhito durmanā anāttamanāḥ praduṣṭamanāstāṃ svaduhitṝnāmantrayate sma - kathaṃ bho na śakyate sa bodhimaṇḍādutthāpayitum? mā khalu mūḍhaḥ ajño 'tha yuṣmākaṃ rūpākṛtiṃ na paśyati?
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, having heard these words, being even more distressed, sorrowful, displeased, and with corrupted mind, addressed his own daughters: "What, can he not be raised from the seat of awakening? Is the fool, the ignorant one, unable to see your beautiful forms?"

body.text: atha khalu tā māraduhitaraḥ svapitaraṃ gāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those daughters of <s>Māra</s> replied to their father in verses —

body.text: ślakṣṇā madhuraṃ ca bhāṣate na ca rakto guru guhyaṃ ca nirīkṣate na ca duṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: "He speaks gently and sweetly, yet he is not enamored; he looks at what is private, yet he is not corrupt;

body.text: īryāṃ caryāṃ ca prekṣate na ca mūḍhaḥ kāyā sarva paneti āśayo sugabhīraḥ // Lal_21.131 //
body.translated_text: he observes conduct and behavior, yet he is not deluded; his disposition is profoundly deep, knowing all bodies thoroughly!" // Lal_21.131 //

children.text: niḥsaṃśayena viditāḥ pṛthu istridoṣāḥ kāmairviraktamanaso na ca rāgaraktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Without doubt, the manifold faults of women are known to him — his mind is dispassionate toward pleasures, and he is not stained by desire.

children.text: naivāstyasau divi bhuvīha naraḥ suro vā yastasya cittacaritaṃ parijānayeyā // Lal_21.132 //
children.translated_text: There exists no one — neither human nor god, in heaven or on earth — who could comprehend the conduct of his mind!" // Lal_21.132 //

children.text: yā istrimāya upadarśita tatra tāta pravilīyu tasya hṛdayaṃ bhaviyaḥ sarāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Whatever feminine illusions were displayed there, O father — [if] his heart should melt, he would become one with passion.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭa ekamapi kampitu nāsya cittaṃ śailendrarāja iva tiṣṭhati so 'prakampyaḥ // Lal_21.133 //
children.translated_text: Having seen all that, not even a single tremor arose in his mind — he stands like the lord of the king of mountains, unshakable!" // Lal_21.133 //

children.text: śatapuṇyatejabharito guṇatejapūrṇaḥ śīle tapasmi carito bahukalpakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Filled with the splendor of a hundred merits, replete with the radiance of virtues,

children.text: brahmā ca deva śubhateja viśuddhasattvā mūrdhnā nipatya caraṇeṣu namanti tasmai // Lal_21.134 //
children.translated_text: he has practiced morality and austerity for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — <s>Brahmā</s> and the gods of pure splendor and purified beings bow at his feet with their heads!" // Lal_21.134 //

children.text: niḥsaṃśayena vinihatya sa mārasenāṃ pūrve jinānumata prāpsyati agrabodhim /
children.translated_text: "Without doubt he will vanquish <s>Māra</s>'s army and, following the former <s>Jinas</s>, will attain supreme awakening!

children.text: tātā na rocati hi no va raṇe vivāde balavatsu vigrahu sukṛcchra ayaṃ prayogaḥ // Lal_21.135 //
children.translated_text: O father, we find no pleasure in battle and conflict — strife with the powerful is extremely difficult; this enterprise [is futile]!" // Lal_21.135 //

children.text: prekṣasva tāta gagane maṇiratnacūḍā saṃbodhisattvanayutāḥ sthita gauraveṇa /
children.translated_text: "Behold, father, in the sky the jewel-crested <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in their tens of thousands stand in reverence!

children.text: ratnākarā kusumadāmavicitritāṅgā saṃprekṣitā daśabalairiha pujanārtham // Lal_21.136 //
children.translated_text: Mines of jewels, their limbs adorned with garlands of flowers — they gaze upon the <s>Daśabala</s> for the purpose of worship!" // Lal_21.136 //

children.text: ye cetanā api ca ye ca acetanā ca vṛkṣāśca śaila garūḍendrasurendrayakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who are sentient and those who are insentient — trees, mountains, <s>Garuḍa</s>-lords, <s>Surendra</s>s, and <s>Yakṣas</s> —

children.text: abhyonatā abhimukhā guṇaparvatasya śreyo bhave pratinivartitumadya tāta // Lal_21.137 //
children.translated_text: all bow facing that mountain of virtues. Better to turn back today, O father!" // Lal_21.137 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

body.text: na taṃ taredyasya na pāramuttare na taṃ khanedyasya na mūlamuddharet /
body.translated_text: "One should not cross that whose further shore one cannot reach; one should not dig up that whose root one cannot extract;

body.text: na kopayettaṃ kṣamayetpunopi taṃ kuryānna taṃ yena bhavecca durmanāḥ // Lal_21.138 //
body.translated_text: one should not provoke him whom one should rather appease; one should not do that by which one would become sorrowful!" // Lal_21.138 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastasmin samaye 'ṣṭau bodhivṛkṣadevatāḥ / tadyathā - śrīḥ vṛddhiḥ tapā śreyasī viduḥ ojobalā satyavādinī samaṅginī ca / tā etā bodhisattvaṃ saṃpūjya ṣoḍaśabhirākārairbodhisattvaṃ śriyā vardhayanti sma, abhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at that time there were eight <s>Bodhi</s>-tree deities, namely: <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), <s>Vṛddhi</s> (Increase), <s>Tapā</s> (Warmth), <s>Śreyasī</s> (Auspiciousness), <s>Vidu</s> (Wise), <s>Ojobalā</s> (Vigor-Strength), <s>Satyavādinī</s> (Truth-Speaker), and <s>Samaṅginī</s> (All-Endowed). They, having worshipped the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, glorified the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with sixteen aspects of fortune, and praised him thus —

children.text: upaśobhase tvaṃ viśuddhasattva candra iva śuklapakṣe /
children.translated_text: "You shine, O purified being, like the moon in the bright half!

children.text: abhivirocase tvaṃ viśuddhabuddha sūrya iva prodayamānaḥ // Lal_21.139 //
children.translated_text: You radiate, O purified <s>Buddha</s>, like the rising sun! // Lal_21.139 //

children.text: praphullitastvaṃ viśuddhasattva padmamiva vārimadhye /
children.translated_text: "You are in full bloom, O purified being, like a lotus in the midst of water!

children.text: nadasi ttvaṃ viśuddhasattva kesarīva vanarājāvanucārī // Lal_21.140 //
children.translated_text: You roar, O purified being, like a lion roaming in the forest-realm! // Lal_21.140 //

children.text: vibhrājase tvaṃ agrasattva parvatarāja iva sāgaramadhye /
children.translated_text: "You shine forth, O supreme being, like the king of mountains in the midst of the ocean!

children.text: abhyudgatastvaṃ viśuddhasattva cakravāla iva parvataḥ // Lal_21.141 //
children.translated_text: You tower aloft, O purified being, like <s>Cakravāḍa</s> mountain! // Lal_21.141 //

children.text: duravagāhastvaṃ agrasattva jaladhara ivra ratnasaṃpūrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are unfathomable, O supreme being, like a rain-cloud filled with jewels!

children.text: vistīrṇabuddhirasi lokanātha gaganamivāparyantam // Lal_21.142 //
children.translated_text: Your wisdom is vast, O Lord of the World, limitless like the sky! // Lal_21.142 //

children.text: susthitabuddhirasi viśuddhasattva dharaṇitalavatsarvasattvopajīvyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your wisdom is firm, O purified being — like the surface of the earth, you sustain all beings!

children.text: akaluṣabuddhirasi agrasattva anavatapta iva saraḥ sadā prasannaḥ // Lal_21.143 //
children.translated_text: Your wisdom is unstained, O supreme being — like Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, always clear! // Lal_21.143 //

children.text: aniketabuddhistvaṃ agrasattva māruta iva sarvaloke sadāprasaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Your wisdom is homeless, O supreme being — like the wind, ever active in all worlds!

children.text: durāsadasttvaṃ agrasattva tejorāja iva sarvamanyunā prahīnaḥ // Lal_21.144 //
children.translated_text: You are unapproachable, O supreme being — like the lord of fire, free from all wrath! // Lal_21.144 //

children.text: balavānasi tvaṃ agrasattva nārāyaṇa iva durdharṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are mighty, O supreme being — invincible like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!

children.text: dṛḍhasamādānastvaṃ lokanātha anutthātā bodhimaṇḍā // Lal_21.145 //
children.translated_text: Your resolve is firm, O Lord of the World — you shall not rise from the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>! // Lal_21.145 //

children.text: anivartyastvaṃ agrasattva indrakarotsṛṣṭa iva vajraḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are irreversible, O supreme being — like a thunderbolt hurled from <s>Indra</s>'s hand!

children.text: sulabdhalābhastvaṃ agrasattva daśabalasamagryo 'cirādbhaviṣyasi // Lal_21.146 //
children.translated_text: You have gained well, O supreme being — you shall soon become one who possesses all ten powers!" // Lal_21.146 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo bodhivṛkṣadevatāḥ ṣoḍaśākāraṃ bodhisattvaṃ śriyā vardhayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree deities glorified the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with these sixteen aspects of fortune. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavaḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākārairmāraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ durbalaṃ kurvanti sma / katamaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ? tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Thereupon, O monks, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) gods weakened <s>Māra</s> the Evil One with sixteen aspects. With which sixteen? Namely —

children.text: dhvastastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ jīrṇakroñca iva dhyāyase /
children.translated_text: "You are ruined, O Evil One — you brood like an aged heron!

children.text: durbalastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ jīrṇagaja iva paṅkamagraḥ // Lal_21.147 //
children.translated_text: You are feeble, O Evil One — like an aged elephant mired in mud! // Lal_21.147 //

children.text: ekākyasi tvaṃ pāpīyaṃ nirjita iva śūrapratijñaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are alone, O Evil One — like a defeated one who had boasted of heroism!

children.text: advitīyastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ aṭavyāṃ tyakta iva rogārtaḥ // Lal_21.148 //
children.translated_text: You are without a companion, O Evil One — like one afflicted by disease, abandoned in the wilderness! // Lal_21.148 //

children.text: abalastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ bhārakliṣṭa iva balīvardaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are powerless, O Evil One — like an ox oppressed by its burden!

children.text: apaviddhastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ vātakṣipta iva taruḥ // Lal_21.149 //
children.translated_text: You are cast away, O Evil One — like a tree uprooted by the wind! // Lal_21.149 //

children.text: kupathasthitasvaṃ pāpīyaṃ mārgabhraṣṭa iva sārthikaḥ /
children.translated_text: "You are on a wrong path, O Evil One — like a caravan-leader who has lost the way!

children.text: dīnahīnastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ matsariṇa iva daridrapuruṣaḥ // Lal_21.150 //
children.translated_text: You are wretched and lowly, O Evil One, like a destitute man full of envy! // Lal_21.150 //

children.text: mukharastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ vāyasa iva pragalbhaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are loud-mouthed, O Evil One, impudent like a crow;

children.text: mānābhibhūtastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ akṛtajña iva ḍhurvinītaḥ // Lal_21.151 //
children.translated_text: overcome by pride, O Evil One, ungrateful like one broken to the yoke! // Lal_21.151 //

children.text: palāyiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ koṣṭuka iva siṃhanādena /
children.translated_text: You shall flee today, O Evil One, like a jackal at the lion's roar;

children.text: vidhuneṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ vairambhavāyuvikṣipta iva pakṣī // Lal_21.152 //
children.translated_text: you shall be shaken today, O Evil One, like a bird tossed by a whirlwind! // Lal_21.152 //

children.text: akālajñastvaṃ pāpīyaṃ puṇyaparikṣīṇa iva bhaikṣukaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are ignorant of timing, O Evil One, like a beggar whose merit is exhausted;

children.text: vivarjiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bhinnabhājanabhiva pāṃśupratipūrṇam // Lal_21.153 //
children.translated_text: you shall be cast aside today, O Evil One, like a broken vessel filled with dust! // Lal_21.153 //

children.text: nigṛhīṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena mantreṇevoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: You shall be subdued today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as serpents by a spell;

children.text: sarvabalaprahīṇo 'si pāpīyaṃ chinnakaracaraṇa ivoruṇḍaḥ // Lal_21.154 //
children.translated_text: you are bereft of all strength, O Evil One, like a torso with hands and feet cut off! // Lal_21.154 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākārairmāraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ durbalamakārṣuḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika Devaputras</s> weakened <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, in sixteen ways. //

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo bodhiparicārikā devaputrāḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākārairmāraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ vichacdayanti sma / katamaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ? tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Thereupon, O monks, the <s>Devaputras</s> who attend the <s>Bodhi</s>[-seat] discouraged <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, in sixteen ways. Which sixteen? As follows —

children.text: adya tvaṃ pāpīyaṃ nirjeṣyase bodhisattvena parasainya iva śūreṇa /
children.translated_text: Today you, O Evil One, shall be conquered by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as an enemy army by a hero;

children.text: nigṛhīṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena durbalamalla iva mahāmallena // Lal_21.155 //
children.translated_text: you shall be subdued today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a weak wrestler by a mighty wrestler! // Lal_21.155 //

children.text: abhibhaviṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena khadyotakamiva sūryamaṇḍalena /
children.translated_text: You shall be overpowered today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a firefly by the disk of the sun;

children.text: vidhvaṃsayiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena muñjamuṣṭimiva mahāmārutena // Lal_21.156 //
children.translated_text: you shall be scattered today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a handful of <s>muñja</s>-grass by a great wind! // Lal_21.156 //

children.text: vitrāsiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena kesariṇeva śṛgālaḥ /
children.translated_text: You shall be frightened today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a jackal by a lion;

children.text: prapātiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsāla iva mūlachinnam // Lal_21.157 //
children.translated_text: you shall fall today, O Evil One, before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a great <s>sāla</s>-tree cut at the root! // Lal_21.157 //

children.text: vilopsyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvenāmitranagaramiva mahārājena /
children.translated_text: You shall be plundered today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as an enemy city by a great king;

children.text: viśoṣiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena goṣpadavārīva mahātapena // Lal_21.158 //
children.translated_text: you shall be dried up today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as water in a cow's hoofprint by great heat! // Lal_21.158 //

children.text: palāyiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena vadhyavimukta iva dhūrtapuruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: You shall flee today, O Evil One, from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like a scoundrel released from execution;

children.text: udbhrāmiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena agnidāheneva madhukaravṛndam // Lal_21.159 //
children.translated_text: you shall be scattered today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a swarm of bees by a fire! // Lal_21.159 //

children.text: roṣiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena rāṣṭrabhraṣṭa iva dharmarājaḥ /
children.translated_text: You shall rage today, O Evil One, against the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like a righteous king banished from his realm;

children.text: dhyāyiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena jīrṇakroñca iva lūnapakṣaḥ // Lal_21.160 //
children.translated_text: you shall brood today, O Evil One, because of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like an aged <s>krauñca</s>-crane with clipped wings! // Lal_21.160 //

children.text: vibhartsyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena kṣīṇapathyādana ivāṭavīkāntāre /
children.translated_text: You shall be reproached today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like one whose provisions are exhausted in a wilderness;

children.text: vilapiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena bhinnayānapātra iva mahārṇave // Lal_21.161 //
children.translated_text: you shall lament today, O Evil One, because of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, like one whose vessel is wrecked in the great ocean! // Lal_21.161 //

children.text: āmlāyiṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena kalpadāha iva tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ /
children.translated_text: You shall wither today, O Evil One, before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as grasses and trees in the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>;

children.text: vikiriṣyase tvamadya pāpīyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāvajreṇeva girikūṭam // Lal_21.162 //
children.translated_text: you shall be shattered today, O Evil One, by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as a mountain peak by a great <s>vajra</s>! // Lal_21.162 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo bodhiparicārikā devaputrāḥ ṣoḍaśākārairmāraṃ vicchandayanti sma / na ca māraḥ pāpīyān vinivartate sma //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, the <s>Devaputras</s> who attend the <s>Bodhi</s>[-seat] discouraged <s>Māra</s> in sixteen ways. But <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One, did not turn back. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said:

children.text: bhūtāṃ codana śrutva devatagaṇā na nivartate so 'ntako
children.translated_text: Having heard the true exhortation of the host of gods, that Destroyer does not turn back:

children.text: ucchethā hanathā vilumpatha imāṃ mā dāsyathā jīvitam /
children.translated_text: 'Cut him down! Strike him! Plunder him! Do not grant him his life!

children.text: eṣottīrṇa svayaṃ mamāpi viṣayāṃ tāriṣyate cāparāṃ
children.translated_text: This one, having crossed over himself from my domain too, will ferry others across;

children.text: nānyaṃ mokṣa vademi kiṃci śramaṇe utthāpayetprakramet // Lal_21.163 //
children.translated_text: I declare no other release whatsoever — make this ascetic arise and depart!' // Lal_21.163 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: meruḥ parvatarāja sthānatu cale sarvaṃ jaganno bhavet
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains, move from its place — let the entire world cease to exist;

children.text: sarve tārakasaṃgha bhūmi prapate sajyotiṣendurnabhāt /
children.translated_text: let all the hosts of stars fall to earth from the sky, together with the moon and luminaries;

children.text: sarvā sattva kareya ekamatayaḥ śuṣyenmahāsāgaro
children.translated_text: let all beings be of one mind — let the great ocean dry up —

children.text: na tveva drumarājamūlupagataścālyet asmadvidhaḥ // Lal_21.164 //
children.translated_text: yet one such as I, who has reached the base of the king of trees, shall never be moved!' // Lal_21.164 //

body.text: māra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: kāmeśvaro 'smi vasitā iha sarvaloke devā sadānavagaṇā manujāśca tiryā /
children.translated_text: 'I am the lord of desires, the ruler here of the entire world — gods, together with <s>Dānava</s> hosts, humans, and animals;

children.text: vyāptā mayā mama vaśena ca yānti sarve uttiṣṭha mahya viṣayastha vacaṃ kuruṣva // Lal_21.165 //
children.translated_text: all are pervaded by me and go under my power — arise! Remain in my domain and obey my word!' // Lal_21.165 //

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: kāmeśvaro 'si yadi vyaktamanīśvaro 'si dharmeśvaro 'hamapi paśyasi tattvato mām /
children.translated_text: 'If you are the lord of desires, clearly you are no [true] lord — I too am the lord of <s>dharma</s>; behold me in truth!

children.text: kāmeśvaro 'si yadi durgati na prayāsi prāpsyāmi bodhimavaśasya tu paśyataste // Lal_21.166 //
children.translated_text: If you are the lord of desires, [then] you do not go to a bad destination? I shall attain awakening — behold, you who are powerless!' // Lal_21.166 //

body.text: māra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: ekātmakaḥ śramaṇa kiṃ prakaroṣi raṇye yaṃ prārthayasyasulabhaḥ khalu saṃprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are alone, O ascetic — what will you accomplish in this wilderness? What you seek is indeed hard to obtain;

children.text: bhṛgvaṅgiraprabhṛtibhistapaso prayatnā prāptaṃ na tatpadavaraṃ manujaḥ kutastvam // Lal_21.167 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and others, despite their efforts in <s>tapas</s> (austerity), that supreme state was not attained — you are merely human, how then you?' // Lal_21.167 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

body.text: ajñānapūrvaku tapo ṛṣibhiḥ pratapto krodhābhibhūtamatibhirdivalokakāmaiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>tapas</s> performed by those <s>ṛṣis</s> was preceded by ignorance — they were overcome by anger, desiring the world of heaven;

body.text: nityaṃ na nityamiti cātmani saṃśrayadbhiḥ mokṣaṃ ca deśagamanasthitamāśrayadbhiḥ // Lal_21.168 //
body.translated_text: taking refuge in the self as either permanent or impermanent, and resorting to liberation as a going-to and abiding-in a particular place. // Lal_21.168 //

children.text: te tatvato 'rtharahitāḥ puruṣaṃ vadanti vyāpiṃ pradeśagata śāśvatamāhureke /
children.translated_text: They, devoid of true meaning, speak of a <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) — all-pervading, yet located in a specific place; some declare [it] eternal;

children.text: mūrtaṃ na mūrtamaguṇaṃ guṇināṃ tathaiva kartā na karta iti cāpyapare bruvanti // Lal_21.169 //
children.translated_text: embodied or formless, without qualities yet possessing qualities — a doer or a non-doer — thus also others declare. // Lal_21.169 //

children.text: prāpyādya bodhi virajāmiha cāsanasthaḥ tvāṃ jitva māra vihataṃ sabalaṃ sasainyam /
children.translated_text: Having attained awakening today, I shall become free from passion, seated here; having conquered you, O <s>Māra</s>, struck down with your forces and army,

children.text: varteṣyi asya jagataḥ prabhavodbhavaṃ ca nirvāṇa duḥkhaśamanaṃ tatha śītibhāvam // Lal_21.170 //
children.translated_text: I shall set in motion for this world [the teaching of] arising and origination, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the quelling of suffering, and the state of peace.' // Lal_21.170 //

children.text: māraḥ kruddho duṣṭo ruṣṭaḥ paruṣagira puna tu bhaṇate gṛhāṇa sugautamaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, angry, wicked, enraged, speaking harsh words, said again: 'Seize this <s>Gautama</s>!

children.text: eṣo hyeko 'raṇye nyasto grahiya mama puratu vrajathā laghuṃ vaśu kurvathā /
children.translated_text: This one is alone, cast in the wilderness — grab him! Come before me! Quickly bring him under control!

children.text: śīghraṃ gatvā mahyaṃ gehe haḍinigaḍayugalavikṛtaṃ karotha duvārikaṃ
children.translated_text: Go swiftly — in my house, put him in chains and fetters, make him a doorkeeper!

children.text: svā maṃ drakṣye duḥkhenārtaṃ bahuvividhajavitaravitaṃ marūṇa va ceṭakam // Lal_21.171 //
children.translated_text: Then I shall see him afflicted with suffering, tormented in many varied ways — a servant of the <s>Marutas</s>!' // Lal_21.171 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
