body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: śakyākāśe lekhyaṃ citraṃ bahuvividhavikṛta padaśaḥ prakartu pṛthakpṛthak
children.translated_text: 'One may paint a picture in the sky, with manifold transformations, stroke by stroke, each separately;

children.text: śakyo vāyuḥ pāśairbaddhuṃ diśavidiśagamanajavito nareṇa suyatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: one may bind the wind with ropes, even as it rushes swiftly in every direction, with great effort by a man;

children.text: śakyā kartuṃ candrādityau tamatimiravitimirakarau nabho 'dya mahītalaṃ
children.translated_text: one may make the moon and sun — dispellers of the darkness of darkness — fall from the sky to the earth today;

children.text: śakyo nāhaṃ tvatsādṛśyairbahubhirapi gaṇanavirutairdrumātpraticālitum // Lal_21.172 //
children.translated_text: yet I cannot be moved from the tree by countless [armies] like yours!' // Lal_21.172 //

children.text: abhyutthitā balavatī namuceścamū sā hākāraśaṅkharavabherimṛdaṅgaśabdaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The mighty army of <s>Namuci</s> arose, with the sounds of battle-cries, conches, drums, and <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>;

children.text: ha putra vatsa dayitā kimasi pranaṣṭo dṛṣṭvā imāṃ namucisenamatīva bhīmām // Lal_21.173 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, son! Dear child! Are you lost, having seen this exceedingly terrible army of <s>Namuci</s>?' // Lal_21.173 //

children.text: jāmbūnadākanakacampakagarbhagaurā sukumāra devanarasaṃstuta pūjanīya /
children.translated_text: 'O delicate one, fair as the heart of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold and <s>Campaka</s> flowers, praised and worshipped by gods and men —

children.text: adya prayāsyasi vināśu mahāraṇesmiṃ mārasya eṣyasi vaśaṃ asurasya venduḥ // Lal_21.174 //
children.translated_text: today you shall perish in this great battle — you shall come under the power of <s>Māra</s>, the <s>Asura</s>!' // Lal_21.174 //

body.text: brahmasvareṇa karaviṅkarutasvareṇā tān yakṣarākṣasagaṇāṃ sugato babhāṣe /
body.translated_text: With a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s, with a voice like the song of the <s>Karaviṅka</s> bird, the <s>Sugata</s> addressed those hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>:

body.text: ākāśu trāsayitumicchati yo hyavidvān so 'smadvidhaṃ drumavarād grahaṇāya icchet // Lal_21.174 //
body.translated_text: 'He who, ignorant, wishes to frighten the sky — he would also wish to seize one such as me from the king of trees! // Lal_21.174 //

children.text: bhittvā ca yo raju gaṇeya mahāsahasra lomnā ca sāgarajalaṃ ca samuddharedyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who could split an atom and count the great trichiliocosm, who could lift the ocean's water with a hair,

children.text: vajrāmayāṃ girivarāṃ vikiretkṣaṇācca so cāpi māṃ tarugataṃ na viheṭhayeta // Lal_21.175 //
children.translated_text: and who could shatter in an instant a supreme mountain made of <s>vajra</s> — even he could not harm me, who sit at the tree!' // Lal_21.175 //

children.text: yugamantarasmi sthita māru praduṣṭacitto niṣkoṣa pāṇinamasiṃ pragṛhītva tīkṣṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, standing in the intermediate space, of corrupt mind, drew his sharp sword from its sheath, grasping it in hand:

children.text: uttiṣṭha śīghra śramaṇāsmamatena gaccha mā veṇuyaṣṭi haritāṃ va chinadmi te 'dya // Lal_21.176 //
children.translated_text: 'Arise quickly, O ascetic! Go by my command — lest I cut you down today as one cuts a green bamboo stalk!' // Lal_21.176 //

body.text: bodhisattva āha -
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:

children.text: sarveyaṃ trisahasra medini yadi māraiḥ prapūrṇā bhavet
children.translated_text: 'Even if this entire earth of the trichiliocosm were filled with <s>Māras</s>,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ yatha meru parvatavaraḥ pāṇīṣu khaṅgo bhavet /
children.translated_text: and each of them had in their hands a sword like <s>Meru</s>, the supreme mountain —

children.text: te mahyaṃ na samartha loma calituṃ prāgeva māṃ ghātituṃ
children.translated_text: they would not be able to move a single hair of mine, let alone slay me!

children.text: mā dūṣī nativela saṃpranadahe smāremi te 'nadṛḍham // Lal_21.177 //
children.translated_text: Do not tarry too long, O Wicked One — I shall burn you; I recall your lack of firmness!' // Lal_21.177 //

children.text: vidhyanti śailaśikharāṃ jvalitāgnivarṇāṃ vṛkṣāṃ samūlaka kṣipī tatha tāmraloham /
children.translated_text: They hurl mountain-peaks blazing with fiery color, trees torn up with their roots, and copper-iron;

children.text: uṣṭrāśca gogajamukhāstatha bhairavākṣā āśīviṣā bhujaga dṛṣṭiviṣāśca ghorāḥ // Lal_21.178 //
children.translated_text: camels, creatures with faces of cows and elephants, and those of terrible eyes — venomous serpents and dreadful snakes whose very gaze is poison. // Lal_21.178 //

children.text: megheva utthita caturdiśa garjamānā vajrāśanī tatha ayoguḍa varṣamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Rising like clouds from the four directions, thundering, raining <s>vajra</s>-thunderbolts and iron balls;

children.text: asiśaktitīṣṇaparaśuṃ saviṣāṃśca bāṇāṃ bhindanti medinitalaṃ pramathanti vṛkṣāṃ // Lal_21.179 //
children.translated_text: swords, spears, sharp axes, and poisoned arrows — splitting the surface of the earth, destroying trees. // Lal_21.179 //

children.text: bāhūśataiḥ śaraśatāni kṣipanti keci āśīviṣāṃ hutavahāṃśca mukhā sṛjanti /
children.translated_text: Some hurl hundreds of arrows with hundreds of arms; from their mouths they release venomous snakes and fire;

children.text: makarādikāṃśca jalajānudadhergṛhītvā vidhyanti keci bhujagāṃ garuḍāśca bhūtvā // Lal_21.180 //
children.translated_text: some, seizing <s>makaras</s> and other aquatic creatures from the ocean, hurl them; some, becoming <s>Garuḍas</s>, strike at serpents. // Lal_21.180 //

children.text: kecitsumerusadṛśānayasā guḍāni taptāgnivarṇaśikharā nikṣipanti ruṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some, enraged, cast iron balls resembling <s>Sumeru</s>, with peaks blazing like heated fire;

children.text: āsādya medinitalaṃ kṣubhayanti corvīṃ heṣṭhā paskandha salilasya viloḍayanti // Lal_21.181 //
children.translated_text: reaching the earth's surface they agitate the ground, churning below the body of waters. // Lal_21.181 //

children.text: kecitpatanti puratastatha pṛṣṭhato 'sya vāme ca dakṣiṇa patanti aho ti vatsa /
children.translated_text: Some fall in front and behind him, and to the left and right they fall, crying 'Alas, dear child!'

children.text: viparītahastacaraṇā jvalitottamāṅgā netrebhi niścarati vidyudiva pradīptā // Lal_21.182 //
children.translated_text: with hands and feet inverted, heads aflame — from their eyes lightning issues forth, blazing. // Lal_21.182 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā vikāravikṛtā namucestu senā māyākṛtaṃ ca yatha prekṣati śuddhasattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the army of <s>Namuci</s>, deformed and distorted — the pure-minded one beholds it as an illusion:

children.text: naivātra māru na balaṃ na jaganna cātmā udacandrarūpasadṛśo bhramati trilokaḥ // Lal_21.183 //
children.translated_text: 'There is here no <s>Māra</s>, no force, no world, and no self — the triple world revolves like the form of the moon in water.' // Lal_21.183 //

children.text: cakṣurna istri puruṣo napi cātmanīyaṃ srotaṃ ca ghrāṇa tathā jihva tathaiva kāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The eye is not — there is neither woman nor man nor anything belonging to a self; the ear, the nose, likewise the tongue, and so too the body;

children.text: adhyātmaśūnya bahiśūnya pratītya jātā dharmā ime karakavedakavītivṛttāḥ // Lal_21.184 //
children.translated_text: internally empty, externally empty, arisen through dependent origination — these <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of doer, experiencer, and transmigrator.' // Lal_21.184 //

children.text: so satyavākyamakarotsada satyavādī yeneha satyavacanenima śūnya dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: He, ever a speaker of truth, made a declaration of truth — by which truthful speech these <s>dharmas</s> are [shown to be] empty:

children.text: ye keci saumya vinaye anukūlapakṣāḥ te śastra pāṇiṣu nirīkṣiṣu puṣpadāmāṃ // Lal_21.185 //
children.translated_text: 'May those who are favorably inclined toward the noble discipline see flower-garlands in these hands that hold weapons!' // Lal_21.185 //

children.text: so dakṣiṇe karatale racitāgrajāle tāmrairnakhaiḥ suruciraiḥ sahasrāracakre /
children.translated_text: He, with his right palm — its web of interlaced fingers, copper-colored nails of exceeding beauty, bearing the thousand-spoked wheel,

children.text: jāmbūnadārcisadṛśaiḥ śubhapuṇyajuṣṭe mūrdhnātu yāva spṛśate caraṇāṃ salīlam // Lal_21.186 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with radiance like <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, endowed with auspicious merit — reached gracefully from his head down to touch the feet [of the earth]. // Lal_21.186 //

children.text: bāhuṃ prasārya yatha vidyudivā nabhasthā ābhāṣate vasumatīniya mahya sākṣī /
children.translated_text: Extending his arm like lightning standing in the sky, he addresses the earth: 'Be my witness here!

children.text: citrā mi yajña nayutānapi yaṣṭa pūrve na mi jātu yācanaka bandhakṛtā nu dāsye // Lal_21.187 //
children.translated_text: Wondrous sacrifices, <s>nayutas</s> of them, have I offered in former lives — never have I made a bond refusing a supplicant in giving!' // Lal_21.187 //

children.text: āpo mi sākṣi tatha teja tathaiva vāyu brahmā prajāpati sajotiṣa candrasūryāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Water is my witness, and fire, and likewise wind; <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the luminaries — moon and sun;

children.text: buddhā mi sākṣi daśasu sthita ye diśāsu yatha mahya śīlavrataudgata bodhiaṅgāḥ // Lal_21.188 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the ten directions are my witnesses — they know how my factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>) arose from moral conduct and vows!' // Lal_21.188 //

body.text: dānaṃ mi sākṣi tatha śīlu tathaiva kṣāntiḥ vīryāpi sākṣi tatha dhyāna tathaiva prajñā /
body.translated_text: 'Generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is my witness, and moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), and likewise patience (<s>kṣānti</s>); vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) too is my witness, and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and likewise <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);

body.text: catura pramāṇa mama sākṣi tathā abhijñā anupūrvabodhicari sarva mameha sākṣī // Lal_21.189 //
body.translated_text: the four immeasurables (<s>brahmavihāras</s>) are my witnesses, and the superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>) — all my sequential practice of awakening is my witness here!' // Lal_21.189 //

children.text: yāvanti sattva nikhilā daśasu diśāsu yatteṣu puṇya bala śīlu tathaiva jñānam /
children.translated_text: 'However many beings there are in all the ten directions, whatever merit, strength, moral conduct, and knowledge is in them,

children.text: yajñā nirargaḍa ya yaṣṭa śaṭhaḥ kalībhiḥ te mahya roma śatimāṃ kala nopayanti // Lal_21.190 //
children.translated_text: the unrestricted sacrifices offered even by the deceitful with quarrels — all of those do not approach a hundredth fraction of a single hair of mine!' // Lal_21.190 //

children.text: so pāṇinā dharaṇi āhanate salīlaṃ raṇate iyaṃ vasumatī yatha kaṃsapātrī /
children.translated_text: He strikes the earth with his hand, gracefully — this earth resounds like a bronze vessel;

children.text: māro niśamya ravu mediniye nirastaḥ śṛṇute vacaṃ hanata gṛhṇatu kṛṣṇabandhum // Lal_21.191 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, hearing the sound of the earth, is overthrown — he hears the words: 'Strike! Seize the friend of Darkness!' // Lal_21.191 //

children.text: prasvinnagātru hatateju vivarṇavaktro māro jarābhihatu ātmanu saṃprapaśyī /
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>, his body drenched in sweat, his splendor destroyed, his face discolored, seeing himself struck by old age —

children.text: uratāḍa krandatu bhayārtu anāthabhūto bhrāntaṃ mano namucito gatu citta moham // Lal_21.192 //
children.translated_text: Striking his breast, he cries out, terrified, without protectors; the mind of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) wanders, his thoughts fallen into delusion. // Lal_21.192 //

children.text: hastyaśvayānaratha bhūmitale nirastāḥ dhāvanti rākṣasa kubhāṇḍa piśāca bhītāḥ /
children.translated_text: Elephants, horses, vehicles, and chariots are cast down upon the ground; <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s> flee in terror.

children.text: saṃmūḍha mārga na labhanti alenatrāṇāḥ pakṣī davāgnipataneva nirīkṣya krāntāḥ // Lal_21.193 //
children.translated_text: Bewildered, they find no path, without shelter or refuge — like birds seeing a forest fire descend, they are overcome. // Lal_21.193 //

children.text: mātā svasā pitara putra tathaiva bhrātā pṛcchanti tatra kahi dṛṣṭa kahiṃ gatā vā /
children.translated_text: Mothers, sisters, fathers, sons, and brothers ask one another: 'Where were you seen? Where have you gone?'

children.text: anyonya vigraha karonti tathaiva heṭhāḥ prāptā vayaṃ vyasana jīvita nāvakāśaḥ // Lal_21.194 //
children.translated_text: They quarrel with one another and cause harm: 'We have met with calamity — there is no scope for [our] lives!' // Lal_21.194 //

children.text: sā mārasena vipulā mahatī akṣobhyā vibhraṣṭa sarva viralīkṛta naiva saṃdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That vast, great, unshakable army of <s>Māra</s> — all fallen, scattered, its ranks completely broken.

children.text: divasāni sapta abhijāni paraspareṇa ābhāsi dṛṣṭa yadi jīvasi taṃ khu prītāḥ // Lal_21.195 //
children.translated_text: For seven days they did not recognize each other; [then, saying] 'If you are seen alive, let us rejoice!' // Lal_21.195 //

children.text: sā vṛkṣadevata tadā karuṇāṃ hi kṛtvā vārīghāṭaṃ grahiya siñcati kṛṣṇabandhum /
children.translated_text: Then a tree-goddess, having generated compassion, taking a water-pot, sprinkled [water on] the Dark-Kinsman [<s>Māra</s>]:

children.text: uttiṣṭha śīghra vraja he ma puno vilamba evaṃ hi teṣa bhavate guruuddharāṇām // Lal_21.196 //
children.translated_text: 'Rise quickly! Go, and delay no more! For this is what happens to those who are proud and unyielding.' // Lal_21.196 //

body.text: māra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said —

children.text: duḥkhaṃ bhayaṃ vyasana śoka vināśanaṃ ca dhikkāraśabdamavamānagataṃ ca dainyam /
children.translated_text: Suffering, fear, calamity, grief, destruction, the sound of reproach, contempt, and wretchedness —

children.text: prāpto 'smi adya aparādhya suśuddhasatve aśrutva vākya madhuraṃ hitamātmajānām // Lal_21.197 //
children.translated_text: I have attained [all this] today, having offended against the supremely pure being, not having heeded the sweet and beneficial words of my sons! // Lal_21.197 //

body.text: devatā āha -
body.translated_text: The goddess said —

children.text: bhayaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ vyasanaṃ ca dainyaṃ dhikkāraśabdaṃ vadhabandhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Fear, suffering, calamity, wretchedness, the sound of reproach, slaughter, and bondage —

children.text: doṣānanekāṃ labhate hyavidvān nirāparādheṣvapi rādhyate yaḥ // Lal_21.198 //
children.translated_text: these and many other faults the ignorant one obtains — he who offends against the blameless. // Lal_21.198 //

children.text: devāsurā garuḍa rākṣasa kinnarendrā brahmātha śakra paranirmita sākaniṣṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kinnara</s>-lords, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Paranirmita</s> [gods], up to the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s> —

children.text: bhāṣanti tasya vijayaṃ jaya lokavīra yatredṛśī namucisena tvayā nirastā // Lal_21.199 //
children.translated_text: they proclaim his victory: 'Victory, O hero of the world! — in that such an army of <s>Namuci</s> was vanquished by you!' // Lal_21.199 //

children.text: hārārdhacandra dhvaja chatrapatāka dentī puṣpāgarū tagaracandanacūrṇavarṣāṃ /
children.translated_text: Necklaces, half-moons, banners, parasols, flags, ivory, flowers, <s>aguru</s>, <s>tagara</s>, and showers of sandalwood powder,

children.text: tūryā parāhaniya vākyamudīrayante acchā drume tuva ca śūra jitārisiṃhā // Lal_21.200 //
children.translated_text: instruments played, and joyful words are uttered — clear [in sound], at the tree, [they proclaim:] 'O hero, lion who has conquered his enemies!' // Lal_21.200 //

children.text: atraiva cāsanavare labhase 'dya bodhiṃ āveṇikāṃ daśabalāṃ pratisaṃvidaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Right here, upon this excellent seat, you shall attain today the <s>Bodhi</s>, the distinctive [knowledge], the ten powers, and the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>);

children.text: sarvaṃ ca buddhaviṣayaṃ labhase 'dya śūra maitrā vijitya vipulāṃ śaṭhamārapakṣāṃ // Lal_21.201 //
children.translated_text: and the entire domain of a <s>Buddha</s> you shall attain today, O hero — having conquered, through loving-kindness, the vast, deceitful hosts of <s>Māra</s>! // Lal_21.201 //

children.text: iha māradharṣaṇakṛte ca raṇe pravṛtte saṃbodhisattvabalavikrama yebhi dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: In this battle that took place for the humbling of <s>Māra</s>, those by whom the strength and valor of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was witnessed —

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśakoṭinayutā cature ca viṃśā yebhirmanaḥ praṇihitaṃ varabuddhabodhau // Lal_21.202 //
children.translated_text: thirty-six <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayutas</s> and twenty-four [more] — by them the mind was set upon the supreme awakening of a <s>Buddha</s>. // Lal_21.202 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare māradharṣaṇaparivarto nāmaikaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the twenty-first chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, entitled 'The Chapter on the Humbling of <s>Māra</s>' (<s>Māradharṣaṇaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 22
body.translated_text: [START Chapter 22]

body.text: abhisaṃbodhanaparivarto dvāviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Twenty-Second Chapter: On Perfect Awakening (<s>Abhisaṃbodhanaparivarta</s>). /

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvo nihatamārapratyarthiko marditakaṇṭako raṇaśirasi vijitavijayaḥ uchritachatradhvajapatāko viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdhamaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma / savitarkasavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotibhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma / sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati sma smṛtimān saṃprajānan sukhaṃ kāyena pratisaṃvedayate sma yattadāryā ācakṣate sma - upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārī, niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma / sa sukhasya ca prahāṇādduḥkhasya ca prahāṇātpūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastaṃgamādaduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having vanquished <s>Māra</s> his adversary, having crushed the thorns, victorious in battle with his victory won, with parasol, banner, and flag raised high, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome, unskillful <s>dharmas</s>, with initial application and sustained application, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, attained and dwelt in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. With the stilling of initial and sustained application, through inner serenity and one-pointedness of mind, without initial application, without sustained application, with joy and happiness born of concentration, he attained and dwelt in the second <s>dhyāna</s>. With the fading away of joy, he dwelt in equanimity, mindful and fully aware; he experienced happiness with his body — that which the Noble Ones declare: 'equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness' — he attained and dwelt in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, free from joy. With the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering, and with the prior disappearance of gladness and dejection, neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness, he attained and dwelt in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasyathā samāhite citte pariśuddhe paryavadāte prabhāsvare 'naṅgane vigatopakleśe mṛduni karmaṇyupasthite ānijjyaprāpte rātryāṃ prathame yāme divyasya cakṣuṣo jñānadarśanavidyāsākṣātkriyāyai cittamabhinirharati sma, abhinirnāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind was thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, luminous, stainless, free from defilements, pliant, fit for work, stable, attained to imperturbability — in the first watch of the night, he directed and inclined his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge and vision of the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>). //

body.text: atha bodhisattvo divyena cakṣuṣā pariśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyati sma cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān sugatān durgatān hīnān praṇītān / yathākarmopagān sattvān prajānāti sma - ime bata bhoḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatāḥ, vāṅbhanoduścaritena samānvāgatāḥ, āryāṇāmapavādakāḥ mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ / te mithyādṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetoḥ kāyasya bhedātparaṃ maraṇādapāyadurgativinipātaṃ narakeṣūpapadyante / ime punarbhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatāḥ, vāṅbhanaḥsucaritena samanvāgatāḥ, āryāṇāmanapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ, te samyagdṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetoḥ kāyasya bhedātsugatau svargalokeṣūpapadyante //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with the divine eye, purified, surpassing that of humans, saw beings dying and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, in good destinies and bad, inferior and exalted. He understood beings as faring according to their actions: 'Alas, these beings, endowed with bodily misconduct, verbal and mental misconduct, revilers of the Noble Ones, holding wrong views — by reason of their undertaking of actions and practices born of wrong views, upon the dissolution of the body, after death, they are reborn in the lower realms, in bad destinies, in the downfall, in the hells. But these other beings, endowed with good bodily conduct, good verbal and mental conduct, not revilers of the Noble Ones, holding right views — by reason of their undertaking of actions and practices born of right views, upon the dissolution of the body, they are reborn in good destinies, in the heavenly worlds.' //

body.text: iti hi divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa sattvānāpaśyati sma cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān sugatān durgatān hīnān praṇītān yathākarmopagān / evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvo rātryāṃ prathame yāme vidyāṃ sākṣātkaroti sma, tamo nihanti sma, ālokamutpādayati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, with the divine eye, purified, surpassing that of humans, he saw beings dying and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, in good destinies and bad, inferior and exalted, faring according to their actions. Thus indeed, O monks, in the first watch of the night, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> directly realized [this] knowledge, destroyed darkness, and generated light. //

body.text: atha bodhisattvastathā samāhite citte pariśuddhe paryavadāte prabhāsvare niraṅgane vigatopakleśe mṛduni karmaṇyupasthite āniñjyaprāpte rātryāṃ madhyame yāme pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānadarśanavidyāsākṣātkriyāyai cittamabhinirharati sma, abhinirnāmayati sma, ātmanaḥ parasattvānāṃ cānekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsānanusmarati sma / tadyathā - ekāmapi jātiṃ dve tisraścatasraḥ pañca daśa viṃśati triṃśaccatvāriṃśatpañcāśajjātiśataṃ
body.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind was thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, luminous, stainless, free from defilements, pliant, fit for work, stable, attained to imperturbability — in the middle watch of the night, he directed and inclined his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the recollection of past lives (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñāna</s>). He recollected his own and other beings' manifold past lives — one birth, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred births,

body.text: jātisahasraṃ jātiśatasahasram anekānyapi jātiśatasahasrāṇyapi jātikoṭīmapi jātikoṭīśatamapi jātikoṭīsahasramapi jātikoṭīnayutamapi / anekānyapi jātikoṭīsahasrāṇyapi anekānyapi jātikoṭīśatasahasrāṇyapi anekānyapi jātikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi yāvatsaṃvartakalpamapi vivartakalpamapi saṃvartavivartakalpamapi anekānyapi saṃvartavivartakalpānyanusmarati sma - amutrāhamāsannevaṃnāmā evaṃgotra evaṃjātya evaṃvarṇa evamāhāra evamāyuṣpramāṇamevaṃ cirasthitikaḥ, evaṃ sukhaduḥkhaprativedī / so 'haṃ tataścyutaḥ sannamutropapannaḥ, tataścyutvehopapanna iti sākāraṃ soddeśamanekavidhamātmanaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ ca pūrvanivāsamanusmarati sma //
body.translated_text: a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many hundreds of thousands of births, a <s>koṭi</s> of births, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of births, a thousand <s>koṭis</s>, a <s>nayuta</s> of <s>koṭis</s>, many thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, many <s>nayuta</s>-hundred thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of births, up to an eon of world-contraction, an eon of world-expansion, an eon of contraction and expansion, many eons of contraction and expansion — he recollected: 'There I was, of such a name, such a clan, such a caste, such an appearance, of such food, of such a lifespan, of such a duration; such was my experience of happiness and suffering. Having died there, I was reborn here; having died here, I was reborn there' — thus, with details and descriptions, he recollected the manifold past lives of himself and all beings. //

body.text:
atha bodhisattvastathā samāhitena cittena pariśuddhena paryavadātena prabhāsvareṇa anaṅganena vigatopakleśena mṛdunā karmaṇye sthitenāniñcyaprāptena rātryāṃ paścime yāme aruṇoddhāṭanakālasamaye nandīmukhyāṃ rātrau
duḥkhasamudayāstaṃgatāyā āśravakṣayajñānadarśanavidyāsākṣātkriyāyai cittamabhinirharati sma, abhinirnāmayati sma / tasyaitadabhavat - kṛcchraṃ batāyaṃ loka āpanno yaduta jāyate jīryate mriyate cyavate upapadyate / atha ca punarasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya niḥsaraṇaṃ na saṃprajānāti jarāvyādhimaraṇādikasya / aho batāsya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasyāntaḥkriyā na prajñāyate sarvasya jarāvyādhimaraṇādikasya //
body.translated_text: Then, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind was thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, luminous, stainless, free from defilements, pliant, fit for work, stable, attained to imperturbability — in the last watch of the night, at the time when the dawn arose, on the night whose chief [quality] is delight, [the night] when the arising of suffering ceased — he directed and inclined his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the destruction of the defilements (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>). He thought: 'Alas, this world has fallen into hardship — it is born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn. And yet it does not know the escape from this entire great mass of suffering — from old age, disease, death, and the rest. Alas, when will the end of this entire great mass of suffering — all of old age, disease, death, and the rest — be known?' //

body.text: tato bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - kasmin sati jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati, kiṃpratyayaṃ ca punarjarāmaraṇam? tasyaitadabhūt - jātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ bhavati, jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇam //
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does old age and death come to be? What is the condition for old age and death?' He thought: 'When birth exists, old age and death come to be. Birth is the condition for old age and death.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati jātirbhavati, kiṃpratyayā ca punarjātiḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - bhave sati jātirbhavati bhavapratyayā ca punarjātiḥ //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does birth come to be? What is the condition for birth?' He thought: 'When becoming (<s>bhava</s>) exists, birth comes to be. Becoming is the condition for birth.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasyaitabhavat - kasmin sati bhavo bhavati, kiṃpratyayaśca punarbhavaḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - upādāne sati bhavo bhavati, upādānapratyayo hi bhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does becoming come to be? What is the condition for becoming?' He thought: 'When clinging (<s>upādāna</s>) exists, becoming comes to be. Clinging is the condition for becoming.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasyaitadabhavat - kasmin satyupādānaṃ bhavati, kiṃpratyayaṃ ca punarupādānam? tasyaitadabhavat - tṛṣṇāyāṃ satyāmupādānaṃ bhavati, tṛṣṇāpratyayaṃ hyupādānam //
body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does clinging come to be? What is the condition for clinging?' He thought: 'When craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) exists, clinging comes to be. Craving is the condition for clinging.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati tṛṣṇā bhavati, kiṃpratyayā ca tṛṣṇā? tasyaitadabhavat - vedanāyāṃ satyāṃ tṛṣṇā bhavati, vedanāpratyayā ca tṛṣṇā //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does craving come to be? What is the condition for craving?' He thought: 'When feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) exists, craving comes to be. Feeling is the condition for craving.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhūt - kasmin sati vedanā bhavati, kiṃpratyayā punarvedanā? tasyaitadabhūt - sparśe sati vedanā bhavati, sparśapratyayā hi vedanā //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does feeling come to be? What is the condition for feeling?' He thought: 'When contact (<s>sparśa</s>) exists, feeling comes to be. Contact is the condition for feeling.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati sparśo bhavati, kiṃpratyayaśca punaḥ sparśaḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - ṣaḍāyatane sati sparśo bhavati, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayo hi sparśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does contact come to be? What is the condition for contact?' He thought: 'When the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) exist, contact comes to be. The six sense-bases are the condition for contact.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati ṣaḍāyatanaṃ bhavati, kiṃpratyayaṃ ca punaḥ ṣaḍāyatanam? tasyaitadabhavat - nāmarūpe sati ṣaḍāyatanaṃ bhavati, nānārūpapratyayaṃ hi ṣaḍāyatanam //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists do the six sense-bases come to be? What is the condition for the six sense-bases?' He thought: 'When name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) exists, the six sense-bases come to be. Name-and-form is the condition for the six sense-bases.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati nāmarūpaṃ bhavati, kiṃpratyayaṃ ca punarnāmarūpam? tasyaitadabhavat - vijñāne sati nāmarūpaṃ bhavati, vijñānapratyayaṃ hi nāmarūpam //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does name-and-form come to be? What is the condition for name-and-form?' He thought: 'When consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) exists, name-and-form comes to be. Consciousness is the condition for name-and-form.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati vijñānaṃ bhavanti, kiṃpratyayaṃ punarvijñānam? tasyaitadabhavat - saṃskāreṣu satsu vijñānaṃ bhavati, saṃskārapratyayaṃ ca vijñānam //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists does consciousness come to be? What is the condition for consciousness?' He thought: 'When volitional formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) exist, consciousness comes to be. Volitional formations are the condition for consciousness.' //

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasmin sati saṃskārā bhavanti, kiṃpratyayāśca punaḥ saṃskārāḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ saṃskārā bhavanti, avidyāpratyayā hi saṃskārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then this further thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'When what exists do volitional formations come to be? What is the condition for volitional formations?' He thought: 'When ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) exists, volitional formations come to be. Ignorance is the condition for volitional formations.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasyaitadabhūt - avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam, nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaṃ sparśaḥ, sparśapratyayaṃ vedanā, vedanāpratyayaṃ tṛṣṇā, tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam, upādānapratyayaṃ bhavaḥ, bhavapratyayā jātiḥ, jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti / evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati / samudayaḥ samudaya iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, this thought arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Conditioned by ignorance are volitional formations; conditioned by volitional formations is consciousness; conditioned by consciousness is name-and-form; conditioned by name-and-form are the six sense-bases; conditioned by the six sense-bases is contact; conditioned by contact is feeling; conditioned by feeling is craving; conditioned by craving is clinging; conditioned by clinging is becoming; conditioned by becoming is birth; conditioned by birth arise old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, distress, and despair. Thus is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. Arising! Arising!' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya pūrvamaśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikārādbahulīkārājjñānamudapādi, cakṣurudapādi, vidyodapādi, bhūrirudapādi, medhodapādi, prajñodapādi, ālokaḥ prādurbabhūva / kasminnasati jarāmaraṇaṃ na bhavati, kasya vā nirodhājjarāmaraṇanirodha iti / tasyaitadabhūt - jātyāmasatyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ na bhavati, jātinirodhājjarāmaraṇanirodhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in <s>dharmas</s> not previously heard, from careful attention and thorough cultivation, knowledge arose, vision arose, understanding arose, insight arose, intelligence arose, wisdom arose, illumination appeared: 'When what is absent does old age and death not exist? By the cessation of what does old age and death cease?' This [understanding] arose in him: 'When birth is absent, old age and death do not exist; from the cessation of birth, the cessation of old age and death.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punaretadabhavat - kasminnasati jātirna bhavati, kasya vā nirodhājjātinirodhaḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - bhave 'sati jātirna bhavati, bhavanirodhājjātinirodhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> further [reflected]: 'When what is absent does birth not exist? By the cessation of what does birth cease?' This arose in him: 'When becoming (<s>bhava</s>) is absent, birth does not exist; from the cessation of becoming, the cessation of birth.'

body.text: atha bodhisattvasya punarapyetadabhavat - kasminnasati vistareṇa yāvatsaṃskārā na bhavanti, kasya vā nirodhātsaṃskāranirodhaḥ? tasyaitadabhavat - avidyāyāṃ satyāṃ saṃskārā na bhavanti, avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodhaḥ / saṃskāranirodhādvijñānanirodho yāvajjātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante / evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> further [reflected]: 'When what is absent — in full detail, up to — do the <s>saṃskāras</s> not exist? By the cessation of what does the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> [occur]?' This arose in him: 'When ignorance is absent, <s>saṃskāras</s> do not exist; from the cessation of ignorance, the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>; from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>, the cessation of consciousness — up to — from the cessation of birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress cease. Thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering.'

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bodhisattvasya pūrvamaśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikārādbahulīkārājjñānamudapādi, cakṣurudapādi vidyodapadi, bhūrirudapādi, medhodapādi, prajñodapādi, ālokaḥ prādurbabhūva / so 'haṃ bhikṣavastasmin samaye idaṃ duḥkhamiti yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / ayamāśravasamudayo 'yamāśravanirodhaḥ iyamāśravanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / aya kāmāśravo 'yaṃ bhavāśravo 'yamavidyāśravo 'yaṃ dṛṣṭyāśravaḥ / ihāśravā niravaśeṣato nirudhyante / ihāśravo niravaśeṣamanābhāsamastaṃ gacchatīti / iyamavidyā ayamavidyāsamudayo 'yamavidyānirodha iyamavidyānirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / ihāvidyā apariśeṣamanābhāsamastaṃ gacchatīti peyālam / amī saṃskārā ayaṃ saṃskārasamudayo 'yaṃ saṃskāranirodha iyaṃ saṃskāranirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idaṃ vijñānamayaṃ vijñānasamudayo 'yaṃ vijñānanirodha iyaṃ vijñānanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idaṃ nāmarūpamayaṃ nāmarūpasamudayo 'yaṃ nāmarūpanirodhaḥ iyaṃ nāmarūpanirodhagāminī
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in <s>dharmas</s> not previously heard, from careful attention and thorough cultivation, knowledge arose, vision arose, understanding arose, insight arose, intelligence arose, wisdom arose, illumination appeared. I, O monks, at that time, knew as it truly is: 'This is suffering.' 'This is the origin of the outflows; this is the cessation of the outflows; this is the path leading to the cessation of the outflows' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is the outflow of desire; this is the outflow of becoming; this is the outflow of ignorance; this is the outflow of views. Here the outflows cease without remainder. Here the outflow goes without remainder to non-appearance and extinction.' 'This is ignorance; this is the origin of ignorance; this is the cessation of ignorance; this is the path leading to the cessation of ignorance' — I knew as it truly is. 'Here ignorance goes without remainder to non-appearance and extinction' — and so on in detail. 'These are the <s>saṃskāras</s>; this is the origin of <s>saṃskāras</s>; this is the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>; this is the path leading to the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is consciousness; this is the origin of consciousness; this is the cessation of consciousness; this is the path leading to the cessation of consciousness' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is name-and-form; this is the origin of name-and-form; this is the cessation of name-and-form; this is the path leading to the cessation of name-and-form' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is the six sense-bases; this is the origin of the six sense-bases; this is the cessation of the six sense-bases; this is the path leading to the cessation of the six sense-bases' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is contact; this is the origin of contact; this is the cessation of contact; this is the path leading to the cessation of contact' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is feeling; this is the origin of feeling; this is the cessation of feeling; this is the path leading to the cessation of feeling' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is craving; this is the origin of craving; this is the cessation of craving; this is the path leading to the cessation of craving' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is clinging; this is the origin of clinging; this is the cessation of clinging; this is the path leading to the cessation of clinging' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is becoming; this is the origin of becoming; this is the cessation of becoming; this is the path leading to the cessation of becoming' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is birth; this is the origin of birth; this is the cessation of birth; this is the path leading to the cessation of birth' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is old age; this is the origin of old age; this is the cessation of old age; this is the path leading to the cessation of old age' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is death; this is the origin of death; this is the cessation of death; this is the path leading to the cessation of death' — I knew as it truly is. 'These are grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress. Thus there is the origin of this entire great mass of suffering — up to — thus there is the cessation' — I knew as it truly is. 'This is suffering; this is the origin of suffering; this is the cessation of suffering; this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering' — I knew as it truly is.

body.text: pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanasamudayo 'yaṃ ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ iyaṃ ṣaḍāyatananirodhagāminīṃ pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / ayaṃ sparśo 'yaṃ spaśasamudayo 'yaṃ sparśanirodhaḥ iyaṃ sparśanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / iyaṃ vedanā ayaṃ vedanāsamudayo 'yaṃ vedanānirodha iyaṃ vedanānirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / iyaṃ tṛṣṇā ayaṃ tṛṣṇāsamudayo 'yaṃ tṛṣṇānirodhaḥ iyaṃ tṛṣṇānirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idamupādānamayamupādānasamudayo 'yamupādānanirodhaḥ iyamupādānanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / ayaṃ bhavo 'yaṃ bhavasamudayo 'yaṃ bhavanirodhaḥ iyaṃ bhavanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / iyaṃ jātirayaṃ jātisamudayo 'yaṃ jātinirodhaḥ iyaṃ jātinirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / iyaṃ jarā ayaṃ jarāsamudayo 'yaṃ jarānirodhaḥ iyaṃ jarānirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idaṃ maraṇamayaṃ maraṇasamudayo 'yaṃ maraṇanirodhaḥ iyaṃ maraṇanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / ime śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ / evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati yāvannirodho bhavatīti yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam / idaṃ duḥkhamayaṃ duḥkhasamudayo 'yaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi yathābhūtamajñāsiṣam //
body.translated_text: [continuation of the above passage with the detailed enumeration of the twelve links]

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo bodhisattvena rātryāṃ paścime yāme 'ruṇoddhāṭanakālasamaye nandīmukhyāṃ rātryau yatkiṃcitpuruṣeṇa satpuruṣeṇātipuruṣeṇa mahāpuruṣeṇa puruṣarṣabheṇa puruṣanāgena puruṣasiṃhena puruṣapuṃgavena puruṣaśūreṇa puruṣadhīreṇa puruṣajānena puruṣapadmena puruṣapuṇḍarīkeṇa puruṣadhaureyeṇānuttareṇa puruṣadamyasārathinā evaṃbhūtenāryeṇa jñānena jñātavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ prāptavyaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ sākṣātkartavyam, sarvaṃ tadekacittekṣaṇasamāyuktayā prajñayā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya traividyādhigatā //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, in the last watch of the night, at the time when the dawn breaks — the auspicious night — whatever is to be known, to be awakened to, to be attained, to be seen, to be directly realized by a [true] man, a good man, a supreme man, a great man, a bull among men, a <s>Nāga</s> among men, a lion among men, an excellent among men, a hero among men, a steadfast one among men, a noble among men, a lotus among men, a <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) among men, a foremost among men, an unsurpassed charioteer of beings to be tamed — by such a noble being, with wisdom conjoined with a single moment of mental concentration, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), the triple knowledge was attained.

body.text: tato bhikṣavo devā āhuḥ - avakirata mārṣāḥ puṣpāṇi / abhisaṃbuddho bhagavān / ye tatra devaputrāḥ pūrvabuddhadarśinastasmin saṃnipatitā āsaṃste 'vocan - mā sma tāvanmārṣāḥ puṣpāṇyavakirata yāvattāvadbhagavānnimittaṃ prāduḥkaroti / pūrvakā api samyaksaṃbuddhā nimittamakārṣuḥ, nirmitāmabhinirmiṇvanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the gods said: 'Scatter flowers, sirs! The <s>Bhagavān</s> has fully awakened!' Those <s>devaputras</s> who had seen former <s>Buddhas</s> and were assembled there said: 'Do not yet scatter flowers, sirs, until the <s>Bhagavān</s> produces the sign! Former perfectly awakened ones also produced the sign — they created a magical emanation.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatastān devaputrān vimatiprāptāñjñātvā saptatālamātraṃ vihāyasamabhyudgamya tatrastha idamudānamudānayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then indeed, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing those <s>devaputras</s> to be in doubt, rising up in the sky to the height of seven palm trees, standing there, uttered this <s>udāna</s>:

children.text: chinnavartmopaśāntarajāḥ śuṣkā āsravā na punaḥ sravanti /
children.translated_text: 'The path is cut, the dust is pacified; the dried-up outflows no longer flow;

children.text: chinne vartmani vartata duḥkhasyaiṣo 'nta ucyate // Lal_22.1 //
children.translated_text: when the path is cut, it no longer operates — this is called the end of suffering.' // Lal_22.1 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: tataste devaputrā divyaiḥ kusumaistathāgatamabhyavakiranti sma / tato jānumātraṃ divyānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ saṃstaro 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputras</s> showered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with divine flowers. A layer of divine flowers knee-deep was formed.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgate 'bhisaṃbuddhe vigataṃ tamo 'ndhakāram, viśodhitā tṛṣṇā, vivartitā dṛṣṭiḥ, vikṣobhitāḥ kleśāḥ, viśāritāḥ śalyāḥ, mukto granthiḥ, prapātito mānadhvajaḥ, ucchrepito dharmadhvajaḥ,
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, when the <s>Tathāgata</s> had fully awakened: the darkness of ignorance was dispelled; craving was purified; [wrong] views were turned back; the afflictions were agitated; the darts were extracted; the knot was loosened; the banner of pride was cast down; the banner of <s>Dharma</s> was raised;

body.text: uddhāṭitā anuśayāḥ, jñātā dharmatathatā, avabuddhā bhūtakoṭiḥ, parijñāto dharmadhātuḥ, vyavasthāpitaḥ sattvadhātuḥ, saṃvarṇitaḥ samyaktvaniyato rāśiḥ, vivarṇito mithyātvaniyato rāśiḥ, parigṛhīto 'niyatarāśiḥ, vyavasthāpitāni sattvendriyāṇi, parijñātāḥ sattvacaritāḥ, avabuddhā sattvavyādhiḥ, sattvasamutthānasiddho 'mṛtabhaiṣajaprayogaḥ, utpanno vaidyarājaḥ pramocakaḥ sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ pratiṣṭhāpako nirvāṇasukhe, niṣaṇṇastathāgatagarbhe tathāgatamahādharmarājāsane, sarva ābaddho vimuktipakṣaḥ, praviṣṭaḥ sarvajñatānagaraṃ samavasṛtaṃ sarvabuddhaiḥ, asaṃbhinno dharmadhātuprasarānubodheḥ / prathame saptāhe bhikṣavastathāgatastasminneva bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇo 'sthāt - iha mayā 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ / mayā anavarāgrasya jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasyāntaḥ kṛta iti //
body.translated_text: the latent tendencies were laid bare; the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of phenomena) was known; the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) was awakened to; the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of phenomena) was fully comprehended; the realm of beings was established; the group of those fixed in rightness was praised; the group of those fixed in wrongness was deprecated; the undetermined group was taken in hand; the faculties of beings were established; the conduct of beings was fully known; the disease of beings was awakened to; the application of the deathless medicine for the arising of beings was accomplished; the king of physicians was born — the liberator from all sufferings, the establisher in the bliss of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; he was seated in the <s>Tathāgata</s>-womb, on the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s great <s>Dharma</s>-king throne; all [that pertains to] the side of liberation was bound [i.e., secured]; the city of omniscience was entered — that which is frequented by all <s>Buddhas</s>; unbroken was [his understanding of] the extension of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>'s awakening. For the first seven days, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> remained seated at that very <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>: 'Here I have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. I have made an end to the suffering of beginningless and endless birth, old age, and death.'

body.text: samanantaraprāpte khalu punarbhikṣavo bodhisattvena sarvajñatve atha tatkṣaṇameva daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvāstatkṣaṇaṃ tallavaṃ tanmuhūrtaṃ parasukhasamarpitā abhuvan / sarvalokadhātavaśca mahatāvabhāsenāvabhāsyantaḥ / yā 'pi tā lokāntarikā aghā aghasphuṭā andhakārā iti pūrvavat / ṣaḍvikāraṃ ca daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātavo 'kampat prākampat saṃprākampat / avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat / acalat prācalat saṃprācalat / akṣubhyat prākṣubhyat saṃprākṣubhyat / araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat / agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat / sarvabuddhāśca tathāgatāyābhisaṃbuddhāya sādhukāraṃ dadanti sma / dharmācchādāṃśca saṃpreṣayanti sma / yairdharmācchādairayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturanekaratnasaṃchanno 'bhūt / tebhyaśca ratnachatrebhyaḥ evaṃrūpā raśmijālā niścaranti sma, yairdaśasu dikṣu aprameyāsaṃkhyeyā lokadhātavo 'vabhāsyante / daśasu dikṣu bodhisattvāśca devāputrāścanandaśabdaṃ niścārayāmāsuḥ - utpannaḥ sattvapaṇḍitaḥ / padmo jñānasarasi saṃbhūto 'nupalipto lokadharmaiḥ / samantato mahākaruṇāmeghaṃ sphuritvā dharmadhātubhavanaṃ varṣayiṣyati / dharmavarṣavinaye janabhaiṣajāṅkuraprarohaṇaṃ sarvakuśalamūlabījānāṃ vivardhanaṃ śraddhāṅkurāṇāṃ dātā vimuktiphalānām //
body.translated_text: Indeed, O monks, no sooner had the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attained omniscience than at that very moment, at that instant, at that second, all beings in all world-systems of the ten directions were at that moment established in others' happiness. All world-systems were illuminated with a great radiance. And those inter-world spaces — dark, deeply dark [darkness] — as before [were illuminated]. The world-systems in the ten directions quaked with six kinds of trembling — they shook, greatly shook, and thoroughly shook; they trembled, greatly trembled, and thoroughly trembled; they moved, greatly moved, and thoroughly moved; they churned, greatly churned, and thoroughly churned; they resounded, greatly resounded, and thoroughly resounded; they rumbled, greatly rumbled, and thoroughly rumbled. All the <s>Buddhas</s> gave cries of 'Well done!' to the <s>Tathāgata</s> upon his awakening and sent <s>Dharma</s>-parasols — by which <s>Dharma</s>-parasols this trichiliocosmic world-system was covered with manifold jewels. From those jewel-parasols, such nets of radiance issued forth that they illuminated immeasurable, incalculable world-systems in the ten directions. And <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>devaputras</s> in the ten directions uttered the cry of joy: 'A wise one among beings has been born! A lotus born in the lake of knowledge, unstained by worldly <s>dharmas</s>! Having spread the great <s>Mahākaruṇā</s>-cloud on all sides, he shall rain upon the mansion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. In the discipline of the <s>Dharma</s>-rain, [he is] the sprouter of the medicine-sprout for beings, the grower of all seeds of wholesome roots, the giver of faith-sprouts, the [giver] of the fruits of liberation!'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here this is said —

children.text: māraṃ vijitya sabalaṃ sa hi puruṣasiṃho dhyānāmukhaṃ abhimukhaṃ abhito 'pi śāstā /
children.translated_text: Having conquered <s>Māra</s> with his army, that lion among men, the Teacher, approached the gateway of <s>dhyāna</s> from all sides;

children.text: traividyatā daśabalena yadā hi prāptā saṃkampitā daśa diśo bahukṣatrakoṭyaḥ // Lal_22.2 //
children.translated_text: when the triple knowledge was attained through the ten powers — the ten directions with many <s>koṭis</s> of fields trembled! // Lal_22.2 //

children.text: ye bodhisattva puri āgata dharmakāmā caraṇau nipatya iti bhāṣiṣu māsi klānto /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had formerly come, desiring <s>Dharma</s>, falling at his feet, spoke thus: 'You are weary!

children.text: pratyakṣa asmi camu yādṛśikā subhīmā sā prajñapuṇyabalavīryabalena bhagnā // Lal_22.3 //
children.translated_text: I am an eyewitness to what that fearsome army was like — it was shattered by the power of wisdom, merit, and vigor!' // Lal_22.3 //

body.text: buddhaiśca kṣetranayutaiḥ prahitāni chatrā sādho mahāpuruṣa dharṣita mārasenām /
body.translated_text: Parasols were sent by <s>Buddhas</s> from <s>nayutas</s> of fields: 'Well done, O great being, who have vanquished <s>Māra</s>'s army!

body.text: prāptaṃ tvayā padavaraṃ amṛtaṃ viśokaṃ saddharmavṛṣṭi tribhave abhivarṣa śīghram // Lal_22.4 //
body.translated_text: You have attained the supreme state, the deathless, free from sorrow — rain the true <s>Dharma</s>-rain upon the three worlds quickly!' // Lal_22.4 //

children.text: bāhuṃ prasārya daśadikṣu ca sattvasārā ābhāṣayiṃsu kalaviṅkarutāya vācā /
children.translated_text: Extending their arms in the ten directions, the jewels among beings addressed [him] with a voice like a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird:

children.text: bodhiryathāmanugatā bhavatā viśuddhā tulyaḥ samo 'si yatha sarpiṇi sarpimaṇḍaiḥ // Lal_22.5 //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Bodhi</s> that has been followed by you is pure — you are equal, the same, as circles within circles of clarified butter!' // Lal_22.5 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ kāmāvacarā apsaraso bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgataṃ prāptābhijñaṃ paripūrṇasaṃkalpaṃ vijitasaṃgrāmaṃ nirjitamārapratyarthikamucchritachatradhvajapatākaṃ śūraṃ jayodgataṃ puruṣaṃ mahāpuruṣaṃ vaidyottamaṃ mahāśalyahartāraṃ siṃhaṃ vigatabhayalomaharṣaṃ nāgaṃ sudāntacittanirmalaṃ trimalaviprahīnaṃ vaidyakaṃ traividyatāmanuprāptaṃ pāragaṃ caturoghottīrṇaṃ kṣatriyamekaratnachatradhāriṇaṃ trailokyabrāhmaṇaṃ bāhitapāpakarmāṇaṃ bhikṣuṃ bhinnavidyāṇḍakoṣaṃ śramaṇaṃ sarvasaṅgasamatikrāntaṃ śrotriyaṃ niḥsṛtakleśaṃ śūramaprapātitadhvajaṃ balīyāṃsaṃ daśabaladhāriṇaṃ ratnākaramiva sarvadharmaratnasaṃpūrṇaṃ viditvā bodhimaṇḍābhimukhāstathāgatamābhirgāthābhirabhyastāviṣuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then indeed, O monks, the <s>Apsarases</s> of the desire-realm, [seeing] the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> — who had attained the superknowledges, fulfilled his aspirations, won the battle, conquered <s>Māra</s> the adversary, with parasol, banner, and flags raised aloft — the hero, the victor, the [true] man, the great man, the supreme physician, the great dart-extractor, the lion free from fear and hair-raising, the elephant of well-tamed and stainless mind, free from the three defilements, the physician who has attained the triple knowledge, who has gone beyond, who has crossed the four floods, the <s>kṣatriya</s> bearing a single jewel-parasol, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the three worlds who has warded off evil deeds, the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has broken the shell-egg of ignorance, the <s>śramaṇa</s> who has transcended all attachments, the learned one from whom afflictions have departed, the hero whose banner is not cast down, the mighty one bearing the ten powers, like a jewel-mine filled with all <s>Dharma</s>-jewels — knowing [all this], facing the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, they praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with these verses:

children.text: eṣa drumarājamūle abhijitya mārasainyaṃ sthitu meruvadaprakampyo nirbhīrapralāpī /
children.translated_text: This one, having conquered <s>Māra</s>'s army at the root of the king of trees, stands unshakable like <s>Meru</s>, fearless in [his] speech!

children.text: anekabahukalpakoṭyo dānadamasaṃyamena samudānayaṃ prabodhi teneṣa śobhate 'dya // Lal_22.6 //
children.translated_text: For many hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through giving, self-control, and restraint, he has accumulated [merit]; by that, this one shines today in awakening! // Lal_22.6 //

children.text: anena bahukalpakoṭyaḥ śīlavratātapobhi jihmikṛta śakra brahmā bodhivara eṣatā hi /
children.translated_text: By this one, for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through morality, observances, and austerities, <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> have been outshone — this excellent <s>bodhi</s> is thus [attained]!

children.text: anena bahukalpakoṭyaḥ kṣāntibalavarmitena adhivāsitā dukhāni tena prabha svarṇavarṇā // Lal_22.7 //
children.translated_text: By this one, for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, armored with the power of patience, sufferings were endured — by that, [his] radiance is golden-hued! // Lal_22.7 //

children.text: anena bahukalpakoṭyo vīryabalavikrameṇa parāṅmukhāṃ kṛtāsyā tena māra jita senā /
children.translated_text: By this one, for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, with the valor and might of vigor, [all opponents] were made to turn away — by that, <s>Māra</s>'s army has been conquered!

children.text: anena bahukalpakoṭyo dhyānā abhijñajñānaiḥ saṃpūjitā munīndrastenaiva pūjito 'dya // Lal_22.8 //
children.translated_text: By this one, for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through <s>dhyānas</s>, supernatural knowledges, and wisdom, the lord of sages was honored — by that very [merit] he is worshipped today! // Lal_22.8 //

children.text: anena bahukalpakoṭyaḥ prajñāśratasaṃcayena pragṛhīta sattvakoṭyastena laghu bodhi prāptā /
children.translated_text: By this one, for many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, through the accumulation of wisdom and learning, <s>koṭīs</s> of beings were taken up — by that, <s>bodhi</s> is swiftly attained!

children.text: anena jitu skandhamārastatha mṛtyu kleśamāraḥ anena jitu devaputramārastenāsya nāsti śokaḥ // Lal_22.9 //
children.translated_text: By this one, the <s>skandha-māra</s> (aggregates-māra) has been conquered, and likewise the <s>mṛtyu-māra</s> (death-māra) and <s>kleśa-māra</s> (affliction-māra); by this one, the <s>devaputra-māra</s> has been conquered — therefore he has no sorrow! // Lal_22.9 //

body.text:
eṣo hi devadevo (devairapi pūjanīyaḥ) pūjārahastriloke
puṇyārthikāna kṣetraṃ amṛtāphalasya dātā /
body.translated_text: This one is indeed the god of gods, worthy of worship even by gods, worthy of worship in the three worlds, a field [of merit] for those who seek merit, a giver of the deathless fruit!

body.text: eṣa varadakṣiṇīyo utpātu dakṣiṇāhi
body.translated_text: This one is the supreme worthy recipient [of offerings]; let offerings be produced!

body.text: nāstyuttarasya nāśo yā ca varabodhi labdhā // Lal_22.10 //
body.translated_text: There is no destruction of what is supreme — the excellent <s>bodhi</s> that has been attained! // Lal_22.10 //

children.text: ūrṇā virājate 'sya spharati bahukṣetrakoṭyo jihmikṛta candrasūryā andhakārālokaprāptā /
children.translated_text: His <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows) shines forth, pervading many <s>koṭīs</s> of world-realms; the sun and moon are outshone — those in darkness attain light!

children.text: eva hi surūparūpo vararūpa sādhurūpo varalakṣaṇo hitaiṣī trailokyapūjanīyaḥ // Lal_22.11 //
children.translated_text: Thus is he of beautiful form, supreme form, excellent form, with excellent marks, a well-wisher — worthy of worship by the three worlds! // Lal_22.11 //

children.text: eṣa suviśuddhanetro bahu prekṣate svayaṃbhūḥ kṣatrā ca sattvakāyā cittāni cetanā ca /
children.translated_text: This one of supremely pure eyes, the self-existent one, sees much — the realms, the assemblies of beings, their minds and volitions!

children.text: eṣa suviśuddhaśrotraḥ śṛṇute anantaśabdāṃ divyāṃśca mānuṣāṃśca jinaśabdadharmaśabdāṃ // Lal_22.12 //
children.translated_text: This one of supremely pure hearing hears infinite sounds — divine and human, the sounds of the <s>Jina</s> and the sounds of the <s>dharma</s>! // Lal_22.12 //

children.text: eṣa prabhūtajihvaḥ kalaviṅkamañjughoṣa
children.translated_text: This one of broad tongue, with a voice melodious as the <s>kalaviṅka</s> —

children.text: ḥ śroṣyāma asya dharmaṃ amṛtaṃ praśāntagāmim /
children.translated_text: we shall hear his <s>dharma</s>, deathless, leading to peace!

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca mārasainyaṃ na kṣubhyate mano 'sya
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Māra</s>'s army, his mind is not agitated;

children.text: puna dṛṣṭgha devasaṃghāṃ na ca harṣate sumedhā // Lal_22.13 //
children.translated_text: and again, seeing the hosts of gods, the wise one does not become elated! // Lal_22.13 //

children.text: śastrairna cāpi bāṇairjita ena mārasenā
children.translated_text: Not by weapons nor by arrows was <s>Māra</s>'s army conquered,

children.text: satyavratātapobhi jitu ena duṣṭamallaḥ /
children.translated_text: but by truth, observances, and austerities was that wicked wrestler defeated!

children.text: calito na cāsanā na ca kāyu vedhino 'sya
children.translated_text: He was not moved from his seat, nor did his body tremble;

children.text: na ca snehu nāpi doṣastadanantare abhūvan // Lal_22.14 //
children.translated_text: neither attachment nor aversion arose in that [moment]! // Lal_22.14 //

children.text: lābhā sulabdha teṣāṃ maruṇāṃ narāṇa caiva
children.translated_text: It is a gain, well-gained, for those gods and those humans

children.text: ye tubhya dharma śrutvā pratipattimeṣyatī hi /
children.translated_text: who, having heard your <s>dharma</s>, will attain practice!

children.text: yatpuṇya tvāṃ stavitvā jina puṇyatejarāśe
children.translated_text: By the merit of praising you, O <s>Jina</s> (Victor), mass of merit and splendor,

children.text: sarve bhavema kṣipraṃ yatha tvaṃ manuṣyacandraḥ // Lal_22.15 //
children.translated_text: may we all swiftly become like you, O moon among men! // Lal_22.15 //

children.text: buddhitva bodhi puruṣarṣabhanāyakena saṃkampya kṣatranayutāni vijitya māram /
children.translated_text: Having awakened to <s>bodhi</s>, the bull among men, the leader, having shaken <s>nayutas</s> of realms and conquered <s>Māra</s>,

children.text: brahmasvareṇa kalaviṅkarutasvareṇa prathamena gāthā imi bhāṣita nāyakena // Lal_22.16 //
children.translated_text: with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, with the sound of the <s>kalaviṅka</s>'s call — these first verses were spoken by the Leader: // Lal_22.16 //

body.text: puṇyavipāku sukha sarvaduḥkhāpanetī abhiprāyu sidhyati ca puṇyavato narasya /
body.translated_text: 'The ripening of merit is happiness, the remover of all suffering; the purpose of the meritorious person is accomplished!

body.text: kṣipraṃ ca bodhi spṛśate vinihatya māraṃ śāntāpatho gacchati ca nirvṛtiśītibhāvam // Lal_22.17 //
body.translated_text: Swiftly he touches <s>bodhi</s>, having defeated <s>Māra</s>; he goes the peaceful path and attains the peace of <s>nirvāṇa</s>!' // Lal_22.17 //

children.text: tasmātka puṇyakaraṇe na bhaveta tṛptaḥ śṛṇvaṃśca dharmamamṛtaṃ bhavi ko vitṛptaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, who would be satiated in the making of merit? And who, hearing the deathless <s>dharma</s>, would be satiated?

children.text: vijane vane ca viharaṃ bhavi ko vitṛptaḥ kaḥ sattva arthakaraṇe na bhaveddhi tṛptaḥ // Lal_22.18 //
children.translated_text: Who, dwelling in the solitary forest, would be satiated? And who would be satiated in accomplishing the welfare of beings?' // Lal_22.18 //

children.text: pāṇiṃ prasārya samuvāca ca bodhisattvāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtā brajata kṣetra svakasvakāni /
children.translated_text: Extending his hand, he addressed the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'You have performed worship; go [now] to your respective realms!'

children.text: sarve 'bhivandya caraṇau ca tathāgatasya nānāviyūha gata kṣetra svakasvakāni // Lal_22.19 //
children.translated_text: All, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, went with their diverse arrays to their respective realms. // Lal_22.19 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ namucināṃ mahatīmavasthāṃ vikrīḍitāṃ ca sugatasya tathā salīlam /
children.translated_text: And having seen that great predicament of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) and the <s>Sugata</s>'s graceful play therein,

children.text: bodhāya cittamatulaṃ praṇidhāya sattvāṃ māraṃ vijitya sabalaṃ amṛtaṃ spṛśema // Lal_22.20 //
children.translated_text: generating the incomparable mind of awakening, [may we,] having conquered <s>Māra</s> with his forces, touch the deathless! // Lal_22.20 //

body.text: abhisaṃbuddhasya bhikṣavastathāgatasya bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanopaviṣṭasya tasmin kṣaṇe 'prameyāni buddhavikrīḍitānyabhūvan, yāni na sukaraṃ kalpenāpi nirdeṣṭum //
body.translated_text: O monks, when the <s>Tathāgata</s> was fully awakened (<s>abhisaṃbuddha</s>), seated on the lion-throne at the root of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, at that moment there were immeasurable Buddha-marvels, which could not easily be described even in an [entire] <s>kalpa</s>. //

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said —

children.text: karatalasadṛśābhūtsusthitā medinīyaṃ vikasitaśatapatrāścodgatā raśmijālaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The earth stood level as the palm of the hand; hundred-petaled lotuses arose with nets of rays;

children.text: amaraśatasahasrā onamī bodhimaṇḍaṃ imu prathama nimittaṃ siṃhanādena dṛṣṭam // Lal_22.21 //
children.translated_text: hundreds of thousands of gods bowed toward the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> — this first portent was seen, with a lion's roar! // Lal_22.21 //

children.text: drumaśatatrisahasro bodhimaṇḍe namante girivara tatha neke śailarājaśca meruḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of trees in the trichiliocosm bow at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>; many excellent mountains and <s>Meru</s>, the king of mountains;

children.text: daśabalamadhigamya brahmaśakrā namante idamapi narasiṃhe krīḍitaṃ bodhimaṇḍe // Lal_22.22 //
children.translated_text: having realized the Ten Powers, <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s> bow — this too is the play of the lion among men at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>! // Lal_22.22 //

children.text: raśmiśatasahasrā svośarīrātmabhāvā sphuri jinavara kṣatrā trīṇi śāntā apāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of rays from his own body pervade <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Jina</s>-realms; the three lower realms are pacified;

children.text: tata kṣaṇasumuhūrte śodhitā cākṣaṇāni na ca khilamadadoṣā bādhiṣū kaṃci sattvam // Lal_22.23 //
children.translated_text: in that very moment, the unfortunate circumstances are purified, and no obstruction, pride, hatred, or fault afflicts any being! // Lal_22.23 //

children.text: iyamapi narasiṃhasyāsanasthasya krīḍā śaśiravimaṇivahnividyutābhā ca divyā /
children.translated_text: This too is the play of the lion among men, seated [on his throne] — his divine radiance [surpasses] the moon, sun, gems, fire, and lightning;

children.text: na tapati abhibhūtā bhānuvatyorṇapāśā na ca jagadiha kaścitprekṣate śāstu mūrdham // Lal_22.24 //
children.translated_text: the sunlight is outshone, overcome by the snare of his <s>ūrṇā</s>; and no one in this world can see the Teacher's crown! // Lal_22.24 //

body.text:
iyamapi narasiṃhasyāsanasthasya krīḍā
karatalaspṛśanenā kampitā corvi sarvā /

children.text: yena namucisenā kṣobhitā tūlabhūtā
children.translated_text: by which <s>Namuci</s>'s army was agitated like cotton;

children.text: namuci iṣu gṛhītvā medinī vyālikhedya
children.translated_text: <s>Namuci</s>, seizing his arrows, inscribed [marks] on the earth —

children.text: idamapi narasiṃhasyāsane krīḍitaṃ bhūt // Lal_22.25 //
children.translated_text: this too was the play of the lion among men at his seat! // Lal_22.25 //

body.translated_text: This too is the play of the lion among men, seated [on his throne] — by the touch of his palm, the entire earth trembles;

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: START Parivarta 23
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Parivarta</s> 23.

body.text: saṃstavaparivartastrayoviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The Twenty-Third Chapter: On Praise (<s>Saṃstavaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgataṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya divyaiścandanacūrṇavarṣairabhyavakīrya ābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhituṣṭuvuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) <s>devaputras</s>, having circumambulated the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> and having showered him with divine sandalwood powder, praised him with these appropriate verses —

children.text: utpanno lokapradyoto lokanāthaḥ prabhaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The illuminator of the world has arisen, the Lord of the World, the light-maker!

children.text: andhabhūtasya lokasya cakṣurdātā raṇaṃjahaḥ // Lal_23.1 //
children.translated_text: For the world that has become blind, the giver of sight, the destroyer of battle! // Lal_23.1 //

children.text: bhavān vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ puṇyaiḥ pūrṇamanorathaḥ /
children.translated_text: You have conquered the battle, your wishes are fulfilled by merits!

children.text: saṃpūrṇaḥ śukladharmaiśca jagattvaṃ tarpayiṣyasi // Lal_23.2 //
children.translated_text: You are full of wholesome qualities — you shall satisfy the world! // Lal_23.2 //

children.text: uttīrṇapaṅko hyanighaḥ sthale tiṣṭhati gautamaḥ /
children.translated_text: He has crossed the mire, stainless, <s>Gautama</s> stands on firm ground!

children.text: anyāṃ sattvāṃ mahoghena prodgatastārayiṣyasi // Lal_23.3 //
children.translated_text: Having risen from the great flood, you shall ferry other beings across! // Lal_23.3 //

children.text: udgatastvaṃ mahāprājño lokeṣvapratipudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: You have arisen, O greatly wise one, without equal in the worlds!

children.text: lokadharmairaliptastvaṃ jalasthamiva paṅkajaḥ // Lal_23.4 //
children.translated_text: You are unstained by worldly conditions, like a lotus in water! // Lal_23.4 //

children.text: ciraprasuptamimaṃ lokaṃ tamaskandhāvaguṇṭhitam /
children.translated_text: This world, long asleep, enveloped in the mass of darkness —

children.text: bhavān prajñāpradīpena samarthaḥ pratibodhitum // Lal_23.5 //
children.translated_text: you are able to awaken it with the lamp of wisdom! // Lal_23.5 //

children.text: cirāture jīvaloke kleśavyādhiprapīḍite /
children.translated_text: In this long-ailing world of the living, oppressed by the disease of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: vaidyarāṭ tvaṃ samutpannaḥ sarvavyādhipramocakaḥ // Lal_23.6 //
children.translated_text: you have arisen as the King of Physicians, the liberator from all diseases! // Lal_23.6 //

children.text: bhaviṣyantyakṣaṇā śūnyā tvayi nāthe samudgate /
children.translated_text: Unfortunate circumstances shall become empty when you, the Lord, have arisen;

children.text: manuṣyāścaiva devāśca bhaviṣyanti sukhānvitāḥ // Lal_23.7 //
children.translated_text: humans and gods shall become endowed with happiness! // Lal_23.7 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ tvaddarśanaṃ saumya eṣyase puruṣarṣabha /
children.translated_text: Those who shall come for your sight, O gentle one, O bull among men —

children.text: na te kalpasahasrāṇi jātu yāsyanti durgatim // Lal_23.8 //
children.translated_text: they shall not go to a lower rebirth for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>! // Lal_23.8 //

children.text: paṇḍitāścāpyarogāśca dharmaṃ śroṣyanti ye 'pi te /
children.translated_text: Those who are wise and healthy, who shall hear the <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: gambhīrāścopadhīkṣīṇā bhaviṣyanti viśāradāḥ // Lal_23.9 //
children.translated_text: profound, with substrata exhausted, they shall become confident! // Lal_23.9 //

children.text: mokṣyante ca laghuṃ sarve chittvā vai kleśabandhanam /
children.translated_text: All shall be swiftly liberated, having cut the bonds of afflictions;

children.text: yāsyanti nirupādānāḥ phalaprāptivaraṃ śubham // Lal_23.10 //
children.translated_text: without clinging, they shall attain the supreme, auspicious attainment of the fruit! // Lal_23.10 //

children.text: dakṣiṇīyāśca te loke āhutīnāṃ pratigrahāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are worthy of offerings in the world, recipients of oblations;

children.text: na teṣu dakṣiṇā nyūnā sattvānirvāṇahetukī // Lal_23.11 //
children.translated_text: offerings to them are not diminished — [they are] the cause of beings' <s>nirvāṇa</s>!' // Lal_23.11 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāstathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte prāñjalayastasthuḥ, prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika devaputras</s>, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu cābhāsvarā devaputrāstathāgataṃ bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ divyairnānāprakāraiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanachatradhvajapatākābhiḥ saṃpūjya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya cābhirgāthābhirabhyastāviṣuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) <s>devaputras</s>, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> with various divine flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, parasols, banners, and pennants, having circumambulated three times, praised him with verses —

children.text: gambhīrabuddhe madhurasvarā mune brahmasvarā munivaragīta susvaram /
children.translated_text: 'O one of profound wisdom, O Sage of sweet voice, <s>Brahmā</s>-voiced, with the well-voiced song of the best of sages!

children.text: varāgrabodhi paramārthaprāptā sarvasvare pāragate namaste // Lal_23.12 //
children.translated_text: The supreme, excellent <s>bodhi</s>, the ultimate truth, has been attained — homage to you who have reached the far shore of all sounds! // Lal_23.12 //

children.text: trātāsi dīpo 'si parāyaṇo 'si nātho 'si loke kṛpamaitracittaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are a protector, you are a lamp, you are a refuge, you are a Lord in the world, with a mind of compassion and loving-kindness!

children.text: vaidyottamastvaṃ khalu śalyahartā cikitsakastvaṃ paramaṃ hitaṃkaraḥ // Lal_23.13 //
children.translated_text: You are the supreme physician, the remover of arrows, the healer — the supreme benefactor! // Lal_23.13 //

children.text: dīpaṃkarasya sahadarśanaṃ tvayā samudānitaṃ maitrakṛpābhrajālam /
children.translated_text: From the moment of seeing <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, you gathered the cloud-net of loving-kindness and compassion;

children.text: pramuñca nāthā amṛtasya dhārāṃ śamehi tāpaṃ suramānuṣāṇām // Lal_23.14 //
children.translated_text: release, O Lord, the stream of the deathless! Allay the torment of gods and humans! // Lal_23.14 //

children.text: tvaṃ padmabhūtaṃ tribhaveṣvaliptaṃ tvaṃ merukalpo vicalo hyakampyaḥ /
children.translated_text: You are like a lotus in the three worlds of existence, unstained; you are like <s>Meru</s>, unmoving and unshakable;

children.text: tvaṃ vajrakalpo hyacalapratijña tvaṃ candramā sarvaguṇāgradhārī // Lal_23.15 //
children.translated_text: you are like a <s>vajra</s>, with unwavering resolve; you are like the moon, bearer of supreme virtues! // Lal_23.15 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣava ābhāsvarā devāstathāgatamabhisaṃstutyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu subrahmadevaputrapramukhā brahmakāyikā devāstathāgataṃ bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇamanekamaṇiratnakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrapratyuptena ratnajālenābhichādya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya cābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhyastāviṣuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> (Brahmā-world) gods, headed by the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Subrahma</s>, having covered the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> with a jeweled net inlaid with many <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of jewels and gems, having circumambulated three times, praised him with these appropriate verses —

children.text: śubhavimalaprajña prabhatejadharā dbātriṃśallakṣaṇavarāgradharā /
children.translated_text: 'O one of auspicious, stainless wisdom, bearing the radiance of splendor, bearing the thirty-two supreme excellent marks,

children.text: smṛtimaṃ matimaṃ guṇajñānadharā akilāntakā śirasi vandami te // Lal_23.16 //
children.translated_text: mindful, wise, bearer of virtue and knowledge, indefatigable — I bow at your head! // Lal_23.16 //

children.text: amalā vimalā trimalairvimalā trailokyaviśruta trividyagatā /
children.translated_text: Pure, stainless, free from the three impurities, famed in the three worlds, one who has attained the three knowledges,

children.text: trividhāvimokṣavaracakṣudadā vandāmi tvāṃ trinayanaṃ vimalam // Lal_23.17 //
children.translated_text: giver of the supreme sight of the three kinds of liberation — I worship you, the stainless one of three eyes [of wisdom]! // Lal_23.17 //

children.text: kalikaluṣa uddhṛta sudāntamanā kṛpakaruṇa udgata jagārthakarā /
children.translated_text: Stain and impurity uprooted, well-tamed in mind, compassion and <s>karuṇā</s> (mercy) have arisen [in you], a worker for the world's welfare;

children.text: muni mudita udgata praśāntamanā dvayamativimocaka upekṣaratā // Lal_23.18 //
children.translated_text: O Sage, <s>muditā</s> (joy) has arisen, of tranquil mind, liberator from duality, delighting in <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity)! // Lal_23.18 //

body.text: vrata tapasa udgata jagārthakarā / svacarīviśuddhacaripāragatā /

children.text: catusatyadarśaka vimokṣaratā mukto vimocayasi cānyajagat // Lal_23.19 //
children.translated_text: a seer of the Four Truths, delighting in liberation — liberated yourself, you liberate other worlds too! // Lal_23.19 //

body.translated_text: Arisen from observances and austerities, a worker for the world's welfare, one who has reached the far shore of pure conduct;

children.text: balavīrya āgatu ihā namuci prajñāya vīrya tava maitrya jito /
children.translated_text: <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) came here with strength and vigor — he was conquered by your wisdom, vigor, and <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)!

children.text: prāptaṃ ca te padavaraṃ amṛtaṃ vandāma te śaṭhacamūmathanā // Lal_23.20 //
children.translated_text: You have attained the supreme, deathless state — we worship you, crusher of the deceitful one's army! // Lal_23.20 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ subrahmadevaputrapramukhā brahmakāyikā devāstathāgatamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya ekānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, headed by the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Subrahma</s>, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with these verses, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu te śuklapākṣikā māraputrā yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramya mahāratnachatravitānaistathāgatamabhicchādya prāñjalayastathāgatamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhyastāviṣuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those sons of <s>Māra</s> who were on the side of virtue (<s>śuklapākṣika</s>) approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, covering the <s>Tathāgata</s> with great jeweled parasol-canopies, with palms joined, they praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with these appropriate verses —

children.text: pratyakṣe 'smi bale tavātivipule mārasya ghorā camū
children.translated_text: 'I was present [as witness] to your exceedingly great power — <s>Māra</s>'s terrible army

children.text: yatsā māracamū mahāpratibhayā ekakṣaṇe te jitā /
children.translated_text: that terrifying army of <s>Māra</s> was conquered by you in a single moment!

children.text: na ca te utthitu naiva kāyu trasito no vā girā vyāhṛtā
children.translated_text: You did not rise up, your body was not frightened, nor was a word uttered —

children.text: tvāṃ vandāmahi sarvalokamahitaṃ sarvārthasiddhaṃ munim // Lal_23.21 //
children.translated_text: we worship you, honored by all the world, the Sage whose every purpose is accomplished! // Lal_23.21 //

children.text: mārā koṭisahasranekanayutā gaṅgāṇubhiḥ saṃmitāḥ
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and many <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Māras</s>, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges,

children.text: te tubhyaṃ na samartha bodhisuvaṭā saṃcālituṃ kampitum /
children.translated_text: are unable to move or shake you from the excellent seat of <s>bodhi</s>!

children.text: yajñā koṭisahasranekanayutā gaṅgā yathā vālikā
children.translated_text: Thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> and many <s>nayutas</s> of sacrifices, like the sands of the Ganges,

children.text: yaṣṭā bodhivaṭāsitena bhavatā tenādya vibhrājase // Lal_23.22 //
children.translated_text: were performed by you at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, O seated one — by that you shine today! // Lal_23.22 //

children.text: bhāryā ceṣṭatamā sutāśca dayitā dāsyaśca
