children.translated_text: Beloved wives, and dear sons, and female servants,

children.text: dāsāstathā udyānā nagarāṇi rāṣṭranigamā rājyāni sāntaḥpurāḥ /
children.translated_text: and male servants likewise, parks, cities, kingdoms, provinces, realms with their inner palaces,

children.text: hastā pādaśirottamāṅgamapi vā cakṣūṃṣi jihvā tathā
children.translated_text: hands, feet, head, and eyes too, and tongue likewise —

children.text: tyaktā te varabodhicarya caratā tenādya vibhrājase // Lal_23.23 //
children.translated_text: relinquished by you while practicing the supreme conduct of awakening — by that you now shine forth! // Lal_23.23 //

children.text: uktaṃ yadvacanaṃ tvayā subahuśo buddho bhaviṣyāmyahaṃ
children.translated_text: "The words you spoke so many times — 'I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: tāriṣye bahusattvakoṭinayutā duḥkhārṇavenohyatā /
children.translated_text: I shall ferry across many <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyutas</s> of beings carried away in the ocean of suffering' —

children.text: dhyānādhīndriyabuddhibhiḥ kavacitaḥ saddharmanāvā svayaṃ
children.translated_text: armored with <s>dhyāna</s>, faculties, and wisdom, yourself the ship of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sā caiṣā pratipūrṇa tubhya praṇidhistāriṣyase prāṇinaḥ // Lal_23.24 //
children.translated_text: that aspiration of yours is now fulfilled — you shall ferry across living beings!" // Lal_23.24 //

children.text: yatpuṇyaṃ ca stavitva vādivṛṣabhaṃ lokasya cakṣurdadaṃ
children.translated_text: "By the merit of praising the bull among speakers, who gives eyes to the world,

children.text: sarve bhūtva udagrahṛṣṭamanasaḥ prārthema sarvajñatām /
children.translated_text: may we all, becoming joyful and elated in mind, aspire to omniscience!

children.text: samudānītva varāgrabodhimatulāṃ buddhaiḥ susaṃvarṇitāṃ
children.translated_text: Having gathered the supreme, incomparable, and excellent awakening, well-praised by the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: evaṃ tadvinihatya mārapariṣāṃ buddhema sarvajñatām // Lal_23.25 //
children.translated_text: thus, having vanquished <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, may we awaken to omniscience!" // Lal_23.25 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo māraputrāstathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Māra</s>'s sons, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu paranirmitavaśavartī devaputro 'nekairdevaputraśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto jāmbūnadasuvarṇavarṇaiḥ padmaistathāgatamabhyavakīrya saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhyastāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> god-son, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of god-sons, having scattered lotuses the color of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold over the <s>Tathāgata</s>, praised him face to face with these verses —

children.text: apīḍita aluḍita avitathavacanā apagatatamaraja amṛtagatigatā /
children.translated_text: "Unoppressed, unagitated, whose words are never false, free from the darkness of delusion, gone to the deathless state,

children.text: arahasi divi bhuvi śriyakriyamatulā atidyutismṛtimati praṇipati śirasā // Lal_23.26 //
children.translated_text: you are worthy of incomparable glory and action in heaven and on earth — O you of surpassing splendor and mindfulness, we bow with our heads!" // Lal_23.26 //

children.text: ratikara raṇajaha rajamalamathanā ramayasi suranara suviśadavacanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Giver of delight, renouncer of battle, crusher of the stains of passion, you gladden gods and humans with your supremely clear words;

children.text: vikasita suvipula varatanu kiraṇaiḥ suranarapatiriva jayasi jagadidam // Lal_23.27 //
children.translated_text: with the radiant rays of your excellent, vast, and blossoming body, you conquer this world like the lord of gods and men!" // Lal_23.27 //

children.text: paragaṇipramathana paracarikuśalā priyu bhava naramaru paramati dhunatā /
children.translated_text: "Subduer of hostile forces, skilled in the conduct of others, dear to humans and gods, dispeller of supreme delusion,

children.text: paracari vibhajasi sunipuṇamatimān pathi iha vicaratu daśabalagamane // Lal_23.28 //
children.translated_text: you expound the conduct of others with supremely subtle wisdom — may [beings] walk here on the path of the <s>Daśabala</s>'s way!" // Lal_23.28 //

children.text: tyaji pṛthu bhavagrahi vitathadukha mahā vinayasi suranara yathamati vinaye /
children.translated_text: "Renouncer of the manifold grasping of existence, [remover of] the great falsehood of suffering, you discipline gods and humans according to their dispositions;

children.text: vicarasi catudiśa śaśiriva gagane cakṣu bhava parāyaṇa iha bhuvi tribhave // Lal_23.29 //
children.translated_text: you move in the four directions like the moon in the sky — be the eye, the refuge, here on earth in the three realms!" // Lal_23.29 //

body.text: priyu bhava naramaru na ca khali viṣaye ramayasi śubharati kāmarativirato /
body.translated_text: "Dear to humans and gods, never harsh in [any] domain, you give delight in wholesome joy, free from the pleasures of desire;

body.text: dinadarśi pariṣadi na ti samu tribhave nāthu gati parāyaṇu tvamiha hi jagataḥ // Lal_23.30 //
body.translated_text: compassionate toward those in the assembly, unequaled in the three realms — you are the protector, the path, the refuge of the world here!" // Lal_23.30 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavo vaśavartidevapramukhāḥ parinirmitavaśavartino devaputrāstathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Vaśavartin</s> god-sons, headed by the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> god, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu sunirmito devaputro devasaṃghaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto nānāratnapaṭṭadāmaistathāgatamabhichādya saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhyastāvīt -

children.text: dharmāloka bhavān samudgata trividhamalanucchido
children.translated_text: "You, O Lord, are the radiance of <s>Dharma</s>, arisen, destroyer of the three impurities,

children.text: mohādṛṣṭiavidyaghātako hiriśiribharitaḥ /
children.translated_text: annihilator of delusion, [wrong] views, and ignorance, filled with modesty and splendor!

children.text: mithyāmārgaratāmimāṃ prajāmamṛte thapayito
children.translated_text: You have established this populace, delighting in wrong paths, in the deathless —

children.text: utpanno iha loki cetiyo divi bhuvi mahitaḥ // Lal_23.31 //
children.translated_text: born here in the world as a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), honored in heaven and on earth!" // Lal_23.31 //

body.translated_text: Then the god-son <s>Sunirmita</s>, surrounded and attended by his divine assembly, having covered the <s>Tathāgata</s> with various garlands of jeweled cloth, praised him face to face with these verses —

children.text: tvaṃ vaidyo kuśalacikitsako hyamṛtasukhadado
children.translated_text: "You are a physician, skilled in healing, giver of the bliss of the deathless;

children.text: dṛṣṭikleśamavidyasaṃcayaṃ purimamanuśayam /
children.translated_text: the accumulation of [wrong] views, <s>kleśas</s>, and ignorance, together with the former latent tendencies —

children.text: sarvavyādhyapanesi dehināṃ purimajinapathe
children.translated_text: you remove all diseases of embodied beings on the path of former <s>Jinas</s>.

children.text: tasmādvaidyatamo 'si nāyakā vicarasi dharaṇīm // Lal_23.32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore you are the supreme physician among guides — you walk upon the earth!" // Lal_23.32 //

children.text: candrāsūryaprabhāśca jyotiṣā maṇi tatha jvalanā
children.translated_text: "The radiance of the moon, sun, and stars, of jewels and of fire,

children.text: śakrabrahmaprabhā na bhāsate puratu śirighane /
children.translated_text: the radiance of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> does not shine before your dense splendor.

children.text: prajñālokakarā prabhaṃkarā prabhasiribharitā
children.translated_text: O maker of the light of wisdom, O radiant one, filled with the glory of radiance,

children.text: pratyakṣāstava jñāti adbhute praṇipati śirasā // Lal_23.33 //
children.translated_text: your wondrous kinsmen behold you directly — we bow with our heads!" // Lal_23.33 //

children.text: satyāsatyakathī vināyakā sumadhuravacanā
children.translated_text: "Speaker of truth, O guide, whose words are supremely sweet,

children.text: dāntā śāntamanā jitendriya praśamitamanasā /
children.translated_text: tamed, with tranquil mind, with conquered senses, with pacified mind,

children.text: śāstā śāsaniyāṃ praśāsase naramarupariṣāṃ
children.translated_text: O teacher, you instruct those who need instruction — the assemblies of humans and gods!

children.text: vande śākyamuniṃ nararṣabhaṃ suranaramahitam // Lal_23.34 //
children.translated_text: We salute <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the bull among men, honored by gods and humans!" // Lal_23.34 //

children.text: jñāniṃ jñānakathāgradhārakā jñapayasi tribhave
children.translated_text: "O knower, foremost bearer of the discourse of knowledge, you make known [the truth] in the three realms;

children.text: traividyatrivimokṣadeśakā trimalamalanudā /
children.translated_text: teacher of the three knowledges and the three liberations, remover of the three impurities!

children.text: bhavyābhavya mune prajānase yathamati vinaye
children.translated_text: O sage, you discern the worthy and the unworthy, disciplining [each] according to their capacity.

children.text: vande tvāṃ trisahasri adbhutaṃ divi bhuvi mahitam // Lal_23.35 //
children.translated_text: We salute you, the wonder of the trichiliocosm, honored in heaven and on earth!" // Lal_23.35 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ sunirmito devaputraḥ saparivārastathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte 'sthāt prāñjalīkṛtastathāgataṃ namaskurvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the god-son <s>Sunirmita</s> with his retinue, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu saṃtuṣito devaputraḥ sārdhaṃ tuṣitakāyikairdevairyena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya mahatā divyavastrajālena bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgatamabhisaṃchādya saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhyastauṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then the god-son <s>Saṃtuṣita</s>, together with the <s>Tuṣita</s>-realm gods, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, covering the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> with a great net of divine garments, he praised him face to face with these verses —

children.text: tuṣitālayi yadvasitastvaṃ tatra ti deśitu dharma udāro /
children.translated_text: "When you dwelt in the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, there you taught the sublime <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: na ca chidyati sā anuśāsti adyapi dharmacarī suraputrā // Lal_23.36 //
children.translated_text: and that instruction has not been severed — even today the god-sons practice the <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_23.36 //

children.text: na ca darśana tṛpti labhāmo dharma śṛṇotu na vindati tṛptim /
children.translated_text: "We do not obtain satisfaction from seeing you, nor does one who hears the <s>Dharma</s> find satiation!

children.text: guṇasāgara lokapradīpā vandima te śirasā manasā ca // Lal_23.37 //
children.translated_text: O ocean of virtues, O lamp of the world, we bow to you with our heads and our minds! // Lal_23.37 //

children.text: tuṣitālaya yaccalitastvaṃ śoṣita akṣaṇa sarvi tadā te /
children.translated_text: "When you departed from the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, all unfavorable states were dried up by you;

children.text: yada bodhivaṭe upaviṣṭaḥ sarvajagasya kileśa praśāntāḥ // Lal_23.38 //
children.translated_text: and when you sat at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, the <s>kleśas</s> of the entire world were pacified! // Lal_23.38 //

children.text: yasya kṛtena ca bodhi udārā eṣa ti prāpti jinitvana māram /
children.translated_text: "By whose deeds the sublime awakening — this attainment, having conquered <s>Māra</s> —

children.text: tvā praṇidhī tapasā paripūrṇā kṣipra pravartaya cakramudāram // Lal_23.39 //
children.translated_text: your aspiration is fulfilled by austerity — quickly turn the sublime wheel!" // Lal_23.39 //

children.text: bahu dikṣiṣu prāṇisahasrā dharmaratā kṣuṇiyāmatha dharmam /
children.translated_text: "In many directions, thousands of beings are devoted to the <s>Dharma</s> — let us hear the <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: kṣipra pravartaya cakramudāraṃ mocaya prāṇisahasra bhaveṣu // Lal_23.40 //
children.translated_text: Quickly turn the sublime wheel — liberate thousands of beings in [all] existences!" // Lal_23.40 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ saṃtuṣito devaputraḥ saparivārastathāgatamabhiṣṭatyaikānte 'sthāt prāñjalīkṛtastathāgataṃ namasyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the god-son <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> with his retinue, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text:
atha khalu suyāmadevaputrapramukhāḥ suyāmā devā yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat /
upasaṃkramya nānāpuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanairbodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgataṃ saṃpūjya saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhistuṣṭavuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Suyāma</s> gods, headed by the god-son <s>Suyāma</s>, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, they worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> with various flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments, and praised him face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: sadṛśo 'sti na te kutontare śīla samādhi tathaiva prajñayā /
children.translated_text: "There is none equal to you anywhere — in morality, concentration, or wisdom;

children.text: adhimuktivimuktikovidā śirasā vandima te tathāgatam // Lal_23.41 //
children.translated_text: skilled in conviction and liberation — we bow with our heads to you, O <s>Tathāgata</s>!" // Lal_23.41 //

children.text: dṛṣṭā sa viyūha śobhanā bodhimaṇḍasmi marubhi yā kṛtā /
children.translated_text: "The splendid display seen at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, made by the <s>Marutas</s> (gods) —

children.text: na tamarhati anya kaścanā yatha tvaṃ devamanuṣyapūjitaḥ // Lal_23.42 //
children.translated_text: no other is worthy of that, as you are, honored by gods and men!" // Lal_23.42 //

children.text: na mudhāya bhavān samudgato yasya arthe bahu cīrṇa duṣkarā /
children.translated_text: "Not in vain have you arisen — you for whose sake many difficult austerities were performed;

children.text: vijito hi śaṭhaḥ sasainyakaḥ prāptā bodhi anuttarā tvayā // Lal_23.43 //
children.translated_text: the deceitful one with his army has been conquered, and the unsurpassed awakening has been attained by you!" // Lal_23.43 //

children.text: āloka kṛto daśādiśe prajñādīpena triloka jvālitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Light has been made in the ten directions; the three worlds are illumined by the lamp of wisdom;

children.text: timiraṃ apanāyayiṣyase dāsyasi cakṣuranuttaraṃ jage // Lal_23.44 //
children.translated_text: you will dispel the darkness and give the unsurpassed eye to the world!" // Lal_23.44 //

children.text: bahukalpa stuvanti bhāṣato romarūpasya na cāntu asti te /
children.translated_text: "Even if one praised you for many <s>kalpas</s>, there would be no end to [even] a single hair-tip [of your virtues]!

children.text: guṇasāgara lokaviśrutā śirasā vandima te tathāgatam // Lal_23.45 //
children.translated_text: O ocean of virtues, renowned throughout the world — we bow with our heads to you, O <s>Tathāgata</s>!" // Lal_23.45 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu te suyāmadevaputrapramukhā devāstathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, those gods headed by the god-son <s>Suyāma</s>, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindraḥ sārdhaṃ trāyatriṃśakāyikairdevairnānāpuṣpadhūpadīpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvarachatradhvajapatākāvyūhaistathāgataṃ saṃpūjya ābhirgāthābhirabhyastāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, together with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> with various flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and pennants, praised him with these verses —

children.text: askhalitā anavadyā sadā susthitā merukalpā mune
children.translated_text: "Unfailing, blameless, always well-established, firm as <s>Meru</s>, O sage,

children.text: daśadiśi suvighuṣṭa jñānaprabhā puṇyatejānvitā /
children.translated_text: your radiance of knowledge is proclaimed in the ten directions, endowed with the splendor of merit!

children.text: buddhaśatasahasra saṃpūjitā pūrvi tubhyaṃ mune
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped by you in the past, O sage —

children.text: tasya viśeṣu yena bodhidrume mārasenā jitā // Lal_23.46 //
children.translated_text: by that distinction, <s>Māra</s>'s army has been conquered at the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree!" // Lal_23.46 //

children.text: śīlaśrutasamādhiprajñākarā jñānaketudhvajā
children.translated_text: "Mine of morality, learning, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom, with the banner and flag of knowledge,

children.text: jaramaraṇanighāti vaidyottamā lokacakṣurdadā /
children.translated_text: destroyer of old age and death, supreme physician, giver of eyes to the world!

children.text: trimalakhilaprahīṇa śāntendriyā śāntacittā mune
children.translated_text: With the three impurities and all obstructions abandoned, with senses pacified, with tranquil mind, O sage —

children.text: śaraṇu tavamupema śākyarṣabhā dharmarājā jage // Lal_23.47 //
children.translated_text: we take refuge in you, O bull of the <s>Śākyas</s>, O <s>Dharma</s>-king in the world!" // Lal_23.47 //

body.text:
bodhicarī anantatulyā abhūdvīryasthāmodgatā
prajñābala upāya maitrābalaṃ brāhmapuṇyaṃ balam /
body.translated_text: "The conduct of awakening was boundless and incomparable, arising from the station of vigor — the power of wisdom, skill in means, and loving-kindness, the power of <s>Brahma</s>-merit;

body.text: eti balamanantatulyā bhavaṃ bodhi saṃprasthite
body.translated_text: these boundless and incomparable powers arise when one sets forth toward awakening —

body.text: daśabalabaladhārī adyā punarbodhimaṇḍe bhuto // Lal_23.48 //
body.translated_text: now the bearer of the ten powers has appeared at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>!" // Lal_23.48 //

children.text: dṛṣṭva camu anantasattve surā bhītatrastābhavan
children.translated_text: "Having seen the army of boundless beings, the gods became frightened and alarmed:

children.text: mā khu śramaṇarāju bādhiṣyate bodhimaṇḍe sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May the king of ascetics not be harmed while seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>!'

children.text: na ca bhavatu babhūva tebhyo bhayaṃ no ca kāyeñjanā
children.translated_text: "But there was no fear for him, nor even a quivering of body;

children.text: karahata gurubhāra saṃkampanā mārasenā jitā // Lal_23.49 //
children.translated_text: without moving a hand, <s>Māra</s>'s army, heavy with its burden, was conquered by him!" // Lal_23.49 //

children.text: yatha ca purimakebhi siṃhāsane prāpta bodhi varā
children.translated_text: "Just as the former ones attained the supreme awakening on the lion-throne,

children.text: tatha tvayā anubuddha tulyā samā anyathā tvaṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: so have you awakened equally and alike — you are no different!

children.text: samamanasa samacitta sarvajñatā sthāma prāptaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: With equal mind and equal thought, the station of omniscience has been attained by you —

children.text: tena bhava svayaṃbhu lokottamo puṇyakṣetraṃ jage // Lal_23.50 //
children.translated_text: therefore you are the Self-Born, supreme in the world, the field of merit in the world!" // Lal_23.50 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhikṣavaḥ śakro devānāmindraḥ sārdhaṃ devaputraistrāyatriṃśaistathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte 'sthāt prāñjalīkṛtastathāgataṃ namaskurvan //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, together with the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> god-sons, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājānaḥ sārdhaṃ caturmahārājakāyikairdevaputrairyena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramyābhimuktakacampakasumanāvārṣikadhānuskārimālyadāmaparigṛhītā apsaraḥśatasahasraparivṛtā divyasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā ābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhistuṣṭuvuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings, together with the <s>Caturmahārājakāyika</s> god-sons, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, holding garlands of <s>abhimukta</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>sumanā</s>, <s>vārṣika</s>, <s>dhānuṣkāri</s> flowers, surrounded by a hundred thousand <s>apsaras</s>, and having performed worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with divine music, they praised him with fitting verses —

children.text: sumadhuravacanā manojñaghoṣā śaśi va praśāntikarā prasannacittā /
children.translated_text: "Sweet-voiced, with a delightful tone, bringing peace like the moon, with a serene mind,

children.text: prahasitavadanā prabhūtajihvā paramasuprītikarā mune namaste // Lal_23.51 //
children.translated_text: with a smiling face, with a broad tongue, bestower of supreme joy — homage to you, O sage!" // Lal_23.51 //

children.text: rutaravita ya asti sarvaloke sumadhura premaṇiyā narāmarūṇām /
children.translated_text: "Whatever calls and cries exist in all the world, sweet and lovely to humans and gods —

children.text: bhavata svaru pramukta mañjughoṣo abhibhavate ruta sarvi bhāṣamāṇāṃ // Lal_23.52 //
children.translated_text: your voice, uttered with a beautiful, melodious tone, surpasses the sounds of all who speak!" // Lal_23.52 //

children.text: rāgu samayi doṣamohakleśā prīti janeti amānuṣāṃ viśuddhām /
children.translated_text: "[Your voice] pacifies passion, hatred, delusion, and <s>kleśas</s>, and generates superhuman, pure joy;

children.text: akaluṣahṛdayā niśāmya dharmaṃ ārya vimukti labhanti te hi sarve // Lal_23.53 //
children.translated_text: those of unstained hearts who hear the <s>Dharma</s> — they all attain the noble liberation!" // Lal_23.53 //

body.text: na ca bhava atimanyase avidvāṃ na ca puna vidvamadena jātu mattaḥ /
body.translated_text: "You do not look down upon the unlearned, nor are you ever intoxicated with the pride of learning;

body.text: unnatu na ca naiva conatastvaṃ giririva susthitu sāgarasya madhye // Lal_23.54 //
body.translated_text: you are neither elated nor downcast — like a mountain well-established in the midst of the ocean!" // Lal_23.54 //

children.text: lābha iha sulabdha mānuṣāṇāṃ yatra hi tādṛśu jātu sattva loke /
children.translated_text: "A gain well-gained by humans is [a world] where such a being is born!

children.text: śrīriva padumo dhanasya dātrī tatha tava dāsyati dharmu sarvaloke // Lal_23.55 //
children.translated_text: As <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) — a lotus, giver of wealth — so shall your <s>Dharma</s> [bless] the entire world!" // Lal_23.55 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu caturmahārājapramukhā mahārājakāyikā devā bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Mahārājakāyika</s> gods headed by the Four Great Kings, having praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, stood to one side with palms joined, paying homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalvantarikṣā devāstathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkramyābhisaṃbodheḥ pūjākarmaṇe sarvamantarīkṣaṃ ratnajālena kiṅkiṇījālena ratnachatrai ratnapatākābhī ratnapaṭṭadāmai ratnāvataṃsakairvividhamuktāhārapuṣpadāmārdhakāyikadevatāparigṛhītairardhacandrakaiśca samalaṃkṛtya tathāgatāya niryātayanti sma / niryātya ca saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhirabhyastāviṣuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then the gods of the atmosphere approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s presence for the worship of his awakening. They adorned the entire atmosphere with jeweled nets, nets of tinkling bells, jeweled parasols, jeweled pennants, garlands of jeweled cloth, jeweled ornaments, various garlands of pearl-strings and flowers held by deities of the upper body, and half-moons, and offered them to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having offered, they praised him face to face with these verses —

children.text: asmāku vāsaṃ gagane dhruvaṃ mune paśyāma sattvā cariyā yathā jage /
children.translated_text: "Our abode is firmly in the sky, O sage — we behold the conduct of beings as it is in the world;

children.text: bhavataścariṃ prekṣiya śuddhasattva skhalitaṃ na paśyāma tavaikacitte // Lal_23.56 //
children.translated_text: yet beholding your conduct, O purified being, we see not a single stumble in your mind! // Lal_23.56 //

children.text: ye āgatā pūjana bodhisattvā gaganaṃ sphuṭaṃ tairnaranāyakebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have come to worship — the sky is filled with those guides of men!

children.text: hānirvimānāna na cābhavanta tathā hi te vai gaganātmabhāvāḥ // Lal_23.57 //
ye antarīkṣātu pravarṣi puṣpāṃ syāccūḍabandhā hi mahāsahasrā /
te tubhya kāye patitā aśeṣā nadyo yathā sāgari saṃpraviṣṭāḥ // Lal_23.58 //
paśyāma chatrāṇyavataṃsakā ca mālāguṇāṃ campakapuṣpadāmāṃ /
hārāṃśca candrāṃśca tathārdhacandrāṃ kṣipanti devā na ca saṃskaroti // Lal_23.59 //
vālasya nābhūdavakāśamasmin devaiḥ sphuṭaṃ sarvata antarīkṣam /
kurvanti pūjāṃ dvipadottamasya na ca te mado jāyati vismayo vā // Lal_23.60 //

body.text: evaṃ khalvantarīkṣadevā bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgatamabhiṣṭutyaikānte 'vatasthivantaḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //

atha khalu bhaumā devāstathāgatasya pūjākarmaṇe sarvāvantaṃ dharaṇītalaṃ suśodhitopaliptaṃ gandhodakapariṣiktaṃ puṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ca kṛtvā nānādūṣyavitānavitataṃ ca tathāgatāya niryātayanti sma / ābhirgāthābhirabhituṣṭuvuḥ -

children.text: vajramiva abhedyā saṃsthitā triḥsahasrā vajramayapadenāyaṃ sthito bodhimaṇḍe /
iha mama tvacamāṃsaṃ śuṣyatāmasthimajjā na ca ahu aspṛśitvā bodhi uttheṣya asmāt // Lal_23.61 //
savibhava narasiṃhā sarviyaṃ triḥsahasrā na kariṣu adhisthānaṃ syādvidīrṇaśeṣā /
tādṛśa mahavegā āgatā bodhisattvā yeṣa kramatalebhiḥ kampitā kṣetrakoṭyaḥ // Lal_23.62 //
lābha iha sulabdhā bhūmidevairudārā yatra paramasattvaścaṃkramī medinīye /
yatra ku raju loke sarva obhāsitāste cetibhu trisahasraḥ kiṃ punastubhya kāyaḥ // Lal_23.63 //
hesti śatasahasraṃ yāvataścāpaskandho dharaṇitalu jagasyā yāvataścopajīvyaḥ /
sarva vayu dharemo medinī triḥsahasrāṃ sarva tava dadāmo bhuṅkṣvimāṃ tvaṃ yatheṣṭam // Lal_23.64 //
yatra bhava sthihedvā caṃkramedvā śayedvā ye 'pi sugataputrāḥ śrāvakā gautamasya /
dharmakatha kathentī ye 'pi vā tāṃ śṛṇonti sarvakuśalamūlaṃ bodhiye nāmayāmaḥ // Lal_23.65 //

body.text: evaṃ khalu bhaumā devā bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaṃ tathāgatamabhiṣṭatyaikānte tasthuḥ prāñjalayastathāgataṃ namasyantaḥ //
// iti śrīlalitavistare saṃstavaparivarto nāma trayoviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
START Parivarta 24
trapuṣabhallikaparivartaścaturviṃśaḥ /

iti hi bhikṣavo 'bhisaṃbuddhastathāgato devairabhiṣṭūyamānaḥ paryaṅkamabhindannanimiṣanayano drumarājaṃ prekṣate sma / dhyānaprītyāhāraḥ sukhapratisaṃvedī saptarātraṃ bodhivṛkṣamūle 'bhināmayati sma //

atha saptāhe 'tikrānte kāmāvacarā devaputrā daśagandhodakakumbhasahasrāṇi parigṛhya yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmanti sma / rūpāvacarā api devaputrā daśagandhodakakumbhasahasrāṇi parigṛhya yena tathāgastenopasaṃkrāmanti sma / upasaṃkramya bodhivṛkṣaṃ tathāgataṃ ca gandhodakena snāpayanti sma / gaṇanāsamatikrāntāśca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāstena tathāgatakāyapatitena gandhodakena svakasvakān kāyānupalimpanti sma / anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpādayāmāsuḥ / svabhavane praviṣṭā api ca te devaputrādayo 'virahitā abhūvaṃstena gandhodakagandhena, na cāsmai gandhāya spṛhāmutpādayāmāsuḥ / tenaiva ca prītiprāmodyena tathāgatagauravamanasikāranirjātenāvaivartikā abhūvannanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ //

atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ samantakusumo nāma devaputrastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt / sa tathāgatasya caraṇayornipatya prāñjalistathāgatametadavocat - ko nāmāyaṃ bhagavan samādhiryena samādhinā samanvāgatastathāgataḥ saptarātraṃ viharatyabhinnaparyaṅkaḥ? evamukto bhikṣavastathāgatastaṃ devaputrametadavocat - prītyāhāravyūho nāma devaputra ayaṃ samādhiryena samādhinā samanvāgatastathāgataḥ saptarātraṃ vyāhārṣīdabhinnaparyaṅkaḥ //
atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ samantakusumo devaputrastathāgataṃ gāthābhirabhyastāvīt -

children.text: rathacaraṇanicitacaraṇā daśaśataarajalajakamaladalatejā /
suramukuṭaghṛṣṭacaraṇā vande caraṇau śirighanasya // Lal_24.1 //
abhivandya sugatacaraṇau pramuditacittastadā sa suraputraḥ /
idamavaci vimatiharaṇaṃ praśāntakaraṇaṃ naramarūṇām // Lal_24.2 //
śākyakulanandijananā antakarā rāgadoṣamohānām /
pramlānaantakaraṇā vinehi kāṅkṣāṃ naramarūṇām // Lal_24.3 //
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ daśabalā buddhvā sarvajñatāmaparimāṇām /
saptāhaṃ mahimaṇḍe jinā na bhindanti paryaṅkam // Lal_24.4 //
kiṃ tu khalu paśyamānaḥ saptāhaṃ animeṣeṇa narasiṃhā /
prekṣasi viśuddhacakṣo vikasitaśatapatratulyākṣaḥ // Lal_24.5 //
kiṃ tu bhavateṣa praṇidhī utāhu sarveṣa vādisiṃhānām /
yena drumarājamūle paryaṅka na bhindi saptāham // Lal_24.6 //
sādhu samaśuddhadantā sugandhagandhāmukhaṃ daśabalasya /
pravada vacanaṃ avitathaṃ kuruṣva prītiṃ naramarūṇām // Lal_24.7 //
tamuvāca candravacanaḥ śṛṇuṣva me bhāṣato amaraputra /
asya praśnasyāhaṃ kiṃcinmātraṃ pravakṣyāmi // Lal_24.8 //
rājā yadvadyasminnabhiṣikto bhavati jñātisaṃghena /
saptāhu taṃ pradeśaṃ na jahāti hi dharmatā rājñām // Lal_24.9 //
evameva daśabalā api abhiṣiktā bhonti yada praṇidhipūrṇāḥ /
saptāhu dharaṇimaṇḍe jinā na bhindanti paryaṅkam // Lal_24.10 //
śūro yathārisaṃghāṃ nirīkṣate nirjitāṃ niravaśeṣāṃ /
buddhā pi bodhimaṇḍe kleśāṃ nihatāṃ nirīkṣante // Lal_24.11 //
iha te kāmakrodhā mohaprabhāvā jagatparinikāśāḥ /
sāhoḍhā iva caurā vināśitā ye niravaśeṣāḥ // Lal_24.12 //
iha me hatāna vividhā mānavidhāmanyunā puraniketāḥ /
sarvāśravā prahīnā jñānaṃ cāgraṃ samotpannam // Lal_24.13 //
iha sā akāryakartrī bhavatṛṣṇā cāriṇī tathāvidyā /
sānuśayamūlajātā paṭunā jñānāgninā dagdhā // Lal_24.14 //
iha sā ahaṃ mameti ca kalipāśu durānugāḍhalitamūlā /
nīvaraṇakaṭhinagranthi chinnā me jñānaśastreṇa // Lal_24.15 //
iha te ciraṃ samāyata ullāpanakā vināśaparyantāḥ /
skandhāḥ sopādānā jñānena mayā parijñātāḥ // Lal_24.16 //
iha te dvayasaṃmohā mithyāgrāhā mahānarakaniṣṭhāḥ /
maya uddhṛtā aśeṣā bhūyaśca na jātu jñāsyante // Lal_24.17 //
iha nīvaraṇavanārī dagdhā me kuśalamūlatejena /
caturaśca viparyāsā nirdagdha mayā niravaśeṣāḥ // Lal_24.18 //

body.text: iha sā vitarkamālā saṃjñāsūtreṣu granthitā nipathī //
vinivartitā aśeṣā bodhyaṅgavicitramālābhiḥ // Lal_24.19 //

children.text: durgāni pañcaṣaṣṭi mohānī triṃśatiṃ ca malināni /
catvāriṃśadaghāni chinnā me 'smiṃ dharaṇimaṇḍe // Lal_24.20 //
ṣoḍaśa asaṃvṛtāni aṣṭādaśa dhātavaśca mahimaṇḍe /
kṛcchrāṇi pañcaviṃśati chinnāni mayehasaṃsthena // Lal_24.21 //
viṃśati rajastarāṇi aṣṭāviṃśati jagasya vitrāsāḥ /
iha me samatikrāntā vīryabalaparākramaṃ karitvā // Lal_24.22 //
tatha buddhanarditānī pañcaśatāsmiṃ mayā samanubuddhā /
paripurṇaśatasahasraṃ dharmāna mayā samanubuddham // Lal_24.23 //
iha me 'nuśaya aśeṣā aṣṭānavatiḥ samūlaparyantāḥ /
paryutthānakisalayā nirdagdhā jñānatejena // Lal_24.24 //
kāṅkṣā vimatisamudayā dṛṣṭījaḍajantitā aśubhamūlā /
tṛṣṇānadī trivegā praśoṣitā jñānasūryeṇa // Lal_24.25 //
kuhanalapanaprahāṇaṃ māyāmātsaryadoṣaīrṣyādyam /
iha te kleśāraṇyaṃ chinnaṃ vinayāgninā dagdham // Lal_24.26 //
iha te vivādamūlā ākarṣaṇadurgatīṣu viṣamāsu /
āryāpavādavacanā jñānavaravirecanairvāntā // Lal_24.27 //
iha ruditakranditānāṃ śocitaparidevitāna paryantam /
prāptaṃ mayā hyaśeṣaṃ jñānaguṇasamādhimāgamya // Lal_24.28 //
oghā ayogagranthāḥ śokāḥ śalyā madapramādāśca /
vijitā mayeha sarve satyanayasamādhimāgamya // Lal_24.29 //
iha maya kileśagahanā saṃkalpavirūḍhamūla bhavavṛkṣāḥ /
smṛtiparaśunā aśeṣā chinnā jñānāgninā dagdhā // Lal_24.30 //
iha so mayā hyatibalo asmiṃ mārastrilokavaśavartī /
jñānāsinā śaṭhātmā hato yathendreṇa daityendraḥ // Lal_24.31 //
iha jālinī aśeṣā ṣaḍviṃśaticāriṇī dharaṇimaṇḍe /
prajñāsinā balavatā chittvā jñānāgninā dagdhā // Lal_24.32 //
iha te mūlakleśāḥ sānuśayā duḥkhaśokasaṃbhūtāḥ /
maya udghṛtā aśeṣā prajñābalalāṅgalamukhena // Lal_24.33 //
iha me prajñācakṣurviśodhitaṃ prakṛtiśuddhasattvānām /
jñānāñjanena mahatā mohapaṭalavistaraṃ bhinnam // Lal_24.34 //
iha dhātubhūta caturo madamakaraviloḍitā vipulatṛṣṇāḥ /
smṛtiśamathabhāskarāṃśau viśoṣitā me bhavasamudrāḥ // Lal_24.35 //
iha viṣayakāṣṭhanicayo vitarkasāmo mahāmadanavahniḥ /
nirvāpito 'tidīpto vimokṣarasaśītatoyena // Lal_24.36 //
iha me anuśayapaṭalā āsvādataḍidvitarkanirghoṣāḥ /
vīryabalapavanavegairvidhūya vilayaṃ samupanītā // Lal_24.37 //
iha me hato hyaśeṣaścittacariripurbhavānugatavairī /
prajñāsinā balavatā smṛtivimalasamādhimāgamya // Lal_24.38 //
iha sā dhvajāgradhārī hastyaśvarathocchritā vikṛtarūpā /
namucibalavīryasenā maitrīmāgamya vidhvastā // Lal_24.39 //
iha pañcaguṇasamṛddhāḥ ṣaḍindriyahayā sadā madonmattāḥ /
baddhā mayā hyaśeṣāḥ samādhisaśubhaṃ samāgamya // Lal_24.40 //
iha anunayapratighānāṃ kalahavivādaprahāṇaparyantaḥ /
prāpto mayā hyaśeṣo apratihatasamādhimāgamya // Lal_24.41 //
children.translated_text: I have attained the complete, unobstructed <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption)! // Lal_24.41 //

children.text: iha mamiyitā ca sarve ādhyātmikabāhirā parikṣīṇā /
children.translated_text: Here all my inner and outer <s>āsravas</s> (impurities) have been exhausted;

children.text: kalpitavikalpitāni ca śūnyamiti samādhimāgamya // Lal_24.42 //
children.translated_text: and all that is imagined and fabricated is empty — thus having attained <s>samādhi</s>! // Lal_24.42 //

children.text: iha lālayitā sarve martyā divyā bhavāgraparyantāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here all the cherished ones — mortals, celestials, up to the peak of existence —

children.text: tyaktā mayā hyaśeṣā āgamya samādhimanivartam // Lal_24.43 //
children.translated_text: have been entirely relinquished by me, having attained the irreversible <s>samādhi</s>! // Lal_24.43 //

children.text: sarvabhavabandhanāni ca muktāni mayeha tāni sarvāṇi /
children.translated_text: And all the bonds of all existences have been released by me here;

children.text: prajñābalena nikhilā trividhamiha vimokṣamāgamya // Lal_24.44 //
children.translated_text: completely through the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), having attained the threefold <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation)! // Lal_24.44 //

children.text: iha hetudarśanādvai jitā mayā hetukāstrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through seeing the true cause, the three cause-makers have been conquered by me:

children.text: saṃjñā nityānitye saṃjñā sukhaduḥkha cātmani ca // Lal_24.45 //
children.translated_text: the perception of permanence regarding the impermanent, the perception of happiness regarding suffering, and [the perception of self] regarding the self! // Lal_24.45 //

children.text: iha me karmavidhānā samudayamuditā ṣaḍāyatanamūlā /
children.translated_text: Here my karmic dispositions, arisen from origination, rooted in the six sense-bases,

children.text: chinnā drumendramūle sarvānityaprahāreṇa // Lal_24.46 //
children.translated_text: have been cut down at the root of the great tree by the blow of [seeing] all as impermanent! // Lal_24.46 //

children.text: iha mohatamaḥ kaluṣaṃ duṣṭīkṛta darparoṣasaṃkīrṇam /
children.translated_text: Here the turbid darkness of delusion, corrupted by arrogance and anger,

children.text: bhittvā kṣatre sucirāndhakāraṃ prabhāsitaṃ jñānasūryeṇa // Lal_24.47 //
children.translated_text: having split the long darkness in the field, has been illuminated by the sun of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge)! // Lal_24.47 //

children.text: iha rāgamadanamakaraṃ tṛṣṇormijalaṃ kudṛṣṭisaṃgrāham /
children.translated_text: Here the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with its crocodile of passion and desire, its waves of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), its gathering of wrong views,

children.text: saṃsārasāgaramahaṃ saṃtīrṇo vīryabalanāvā // Lal_24.48 //
children.translated_text: has been crossed over by me, [using] vigor and strength as my boat! // Lal_24.48 //

children.text: iha tanmayānubuddhaṃ yadbuddho rāgadveṣamohāṃśca /
children.translated_text: Here that which has been fully awakened to by me, the <s>Buddha</s> — <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) —

children.text: pradahati cittavitarkāṃ davāgnipatitāniva pataṅgāṃ // Lal_24.49 //
children.translated_text: burns up the thoughts and conceptions, like moths fallen into a forest fire! // Lal_24.49 //

children.text: iha ahu ciraprayāto hyaparimita kalpakoṭinayutāni /
children.translated_text: Here I have long traveled for immeasurable <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: saṃsārapathā kliṣṭo viśrāṃto naṣṭasaṃtāpaḥ // Lal_24.50 //
children.translated_text: afflicted on the path of <s>saṃsāra</s> — [now] I have rested, my torment destroyed! // Lal_24.50 //

children.text: iha tanmayānubuddhaṃ sarvaparapravādibhiryadaprāptam /
children.translated_text: Here that which has been fully awakened to by me, which was unattained by all other teachers —

children.text: amṛtaṃ lokahitārthaṃ jarāmaraṇaśokaduḥkhāntam // Lal_24.51 //
children.translated_text: the deathless, for the welfare of the world, ending old age, death, grief, and suffering! // Lal_24.51 //

children.text: yatra skandhairduḥkhaṃ āyatanaiḥ tṛṣṇasaṃbhavaṃ duḥkham /
children.translated_text: Where there is suffering through the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), where there is suffering arising from <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) through the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) —

children.text: bhūyo na codbhaviṣyati abhayapuramihābhyupagato 'smi // Lal_24.52 //
children.translated_text: it shall not arise again; I have entered the city of fearlessness here! // Lal_24.52 //

children.text: iha te mayānubuddhā ripavo adhyātmikā mahākṛtsnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here those great inner enemies have been fully known by me;

children.text: baddhā ca saṃpradagdhāḥ kṛtāśca me puna bhavaniketāḥ // Lal_24.53 //
children.translated_text: they have been bound and burnt, and my dwellings in [further] existence have been completed! // Lal_24.53 //

children.text: iha tanmayānubuddhaṃ yasyārthe kalpakoṭinayutāni /
children.translated_text: Here that which has been fully awakened to by me — for the sake of which, for <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: tyaktā samāṃsanayanā ratnāni bahūnyamṛtahetoḥ // Lal_24.54 //
children.translated_text: eyes with their flesh were given up, and many jewels, for the sake of the deathless! // Lal_24.54 //

children.text: iha tanmayānubuddhaṃ yadbuddhaṃ prāktanairjinairaparimāṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here that which has been fully awakened to by me, which was awakened to by immeasurable former <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) —

children.text: yasya madhurābhiramyaḥ śabdo lokeṣu vikhyātaḥ // Lal_24.55 //
children.translated_text: whose sweet and delightful sound is renowned in all worlds! // Lal_24.55 //

children.text: iha tanmayānubuddhaṃ pratītyasamudāgataṃ jagacchūnyam /
children.translated_text: Here that which has been fully awakened to by me: the world, arisen through dependent origination, is empty,

children.text: cittekṣaṇe 'nuyātaṃ marīcigandharvapuratulyam // Lal_24.56 //
children.translated_text: perceived through the examination of mind — like a mirage or a gandharva city! // Lal_24.56 //

children.text: iha me tatkhalu śuddhaṃ varanayanaṃ yena (loka) dhātavaḥ sarvāṃ /
children.translated_text: Here my excellent eye has been purified, by which all world-realms —

children.text: paśyāmi pāṇimadhye nyastāni yathā drumaphalāni // Lal_24.57 //
children.translated_text: I see as if placed in the palm of my hand, like fruits on a tree! // Lal_24.57 //

children.text: pūrvenivāsasmaraṇaṃ tisro vidyā mayeha saṃprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Recollection of former abodes — the three knowledges have been attained by me here;

children.text: aparimitakalpanayutā smarāmi svapnādiva vibuddhaḥ // Lal_24.58 //
children.translated_text: I remember immeasurable <s>kalpa-nayutas</s>, as if awakened from a dream! // Lal_24.58 //

children.text: yairādīpta suranarā viparītavisaṃjñino viparyastāḥ /
children.translated_text: By which gods and humans are inflamed, with perverted perceptions and inverted [views] —

children.text: so 'pi ca tathā avitathā iha maya pīto hyamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.59 //
children.translated_text: that too, truly and without falsehood, the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.59 //

children.text: yasyārthāya daśabalā maitrī bhāventi sarvasattveṣu /
children.translated_text: For the sake of which the <s>Daśabalas</s> (Ten-Powered Ones) cultivate <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings —

children.text: maitrībalena jitvā pīto me 'sminnamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.60 //
children.translated_text: having conquered by the power of <s>maitrī</s>, the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.60 //

children.text: yasyārthāya daśabalāḥ karuṇā bhāventi sarvasattveṣu /
children.translated_text: For the sake of which the <s>Daśabalas</s> cultivate <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) toward all beings —

children.text: karuṇābalena jitvā pīto me 'sminnamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.61 //
children.translated_text: having conquered by the power of <s>karuṇā</s>, the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.61 //

children.text: yasyārthāya daśabalā muditā bhāventi sarvasattveṣu /
children.translated_text: For the sake of which the <s>Daśabalas</s> cultivate <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) toward all beings —

children.text: muditābalena jitvā pīto me 'sminnamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.62 //
children.translated_text: having conquered by the power of <s>muditā</s>, the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.62 //

children.text: yasyārthāya daśabalā upekṣa bhāventi kalpanayutāni /
children.translated_text: For the sake of which the <s>Daśabalas</s> cultivate <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) for <s>kalpa-nayutas</s> —

children.text: tamupekṣabalairjitvā pīto me 'sminnamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.63 //
children.translated_text: having conquered that by the powers of <s>upekṣā</s>, the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.63 //

children.text: yatpītaṃ ca daśabalairgaṅgānadīvālikābahutarebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That which was drunk by the <s>Daśabalas</s>, more numerous than the sands of the Ganges River,

children.text: prāgjinasiṃhaiḥ pūrve iha me pīto hyamṛtamaṇḍaḥ // Lal_24.64 //
children.translated_text: by the former lion-like <s>Jinas</s> — the nectar-essence has been drunk by me here! // Lal_24.64 //

children.text: yā bhāṣitā ca vāgme mārasyehāgatasya sasainyasya /
children.translated_text: And the speech that was spoken by me when <s>Māra</s> came here with his army:

children.text: bhetsyāmi na paryaṅkaṃ aprāpya jarāmaraṇapāram // Lal_24.65 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall not break the cross-legged posture without reaching the far shore of old age and death!' // Lal_24.65 //

children.text: bhinnā mayā hyavidyā dīptena jñānakaṭhinavajreṇa /
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) has been shattered by me with the blazing, adamantine <s>vajra</s> of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge);

children.text: prāptaṃ ca daśabalatvaṃ tasmātprabhinadmi paryaṅkam // Lal_24.66 //
children.translated_text: the state of <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten Powers) has been attained — therefore I break the cross-legged posture! // Lal_24.66 //

children.text: prāptaṃ mayārahatvaṃ kṣīṇā me āśravā niravaśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Arhatva</s> (the state of an Arhat) has been attained by me; my <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) are exhausted without remainder;

children.text: bhagnā ca namucisenā bhinadmi tasmāddhi paryaṅkam // Lal_24.67 //
children.translated_text: the army of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) has been broken — therefore I break the cross-legged posture! // Lal_24.67 //

children.text: nīvaraṇakapāṭāni ca pañca mayeha pradāritā sarvā /
children.translated_text: The five door-panels of the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) have all been shattered by me here;

children.text: tṛṣṇālatā vichinnā hanteha bhinadmi paryaṅkam // Lal_24.68 //
children.translated_text: the creeper of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) has been severed — come, I break the cross-legged posture here! // Lal_24.68 //

children.text: atha so manuṣyacandraḥ savilambitamāsanātsamutthāya /
children.translated_text: Then that moon among men, rising slowly from his seat,

children.text: bhadrāsane niṣīdanmahābhīṣekaṃ pratīcchaṃśca // Lal_24.69 //
children.translated_text: sat on the auspicious throne, receiving the great consecration! // Lal_24.69 //

children.text: ratnaghaṭasahasrairapi nānāgandhodakaiśca surasaṃghā /
children.translated_text: With thousands of jeweled vessels and various fragrant waters, the hosts of gods

children.text: snapayanti lokabandhuṃ daśabalaguṇapāramiprāptam // Lal_24.70 //
children.translated_text: bathe the Friend of the World who has reached the perfection of the qualities of the <s>Daśabala</s>! // Lal_24.70 //

children.text: vāditrasahasrairapi samantato devakoṭinayutāni /
children.translated_text: With thousands of musical instruments, all around, <s>koṭī-nayutas</s> of gods,

children.text: atulāṃ karonti pūjāṃ apsaranayutaiḥ saha samagrāḥ // Lal_24.71 //
children.translated_text: offer incomparable worship, together with <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Apsarases</s>, all assembled! // Lal_24.71 //

children.text: evaṃ khalu devasutāḥ sahetu sapratyayaṃ ca sanidānam /
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>devaputras</s>, with cause, with condition, and with basis —

children.text: saptāhu dharaṇimaṇḍe jinā na bhindanti paryaṅkam // Lal_24.72 //
children.translated_text: for seven days the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) do not break the cross-legged posture on the ground-<s>maṇḍala</s>! // Lal_24.72 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo 'bhisaṃbuddhabodhistathāgataḥ prathame saptāhe tatraivāsane 'sthāt - iha mayānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā, iha mayānavarāgrasya jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasyāntaḥ kṛta iti / dvitīye saptāhe tathāgato dīrghacaṃkramaṃ caṃkramyate sma trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātumupagṛhya / tṛtīye saptāhe tathāgato 'nimiṣaṃ bodhimaṇḍamīkṣate sma - iha mayānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyānavarāgrasya jātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhasyāntaḥ kṛta iti / caturthe saptāhe tathāgato daharacaṃkramaṃ caṃkramyate sma pūrvasamudrātpaścimasamudramupagṛhya //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to <s>bodhi</s>, remained on that very seat for the first week, [thinking]: 'Here the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> (enlightenment) has been fully awakened to by me; here the end of birth, old age, death, and suffering, which is without superior or inferior, has been made by me.' In the second week, the <s>Tathāgata</s> walked on a long walking-path encompassing the great trichiliocosm. In the third week, the <s>Tathāgata</s> gazed unblinkingly at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, [thinking]: 'Here the supreme, perfect <s>saṃbodhi</s> has been fully awakened to by me; the end of birth, old age, death, and suffering, which is without superior or inferior, has been made by me.' In the fourth week, the <s>Tathāgata</s> walked on a short walking-path encompassing from the eastern ocean to the western ocean. //

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tathāgatametadavocat - parinirvātu bhagavan, parinirvātu sugata / samaya idānīṃ bhagavataḥ parinirvāṇāya / evamukte bhikṣavastathāgato māraṃ pāpīyāṃsametadavocat - na tāvadahaṃ pāpīyan parinirvāsyāmi yāvanme na sthavirā bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti dāntā vyaktā vinītā viśāradā bahuśrutā dharmānudharmapratipannāḥ pratibalāḥ svayamācāryakaṃ jñānaṃ paridīpayitumutpannotpannānāṃ ca parapravādināṃ saha dharmeṇa nigṛhyābhiprāyaṃ prasādya saprātihāryaṃ dharmaṃ deśayitum / na tāvadahaṃ pāpīyan parinirvāsyāmi yāvanmayā buddhadharmasaṃghavaṃśo lokena pratiṣṭhāpito bhaviṣyati / aparimitā bodhisattvā na vyākṛtā bhaviṣyanti
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'May the Blessed One attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! May the <s>Sugata</s> attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! It is now time for the Blessed One's <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Thus addressed, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> said this to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'I will not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O Evil One, until my elder monks become tamed, skilled, trained, confident, learned, practitioners of <s>dharma</s> in accordance with <s>dharma</s>, capable of illuminating their own teacher's knowledge, and of subduing opponents of other doctrines who arise again and again, rightly, through the <s>dharma</s>, winning them over and teaching the <s>dharma</s> with miracles. I will not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O Evil One, until the lineage of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> has been established in the world by me. Immeasurable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> shall not have been given predictions

body.text: anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / na tāvadahaṃ pāpīyān parinirvāsyāmi yāvanme na catasraḥ parṣado dāntā vinītā vyaktā viśāradā bhaviṣyanti yāvatsaprātihāya dharmaṃ deśayitumiti //
body.translated_text: of supreme, perfect enlightenment. I will not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O Evil One, until my four assemblies become tamed, trained, skilled, and confident, able to teach the <s>dharma</s> with miracles.' //

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyānidaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā ekānte prakrāmya sthito 'bhūt duḥkhī durmanā vipratisārī adhomukhaḥ kāṣṭhena mahīṃ vilikhan viṣayaṃ me 'tikrānta iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, having heard these words, withdrew and stood to one side, sorrowful, dejected, remorseful, face downward, scratching the ground with a stick, [thinking]: 'My domain has been surpassed!' //

body.text: atha khalu tāstisro māraduhitaro ratiścāratiśca tṛṣṇā ca māraṃ pāpīyāṃsaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those three daughters of <s>Māra</s> — <s>Rati</s> (Pleasure), <s>Ārati</s> (Displeasure), and <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (Craving) — addressed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One with a verse:

children.text: durmanāsi kathaṃ tāta procyatāṃ yadyasau naraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Why are you dejected, father? Tell us! If that man —

children.text: rāgapāśena taṃ buddhvā kuñjaraṃ vā nayāmahe // Lal_24.73 //
children.translated_text: we shall bind him with the noose of passion and lead him like an elephant!' // Lal_24.73 //

children.text: ānayitvā ca taṃ śīghraṃ kariṣyāma vaśe tava /
children.translated_text: 'Having brought him quickly, we shall place him under your power!'

body.text: māra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: arahan sugato loke na rāgasya vaśaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Sugata</s> in the world, would not come under the sway of passion;

children.text: viṣayaṃ me hyatikrāntastasmācchocāmyahaṃ bhṛśam // Lal_24.75 //
children.translated_text: he has surpassed my domain — therefore I grieve greatly!' // Lal_24.75 //

body.text: tatastāḥ strīcāpalyādaviditaprabhāvā api bodhisattvabhūtasyaiva tathāgatasya piturvacanamaśrutvaiva prabhūtayauvanamadhyayauvanadhāriṇyo bhūtvā vicakṣuḥkarmaṇe tathāgatasyāntikamupasaṃkrāntāḥ strīmāyā ati tatsarvamakārṣuḥ / tāśca tathāgato na manasi karoti sma / bhūyaśca tā jarājarjarā adhyatiṣṭhan / tatastāḥ piturantike gatvaivamāhuḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those [daughters], out of feminine fickleness, not knowing the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who had already become a <s>Bodhisattva</s> (i.e., a Buddha), not heeding their father's words, assumed forms of abundant youth and middle youth, and approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s presence to lead his eyes astray. They performed all manner of feminine wiles. But the <s>Tathāgata</s> paid them no attention. Furthermore, he caused them to appear as decrepit old women. Then they went before their father and said:

children.text: satyaṃ vadasi nastāta na rāgeṇa sa nīyate /
children.translated_text: 'You speak the truth, father — he is not led by passion!

children.text: viṣayaṃ me hyatikrāntastasmācchocāmyahaṃ bhṛśam // Lal_24.76 //
children.translated_text: He has surpassed my domain — therefore I grieve greatly!' // Lal_24.76 //

children.text: vīkṣeta yadyasau rūpaṃ yadasmābhirvinirmitam /
children.translated_text: 'If he were to look upon the form that was created by us

children.text: gautamasya vināśārthaṃ tato 'sya hṛdayaṃ sphuṭet // Lal_24.77 //
children.translated_text: for <s>Gautama</s>'s destruction — then his heart would burst!' // Lal_24.77 //

body.text: tatsādhu nastātedaṃ jarājarjaraśarīramantardhāpaya //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, good father, cause this decrepit, aged body to disappear!' //

body.text: māra āha -
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: nāhaṃ paśyāmi taṃ loke puruṣaṃ sacarācare /
children.translated_text: 'I do not see that person in the world of moving and unmoving beings

children.text: buddhasya yo hyadhiṣṭhānaṃ śaknuyātkartumanyathā // Lal_24.78 //
children.translated_text: who could make the <s>Buddha</s>'s resolve otherwise!' // Lal_24.78 //

children.text: śīghraṃ gatvā nivedaya atyayaṃ svakṛtaṃ muneḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Go quickly and confess to the Sage the transgression you have committed;

children.text: sarvaṃ paurāṇakaṃ kāyaṃ kariṣyati yathāmatam // Lal_24.79 //
children.translated_text: he will restore all your former bodies as he sees fit!' // Lal_24.79 //

body.text: tatastā gatvā tathāgataṃ kṣamāpayanti sma - atyayaṃ no bhagavān pratigṛhṇātu / atyayaṃ no sugato pratigṛhṇātu yathā bālānāṃ yathā mūḍhānāṃ yathā vyaktānāmakuśalānāmakṣetrajñānāṃ yā vayaṃ bhagavantamāsādayitavyaṃ manyāmahe / tatastāstathāgato gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then they went and begged the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s forgiveness: 'May the Blessed One accept our transgression! May the <s>Sugata</s> accept our transgression — as that of fools, as that of deluded ones, as that of the unwise, the unskillful, those ignorant of what is proper — we who presumed to assail the Blessed One!' Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> addressed them with a verse:

children.text: giriṃ nakhairvilikhetha lohaṃ dantairvikhādatha /
children.translated_text: 'You would scratch a mountain with your nails; you would gnaw iron with your teeth;

children.text: śirasā vibhitsatha girimagādhe gādhameṣata // Lal_24.80 //
children.translated_text: you would split a mountain with your head; you would seek a foothold in the fathomless! // Lal_24.80 //

body.text: tasmādyuṣmākaṃ dārikā atyayaṃ pratigṛhṇāmi / tatkasmāt? vṛddhireṣā ārye dharmavinaye yo 'tyayamatyayato dṛṣṭvā pratideśayatyāyatyāṃ ca saṃvaramāpadyate //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, daughters, I accept your transgression. Why? For this is growth in the Noble <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>: that one who, having seen a transgression as a transgression, confesses it and undertakes restraint for the future.' //

body.text: pañcame saptāhe bhikṣavastathāgato mucilindanāgarājabhavane viharati sma saptāhe mahādurdine / atha khalu mucilindanāgarājaḥ svabhavanānniṣkramya tathāgatasya kāye saptakṛdbhogena pariveṣṭya phaṇaiśchādayati sma - mā bhagavataḥ kāyaṃ śītavātāḥ prākṣuriti / pūrvasyā api diśo 'nye 'pi saṃbahulā nāgarājā āgatya tathāgatasya kāyaṃ saptakṛdbhogaiḥ pariveṣṭya phaṇaiśchādayanti sma - mā bhagavataḥ kāyaṃ śītavātāḥ prākṣuriti / yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottarābhyo digbhyo nāgarājā āgatya tathāgatasya kāyaṃ saptakṛtvo bhogaiḥ pariveṣṭya phaṇaiśrchādayanti - sma mā bhagavataḥ kāyaṃ śītavātāḥ prākṣuriti / sa ca nāgarājabhogarāśirmeruparvatendravaduccaistvena sthito 'bhūt / na ca tairnāgarājaistādṛśaṃ kadācitsukhaṃ prāptaṃ pūrvaṃ yādṛśaṃ teṣāṃ tāni saptarātriṃdivasāni tathāgatakāyasaṃnikarṣādāsīt / tataḥ saptāhasyātyayena tataste nāgarājā vyapagatadurdinaṃ viditvā tathāgatasya kāyādbhogānapanīya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya svakasvakāni bhavanānyupajagmuḥ / mucilindo 'pi nāgarājastathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya svabhavanaṃ prāvikṣat //
body.translated_text: In the fifth week, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> dwelt in the abode of <s>Mucilinda</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king, during a great storm lasting seven days. Then <s>Mucilinda</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king, coming forth from his abode, enveloped the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body seven times with his coils and sheltered [him] with his hoods — [thinking:] 'May cold winds not touch the Blessed One's body!' From the eastern direction too, many other <s>Nāga</s> kings came and enveloped the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body seven times with their coils and sheltered [him] with their hoods — [thinking:] 'May cold winds not touch the Blessed One's body!' As in the eastern direction, so from the southern, western, and northern directions, <s>Nāga</s> kings came and enveloped the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body seven times with their coils and sheltered [him] with their hoods — [thinking:] 'May cold winds not touch the Blessed One's body!' That mass of <s>Nāga</s> king coils stood as lofty as Mount <s>Meru</s>. And those <s>Nāga</s> kings had never previously experienced such happiness as they felt during those seven days and nights from the proximity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body. Then, at the end of the seven days, those <s>Nāga</s> kings, knowing that the storm had passed, withdrew their coils from the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, bowed at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet with their heads, circumambulated three times, and went to their respective abodes. <s>Mucilinda</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king too, bowed at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet with his head, circumambulated three times, and entered his own abode. //

body.text: ṣaṣṭhe saptāhe tathāgato mucilindabhavanādajapālasya nyagrodhamūlaṃ gacchati sma / antare ca mucilindabhavanasyāntarāccājapālasya nadyā nairañjanāyāstīre carakaparivrājakavṛddhaśrāvakagautamanirgranthājīvikādayastathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvābhibhāṣante sma - api bhagavatā gautamenedaṃ saptāhamakāladurdinaṃ samyaksukhena vyatināmitam?
body.translated_text: In the sixth week, the <s>Tathāgata</s> went from <s>Mucilinda</s>'s abode to the root of the <s>Ajapāla</s> <s>Nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree. And in the interval between <s>Mucilinda</s>'s abode and <s>Ajapāla</s>'s [tree], on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, wandering ascetics — <s>Carakas</s>, <s>Parivrājakas</s>, elderly <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Gautamas</s>, <s>Nirgranthas</s>, <s>Ājīvikas</s>, and others — having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, addressed him: 'Has the Blessed One <s>Gautama</s> passed these seven days of untimely storms in perfect comfort?'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatastasyāṃ velāyāmidamudānayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> at that time uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>) —

children.text: sukho vivekastuṣṭasya śrutadharmasya paśyataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The happiness of seclusion belongs to one who is content, who has heard the <s>dharma</s> and sees [the truth];

children.text: avyābadhyaṃ sukhaṃ loke prāṇibhūteṣu saṃyataḥ // Lal_24.81 //
children.translated_text: non-harming is happiness in the world — restraint toward living beings! // Lal_24.81 //

children.text: sukhā virāgatā loke pāpānāṃ samatikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Happy is dispassion in the world, the transcending of evils!

children.text: asmin mānuṣyaviṣaye etadvai paramaṃ sukham // Lal_24.82 //
children.translated_text: In this human realm, this indeed is the supreme happiness!' // Lal_24.82 //

body.text: paśyati sma bhikṣavastathāgato lokamādīptaṃ pradīptaṃ jātyā jarayā vyādhibhirmaraṇena śokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ / tatra tathāgata idamihodānamudānayati sma -
body.translated_text: O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> saw the world burning, ablaze — with birth, old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> uttered this inspired utterance —

children.text: ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃtāpajātaḥ śabdasparśarasarūpagandhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This world is born into torment through sounds, touches, tastes, forms, and scents;

children.text: bhayabhīto bhayaṃ bhūyo mārgate bhavatṛṣṇayā // Lal_24.83 //
children.translated_text: frightened by fear, it seeks fear further, through craving for existence!' // Lal_24.83 //

body.text: saptame saptāhe tathāgato tārāyaṇamūle viharati sma / tena khalu punaḥ samayenottarāpathakau dvau bhrātarau trapuṣabhallikanāmakau vaṇijau paṇḍitau nipuṇau vividhapaṇyaṃ gṛhītvā mahālabdhalābhau dakṣiṇāpathāduttarāpathaṃ gacchete sma mahatā sārthena pañcabhirdhuraśataiḥ suparipūrṇaiḥ / tayoḥ sujātaḥ kīrtiśca nāmājāneyau dvau balīvardāvāstām / nāsti tayorlagnabhayam / yatrānye balīvardā na
body.translated_text: In the seventh week, the <s>Tathāgata</s> dwelt at the root of the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> tree. Now at that time, two brothers from the Northern Road, merchants named <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>, wise and clever, having taken various wares, having gained great profit, were traveling from the Southern Road to the Northern Road with a great caravan of five hundred carts, well-laden. They had two noble bulls named <s>Sujāta</s> and <s>Kīrti</s>. There was no fear of [the bulls] getting stuck. Where other bulls could not

body.text: vahanti sma tatra tau yujyete sma / yatra cāgrato bhayaṃ bhavati sma tatra, tau kīlabaddhāviva tiṣṭhete sma / na ca tau pratodena vāhyete sma / utpalahastakena vā sumanādāmakena vā tau vāhyete sma / teṣāṃ tārāyaṇasamīpe kṣīrikāvananivāsinīdevatādhiṣṭhānātte śakaṭāḥ sarve viṣṭhitā na vahanti sma / vastrādīni ca sarvaśakaṭāṅgāni ca chidyante sma, bhidyante ca / śakaṭācakrāṇi ca nābhīparyantaṃ bhūmau nimagnāni sarvaprayatnairapi te śakaṭā na vahanti sma / te vismitā bhītāścābhūvan - kiṃ nu khalvatra kāraṇam, ko 'yaṃ vikāro yadime sthale śakaṭā viṣṭhitāḥ? taistau sujātakīrtibalīvardau yojitau / tāvapi na vahete sma sotpalahastena ca sumanādāmakena ca vāhyamānau / teṣāmetadabhavat - asaṃśayaṃ purataḥ kiṃcidbhayaṃ yenaitāvapi na vahataḥ / tairaśvadūtāḥ purataḥ preṣitāḥ / aśvadūtāḥ pratyāgatāḥ / prāhurnāsti kiṃcidbhayamiti / tayāpi devatayā svarūpaṃ saṃdarśya āśvāsitāḥ - mā bhetavyamiti / tāvapi balīvadau yena tathāgatastena śakaṭā prakarṣitau yāvatte paśyanti sma tathāgataṃ vaiśvānaramiva pradīptaṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaciroditamiva dinakaraṃ śriyā daidīpyamānam / dṛṣṭvā ca te vismitā babhūvuḥ - kiṃ nu khalvayaṃ brahmā ihānuprāpta utāho śakro devendra utāho vaiśravaṇa utāho sūryacandrau vā utāho kiṃcidgiridevataṃ vā nadīdevataṃ vā / tatastathāgataḥ kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi prakaṭāyati sma / tataste āhuḥ - pravrajitaḥ khalvayaṃ kāṣāyasaṃvṛto nāsmādbhayamastīti / te prasādaṃ pratilabdhā anyonyamevamāhuḥ - pravrajitaḥ khalvayaṃ kālabhojī bhaviṣyati / asti kiṃcit? āhuḥ - asti madhutarpaṇaṃ likhitakāścekṣavaḥ / te madhutarpaṇamikṣulikhitakāṃścādāya yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivanditvā tripradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte tasthuḥ / ekānte sthitāste tathāgatamevamāhuḥ - pratigṛhṇātu bhagavannidaṃ piṇḍapātramasmākamanukampāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: pull, those two would be yoked. And where danger lay ahead, those two would stand as if fastened to a post. They were not driven with a goad, but with a lotus-stalk or a <s>sumanā</s> (jasmine) garland. Near the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> [tree], by the influence of a tree-deity dwelling in a <s>kṣīrikā</s> (milk-tree) grove, all their carts stopped and would not move. Garments and all parts of the carts were being torn and broken. The cart-wheels sank into the ground up to the hubs, and despite all efforts those carts would not move. They were amazed and frightened: 'What can be the cause here? What is this disruption, that these carts have stopped on level ground?' They yoked those two bulls <s>Sujāta</s> and <s>Kīrti</s>. Even those two would not pull, though urged with the lotus-stalk and jasmine garland. They thought: 'Undoubtedly there is some danger ahead, since even these two will not pull.' They sent horse-scouts ahead. The scouts returned and said: 'There is no danger.' And that deity, having shown her own form, reassured them: 'Do not be afraid!' Those two bulls then pulled the carts toward where the <s>Tathāgata</s> was, until they saw the <s>Tathāgata</s> — blazing like the universal fire, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, resplendent with glory like the newly-risen sun. Having seen [him], they were amazed: 'Is this <s>Brahmā</s> who has come here? Or <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods? Or <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>? Or the sun and moon? Or some mountain deity or river deity?' Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> revealed his saffron robes. Then they said: 'This is indeed a renunciant, covered in saffron — there is nothing to fear from him!' Having gained faith, they said to one another: 'This renunciant must eat at the proper time. Is there anything?' They said: 'There is honey-cake and sugarcane sticks.' Taking the honey-cake and sugarcane sticks, they approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, they bowed at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet with their heads, circumambulated three times, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, they said to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'May the Blessed One accept this alms-food from us, out of compassion!' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhūat - sādhu khalvidaṃ syādyadahaṃ hastābhyāṃ pratigṛhṇīyām / kasmin khalu pūrvakaistathāgataiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pratigṛhītam? pātreṇetyajñāsīt //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> thought: 'It would indeed be good if I were to receive [it] with [my] hands. But in what [vessel] was it received by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones?' He knew: 'In a bowl.' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgatasya bhojanakālasamaya iti viditvā tatkṣaṇameva catasṛbhyo digbhyaścatvāro mahārājā āgatya catvāri sauvarṇāni pātrāṇyādāya tathāgatasyopanāmayanti sma - pratigṛhṇātu bhagavannimāni sauvarṇāni(catvāri)pātrāṇyasmākamanukampāmupādāya / tāni na śramaṇapratirūpāṇi iti kṛtvā tathāgato na pratigṛhṇīte sma / evaṃ catvāri rūpyamayāni catvāri vaiḍūryamayāni sphaṭikamayāni musāragalvamayāni aśmagarbhamayāni / tataścatvāri sarvaratnamayāni pātrāṇi gṛhītvā tathāgatasyopanāmayanti sma / na śramaṇasya sārūpyāṇi iti kṛtvā tathāgato na pratigṛhṇīte sma //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, knowing that it was the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s mealtime, at that very moment the four Great Kings (<s>Mahārājas</s>) came from the four directions and, taking four golden bowls, offered them to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'May the Blessed One accept these four golden bowls from us, out of compassion!' Thinking 'They are not befitting a <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant),' the <s>Tathāgata</s> did not accept them. Likewise [he declined] four silver [bowls], four of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), of crystal, of coral, of agate. Then, taking four bowls made of all [kinds of] jewels, they offered them to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thinking 'They are not fitting for a <s>śramaṇa</s>,' the <s>Tathāgata</s> did not accept them. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasya punaretadabhūt - evaṃ katamadvidhaiḥ pātraiḥ pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pratigṛhītam? śailapātrairityajñāsīt / evaṃ ca cittamutpannaṃ tathāgatasya //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> again thought: 'What kind of bowls were accepted by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones?' He knew: 'Stone bowls!' And this thought arose in the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu vaiśravaṇo mahārājastadanyāstrīn mahārājānāmantrayate sma - imāni khalu punarmārṣāścatvāri śailapātrāṇi nīlakāyikairdavaputrairasmabhyaṃ dattāni - tatrāsmākametadabhūt - eṣu vayaṃ paribhokṣyāma iti / tato vairocano nāma nīlakāyiko devaputraḥ so 'smānevamāha -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King, addressed the other three Great Kings: 'These four stone bowls, venerable ones, were given to us by the <s>Nīlakāyika devaputras</s> — and we had thought: "We shall use these as vessels." Then a <s>Nīlakāyika devaputra</s> named <s>Vairocana</s> said to us:"

children.text: ma eṣu bhokṣyatha bhājaneṣu dhāretibhe cetiyasaṃmatīte /
children.translated_text: "Do not eat in these vessels! They are sanctified, revered as shrines!

children.text: bhavitā jinaḥ śākyamunīti nāmnā tasyeti pātrāṇyupanāmayethā // Lal_24.84 //
children.translated_text: There shall be a <s>Jina</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> — offer these bowls to him!" // Lal_24.84 //

body.text: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ samayaśca mārṣā upanāmituṃ śākyamunerhi bhājanā / saṃgītitūryasvaranāditena dāsyāma pātrāṇi vidhāya pūjām // Lal_24.85 //
body.translated_text: "This is the time and occasion, venerable ones, to offer vessels to <s>Śākyamuni</s>! With the sounds of song, music, and musical instruments, let us give the bowls, having arranged the worship!" // Lal_24.85 //

children.text: sa bhājanaṃ dharmamayaṃ hyabhedyaṃ ime ca śailāmaya bhedya bhājanā /
children.translated_text: "He is a vessel of <s>dharma</s>, indestructible; but these are stone vessels, breakable;

children.text: pratigrahītuṃ kṣamate na cānyaḥ pratigrahārthāya vrajāma hanta // Lal_24.86 //
children.translated_text: yet he is able to accept [them] — no other is [worthy]; let us go to [make] the offering!' // Lal_24.86 //

body.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājāḥ svasvajanapārṣadyāḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītisaṃprabhāṇitena svaiḥ svaiḥ pāṇibhistāni pātrāṇi parigṛhya yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramya tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kṛtvā tāni pātrāṇi divyakusumapratipūrṇāni tathāgatāyopanāmayanti sma //
body.translated_text: Then the four Great Kings, each with their own assemblies, with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, instrumental music, percussion, and ensemble singing, taking those bowls in their respective hands, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, having worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they offered those bowls, filled with divine flowers, to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - amī khalu punaścatvāro mahārājāḥ śraddhāḥ prasannāḥ mama catvāri śailapātrāṇyupanāmayanti / na ca me catvāri śailapātrāṇi kalpante / athaikasya pratigṛhīṣyāmi, trayāṇāṃ vaimanasyaṃ syāt / yannvahamimāni catvāri pātrāṇi pratigṛhyaikaṃ pātramadhitiṣṭheyam / atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ prasārya vaiśravaṇaṃ mahārājaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> thought: 'These four Great Kings, faithful and devoted, are offering me four stone bowls. But four stone bowls are not appropriate for me. If I accept one, the [other] three will be displeased. Let me accept these four bowls and then merge [them into] one bowl.' Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, extending his right hand, addressed <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King, in verse —

children.text: upanāmayasva sugatasya bhājanaṃ tvaṃ bheṣyase bhājanamagrayāne /
children.translated_text: 'Offer the vessel to the <s>Sugata</s>! You shall become a vessel for the supreme vehicle!

children.text: asmadvidhebhyo hi pradāya bhājanaṃ smṛtirmatiścaiva na jātu hīyate // Lal_24.87 //
children.translated_text: For those who give vessels to ones like me, their mindfulness and wisdom are never diminished!' // Lal_24.87 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato vaiśravaṇasya mahārājasyāntikāttatpātraṃ pratigṛhṇīte sma anukampāmupādāya / pratigṛhya ca dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahārājaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> accepted that bowl from <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King, out of compassion. Having accepted it, he addressed <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the Great King, in verse —

children.text: yo bhājanaṃ deti tathāgatasya na tasya jātu smṛti prajña hīyate /
children.translated_text: 'One who gives a vessel to the <s>Tathāgata</s> — his mindfulness and wisdom are never diminished!

children.text: atināmya kālaṃ ca sukhaṃsukhena yāvatpadaṃ budhyati śītibhāvam // Lal_24.88 //
children.translated_text: Passing through time in happiness and comfort, he eventually realizes the state of peace!' // Lal_24.88 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mahārājasyāntikāttatpātraṃ pratigṛhṇīte sma anukampāmupādāya / pratigṛhya ca virūḍhakaṃ mahārājaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> accepted that bowl from <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the Great King, out of compassion. Having accepted it, he addressed <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the Great King, in verse —

children.text: dadāsi yastvaṃ pariśuddhabhājanaṃ viśuddhacittāya tathāgatāya /
children.translated_text: 'You who give a perfectly pure vessel to the <s>Tathāgata</s> of purified mind —

children.text: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ laghu śuddhacittaḥ praśaṃsito devamanuṣyaloke // Lal_24.89 //
children.translated_text: you shall swiftly become pure-minded, praised in the world of gods and humans!' // Lal_24.89 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato virūḍhakasya mahārājasyāntikāttatpātraṃ pratigṛhṇīte sma anukampāmupādāya / pratigṛhya ca virūpākṣaṃ mahārājaṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> accepted that bowl from <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the Great King, out of compassion. Having accepted it, he addressed <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the Great King, in verse —

children.text: acchidraśīlasya tathāgatasya acchidravṛttasya acchidrabhājanam /
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Tathāgata</s> of flawless morality and flawless conduct, [you give] a flawless vessel!

children.text: acchidracittaḥ pradadāsi śraddhayā acchidra te bheṣyati puṇyadakṣiṇā // Lal_24.90 //
children.translated_text: You give with flawless mind and faith — your merit-offering shall be flawless!' // Lal_24.90 //

body.text: pratigṛhṇīte sma bhikṣavastathāgato virūpākṣasya mahārājasyāntikāttatpātraṃ anukampāmupādāya / pratigṛhya caikaṃ pātramadhitiṣṭhati sma adhimuktibalena / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmidamudānamudānayati sma -
body.translated_text: O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> accepted that bowl from <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the Great King, out of compassion. Having accepted it, he merged [them into] one bowl by the power of resolve. And at that moment he uttered this inspired utterance —

children.text: dattāni pātrāṇi pure bhave mayā phalapūritā premaṇiyā ca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: 'In former births I gave bowls filled with fruit, made with love;

children.text: tenemi pātrāścaturaḥ susaṃsthitā dadanti devāścaturo maharddhikāḥ // Lal_24.91 //
children.translated_text: by that [merit], these four well-fashioned bowls are given [to me] by the four gods of great supernatural power!' // Lal_24.91 //

body.text: tatredamucyate /
body.translated_text: Concerning this, it was said —

children.text: sa saptarātraṃ varabodhivṛkṣaṃ saṃprekṣya dhīraḥ paramārthadarśī /
children.translated_text: For seven nights, the steadfast one, the seer of ultimate truth, gazed upon the excellent <s>Bodhi</s>-tree —

children.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ prakāraiḥ pravikampya corvī abhutthitaḥ siṃhagatirnṛsiṃhaḥ // Lal_24.92 //
children.translated_text: Having caused the earth to tremble in six ways, that lion among men, of lion-gait, arose. // Lal_24.92 //

body.text: samanta nāgendravilambagāmī krameṇa tārāyaṇamūlametya /
body.translated_text: Walking everywhere with the slow gait of the lord of elephants, he approached step by step the foot of the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> tree,

body.text: upāviśanmeruvadaprakampyo dhyānaṃ samādhiṃ ca muniḥ pradadhyau // Lal_24.93 //
body.translated_text: and sat down, unshakeable like <s>Meru</s> — the sage meditated in <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>. // Lal_24.93 //

children.text: tasmiṃśca kāle trapuṣaśca bhalliko bhrātṛdvayaṃ vaṇijagaṇena sārdham /
children.translated_text: At that time, <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>, two brothers, together with a caravan of merchants,

children.text: śakaṭāni te pañca dhanena pūrṇā saṃpuṣpite sālavane praviṣṭāḥ // Lal_24.94 //
children.translated_text: with five hundred carts full of goods, entered the flowering <s>Śāla</s> grove. // Lal_24.94 //

children.text: maharṣitejena ca akṣamātraṃ cakrāṇi bhūmau viviśuḥ kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: By the power of the great sage, the wheels sank into the earth axle-deep in an instant;

children.text: tāṃ tādṛśīṃ prekṣya ca te avasthāṃ mahadbhayaṃ vaṇijagaṇasya jātam // Lal_24.95 //
children.translated_text: seeing such a condition, great fear arose in the merchant caravan. // Lal_24.95 //

children.text: te khaḍgahastāḥ śaraśaktipāṇayo vane mṛgaṃ vā mṛgayan ka eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sword in hand, with arrows and spears at the ready, searching as if for a deer in the forest — 'Who is this?'

children.text: vīkṣanta te śāradacandravaktraṃ jinaṃ sahasrāṃśumivābhramuktam // Lal_24.96 //
children.translated_text: They beheld the <s>Jina</s>, whose face was like the autumn moon, like the thousand-rayed [sun] released from clouds. // Lal_24.96 //

children.text: prahīnakopā apanītadarpāḥ praṇamya mūrdhnā vimṛṣuḥ ka eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their anger abandoned, their pride removed, bowing with their heads, they wondered: 'Who is this?'

children.text: nabhastalāddevata vāca bhāṣate buddho hyayaṃ lokahitārthakārī // Lal_24.97 //
children.translated_text: From the sky a deity spoke these words: 'This is a <s>Buddha</s>, one who acts for the welfare of the world!' // Lal_24.97 //

children.text: rātriṃdivā sapta na cānnapānaṃ anena bhuktaṃ karuṇātmakena /
children.translated_text: 'For seven days and nights, this compassionate one has not eaten food or drink;

children.text: yadicchathā ātmana kleśaśāntiṃ bhojethimaṃ bhāvitakāyacittam // Lal_24.98 //
children.translated_text: if you desire the pacification of your own afflictions, feed this one whose body and mind are cultivated!' // Lal_24.98 //

children.text: śabdaṃ ca te taṃ madhuraṃ niśāmya vanditva kṛtvā ca jinaṃ pradakṣiṇam /
children.translated_text: Hearing that sweet sound, having paid homage and circumambulated the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: prītāstataste sahitaiḥ sahāyaiḥ jinasya piṇḍāya matiṃ pracakruḥ // Lal_24.99 //
children.translated_text: those delighted ones, together with their companions, resolved to offer alms-food to the <s>Jina</s>. // Lal_24.99 //

body.text: tena khalu bhikṣavaḥ samayena trapuṣabhallikānāṃ vaṇijāṃ pratyantakarvaṭe goyūthaṃ prativasati sma / atha tā gāvastasmin kāle tasmin samaye sarpimaṇḍaṃ pradugdhā abhūvan / atha gopālāstatsarpimaṇḍamādāya yena trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijau tenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramyemāṃ prakṛtimārocayanti sma - yatkhalu yūyaṃ bhaṭṭā jānīyāta - sarvāstā gāvaḥ sarpimaṇḍaṃ pradugdhāḥ / tatkimetatpraśastamāhosvinneti?
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> had a herd of cows dwelling in a border village. Then those cows at that time, at that moment, yielded cream. Then the cowherds, taking that cream, approached the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>. Having approached, they reported this matter: 'May the masters know — all those cows have yielded cream. Is this auspicious or not?'

body.text: tatra lolupajātyā brāhmaṇā evamāhuḥ - amaṅgalyametadbāhmaṇānām / mahāyajño yaṣṭavya iti //
body.translated_text: There, greedy <s>brāhmaṇas</s> said thus: 'This is inauspicious for <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. A great sacrifice must be performed.'
