body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena trapuṣabhallikānāṃ vaṇijāṃ śikhaṇḍī nāma brāhmaṇaḥ pūrvajātisālohito brahmaloke pratyājāto 'bhūt / sa brāhmaṇarūpamabhinirmāya tān vaṇijo gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> had a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, a blood-relative from a former life who had been reborn in the <s>Brahma</s>-world. He, having created a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-form, addressed those merchants with verses:

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ praṇidhiḥ pūrve bodhiprāptastathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your former aspiration [is fulfilled] — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has attained awakening!

children.text: asmākaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuktvā dharmacakraṃ pravartayet // Lal_24.100 //
children.translated_text: Having eaten our food, he shall turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma)!' // Lal_24.100 //

children.text: sa caiṣa praṇidhiḥ pūrṇo bodhiprāptastathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That aspiration is fulfilled — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has attained awakening;

children.text: āhāramupanāmyeta bhuktvā cakraṃ pravartayet // Lal_24.101 //
children.translated_text: offer food [to him] — having eaten, he shall turn the Wheel!' // Lal_24.101 //

children.text: sumaṅgalaṃ sunakṣatraṃ gavāṃ vaḥ sarpidohanam /
children.translated_text: 'Most auspicious, under a good constellation, is the cream-yielding of your cows;

children.text: puṇyakarmaṇastasyaiṣa anubhāvo maharṣiṇaḥ // Lal_24.102 //
children.translated_text: this is the effect of meritorious deeds, the power of that great sage!' // Lal_24.102 //

children.text: evaṃ saṃcodya vaṇijaḥ śikhaṇḍī bhavanaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having thus urged the merchants, <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> went to his abode;

children.text: udagramanasaḥ sarve babhuvustrapuṣāhvayāḥ // Lal_24.103 //
children.translated_text: all those called <s>Trapuṣa</s> became elevated in mind.' // Lal_24.103 //

children.text: kṣīraṃ yadāsīcca hi gosahasrā aśeṣatastaṃ samudānayitvā /
children.translated_text: The milk that was from a thousand cows — gathering all of it completely,

children.text: agraṃ ca tasmātparigṛhya ojaḥ sādheṃsu te bhojana gauraveṇa // Lal_24.104 //
children.translated_text: and extracting from it the foremost essence, they prepared [it] with great reverence as food. // Lal_24.104 //

children.text: śataṃ sahasraikapalasya mūlyaṃ yā ratnapātrī abhu candranāmikā /
children.translated_text: A jeweled bowl named <s>Candra</s> (Moon), worth a hundred thousand [coins] for a single <s>pala</s> [weight],

children.text: caukṣāṃ sudhautāṃ vimalāṃ ca kṛtvā samatīrthikāṃ pūriṣu bhojanena // Lal_24.105 //
children.translated_text: having made it clean, well-washed, and spotless, they filled it level to the brim with food. // Lal_24.105 //

children.text: madhuṃ gṛhītvā tatha ratnapātrīṃ tārāyaṇīmūlamupetya śāstuḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking honey and that jeweled bowl, they approached the foot of the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> tree where the Teacher [sat]:

children.text: pratigṛhṇa bhakte anugṛhṇa cāsmān idaṃ praṇītaṃ paribhuṅkṣva bhojyam // Lal_24.106 //
children.translated_text: 'Accept this food and favor us! Partake of this excellent meal!' // Lal_24.106 //

children.text: anukampanārthāya ubhau ca bhrātṛṇāṃ pūrvāśayaṃ jñātva ca bodhiprasthitau /
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for both brothers, knowing their former disposition and that they had set out toward awakening,

children.text: pratigṛhītvā paribhuñji śāstā bhuktvā kṣipī pātri nabhastalesmiṃ // Lal_24.107 //
children.translated_text: the Teacher accepted and ate; having eaten, he threw the bowl into the sky. // Lal_24.107 //

children.text: subrahmanāmā ca hi devarājo jagrāha yastāṃ vararatnapātrīm /
children.translated_text: The divine king named <s>Subrahma</s> caught that excellent jeweled bowl;

children.text: adhunāpyasau tāṃ khalu brahmaloke saṃpūjayatyanyasuraiḥ sahāyaḥ // Lal_24.108 //
children.translated_text: even now he worships it in the <s>Brahma</s>-world together with other gods. // Lal_24.108 //

body.text: atha khalu tathāgatastasyāṃ velāyāṃ teṣāṃ trapuṣabhallikānāṃ vaṇijānāmimāṃ saṃharṣaṇāmakārṣīt -
body.translated_text: Then indeed, at that time, the <s>Tathāgata</s> gave this benediction to the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>:

children.text: diśāṃ svastikaraṃ divyaṃ maṅgalyaṃ cārthasādhakam /
children.translated_text: 'May there be divine well-being for the directions, auspiciousness and the accomplishment of goals;

children.text: arthā vaḥ śāsatāṃ sarve bhavatvāśu pradakṣiṇā // Lal_24.109 //
children.translated_text: may all your aims succeed — may there be prosperity for you swiftly!' // Lal_24.109 //

children.text: śrīrvo 'stu dakṣiṇe haste śrīrvo vāme pratiṣṭhitā /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) be in your right hand, may <s>Śrī</s> be established in your left;

children.text: śrīrvo 'stu sarvasāṅgeṣu māleva śirasi sthitā // Lal_24.110 //
children.translated_text: may <s>Śrī</s> be in all your limbs, resting on your head like a garland!' // Lal_24.110 //

children.text: dhanaiṣiṇāṃ prayātānāṃ vaṇijāṃ vai diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: 'For merchants seeking wealth, who have set forth to the ten directions,

children.text: utpadyantāṃ mahālābhāste ca santu sukhodayāḥ // Lal_24.111 //
children.translated_text: may great profits arise, and may they bring happiness!' // Lal_24.111 //

children.text: kāryeṇa kenacidyena gacchathā pūrvikāṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever purpose you go toward the eastern direction,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi vaḥ pālentu ye tasyāṃ diśi saṃsthitā // Lal_24.112 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) that are established in that direction protect you!' // Lal_24.112 //

children.text: kṛttikā rohiṇī caiva mṛgaśirārdrā punarvasuḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśirā</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>,

children.text: puṣyaścaiva tathāśleṣā ityeṣāṃ pūrvikādiśām // Lal_24.113 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Āśleṣā</s> — these are of the eastern direction.' // Lal_24.113 //

children.text: ityete sapta nakṣatrā lokapālā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These seven <s>nakṣatras</s>, world-protectors, glorious,

children.text: adhiṣṭhitā pūrvabhāge devā rakṣantu sarvataḥ // Lal_24.114 //
children.translated_text: appointed in the eastern quarter — may the gods protect you from all sides!' // Lal_24.114 //

children.text: teṣāṃ cādhipatī rājā dhṛtarāṣṭreti viśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their overlord king is known as <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>;

children.text: sa sarvagandharvapatiḥ sūryeṇa saha rakṣatu // Lal_24.115 //
children.translated_text: he, lord of all <s>Gandharvas</s>, together with <s>Sūrya</s>, may he protect [you]!' // Lal_24.115 //

children.text: putrā pi tasya bahava ekanāmā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His sons are many, of one name, wise —

children.text: aśītirdaśa caikaśca indranāmā mahābalā /
children.translated_text: ninety-one, named <s>Indra</s>, of great power;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.116 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.116 //

children.text: pūrvasmin vai diśo bhāge aṣṭau devakumārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the eastern quarter there are eight divine maidens:

children.text: jayantī vijayantī ca siddhārthā aparājitā // Lal_24.117 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Vijayantī</s>, <s>Siddhārthā</s>, <s>Aparājitā</s>,' // Lal_24.117 //

children.text: nandottarā nandisenā nandinī nandavardhanī /
children.translated_text: '<s>Nandottarā</s>, <s>Nandisenā</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Nandavardhanī</s> —

children.text: tā pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.118 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.118 //

children.text: pūrvasmin vai diśo bhāge cāpālaṃ nāma cetiyam /
children.translated_text: 'In the eastern quarter there is a shrine named <s>Cāpāla</s>,

children.text: avustaṃ jinebhi jñātamarhantebhi ca tāyibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: inhabited by <s>Jinas</s> and known by <s>Arhats</s> and protectors;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.119 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.119 //

children.text: kṣemāśca vo diśaḥ santu mā ca vaḥ pāpamāgamat /
children.translated_text: 'May the directions be safe for you, and may no evil come upon you;

children.text: labdhārthāśca nivartadhvaṃ sarvadevebhi rakṣitāḥ // Lal_24.120 //
children.translated_text: having obtained your goals, may you return, protected by all the gods!' // Lal_24.120 //

children.text: yena kenacitkṛtyena gacchethā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever purpose you go toward the southern direction,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi vaḥ pālentu ye tāṃ diśamadhiṣṭhitā // Lal_24.121 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>nakṣatras</s> that are established in that direction protect you!' // Lal_24.121 //

children.text: maghā ca dvau ca phālgunyau hastā citrā ca pañcamī /
children.translated_text: '<s>Maghā</s>, the two <s>Phālgunīs</s>, <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Citrā</s> as the fifth,

children.text: svātiścaiva viśākhā ca eteṣāṃ dakṣiṇā diśā // Lal_24.122 //
children.translated_text: <s>Svāti</s>, and <s>Viśākhā</s> — these are of the southern direction.' // Lal_24.122 //

children.text: ityete sapta nakṣatrā lokapālā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These seven <s>nakṣatras</s>, world-protectors, glorious,

children.text: ādiṣṭā dakṣiṇe bhāge te vo rakṣantu sarvataḥ // Lal_24.123 //
children.translated_text: appointed in the southern quarter — may they protect you from all sides!' // Lal_24.123 //

children.text: teṣāṃ cādhipatī rājā virūḍhaka iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their overlord king is known as <s>Virūḍhaka</s>;

children.text: sarvakumbhāṇḍādhipatiryamena saha rakṣatu // Lal_24.124 //
children.translated_text: lord of all <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, together with <s>Yama</s>, may he protect [you]!' // Lal_24.124 //

children.text: putrā pi tasya bahava ekanāmā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His sons are many, of one name, wise —

children.text: aśītirdaśa caikaśca indranāmā mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: ninety-one, named <s>Indra</s>, of great power;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.125 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.125 //

children.text: dakṣiṇe 'smin diśo bhāge aṣṭau devakumārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the southern quarter there are eight divine maidens:

children.text: śriyāmatī yaśamatī yaśaprāptā yaśodharā // Lal_24.126 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śriyāmatī</s>, <s>Yaśamatī</s>, <s>Yaśaprāptā</s>, <s>Yaśodharā</s>,' // Lal_24.126 //

children.text: suutthitā suprathamā suprabuddhā sukhāvahā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Suutthitā</s>, <s>Suprathamā</s>, <s>Suprabuddhā</s>, <s>Sukhāvahā</s> —

children.text: tā pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.127 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.127 //

children.text: dakṣiṇe 'smin diśo bhāge padmanāmena cetikam /
children.translated_text: 'In the southern quarter there is a shrine named <s>Padma</s> (Lotus),

children.text: nityaṃ jvalitatejena divyaṃ sarvaprakāśitam /
children.translated_text: eternally blazing with splendor, divine, illuminating all;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.128 //
children.translated_text: may it also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.128 //

children.text: kṣemāśca vo diśaḥ santu mā ca vaḥ pāpamāgamat /
children.translated_text: 'May the directions be safe for you, and may no evil come upon you;

children.text: labdhārthāśca nivartadhvaṃ sarvadevebhi rakṣitāḥ // Lal_24.129 //
children.translated_text: having obtained your goals, may you return, protected by all the gods!' // Lal_24.129 //

children.text: yena kenacitkṛtyena gacchethā paścimāṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever purpose you go toward the western direction,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi vaḥ pālentu ye tāṃ diśamadhiṣṭhitā // Lal_24.130 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>nakṣatras</s> that are established in that direction protect you!' // Lal_24.130 //

children.text: anurādhā ca jeṣṭhā ca mūlā ca dṛḍhavīryatā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūlā</s>, of firm vigor,

children.text: dvāvāṣāḍhe abhijicca śravaṇo bhavati saptamaḥ // Lal_24.131 //
children.translated_text: the two <s>Āṣāḍhās</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s> as the seventh.' // Lal_24.131 //

children.text: ityete sapta nakṣatrā lokapālā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These seven <s>nakṣatras</s>, world-protectors, glorious,

children.text: ādiṣṭā paścime bhāge te vo rakṣantu sarvadā // Lal_24.132 //
children.translated_text: appointed in the western quarter — may they protect you always!' // Lal_24.132 //

children.text: teṣāṃ cādhipatī rājā virūpākṣeti taṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their overlord king is known as <s>Virūpākṣa</s>;

children.text: sa sarvanāgādhipatirvarūṇena saha rakṣatu // Lal_24.133 //
children.translated_text: he, lord of all <s>Nāgas</s>, together with <s>Varuṇa</s>, may he protect [you]!' // Lal_24.133 //

children.text: putrā pi tasya bahavaḥ ekanāmā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His sons are many, of one name, wise —

children.text: aśītirdaśa caikaśca indranāmā mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: ninety-one, named <s>Indra</s>, of great power;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.134 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.134 //

body.text: paścime 'smin diśo bhāge aṣṭau devakumārikāḥ

children.text: alambuśā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkā tathāruṇā // Lal_24.135 //
children.translated_text: <s>Alambuśā</s>, <s>Miśrakeśī</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>, and <s>Aruṇā</s>,' // Lal_24.135 //

body.translated_text: 'In the western quarter there are eight divine maidens:

children.text: ekādaśā navamikā śītā kṛṣṇā ca draupadī /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ekādaśā</s>, <s>Navamikā</s>, <s>Śītā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>Draupadī</s> —

children.text: tā pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.136 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.136 //

children.text: paścime 'smin diśo bhāge aṣṭaṅgo nāma parvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the western quarter there is a mountain named <s>Aṣṭāṅga</s>,

children.text: pratiṣṭhā candrasūryāṇāṃ aṣṭamarthaṃ dadātu vaḥ /
children.translated_text: the support of the moon and sun — may it grant you the eightfold aim;

children.text: so 'pi va adhipāletu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.137 //
children.translated_text: may it also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.137 //

children.text: kṣemāśca vo diśaḥ santu mā ca vaḥ pāpamāgamat /
children.translated_text: 'May the directions be safe for you, and may no evil come upon you;

children.text: labdhārthāśca nivartadhvaṃ sarvadevebhi rakṣitāḥ // Lal_24.138 //
children.translated_text: having obtained your goals, may you return, protected by all the gods!' // Lal_24.138 //

children.text: yena kenacitkṛtyena gacchethā uttarāṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever purpose you go toward the northern direction,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi vaḥ pālentu ye tāṃ diśamadhiṣṭhitā // Lal_24.139 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>nakṣatras</s> that are established in that direction protect you!' // Lal_24.139 //

children.text: dhaniṣṭhā śatabhiṣā caiva dve ca purvottarāpare /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, the two — <s>Pūrvottarā</s> and <s>Aparā</s>,

children.text: ravatī aśvinī caiva bharaṇī bhavatī saptamī // Lal_24.140 //
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s> as the seventh.' // Lal_24.140 //

children.text: ityete sapta nakṣatrā lokapālā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These seven <s>nakṣatras</s>, world-protectors, glorious,

children.text: ādiṣṭā uttare bhāge te vo rakṣantu sarvadā // Lal_24.141 //
children.translated_text: appointed in the northern quarter — may they protect you always!' // Lal_24.141 //

children.text: teṣāṃ cādhipatī rājā kubero naravāhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Their overlord king is <s>Kubera</s>, borne by men (<s>Naravāhana</s>);

children.text: sarvayakṣāṇāmadhipatirmāṇibhadreṇa saha rakṣatu // Lal_24.142 //
children.translated_text: lord of all <s>Yakṣas</s>, together with <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, may he protect [you]!' // Lal_24.142 //

children.text: putrā pi tasya bahava ekanāmā vicakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'His sons are many, of one name, wise —

children.text: aśītirdaśa caikaśca indranāmā mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: ninety-one, named <s>Indra</s>, of great power;

children.text: te pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.143 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.143 //

children.text: uttare 'smin diśo bhāge aṣṭau devakumārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the northern quarter there are eight divine maidens:

children.text: ilādevī surādevī pṛthvī padmāvatī tathā // Lal_24.144 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ilādevī</s>, <s>Surādevī</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, and <s>Padmāvatī</s>,' // Lal_24.144 //

children.text: upasthitā mahārājā āśā śraddhā hirī śirī /
children.translated_text: 'Attendant great queens — <s>Āśā</s>, <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Hirī</s>, <s>Śirī</s> —

children.text: tā pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.145 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.145 //

children.text: uttare 'smin diśo bhāge parvato gandhamādanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the northern quarter there is the mountain <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: āvāso yakṣabhūtānāṃ citrakūṭaḥ sudarśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: the abode of <s>Yakṣas</s> and spirits — <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>;

children.text: te 'pi va adhipālentu ārogyena śivena ca // Lal_24.146 //
children.translated_text: may they also guard you with health and well-being!' // Lal_24.146 //

children.text: kṣemāśca vo diśaḥ santu mā ca vaḥ pāpamāgamat /
children.translated_text: 'May the directions be safe for you, and may no evil come upon you;

children.text: labdhārthāśca nivartadhvaṃ sarvadevebhi rakṣitāḥ // Lal_24.147 //
children.translated_text: having obtained your goals, may you return, protected by all the gods!' // Lal_24.147 //

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśati nakṣatrā sapta sapta caturdiśam /
children.translated_text: 'Twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, seven for each of the four directions;

children.text: dvātriṃśaddevakanyāśca aṣṭāvaṣṭau caturdiśam // Lal_24.148 //
children.translated_text: thirty-two divine maidens, eight for each of the four directions;' // Lal_24.148 //

children.text: aṣṭau śramaṇā (cāṣṭau) brāhmaṇā(aṣṭau) janapadeṣu naigamāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Eight <s>śramaṇas</s>, eight <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, [eight] townspeople in the provinces;

children.text: aṣṭau devāḥ saindrakāste vo rakṣantu sarvataḥ // Lal_24.149 //
children.translated_text: eight gods with <s>Indra</s> — may they protect you from all sides!' // Lal_24.149 //

children.text: svasti vo gacchatāṃ bhotu svasti bhotu nivartatām /
children.translated_text: 'May there be well-being for those who go, may there be well-being for those who return;

children.text: svasti paśyata vai jñātiṃ svasti paśyantu jñātayaḥ // Lal_24.150 //
children.translated_text: may there be well-being in seeing kinsmen, and may kinsmen see [you] in well-being!' // Lal_24.150 //

children.text: sendrā yakṣā mahārājā arhantamanukampitāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Yakṣas</s> with <s>Indra</s>, the great kings, favored by the <s>Arhat</s> —

children.text: sarvatra svasti gacchadhvaṃ prāpsyadhvamamṛtaṃ śivam // Lal_24.151 //
children.translated_text: may you go everywhere in well-being, and may you attain the deathless, auspicious [state]!' // Lal_24.151 //

children.text: saṃrakṣitā brāhmaṇa vāsavena vimukticittaiśca anāśravaiśca /
children.translated_text: 'Protected by <s>Vāsava</s>, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, and by those of liberated minds, free from outflows —

children.text: nāgaiśca yakṣaiśca sadānukampitāḥ pāletha āyuḥ śaradāṃ śataṃ samam // Lal_24.152 //
children.translated_text: and always protected by <s>Nāgas</s> and <s>Yakṣas</s>, may you guard your lives for a full hundred autumns!" // Lal_24.152 //

children.text: pradakṣiṇāṃ dakṣiṇalokanāthaḥ teṣāṃ diśaiṣa 'pratimo vināyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The Lord of the World, the incomparable Guide, bestows upon them the gift of circumambulation;

children.text: anena yūyaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā madhusaṃbhavā nāma jinā bhaviṣyatha // Lal_24.153 //
children.translated_text: by this meritorious deed, you shall become <s>Jinas</s> named <s>Madhusaṃbhava</s> (Born of Honey)!" // Lal_24.153 //

children.text: prathamādidaṃ lokavināyakasya asaṅgato vyākaraṇaṃ jinasya /
children.translated_text: "This is the first prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of the Guide of the World, of the unattached <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: paścādanantā bahubodhisattvā ye vyākṛtā bodhayi no vivartyāḥ // Lal_24.154 //
children.translated_text: afterward, innumerable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were predicted for awakening — they are irreversible!" // Lal_24.154 //

children.text: śrutvā imaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ jinasya udagracittā paramāya prītyā /
children.translated_text: "Having heard this prediction of the <s>Jina</s>, elated in mind with supreme joy,

children.text: tau bhrātarau sārdhaṃ sahāyakaistaiḥ buddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ śaraṇa prapannāḥ // Lal_24.155 //
children.translated_text: those two brothers together with their companions took refuge in the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>." // Lal_24.155 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare trapuṣabhallikaparivarto nāma caturviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter of the noble <s>Lalitavistara</s>, named the <s>Trapuṣa-Bhallika</s> Chapter. //

body.text: START Parivarta 25
body.translated_text: START Chapter 25

body.text: adhyeṣaṇāparivartaḥ pañcaviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The twenty-fifth chapter: the Chapter on the Entreaty (<s>Adhyeṣaṇā</s>).

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgatasya tārāyaṇamūle viharataḥ prathamābhisaṃbuddhasyaikasya rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasya lokānuvartanāṃ pratyetadabhavat - gambhīro batāyaṃ mayā dharmo 'dhigato 'bhisaṃbuddhaḥ śāntaḥ praśānta upaśāntaḥ praṇīto durdṛśo duranubodho 'tarko 'vitarkāvacaraḥ / alamāryaḥ paṇḍitavijñavedanīyo yaduta sarvopadhiniḥsargo 'vedito 'niveditaḥ sarvaveditanirodhaḥ paramārtho 'nālayaḥ / śītībhāvo 'nādāno 'nupādāno 'vijñapto 'vijñāpanīyo 'saṃskṛtaḥ ṣaḍviṣayasamatikrāntaḥ / akalpo 'vikalpo 'nabhilāpyaḥ / aruto 'ghoṣo 'nudāhāraḥ / anidarśano 'pratighaḥ sarvālambanasamatikāntaḥ śamathadharmopacchedaḥ / śūnyatānupalambhaḥ / tṛṣṇākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam / ahaṃ cedimaṃ parebhyo dharmaṃ deśayeyam, te cennājānīyuḥ, sa me syātklamatho mithyāvyāyāmo 'kṣaṇadharmadeśanatā ca / yannvahamalpotsukastūṣṇībhāvena vihareyam / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> dwelt at the root of the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> tree, having just attained supreme awakening, alone, in solitude, in meditative seclusion, this thought arose in him regarding the ways of the world: "Profound indeed is this <s>Dharma</s> that has been realized and fully awakened by me — peaceful, utterly peaceful, tranquil, sublime, hard to see, hard to comprehend, beyond reasoning, beyond the sphere of discursive thought. It is to be known only by the noble and the learned wise — namely, the relinquishment of all substrates, the unperceived and unperceivable, the cessation of all perception, the ultimate reality, non-attachment. It is cooling, non-grasping, non-clinging, non-cognizable, not to be communicated, unconditioned, transcending the six sense-objects. It is without conceptualization, without discrimination, inexpressible. It is without sound, without utterance, without declaration. It is without indication, without obstruction, transcending all objects of support, cutting off the dharmas of tranquility. It is emptiness and non-apprehension; the extinction of craving, dispassion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. If I were to teach this <s>Dharma</s> to others and they would not understand it, that would be weariness and fruitless effort for me, and an untimely teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Let me rather dwell with little concern, in silence." And at that moment he spoke this verse —

children.text: gambhīra śānto virajaḥ prabhāsvaraḥ prāpto mi dharmo hyamṛto 'saṃskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Profound, peaceful, stainless, radiant — I have attained the <s>Dharma</s>, deathless and unconditioned;

children.text: deśeya cāhaṃ na parasya jāne yannūna tūṣṇī pavane vaseyam // Lal_25.1 //
children.translated_text: were I to teach it, none other would understand — let me rather dwell in silence in the forest!" // Lal_25.1 //

children.text: apagatagirivākpatho hyalipto yatha gaganaṃ tathā svabhāvadharmam /
children.translated_text: "Gone beyond the path of speech, like a mountain, unattached — like space, such is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: cittamana vicāravipramuktaṃ paramasuāścariyaṃ paro vijāne // Lal_25.2 //
children.translated_text: the mind freed from thought and investigation — how could another comprehend this supremely wondrous [truth]?" // Lal_25.2 //

children.text: na ca punarayu śakya akṣarebhiḥ praviśatu anarthayogavipraveśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And moreover, this cannot be entered through syllables — [for one who] enters into the engagement with the meaningless;

children.text: purimajinakṛtādhikārasattvāḥ te imu śruṇitva hi dharmu śraddadhanti // Lal_25.3 //
children.translated_text: but beings in whom the roots of merit were cultivated under former <s>Jinas</s> — they, hearing this <s>Dharma</s>, will have faith!" // Lal_25.3 //

children.text: na ca punariha kaścidasti dharmaḥ so pi na vidyate yasya nāstibhāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And moreover, there is no <s>dharma</s> here whatsoever — even that does not exist, for whom there is no existence;

children.text: hetukriyaparaṃparā ya jāne tasya na bhotiha astināstibhāvāḥ // Lal_25.4 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the chain of causal activity — for him there is neither existence nor non-existence here!" // Lal_25.4 //

children.text: kalpaśatasahasra aprameyā ahu caritaḥ purime jinasakāśe /
children.translated_text: "For immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> I practiced in the presence of former <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: na ca maya pratilabdha eṣa kṣāntī yatra na ātma na sattva naiva jīvaḥ // Lal_25.5 //
children.translated_text: and I did not obtain this patient acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) — wherein there is no self, no being, and no soul!" // Lal_25.5 //

children.text: yada maya pratilabdha eṣa kṣāntī mriyati na ceha na kaści jāyate vā /
children.translated_text: "When I obtained this patient acceptance — [the understanding that] none dies here and none is born,

children.text: prakṛti imi nirātma sarvadharmāḥ tada māṃ vyākari buddha dīpanāmā // Lal_25.6 //
children.translated_text: that all <s>dharmas</s> are by nature selfless — then the <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> (Lamp-Bearer) predicted me!" // Lal_25.6 //

children.text: karuṇa mama ananta sarvaloke paratu na cārthanatāmahaṃ pratīkṣe /
children.translated_text: "My compassion is boundless toward all the world; yet I do not await entreaty from others;

children.text: yada puna janatā prasanna brahme tena adhīṣṭu pravartayiṣya cakram // Lal_25.7 //
children.translated_text: but when the people are ready, O <s>Brahmā</s>, then, being resolved, I shall turn the wheel!" // Lal_25.7 //

children.text: eva ca ayu dharma grāhyu me syāt saci mama brahma krame nipatya yācet /
children.translated_text: "And this <s>Dharma</s> should indeed be grasped by me — if <s>Brahmā</s> comes and, bowing in proper fashion, entreats me:

children.text: pravadahi virajā praṇītu dharmaṃ santi vijānaka sattva svākarāśca // Lal_25.8 //
children.translated_text: "Proclaim the stainless, sublime <s>Dharma</s> — there are beings of good disposition who can understand!"" // Lal_25.8 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgatastasmin samaye ūrṇākośātprabhāmutsṛjati sma yayā prabhayā trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturmahatā suvarṇavarṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, at that time the <s>Tathāgata</s> released a radiance from his <s>ūrṇā</s>-tuft, by which radiance the great trichiliocosm became suffused with a great golden-colored light. //

body.text: atha khalu daśatrisāhasramahāsāhasrādhipatiḥ śikhī mahābrahmā buddhānubhāvenaiva tathāgatasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāsīt - alpotsukatāyai bhagavataścittamabhinataṃ na dharmadeśanāyāmiti / tasyaitadabhavat - yannvahamupasaṃkramya tathāgatamadhyeṣyeyaṃ dharmacakrapravartanatāyai //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of ten trichiliocosms, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power itself, knew with his mind the thought and deliberation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s mind: "The Blessed One's mind is inclined toward little concern, not toward teaching the <s>Dharma</s>." This thought arose in him: "Let me approach and entreat the <s>Tathāgata</s> to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>!" //

body.text: atha khalu śikhī mahābrahmā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tadanyān brahmakāyikān devaputrānāmantrayate sma - naśyati batāyaṃ mārṣā loko vinaśyati, yatra hi nāma tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyālpotsukatāyai cittamabhināmayati na dharmadeśanāyām / yannu vayamupasaṃkramya tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamadhyeṣyemahi dharmacakrapravartanāya //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, at that moment addressed the other <s>Brahmakāyika</s> god-sons: "Alas, sirs, this world is perishing, it is being destroyed, inasmuch as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, inclines his mind toward little concern and not toward teaching the <s>Dharma</s>! Let us approach and entreat the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>!" //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śikhī mahābrahmā aṣṭaṣaṣṭyā brāhmaṇaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya prāñjalistathāgatametadavocat naśyati batāyaṃ bhagavan lokaḥ, praṇaśyati batāyaṃ bhagavan lokaḥ, yatra hi nāma tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyālpotsukatāyai cittamabhināmayati na dharmadeśanāyām / tatsādhu deśayatu
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, surrounded and attended by six hundred and eighty thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet and, with palms joined, said to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: "Alas, Blessed One, this world is perishing! Alas, Blessed One, this world is being destroyed! For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, inclines his mind toward little concern and not toward teaching the <s>Dharma</s>! May the Blessed One

body.text: bhagavān dharmam, deśayatu sugato dharmam / santi sattvāḥ svākārāḥ suvijñāpakāḥ śaktā bhavyāḥ pratibalāḥ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājñātum / tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: please teach the <s>Dharma</s>! May the <s>Sugata</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>! There are beings of good disposition, easy to instruct, capable, worthy, and able to comprehend the meaning of the Blessed One's words!" And at that moment he spoke this verse —

children.text: samudāniya jñānamahāgramaṇḍalaṃ visṛjya raśmīn daśadikṣu caiva /
children.translated_text: "Having gathered the great orb of knowledge and emitting rays in the ten directions,

children.text: tadañja jñānāṃśu nṛpadmabodhakā upekṣakastiṣṭhasi vādibhāskaraḥ // Lal_25.9 //
children.translated_text: those rays of knowledge that awaken the lotus of men — you stand in equanimity, O sun among speakers! // Lal_25.9 //

children.text: nimantrayitvāryadhanena sattvāṃ āśvāsayitvā bahuprāṇakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having invited beings with the noble treasure, having consoled many <s>koṭis</s> of living beings,

children.text: na yuktametattava lokabandho yaṃ tūṣṇibhāvena upekṣase jagat // Lal_25.10 //
children.translated_text: it is not fitting for you, O friend of the world, to regard the world with silence! // Lal_25.10 //

children.text: parāhanasvottamadharmadundubhiṃ saddharmaśaṅkhaṃ ca prapūrayāśu /
children.translated_text: "Beat the supreme drum of <s>Dharma</s>! Quickly fill the conch of the true <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: ucchrepayasva mahadharmayūpaṃ prajvālayasva mahadharmadīpam // Lal_25.11 //
children.translated_text: Raise the great pillar of <s>Dharma</s>! Light the great lamp of <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_25.11 //

children.text: pravarṣa vai dharmajalaṃ pradhānaṃ pratārayemāṃ bhavasāgarasthāṃ /
children.translated_text: "Rain down the supreme water of <s>Dharma</s>! Ferry across those standing in the ocean of existence!

children.text: pramocayemāṃ mahavyādhikliṣṭāṃ kleśāgnitapte praśamaṃ kuruṣva // Lal_25.12 //
children.translated_text: Liberate those afflicted by the great disease! Bring peace to those burned by the fire of <s>kleśas</s>! // Lal_25.12 //

children.text: nidarśaya tvaṃ khalu śāntimārgaṃ kṣemaṃ śivaṃ nirjaratāmaśokam /
children.translated_text: "Show the path of peace — secure, auspicious, free from old age, free from sorrow!

children.text: nirvāṇamārgāgamanādanāthe vipathasthite nātha kṛpāṃ kuruṣva // Lal_25.13 //
children.translated_text: To those on wrong paths, without a protector, unable to reach the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — have compassion, O Protector! // Lal_25.13 //

children.text: vimokṣadvārāṇi apāvṛṇiṣva pracakṣva taṃ dharmanayaṃ hyakopyam /
children.translated_text: "Throw open the doors of liberation! Proclaim that unshakable method of <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: jātyandhabhūtasya janasya nātha tvamuttamaṃ śodhaya dharmacakṣuḥ // Lal_25.14 //
children.translated_text: For the people who are born blind, O Protector, purify the supreme eye of <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_25.14 //

children.text: na brahmaloke na ca devaloke na yakṣagandharvamanuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: "Not in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, nor in the world of gods, not among <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, or in the human world —

children.text: lokasya yo jātijarāpanetā nānyo 'sti tvatto hi manuṣyacandraḥ // Lal_25.15 //
children.translated_text: there is no other remover of birth and old age for the world than you, O Moon among men! // Lal_25.15 //

children.text: adhyeṣako 'haṃ tava dharmarāja adhyācarākṛtvana sarvadevān /
children.translated_text: "I am the entreater of you, O <s>Dharma</s>-king, having approached you on behalf of all the gods;

children.text: anena puṇyena ahaṃ pi kṣipraṃ pravartayeyaṃ varadharmacakram // Lal_25.16 //
children.translated_text: by this merit, may I too quickly turn the supreme wheel of <s>Dharma</s>!" // Lal_25.16 //

body.text: adhivāsayati sma bhikṣavastathāgataḥ śikhino brahmaṇastūṣṇībhāvena sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasyānugrahārthamanukampāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O monks, consented to <s>Śikhī Brahmā</s>'s [entreaty] through silence, out of grace and compassion for the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu śikhī mahābrahmā tathāgatasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā divyaiścandanacūrṇairagurucūrṇaiśca tathāgatamabhyavakīrya prītiprāmodyajātastatraivāntaradhāt //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, knowing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s consent through his silence, having scattered divine sandalwood powder and <s>aguru</s> (aloe) powder over the <s>Tathāgata</s>, filled with joy and gladness, vanished right there. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasya dharmālokasyādarotpādanārthaṃ śikhinaśca mahābrahmaṇaḥ punaḥ punastathāgatādhyeṣaṇayā kuśalamūlavivṛddhyarthaṃ dharmasya cātigambhīrodāratāmupādāya punarapyekasya rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasyāyamevaṃrūpaṃ cetovitarko 'bhūt - gambhīraḥ khalvayaṃ mayā dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddhaḥ sūkṣmo nipuṇo duranubodhaḥ atarko 'tarkāvacaraḥ paṇḍitavijñavedanīyaḥ sarvalokavipratyanīko durdṛśaḥ sarvopadhiniḥsargaḥ sarvasaṃskāropaśamaḥ sarvatamopacchedaḥ śūnyatānupalambhastṛṣṇākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam / ahaṃ cedidaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam, pare ca me na vibhāvayeyuḥ, sā me paramā viheṭhā bhavet / yannvahamalpotsukavihāreṇaiva vihareyam //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, in order to generate respect for the <s>Dharma</s>-radiance, and for the increase of the roots of merit through <s>Śikhī</s> the Great <s>Brahmā</s>'s repeated entreaty of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and considering the extreme profundity and sublimity of the <s>Dharma</s>, this thought arose again in the [<s>Tathāgata</s>], who was alone, in solitude, in meditative seclusion: "Profound indeed is this <s>Dharma</s> that has been fully awakened by me — subtle, refined, hard to comprehend, beyond reasoning, beyond the sphere of discursive thought, to be known only by the learned wise, contrary to all the world, hard to see: the relinquishment of all substrates, the pacification of all formations, the cutting off of all darkness, emptiness and non-apprehension, the extinction of craving, dispassion, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. If I were to teach this <s>Dharma</s> and others could not fathom it, that would be the supreme vexation for me. Let me rather dwell in a state of little concern." //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śikhī mahābrahmā buddhānubhāvena punarapi tathāgatasyetadamevaṃrūpeṇa cetaḥ - parivitarkamājñāya yena śakro devānāmindrastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - yatkhalu kauśika jānīyāstathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyālpotsukatāyai cittaṃ nataṃ na dharmadeśanāyām / nakṣyate batāyaṃ kauśika lokaḥ, vinakṣyate batāyaṃ kauśika lokaḥ, mahāvidyāndhakārakṣipto batāyaṃ kauśika loko bhaviṣyati, yatra hi nāma tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyālpotsukatāyai cittaṃ nataṃ na dharmasaṃprakāśanāyām / kasmādvayaṃ na gacchāmastathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dharmacakrapravartanāyādhyeṣitum? tatkasmāt? na hyanadhyeṣitāstathāgatā dharmacakraṃ pravartayanti / sādhu mārṣeti śakro brahmā bhaumāśca devā antarīkṣāścāturmahārājakāyikāstrāyatriṃśā yāmāstuṣitā nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikā ābhāsvarā bṛhatphalā śubhakṛtsnā saṃbahulāni ca śuddhāvāsakāyika devaputraśatasahasrāṇyatikrāntavarṇā atikrāntāyāṃ rātrau kevalaṃ tārāyaṇamūlaṃ divyena varṇena divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāman / upasaṃkramya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandya pradakṣiṇīkṛtya caikānte tasthuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Śikhī</s> the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, again knowing by the <s>Buddha</s>'s power this thought of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, approached <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. Having approached, he said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "Know, <s>Kauśika</s>, that the mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is inclined toward little concern and not toward teaching the <s>Dharma</s>! Alas, <s>Kauśika</s>, this world will perish! Alas, <s>Kauśika</s>, this world will be destroyed! Alas, <s>Kauśika</s>, this world will be cast into the great darkness of ignorance, inasmuch as the mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is inclined toward little concern and not toward illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>! Why do we not go and entreat the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>? Why? Because <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> without being entreated!" "Excellent, sir!" said <s>Śakra</s>. Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the earthly gods, the atmospheric gods, the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyikas</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s>, the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, the <s>Bṛhatphalas</s>, the <s>Śubhakṛtsnas</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-sons — all of surpassing radiance — in the latter part of the night, illuminating the entire <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> tree-root with a divine radiance and divine splendor, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, circumambulated him, and stood to one side. //

body.text: atha khalu śakro devānāmindro yena tathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya tathāgataṃ gāthayābhituṣṭāva -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with a verse —

children.text: uttiṣṭha vijitasaṃgrāma prajñākārā timisrā vivara loke /
children.translated_text: "Arise, O Victor of the battle! O mine of wisdom, dispel the darkness in the world!

children.text: cittaṃ hi te vimuktaṃ śaśiriva pūrṇo grahavimuktaḥ // Lal_25.17 //
children.translated_text: Your mind is liberated — like the full moon released from the grip [of an eclipse]!" // Lal_25.17 //

body.text: evamukte tathāgatastūṣṇīmevāsthāt //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Tathāgata</s> remained silent. //

body.text: atha khalu śikhī mahābrahmā śakraṃ devānāmindrametadavocat - naiva kauśika tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā adhyeṣyante dharmacakrapravartanatāyai yathā tvamadhyeṣase //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, said to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: "<s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are not to be entreated to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> in the manner in which you entreat!" //

body.text: atha khalu śikhī mahābrahmā ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena tathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya tathāgataṃ gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhī</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, and bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, addressed the <s>Tathāgata</s> with a verse —

children.text: uttiṣṭha vijitasaṃgrāma prajñākārā timisrā vivara loke /
children.translated_text: "Arise, O Victor of the battle! O mine of wisdom, dispel the darkness in the world!

children.text: deśaya tvaṃ mune dharmaṃ ājñātāro bhaviṣyanti // Lal_25.18 //
children.translated_text: Teach the <s>Dharma</s>, O sage — there will be those who comprehend!" // Lal_25.18 //

body.text: evamukte bhikṣavastathāgataḥ śikhinaṃ mahābrahmāṇametadavocat - gambhīraḥ khalvayaṃ mahābrahman mayā dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddhaḥ sūkṣmo nipuṇaḥ peyālaṃ yāvatsā me syātparamā viheṭhā / api ca me brahmannime gāthe 'bhīkṣṇaṃ pratibhāsaḥ -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> said this to <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s>: 'Profound indeed, O <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, is the <s>dharma</s> that has been fully awakened to by me — subtle, refined' — and so forth (<s>peyāla</s>) — 'up to: that would be my supreme vexation. Moreover, O <s>Brahmā</s>, these verses constantly appear to me:' —

children.text: pratisrotagāmi mārgo gambhīro durdṛśo mama /
children.translated_text: 'The path is against the stream, profound, difficult for me to see;

children.text: na taṃ drakṣyanti rāgāndhā alaṃ tasmātprakāśitum // Lal_25.19 //
children.translated_text: those blinded by passion will not see it — therefore enough with proclaiming it!' // Lal_25.19 //

children.text: anusrotaṃ pravāhyante kāmeṣu patitā prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Beings, fallen into sensual pleasures, are carried along with the current;

children.text: kṛcchreṇa me 'yaṃ saṃprāptaṃ alaṃ tasmātprakāśitum // Lal_25.20 //
children.translated_text: this has been attained by me with great difficulty — therefore enough with proclaiming it!' // Lal_25.20 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śikhī mahābrahmā śakraśca devānāmindrastathāgataṃ tūṣṇībhūtaṃ viditvā sārdhaṃ tairdevaputrairduḥkhitā durmanāstatraivāntaradhāyiṣuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing the <s>Tathāgata</s> had become silent, together with those <s>devaputras</s>, sorrowful and dejected, disappeared right there. //

body.text: trirapi ca tathāgatasyālpotsukatāyai cittaṃ namayati sma //
body.translated_text: Three times also the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s mind inclined toward having little enthusiasm [for teaching]. //

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena māgadhakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāmimānyevaṃrūpāṇi pāpakāni akuśalāni dṛṣṭigatānyutpannānyabhūvan / tadyathā / kecidevamāhuḥ - vātā na vāsyanti / kecidevamāhuḥ - agnirna jvaliṣyati / kecidāhuḥ - devo na varṣiṣyati / kecidāhuḥ - nadyo na vahyanti / kecidāhuḥ - śasyāni na prajāsyanti / kecidāhu - pakṣiṇa ākāśe na kramiṣyanti / kecidāhuḥ - gurviṇyo nārogyeṇa prasaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, among the people of <s>Magadha</s>, these kinds of evil, unwholesome wrong views had arisen. Namely: some said 'The winds will not blow'; some said 'Fire will not burn'; some said 'The rains will not fall'; some said 'The rivers will not flow'; some said 'The crops will not grow'; some said 'Birds will not fly in the sky'; some said 'Pregnant women will not deliver safely.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śikhī mahābrahmā tathāgatasyaivamevaṃrūpaṃ cittavitarkamājñāya māgadhakānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāmimāni dṛṣṭigatāni viditvā atikrāntāyāṃ rātrāvabhisaṃkrāntena varṇena sarvāvantaṃ tārāyaṇamūlaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya yena tathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivandyaikāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena tathāgatastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya tathāgataṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, knowing such a thought-process of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and knowing these wrong views among the people of <s>Magadha</s>, when the night had passed, with a surpassing radiance illuminating the entire root of the <s>Tārāyaṇa</s> (star-tree) with divine splendor, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, having bowed his head at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having placed his right knee on the ground, and having raised his joined palms toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he addressed the <s>Tathāgata</s> with verses:

children.text: vādo babhūva samalairvicintito dharmo 'viśuddho magadheṣu pūrvam /
children.translated_text: 'A doctrine was formerly devised in <s>Magadha</s> by the defiled — impure;

children.text: amṛtaṃ mune tadvivṛṇīṣva dvāraṃ śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ vimalena buddham // Lal_25.21 //
children.translated_text: O Sage, open that door of the deathless! Let them hear the <s>dharma</s> awakened to by the stainless one! // Lal_25.21 //

children.text: kṛtasvakārtho 'si bhujiṣyatāṃ gato duḥkhābhisaṃskāramalāpakṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You have accomplished your own purpose; you have attained the state of freedom; you have removed the stain of suffering and conditioned formations;

children.text: na hānivṛddhī kuśalasya te 'sti tvamagradharmeṣviha pāramiṃ gataḥ // Lal_25.22 //
children.translated_text: there is no decrease or increase of wholesome [qualities] for you — you have gone to the perfection of the highest truths here! // Lal_25.22 //

children.text: na te mune sadṛśa ihāsti loke kuto 'dhikaḥ syādiha te maharṣe /
children.translated_text: 'There is no one equal to you in this world, O Sage — how could there be anyone superior to you, O Great Seer?

children.text: bhavānihāgrastribhave virocate giriryathā 'sāvasurālayasthaḥ // Lal_25.23 //
children.translated_text: You shine here, supreme in the three realms of existence, like a mountain standing above the abode of <s>Asuras</s>! // Lal_25.23 //

children.text: mahākṛpāṃ jānaya duḥkhite jane na tvādṛśā jātu bhavantyupekṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Arouse great compassion for suffering people! Those like you never become indifferent;

children.text: bhavān viśāradyabalaiḥ samanvitaḥ tvameva śakto janatāṃ pratāritum // Lal_25.24 //
children.translated_text: you are endowed with the powers of fearlessness — you alone are able to ferry humanity across! // Lal_25.24 //

children.text: iyaṃ suśalyā sucirāturā prajā sadevakā saśramaṇā dvijākhilā /
children.translated_text: 'These beings are long afflicted, grievously ill — the world with its gods, with ascetics and brahmins, all of them;

children.text: āroginī bhotu nirāturajvarā na cāparaḥ śaraṇamihāsya vidyate // Lal_25.25 //
children.translated_text: may it become healthy, free from illness and fever — for there is no other refuge for them here! // Lal_25.25 //

children.text: cirānubaddhāstava devamānuṣāḥ kalyāṇacittā amṛtārthinaśca /
children.translated_text: 'Long have gods and humans followed you, with virtuous intentions and desiring the deathless;

children.text: dharmaṃ yamevādhigamiṣyate jino yathāvadanyūnamudāhariṣyati // Lal_25.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> to which the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) has attained — he will proclaim it fully, without diminishment! // Lal_25.26 //

children.text: tasmāddhiyā cāmisu vikrama tvāṃ vinayasva sattvāṃ ciranaṣṭamārgāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, with wisdom and valor, exert yourself; tame beings who have long lost the path!

children.text: aviśrutārthā śamanāya kāṅkṣitāḥ sudurbalā bṛṃhaṇakāṅkṣiṇo vā // Lal_25.27 //
children.translated_text: Those who have not heard the meaning, desiring pacification — or the very weak, desiring nourishment! // Lal_25.27 //

children.text: iyaṃ tṛṣārtā janatā mahāmune udīkṣate dharmajalaṃ tavāntike /
children.translated_text: 'These beings, O Great Sage, are thirsty, looking expectantly for the water of <s>dharma</s> in your presence;

children.text: megho yathā saṃtṛṣitāṃ vasuṃdharāṃ kuru tarpaṇāṃ nāyaka dharmavṛṣṭyā // Lal_25.28 //
children.translated_text: like a cloud [refreshing] the parched earth, O Leader, satisfy them with a rain of <s>dharma</s>! // Lal_25.28 //

body.text: cirapraṇaṣṭā vicaranti mānavā bhave kudṛṣṭīgahane sakaṇṭake /
body.translated_text: 'Long lost, humans wander in existence, in the thorny thicket of wrong views;

body.text: akaṇṭakaṃ mārgamṛjuṃ pracakṣva taṃ yaṃ bhāvayitvā hyamṛtaṃ labheyam // Lal_25.29 //
body.translated_text: declare that straight, thornless path, cultivating which they may attain the deathless! // Lal_25.29 //

children.text: andhāprapāte patitā hyanāyakā noddhartumanyairiha śakyamete /
children.translated_text: 'Fallen into a blind precipice, without a guide — they cannot be pulled up by others here;

children.text: mahāprapāte patitāṃ samuddhara chandaṃ samutpādya vṛṣo 'si buddhimān // Lal_25.30 //
children.translated_text: rescue those fallen into the great precipice! Generate the aspiration — you are a bull, you are wise! // Lal_25.30 //

children.text: na saṃgatiste 'sti sadā mune ciraṃ kadācidaudumbarapuṣpasaṃnibhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your arising is never constant, O Sage — like the flower of the <s>udumbara</s>, at rare times

children.text: jināḥ pṛthivyāṃ prabhavanti nāyakāḥ prāptākṣaṇo mocaya nātha sattvāṃ // Lal_25.31 //
children.translated_text: do <s>Jinas</s>, the Leaders, appear on earth — the opportune moment has arrived, O Protector, liberate beings! // Lal_25.31 //

children.text: abhūcca te pūrvabhaveṣviyaṃ matiḥ tīrṇaḥ svayaṃ tārayitā bhaveyam /
children.translated_text: 'In your former existences, this was your resolve: Having myself crossed over, I shall become a ferryman for others;

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ pāragato 'si sāṃprataṃ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ kuru satyavikramaḥ // Lal_25.32 //
children.translated_text: without doubt you have now gone to the far shore — fulfill your true vow, O one of true valor! // Lal_25.32 //

children.text: dharmolkayā vidhama mune 'ndhakārā ucchrepaya tvaṃ hi tathāgatadhvajam /
children.translated_text: 'Dispel the darkness with the torch of <s>dharma</s>, O Sage! Raise the banner of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!

children.text: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ pratilābhyudīraṇe mṛgādhipo vā nada dundubhisvaraḥ // Lal_25.33 //
children.translated_text: This is the time to speak out and proclaim — roar like the king of beasts, with a voice like a drum! // Lal_25.33 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgataḥ sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ buddhacakṣuṣā vyavalokayan sattvān paśyati sma hīnamadhyapraṇītānuccanīcamadhyamān svākārān suviśodhakān durākārān durviśodhakānuddhāṭitajñānavipañcijñān padaparamāṃstrīn sattvarāśīnekaṃ mithyatvaniyatamekaṃ samyaktvaniyatamekamaniyatam / tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavaḥ puruṣaḥ puṣkariṇyāstīre sthitaḥ paśyati jalaruhāṇi kānicidudakāntargatāni kānicidudakasamāni kānicidudakābhyudgatāni, evameva bhikṣavastathāgataḥ sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ buddhacakṣuṣā vyavalokayan paśyati sma sattvāṃstriṣu rāśiṣu vyavasthitān //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, surveying the entire world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, saw beings — inferior, middling, and excellent; high, low, and medium; of good disposition and easy to purify, of bad disposition and hard to purify; those with faculties opened to knowledge and discernment, and those for whom words are the utmost limit — the mass of beings: one group fixed in wrong course, one fixed in right course, and one unfixed. Just as, O monks, a man standing on the bank of a lotus-pond sees lotuses — some submerged in the water, some level with the water, some risen above the water — even so, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, surveying the entire world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, saw beings established in the three groups. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - deśayeyaṃ cāhaṃ dharmaṃ na vā deśayeyam / sa eṣa mithyatvaniyato rāśirnaivāyaṃ dharmamājānīyāt / deśayeyaṃ cāhaṃ vā dharmaṃ na vā deśayeyam / yo 'yaṃ samyaktvaniyato rāśirājñāsyatyevaiṣa dharmam / (yatkhalu punarayamaniyato rāśirājñāsyatyevaiṣa dharmam / ) yatkhalu punarayamaniyato rāśiḥ, tasmai saceddharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmi, ājñāsyati / uta na deśayiṣyāmi, nājñāsyate //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> thought thus: 'Whether I teach the <s>dharma</s> or do not teach it — that group fixed in the wrong course would not understand this <s>dharma</s>. Whether I teach the <s>dharma</s> or do not teach it — that group fixed in the right course will certainly understand this <s>dharma</s>. But as for this unfixed group — if I teach the <s>dharma</s> to them, they will understand. But if I do not teach, they will not understand.' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato 'niyatarāśivyavasthitān sattvānārabhya mahākaruṇāmavakrāmayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with regard to beings established in the unfixed group, gave rise to great compassion. //

body.text: atha khalu tathāgata ātmanaścemaṃ samyagjñānamadhikṛtya śikhinaśca mahābrahmaṇo 'dhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā śikhinaṃ mahābrahmāṇaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having considered his own right knowledge and having understood the entreaty of <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, addressed <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s> with verses:

children.text: apāvṛtāsteṣāmamṛtasya dvārā brahman ti satataṃ ye śrotavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Open for them are the doors of the deathless, O <s>Brahmā</s> — those who have ears, constantly!

children.text: praviśanti śraddhā naviheṭhasaṃjñāḥ śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ magadheṣu sattvāḥ // Lal_25.34 //
children.translated_text: They shall enter with faith, not with the perception of vexation; beings in <s>Magadha</s> shall hear the <s>dharma</s>!' // Lal_25.34 //

body.text: atha khalu śikhī mahābrahmā tathāgatasyādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastathāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā tatraivāntaradhāt //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śikhin</s> <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, knowing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s consent, was delighted, elated, overjoyed, filled with gladness and mental delight. Having bowed his head at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, he disappeared right there. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo bhaumā devāstasyāṃ velāyāmantarīkṣebhyo devebhyo ghoṣamudīrayanti sma, śabdamanuśrāvayanti sma - adya mārṣā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena dharmacakrapravartanāyai pratiśrutam / tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / parihāsyante bata bho mārṣā asurāḥ kāyāḥ / divyāḥ kāyāḥ paripūriṃ gabhiṣyanti / bahavaśca sattvā loke parinirvāsyanti / evamevāntarīkṣā devā bhaumebhyo devebhyaḥ pratiśratya cāturmahārājikānāṃ devānāṃ ghoṣamudīrayanti sma / cāturmahārājikāstrāyatriṃśānām, trāyatriṃśā yāmānām, yāmā tuṣitanirmāṇaratīnām, nirmāṇaratayaḥ paranirmitavaśavartinām, te 'pi brahmakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ ghoṣamudīrayanti sma, śabdamanuśrāvayanti sma - adya mārṣāstathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena dharmacakrapravartanāyai pratiśrutam / tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / parihāsyante bata bho mārṣā asurāḥ kāyāḥ / divyāḥ kāyā vivardhiṣyante / bahavaśca sattvā loke parinirvāsyantīte //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the earthly gods at that moment sent forth a proclamation to the gods of the sky, making the sound heard: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, has consented to turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s>! This will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great mass of people, of gods and humans! The bodies of <s>Asuras</s>, sirs, will diminish! The divine bodies will be filled! And many beings in the world will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!' Likewise the gods of the sky relayed to the earthly gods, and the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods proclaimed to the <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Trāyatriṃśa</s> to the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> to the <s>Tuṣita</s> and <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> to the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, and they too proclaimed to the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, making the sound heard: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, has consented to turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s>! This will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great mass of people, of gods and humans! The bodies of <s>Asuras</s>, sirs, will diminish! The divine bodies will increase! And many beings in the world will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!' //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastatkṣaṇaṃ tanmuhurtaṃ tallavaṃ yāvadbahmakāyikā devāstasmādbhaumādārabhya ekavāgekanirnāda ekanirghoṣo 'bhyudgato 'bhūt - adya mārṣāstathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena dharmacakrapravartanāyai pratiśrutamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O monks, at that instant, at that moment, at that second, from the earthly [gods] up to the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, a single voice, a single sound, a single proclamation arose: 'Today, sirs, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>, has consented to turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s>!' //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo dharmaruciśca nāmā bodhivṛkṣadevatā dharmakāyaśca dharmamatiśca dharmacārī ca, ete catvāro bodhivṛkṣadevatāstathāgatasya caraṇayornipatyaivamāhuḥ - kva bhagavān dharmacakraṃ pravartiṣyatīti? evamukte bhikṣavastathāgatastān devatānetadavocat - vārāṇasyāmṛṣipatane mṛgadāve / te āhuḥ - parīttajanakāyā bhagavan vārāṇasī mahānagarī, parīttadrumachāyaśca mṛgadāvaḥ / santyanyāni bhagavan mahānagarāṇi ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāni subhikṣāṇi ramaṇīyāni ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi udyānavanaparvatapratimaṇḍitāni / teṣāṃ bhagavānanyatame dharmacakraṃ pravartayatu / tathāgato 'vocatmaivaṃ bhadramukhāḥ / tatkasmāt?
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the Bodhi-tree deities named <s>Dharmaruci</s>, <s>Dharmakāya</s>, <s>Dharmamati</s>, and <s>Dharmacārī</s> — these four Bodhi-tree deities, falling at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, said: 'Where will the Blessed One turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s>?' Thus addressed, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> said to those deities: 'At <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (Seer's Resort), in the Deer Park at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.' They said: 'The great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> has only a small population, Blessed One, and the Deer Park has little shade of trees. There are other great cities, Blessed One — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, thronging with many people, adorned with parks, forests, and mountains. May the Blessed One turn the wheel of <s>dharma</s> in one of those.' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said: 'Do not [say] so, good-faced ones! Why?'

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ yajñasahasrakoṭinayutā ye tatra yaṣṭā mayā
children.translated_text: 'Sixty <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> thousands of sacrifices were performed by me there;

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ buddhasahasrakoṭinayutā ye tatra saṃpūjitā /
children.translated_text: sixty <s>koṭī-nayuta</s> thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped by me there;

children.text: paurāṇāmṛṣiṇāmihālayu varo vārāṇasī nāmavā
children.translated_text: it is the excellent resort of the ancient sages — <s>Vārāṇasī</s> by name,

children.text: devānāgamabhiṣṭuto mahitalo dharmābhinimnaḥ sadā // Lal_25.35 //
children.translated_text: praised by the coming of gods, with hallowed ground, always inclined toward <s>dharma</s>! // Lal_25.35 //

children.text: buddhā koṭisahasra naikanavatiḥ pūrve smarāmī aha
children.translated_text: 'Ninety-one thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> of the past I remember,

children.text: ye tasminnṛṣisāhvaye vanavare vartīsu cakrottamam /
children.translated_text: who in that excellent forest called <s>Ṛṣi</s> (Seers) turned the supreme wheel;

children.text: śāntaṃ cāpyupaśāntadhyānabhimukhaṃ nityaṃ mṛgaiḥ sevitaṃ
children.translated_text: peaceful, and facing the meditation of those who have attained tranquility, always frequented by deer —

children.text: ityarthe ṛṣisāhvaye vanavare vartiṣyi cakrottamam // Lal_25.36 //
children.translated_text: for this reason, in the excellent forest called <s>Ṛṣi</s>, I shall turn the supreme wheel!' // Lal_25.36 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare 'dhyeṣaṇāparivarto nāma pañcaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter of the glorious <s>Lalitavistara</s>, named the Chapter on Entreaty (<s>Adhyeṣaṇāparivarta</s>). //

body.text: START Parivarta 26
body.translated_text: START Chapter 26

body.text: dharmacakrapravartanaparivartaḥ ṣaḍviṃśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The twenty-sixth: the Chapter on Turning the Wheel of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmacakrapravartanaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgataḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ sarvabandhanasamucchinnaḥ sarvakleśoddhṛto nirvāntamalakleśo nihatamārapratyarthikaḥ sarvabuddhadharmanayānupraviṣṭaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī daśabalasamanvāgataścaturvaiśāradyaprāpto 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmapratipūrṇaḥ pañcacakṣuḥsamanvāgato 'nāvaraṇena buddhacakṣuṣā sarvāvantaṃ lokamavalokyaivaṃ cintayati sma - kasmā ayamahaṃ sarvaprathamaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam? katamaḥ sattvaḥ śuddhaḥ svākāraḥ suvineyaḥ suvijñāpakaḥ suviśodhako mandarāgadoṣamoho 'parokṣavijñāno yo 'śrutavān dharmasya parihīyate? tasmāyahaṃ sarvaprathamaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam, yaśca me dharmaṃ deśitamājānīyānna ca māṃ sa viheṭhayet //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> — who had accomplished his task, done what was to be done, severed all bonds, extracted all afflictions, with defilements extinguished, who had conquered <s>Māra</s> the adversary, entered into the method of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, omniscient, all-seeing, endowed with the ten powers, having attained the four confidences, fulfilled in the eighteen special <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, endowed with the five eyes — surveying the entire world with his unobstructed <s>Buddha</s>-eye, reflected thus: 'To whom should I first teach the <s>Dharma</s>? Which being is pure, of good disposition, easy to discipline, easy to instruct, easy to purify, of slight passion, hatred, and delusion, of direct understanding, who through not hearing the <s>Dharma</s> is declining? To that one I should first teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and one who understands my teaching of <s>Dharma</s> would not vex me.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhūt - rudrakaḥ khalu rāmaputraḥ śuddhaḥ svākāraḥ suvijñāpakaḥ suviśodhako mandarāgamoho 'parokṣavijñānaḥ / so 'śravaṇāddharmasya parihīyate / śrāvakebhyo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasahavratāyai dharmaṃ deśayati / kutrāsāvetarhi prativasatītyājñāsīt / adya saptāhakālagata iti / devatā api tathāgatasya caraṇayornipatyaivamāhuḥ - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata, adya saptāhakālagato rudrako rāmaputraḥ / tasya me bhikṣava etadabhūt - mahāhānirvartate rudrakasya rāmaputrasya, ya imameva supraṇītaṃ dharmamaśrutvā kālagataḥ / sacedasāvimaṃ dharmamaśroṣyadājñāsyat / tasmai cāhaṃ prathamaṃ dharma deśayiṣyam, na ca māṃ sa vyaheṭhayiṣyat //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: '<s>Rudraka</s>, the son of <s>Rāma</s>, is pure, of good disposition, easy to instruct, easy to purify, of slight passion and delusion, of direct understanding. Through not hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, he is declining. He teaches his disciples [only] the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception as the co-practice [of the path]. Where does he now dwell?' He knew: 'He died seven days ago.' Deities also, falling at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, said thus: 'So it is, Blessed One! So it is, <s>Sugata</s>! <s>Rudraka</s>, the son of <s>Rāma</s>, died seven days ago.' Then this occurred to me, O monks: 'It is a great loss for <s>Rudraka</s>, the son of <s>Rāma</s>, that he died without hearing this supremely excellent <s>Dharma</s>. Had he heard this <s>Dharma</s>, he would have understood. To him I would have first taught the <s>Dharma</s>, and he would not have vexed me.'

body.text: punarapi bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhūt - ko 'nyaḥ sattvaḥ śuddhaḥ suvineyaḥ pūrvavadyāvanna ca dharmadeśanāṃ viheṭhayediti / tato bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - ayaṃ khalvapyārāḍaḥ kālāpaḥ śuddho yāvanna ca me dharmadeśanāṃ viheṭhayediti / samanvāharati sma bhikṣavastathāgataḥ kutrāsāvetarhīti / samanvāharaṃścājñāsīdadya trīṇyahāni kālagatasyeti / śuddhāvāsakāyikā api ca devatā enamarthaṃ tathāgatasyārocayanti sma - evametadbhagavan, evametatsugata / adya tryahaṃ kālagatasyārāḍasya kālāpasya / tatastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - mahāhānirvartate arāḍasya kālāpasya, ya imamevaṃ supraṇītaṃ dharmamaśrutvā kālagata iti //
body.translated_text: Again, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'What other being is pure, easy to discipline — as before — who would not be vexed by the teaching of <s>Dharma</s>?' Then, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'This <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s> is also pure — up to — and he would not be vexed by my teaching of <s>Dharma</s>.' The <s>Tathāgata</s> investigated, O monks: 'Where does he now dwell?' And investigating, he knew: 'He died three days ago.' The <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> deities also reported this matter to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'So it is, Blessed One! So it is, <s>Sugata</s>! It is three days since <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s> died.' Then this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'It is a great loss for <s>Ārāḍa Kālāpa</s>, that he died without hearing this supremely excellent <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: punarapi bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhūt - kaḥ khalvanyaḥ sattvaḥ śuddhaḥ svākāro yāvanna ca me dharmadeśanāṃ viheṭhayediti //
body.translated_text: Again, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'What other being is pure, of good disposition — up to — who would not be vexed by my teaching of <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - te khalu pañcakā bhadravargīyāḥ śuddhāḥ svākārāḥ suvijñāpakāḥ suviśodhakā mandarāgadoṣamohā aparokṣavijñānāḥ / te 'śravaṇāddharmasya parihīyante / taiścāhaṃ duṣkaracaryāṃ carannupasthito 'bhūvam / te mayā dharmaṃ deśitamājñāsyanti, na ca me ha viheṭhayiṣyanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'The five of the auspicious group (<s>pañcaka bhadravargīya</s>) are pure, of good disposition, easy to instruct, easy to purify, of slight passion, hatred, and delusion, of direct understanding. Through not hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, they are declining. Moreover, they attended me while I was practicing austerities. They will understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught by me, and they will not vex me.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - yannvahaṃ pañcakebhyo bhadravargīyebhyaḥ prathamaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Let me teach the <s>Dharma</s> first to the five of the auspicious group.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgatasya punaretadabhavat - kasminnetarhi pañcakā bhadravargīyāḥ prativasanti? atha tathāgataḥ sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ buddhacakṣuṣā vyavalokayan paśyati sma / adrākṣītpañcakān bhadravargīyān vārāṇasyāṃ viharata ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve / dṛṣṭvā ca tathāgatasyaitadabhavat - yannvahaṃ pañcakebhyo bhadravargīyebhyaḥ sarvaprathamaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam / te hi mama sarvaprathamaṃ dharmaṃ deśitamājñāsyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? caritāvino hi te bhikṣavaḥ suparipaṇḍitaśukladharmāṇo mokṣamārgābhimukhā nibandhāpanītāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, this further occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Where do the five of the auspicious group now dwell?' Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, surveying the entire world with his <s>Buddha</s>-eye, saw [them]. He saw the five of the auspicious group dwelling at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, the Deer Park. Having seen, this occurred to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Let me teach the <s>Dharma</s> first of all to the five of the auspicious group. For they will first understand the <s>Dharma</s> taught by me. For what reason? Those monks have practiced, are well-trained in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, face toward the path of liberation, and have removed their fetters.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgata evamanuvicintya bodhimaṇḍādutthāya trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃprakampyānupūrveṇa magadheṣu caryāṃ caran kāśiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ prakrāmat / atha gayāyāṃ bodhimaṇḍasya cāntarādanyatama ājīvako 'drākṣīttathāgataṃ dūrata evāgacchantam / dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena tathāgatastenopajagāma / upetyaikānte 'sthāt / ekānte sthitaśca bhikṣava ājīvakastathāgatena sārdhaṃ vividhāṃ saṃmodanīṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā evamāha - viprasannāni te āyuṣman gautama indriyāṇi / pariśuddhaḥ paryavadātaḥ pītanirbhāsaśca te chavivarṇaḥ tadyathāpi nāma śāradaṃ kālaṃ pāṇḍuravarṇaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ pītanirbhāsaṃ bhavati, evameva bhavato gautamasya pariśuddhānīndriyāṇi pariśuddhaṃ mukhamaṇḍalaṃ paryavadātam / tadyathāpi nāma tālaphalasya pakvasya samanantaravṛntacyutasya bandhanāśrayaḥ pītanirbhāso bhavati pariśuddhaḥ paryavadātaḥ, evameva bhavato gautamasya pariśuddhānīndriyāṇi pariśuddhaṃ mukhamaṇḍalaṃ paryavadātam / tadyathāpi nāma jāmbūnadavarṇaniṣkaḥ ulkāmukhaprakṛṣṭo dakṣiṇakarmāraputreṇa suparikarmakṛtaḥ pāṇḍukambalopanikṣipto varṇavān bhavati pariśuddhaḥ paryavadātaḥ pītanirbhāso 'tīva prabhāsvaraḥ, evameva bhavato gautamasya viprasannānīndriyāṇi, pariśuddhastvagvarṇaḥ, paryavadātaṃ mukhamaṇḍalam / kasminnāyuṣman gautama brahmacaryamuṣyate? evamukte bhikṣavastathāgatastamājīvakaṃ gāthayā pratyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having thus reflected, rising from the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, causing the trichiliocosm to tremble, traveling gradually through the <s>Magadha</s> country, set forth on a journey in the <s>Kāśi</s> region. And between <s>Gayā</s> and the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, a certain <s>Ājīvaka</s> saw the <s>Tathāgata</s> coming from afar. Having seen, he approached the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, that <s>Ājīvaka</s>, O monks, having exchanged various greetings with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, said thus: 'Your faculties are serene, venerable <s>Gautama</s>. Your complexion is pure, clear, and golden-hued — just as in the autumn season, the clear sky is bright, golden-hued, and radiant; even so are the faculties of venerable <s>Gautama</s> pure and his facial countenance clear. Just as a ripe <s>tāla</s> (palm) fruit, freshly fallen from the stalk, freed from its attachment, is golden-hued, pure, and clear; even so are the faculties of venerable <s>Gautama</s> pure and his facial countenance clear. Just as a <s>jāmbūnada</s> (gold) disc, drawn through the forge, well-worked by a skilled southern goldsmith, placed on a white woolen cloth, is lustrous, pure, clear, golden-hued, and exceedingly radiant; even so are the faculties of venerable <s>Gautama</s> serene, his skin-complexion pure, and his facial countenance clear. Under whom, venerable <s>Gautama</s>, do you lead the holy life?' When this was said, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> replied to that <s>Ājīvaka</s> with a verse:

children.text: ācāryo na hi me kaścitsadṛśo me na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'No teacher is mine; none exists equal to me;

children.text: eko 'hamasmi saṃbuddhaḥ śītībhūto nirāśravaḥ // Lal_26.1 //
children.translated_text: I alone am the Fully Awakened One, cooled, free from outflows.' // Lal_26.1 //

body.text: so 'vocat - arhaṃ khalu gautamamātmānaṃ prātijānīṣe / tathāgato 'vocat -
body.translated_text: He said: 'So you, <s>Gautama</s>, claim yourself to be an <s>Arhat</s>?' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said:

children.text: ahamevārahaṃ loke śāstā hyahamanuttaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I indeed am the <s>Arhat</s> in the world; I am the Teacher, unsurpassed;

children.text: sadevāsuragandharve nāsti me pratipudgalaḥ // Lal_26.2 //
children.translated_text: among gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, no one is my equal.' // Lal_26.2 //

body.text: so 'vocat - jinaṃ khalu gautama mātmānaṃ pratijānīṣe / tathāgato 'vocat -
body.translated_text: He said: 'So you, <s>Gautama</s>, claim yourself to be a <s>Jina</s> (Victor)?' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said:

children.text: jinā hi mādṛśā jñeyā ye prāptā āśravakṣayam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Jinas</s> are to be known as those like me who have attained the destruction of outflows;

children.text: jitā me pāpakā dharmāstenopaga jino hyaham // Lal_26.3 //
children.translated_text: evil <s>dharmas</s> have been conquered by me — therefore know that I am a <s>Jina</s>!' // Lal_26.3 //

body.text: so 'vocat - kva tarhyāyuṣman gautama gamiṣyasi? tathāgato 'vocat -
body.translated_text: He said: 'Where then, venerable <s>Gautama</s>, will you go?' The <s>Tathāgata</s> said:

children.text: vārāṇasīṃ gamiṣyāmi gatvā vai kāśināṃ purīm /
children.translated_text: 'I shall go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>;

children.text: andhabhūtasya lokasya kartāsmyasadṛśāṃ prabhām // Lal_26.4 //
children.translated_text: for the world that has become blind, I shall create an incomparable radiance.' // Lal_26.4 //

children.text: vārāṇasīṃ gamiṣyami gatvā vai kāśināṃ purīm /
children.translated_text: 'I shall go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>;

children.text: śabdahīnasya lokasya tāḍayiṣye 'mṛtadundubhim // Lal_26.5 //
children.translated_text: for the world bereft of sound, I shall beat the drum of the deathless.' // Lal_26.5 //

children.text: vārāṇasīṃ gamiṣyāmi gatvā vai kāśināṃ purīm /
children.translated_text: 'I shall go to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>;

children.text: dharmacakraṃ pravartiṣye lokeṣvaprativartitam // Lal_26.6 //
children.translated_text: I shall turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, never turned before in all the worlds.' // Lal_26.6 //

body.text: tadbhaviṣyasi gautama ityuktvā sa ājīvako dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ prākrāmat / tathāgato 'pyuttarāmukhaḥ prākrāmat //
body.translated_text: Having said 'So be it, <s>Gautama</s>,' that <s>Ājīvaka</s> departed facing south. The <s>Tathāgata</s> also departed facing north.

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgato gayāyāṃ sudarśanena nāgarājena nimantrito 'bhut vāsena bhaktena ca / tatastathāgato rohitavastumagamat, tasmādurubilvākalpaṃ tasmādaṇālamagamat, tataḥ sārathipuram / eṣu ca sarveṣu bhikṣavastathāgato gṛhapatibhirbhaktena vāsena copanimantryamāṇo 'nupūrveṇa gaṅgāyā nadyāstīramupāgamat //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> was invited by the <s>Nāga</s> king named <s>Sudarśana</s> at <s>Gayā</s> with lodging and food. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> went to <s>Rohitavastu</s>, from there to <s>Urubilvākalpa</s>, from there to <s>Anāla</s>, and then to <s>Sārathipura</s>. In all these [places], O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, being invited by householders with food and lodging, traveling gradually, approached the bank of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena gaṅgā mahānadī suparipūrṇā samatīrthakā vahati sma //
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s> was flowing full to its banks, level with the fords.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato nāvikasamīpamupāgamatpārasaṃtaraṇāya / sa prāha - prayaccha gautama tarapaṇyam / na me 'sti mārṣa tarapaṇyamityuktvā tathāgato vihāyasā pathā tīrātparaṃ tīramagamat / tataḥ sa nāvikastaṃ dṛṣṭvātīva vipratisāryabhūt - evaṃvidho dakṣiṇīyo mayā na tārita iti / hā kaṣṭamiti kṛtvā mūrchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ patitaḥ / tata enāṃ prakṛtiṃ nāviko rājñe bimbisārāya ārocayāmāsa - śramaṇaḥ svāmi gautamastarapaṇyaṃ yācamāno nāsti tarapaṇyamityuktvā vihāyasā atastīrātparaṃ tīraṃ gata iti / tacchrutvā tadagreṇa rājñā bimbisāreṇa sarvapravrajitānāṃ tarapaṇyamutsṛṣṭamabhavat //
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> approached a boatman for crossing to the other side. He said: 'Pay the ferry toll, <s>Gautama</s>.' 'I have no ferry toll, friend' — having said this, the <s>Tathāgata</s> went from this bank to the far bank by the aerial path. Then that boatman, seeing this, became exceedingly remorseful: 'Such a worthy one was not ferried by me!' Crying 'Alas!' he fell unconscious to the ground. Then that boatman reported this matter to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Lord, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, when asked for the ferry toll, saying "I have no ferry toll," went from this bank to the far bank through the sky.' Having heard this, from that time forward King <s>Bimbisāra</s> abolished the ferry toll for all renunciants.
