body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgato 'nupūrveṇa janapadacaryāṃ caran yena vārāṇasī mahānagarī tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya kālyameva nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vārāṇasīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat / tasyāṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātrapratikrāntaḥ yena ṛṣipatano mṛgadāvo yena ca pañcakā bhadravargīyāstenopasaṃkrāmati sma / adrākṣuḥ khalu punaḥ pañcakā bhadravargīyāstathāgataṃ dūrata evāgacchantam / dṛṣṭvā ca kriyābandhamakārṣuḥ - eṣa sa āyuṣmantaḥ śramaṇo gautama āgacchati sma śaithiliko bāhulikaḥ pradhānavibhraṣṭaḥ / anena khalvapi tayāpi tāvatpūrvikayā duṣkaracaryayā na śakitaṃ kiṃciduttarimanuṣyadharmādalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaṃ sākṣātkartum / kiṃ punaretarhi audārikamāhāramāharan sukhallikāyogamanuyukto viharan / abhavyaḥ khalveṣa śaithiliko bāhulikaḥ / nāsya kenacitpratyudgantavyaṃ na pratyutthātavyam / na pātracīvaraṃ pratigrahītavyaṃ nāśanaṃ dātavyaṃ na pānīyaṃ paribhogyaṃ na pādapratiṣṭhānaṃ sthāpayitvātiriktānyāsanāni / vaktavyaṃ ca -
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, traveling gradually through the countryside, approached the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Having approached, in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. Having wandered for alms in that [city], having finished his meal, returning from his alms-round, he approached <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, the Deer Park, and the five of the auspicious group. The five of the auspicious group saw the <s>Tathāgata</s> coming from afar. Having seen, they made an agreement: 'This, venerable ones, is the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> coming — the lax one, the indulgent one, fallen from exertion. Even by that former austere practice he was not able to realize any superhuman state, any distinction of noble knowledge and vision. How much less so now, when he eats coarse food and is devoted to the practice of comfort! This lax and indulgent one is unworthy. No one should go forth to meet him, nor rise for him. His bowl and robe should not be received, no seat offered, no water given, no footrest placed — only a surplus seat [may be set out]. And he should be told:

body.text: saṃvidyanta imānyāyuṣman gautama atiriktānyāsanāni / sacedākāṅkṣasi niṣīdeti / āyuṣmāṃstvājñānakauṇḍinyaścittenādhivāsayati sma / vācā ca na pratikṣipati sma / yathā yathā ca bhikṣavastathāgato yena pañcakā bhadravargīyāstenopasaṃkrāmati sma, tathā tathā te svakasvakeṣvāsaneṣu na ramante sma, utthātukāmā abhūvan / tadyathāpi nāma pakṣī śakuniḥ pañjaragataḥ syāt, tasya ca pañjaragatasyādho 'gnirdagdho bhavet / so 'gnisaṃtaptastvaritamūrdhvamutpatitukāmo bhavet pratretukāmaśca, evameva yathā yathā tathāgataḥ pañcakānāṃ bhadravargīyāṇāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāmati sma, tathā tathā pañcakā bhadravargīyāḥ svakasvakeṣvāsaneṣu na ramante sma, utthātukāmā abhūvan / tatkasmāt? na sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate yastathāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā āsanānna pratyuttiṣṭhet / yathā yathā ca tathāgataḥ pañcakān bhadravargīyānupasaṃkrāmati sma, tathā tathā pañcakā bhadravargīyāstathāgatasya śriyaṃ tejaścāsahamānā āsanebhyaḥ prakampyamānāḥ sarve kriyākāraṃ bhittvā cotthāyāsanebhyaḥ, kaścitpratyudgacchati sma, kaścitpratyudgamya pātracīvaraṃ pratigṛhṇāti sma / kaścidāsanamupanāmayati sma / kaścitpādapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ kaścitpādaprakṣālanodakamupasthāpayati sma / evaṃ cāvocat - svāgataṃ te āyuṣman gautama, svāgataṃ te āyuṣman gautam / niṣīdedamāsanaṃ prajñaptam / nyaṣīdatkhalvapi bhikṣavastathāgataḥ prajñapta evāsane / pañcakā pi bhadravargīyāste tathāgatena sārdhaṃ vividhāṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ kathāṃ kṛtvaikānte niṣeduḥ / ekānte niṣaṇṇāśca te pañcakā bhadravargīyāstathāgatametadavocan - viprasannāni te āyuṣman gautamendriyāṇi, pariśuddhaśchavivarṇa iti hi sarvaṃ pūrvavat / tadasti te āyuṣman gautama kaściduttarimanuṣyadharmāṃdalamāryajñānadarśanaviśeṣaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ? evamukte bhikṣavastathāgataḥ pañcakān bhadravargīyānevamāha - mā yūyaṃ bhikṣavastathāgatamāyuṣmadvādena samudācariṣṭa / mā vo bhūddīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya / amṛtaṃ mayā bhikṣavaḥ sākṣātkṛto 'mṛtagāmī ca mārgaḥ / buddho 'hamasmi bhikṣavaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī śītībhūto 'nāśravaḥ / vaśī sarvadharmeṣu / dharmamahaṃ bhikṣavo deśayiṣyāmi, āśu gacchata śṛṇuta pratipadyadhvam / śrotamavadadhata ahamavavadāmyanuśāsmi / yathā mayā samyagavavaditāḥ samyaganuśiṣṭā yūyamapyāśravāṇāṃ cetovimuktaṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ ca dṛṣṭa eva dharme sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya pravedayiṣyatha - kṣīṇā no jātiruṣitaṃ ca brahmacaryam, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyam, nāparamityato 'nyadbhavaṃ prajānāma iti / nanu ca yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣava etadabhūt - ayaṃ khalvāyuṣmanta āgacchati śramaṇo gautamaḥ śaithiliko bāhulikaḥ pradhānavibhraṣṭa iti pūrvavat / sacedākāṅkṣasi niṣīdeti / teṣāṃ ca ehi bhikṣava ityukte yatkiṃcittīrthikaliṅgaṃ tīrthikadhvajaḥ, sarvo 'sau tatkṣaṇamevāntaraghāt / tricīvaraṃ pātraṃ ca prādurabhūt, tadanu chinnāśca keśāḥ / tadyathāpi nāma varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣorīryāpathaḥ saṃvṛtto 'bhut / saiva ca teṣāṃ pravrajyābhūtsaivopasaṃpadbhikṣubhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: "There are, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, these extra seats available. If you wish, please sit down." The Venerable <s>Ājñānakauṇḍinya</s> consented in his mind, but did not refuse with words. And, O monks, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> approached the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, they found themselves unable to remain in their own seats and wished to rise — just as a caged bird, when a fire is lit below its cage, being scorched by the fire, would wish to fly quickly upward and escape; even so, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> approached the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, they were unable to remain in their own seats and wished to rise. Why? Because there exists no being in the entire world of beings who, having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, would not rise from his seat. And as the <s>Tathāgata</s> approached the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, unable to bear the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s glory and splendor, shaken from their seats, they all broke their agreed resolve and rose from their seats: one went forward to greet him, one received his bowl and robe after greeting him, one offered a seat, one set out a footrest, and one brought water for washing his feet. And they said: "Welcome, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>! Welcome, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>! Please sit down — this seat has been prepared." And indeed, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> sat down on the prepared seat. The five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s> too, having engaged in various cordial and delightful conversation with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s> said to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: "Your faculties are serene, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, and your complexion is pure" — and so on, all as before. "Have you, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, realized any superhuman state, any noble distinction of knowledge and vision?" When this was said, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> said to the five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>: "Do not, monks, address the <s>Tathāgata</s> as 'Venerable.' May this not be to your harm, disadvantage, and suffering for a long time! O monks, I have realized the deathless and the path leading to the deathless. I am a <s>Buddha</s>, monks — omniscient, all-seeing, cooled, free from defilements, master of all <s>dharmas</s>. I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>, monks. Come quickly, listen, and practice! Lend your ears — I shall instruct and admonish you. If you are properly instructed and properly admonished by me, you too, having realized in this very life the freedom of mind from defilements and the freedom through wisdom, will declare: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done; we know that there is no further existence beyond this.' Was it not, monks, that you thought: 'Here comes the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, the lax one, the luxurious one, fallen from striving' — and so on as before — 'If you wish, please sit down?'" And when the words "Come, monks" were spoken, whatever marks and insignia of other sectarians they bore all vanished at that very instant. The triple robe and bowl appeared, and their hair was cut. It was as if the deportment of a monk ordained for a hundred years had been accomplished. And that itself was their going forth, that itself was their ordination and admission to monkhood. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastasyāṃ velāyāṃ pañcakā bhadravargīyā bhikṣavastathāgatasya caraṇayornipatyātyayaṃ deśayanti sma / tathāgatasyāntike śāstṛsaṃjñāṃ premaṃ ca prasādaṃ ca gauravaṃ cotpādayanti sma / gauravajātāśca bahuvicitrapuṣkariṇyāṃ tathāgatasya snānaparikarma kurvanti sma / snānapratyuttīrṇasya
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at that time the five <s>Bhadravargīya</s> monks fell at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet and confessed their transgressions. They generated in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s presence the recognition of a teacher, as well as affection, faith, and reverence. Filled with reverence, they performed the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bathing service at the beautiful and wondrous lotus-pond. After the <s>Tathāgata</s> had emerged from the bath,

body.text: ca bhikṣavastathāgatasyaitadabhavat - kasmin khalu pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairniṣadya dharmacakraṃ pravartitam? yasmiṃśca bhikṣavaḥ pṛthivīpradeśe pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhirdharmacakraṃ pravartitamabhūt, atha tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe saptaratnamayamāsanasahasraṃ prādurabhūt //
body.translated_text: O monks, this thought arose in the <s>Tathāgata</s>: "At which [spot] did the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones sit when they turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>?" And at the very spot where the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, had turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, a thousand seats made of the seven precious jewels appeared. //

body.text: atha tathāgataḥ pūrvakāṇāṃ tathāgatānāṃ gauraveṇa trīṇyāsanāni pradakṣiṇīkṛtya siṃha iva nirbhīścaturtha āsane paryaṅkamābhujya niṣīdati sma / pañcakā api bhikṣavastathāgatasya pādau śirobhirabhivandya tathāgatasya purato niṣeduḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, out of reverence for the former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, circumambulated three seats and, fearless like a lion, sat down cross-legged on the fourth seat. The five monks also bowed at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet with their heads and sat down before the <s>Tathāgata</s>. //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpāṃ kāyātprabhāṃ tathāgataḥ prāmuñcadyayā prabhayā ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturmahatāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt / tena cāvabhāsena yā api lokāntarikā aghā aghasphuṭā andhakāratamisrā yatremau candrasūryau evaṃmaharddhikāvevaṃ mahānubhāvāvevaṃ maheśākhyau ābhayā ābhāṃ varṇenaṃ varṇaṃ tejasā tejo nābhitapato nābhivirocataḥ / tatra ye sattvā upapannāste svakasvakamapi bāhuṃ prasāritaṃ na paśyanti sma, tatrāpi tasmin samaye mahata udārasyāvabhāsasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhut / ye ca tatra sattvā upapannāste tenāvabhāsena parisphuṭāḥ samānā anyonyaṃ paśyanti sma / anyonyaṃ saṃjānante sma / evaṃ cāhuḥ - anye 'pi kila bhoḥ sattvā ihopapannāḥ, anye 'pi kila bhoḥ sattvā ihopapannāḥ iti / ayaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāramaṣṭādaśamahānimittamabhūt - akampat prākampat saṃprākampat / avedhat prāvedhat saṃprāvedhat / acalat prācalat saṃprācalat / akṣubhyat prākṣubhyat saṃprākṣubhyat / araṇat prāraṇat saṃprāraṇat / agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat / ante 'vanamati sma, madhye unnamati sma / madhye 'vanamati sma ante unnamati sma / pūrvasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, paścimāyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / paścimāyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, pūrvasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, uttarasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / uttarasyāṃ diśyavanamati sma, dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśyunnamati sma / tasmiṃśca samaye harṣaṇīyāstoṣaṇīyāḥ premaṇīyāḥ prasādanīyā avalokanīyāḥ prahlādanīyā nirvarṇanīyā aprativarṇanīyā asecanīyā apratikūlā anuttrāsakarāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante sma / na ca kasyacitsattvasya tasmin kṣaṇe viheṭhā vā trāso vā bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vābhūt / na ca bhūyaḥ sūryacandramasorna śakrabrahmalokapālānāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe prabhāḥ prajñāyante sma / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokopapannāśca sattvāstasmin kṣaṇe vigataduḥkhā abhuvan sarvasukhasamarpitāḥ / na ca kasyacitsattvasya rāgo bādhate sma, dveṣo vā moho vā īrṣyā vā mātsaryaṃ vā māno vā mrakṣo vā mado vā krodho vā vyāpādo vā paridāho vā / sarvasattvāstasmin kṣaṇe maitracittāḥ hitacittāḥ parasparaṃ mātāpitṛsaṃjñino 'bhūvan / tataśca prabhāvyūhādimā gāthā niścaranti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at that time the <s>Tathāgata</s> released from his body such a radiance that this great trichiliocosm became suffused with a great splendor. And by that splendor, even the interstitial hells — those dark, gloomy, pitch-black [places] where the sun and moon, possessing such great supernatural power, such great might, such great sovereignty, do not illuminate with their light, do not brighten with their radiance, do not warm with their heat — and those beings who had been reborn there, who could not even see their own outstretched arms — even there, at that time, the manifestation of a great and sublime splendor occurred in the world. And those beings who had been reborn there, being pervaded by that splendor, could see one another and recognize one another, and they said: "Indeed, sirs, other beings too have been reborn here! Indeed, sirs, other beings too have been reborn here!" And this great trichiliocosm experienced six kinds of trembling with eighteen great portents — it quaked, violently quaked, and thoroughly quaked; it trembled, violently trembled, and thoroughly trembled; it shook, violently shook, and thoroughly shook; it rumbled, violently rumbled, and thoroughly rumbled; it roared, violently roared, and thoroughly roared; it thundered, violently thundered, and thoroughly thundered. The edges sank down and the middle rose up; the middle sank down and the edges rose up. The east sank and the west rose; the west sank and the east rose. The south sank and the north rose; the north sank and the south rose. And at that time, sounds were heard that were gladdening, satisfying, endearing, faith-inspiring, beautiful to behold, exhilarating, delightful, incomparable, pleasant, inoffensive, and free from causing terror. And at that moment no being experienced vexation, alarm, fear, or paralysis. And moreover, at that moment the radiance of the sun and moon, of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians could not be perceived. And all beings reborn in the hells, among animals, and in the world of <s>Yama</s> were at that moment free from suffering and endowed with all happiness. And no being was afflicted by desire, hatred, delusion, envy, avarice, pride, hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, malice, or torment. All beings at that moment had minds of loving-kindness, minds of beneficence, and regarded one another as mothers and fathers. And from that display of radiance, these verses issued forth —

children.text: yo 'sau tuṣitālayāccyutvā okrāntu mātukukṣau hi /
children.translated_text: "He who, having descended from the <s>Tuṣita</s> abode, entered his mother's womb,

children.text: jātaśca lumbinivane pratigṛhītaḥ śacīpatinā // Lal_26.7 //
children.translated_text: and was born in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, received by the Lord of <s>Śacī</s> (<s>Indra</s>)! // Lal_26.7 //

children.text: yaḥ siṃhavikramagatiḥ saptapadā vikramī asaṃmūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who walked with a lion's bold stride, taking seven steps, unconfused,

children.text: brahmasvarāmatha giraṃ pramumoca jagatyahaṃ śreṣṭhaḥ // Lal_26.8 //
children.translated_text: and uttered the word with a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice: 'I am the foremost in the world!' // Lal_26.8 //

children.text: caturo dvīpāṃstyaktvā pravrajitaḥ sarvasattvahitahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having renounced the four continents, he went forth for the benefit of all beings;

children.text: duṣkaratapaścaritvā upāgamadyena mahimaṇḍaḥ // Lal_26.9 //
children.translated_text: having practiced difficult austerities, he came to this great maṇḍala of the earth! // Lal_26.9 //

children.text: sabalaṃ nihatya māraṃ bodhiprāpto hitāya lokasya /
children.translated_text: "Having defeated <s>Māra</s> with his army and attained awakening for the welfare of the world,

children.text: vārāṇasīmupagato dharmacakraṃ pravartayitā // Lal_26.10 //
children.translated_text: he has come to <s>Vārāṇasī</s> — he shall turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_26.10 //

children.text: sabrahmaṇā saha surairadhyeṣṭo vartayasva śamacakram /
children.translated_text: "Entreated by <s>Brahmā</s> together with the gods: 'Turn the wheel of peace!' —

children.text: adhivāsitaṃ ca muninā loke kāruṇyamutpādya // Lal_26.11 //
children.translated_text: the sage consented, generating compassion for the world! // Lal_26.11 //

children.text: so 'yaṃ dṛḍhapratijño vārāṇasimupagato mṛgadāvam /
children.translated_text: "He of firm resolve has come to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the Deer Park;

children.text: cakraṃ hyanuttaramasau pravartayitātyadbhutaṃ śrīmān // Lal_26.12 //
children.translated_text: this glorious one shall turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel! // Lal_26.12 //

children.text: yaḥ śrotukāmu dharmaṃ yaḥ kalpanayutaiḥ samārjitu jinena /
children.translated_text: "Whoever is desirous of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, which was accumulated by the <s>Jina</s> through ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: śīghramasau tvaramāṇo āgacchatu dharmaśravaṇāya // Lal_26.13 //
children.translated_text: let him come quickly, hastening, for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>! // Lal_26.13 //

children.text: duravāpyaṃ mānuṣyaṃ buddhotpādaḥ sudurlabhā śraddhā /
children.translated_text: "Human birth is hard to obtain, the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is extremely rare, faith is [extremely rare],

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ ca dharmaśravaṇaṃ aṣṭākṣaṇavivarjana durāpāḥ // Lal_26.14 //
children.translated_text: and the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> is supreme — freedom from the eight unfavorable conditions is hard to attain! // Lal_26.14 //

children.text: prāptāśca te 'dya sarve buddhotpādaḥ kṣaṇastathā śraddhā /
children.translated_text: "And all these have been obtained by you today — the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, the opportune moment, and faith;

children.text: dharmaśravaṇaśca varaḥ pramādamakhilaṃ vivarjayata // Lal_26.15 //
children.translated_text: and the supreme hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> — abandon all heedlessness! // Lal_26.15 //

children.text: bhavati kadācidavasthā yaḥ kalpanayutairna śrūyate dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "There is a condition when for ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> the <s>Dharma</s> is not heard;

children.text: saṃprāptaḥ sa ca vādya pramādamakhilaṃ vivarjayata // Lal_26.16 //
children.translated_text: that [moment] has now arrived today — abandon all heedlessness! // Lal_26.16 //

children.text: bhaumādīn devagaṇān saṃcodayatī ca brahmaparyantām /
children.translated_text: "[This voice] urges the hosts of gods, from the earthly gods up to <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: āyāta laghuṃ sarve vartayitā nāyako hyamṛtacakram // Lal_26.17 //
children.translated_text: 'Come quickly, all! The Guide shall turn the wheel of the deathless!' // Lal_26.17 //

children.text: saṃcoditāśca mahatā devaghoṣeṇa tatkṣaṇaṃ sarve /
children.translated_text: "And urged by that great divine proclamation, all at that instant,

children.text: tyaktvā devasamṛddhiṃ prāptā buddhasya te pārśve // Lal_26.18 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned their divine splendor, arrived at the <s>Buddha</s>'s side." // Lal_26.18 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo bhaumaidevairvārāṇasyāṃ ṛpipatane mṛgadāve dharmacakrapravartanārthaṃ tathāgatasya mahāmaṇḍalamātro 'dhiṣṭhito 'bhūt citro darśanīyo vipulo vistīrṇaḥ saptayojanaśatānyāyāmo vistāreṇa / upariṣṭāśca devaiśchatradhvajapatākāvitānasamalaṃkṛtaṃ gaganatalaṃ samalaṃkṛtamabhūt / kāmāvacarai rūpāvacaraiśca devaputraiścaturaśītisiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi tathāgatāyopanāmitānyabhūvan - iha niṣadya bhagavān dharmacakraṃ pravartayatu asmākamanukampāmupādāyeti //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, by the earthly gods, at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Sages' Fall), in the Deer Park, for the purpose of the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, a great <s>maṇḍala</s> was prepared for the <s>Tathāgata</s> — splendid, beautiful, vast, and extensive, seven hundred <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth. And above, the expanse of the sky was adorned by the gods with parasols, banners, pennants, and canopies. And by gods of the Desire Realm and the Form Realm, eighty-four hundred thousand lion-thrones were offered to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: "May the Blessed One sit here and turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, out of compassion for us!" //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastasmin samaye pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarābhyo digbhya ūrdhvamadhaḥ samantāddaśabhyo digbhyo bahavo bodhisattvakoṭyaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānasamanvāgatā āgatya tathāgatasya caraṇayornipatya dharmacakrapravartanāyādhyeṣante sma / ye ceha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau śakro vā brahmā vā lokapālā
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at that time, from the eastern, southern, western, northern, upper, lower — from all ten directions — many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, endowed with their former vows, came and, falling at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet, entreated him to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. And those in this great trichiliocosm — whether <s>Śakra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s> or the World-Guardians

body.text: vā tadanye vā maheśākhyamaheśākhyā devaputrāste 'pi sarve tathāgatasya caraṇayoḥ śirobhiḥ praṇipatya tathāgatamadhyeṣante sma dharmacakrapravartanāya - pravartayatu bhagavān dharmacakram, pravartayatu sugato dharmacakraṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / yajasva bhagavan dharmayajñam, pravarṣa mahādharmavarṣam, ucchrepaya mahādharmadhvajam, prapūraya mahādharmaśaṅkham, pratāḍaya mahādharmadundubhim //
body.translated_text: or others, both the <s>Maheśākhya</s> and non-<s>Maheśākhya</s> god-sons — they all bowed their heads at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s feet and entreated the <s>Tathāgata</s> to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>: "May the Blessed One turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>! May the <s>Sugata</s> turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of gods and humans! Perform, O Blessed One, the sacrifice of <s>Dharma</s>! Rain down the great rain of <s>Dharma</s>! Raise the great banner of <s>Dharma</s>! Fill the great conch of <s>Dharma</s>! Strike the great drum of <s>Dharma</s>!" //

body.text: tatredamucyate /
body.translated_text: Here the following was said: /

children.text: trisahasra ito bahu brahma sureśvara pāla tathā
children.translated_text: From this trichiliocosm, many <s>Brahmās</s>, lords of gods, and <s>Pālas</s>

children.text: upagamya jinasya kramebhi nipatya udāhariṣu /
children.translated_text: approached the <s>Jina</s> step by step, prostrated, and declared: /

children.text: smara pūrvapratijñāṃ mahāmuni yā tvaya vāca kṛtā
children.translated_text: "Remember your former vow, O great sage — that which you spoke with your voice:

children.text: ahu jyeṣṭhu viśiṣṭu prajāya kariṣye dukhasya kṣayam // Lal_26.19 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall be the eldest, the supreme among beings — I shall make an end of suffering!'" // Lal_26.19 //

children.text: tvaya dharṣitu mārū sasainyu drumendri sthihitva mune
children.translated_text: "By you was <s>Māra</s> with his army vanquished, O sage, standing at the king of trees;

children.text: varabodhi vibuddha suśānti nipātita kleśadrumāḥ /
children.translated_text: having awakened to the excellent <s>bodhi</s>, supreme peace, you have felled the trees of <s>kleśas</s>. /

children.text: abhiprāyu prapūrṇa aśeṣa ya cintita kalpaśatā
children.translated_text: Your purpose is completely fulfilled — all that was contemplated for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: janatāṃ prasamīkṣya anāyika vartaya cakravaram // Lal_26.20 //
children.translated_text: beholding the people without a leader, turn the wheel supreme!" // Lal_26.20 //

children.text: sugatasya prabhāya prabhāsita kṣetrasahasraśatā
children.translated_text: "By the <s>Sugata</s>'s radiance, hundreds of thousands of fields are illuminated;

children.text: bahavaḥ śatabuddhasutāśca upāgata ṛddhibalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: many hundreds of <s>Buddha</s>-sons have come by their powers of <s>ṛddhi</s>. /

children.text: vividhāṃ sugatasya karitvana pūja mahānicayāṃ
children.translated_text: Having made manifold and great heaps of worship to the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: stavayiṃsu tathāgatu bhūtaguṇebhi adhyeṣitu kāruṇikam // Lal_26.21 //
children.translated_text: they praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with true qualities, entreating the Compassionate One." // Lal_26.21 //

children.text: karuṇāghana vidyutaprajña vipaśyana vāyusamā
children.translated_text: "[You are] a cloud of compassion, with lightning of wisdom, with insight like the wind;

children.text: abhigarjitu kalpasahasra nimantritu sarvajagat /
children.translated_text: having thundered for thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, having invited the entire world — /

children.text: aṣṭāṅgikamārgajalo dhara varṣa samehi jagasya tṛṣāṃ
children.translated_text: O rain-cloud bearing the water of the eightfold noble path, rain down! Quench the thirst of the world!

children.text: balaindriyadhyānavimokṣa vivardhaya sasyadhanam // Lal_26.22 //
children.translated_text: With powers, faculties, <s>dhyānas</s>, and liberations, make the harvest of grain increase!" // Lal_26.22 //

children.text: bahukalpasahasra suśikṣitu śūnyatattva sthitā
children.translated_text: "For many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, you trained well — established in the truth of emptiness;

children.text: samudānitu dharmaju bheṣaju jānitu sattvacarī /
children.translated_text: you have gathered the medicine born of <s>Dharma</s>, you know the conduct of beings. /

children.text: janatā iya vyādhiśatebhi upadruta kleśagaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: These people are afflicted by hundreds of diseases, assailed by hosts of <s>kleśas</s>;

children.text: jinavaidya pramocaya vartaya dharmacakravaram // Lal_26.23 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s>-physician, liberate them! Turn the supreme wheel of <s>Dharma</s>!" // Lal_26.23 //

children.text: ṣaḍi pāramite cirarātru vivardhitu kośu tvayā
children.translated_text: "For a long time you have cultivated your treasury of the six <s>pāramitās</s>;

children.text: asamaṃ tu acālyu praṇītu susaṃcitu dharmadhanam /
children.translated_text: unequalled, unshakable, sublime — you have well accumulated the wealth of <s>Dharma</s>. /

children.text: praja sarva anātha daridra anāyika dṛṣṭva imāṃ
children.translated_text: Seeing these people — all unprotected, destitute, without a leader —

children.text: vicaraṃ dhana sapta vināyaka cakra pravartayahī // Lal_26.24 //
children.translated_text: distribute the seven treasures, O Guide! Turn the wheel!" // Lal_26.24 //

children.text: dhanadhānya hiraṇyasuvarṇa tathaiva ca vastra śubhā
children.translated_text: "Wealth, grain, gold and silver, likewise beautiful garments,

children.text: vara puṣpa vilepana dhūpana cūrṇa gṛhāśca varāḥ /
children.translated_text: fine flowers, ointments, incense, powders, and excellent houses — /

children.text: antaḥpura rājya priyātmaja tyakta praharṣayato
children.translated_text: inner chambers, kingdoms, beloved sons — all these you abandoned with joy,

children.text: jina bodhi gaveṣata sātivibuddha pravartaya cakravaram // Lal_26.25 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s>, seeking <s>bodhi</s>, supremely awakened — turn the wheel supreme!" // Lal_26.25 //

children.text: tatha śīlu akhaṇḍu akalmaṣu rakṣitu kalpaśatāṃ
children.translated_text: "Likewise, morality — unbroken, unstained — you guarded for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sada kṣānti subhāvita vīrya alīnu abhūṣi tava /
children.translated_text: patience was always well-cultivated, vigor unwavering — such was yours. /

children.text: vara dhyāna abhijña vipaśyana prajña upekṣa mune
children.translated_text: Supreme <s>dhyāna</s>, superknowledges, insight, wisdom, equanimity, O sage —

children.text: paripūrṇa manoratha nirjvara vartaya cakravaram // Lal_26.26 //
children.translated_text: your heart's desire is fulfilled, you are free from affliction — turn the wheel supreme!" // Lal_26.26 //

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartī nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāṃ cakraṃ sarvaratnapratyuptaṃ sarvaratnapraśobhitaṃ nānāratnālaṃkāravyūhavibhūṣitaṃ sahasrāraṃ sahasraraśmi sanābhikaṃ sanemikaṃ sapuṣpadāmaṃ sahemajālaṃ sakiṅkiṇījālaṃ sagandhahastaṃ sapūrṇakumbhaṃ sanandikāvartaṃ sasvastikālaṃkṛtaṃ nānāraṅgaraktadivyavastropaśobhitaṃ divyapuṣpagandhamālyavilepanānuliptaṃ sarvākāravaropetaṃ tathāgatāya dharmacakrapravartanāya pūrvapraṇidhānābhinirhṛtaṃ bodhisattvāśayaviśodhitaṃ tathāgatapūjārhaṃ sarvatathāgatasamanvāhṛtaṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānāvilopitaṃ pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pratyeṣitaṃ pravartitapūrvaṃ ca dharmacakramupanāmayati sma / upanāmya ca kṛtāñjalipuṭastathāgatamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, at that moment the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Sahacittotpāda-dharmacakrapravartin</s> ("He who turns the Dharma-wheel simultaneously with the arising of the thought") presented to the <s>Tathāgata</s> a wheel for turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> — adorned with all jewels, resplendent with all jewels, decorated with ornamental arrays of various gems, having a thousand spokes, a thousand rays, with hub and rim, with garlands of flowers, with a golden net, with a net of bells, with a perfumed handle, with a full vase, with <s>nandikāvarta</s> [auspicious marks], adorned with <s>svastika</s> patterns, beautified with divine fabrics dyed in various colors, anointed with divine flowers, incense, garlands, and unguents, endowed with all the finest marks, produced by the prior vows of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for turning the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, purified by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration, worthy of <s>Tathāgata</s>-worship, blessed by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, not destroyed by the empowerment of all Buddhas, previously sought out and turned by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. Having presented it, with palms joined, he praised the <s>Tathāgata</s> with these verses —

children.text: dīpaṃkareṇa yada vyākṛtu śuddhasattvo buddho bhaviṣyasi hi tvaṃ narasiṃhasiṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "When <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> predicted [you], O pure being — 'You shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, a lion among men!' —

children.text: tasmiṃ samāsi praṇidhī iyamevarūpā saṃbodhiprāptu ahu dharma adhyeṣayeyam // Lal_26.27 //
children.translated_text: at that time you made this very vow: 'Having attained <s>saṃbodhi</s>, I shall entreat the <s>Dharma</s>!'" // Lal_26.27 //

children.text: na ca śakya sarvi gaṇanāya anupraveṣṭuṃ ye āgatā daśadiśebhirihāgrasattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: "And the foremost beings who have come here from the ten directions cannot all be counted or enumerated;

children.text: adhyeṣi śākyakulanandana dharmacakre prahvā kṛtāñjalipuṭāścaraṇau nipatya // Lal_26.28 //
children.translated_text: they entreat the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> clan to turn the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, bowed down with palms joined, prostrating at his feet!" // Lal_26.28 //

children.text: yā bodhimaṇḍi prakṛtā ca surairviyūhā yā vā viyūha kṛta sarvajinātmajebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "The adornments at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> made by the gods, and the arrays created by all the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: sā sarva saṃsthita viyūha ti dharmacakre paripūrṇakalpa bhaṇamānu kṣayaṃ na gacchet // Lal_26.29 //
children.translated_text: all those abiding arrays would not come to exhaustion even if described for a full <s>kalpa</s>!" // Lal_26.29 //

children.text: trisahasri loki gaganaṃ sphuṭa devasaṃghaiḥ dharaṇītalaṃ asurakinnaramānuṣaiśca /
children.translated_text: "In the trichiliocosm, the sky is filled with hosts of gods, and the surface of the earth with <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and humans;

children.text: utkāsaśabdu napi śrūyati tanmuhūrtaṃ sarvi prasannamanaso jinamabhyudīkṣan // Lal_26.30 //
children.translated_text: not even a clearing-of-throat sound is heard at that moment — all, with joyful minds, gaze upon the <s>Jina</s>!" // Lal_26.30 //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavastathāgato rātryāḥ prathame yāme tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati sma / rātryā madhyame yāme saṃrañjanīyāṃ kathāṃ pravartayati sma / rātryāḥ paścime yāme pañcakān bhadravargīyānāmantryaitadavocat - dvāvimau bhikṣavaḥ pravrajitasyāntāvakramau / yaśca kāmeṣu kāmasukhallikā yogo hīno grāmyaḥ pārthagjaniko nālamāryo 'narthopasaṃhito nāyatyāṃ brahmacaryāya na nirvide na virāgāya na nirodhāya nābhijñāya na saṃbodhaye na nirvāṇāya saṃvartate / yā ceyamamadhyamā pratipadā ātmakāyaklamathānuyogo duḥkho 'narthopasaṃhito dṛṣṭadharmaduḥkhaścāyatyāṃ ca duḥkhavipākaḥ / etau ca bhikṣavo dvāvantāvanupagamya madhyamayaiva pratipadā tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayati - yaduta samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvāk samyakkarmāntaḥ samyagājīvaḥ samyagvyāyāmaḥ samyaksmṛtiḥ samyaksamādhiriti / catvārīmāni bhikṣava āryasatyāni / katamāni catvāri? duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasamudayo duḥkhanirodho duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipat / tatra katamad duḥkham? jātirapi duḥkhaṃ jarāpi duḥkhaṃ vyādhirapi duḥkhaṃ maraṇamapi apriyasaṃprayogo 'pi priyaviprayogo 'pi duḥkham / yadapi icchan paryeṣamāṇo na labhate tadapi duḥkham / saṃkṣepāt pañcopādānaskadhā duḥkham / idamucyate duḥkham / tatra katamo duḥkhasamudayaḥ? yeyaṃ tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī ayamucyate duḥkhasamudayaḥ / tatra katamo duḥkhanirodhaḥ? yo 'syā eva tṛṣṇāyāḥ punarbhavikyā nandīrāgasahagatāyāstatratatrābhinandinyā janikāyā nirvartikāyā aśeṣo virāgo nirodhaḥ ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ / tatra katamā duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipat? eṣa evāryāṣṭāṅgamārgaḥ / tadyathā / samyagdṛṣṭiryāvatsamyaksamādhiriti / idamucyate duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadāryasatyamiti / imāni bhikṣavaścatvāryāryasatyāni / iti duḥkhamiti me bhikṣavaḥ purvamaśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikārādbahulīkārājjñānamutpannaṃ cakṣurutpannaṃ vidyotpannā bhūrirutpannā meghotpannā prajñotpannā ālokaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / ayaṃ duḥkhasamudaya iti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikārādbahulīkārājjñānamutpannaṃ cakṣurutpannaṃ vidyotpannā bhūrirutpannā meghotpannā prajñotpannā ālokaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / ayaṃ duḥkhanirodha iti me bhikṣavaḥ sarvaṃ pūrvavadyāvadālokaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavadeva peyālaṃ yāvadālokaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / yatkhalvidaṃ duḥkhaṃ parijñeyamiti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavadeva peyālaṃ yāvadālokaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / sa khalvayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ prahātavya iti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśrateṣu dharmeṣu sarvaṃ yāvadāloka iti / sa khalvayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavya iti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavadyāvadāloka iti / sā khalviyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadbhāvayitavyeti pūrvavadyāvadāloka iti / tatkhalvidaṃ duḥkhaṃ parijñātamiti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśrateṣu iti peyālam / sa khalvayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ prahīṇa iti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśruteti peyālam / sa khalvayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛta iti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśruteti peyālam / sā khalviyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadbhāviteti me bhikṣavaḥ pūrvamaśruteṣu dharmeṣu yoniśomanasikārādbahulīkārājjñānamutpannaṃ cakṣurutpannaṃ bhūrirutpannā vidyotpannā medhotpannā prajñotpannā ālokaḥ prādūrbhūtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the first watch of the night, consented through silence. In the middle watch of the night, he delivered a discourse of edification. In the last watch of the night, he addressed the group of five <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, saying: "There are, O monks, two extremes that should not be pursued by one who has gone forth. What are they? That which is devotion to sense-pleasures and sensual indulgence — which is low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, unprofitable, and does not conduce to <s>nirveda</s> (disenchantment), to <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), to <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), to <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), to <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening), or to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And that which is this middle path — self-mortification of one's own body, which is painful, unprofitable, productive of suffering in the present and yielding suffering as its fruit in the future. Avoiding these two extremes, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> by the middle path — namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. These, O monks, are the four noble truths. What four? Suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Therein, what is suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, illness is suffering, death is suffering; association with the unpleasant is suffering, separation from the pleasant is suffering; not obtaining what one seeks — that too is suffering. In brief, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering. This is called suffering. Therein, what is the origin of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, finding pleasure here and there — this is called the origin of suffering. Therein, what is the cessation of suffering? It is the complete fading away and cessation, the relinquishment, abandonment, and release from that very craving for renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, finding pleasure here and there — this is the cessation of suffering. Therein, what is the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this noble eightfold path — namely: right view up to right concentration. This is called the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. These, O monks, are the four noble truths. 'This is suffering' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, through proper mental attention and sustained application, knowledge arose in me, vision arose, understanding arose, insight arose, intelligence arose, wisdom arose, light appeared. 'This is the origin of suffering' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, through proper mental attention and sustained application, knowledge arose in me, vision arose, understanding arose, insight arose, intelligence arose, wisdom arose, light appeared. 'This is the cessation of suffering' — thus, O monks, all as before up to: light appeared. 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering' — thus, O monks, as before in abbreviated form up to: light appeared. 'This suffering is to be fully known' — thus, O monks, as before in abbreviated form up to: light appeared. 'This origin of suffering is to be abandoned' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, all up to: light [appeared]. 'This cessation of suffering is to be directly realized' — thus, O monks, as before up to: light [appeared]. 'This path leading to the cessation of suffering is to be cultivated' — as before up to: light [appeared]. 'This suffering has been fully known' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, in abbreviated form. 'This origin of suffering has been abandoned' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, in abbreviated form. 'This cessation of suffering has been directly realized' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, in abbreviated form. 'This path leading to the cessation of suffering has been cultivated' — thus, O monks, regarding things previously unheard, through proper mental attention and sustained application, knowledge arose in me, vision arose, insight arose, intelligence arose, wisdom arose, light appeared. //

body.text: iti hi bhikṣavo yāvadeva me eṣu caturṣvāryasatyeṣu yoniśo manasi kurvato evaṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ jñānadarśanamutpadyate, na tāvadahaṃ bhikṣavo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'smi iti pratijñāsiṣam / na ca me jñānadarśanamutpadyate / yataśca me bhikṣava eṣu caturṣvāryasatyeṣvevaṃ triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ jñānadarśanamutpannam, akopyā ca me cetovimuktiḥ, prajñāvimuktiśca sākṣātkṛtā, tato 'haṃ bhikṣavo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'smi iti pratijñāsiṣam / jñānadarśanaṃ me udapādi / kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryam, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyam, nāparasmādbhavaṃ prajānāmi //
body.translated_text: Thus, O monks, so long as my knowledge and vision regarding these four noble truths with their three turnings and twelve aspects had not yet arisen through proper attention, I did not claim, O monks, that I had fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening, nor had my knowledge and vision arisen. But from the time, O monks, when my knowledge and vision regarding these four noble truths with their three turnings and twelve aspects had arisen, and my <s>cetovimukti</s> (liberation of mind) became unshakable, and my <s>prajñāvimukti</s> (liberation through wisdom) was directly realized — from that time, O monks, I claimed that I had fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect and complete awakening. Knowledge and vision arose in me: 'Destroyed is my birth, lived is the holy life, done is what was to be done — I know no further becoming!' //

body.text: tatredamucyate /
body.translated_text: Here the following was said: /

children.text: vācāya brahmaruta kinnaragarjitāya aṃśaiḥ sahasranayutebhi samudgatāya /
children.translated_text: With a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s speech, like a <s>Kinnara</s>'s roar, endowed with thousands and ten-thousands of qualities,

children.text: bahukalpakoṭi sada satyasubhāvitāya kauṇḍinyamālapati śākyamuniḥ svayaṃbhūḥ // Lal_26.31 //
children.translated_text: always well-cultivated in truth for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Self-Arisen, [addressed] <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the chief: // Lal_26.31 //

children.text: cakṣuranityamadhruvaṃ tatha śrota ghrāṇaṃ jihvā pi kāya mana duḥkhā anātma śūnyā /
children.translated_text: "The eye is impermanent and unstable, likewise ear and nose; tongue, body, and mind are suffering, selfless, and empty;

children.text: jaḍāsvabhāva tṛṇakuḍma ivā nirīhā naivātra ātma na naro na ca jīvamasti // Lal_26.32 //
children.translated_text: inert by nature, like grass or a wall, without agency — herein there is no self, no person, and no living being!" // Lal_26.32 //

children.text: hetuṃ pratītya imi saṃbhuta sarvadharmā atyantadṛṣṭivigatā gaganaprakāśā /
children.translated_text: "Dependent on causes, all these <s>dharmas</s> arise — free from the view of eternalism, like space;

children.text: na ca kārako 'sti tatha naiva ca vedako 'sti na ca karma paśyati kṛtaṃ hyaśubhaṃ śubhaṃ vā // Lal_26.33 //
children.translated_text: there is no doer here, likewise no experiencer — and karma does not perceive the good or evil that is done!" // Lal_26.33 //

children.text: skandhā pratītya samudeti hi duḥkhamevaṃ saṃbhonti tṛṣṇa salilena vivardhamānā /
children.translated_text: "Dependent on the <s>skandhas</s>, suffering arises thus — [the aggregates] grow, nourished by the water of craving;

children.text: mārgeṇa dharmasamatāya vipaśyamānā atyantakṣīṇa kṣayadharmatayā niruddhāḥ // Lal_26.34 //
children.translated_text: seeing through the path of the equality of <s>dharmas</s>, they are utterly exhausted, ceased by the nature of destruction!" // Lal_26.34 //

children.text: saṃkalpakalpajanitena ayoniśena bhavate avidya na pi saṃbhavako 'sya kaści /
children.translated_text: "Through improper mental construction born of thought and conceptualization, ignorance arises — yet there is no one who produces it; /

children.text: saṃskārahetu dadate na ca saṃkramo 'sti vijñānamudbhavati saṃkramaṇaṃ pratītya // Lal_26.35 //
children.translated_text: Conditioned formations give the cause, yet there is no transmigration; consciousness arises dependent on a transition [that itself does not transmigrate]. // Lal_26.35 //

children.text: vijñāna nāma tatha ca rūpa samutthitāsti nāme ca rūpi samudenti ṣaḍindriyāṇi /
children.translated_text: From consciousness arise name-and-form; from name-and-form arise the six sense-faculties;

children.text: ṣaḍindiyairnipatito iti sparśa uktaḥ sparśena tisra anuvartati vedanā ca // Lal_26.36 //
children.translated_text: from the six sense-faculties comes what is called contact; from contact follow the three [kinds of] feeling. // Lal_26.36 //

children.text: yatkiṃci vedayitu sarva satṛṣṇa uktā tṛṣṇāta sarva upajāyati duḥkhaskandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is felt — all of that is said to be accompanied by craving; from craving the entire mass of suffering arises;

children.text: upādānato bhavati sarva bhavapravṛttiḥ bhavapratyayā ca samudeti hi jātirasya // Lal_26.37 //
children.translated_text: from clinging comes all the activity of existence; and conditioned by existence, birth arises for this [being]. // Lal_26.37 //

children.text: jātīnidāna jaravyādhidukhāni bhonti upapatti naika vividhā bhavapañjare 'smin /
children.translated_text: Having birth as their cause, old age, disease, and sufferings arise — manifold and various rebirths in this cage of existence;

children.text: evameṣa sarva iti pratyayato jagasya na ca ātma pudgalu na saṃkramako 'sti kaści // Lal_26.38 //
children.translated_text: thus all this arises from conditions for the world — yet there is no self, no person, and no transmigrator whatsoever. // Lal_26.38 //

children.text: yasminna kalpu na vikalpu yonimāhuḥ yadyoniśo bhavati na tatra avidya kāci /
children.translated_text: That in which there is no conceptual construction nor discrimination — that they call the source; when arising from this source, there is no ignorance whatsoever;

children.text: yasminnirodhu bhavatīha avidyatāyāḥ sarve bhavāṅga kṣayakṣīṇa kṣayaṃ niruddhā // Lal_26.39 //
children.translated_text: when here the cessation of ignorance occurs, all the links of existence, decayed and diminished, cease in destruction. // Lal_26.39 //

children.text: evameṣa pratyayata buddha tathāgatena tena svayaṃbhu svakamātmanu vyākaroti /
children.translated_text: Thus this [truth of] dependent origination was awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; therefore the Self-Arisen One proclaims it concerning his own self:

children.text: na skandha āyatana dhātu vademi buddhaṃ nānyatra hetvavagamādbhavatīha buddhaḥ // Lal_26.40 //
children.translated_text: 'I do not declare that the <s>Buddha</s> is the aggregates, sense-bases, or elements — nor does a <s>Buddha</s> come to be here apart from the comprehension of causes.' // Lal_26.40 //

children.text: bhūmirna cātra paratīrthika niḥsṛtānāṃ śūnyā pravādi iha īdṛśa dharmayoge /
children.translated_text: There is no ground here for those who have gone forth to other sects — empty are their declarations in this engagement with the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: ye pūrvabuddhacaritā suviśuddhasattvāḥ te śaknuvanti imi dharma vijānanāya // Lal_26.41 //
children.translated_text: those of supremely pure being who have practiced under former <s>Buddhas</s> — they are able to comprehend these <s>dharmas</s>. // Lal_26.41 //

children.text: evaṃ hi dvādaśākāraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam /
children.translated_text: Thus indeed the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of <s>Dharma</s>) was turned in its twelve aspects;

children.text: kauṇḍinyena ca ājñātaṃ nirvṛttā ratanā trayaḥ // Lal_26.42 //
children.translated_text: and it was understood by <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> — the Three Jewels were established. // Lal_26.42 //

children.text: buddho dharmaśca saṃghaśca ityetadratanatrayam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> — this is the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>);

children.text: parasparāṃ gataḥ śabdo yāvad brahmapurālayam // Lal_26.43 //
children.translated_text: the sound went forth in all directions, reaching up to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>. // Lal_26.43 //

children.text: vartitaṃ virajaṃ cakraṃ lokanāthena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: The stainless wheel was turned by the Protector, the Lord of the World;

children.text: utpannā ratanā trīṇi loke paramadurlabhā // Lal_26.44 //
children.translated_text: the Three Jewels arose in the world — supremely rare. // Lal_26.44 //

children.text: kauṇḍinyaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā pañcakāścaiva bhikṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> as the first, the five monks,

children.text: ṣaṣṭīnāṃ devakoṭīnāṃ dharmacakṣurviśodhitam // Lal_26.45 //
children.translated_text: and sixty <s>koṭis</s> of gods — their <s>Dharma</s>-eye was purified. // Lal_26.45 //

children.text: anye cāśītikoṭyastu rūpadhātukadevatāḥ /
children.translated_text: And another eighty <s>koṭis</s> of Form Realm deities —

children.text: teṣāṃ viśodhitaṃ cakṣu dharmacakrapravartane // Lal_26.46 //
children.translated_text: their [<s>Dharma</s>-]eye was purified at the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s>. // Lal_26.46 //

children.text: caturaśītisahasrāṇi manuṣyāṇāṃ samāgatā /
children.translated_text: Eighty-four thousand human beings had assembled;

children.text: teṣāṃ viśodhitaṃ cakṣu muktā sarvebhi durgatī // Lal_26.47 //
children.translated_text: their [<s>Dharma</s>-]eye was purified — they were freed from all bad destinations. // Lal_26.47 //

children.text: daśadiśatu ananta buddhasvaro gacchi tasmiṃ kṣaṇe
children.translated_text: In the ten directions went the infinite <s>Buddha</s>-voice at that moment;

children.text: ruta madhura manojña saṃśrūyante cāntarīkṣe śubha /
children.translated_text: sweet, pleasant, auspicious sounds were heard in the sky:

children.text: eṣa daśabalena śākyarṣiṇā dharmacakrottamaṃ
children.translated_text: 'This supreme <s>Dharmacakra</s>, by the Ten-Powered One, the sage of the <s>Śākyas</s>,

children.text: ṛṣipatanamupetya vārāṇasī vartito nānyathā // Lal_26.48 //
children.translated_text: having reached <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Deer Park) at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, has been turned — and not otherwise!' // Lal_26.48 //

children.text: daśa diśita yi keci buddhaśatā sarvi tūṣṇībhutāḥ
children.translated_text: In the ten directions, all the hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s> had fallen silent;

children.text: teṣa muninaye upasthāyakāḥ sarvi pṛcchī jināṃ /
children.translated_text: the attendants of those lords of sages all asked the <s>Jinas</s>:

children.text: kimiti daśabalebhi dharmākathā chinna śrutvā rūtaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Why have the Ten-Powered Ones cut off their <s>Dharma</s>-discourse? Having heard the sound,

children.text: sādhu bhaṇata śīghra kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tūṣṇībhāvena sthitāḥ // Lal_26.49 //
children.translated_text: please tell us quickly — for what reason do they stand in silence?' // Lal_26.49 //

children.text: purvabhavaśatebhi vīryābalai bodhi samudāniyā
children.translated_text: 'Through the vigor and strength of hundreds of former existences, awakening was accumulated;

children.text: bahava śatasahasra paścānmukhā bodhisattvā kṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were inspired to follow him;

children.text: tena hitakareṇa uttaptatā prāpta bodhiḥ śivā
children.translated_text: by that benefactor, burning with zeal, the auspicious awakening was attained —

children.text: cakra triparivarta prāvartitā tena tūṣṇībhutāḥ // Lal_26.50 //
children.translated_text: the wheel of three turnings was set in motion — therefore they have fallen silent.' // Lal_26.50 //

children.text: imu vacana śruṇitva teṣāṃ munīsattvakoṭyaḥ śatā
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of noble beings of those sages,

children.text: maitrabala janitva saṃprasthitā agrabodhiṃ śivām /
children.translated_text: generating the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), set out toward the supreme, auspicious awakening:

children.text: vayamapi anuśikṣi tasyā mune vīryasthāmodgataṃ
children.translated_text: 'We too shall train after the example of that sage, arisen in the vigor of resolve —

children.text: kṣipra bhavema loki lokottamā dharmacakṣurdadāḥ // Lal_26.51 //
children.translated_text: may we swiftly become supreme in the world, bestowers of the <s>Dharma</s>-eye!' // Lal_26.51 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ime bhagavan daśadiglokadhātusaṃnipatitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhagavataḥ sakāśāddharmacakrapravartanavikurvaṇasya praveśaṃ śrotukāmāḥ / tatsādhu bhagavān deśayatu tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ kiyadrūpaṃ tathāgatena dharmacakraṃ pravartitam? bhagavānāha - gambhīraṃ maitreya dharmacakraṃ grāhānupalabdhitvāt / durdarśaṃ taccakraṃ dvayavigatatvāt / duranubodhaṃ taccakraṃ manasikārāmanasikāratvāt / durvijñānaṃ taccakraṃ jñānavijñānasamatānubaddhatvāt / anāvilaṃ taccakraṃ anāvaraṇavimokṣapratilabdhatvāt / sūkṣmaṃ taccakraṃ anupamopanyāsavigatatvāt / sāraṃ taccakraṃ vajropamajñānapratilabdhatvāt / abhedyaṃ taccakraṃ pūrvāntasaṃbhavatvāt / aprapañcaṃ taccakraṃ sarvaprapañcopārambhavigatatvāt /
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'These <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> assembled from the world-systems of the ten directions wish to hear from the Blessed One the entry into the miraculous display of turning the <s>Dharmacakra</s>. May the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, please teach — of what nature was the <s>Dharmacakra</s> turned by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Profound is that <s>Dharmacakra</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, because there is no apprehension of a grasper. Hard to see is that wheel, because it is devoid of duality. Hard to comprehend is that wheel, because of the [identity of] attention and non-attention. Hard to know is that wheel, because it is bound to the equality of knowledge and consciousness. Undefiled is that wheel, because unobstructed liberation has been attained. Subtle is that wheel, because it is devoid of incomparable presentation. Essential is that wheel, because <s>vajra</s>-like knowledge has been attained. Indestructible is that wheel, because of its arising from the beginningless past. Without conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>) is that wheel, because it is devoid of all grasping at conceptual proliferation.'

body.text: akopyaṃ taccakraṃ atyantaniṣṭhatvāt / sarvatrānugataṃ taccakraṃ ākāśasadṛśatvāt / tatkhalu punarmaitreya dharmacakraṃ sarvadharmaprakṛtisvabhāvaṃ saṃdarśanavibhavacakraṃ anutpādānirodhāsaṃbhavacakraṃ anālayacakraṃ akalpāvikalpadharmanayavistīraṇacakraṃ śūnyatācakraṃ animittacakraṃ apraṇihitacakraṃ anabhisaṃskāracakraṃ vivekacakraṃ virāgacakraṃ virodhacakraṃ tathāgatānubodhacakraṃ dharmadhātvasaṃbhedacakram / bhūtakoṭyavikopanacakraṃ asaṅgānāvaraṇacakraṃ pratītyāvatārobhayāntadṛṣṭisamatikramaṇacakraṃ anantamadhyadharmadhātvavikopanacakraṃ anābhogabuddhakāryapratipraśrabdhacakraṃ apravṛtyabhinirvṛtticakraṃ atyantānupalabdhicakraṃ anāyūhāniryūhacakraṃ
body.translated_text: 'Unshakable is that wheel, because of its absolute finality. Pervading everywhere is that wheel, because it is like space. Furthermore, O <s>Maitreya</s>, that <s>Dharmacakra</s> has the inherent nature of the essential nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; it is the wheel of the display of demonstration; the wheel of non-arising, non-cessation, and non-occurrence; the wheel without substratum; the wheel of the expansion of the <s>dharma</s>-method of non-construction and non-discrimination; the wheel of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>); the wheel of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>); the wheel of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>); the wheel of non-fabrication; the wheel of seclusion (<s>viveka</s>); the wheel of dispassion (<s>virāga</s>); the wheel of cessation (<s>virodha</s>); the wheel of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s awakening; the wheel of the non-differentiation of the <s>dharma</s>-realm (<s>dharmadhātu</s>); the wheel of the unshakability of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>); the wheel of non-attachment and non-obstruction; the wheel of entering dependent origination and transcending the views of both extremes; the wheel of the unshakability of the <s>dharma</s>-realm which has neither end nor middle; the wheel of the effortless accomplishment and repose of the <s>Buddha</s>'s activity; the wheel of attainment through non-activity; the wheel of absolute non-apprehension; the wheel of neither accumulation nor deduction

body.translated_text: ; the wheel of the inexpressible; the wheel of the nature-as-it-is; the wheel of entering into the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> as a single domain; the wheel of the sovereign bestowal and turning-back of the discipline of beings at inauspicious times; the wheel of entering the method of ultimate truth through non-dual attribution; the wheel of convergence in the <s>dharma</s>-realm. Immeasurable is that wheel, transcending all measures. Innumerable is that wheel, beyond all counting. Inconceivable is that wheel, transcending the path of thought. Incomparable is that wheel, beyond comparison. Inexpressible is that wheel, beyond the path of all sounds, voices, and speech. Immeasurable, incomparable, beyond analogy, like space itself, neither annihilated nor eternal, entering into dependent origination without contradiction, peaceful, supremely tranquil, reality, suchness, unfalseness, unalterableness, unchangeableness, moving in the sounds of all beings. The subduing of <s>Māras</s>; the defeat of non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthikas</s>); the transcending of the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s>; the entering into the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>; fully known by noble persons (<s>āryapudgalas</s>); followed by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; embraced by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; praised by all <s>Buddhas</s>; unbroken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Of such a nature, O <s>Maitreya</s>, is the <s>Dharmacakra</s> turned by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — by the turning of which he is called <s>Tathāgata</s>; called Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>); called Self-Arisen (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>); called Lord of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmasvāmī</s>); called Leader (<s>Nāyaka</s>); called Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>); called Chief Guide (<s>Pariṇāyaka</s>); called Caravan-Leader (<s>Sārthavāha</s>); called Sovereign over All <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>Sarvadharmavaśavartī</s>); called Lord of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmeśvara</s>); called Turner of the <s>Dharma</s>-Wheel (<s>Dharmacakrapravartī</s>); called Lord of <s>Dharma</s>-Giving (<s>Dharmadānapati</s>); called Lord of Sacrifice (<s>Yajñasvāmī</s>); called He of Well-Performed Sacrifice (<s>Suyaṣṭayajña</s>); called He of Accomplished Vow (<s>Siddhivrata</s>); called He of Fulfilled Purpose (<s>Pūrṇābhiprāya</s>); called Instructor (<s>Deśika</s>); called Consoler (<s>Āśvāsaka</s>); called Maker of Well-Being (<s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>); called Hero (<s>Śūra</s>); called He who Abandons Battle (<s>Raṇaṃjaha</s>); called Victor of the Battle (<s>Vijitasaṃgrāma</s>); called He of Raised Parasol, Banner, and Pennant (<s>Ucchritachatradhvajapatāka</s>); called Maker of Light (<s>Ālokakara</s>); called Maker of Radiance (<s>Prabhaṃkara</s>); called Dispeller of Darkness (<s>Tamonuda</s>); called Torch-Bearer (<s>Ulkādhārī</s>); called Great King of Physicians (<s>Mahāvaidyarāja</s>); called Healer of Beings (<s>Bhūtacikitsaka</s>); called Great Extractor of Thorns (<s>Mahāśalyahartā</s>); called He whose Knowledge-Vision is Free from Darkness (<s>Vitimirajñānadarśana</s>); called All-Seeing (<s>Samantadarśī</s>); called All-Surveying (<s>Samantavilokita</s>); called All-Eyed (<s>Samantacakṣu</s>); called All-Radiant (<s>Samantaprabha</s>); called All-Illuminating (<s>Samantāloka</s>); called All-Faced (<s>Samantamukha</s>); called All-Light-Making (<s>Samantaprabhākara</s>); called All-Moon (<s>Samantacandra</s>); called All-Pleasing (<s>Samantaprāsādika</s>); called He of Neither Accumulation nor Deduction without Any Fixed Position (<s>Apratiṣṭhānāyūhāniryūha</s>); called Equal to the Earth (<s>Dharaṇīsama</s>), because he is neither elevated nor depressed; called Equal to the King of Mountains (<s>Śailendrasama</s>), because he is unshakable; called the Glory of All Worlds (<s>Sarvalokaśrī</s>), because he is endowed with the virtues of all worlds; called He whose Crown cannot be Seen (<s>Anavalokitamūrdha</s>), because he surpasses all worlds; called Ocean-like (<s>Samudrakalpa</s>), because he is profound and hard to fathom; called Treasury of <s>Dharma</s>-Jewels (<s>Dharmaratnākara</s>), because he is filled with all the jewels of <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening; called Equal to the Wind (<s>Vāyusama</s>), because he has no fixed abode; called He of Unattached Intellect (<s>Asaṅgabuddhi</s>), because his mind is unattached, unbound, and free; called He of Non-Regressing <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Avaivartikadharma</s>), because he possesses the penetrating knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>; called Equal to Fire (<s>Tejaḥsama</s>), because he is hard to approach and has destroyed all afflictions through burning, having eliminated all attachment; called Equal to Water (<s>Apsama</s>), because his body and mind are undefiled, of pure intention, stainless, and washed clean of evil; called Equal to Space (<s>Ākāśasama</s>), because he has attained the superknowledge of unattached knowledge whose domain is the infinite, middle-less <s>dharma</s>-realm; called He who Dwells in Unobstructed Knowledge and Liberation (<s>Anāvaraṇajñānavimokṣavihārī</s>), because all obstructing <s>dharmas</s> have been well abandoned; called He whose Body extends through all <s>Dharma</s>-Realms (<s>Sarvadharmadhātuprasṛtakāya</s>), because he transcends the path of the eye, being like space; called Supreme Being (<s>Uttamasattva</s>), because he is undefiled by all worldly domains; called Unattached Being (<s>Asaṅgasattva</s>); called He of Immeasurable Intellect (<s>Apramāṇabuddhi</s>); called Teacher of Supramundane <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Lokottaradharmadeśika</s>); called Teacher of the World (<s>Lokācārya</s>); called Physician of the World (<s>Lokavaidya</s>); called He who has Risen above the World (<s>Lokābhyudgata</s>); called He Unstained by Worldly <s>Dharmas</s> (<s>Lokadharmānupalipta</s>); called Lord of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>); called Elder of the World (<s>Lokajyeṣṭha</s>); called Best of the World (<s>Lokaśreṣṭha</s>); called Sovereign of the World (<s>Lokeśvara</s>); called He Honored by the World (<s>Lokamahita</s>); called Refuge of the World (<s>Lokaparāyaṇa</s>)

body.translated_text: he is called 'one who has gone to the far shore of the world' (<s>lokapāraṃgata</s>). He is called 'lamp of the world' (<s>lokapradīpa</s>). He is called 'transcender of the world' (<s>lokottara</s>). He is called 'teacher of the world' (<s>lokaguru</s>). He is called 'benefactor of the world' (<s>lokārthakara</s>). He is called 'one who follows the world [compassionately]' (<s>lokānuvartaka</s>). He is called 'knower of the world' (<s>lokavid</s>). He is called 'one who has attained sovereignty over the world' (<s>lokādhipateyaprāpta</s>). He is called 'greatly worthy of offerings' (<s>mahādakṣiṇīya</s>). He is called 'worthy of worship' (<s>pūjārha</s>). He is called 'great field of merit' (<s>mahāpuṇyakṣetra</s>). He is called 'great being' (<s>mahāsattva</s>). He is called 'foremost being' (<s>agrasattva</s>). He is called 'excellent being' (<s>varasattva</s>). He is called 'supreme being' (<s>pravarasattva</s>). He is called 'highest being' (<s>uttamasattva</s>). He is called 'unsurpassed being' (<s>anuttarasattva</s>). He is called 'unequaled being' (<s>asamasattva</s>). He is called 'incomparable being' (<s>asadṛśasattva</s>). He is called 'constantly absorbed in concentration' (<s>satatasamāhita</s>). He is called 'one who abides in the equality of all dharmas' (<s>sarvadharmasamatāvihārī</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the path' (<s>mārgaprāpta</s>). He is called 'shower of the path' (<s>mārgadarśaka</s>). He is called 'guide of the path' (<s>mārgadeśika</s>). He is called 'one firmly established on the path' (<s>supratiṣṭhitamārga</s>). He is called 'one who has completely transcended <s>Māra</s>'s domain' (<s>māraviṣayasamatikrānta</s>). He is called 'destroyer of <s>Māra</s>'s circle' (<s>māramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsakara</s>). He is called 'one in the state beyond aging and death' (<s>ajarāmaraśītībhāva</s>). He is called 'one from whom the mass of darkness has departed' (<s>vigatatamondhakāra</s>). He is called 'one free from thorns' (<s>vigatakaṇṭaka</s>). He is called 'one free from doubt' (<s>vigatakāṅkṣa</s>). He is called 'one free from afflictions' (<s>vigatakleśa</s>). He is called 'one whose uncertainty is removed' (<s>vinītasaṃśaya</s>). He is called 'one whose perplexity is uprooted' (<s>vimatisamuddhaṭita</s>). He is called 'one who is detached' (<s>virakta</s>). He is called 'one who is liberated' (<s>vimukta</s>). He is called 'one who is purified' (<s>viśuddha</s>). He is called 'one free from passion' (<s>vigatarāga</s>). He is called 'one free from fault' (<s>vigatadoṣa</s>). He is called 'one free from delusion' (<s>vigatamoha</s>). He is called 'one whose defilements are exhausted' (<s>kṣīṇāśrava</s>). He is called 'one free from afflictions' (<s>niḥkleśa</s>). He is called 'one who has gained mastery' (<s>vaśībhūta</s>). He is called 'one with well-liberated mind' (<s>suvimuktacitta</s>). He is called 'one with well-liberated wisdom' (<s>suvimuktaprajña</s>). He is called 'a thoroughbred' (<s>ājāneya</s>). He is called 'a great elephant' (<s>mahānāga</s>). He is called 'one who has done what was to be done' (<s>kṛtakṛtya</s>). He is called 'one who has accomplished the task' (<s>kṛtakaraṇīya</s>). He is called 'one who has laid down the burden' (<s>apahṛtabhāra</s>). He is called 'one who has attained his own purpose' (<s>anuprāptasvakārtha</s>). He is called 'one whose fetters to existence are exhausted' (<s>parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojana</s>). He is called 'one liberated through the knowledge of equality' (<s>samatājñānavimukta</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all minds' (<s>sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāpta</s>). He is called 'one endowed with mindfulness, intelligence, understanding, and wisdom' (<s>smṛtimatigatibuddhisaṃpanna</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the light of thorough insight into the foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of spiritual power, faculties, powers, and factors of awakening' (<s>smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇaṛddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgasamarthavidarśanālokaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>' (<s>uttīrṇasaṃsārārṇava</s>). He is called 'one who has gone to the far shore' (<s>pāraga</s>). He is called 'one who has reached dry land' (<s>sthalagata</s>). He is called 'one who has attained security' (<s>kṣemaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one who has attained fearlessness' (<s>abhayaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one who has crushed the thorn of afflictions' (<s>marditakleśakaṇṭaka</s>). He is called 'a man' (<s>puruṣa</s>). He is called 'a great man' (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>). He is called 'a lion among men' (<s>puruṣasiṃha</s>). He is called 'one from whom fear and hair-raising [dread] have departed' (<s>vigatabhayalomaharṣaṇa</s>). He is called 'an elephant' (<s>nāga</s>). He is called 'one who is stainless' (<s>nirmala</s>). He is called 'one who has abandoned the three stains' (<s>trimalamalaprahīṇa</s>). He is called 'a knower' (<s>vedaka</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the three knowledges' (<s>traividyānuprāpta</s>). He is called 'one who has crossed the four floods' (<s>caturoghottīrṇa</s>). He is called 'one gone to the far shore' (<s>pāraga</s>). He is called 'a noble warrior' (<s>kṣatriya</s>). He is called 'a true brahmin' (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>). He is called 'bearer of the single jeweled parasol' (<s>ekaratnachatradhārī</s>). He is called 'one who has carried forth the supreme <s>dharma</s>' (<s>vāhitapāradharma</s>). He is called 'a mendicant' (<s>bhikṣu</s>). He is called 'one who has broken the egg-shell of ignorance' (<s>bhinnāvidyāṇḍakośa</s>). He is called 'an ascetic' (<s>śramaṇa</s>). He is called 'one who has transcended the path of attachment to possessions' (<s>arthasaṅgapathasamatikrānta</s>). He is called 'one learned in scripture' (<s>śrotriya</s>). He is called 'one from whom afflictions have departed' (<s>niḥsṛtakleśa</s>). He is called 'one who is powerful' (<s>balavān</s>). He is called 'bearer of the ten powers' (<s>daśabaladhārī</s>). He is called 'Blessed One' (<s>Bhagavān</s>). He is called 'one whose body is cultivated' (<s>bhāvitakāya</s>). He is called 'king of kings' (<s>rājātirāja</s>). He is called 'king of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>dharmarāja</s>). He is called 'instructor who turns the supreme, excellent wheel of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>varapravaradharmacakrapravartyanuśāsaka</s>). He is called 'one whose teaching of <s>dharma</s> is unshakable' (<s>akopyadharmadeśaka</s>). He is called 'one anointed with the knowledge of omniscience' (<s>sarvajñajñānābhiṣikta</s>). He is called 'one whose headband is the stainless, unattached, great, unobstructed knowledge' (<s>asaṅgamahājñānavimalaviruktapaṭṭabaddha</s>). He is called 'one endowed with the jewels of the seven factors of awakening' (<s>saptabodhyaṅgaratnasamanvāgata</s>). He is called 'one who has attained distinction in all <s>dharmas</s>' (<s>sarvadharmaviśeṣaprāpta</s>)

body.translated_text: . He is called 'one whose face is beheld by all noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> who are his ministers' (<s>sarvāryaśrāvakāmātyāvalokitamukhamaṇḍala</s>). He is called 'one surrounded by <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>Mahāsattva</s> sons' (<s>bodhisattvamahāsattvaputraparivāra</s>). He is called 'one whose <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline) is well-trained' (<s>suvinītavinaya</s>). He is called 'one whose <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are well-predicted' (<s>suvyākṛtabodhisattva</s>). He is called 'one like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>' (<s>vaiśravaṇasadṛśa</s>). He is called 'one whose treasury distributes the seven noble riches' (<s>saptāryadhanaviśrāṇitakośa</s>). He is called 'one who has fully renounced' (<s>tyaktatyāga</s>). He is called 'one endowed with all happiness and prosperity' (<s>sarvasukhasaṃpattisamanvāgata</s>). He is called 'giver of all aspirations' (<s>sarvābhiprāyadātā</s>). He is called 'guardian of the welfare and happiness of the entire world' (<s>sarvalokahitasukhānupālaka</s>). He is called 'one like <s>Indra</s>' (<s>indrasama</s>). He is called 'bearer of the <s>vajra</s> of the power of knowledge' (<s>jñānabalavajradhārī</s>). He is called 'one with eyes in all directions' (<s>samantanetra</s>). He is called 'one who sees with unobstructed knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>' (<s>sarvadharmānāvaraṇajñānadarśī</s>). He is called 'one who displays knowledge in all directions' (<s>samantajñānavikurvaṇa</s>). He is called 'one who has entered the vision of the vast dramatic display of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>vipuladharmanāṭakadarśanapraviṣṭa</s>). He is called 'one like the moon' (<s>candrasama</s>). He is called 'one at whose sight the whole world is never satiated' (<s>sarvajagadatṛptadarśana</s>). He is called 'one of universally vast, pure radiance' (<s>samantavipulaviśuddhaprabha</s>). He is called 'one whose radiance produces joy and gladness' (<s>prītiprāmodyakaraprabha</s>). He is called 'one whose light appears facing all beings' (<s>sarvasattvābhimukhadarśanābhāsa</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the reflection in the vessel of the mental dispositions of all beings in the world' (<s>sarvajagaccittāśayabhājanapratibhāsaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one of great array' (<s>mahāvyūha</s>). He is called 'one surrounded by the constellation of those in training and those beyond training' (<s>śaikṣāśaikṣajyotirgaṇaparivāra</s>). He is called 'one like the orb of the sun' (<s>ādityamaṇḍalasama</s>). He is called 'one who has dispelled the darkness of delusion' (<s>vidhūtamohāndhakāra</s>). He is called 'great king of banners' (<s>mahāketurāja</s>). He is called 'one of immeasurable, infinite rays' (<s>apramāṇānantaraśmi</s>). He is called 'one who displays great radiance' (<s>mahāvabhāsasaṃdarśaka</s>). He is called 'one never confused in explaining the answers to all questions' (<s>sarvapraśnavyākaraṇanirdeśāsaṃmūḍha</s>). He is called 'one who destroys the great darkness of ignorance' (<s>mahāvidyāndhakāravidhvaṃsanakara</s>). He is called 'one whose discernment is free from conceptual construction, illuminated by the light of great knowledge' (<s>mahājñānālokavilokitabuddhinirvikalpa</s>). He is called 'one whose domain is the measure of rays of equality toward all beings in the world, released through great loving-kindness, mercy, and compassion' (<s>mahāmaitrīkṛpākaruṇāsarvajagatsamaraśmipramuktapramāṇaviṣaya</s>). He is called 'one whose sphere is the deep, hard-to-fathom, hard-to-behold [realm] of the perfection of wisdom' (<s>prajñāpāramitāgambhīradurāsadadurnirīkṣamaṇḍala</s>). He is called 'one like <s>Brahmā</s>' (<s>brahmasama</s>). He is called 'one of peaceful deportment' (<s>praśānteryāpatha</s>). He is called 'one endowed with distinction in all modes of deportment' (<s>sarveryāpathacaryāviśeṣasamanvāgata</s>). He is called 'bearer of the supreme form' (<s>paramarūpadhārī</s>). He is called 'one whose appearance never cloys' (<s>asecanakadarśana</s>). He is called 'one of tranquil faculties' (<s>śāntendriya</s>). He is called 'one of tranquil mind' (<s>śāntamānasa</s>). He is called 'one whose accumulation of tranquility is complete' (<s>śamathasaṃbhāraparipūrṇa</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the highest tranquility' (<s>uttamaśamathaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one who has attained the supreme taming and tranquility' (<s>paramadamaśamathaprāpta</s>). He is called 'one whose accumulation of tranquility and insight is complete' (<s>śamathavidarśanāparipūrṇasaṃbhāra</s>). He is called 'guarded, with conquered faculties, well-tamed like an elephant, like a clear, untroubled, limpid lake' (<s>gupto jitendriyo nāga iva sudānto hrada ivāccho 'nāvilo viprasanna</s>). He is called 'one who has thoroughly abandoned all the obscurations of the latent tendencies of afflictions' (<s>sarvakleśavāsanāvaraṇasuprahīṇa</s>). He is called 'one endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man' (<s>dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇasamanvāgata</s>). He is called 'the supreme person' (<s>paramapuruṣa</s>). He is called 'one whose body is variously adorned, surrounded by the eighty minor marks' (<s>aśītyanuvyañjanaparivāravicitraracitagātra</s>). He is called 'bull among men' (<s>puruṣarṣabha</s>). He is called 'one endowed with the ten powers' (<s>daśabalasamanvāgata</s>). He is called 'the unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed, who has attained the four confidences' (<s>caturvaiśāradyaprāptānuttarapuruṣadamyasārathi</s>). He is called 'Teacher' (<s>Śāstā</s>). He is called 'one who has fulfilled the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>' (<s>aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmaparipūrṇa</s>). He is called 'one whose actions of body, speech, and mind are blameless' (<s>aninditakāyavāṅmanaskarmānta</s>). He is called 'one who abides in emptiness, because his sphere of knowledge and vision is well-purified and endowed with all excellent aspects' (<s>śūnyatāvihārī</s>). He is called 'one who abides in the signless, because of awakening to the equality of dependent origination' (<s>ānimittavihārī</s>). He is called 'one who abides in the wishless, because of penetrating the truth of ultimate reality' (<s>apraṇihitavihārī</s>). He is called 'one whose domain is beyond conditioned formations, because of being unstained by all courses of action' (<s>anabhisaṃskāragocara</s>). He is called 'a speaker of truth, because all conditioned formations have been completely calmed' (<s>bhūtavādī</s>). He is called 'one who speaks what is true and not otherwise, because his domain of knowledge is not disturbed from the limit of reality' (<s>avitathānanyathāvādī</s>). He is called 'one who has well-attained the <s>dharma</s> of the forest (solitude), because his domain is the characteristic of characteristiclessness of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma), and space' (<s>araṇyadharmasupratilabdha</s>). He is called 'one whose seeing and hearing is never fruitless, because he abides in the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> as illusion, mirage, dream, reflection of the moon in water, echo, and reflected image' (<s>amoghadarśanaśravaṇa</s>). He is called 'one whose steps are never in vain, because he generates the cause of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' (<s>amoghapadavikramī</s>). He is called 'one who has cast off weariness, because of valor and exertion in taming beings' (<s>utkṣiptaparikheda</s>). He is called 'one who has established the crossing, because of having completely cut off ignorance, existence, and craving' (<s>sthāpitasaṃkrama</s>). He is called 'one who has conquered the adversaries of <s>Māra</s> and afflictions, because of teaching the path leading to liberation' (<s>nirjitamārakleśapratyarthika</s>). He is called 'one who has crossed beyond the mire of sensual desire, because of being unstained by all conduct in <s>Māra</s>'s domain' (<s>uttīrṇakāmapaṅka</s>). He is called 'one who has cast down the banner of pride, because of having completely transcended the desire-realm' (<s>pātitamānadhvaja</s>)
