body.translated_text: it is said. Because he has transcended the Form Realm, he is called "one whose banner of wisdom is raised aloft." Because he has transcended the Formless Realm, he is called "one who has transcended the domain of all worlds." Because his body is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Body of <s>Dharma</s>) and his form is knowledge, he is called a "great tree." Because he is well-endowed with the fruit of liberation, blossoming with the flowers of the knowledge of innumerable virtue-jewels, he is called "like the <s>udumbara</s> flower." Because the manifestation and sight of him is rare, he is called "like the wish-fulfilling jewel, the king of jewels." Because he fulfills all wishes according to the proper method of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he is called "one with well-established feet." Because of his firm, unshakable resolve in the practice of generosity, morality, austerity, vows, and the holy life for a long time, he is called "one whose soles are marked with a thousand variegated <s>svastika</s>, <s>nandyāvarta</s>, and wheel patterns." Because of his long-standing protection and guardianship of mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings according to <s>Dharma</s>, and because of his not abandoning those who come for refuge, he is called "one with projecting heels" (<s>āyatapārṣṇi</s>). Because of his long-standing abstention from taking life, he is called "one with long fingers" (<s>dīrghāṅguli</s>). Because of his long-standing practice of restraining others from taking life and inducing other beings [to do the same], he is called "protector of many people" (<s>bahujanatrāta</s>). Because of his long-standing proclamation of the virtues of abstaining from taking life, he is called "one with soft, tender hands and feet" (<s>mṛdutaruṇahastapāda</s>). Because of his long-standing service and attendance upon mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings — bathing, anointing, rubbing with clarified butter and oil — and because of the exertion of his own hands in caring for their bodies, he is called "one with webbed fingers and toes" (<s>jālāṅgulihastapāda</s>). Because of his long-standing skill in gathering beings through the four means of attraction — giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and equal treatment — and because he was well-trained in these, he is called "one with prominent insteps" (<s>ucchaṅgapāda</s>). Because of his long-standing reliance on increasingly superior and distinguished roots of virtue, he is called "one whose body-hair grows upward and curls to the right" (<s>ūrdhvāṅgadakṣiṇāvartaromakūpa</s>). Because of his long-standing practice of circumambulating mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, those worthy of offerings, and <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines, hearing the <s>Dharma</s> with wonder and hair-raising joy, gladdening other beings, and exerting himself in teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, he is called "one with antelope-like calves" (<s>eṇeyajaṅgha</s>). Because of his long-standing skill in respectfully hearing, grasping, retaining, reciting, explaining, ascertaining the meaning and word of the <s>Dharma</s>, and reaching conclusions, and because of his offering of refuge and respectful <s>Dharma</s>-teaching without contempt to beings facing old age, disease, and death, he is called "one whose male organ is ensheathed" (<s>kośopagatabastiguhya</s>). Because of his long-standing support of the holy life of <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and other celibates — providing all requisites, giving power to the naked, abstaining from approaching others' wives — and because of his firm resolve to guard modesty and moral shame while proclaiming the virtues of the holy life, he is called "one with arms reaching to the knees" (<s>pralambabāhu</s>). Because of his long-standing practice of restraint of hands, restraint of feet, not harming beings, and being endowed with bodily, verbal, and mental acts of loving-kindness, he is called "one proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> tree" (<s>nyagrodhaparimaṇḍala</s>). Because of his long-standing knowledge of the proper measure of food, eating sparingly, practicing noble restraint, providing medicine for the sick, not despising the lowly, not trampling on the unprotected, repairing dilapidated <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines and erecting <s>stūpas</s>, and giving fearlessness to beings afflicted by fear, he is called "one with soft, tender, delicate skin" (<s>mṛdutaruṇasūkṣmacchavi</s>). Because of his long-standing bathing, anointing, rubbing with clarified butter and oil for mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings — providing warm water in cold weather and cool water in hot weather, shade and warmth and seasonal comforts — providing beds and seats spread with soft, tender, cotton-like, delicate, fine fabrics — and providing fragrant oil, fine cloth, banners, and pennants for <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines, he is called "one with golden-colored skin" (<s>suvarṇacchavi</s>). Because of his long-standing cultivation of loving-kindness without hostility toward all beings, his practice of patience and gentleness, his inducing other beings [to adopt the same], his proclaiming the virtues of non-enmity and non-malice, and his adorning <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines and <s>Tathāgata</s> images with gold inlay, golden flowers, sprinkling of gold dust, golden-colored cloth, pennants, and banners, and offering golden vessels and golden garments, he is called "one whose each hair grows from a single pore" (<s>ekaikanicitaromakūpa</s>). Because of his long-standing approach to the learned, his questioning about what is wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, to be practiced and not, low, middle, and excellent <s>dharmas</s>, his investigation and examination of meanings without confusion, and his practice of removing from <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines the webs of spiders, stale offerings, and various grasses and pebbles, he is called "one with seven prominences" (<s>saptotsada</s>).

body.text: dīrgharātraṃ mātāpitṛjyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhapūjyaśramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakādibhya upāgatebhyaḥ satkṛtya yathābhiprāyamannapānāsanavastrāpaśrayapradīpakalpitajīvikapariskārasaṃpradānakūpapuṣkariṇīśītajalaparīpūrṇamahājanopabhogānupradānatvātsiṃhapūrvārdhakāya ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ mātāpitṛśramaṇabrāhmaṇagurudakṣiṇīyāvanamanapraṇamanābhivādanābhayapradānadurbalāparibhavaśaraṇāgatāparityāgadṛḍhasargadānānutsargatvāccitāntarāṃsa ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ svadoṣaparitulanapraskhalitaparachidrādoṣadarśanavivādamūlaparabhedakaramantraparivarjanasupratinissargamantrasvārakṣitavākkarmāntatvātsusaṃvṛttaskandha ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ mātāpitṛśramaṇabrāhmaṇagurudakṣiṇīyānāṃ pratyutthānapratyudramanābhivādanakāmānāṃ ca sarvaśāstravaiśāradyena vivādakāmasattvanigrahasvadharmavinayānulomanasamyakpravṛttarājāmātyasamyakpravṛttakuśaladharmapathapratiṣṭhāpanaprabhāvanatathāgataśāsanaparigrahasaṃdhāraṇasarvakuśalacaryāsamādāpana pūrvaṃgamatvātsiṃhahanurityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ sarvavastuparityāgayathābhiprāyayācanakapriyābhidhānamupasaṃkrāntānāṃ cāvimānanājihmīkaraṇāvikṣepaṃ sarveṣāṃ yathābhiprāyaparipūraṇadānaparityāgadṛḍhasamādānānutsargatvāccatvāriṃśatsamadanta ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ piśunavacanaparivarjanabhedamantrāgrahaṇasaṃdhisāmagrīrocanasamagrāṇāṃ cedācittena piśunavacanavigarhaṇasaṃdhisāmagrīguṇavarṇaprakāśanaprayogatvātsuśukladanta ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaparivarjanaśuklapakṣakuśalopacayakṛṣṇakarmakṛṣṇavipākaparivarjanaśuklakarmaśuklavipākasaṃvarṇanakṣīrabhojanaśuklavastrapradānatathāgatacaityeṣu sudhākṛtakakṣīramiśrasaṃpradānasumanāvārṣikīdhānuskārimālāguṇapuṣpadāmaśuklavarṇakusumānupradānatvādaviraladanta ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ hāsyoccaṭyanavivarjanānandakaraṇavāganurakṣaṇānandakaraṇavāgudīraṇaparaskhalitāparachidrāparimārgaṇasarvasattvasamacittasamādāpanasamaprayogasamadharmadeśanadṛḍhasamādānāparityāgatvādrasarasāgravānityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ sarvasattvāviheṭhanāvihiṃsanavividhavyādhispṛṣṭopasthānaglānabhaiṣajyānupradānatvātsarvarasārthikebhyaśca sarvarasapradānāparikhedatvādbahmasvara ityucyate / dīrgharātramanṛtaparuṣakarkaśaśāṭhyaparakaṭukaparābhiṣaṅginyapriyaparamarbhaghaṭṭanavākparivarjanamaitrīkaruṇāprayogamuditāprāmodyakaraṇīsnigdhamamadhuraślakṣṇahṛdayaṃgamasarvendriyaprahlādakaraṇīsamyagvākyasamyakprayogatvādabhinīlanetra ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ mātāpitṛvatsarvasattvāpratihatacakṣuprayogaikaputravadyācanakamaitrīkāruṇyapūrvaṃgamasaṃprekṣaṇājihmīkaraṇaprasannendriyatathāgatacaityānimiṣanayanasaṃprekṣaṇaparasattvatathāgatadarśanasamādāpanadṛḍhasamādānatvādgopekṣanetra ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ hīnacetovivarjanodāravipulādhimuktiparipūraṇānuttaradharmachandasattvasamādāpanabhṛkuṭīmukhavivarjanasmitamukhasarvakalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇābhimukhapūrvaṃgamasarvakuśalopacayāvaivartikatvāprabhūtajihva ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ sarvavāgdoṣavivarjanasarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhadharmabhāṇakāpramāṇaguṇavarṇasaṃprakāśanatathāgatasūtrāntalikhanavācanapaṭhanavijñāpanaṃ teṣāṃ ca dharmāṇāmarthapadaprabhedaparasattvasaṃprāpaṇakauśalyatvāduṣṇīṣānavalokitamūrdha ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ mātāpitṛśramaṇabrāhmaṇagurudakṣiṇīyānāṃ mūrdhnāṃ caraṇatalapraṇipatanapravrajitavandanābhivādanakeśāvaropaṇasugandhatailamūrdhnipariṣiñcanaṃ sarvayācanakebhyaścūrṇamālyamālāguṇamūrdhābharaṇānupradānatvād
body.translated_text: Because of his long-standing respectful provision of food, drink, seats, garments, shelter, lamps, and means of livelihood as wished for to mother, father, elders, worthies, the venerable, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and forest-dwellers and others who have come forward, and because of his providing wells and lotus-ponds filled with cool water for the enjoyment of the multitude, he is called "one with a chest like a lion" (<s>siṃhapūrvārdhakāya</s>). Because of his long-standing bowing, saluting, and paying homage at the heads and feet of mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings, giving fearlessness, not despising the weak, not abandoning those who come for refuge, and firmly and unreservedly giving, he is called "one with broad shoulders" (<s>citāntarāṃsa</s>). Because of his long-standing examination of his own faults, his avoidance of seeking out the stumbles and defects of others, his renunciation of dispute-causing and divisive counsel, his well-surrendered counsel, and his guarded verbal conduct, he is called "one with well-rounded shoulders" (<s>susaṃvṛttaskandha</s>). Because of his long-standing standing up, going forward, and saluting mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings, and because of his leading all wholesome practices — subduing disputatious beings through mastery of all sciences, establishing the proper conduct of kings and ministers on the path of wholesome <s>dharma</s>, upholding and maintaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, and inducing others to adopt all wholesome conduct — he is called "one with a jaw like a lion" (<s>siṃhahanu</s>). Because of his long-standing relinquishment of all possessions, his speaking endearingly to those who come requesting as they wish, his not disdaining, deceiving, or dismissing them, his fulfilling all their wishes, and his firm, unreserved resolve in giving and relinquishment, he is called "one with forty even teeth" (<s>catvāriṃśatsamadanta</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of slanderous speech, his non-acceptance of divisive counsel, his delight in harmony and concord, his censure of slanderous speech with sincere mind, and his practice of proclaiming the virtues of harmony and concord, he is called "one with very white teeth" (<s>suśukladanta</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of the dark side and accumulation of virtue on the bright side, his avoidance of dark actions with dark results and his praising of bright actions with bright results, his giving of milk-food and white garments, his providing <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines with whitewash and milk mixtures, and his offering of garlands of <s>sumanā</s>, <s>vārṣikī</s>, and <s>dhānuṣkāri</s> flowers, wreaths of virtue-flowers, and white-colored blossoms, he is called "one with teeth without gaps" (<s>aviraladanta</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of mockery and ridicule, his guarding of joyful speech, his uttering of joyful speech, his not seeking out the stumbles and defects of others, his firm and unrelinquished resolve in inducing all beings to equal-mindedness, equal practice, and equal <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, he is called "one possessing the foremost of tastes" (<s>rasarasāgravān</s>). Because of his long-standing non-harming and non-injuring of all beings, his attendance upon those afflicted by various diseases, his providing medicine for the sick, and his untiring provision of all flavors to those seeking all flavors, he is called "one with a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice" (<s>brahmasvara</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of false, harsh, rough, deceitful, bitter, accusatory, unpleasant, offensive, and irritating speech, and his practice of loving-kindness and compassion, his generating of joy and gladness, and his proper utterance and proper practice of affectionate, sweet, gentle, heart-touching, delighting-all-faculties words, he is called "one with deep-blue eyes" (<s>abhinīlanetra</s>). Because of his long-standing practice of gazing upon all beings as a mother and father would, with unobstructed vision, looking upon each as an only child, with loving-kindness and compassion as his foremost [intention], with sincere gaze, without deceit, with serene faculties, gazing at <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines with unblinking eyes, and inducing other beings to behold the <s>Tathāgata</s> with firm resolve, he is called "one with eyes like a cow" (<s>gopekṣanetra</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of low-minded thinking, his fulfillment of noble, vast conviction, his inducing beings to desire the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>, his avoidance of frowning faces, his having a smiling face, his approaching all good friends face-to-face as foremost, and his irreversibility in the accumulation of all wholesome [qualities], he is called "one with a broad tongue" (<s>prabhūtajihva</s>). Because of his long-standing avoidance of all faults of speech, his proclaiming the immeasurable virtues of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>Dharma</s>-speaker [paths], his writing, reciting, reading, and explaining <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>sūtras</s>, and his skill in conveying to other beings the distinctions of meaning and word of those <s>dharmas</s>, he is called "one whose head has an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> that cannot be seen from above" (<s>uṣṇīṣānavalokitamūrdha</s>). Because of his long-standing bowing with his head at the feet of mother, father, <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, teachers, and those worthy of offerings, saluting and paying homage to the ordained, shaving the hair, anointing the head with fragrant oil, and providing all who request with flower-powder, garlands, wreaths of virtue, and head-ornaments,

bhrūmadhye sujātapradakṣiṇāvartottaptaviśuddhavarṇābhāsorṇa ityucyate / dīrgharātraṃ nirargalasarvayajñayajanasamādapanasarvakalyāṇamitrānuśāsanyanuddharadharmabhāṇakānāṃ dautyaprekṣaṇe diggamanāgamanāparikhedanasarvabuddhabodhisattvaprattyekabuddhāryaśrāvakadharmabhāṇakamātāpitṛgurudakṣiṇīyatamondhakāravidhamanatailadhṛtatṛṇolkāpradīpanānāgandhatailapradīpasarvākāravaropetaprāsādikatathāgatapratimākāraṇakṣīrapratibhāsaratnottīrṇakośapratimaṇḍanaparasattvabodhacittāmukhīkaraṇakuśalasaṃbhāraviśeṣatvānmahāsthāmaprāpta ityucyate / mahānārāyaṇabalopetatvānmahānārāyaṇa ityucyate / koṭīśatamāradharṣaṇabalopetatvātsarvaparapramardaka ityucyate / daśatathāgatabalopetatvāddaśatathāgatabalopeta ityucyate / sthānāsthānajñānakuśalahīnaprādeśikayānavivarjanamahāyānaguṇasamudānayanabalopetātṛptabalaprayogatvātsthānajñānabalopeta ityucyate / atītānāgatapratyutpannakarmasamādānahetuśovipākaśojñānabalopetatvādatītānāgatapratyutpannasarvakarmasamādānahetuvipākajñānabalopeta ityucyate / sarvasattvendriyavīryavimātratājñānabalopetatvātsarvasattvendriyavīryavimātratājñānabalopeta ityucyate / anekadhātunānādhātulokapraveśajñānabalopetatvādanekadhātunānādhātulokapraveśajñānabalopeta ityucyate / anekādhimuktinānādhimuktiniravaśeṣādhimuktivimuktijñānabalopetatvādanekādhimuktinānādhimuktisarvaniravaśeṣādhimuktijñānabalopeta ityucyate / sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalopetatvātsarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalopeta ityucyate / sarvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthāpanajñānabalopetatvāsarvadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthāpanajñānabalopeta ityucyate / anekavidhapūrvanivāsānusmṛtyāsaṅgajñānabalopetatvādanekavidhapūrvanivāsānusmṛtyāsaṅgajñānabalopeta ityucyate / niravaśeṣasarvarūpānāvaraṇadarśanadivyacakṣurjñānabalopetatvānniravaśeṣasarvarūpānāvaraṇadarśanadivyacakṣurjñānabalopeta ityucyate / sarvaṃvāsanānusaṃdhigataniravaśeṣasarvāśravakṣayajñānabalopetatvātsarvavāsanānusaṃdhigataniravaśeṣasarvāśravakṣayajñānabalopeta ityucyate / niravaśeṣasarvadharmābhisaṃbuddhapratijñārohaṇasadevalokānabhibhūtapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāptatvānniravaśeṣasarvadharmābhisaṃprabuddhatijñārohaṇasadevaloke 'nabhibhūtapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāpta ityucyate / sarvasāṃkleśikāntarāyikadharmāntarāyakaraṇānirvāṇasyetitatpratijñārohaṇasadevake loke 'nāchedyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāptatvāsarvasāṃkleśikāntarāyikadharmāntarāyakaraṇānirvāṇasyeti tatpratijñārohaṇasadevake loke 'nāchedyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāpta ityucyate / nairyāṇikīṃ pratipadaṃ pratipadyamāno nirvāṇamārāgayiṣyatīti pratijñārohaṇasadevake loke 'praticodyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāptatvānnairyāṇikīṃ pratipadaṃ pratipadyamāno nirvāṇamārāgayiṣyatīti pratijñārohaṇasadevake loke 'praticodyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāpta ityucyate / savāśravakṣayajñānaprahāṇajñānapratijñārohaṇasadevake loke 'vivartyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāptatvātsarvāśravakṣayajñānaprahāṇajñānapratijñārohaṇasadevake
loke 'vivartyapratijñāvaiśāradyaprāpta ityucyate / askhalitapadadharmadeśakatvādaskhalitapadadharmadeśaka ityucyate / arutānabhilāpyadharmasvabhāvānubuddhatvādarutānabhilāpyadharmasvabhāvānubuddha ityucyate / aviratatvādavirata ityucyate / sarvasattvarutāpramāṇabuddhadharmarutanirghoṣādhiṣṭhānasamarthatvātsarvasattvarutāpramāṇabuddhadharmarutanirghoṣādhiṣṭhānasamartha ityucyate /
body.translated_text: between the eyebrows there is a well-formed, clockwise-turning, heated, purely-colored radiant <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft) — thus he is called [possessor of the <s>ūrṇā</s>]. Because for a long time he urged all beings to unrestricted sacrifice and worship, followed the instruction of all spiritual friends, supported <s>Dharma</s>-preachers without pulling them down, [and] because of his tirelessness in going and coming as an envoy to the directions, his dispelling of the darkness of blind ignorance for all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, parents, and teachers worthy of offerings, through oil-maintained grass-torches, lamps with various fragrant oils, his making of <s>Tathāgata</s> images endowed with all excellent marks and inspiring faith, his adorning of reliquary shrines surpassing [mere] milk-like appearance and jewel[-work], and his turning others' minds toward <s>bodhicitta</s> — because of the special distinction of his wholesome accumulations — he is called <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> (Arrived at Great Power). Because he is endowed with the power of the great <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he is called <s>Mahānārāyaṇa</s>. Because he is endowed with the power to vanquish hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>, he is called Crusher of All Opponents. Because he is endowed with the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers, he is called Endowed with the Ten <s>Tathāgata</s> Powers. Because he is endowed with the power of the knowledge of what is possible and impossible, being skilled in avoiding inferior and partial vehicles, gathering the qualities of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, insatiable in the exertion of power — he is called Endowed with the Power of Knowledge of What Is Possible. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power regarding the karmic undertakings, causes, and results of the past, future, and present — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of All Karmic Undertakings, Causes, and Results of Past, Future, and Present. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of the varied measures of all beings' faculties and vigor — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of the Varied Measures of All Beings' Faculties and Vigor. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of entering the world of many elements and diverse elements — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of Entering the World of Many and Diverse Elements. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of manifold dispositions, diverse dispositions, and the complete liberation of all dispositions without remainder — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of All Manifold and Diverse Dispositions Without Remainder. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of the path leading everywhere — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of the Path Leading Everywhere. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of establishing the defilement and purification of all <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of Establishing the Defilement and Purification of All <s>Dhyānas</s>, Liberations, <s>Samādhis</s>, and Attainments. Because he is endowed with the unobstructed knowledge-power of manifold recollection of former abodes — he is called Endowed with the Unobstructed Knowledge-Power of Manifold Recollection of Former Abodes. Because he is endowed with the divine-eye knowledge-power of seeing all forms without obstruction and without remainder — he is called Endowed with the Divine-Eye Knowledge-Power of Seeing All Forms Without Obstruction and Without Remainder. Because he is endowed with the knowledge-power of the complete destruction of all outflows including all latent tendencies — he is called Endowed with the Knowledge-Power of the Complete Destruction of All Outflows Including All Latent Tendencies. Because he has attained the confidence of the undefeated declaration before the world with its gods that he has fully awakened to all <s>dharmas</s> without remainder — he is called Attainer of the Confidence of the Undefeated Declaration Before the World With Its Gods That He Has Fully Awakened to All <s>Dharmas</s>. Because he has attained the confidence of the unbreakable declaration before the world with its gods that all defiling and obstructing <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — he is called Attainer of the Confidence of the Unbreakable Declaration Before the World With Its Gods. Because he has attained the confidence of the unopposed declaration before the world with its gods that one who practices the path leading out will reach <s>nirvāṇa</s> — he is called Attainer of the Confidence of the Unopposed Declaration Before the World With Its Gods. Because he has attained the confidence of the irreversible declaration before the world with its gods of the knowledge of the destruction of all outflows and the knowledge of abandonment — he is called Attainer of the Confidence of the Irreversible Declaration Before the World With Its Gods. Because he teaches <s>Dharma</s> with unfailing words, he is called Teacher of <s>Dharma</s> with Unfailing Words. Because he has awakened to the unspoken, inexpressible intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>, he is called Awakened to the Unspoken, Inexpressible Intrinsic Nature of <s>Dharmas</s>. Because he is unceasing, he is called Unceasing. Because he is capable of establishing the incomparable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s> sound in the voices of all beings — he is called Capable of Establishing the Incomparable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s> Sound in All Beings' Voices.

body.text: amuṣitasmṛtitvādamuṣitasmṛtirityucyate / nānātvasaṃjñāvigatatvānnānātvasaṃjñāvigata ityucyate / sarvacittasamāhitasumāhitasattvātsarvacittasamāhitasusamāhita ityucyate / apratisaṃkhyāsamupekṣakatvādapratisaṃkhyāsamupekṣaka ityucyate / chandasaṃskārasamādhyaparihīnatvācchandasaṃskārasamādhyaparihīna ityucyate / vīryasaṃskārasamādhyanāchedyāparihīnavīryatvādvīryasaṃskārasamādhyaparihīnavīrya ityucyate / smṛtyaparihīnatvādaparihīnasmṛtirityucyate / aparihīnaprajñatvādaparihīnaprajña ityucyate / vimuktyaparihīnatvādaparihīnavimuktirityucyate / vimuktijñānadarśanāprahīnatvādaparihīnavimuktijñānadarśana ityucyate / sarvakāyakarmavākkarmamanaskarmajñānapūrvaṃgamajñānānuparivartisamanvāgatatvātsarvakāyavāṅbhamanaskarmajñānapūrvaṃgamajñānānuparivartijñānasamanvāgata ityucyate / atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasvasaṅgāpratihatajñānadarśanasamanvāgatatvāt tryadhvāsaṅgāpratihatajñānadarśanasamanvāgata ityucyate / anāvaraṇavimokṣapratilabdhatvādanāvaraṇavimokṣapratilabdha ityucyate / adhiṣṭhitasarvasattvacaritapraveśakauśalyāvasthitatvodadhiṣṭhitasarvasattvacaritapraveśakauśalyāvasthita ityucyate / yathāpratyarhadharmadeśanākuśalatvādyathāpratyarhadharmadeśanākuśala ityucyate / sarvasvarāṅgamaṇḍalaparamapāramitāprāptatvātsarvasvarāṅgamaṇḍalaparamapāramitāprāpta ityucyate / sarvarutapratirutaniścāraṇakauśalyaprāptatvāddevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaruta ityucyate / brahmasvararutaravitanirghoṣa ityucyate / kalaviṅkarutasvara ityucyate / dundubhisaṃgītirutasvara ityucyate / dharaṇītalanirnādanirghoṣasvara ityucyate / sāgaranāgendrameghastanitagarjitaghoṣasvara ityucyate / siṃhavṛṣabhitābhigarjitanirghoṣasvara ityucyate / sarvasattvarutaravitānucaraṇasaṃtoṣaṇasvara ityucyate / asaṅgānāvaraṇasarvaparṣanmaṇḍalābhirādhanasvara ityucyate / ekarutātsarvarutasaṃprāpanasvara ityucyate / brahmendrapūjita ityucyate / devendrasatkṛta ityucyate / nāgendranamaskṛta ityucyate / yakṣendrāvalokitamukhamaṇḍala ityucyate / gandharvendropagīta ityucyate / rākṣasendraprasannendriyāninimiṣanayanasaṃprekṣita ityucyate / asurendrābhipraṇata ityucyate / garuḍendrāvihiṃsāprekṣita ityucyate / kinnarendrābhiṣṭuta ityucyate / mahoragendrābhilaṣitadarśana ityucyate / manujendrābhisaṃpūjita ityucyate / ahargaṇasevita ityucyate / sarvabodhisattvasamādāyakasamuttejakasaṃhaprarṣaka ityucyate / nirāmiṣadharmadeśaka ityucyate / akṣuṇṇapadavyañjanāvandhyadharmadeśaka ityucyate / kālānatikramaṇadharmadeśaka ityucyate / idaṃ tanmaitreya dharmacakrapravartanaṃ tathāgataguṇavarṇapradeśasya yatkiṃcidavatāramātraṃ saṃkṣepeṇa nirdeśitaḥ vistareṇa punamaitreya tathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā nirdiśet / na cāsya nirdiśyamānasya paryanto bhavet //
body.translated_text: Because his mindfulness is unimpaired, he is called One of Unimpaired Mindfulness. Because he is free from the perception of diversity, he is called Free from the Perception of Diversity. Because all his minds are concentrated and well-concentrated, he is called One Whose Every Mind Is Concentrated and Well-Concentrated. Because he is one of impartial equanimity without deliberation, he is called One of Impartial Equanimity Without Deliberation. Because his <s>samādhi</s> of aspiration-formations is undiminished, he is called Undiminished in the <s>Samādhi</s> of Aspiration-Formations. Because his vigor in the <s>samādhi</s> of effort-formations is unbreakable and undiminished, he is called Undiminished in Vigor of the <s>Samādhi</s> of Effort-Formations. Because his mindfulness is undiminished, he is called One of Undiminished Mindfulness. Because his wisdom is undiminished, he is called One of Undiminished Wisdom. Because his liberation is undiminished, he is called One of Undiminished Liberation. Because his knowledge-and-vision of liberation is undiminished, he is called One of Undiminished Knowledge-and-Vision of Liberation. Because all his bodily, verbal, and mental actions are preceded by knowledge and accompanied by knowledge — he is called One Whose Every Bodily, Verbal, and Mental Action Is Preceded by and Accompanied by Knowledge. Because he is endowed with unobstructed, unhindered knowledge-and-vision regarding the past, future, and present — he is called Endowed with Unobstructed, Unhindered Knowledge-and-Vision of the Three Times. Because he has attained the unobstructed liberation, he is called Attainer of Unobstructed Liberation. Because he is established in the skill of entering the conduct of all beings with [his] empowerment — he is called Established in the Skill of Entering the Conduct of All Beings With Empowerment. Because he is skilled in teaching <s>Dharma</s> as befits each being, he is called Skilled in Teaching <s>Dharma</s> as Befits Each. Because he has attained the supreme perfection of all vocal and limb features, he is called Attainer of the Supreme Perfection of All Vocal and Limb Features. Because he has attained skill in producing all sounds and echoes — he is called [possessor of] the voices of <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>. He is called One of <s>Brahma</s>-voice sound and resonance. He is called One of <s>Kalaviṅka</s>-bird voice. He is called One of <s>Dundubhi</s>-drum concert voice. He is called One Whose Voice Resounds Like the Surface of the Earth. He is called One Whose Voice Is Like the Thunder of Ocean-<s>Nāga</s>-Lord Clouds. He is called One Whose Voice Is Like the Roar of a Lion. He is called One Whose Voice Follows, Resonates With, and Satisfies the Voices of All Beings. He is called One Whose Voice, Unobstructed and Unhindered, Delights All Assemblies. He is called One Who from a Single Sound Produces All Sounds. He is called Worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>. He is called Honored by <s>Devendra</s>. He is called Saluted by <s>Nāgendra</s>. He is called One Whose Face Is Gazed Upon by <s>Yakṣendra</s>. He is called Hymned by <s>Gandharvendra</s>. He is called One Beheld With Serene Faculties and Unblinking Eyes by <s>Rākṣasendra</s>. He is called One Before Whom <s>Asurendra</s> Bows. He is called One Beheld Without Harm by <s>Garuḍendra</s>. He is called Praised by <s>Kinnarendra</s>. He is called One Whose Sight Is Desired by <s>Mahoragendra</s>. He is called Worshipped by <s>Manujendra</s> (Lord of Humans). He is called Attended by the Hosts of Days. He is called Encourager, Inspirer, and Rejoicer of All <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. He is called Teacher of <s>Dharma</s> Without Material Incentive. He is called Teacher of <s>Dharma</s> Whose Words and Syllables Are Intact and Never Barren. He is called Teacher of <s>Dharma</s> Who Does Not Transgress the Proper Time. This, O <s>Maitreya</s>, is the description of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities in the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> — whatever slight entrance has been indicated in brief. In full, O <s>Maitreya</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could expound for a <s>kalpa</s> or remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>, and even then there would be no end to this exposition.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke this verse:

children.text: gambhīraṃ durdṛśaṃ sūkṣmaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam /
children.translated_text: 'Profound, hard to see, subtle — the <s>Dharmacakra</s> has been turned;

children.text: yatra mārā na gāhante sarve ca paratīrthikāḥ // Lal_26.52 //
children.translated_text: wherein <s>Māras</s> cannot fathom, nor any of the other sectarians.' // Lal_26.52 //

children.text: anālayaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ anutpādamasaṃbhavam /
children.translated_text: 'Without attachment, without proliferation, unborn, unarisen,

children.text: viviktaṃ prakṛtīśūnyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam // Lal_26.53 //
children.translated_text: isolated, empty by nature — the <s>Dharmacakra</s> has been turned.' // Lal_26.53 //

children.text: anāyūhamaniryūhamanimittamalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Without exertion, without extraction, signless, without characteristics,

children.text: samatādharmanirdeśaṃ cakraṃ buddhena varṇitam // Lal_26.54 //
children.translated_text: a teaching of the equality of <s>dharmas</s> — the wheel described by the <s>Buddha</s>.' // Lal_26.54 //

children.text: māyāmarīci svapnaṃ ca dakacandra pratiśrutkā /
children.translated_text: 'Illusion, mirage, dream, reflection of the moon in water, echo —

children.text: yathaite tathā taccakraṃ lokanāthena vartitam // Lal_26.55 //
children.translated_text: as these are, so is that wheel turned by the Lord of the World.' // Lal_26.55 //

children.text: pratītyadharmaotāramanucchedamaśāśvatam /
children.translated_text: 'An entrance into dependent <s>dharmas</s>, neither annihilation nor eternalism,

children.text: sarvadṛṣṭisamucchedo dharmacakramiti smṛtam // Lal_26.56 //
children.translated_text: the cutting off of all views — this is called the <s>Dharmacakra</s>.' // Lal_26.56 //

children.text: ākāśena sadā tulyaṃ nirvikalpaṃ prabhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: 'Always equal to space, free from conceptual elaboration, radiant,

children.text: anantamadhyanirdeśaṃ dharmacakramihocyate // Lal_26.57 //
children.translated_text: infinite, a teaching of the middle — this is here called the <s>Dharmacakra</s>.' // Lal_26.57 //

children.text: astināstivinirmuktamātmyanairātmyavarjitam /
children.translated_text: 'Free from existence and non-existence, devoid of self and non-self,

children.text: prakṛtyājātinirdeśaṃ dharmacakramihocyate // Lal_26.58 //
children.translated_text: a teaching of the unborn nature — this is here called the <s>Dharmacakra</s>.' // Lal_26.58 //

children.text: bhūtakoṭīmakoṭīṃ ca tathatāyāṃ tathatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The limit of reality as non-limit, suchness in its suchness —

children.text: advayo dharmanirdeśo dharmacakraṃ nirucyate // Lal_26.59 //
children.translated_text: a non-dual teaching of <s>Dharma</s> — this is called the <s>Dharmacakra</s>.' // Lal_26.59 //

children.text: cakṣuḥ svabhāvataḥ śūnyaṃ śrotaṃ ghrāṇaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: 'The eye is empty by its own nature, as are the ear and nose;

children.text: jihvā kāyaṃ ca cittaṃ ca śūnyātmāno nirīhakaḥ // Lal_26.60 //
children.translated_text: tongue, body, and mind — their self is empty, without agency.' // Lal_26.60 //

children.text: idaṃ tadīddaśaṃ cakraṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam /
children.translated_text: 'This is that wheel of such a kind — the <s>Dharmacakra</s> has been turned;

children.text: bodhayatyabudhān sattvāṃstena buddho nirucyate // Lal_26.61 //
children.translated_text: it awakens unawakened beings — therefore he is called <s>Buddha</s>.' // Lal_26.61 //

children.text: svayaṃ mayānubuddho 'yaṃ svabhāvo dharmalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'This own-nature, the characteristic of <s>Dharma</s>, was awakened to by me myself;

children.text: ṛte paropadeśena svayaṃbhūstatha cakṣumān // Lal_26.62 //
children.translated_text: without instruction from another — therefore [he is] the Self-Arisen, the Seer.' // Lal_26.62 //

children.text: sarvadharmavaśiprāpto dharmasvāmī nirucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Having attained mastery over all <s>dharmas</s>, he is called Lord of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: nayānayajño dharmeṣu nāyakastena cocyate // Lal_26.63 //
children.translated_text: knowing the right and wrong methods in <s>dharmas</s>, he is therefore called Leader.' // Lal_26.63 //

children.text: yathā bhavanti vaineyā vinayāmyamitāṃ janāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'As beings are to be disciplined, I discipline immeasurable people;

children.text: vineyapāramiprāptastena prokto vināyakaḥ // Lal_26.64 //
children.translated_text: having reached the perfection of disciplining — therefore he is called <s>Vināyaka</s> (Guide).' // Lal_26.64 //

children.text: naṣṭamārgā hi ye sattvā mārgaṃ deśemi uttamam /
children.translated_text: 'For those beings who have lost the path, I teach the supreme path;

children.text: nayāmi pārimaṃ tīraṃ tasmādasmi vināyakaḥ // Lal_26.65 //
children.translated_text: I lead [them] to the further shore — therefore I am the Guide.' // Lal_26.65 //

children.text: saṃgrahāvastujñānena saṃgṛhya janatāmaham /
children.translated_text: 'Through the knowledge of the bases of gathering [disciples], I gather the people;

children.text: saṃsārāṭavinistīrṇaḥ sārthavāhastato hyaham // Lal_26.66 //
children.translated_text: having crossed over the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> — therefore I am the Caravan-Leader.' // Lal_26.66 //

children.text: vaśavartī sarvadharmeṣu tena dharmeśvaro jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having sovereignty over all <s>dharmas</s>, therefore the <s>Jina</s> is Lord of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmacakraṃ pravartitvā dharmarājo nirucyate // Lal_26.67 //
children.translated_text: having turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s>, he is called <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of <s>Dharma</s>).' // Lal_26.67 //

children.text: dharmadānapatiḥ śāstā dharmasvāmī niruttaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, Teacher, Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, unsurpassed,

children.text: suyaṣṭayajñasiddhārthaḥ pūrṇāśaḥ siddhamaṅgalaḥ // Lal_26.68 //
children.translated_text: his sacrifice well-performed, his aims accomplished, his wishes fulfilled, auspicious and successful.' // Lal_26.68 //

children.text: āśvāsakaḥ kṣemadarśī śūro mahāraṇaṃjahaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Consoler, seer of security, hero, abandoner of the great battle,

children.text: uttīrṇasarvasaṃgrāmo mukto mocayitā prajāḥ // Lal_26.69 //
children.translated_text: having crossed over every conflict, liberated — he liberates beings.' // Lal_26.69 //

children.text: ālokabhūto lokasya prajñājñānaprabhaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A light for the world, a radiance-maker of wisdom-knowledge,

children.text: ajñānatamaso hantā ulkādhāri mahāprabhaḥ // Lal_26.70 //
children.translated_text: destroyer of the darkness of ignorance, torch-bearer, of great radiance.' // Lal_26.70 //

children.text: mahāvaidyo mahājñānī mahākleśacikitsakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The great physician, the great knower, the great healer of afflictions,

children.text: sattvānāṃ kleśaviddhānāṃ śalyahartā niruttaraḥ // Lal_26.71 //
children.translated_text: He is the unsurpassed remover of the arrow from beings pierced by <s>kleśas</s>. // Lal_26.71 //

children.text: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvavyañjanaśobhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with all the [major] marks, adorned with all the [minor] characteristics,

children.text: samantabhadrakāyena hīnānāṃ cānuvartakaḥ // Lal_26.72 //
children.translated_text: with a body universally auspicious, he is one who adapts to those of lesser [capacity]. // Lal_26.72 //

children.text: daśabhirbalabhirbalavān vaiśāradyaviśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mighty with the ten powers, skilled in the [four] confidences,

children.text: āveṇikairaṣṭadaśai agrayānī mahāmuniḥ // Lal_26.73 //
children.translated_text: with the eighteen unique [Buddha-qualities] — the foremost vehicle, the great sage! // Lal_26.73 //

children.text: eṣa saṃkṣepanirdeśo dharmacakrapravartane /
children.translated_text: This is a summary exposition regarding the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: tathāgataguṇavarṇaḥ parītto 'yaṃ prakāśitaḥ // Lal_26.74 //
children.translated_text: this description of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities has been set forth in brief. // Lal_26.74 //

children.text: buddhajñānamanantaṃ hi ākāśavipulaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge is infinite, equal to the vastness of space;

children.text: kṣapayetkalpa bhāṣanto na ca buddhaguṇakṣayaḥ // Lal_26.75 //
children.translated_text: one could exhaust a <s>kalpa</s> speaking, yet the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities would not be exhausted! // Lal_26.75 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: iti śrīlalitavistare dharmacakrapravartanaparivarto nāma ṣaḍviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter of the noble <s>Lalitavistara</s>, called "The Turning of the Wheel of <s>Dharma</s>." //

body.text: START Parivarta 27
body.translated_text: START Chapter 27

body.text: nigamaparivartaḥ saptaviṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: The twenty-seventh chapter: the Conclusion (<s>Nigamaparivarta</s>). /

body.text: atha khalu devaputrā yaistathāgato 'dhīṣṭo 'bhūdasya dharmaparyāyasya saṃprakāśanāya saha maheśvaranandasunandacandanamahitaśāntapraśāntavinīteśvarapramukhā aṣṭādaśaḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrasahasrāṇi ye tathāgatasya dharmacakrapravartane 'pi saṃnipatitā abhūvan / tatra bhagavāṃstān maheśvaradevaputrapramukhān śuddhāvāsakāyikān devaputrānāmantrayate sma - ayaṃ sa mārṣā lalitavistaro nāma dharmaparyāyasūtrānto mahāvaipulyabodhisattvavikrīḍitaḥ buddhaviṣaye lalitapraveśa ātmopanāyikastathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ / taṃ yūyamudgṛhṇīdhvaṃ dhārayata vācayata ca / evamiyaṃ dharmanetrī vaistārikī bhaviṣyati / bodhisattvayānikāśca pudgalā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā dṛḍhataraṃ vīryamālapsyante / anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvudārādhimuktikāśca sattvā mahādharmavarṣavegaṃ saṃjānayiṣyanti / mārapakṣaśca nigṛhīto bhaviṣyati / sarvaparapravādinaścāvatāraṃ na lapsyante / yuṣmākaṃ ca taddharmadeśanādhyeṣaṇā kuśalamūlaṃ mahārthikaṃ bhaviṣyati mahāphalaṃ mahānuśaṃsam //
body.translated_text: Then the god-sons by whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> had been requested for the proclamation of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — eighteen thousand <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-sons led by <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, <s>Praśānta</s>, and <s>Vinīteśvara</s>, who had also assembled at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> — the Blessed One addressed those <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-sons led by <s>Maheśvara</s>: "This, sirs, is the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called the <s>Lalitavistara</s>, the conclusion of the <s>sūtra</s>, a great extensive [text on] the play of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a graceful entry into the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, one's own guide — spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You should take it up, retain it, and recite it! Thus this eye of <s>Dharma</s> will become widespread. And persons of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, will attain even firmer vigor. Beings of noble aspiration toward the unsurpassed, perfect awakening will generate the momentum of the great rain of <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Māra</s>'s faction will be restrained. All opponents of other doctrines will find no opening. And your root of merit from entreating this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching will be of great purpose, great fruit, and great benefit." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā asya lalitavistarasya dharmaparyāyasyāñjaliṃ saṃpragṛhītaṃ kariṣyati, so 'ṣṭāvutkṛṣṭān dharmān pratilapsyate / katamānaṣṭau? tadyathā - utkṛṣṭa rūpaṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭabalaṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭaparivāraṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭapratibhānaṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭanaiṣkramyaṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭacittapariśuddhiṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭasamādhipadaṃ pratilapsyate / utkṛṣṭaprajñāvabhāsaṃ pratilapsyate / imānyaṣṭāvutkṛṣṭān dharmān pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, will make a reverential salutation (<s>añjali</s>) to this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s>, he will obtain eight eminent qualities. Which eight? Namely: he will obtain eminent form; he will obtain eminent strength; he will obtain an eminent retinue; he will obtain eminent eloquence; he will obtain eminent renunciation; he will obtain eminent purity of mind; he will obtain an eminent state of <s>samādhi</s>; he will obtain the eminent radiance of wisdom. These eight eminent qualities he will obtain." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣitukāmasya dharmabhāṇakasya dharmāsanaṃ prajñāpayiṣyati, tasyāṣṭāvāsanapratilambhāḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyāḥ sahaprajñapte āsane / katame 'ṣṭau? tadyathā - śreṣṭhyāsanapratilambhaḥ / gṛhapatyāsanapratilambhaḥ / cakravartyāsanapratilambhaḥ / lokapālāsanapratilambhaḥ / śakrāsanapratilambhaḥ / vaśavartyāsanapratilambhaḥ / brahmāsanapratilambhaḥ / bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatasya bodhisattvabhūtasyāpratyudāvartyanihatamārapratyarthikasiṃhāsanapratilambhaḥ / anuttarāsamyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya ato 'nuttaradharmacakrapravartanāsanapratilambhaśca pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ / ime 'ṣṭāvāsanapratilambhāḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, will prepare a <s>Dharma</s>-seat for a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher who wishes to recite this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s>, for him eight attainments of seats are to be expected the moment the seat is prepared. Which eight? Namely: the attainment of a merchant's seat; the attainment of a householder's seat; the attainment of a <s>Cakravartin</s>'s seat; the attainment of a world-protector's seat; the attainment of <s>Śakra</s>'s seat; the attainment of a sovereign's seat; the attainment of <s>Brahmā</s>'s seat; and the attainment of the lion-throne of one who, as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, has gone to the supreme and foremost <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> and cannot be turned back, having vanquished <s>Māra</s> the adversary; and the attainment of the seat for turning the unsurpassed wheel of <s>Dharma</s> of one who has fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect awakening — this too is to be expected. These are the eight attainments of seats to be expected." //

body.text: ya kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣamāṇāya sādhukāraṃ dāsyati, so 'ṣṭau vākpariśuddhīḥ pratilapsyate / katamā aṣṭau? tadyathā - yathāvāditathākāritāṃ satyānuparivartivākkarmapariśuddhyā / ādeyavacanatāṃ parṣadabhibhavanatayā / grāhyavacanatāṃ anuddhuratayā / ślakṣṇamadhuravacanatāṃ apāruṣyasattvasaṃgrahaṇatayā / kalaviṅkarutasvaratāṃ kāyacittodbilyakaraṇatayā / taduktavacanatāṃ sarvasattvairanabhibhavanatayā / brahmasvaratāṃ sarvasvarābhibhavanatayā / siṃhaghoṣābhigarjitasvaratāṃ sarvaparapravādibhiranabhibhavanatayā /
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, will applaud with 'well said!' (<s>sādhukāra</s>) one who is reciting this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s>, he will obtain eight purities of speech. Which eight? Namely: purity of speech-action through being one whose deeds match his words, following truth; having authoritative speech through overpowering the assembly; having credible speech through being without harshness; having smooth and sweet speech through gathering beings without cruelty; having a voice like a <s>Kalaviṅka</s> bird through causing elation of body and mind; having irrefutable speech through being unconquerable by all beings; having the voice of <s>Brahmā</s> through surpassing all voices; having a voice like a lion's roar through being unconquerable by all proponents of other doctrines; /

body.text: buddhasvaratāṃ sarvasattvendriyaparitoṣaṇatayā / imā aṣṭau vākkarmapariśuddhīḥ pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: having the voice of a <s>Buddha</s> through satisfying the faculties of all beings. These eight purities of speech-action he will obtain." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pustakalikhitaṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyati satkariṣyati gurukariṣyati mānayiṣyati pūjayiṣyati, amātsaryacittatayā caturdiśamasya dharmaparyāyasya varṇanāṃ bhāṣiṣyate varṇanāṃ coccārayiṣyati - āgacchatemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhitaṃ dhārayata vācayata cintayata svādhyāyateti, so aṣṭau mahānidhānāni pratilapsyate / katamānyaṣṭau mahānidhānāni? yaduta smṛtinidhānaṃ asaṃmoṣaṇatayā / matinidhānaṃ buddhiprabhedanatayā / gatinidhānaṃ sarvasūtrāntārthagatyanurāgatayā / dhāraṇīnidhānaṃ sarvaśrutādhāraṇatayā / pratibhānanidhānaṃ pratilabhate sarvasattvasubhāṣitasaṃbhāṣaṇatayā / dharmanidhānaṃ pratilabhate saddharmapratilakṣaṇatayā / bodhicittanidhānaṃ triratnavaṃśānupacchedanatayā / pratipattinidhānaṃ cānutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambhatayā / imānyaṣṭau nidhānāni pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, having had this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s> written in a book, will retain it, honor it, revere it, esteem it, and worship it, and with a mind free of selfishness will proclaim the praise of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the four directions, uttering the praise: 'Come! Retain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in written form, recite it, reflect upon it, study it!' — he will obtain eight great treasuries. Which eight great treasuries? Namely: the treasury of mindfulness, through not forgetting; the treasury of intellect, through the penetration of wisdom; the treasury of comprehension, through devotion to understanding the meaning of all <s>sūtrāntas</s>; the treasury of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, through retaining all that is heard; the treasury of eloquence, through engaging in well-spoken discourse with all beings; the treasury of <s>Dharma</s>, through discerning the true <s>Dharma</s>; the treasury of <s>bodhicitta</s>, through not cutting off the lineage of the Three Jewels; and the treasury of practice, through attaining the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>. These eight treasuries he will obtain." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ supravartitaṃ kṛtvā dhārayiṣyati, so 'ṣṭau saṃbhārān paripurayiṣyati / katamānaṣṭau? tadyathā - yaduta dānasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati amātsaryacittatayā / śīlasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati sarvakalyāṇābhiprāyaparipūraṇatayā / śrutasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati asaṅgaprajñāsamudānayanatayā / śamathasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati sarvasamādhisamāpattyāmukhīkaraṇatayā / vidarśanāsaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati traividyavidyāpratipūryā / puṇyasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkāraviśuddhyā / jñānasaṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati sarvasattvayathādhimuktisaṃtoṣaṇatayā / mahākaruṇā saṃbhāraṃ paripūrayiṣyati sarvasattvaparipācanāparikhedatayā / imānaṣṭau saṃbhārān paripūrayiṣyati //
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, having set this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s> into proper circulation, will retain it, he will fulfill eight accumulations. Which eight? Namely: he will fulfill the accumulation of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) through a mind free of selfishness; he will fulfill the accumulation of <s>śīla</s> (morality) through fulfilling all wholesome intentions; he will fulfill the accumulation of learning through generating unobstructed wisdom; he will fulfill the accumulation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm) through mastering all <s>samādhis</s> and attainments; he will fulfill the accumulation of <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight) through the fulfillment of the threefold knowledge; he will fulfill the accumulation of merit through the purification of the marks, characteristics, and <s>Buddha</s>-field adornments; he will fulfill the accumulation of knowledge through satisfying all beings according to their dispositions; he will fulfill the accumulation of great compassion through unwearying devotion to the ripening of all beings. These eight accumulations he will fulfill." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati, evaṃcitto yaduta kathamamī sattvā eṣāmevarūpāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhino bhaveyuriti, sa tena kuśalamūlenāṣṭau mahāpuṇyatāḥ pratilapsyate / katamā aṣṭau? tadyathā - rājā bhavati cakravartī, iyaṃ prathamā mahāpuṇyatā / caturmahārājakāyikānāṃ devānāmādhipatyaṃ kārayiṣyati, iyaṃ dvitīyā mahāpuṇyatā / śakro bhaviṣyati devendraḥ iyaṃ tṛtīyā mahāpuṇyatā / suyāmo bhaviṣyati devaputraḥ, iyaṃ caturthī mahāpuṇyatā saṃtuṣito bhaviṣyati, iyaṃ pañcamī mahāpuṇyatā / sunirmito bhaviṣyati, iyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī mahāpuṇyatā / vaśavartī bhaviṣyati devarājaḥ, iyaṃ saptamī mahāpuṇyatā / brahmā bhaviṣyati mahābrahmā, iyaṃ aṣṭamī mahāpuṇyatā / ante ca tathāgato bhaviṣyati arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvākuśaladharmaprahīnaḥ sarvakuśaladharmasamanvāgataḥ / imā aṣṭau mahāpuṇyatāḥ pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, will explain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s> extensively to others, with this thought: 'How may these beings become recipients of such qualities of <s>Dharma</s>?' — by that root of merit he will obtain eight great stations of merit. Which eight? Namely: he will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> king — this is the first great station of merit. He will exercise sovereignty over the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods — this is the second great station of merit. He will become <s>Śakra</s>, lord of gods — this is the third great station of merit. He will become the god-son <s>Suyāma</s> — this is the fourth great station of merit. He will become <s>Saṃtuṣita</s> — this is the fifth great station of merit. He will become <s>Sunirmita</s> — this is the sixth great station of merit. He will become <s>Vaśavartin</s>, the god-king — this is the seventh great station of merit. He will become <s>Brahmā</s>, the great <s>Brahmā</s> — this is the eighth great station of merit. And ultimately he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, having abandoned all unwholesome qualities and endowed with all wholesome qualities. These are the eight great stations of merit he will obtain." //

body.text: yaḥ kaścinmārṣā imaṃ lalitavistaraṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣyamāṇamavahitaśrotaḥ śroṣyati, so 'ṣṭau cittanirmalatāḥ pratilapsyate / katamā aṣṭau? tadyathā - yaduta maitrīṃ pratilapsyate sarvadoṣanirghātāya / karuṇāṃ pratilapsyate sarvavihiṃsotsargāya / muditāṃ pratilapsyate sarvāratyapakarṣaṇatāyai / upekṣāṃ pratilapsyate anunayapratighotsargāya / catvāri dhyānāni pratilapsyate sarvarūpadhātuvaśavartitāyai / catasra
body.translated_text: "Whoever, sirs, will listen with attentive ears to this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s> being recited, he will obtain eight purities of mind. Which eight? Namely: he will obtain <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) for the eradication of all faults; he will obtain <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) for the abandonment of all harm; he will obtain <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy) for the removal of all discontent; he will obtain <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) for the abandonment of attachment and aversion; he will obtain the four <s>dhyānas</s> for mastery over the entire realm of form; he will obtain the four

body.text: ārūpyasamāpattīḥ pratilapsyate cittavaśavartitāyai / pañcābhijñāḥ pratilapsyate anyabuddhakṣetragamanatāyai / sarvavāsanānusaṃdhisamuddhāraṃ pratilapsyate śūraṃgamasamādhipratilambhāya / imā aṣṭau cittanirmalatāḥ pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) for mastery over the mind; he will obtain the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) for the ability to travel to other <s>Buddha</s>-fields; he will obtain the eradication of all latent tendencies and their connections through attaining the <s>Śūraṅgama-samādhi</s> (heroic concentration). These are the eight purities of mind he will obtain." //

body.text: yasmiṃśca mārṣā grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vā janapadapradeśe vā caṃkrame vā vihāre vā ayaṃ lalitavistaro dharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyati, tatrāṣṭau bhayāni na prabhaviṣyanti sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam / katamānyaṣṭau? tadyathā - yaduta rājasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / caurasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / vyālasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / durbhikṣakāntārasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / anyonyakalahavivādavigrahasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / devasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / nāgasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / yakṣasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / sarvopadravasaṃkṣobhabhayaṃ na bhaviṣyati / imāni mārṣāstatrāṣṭau bhayāni na bhaviṣyanti (sthāpayitvā pūrvakarmavipākam) //
body.translated_text: "And wherever, sirs — in a village, city, town, district, province, promenade, or monastery — this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Lalitavistara</s> will circulate, there eight dangers will not prevail, setting aside the ripening of former <s>karma</s>. Which eight? Namely: there will be no danger of upheaval from kings; there will be no danger of upheaval from thieves; there will be no danger of upheaval from wild beasts; there will be no danger of upheaval from famine and desolation; there will be no danger of upheaval from mutual quarrels, disputes, and conflicts; there will be no danger of upheaval from gods; there will be no danger of upheaval from <s>nāgas</s>; there will be no danger of upheaval from <s>yakṣas</s>; there will be no danger of upheaval from any calamity whatsoever. These, sirs, are the eight dangers that will not prevail there (setting aside the ripening of former <s>karma</s>)." //

body.text: saṃkṣepānmārṣā yadi tathāgataḥ kalpasthitikenāyuṣpramāṇena rātriṃdivamadhiṣṭhamāno 'sya dharmaparyāyasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate, naivāsya dharmaparyāyasya varṇaparyanto bhavenna ca tathāgatapratibhānasya kṣayo bhavet / api tu khalu punarmārṣā yathaiva tathāgatasya śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktijñānadarśanamapramāṇamaparyantam, evameva mārṣā ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati likhiṣyati lekhayiṣyati paryavāpsyati pravartayiṣyati, parṣanmadhye ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati - anena cittena kathamamī sattvā evamudārasya dharmasya lābhinaḥ syuriti, teṣāmapi nāsti puṇyaparyantaḥ //
body.translated_text: "In brief, sirs, even if the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with a lifespan lasting a <s>kalpa</s>, were to praise this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse day and night without ceasing, the praise of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse would not come to an end, nor would the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s eloquence be exhausted. Moreover, sirs, just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge-and-vision are immeasurable and boundless, even so, sirs, whoever will take up, retain, recite, write, cause to be written, master, and circulate this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and will expound it extensively in the midst of an assembly — with this thought: 'How may these beings become recipients of such sublime <s>Dharma</s>?' — for them too, the merit is without limit." //

body.text: tataḥ khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapamāmantrayate sma āyuṣmantaṃ cānandaṃ maitreyaṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam - imāmahaṃ mārṣā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasrasamudānītāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ yuṣmākaṃ haste paridāmyanuparindāmi paramayā parindanayā, svayaṃ caivamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayata, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayata //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "Sirs, this unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, accumulated over innumerable <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, I place and entrust into your hands with the supreme entrustment. You yourselves should retain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and proclaim it extensively to others!" //

body.text: ityuktvā ca bhagavānasyaiva dharmaparyāyasya bhūyasyā mātrayānuparindanārthaṃ tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Having said this, the Blessed One, for the sake of even greater entrustment of this very <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, spoke this verse at that time —

children.text: sattvā dṛṣṭā ye mayā buddhadṛṣṭyā syuste 'rhantaḥ śariputreṇa tulyāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The beings whom I have beheld with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye — even if they were <s>Arhats</s> equal to <s>Śāriputra</s>,

children.text: tāṃścetkaścitpūjayetkalpakoṭī tulyāṃ gaṅgāvālikābhiyathaiva // Lal_27.1 //
children.translated_text: and someone were to worship them for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — // Lal_27.1 //

children.text: pratyekabuddhāya tu yaśca pūjāṃ kuyādahorātramapi prahṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: "yet one who would perform worship to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, joyfully, day and night,

children.text: mālyaiḥ prakāraiśca tathāparaiśca tasmādayaṃ puṇyakṛto viśiṣyate // Lal_27.2 //
children.translated_text: with garlands and with other offerings of various kinds — his merit-making would surpass even that! // Lal_27.2 //

children.text: syuḥ sarvasattvā yadi pratyayairjinā tāṃ pūjayetkaścidihāpramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If all beings were to become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> by their own [spiritual] causes, and someone were to worship them here diligently,

children.text: puṣpaiśca gandhaiśca vilepanaiśca kalpānanekāṃ satataṃ hi tatparam // Lal_27.3 //
children.translated_text: with flowers, perfumes, and ointments, constantly, for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>, devoted solely to that — // Lal_27.3 //

children.text: ekasya yaścaiva tathāgatasya kuryātpraṇāmaṃ api caikaśo 'pi /
children.translated_text: "yet one who would make a single bow to even one <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: prasannācitto 'tha vadennamo 'rhate tasmādidaṃ śreṣṭhataraṃ ca puṇyam // Lal_27.4 //
children.translated_text: with a serene mind saying "Homage to the <s>Arhat</s>!" — that merit would be superior even to that! // Lal_27.4 //

children.text: buddhā bhaveyuryadi sarvasattvā tāṃ pūjayedyaśca yathaiva pūrvam /
children.translated_text: "If all beings were to become <s>Buddhas</s> and one were to worship them as before,

children.text: divyaiśca puṣpairatha mānurṣairvaraiḥ kalpānanekāṃ bahubhiḥ prakāraiḥ // Lal_27.5 //
children.translated_text: with divine and the finest human flowers, for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>, in many ways — // Lal_27.5 //

children.text: yaścaiva saddharmavilopakātle tyaktvā svakāye ca tathaiva jīvitam /
children.translated_text: "yet one who, at a time when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being destroyed, were to renounce even his own body and life

children.text: vadyādahorātramidaṃ hi sūtraṃ viśiṣyate puṇyamidaṃ hi tasmāt // Lal_27.6 //
children.translated_text: and recite this <s>sūtra</s> day and night — that merit would surpass even that! // Lal_27.6 //

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ pūjayituṃ vināyakāṃ pratyekabuddhāṃśca tathaiva śrāvakāṃ /
children.translated_text: "Whoever desires to worship the Guides, the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the <s>Śrāvakas</s>,

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ samutpādya sa bodhicitta idaṃ sadā sūtravaraṃ dadhātu // Lal_27.7 //
children.translated_text: let him firmly generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) and always retain this supreme <s>sūtra</s>! // Lal_27.7 //

children.text: rājā hyayaṃ sarvasubhāṣitānāṃ yo 'bhyudgataḥ sarvatathāgatānām /
children.translated_text: "For this is the king of all well-spoken words, which has arisen from all <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: gṛhe sthitastasya tathāgataḥ sadā tiṣṭhedidaṃ yatra hi sūtraratnam // Lal_27.8 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s> always dwells in the house where this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s> is found! // Lal_27.8 //

children.text: pratibhāṃ sa prāpnoti śubhāmanantāṃ ekaṃ padaṃ vakṣyati kalpakoṭī /
children.translated_text: "He will obtain splendid, boundless eloquence — he will expound a single word for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: na vyañjanā bhraśyati nāpi cārthā dadyācca yaḥ sūtramida parebhyaḥ // Lal_27.9 //
children.translated_text: and neither the syllables nor the meaning will be lost — whoever gives this <s>sūtra</s> to others! // Lal_27.9 //

body.text: anuttaro 'sau naranāyakānāṃ sattvo na kaścitsadṛśo 'sya vidyate /
body.translated_text: "He is unsurpassed among the guides of men — no being is found equal to him;

body.text: bhavetsamudreṇa samaśca so 'kṣayaḥ śrutvā hi yo dharmamimaṃ prapadyate // Lal_27.10 //
body.translated_text: he would become inexhaustible as the ocean — whoever, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>, puts it into practice!" // Lal_27.10 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: idamavocadbhagavānāttamanāḥ / te maheśvaradevaputrapūrvaṃgamāḥ śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrā maitreyapūrvaṃgamāśca sarvabodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahākāśyapapūrvaṃgamāśca sarvamahāśrāvakāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan //
body.translated_text: This the Blessed One spoke, and they were delighted. The <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> god-sons led by the god-son <s>Maheśvara</s>, all the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> led by <s>Maitreya</s>, all the great <s>Śrāvakas</s> led by <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> — all rejoiced at the Blessed One's words. //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus. //

body.text: // iti śrīlalitavistare nigamaparivarto nāma saptaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: // Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter of the noble <s>Lalitavistara</s>, named the Conclusion Chapter (<s>Nigamaparivarta</s>). //

body.text: samāptaṃ cedaṃ sarvabodhisattvacaryāprasthānam //
body.translated_text: Here ends the introduction to the conduct of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. //

body.text: // śrīlalitavistaro nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ ratnarājaṃ parisamāptam //
body.translated_text: // The noble <s>Lalitavistara</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>, the King of Jewels, is completed. //

children.text: ye dharma hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Of those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic. //
